# Anfield Derby

*This page is about the battle. For other uses, see: Anfield Derby (disambiguation)*

"*You're going to die tomorrow, Lord Baryatinsky. Sleep well.*"
―Sofia Volkonskaya to Radomir Baryatinsky
The **Anfield Derby** was a major battle late in the Five Stadiums Cup, fought as part of the northern theater of the conflict in 303 AC. It saw a Volkonsky\-Dolgorukov\-Free Folk coalition force led by Ivan Morozov and Sofia Volkonskaya engage Lord Radomir Baryatinsky, Keeper of Camp Nou District, and his allied vassal houses for control of Anfield. The battle resulted in House Volkonsky being restored to its status as the ruling house of the Camp Nou District, whilst marking the end of House Baryatinsky.

This battle's conclusion marks the end of the northern theater of the Five Stadiums Cup.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Prelude

"*A monster has taken our home and our brother. We have to go back to Anfield and save them both!*"
―Sofia Volkonskaya to Ivan SnowFollowing the death of King Roman Volkonsky and most of his bannermen at the Maracana Night, the Silver Tribune named House Baryatinsky the new ruling Great House of the Camp Nou District. However, to cement their hold on the Camp Nou District following the murders of King Makar Orlov and his Hand, Lord Tikhon Sheremetev, the Baryatinskys decided to betray the Sheremetevs. To that end, they secured a marriage alliance through Lord Daniil Bestuzhev between Sofia Volkonskaya (formerly the Sheremetevs' hostage) with Radomir Baryatinsky, Lord Ruslan Baryatinsky's recently\-legitimized bastard son. With help from the Baryatinskys' prisoner, Timofey Stroganov, Sofia escaped her home during Stepan Orlov's ill\-fated attack on Anfield and fled to Wembley Park with Elena Tatischeva and Klim Panin. There, she reunited with her half\-brother, Ivan Morozov, who was on the verge of leaving the Anfield Guard following his death and resurrection.

With Sofia's escape and her refuge with Ivan at Wembley Park, and the birth of a son to Ruslan Baryatinsky and his new wife, Walda Baryatinsky, Radomir's position as Ruslan's heir was now shrouded in uncertainty. In a bid to secure his position, Radomir murdered his father and orchestrated the brutal deaths of his stepmother and newborn half\-brother by feeding them to his hounds. The ruthless act propelled Radomir into the position as the new head of House Baryatinsky, Lord of the Dreadfort, Lord of Anfield, and Keeper of Camp Nou District.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Prelude

Sofia implored Ivan to help her take back Anfield from the Baryatinskys. Although Ivan was initially hesitant due to his weariness from fighting, he eventually agreed after receiving a letter from Radomir. In the letter, Radomir denounced Ivan as a traitor for allowing the wildlings to cross the Sudtribune. Furthermore, Radomir revealed that he was holding Ivan and Sofia's younger brother, Rickon, hostage and demanded Sofia's return, warning that he would slaughter Ivan, Rickon and the wildlings, before having Sofia gang\-raped if he refused. Ivan and Sofia resolved to march south to confront the Baryatinskys in order to save their younger brother and retake Anfield.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Raising an army

"*There are more than three other houses in the Camp Nou District: Gorchakov, Mamonov, Chertkov, Mazin, Hornwood. Two dozen more. Together they equal all the others. We can start small and build.*"
―Ivan Morozov
With the Vyazemskys and Uvarovs having declared for Radomir due to their anger toward Roman and Ivan, respectively, Ivan and Sofia are forced to rely on the support of the the meager forces of the minor Northern Houses to aid them. They manage to persuade the Free Folk, House Mazin, House Hornwood, and House Mamonov to join them. However, Lord Egor Gorchakov, head of House Gorchakov, refuses to declare for them, citing both his hatred for the wildlings and his anger at Roman for failing to protect them from Stepan Stroganov's invasion. Similarly, House Milyutin also declines to support the Volkonskys, with Lord Fedor Milyutin refusing to have more Milyutins die for a cause he believed was lost. Sofia sends Brienne to the Mersey Grounds to treat with her great\-uncle, Viktor Trubetskoy, who is under siege at Riverrun. Unfortunately, Brynden refuses to leave his home and is later killed when the castle falls to House Demidov and House Sheremetev. Brienne and Podrick, however, are able to escape Riverrun's fall through the river.

Despite gathering a number of allies, the coalition force is still heavily outnumbered by the Baryatinskys. Ivan is adamant that they attack Anfield as soon as possible to prevent Radomir from gathering more men or to avoid the weather turning against them, like it did for Stepan Orlov. Sofia argues they still need more men and wants to try to recruit more houses. When Ivan argues that they are out of time and must strike now, Sofia secretly writes a letter to Littlefinger calling for help.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Parley and recess

"*There's no need for a battle. Thousands of men don't need to die. Only one of us. Let's end this the old way: you against me.*"
―Ivan Morozov to Radomir BoltonOn the day before the battle, the Volkonsky leadership agrees to parley with the Baryatinskys. Radomir immediately offers terms for Ivan's surrender: return Sofia to him, bend the knee and acknowledge Radomir as the Lord of Anfield and Keeper of Camp Nou District. In exchange, Radomir claims he will not harm his men and Ivan will be pardoned for deserting his post as Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard. Ivan rejects the terms, knowing that Radomir has broken his own surrender terms multiple times in the past, and instead opts for a different solution to save both the armies: single combat to determine the fate of the Camp Nou District.

Radomir rejects Ivan's terms in turn, as he has heard of Ivan's reputation as the best swordsman in the Camp Nou District, and he knows his army is more numerous and better equipped than Ivan's. Ivan retorts by pointing out that Radomir's army is built on shaky loyalty, whereas his own know that their leader would live and die for them. This angers Radomir, and prompts him to threaten to kill Rickon if Ivan will not surrender. It is at this moment Sofia questions whether Radomir really has their brother; Boris Uvarov answers by pulling out Shaggydog's severed head and throwing it at their feet. When Radomir starts to speak again, Sofia confidently tells him that he is going to die when they meet on the battlefield the next day and to sleep well.

text:
# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Parley and recess

At the Volkonsky camp, plans are drawn up for the coming battle. Knowing that Radomir's numbers are superior, and Semyon Apraksin not wanting to be annihilated by mounted soldiers as when Stepan and Davos defeated the wildings, they will instead bait him into a "double envelopment", using his recklessness and anger against him. After Davos, Semyon Apraksin, and the rest of the lords are dismissed for the evening, Sofia approaches Ivan, rebuking him for not consulting her. She goes on to tell Ivan he doesn't know how Radomir's mind works and that he likes toying with people. The two proceed to argue, with Sofia stating to Ivan they need more men and should wait to attack with a larger force. Ivan replies that he believes they have already recruited all the men who will fight for them. He goes on to tell Sofia that he vows to protect her. However, Sofia, jaded by years of failures and disappointments, replies that no one can protect her or anyone now.

Meanwhile, Davos and Semyon Apraksin take a walk out into the camp, comparing their experiences serving Stepan and Mance, respectively, and the ultimate futility of believing in kings. After some banter, Davos walks up the hill to where he sees a funeral pyre. Spotting and picking up the toy stag he gave to Shireen before Stepan' ill fated attack on the Baryatinskys, he comes to the conclusion that Ekaterina Lomonosova must have sacrificed Shireen to the Lord of Light.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > The battle

"*Who owns the Camp Nou District?!*"
―Boris Uvarov rouses the Baryatinsky infantry.The battle begins with the Volkonsky army deployed near a treeline to prevent themselves from being attacked unaware from behind. Across the field is the much larger Baryatinsky army, which has placed archery distance markers with burning, flayed corpses attached to them to demoralize the Volkonsky troops. Radomir trots out on his horse to the front of the formation, bringing a prisoner: Alexei Volkonsky himself. Radomir acts at first as if he will slit Rickon's throat, but instead cuts his bonds and sadistically insists that they play a game. He points at Ivan and tells Rickon, "Run to your brother." Rickon starts running straight toward Ivan, while Radomir shoots and purposely misses with a war bow. Just when Rickon is about to reach Ivan, however, Radomir's final deliberate shot hits Rickon through the heart, killing him almost instantly.

Enraged and maddened with grief, Ivan charges full tilt at the Baryatinsky army, whom Radomir immediately orders to loose their arrows on him. Alarmed, Davos orders in the Volkonsky cavalry to charge after their commander, with the Volkonsky and wildling infantry closely following behind. The first Baryatinsky volley down Ivan's horse, forcing him to the ground. Ivan quickly recovers and prepares for his last stand by drawing Longclaw as he seemingly faces down the Baryatinsky cavalry alone. He is saved by the timely arrival of the Volkonsky cavalry as they collide with their Baryatinsky counterparts, and the battle becomes a bloody storm of swords. Countless men on both sides fall in battle so quickly that they begin to form small hills of the dead.

text:
# Anfield Derby
Section: History > The battle

Radomir orders his archers to shoot at the Volkonsky forces and their own cavalry, while Davos refrains from doing the same and leads his archers to join Ivan and the rest of their forces in battle. The arrow volley kills scores of both Volkonsky and Baryatinsky men, and soon, the small hills become a wall of the fallen. Although Radomir loses many of his men to friendly fire, it becomes clear that they are intentionally being sacrificed as part of a sadistic plan to prevent his enemy from retreating. Seeing the Volkonsky infantry and archers, alongside Wun Wun and wildling warriors, engaging in combat with the Baryatinsky forces, Radomir sends forward his remaining forces, led by Boris Uvarov, into battle. The Baryatinsky infantry succeeds in encircling the remaining Volkonsky army, boxing them in with a shield phalanx.

The Baryatinsky phalanx acts as a noose, tightening around the beleaguered Volkonsky and wildling forces, who sustain heavy casualties in the process. As they retreat inward toward the wall of dead, they trample the wounded and squeeze so tightly that many are soon unable to properly move. Smalljon leads a small force over the wall of dead to ensure that none of Volkonsky forces can escape. Ivan is barely able to save himself from being crushed to death as his troops are squeezed into a close\-knit circle.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > The endgame

"*You suggested one\-on\-one combat, didn't you? I've reconsidered. I think that sounds like a wonderful idea.*"
―Radomir Baryatinsky to Ivan Morozov
Just when all hope seems lost for the Volkonskys and Free Folk, a war horn sounds off in the distance. Around the bend appears a large mounted host of the Knights of the Dortmund Heights, led by Lord Bestuzhev, Lady Sofia, and Lord Rodion Panin. The newly arrived Dolgorukov reinforcements quickly turn the tide in favor of the Volkonskys. With the phalanx facing inward towards the Volkonsky forces, the Dortmund Heights knights are able to attack the Baryatinskys' undefended side, wiping away Radomir's phalanx and freeing the Volkonsky soldiers. Semyon Apraksin, meanwhile, kills Smalljon in a brutal duel. Radomir, with his infantry force all but destroyed, decides to retreat to Anfield to hold out in a siege. In a murderous fury, Ivan gives chase alongside Semyon Apraksin and Wun Wun.

text:
# Anfield Derby
Section: History > The endgame

Despite his general's concerns, Radomir expresses confidence they can withstand the Volkonskys since they hold Anfield and the Volkonskys lack the manpower for a protracted siege. His plan goes awry, however, when Wun Wun breaks down the main gate, allowing the Volkonskys and Dolgorukovs to pour through. They swiftly kill all remaining Baryatinsky archers and infantry in the castle. Wun Wun collapses to his knees after being hit by several arrows, bolts, and javelins. Before Ivan can comfort his friend, however, Radomir kills the giant with an arrow through the eye. Radomir, refusing to surrender, taunts Ivan, saying that he finally accepts his proposal of single combat before shooting arrows at an unarmed Ivan. Enraged, Ivan grabs a shield from a fallen Mamonov soldier and while boldly advancing, blocks three of Radomir's shots. When he reaches Radomir, he smacks the bow out of his hands and knocks him to the ground. With Radomir down, Ivan pins him and proceeds to beat him savagely. Though it seems he will kill Radomir, Ivan stops when he sees Sofia, realizing she has as much right to revenge as he does. Ivan orders Radomir locked in the kennels, and the Flayed Man banners drop to the ground in a cluttered heap while the Direwolf banner is raised above Anfield for the first time in three years. With Radomir's defeat, the Baryatinskys' rule of the Camp Nou District is over, and House Volkonsky and its allies retake the Camp Nou District with a decisive, albeit costly, victory.

text:
# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Aftermath

**Radomir Baryatinsky**: "*You can't kill me. I'm part of you now.*"
**Sofia Volkonskaya**: "*Your words will disappear. Your house will disappear. Your name will disappear. All memory of you will disappear.*"
— Sofia Volkonskaya and Radomir Baryatinsky.

Although House Volkonsky was restored to their seat at Anfield as a Great House of the Camp Nou District and gained the support of House Dolgorukov in the Five Stadiums Cup, the price of this victory was high. The Volkonsky\-Free Folk coalition sustained heavy losses in the battle, leaving no Northern house with a significant force left to oppose Littlefinger, the Midnight Regent, the Silver Tribune, or even Daria Romanova, should either one of them decide to conquer the Camp Nou District, save for those who sat out the conflict, such as the Milyutins, the Chertkovs, and the Gorchakovs. Worse, the heir apparent to Anfield and House Volkonsky, Rickon, was now dead, leaving the newly restored Great House in the hands of an illegitimate son and an eldest daughter. Following the battle, Ivan orders Rickon to be buried next to their father, while Sofia decides to visit Radomir in the kennels, ironically the same place he kept Timofey over the course of a year.

# Anfield Derby
Section: History > Aftermath

Upon seeing Sofia, Radomir tries to goad her one last time, telling her that he will always be a part of her now. She throws back the insult by pointing out that very soon, his legacy and that of House Baryatinsky will be forever erased from history. Radomir soon notices his hounds coming closer to him, the kennel doors having been left open. # Anfield Guard

*This page is about the military order. For the short, see: The Anfield Guard*

"*Night gathers, and now my watch begins. It shall not end until my death. I shall take no wife, hold no lands, father no children. I shall wear no crowns and win no glory. I shall live and die at my post. I am the sword in the darkness. I am the watcher on the walls. I am the shield that guards the realms of men. I pledge my life and honor to the Anfield Guard, for this night and all the nights to come.*"
―The Anfield Guard oath
The **Anfield Guard** is a military order which holds and guards the Sudtribune to keep the wildlings and Frost Wanderers from crossing into the Greater Wembley. The order is a shadow of its former strength and its meager forces have been decimated by recent attacks from both wildlings and Frost Wanderers. For the past couple of centuries, the order has been led from Wembley Park.

The Anfield Guard is organized in three departments: the Rangers, who fight, defend the Sudtribune and patrol the Haunted Forest; the Builders, who maintain the Sudtribune and the castles; and the Stewards, who support and feed the members of the Watch.

Following the Breaching of the Sudtribune, Ivan Morozov called for the remaining members of the Anfield Guard to come to Anfield to help defend against the Midnight Regent and the Army of the Dead, since the Sudtribune no longer serves any defensive purpose. With the extinction of the Frost Wanderers in the Camp Nou Derby, the Watch's purpose has been fulfilled, but continues to serve as a quarantine for the banished, poor and unfortunate.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Background

According to legend, the Anfield Guard was founded 8,000 years ago, in the last days of the Long Night. Their original purpose was to defend against the Frost Wanderers, but after the demons' disappearance, the order was also tasked with keeping other dangers at bay. They now protect the Greater Wembley from threats beyond their northern border, such as wildlings and giants, and, should the need arise, Frost Wanderers. They man, maintain and defend a vast structure known as the Sudtribune, a 700 foot tall and 300\-mile long barrier which separates the Greater Wembley from the lands to the far north. It is formed mostly from ice with small trenches and wooden fortifications covering the top. The Watch have built nineteen castles along the southern edge of the Sudtribune to house their men. However, the Watch's gradually shrinking numbers meant that all but three of these had to be abandoned. They also control a region south of the Sudtribune known as the Gift, from which they obtain supplies and provisions. The region was donated to them by House Volkonsky, the Kings in the Camp Nou District, thousands of years ago.

Members of the Anfield Guard swear an oath of duty that prohibits marriage, family, and land ownership which lasts until their death. Recruits renounce all past allegiances and birthrights. Joining the Watch provides absolution for past crimes and immunity from further punishment. Brothers start with a clean slate and can rise within the ranks whatever their origins.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Background

However, even though the Anfield Guard vows are meant to be for life, it is possible for one to leave the organization without execution, so long as it is with the ruling monarch's approval. For instance, Stepan Orlov, a claimant to the Silver Tribune and the King in the Narrow Sea, offers Ivan a chance to leave the Anfield Guard and serve him in exchange for legitimization, though this may partially be due to the fact that the Anfield Guard is not taken as seriously by most as it once was, and Stepan was desperate enough to turn to Ivan Morozov for aid. Another instance is Sam, who was allowed to leave for Azteca, to become a maester of the Watch by Ivan.

They describe one another as "sworn brothers" because of the oath. Men of the Watch dress entirely in black, giving rise to the nickname "crows" \- which is what the Free Folk commonly call them \- or "black brothers." Members of the Anfield Guard are not specifically forbidden from seeing their families, but they cannot leave the Sudtribune without permission. Desertion is punishable by death. First Ranger Andrei Volkonsky would often visit his family at Anfield while representing the Anfield Guard.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Background

The Watch was once highly regarded and their ranks were filled with volunteers from noble houses, as serving was a sign of selfless devotion to the protection of the realm. However, while the Anfield Guard still has noble\-born sons and noble\-blooded illegitimate sons from Great Houses, many recruits are now also criminals avoiding punishment, nobles avoiding scandal, orphans, and other social outcasts. Men known as wandering crows, such as Nikolai Potemkin, travel around the Greater Wembley gathering recruits for the Watch, offering them escape on the Sudtribune. For some families, the Sudtribune is a convenient place to exile embarrassing or disgraced family members: Sam was disowned by his own father and ordered to join the Watch on threat of death, while Tikhon had plans to exile his own son Terenty to the Sudtribune so as to avoid executing him for allegedly murdering Joffrey. However, other families, such as House Volkonsky, view the Anfield Guard as an honorable and noble calling. Generations of Volkonskys have joined the Anfield Guard for the sake of honor.

By the reign of King Rodion Orlov, the institution has fallen into disrepute and is largely ignored by the throne. It is severely undermanned; dwindling numbers have led to all but three of the Sudtribune's nineteen castles being abandoned. The Anfield Guard is now led from its stronghold at Wembley Park. The Shadow Tower and Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea are the only other castles that are still manned. Meanwhile, trouble is stirring beyond the Sudtribune. A large wildling army under a new King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune, Serafim Bestuzhev, is advancing south, and there are rumors that the Frost Wanderers, long since thought to be extinct, have returned. At the time Ivan arrives at Wembley Park, the Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard is Luka Mamonov.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Background

Although joining the Anfield Guard is often a punishment for many, it can also be a positive thing in the long run; the Watch is highly egalitarian compared to the rest of Greater Wembley, and in a rigidly hierarchical society, joining can offer a rare chance at redemption and turning one's life around. At the Sudtribune, every man is given what he earns, no matter their status, and even lowborn or bastard recruits can become high\-ranking officers and commanders for their service. However, the Anfield Guard is not completely egalitarian; both noble\-born sons and illegitimate sons of lords are typically favored for advancement over those with no noble blood, though this may also be for the practical reason that recruits from noble households are generally more familiar with the duties required of the Watch, such as combat skill. This is clearly demonstrated when Ivan easily defeats the other recruits in sparring practice, and Terenty points out that none of the others have had the kind of training Ivan received from Ser Anton Karamzin.

# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Increased wildling activity beyond the Sudtribune leads the Watch to send out several patrols to investigate. Some do not return. A three\-man scouting party consisting of Ser Waymar Royce, Gared, and Will is sent out, but only Will returns \- then frantically tries to desert the Watch by running south but was caught. He rambles that the legendary Frost Wanderers killed his companions, but he is disbelieved as a madman and beheaded by Eduard Volkonsky for desertion.

When Terenty makes a visit to the Sudtribune while traveling to Anfield, he is met at Wembley Park by Lord Commander Luka Mamonov and Maester Akim Romanov. They implore him to bring news to the king that the Anfield Guard is severely undermanned and undersupported: they are down to under a thousand members, and barely have the resources to feed and support the few men they still have. Mamonov warns Terenty about disturbing rumors coming from beyond the Sudtribune, about missing scouting parties, and the one man who did survive an attack say it was the Frost Wanderers finally returning, just before he was executed. Akim Romanov warns that they have had a very long summer lasting for years, and that the coming winter may also be long and bitter \- and only the gods can help them if they do not do more to prepare for what's coming.

# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Following the defeat of the wildling army and the execution of Serafim Bestuzhev, the Anfield Guard elects Ivan as its new Lord Commander, who attempts to rebuild the Watch and pay more attention to the growing threat of the Frost Wanderers. Ivan was able to convince a few minor houses to send more men to the Sudtribune and opts to make peace between the Anfield Guard and the wildlings to save them from dying and becoming part of the Frost Wanderer army, having come to feel sympathy for them as they are men, women, and children who were born on the other side of the Sudtribune and are also fleeing the Frost Wanderers. Ivan, Edd, other Watchmen, and Semyon Apraksin go on a rescue mission to Hardhome to save the wildlings but the Midnight Regent attacks Hardhome. Ivan and his party return with the surviving wildlings and bring them south of the Sudtribune. This decision is met with harsh criticism by many of the black brothers, including Makar Tchaadayev, Nikita Panin and Matvey Mordvinov. Ivan is later stabbed by his own brothers in a mutiny and left for dead.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

After the Breaching of the Sudtribune, the Anfield Guard abandon their castles and travel south towards Anfield to aid in its defense.

Many of the defenders, among them members of the Watch, perish in the Camp Nou Derby. With the extinction of the Frost Wanderers, the purpose of the Anfield Guard has been served. However, as Terenty mentions, the Anfield Guard continues to serve as a quarantine to the poor, banished, and unfortunate. The surviving members returned to the castles along with the wildlings after the battle.

Following the Battle of Wembley, Ivan assassinates Daria. In order to avoid a war between the Unsullied and Ivan's supporters, Terenty, as his position as Tribune Steward to Boris, regretfully informs him that Boris has banished him to the Anfield Guard again, which Ivan accepts.

After reaching Wembley Park, Ivan reunites with Semyon Apraksin, Ghost and all the remaining Free Folk. He leaves along with the Free Folk for the lands beyond the Sudtribune, looking forlornly when the gate of the keep closes behind him.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: Organization > Structure

Men of the Anfield Guard are divided between three different orders: the Rangers, the Builders, and the Stewards. Each order is led by its own officer, each appointed by the Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard: the First Ranger, First Builder, and First Steward (who is sometimes interchangeably called Lord Steward).

- Rangers \- the true warriors of the Anfield Guard. While all black brothers are expected to have some basic arms training and to take up a sword in defense of the Sudtribune itself, the Rangers are the ones who are sent on dangerous scouting expeditions beyond the Sudtribune, to track wildlings movements. When the Watch was more numerous in past centuries they formed the core fighting group sent to destroy large wildling warbands who attempted to pass south of the Sudtribune.
- Builders \- who physically maintain the structures of the Anfield Guard, and repair the Sudtribune itself. Miners, masons, foresters, carpenters and other such roles are part of the Builders.
- Stewards \- who provide for the day\-to\-day needs of the Watch: gathering, cooking, and serving food, repairing clothes and equipment, tending to the horses and messenger\-ravens, and gathering firewood. Due to its catering, technical and quartermaster functions, the Stewards are by far the largest of the three orders.

# Anfield Guard
Section: Organization > Structure

Each castle of the Anfield Guard also has a maester assigned to it. These maesters take the oath of the Anfield Guard and are considered full black brothers, but are not considered part of the three orders, nor are they their own 'order'. Given that there were never more than nineteen castles along the Sudtribune, there were never more than nineteen maesters in the Anfield Guard at any one time. Since there are only three active castles on the Sudtribune in modern times, there are now presumably only three maesters in the Anfield Guard at a time.

# Anfield Guard
Section: Organization > Leadership

The leader of the Anfield Guard is the Lord Commander. Each Lord Commander serves for life, and a new Lord Commander is democratically elected from any black brother by all other members of the Anfield Guard in a choosing.

It is unknown if there is any formal procedure to depose a Lord Commander and elect a new one, in cases where the current Lord Commander violates his oaths or is deemed medically unfit to lead, etc.

# Anfield Guard
Section: Organization > Recruitment

"*Raper, raper, horse thief, ninth\-born son, raper, thief, thief AND raper...*"
―An officer at Wembley Park reviewing a line of new recruits who are joining the Anfield Guard.
Recruiters commonly known as "wandering crows" travel to the cities of southern Greater Wembley to gather up new recruits to join the Anfield Guard. In recent years, most of these tend to be criminals, murderers, rapers, and thieves taken from the dungeons of major cities and towns. A few also join because they are desperately poor and have no other better options. Once in a great while a younger son or bastard son of a major noble House will decide to join the Anfield Guard, but they can often afford to travel to the Anfield Guard on their own initiative \- such as Ivan Morozov (a bastard) and Waymar Royce (a third\-born son).

Recruiters are few in number, and they are not considered a separate order in the Anfield Guard. Instead, they are drawn from trusted members of the three orders, often those who can no longer fight well due to injuries but who can still travel.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: Organization > Military strength

Late in the reign of King Rodion Orlov, the Anfield Guard has dwindled to under one thousand members \- many of them composed of old men, untrained boys, and convicted felons. While there are nineteen castles along the Sudtribune, the Watch only has enough men to continue to man three of them: their headquarters Wembley Park in the middle, the Shadow Tower at the western end, and their port Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea at the eastern end. Furthermore, with the breakout of The Five Stadiums Cup, recruitment for the Watch has drastically decreased.

The Watch takes severe losses in Luka Mamonov's disastrous expedition beyond the Sudtribune, losing nearly three hundred men as a result. Combined with heavy losses during the battle for the Sudtribune, as well as losses from other wildling attacks, by the time that King Stepan Orlov arrives at the Sudtribune, the entire organization had less than half (around 500 men) of its military strength remain. After becoming Lord Commander, Ivan convinces a few minor houses (Houses Ashford, Caulfield, Smallwood, Mazin, and Wibberley) to send men to the Anfield Guard. The Watch suffers further losses after the Massacre at Hardhome and the Mutiny at Wembley Park, leading Ivan to order the surviving wildlings to help garrison the remaining castles, likely raising their numbers by a few hundreds. However, much of this new strength is lost at the breaching of the Sudtribune, with only a dozen left alive from Eastwatch.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: Possessions > Castles along the Sudtribune

There are nineteen castles spread out along the southern face of the Sudtribune as bases for the Anfield Guard. Patrols from these castles would travel along the top of the Sudtribune watching for threats from the north, or repairing damage to the Sudtribune. Each castle also contained a tunnel cut under the Sudtribune, through which scouting parties would travel to the north to track wildling movements.

As the Anfield Guard dwindled over the centuries, however, most of these castles were abandoned, and their tunnels sealed with ice. By the end of the reign of King Rodion Orlov, only three major castles along the Sudtribune are still manned: Wembley Park, the Shadow Tower, and Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea. In Arc Three also appears the ruin of was was once the Nightfort.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: Possessions > The Gift

The Gift is a region to the south of the Sudtribune under the direct control of the Anfield Guard. It lies at the northern edge of the region known as the Camp Nou District. It was donated to the Anfield Guard by House Volkonsky when the order was founded thousands of years ago, in order to support the Anfield Guard with food and provisions. The Gift is officially not subject to the authority of Anfield, and is technically not part of "Camp Nou District", but is a special administrative zone directly ruled by the Anfield Guard.

The Gift is sparsely populated by only a handful of smallfolk, as most have relocated to the south over the generations while the Anfield Guard dwindled and wildling raiding parties over or around the Sudtribune increased in frequency. The northern areas closer to the Sudtribune are almost completely empty. The closest significant settlement near the Sudtribune is Mole's Town, located a few miles down the Kingsroad from Wembley Park.

# Anfield Guard
Section: Notable members > Past Lord Commanders

The original headquarters of the Anfield Guard was the Nightfort, the first castle built at the Sudtribune, and thus for thousands of years, it was where the Lord Commander of the Watch resided. A little over two hundred years before the Five Stadiums Cup, during the reign of King Jaehaerys I Romanov, the Anfield Guard abandoned the Nightfort because they could no longer maintain it with their dwindling resources. Instead, they relocated their headquarters to Wembley Park, where all subsequent Lord Commanders were based.

- The "Night's King" \- one of the early Lord Commanders who, according to legend, lived eight thousand years ago. The legends say that he was seduced by a female Frost Wanderer, declared himself king of the Anfield Guard, and conducted human sacrifices at the Nightfort. It took an alliance between the Volkonsky King in the Camp Nou District and the wildling King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune Joramun to overthrow him, and restore the Anfield Guard.
- Stepan Dashkov \- held the position during the reign of King Aegon V Romanov.

# Anfield Guard
Section: Oath

When joining the Anfield Guard, all members must swear the following oath, either in a sept if they are of the Faith of the Seven, or before a heart tree if they follow the Old Gods.

> *Hear my words and bear witness to my vow. Night gathers, and now my watch begins. It shall not end until my death. I shall take no wife, hold no lands, father no children. I shall wear no crowns and win no glory. I shall live and die at my post. I am the sword in the darkness. I am the watcher on the walls. I am the shield that guards the realms of men. I pledge my life and honor to the Anfield Guard, for this night and all the nights to come.*

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: Quotes

"*The Anfield Guard is the only thing standing between the realm and what lies beyond and it has become an army of undisciplined boys and tired old men. There are less than a thousand of us now. We can't man the other castles on the Sudtribune. We can't properly patrol the wilderness. We have barely enough resources to keep our lads armed and fed.*"
―Maester Akim Romanov to Terenty Sheremetev

"*We've been guarding the Districts for eight thousand years.*"
―Ivan Morozov to Ser Yakov Sheremetev

"*There's great honor serving in the Anfield Guard. The Volkonskys have manned the Sudtribune for thousands of years. And you are a Volkonsky. You might not have my name, but you have my blood.*"
―Eduard Volkonsky to Ivan Morozov

"*Here, a man gets what he earns, when he earns it.*"
―Andrei Volkonsky to Ivan Morozov

"*You came to us as outlaws, poachers, rapers, killers, thieves. You came alone, in chains, without friends or honor. You came to us rich and you came to us poor. Some of you bear the names of proud Houses, others only bastard names or no names at all. It does not matter. All that is in the past. Here on the Sudtribune, we are all one House.*"
―Luka Mamonov to the recruits

"*You knelt as boys; rise now, as men of the Anfield Guard*"
―Nikita Panin to Serafim Tatischev and Ivan Morozov after taking their vows.

"*Don't go home. Join the Anfield Guard. Once a man has taken the black, he is beyond reach of the law. All his past crimes are forgiven.*"
―Maester Arseny Apraksin advises Timofey Stroganov to join the Anfield Guard.
body:
"*The Anfield Guard is the only thing standing between the realm and what lies beyond and it has become an army of undisciplined boys and tired old men. There are less than a thousand of us now. We can't man the other castles on the Sudtribune. We can't properly patrol the wilderness. We have barely enough resources to keep our lads armed and fed.*"
―Maester Akim Romanov to Terenty Sheremetev

"*We've been guarding the Districts for eight thousand years.*"
―Ivan Morozov to Ser Yakov Sheremetev

"*There's great honor serving in the Anfield Guard. The Volkonskys have manned the Sudtribune for thousands of years. And you are a Volkonsky. You might not have my name, but you have my blood.*"
―Eduard Volkonsky to Ivan Morozov

"*Here, a man gets what he earns, when he earns it.*"
―Andrei Volkonsky to Ivan Morozov

"*You came to us as outlaws, poachers, rapers, killers, thieves. You came alone, in chains, without friends or honor. You came to us rich and you came to us poor. Some of you bear the names of proud Houses, others only bastard names or no names at all. It does not matter. All that is in the past. Here on the Sudtribune, we are all one House.*"
―Luka Mamonov to the recruits

"*You knelt as boys; rise now, as men of the Anfield Guard*"
―Nikita Panin to Serafim Tatischev and Ivan Morozov after taking their vows.

"*Don't go home. Join the Anfield Guard. Once a man has taken the black, he is beyond reach of the law. All his past crimes are forgiven.*"
―Maester Arseny Apraksin advises Timofey Stroganov to join the Anfield Guard.

# Anfield Guard
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the First Ranger is Andrei Volkonsky, while the Lord Commander is Luka Mamonov, the father of Vsevolod Mamonov. The Anfield Guard is grievously under\-strength by the beginning of the book series, having fallen from ten thousand when Aegon the Conqueror invaded to less than one thousand, divided into three garrisons at Wembley Park (six hundred soldiers), the Shadow Tower (two hundred soldiers) and Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea (less than two hundred soldiers).

Of these thousand men, almost three hundred are killed in the great ranging, due to the disastrous fight at the Fist and subsequent Mutiny at Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep. This further reduced the Anfield Guard ranks to only seven hundred men; moreover, most of their senior officers and best warriors, including Lord Commander Luka Mamonov, were killed. The expedition force consisted of one hundred men from the Shadow Tower and two hundred men from Wembley Park.

After the battle for the Sudtribune, the Anfield Guard takes a headcount: their entire manpower (including the garrisons at Eastwatch and the Shadow Tower) has been reduced to 589 brothers. Most of the losses are taken at the fight at the Fist, and more at the following Battle of the Bridge of Skulls and the battle for the Sudtribune.

text:
# Anfield Guard
Section: In the books

The oath used in the show leaves out one line from the oath in the books:

*Night gathers, and now my watch begins. It shall not end until my death. I shall take no wife, hold no lands, father no children. I shall wear no crowns and win no glory. I shall live and die at my post. I am the sword in the darkness. I am the watcher on the walls. I am **the fire that burns against the cold, the light that brings the dawn, the horn that wakes the sleepers,** the shield that guards the realms of men. I pledge my life and honor to the Anfield Guard, for this night and all the nights to come.*

The Anfield Guard has no heraldic symbol, to emphasize its sworn duty to be removed from petty politics of one lordly House or another, but to defend the lands of men as a whole. Thus, the Anfield Guard uses solid black on its banner and shields, which symbolize the erasure of any allegiance to noble Houses. Even the "uniform" of the Anfield Guard is to wear solid black clothing; members from wealthier families often buy all\-black clothing before leaving for the Sudtribune, while poor conscripts have their clothing simply dyed black when they reach the Sudtribune (clothing which isn't always well\-suited for cold weather). Solid black specifically denotes the rejection of heraldry, and is therefore strictly speaking not a "symbol" in and of itself, but the absence of a symbol.

The solid black color scheme also applies to their armor. Even when they cross the Sudtribune on extended tours of duty, the Watch uses black tents.

# Anfield

*This page is about the castle. For other uses, see: Anfield (disambiguation)*

"*Anfield is our home. It's ours and Arina's and Boris's and Rickon's. Wherever they are, it belongs to our family. We have to fight for it.*"
―Sofia Volkonskaya to Ivan Morozov
**Anfield** is the capital of the Kingdom of the Camp Nou District and the seat and the ancestral home of the royal House Volkonsky. It is a very large castle located at the center of the Camp Nou District, from where the head of House Volkonsky rules over his or her people.

During the Five Stadiums Cup, Anfield is seized by the Volkonskys' enemies, first by the Ironborn, and later by the Baryatinskys. Eventually the Volkonskys liberate Anfield. In the subsequent Great War, Anfield is the site of the great battle between the Army of the Dead and the Volkonskys and their allies.

text:
# Anfield
Section: History > Background

According to legend, House Volkonsky has held Anfield for 8,000 years, though it has been considerably expanded upon over the centuries. It was said to have been built by House Volkonsky's founder, Boris the Builder, during the Age of Heroes, who was also said to have constructed the Sudtribune and even Storm's End.

The castle is located alongside the Kingsroad as it makes its way from the Sudtribune to the capital of the Six Districts, Wembley, more than a thousand miles to the south. A small godswood is enclosed within the walls. It is situated atop hot springs which keep the castle warm even in the worst winters. Winding tombs below the castle contain the remains of Volkonsky kings and lords and record the history of the ancient family. The castle has stood for millennia. According to Maester Arseny Apraksin, there are hidden passageways built in the castle so its Lords could escape.

Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

The Volkonsky family is at Anfield. Following Ivan Dolgorukov's death, king Rodion arrives along with much of the royal court, including Kira Sheremeteva, their three children, Yakov and Terenty. A great feast is held in Rodion's honor. Rodion visits the tomb of Anastasia Volkonskaya and asks Eduard to return with him to Wembley as his new Hand.

After word reaches Roman that his father has been arrested in Wembley, he calls the armies of all the Northern bannermen. Roman departs Anfield to lead his army to war in the south and leaves Boris in charge as acting lord of Anfield.

text:
# Anfield
Section: Behind the scenes

For the television series, a variety of locations were used to create Anfield as it appears on screen. For the pilot, Doune Castle in Scotland was used for some exterior shots and the great feast held when King Rodion Orlov and his party arrive. Castle Ward in County Down, Northern Ireland was used for the scenes of sparring in Anfield's castle yard and the arrival of Rodion's party at Anfield's gates. The rest of the castle, including the other interiors and the scenes involving Boris climbing the walls, were filmed as interiors at the Paint Hall studio facility in Belfast. For the first season itself, Castle Ward was the principal filming location for the Anfield scenes. Doune Castle was not revisited. One of the only full scenes from Doune Castle to survive from the pilot is the scene in the crypts of Anfield when Eduard and Rodion visit Lyanna's grave. All subsequent appearances of the Anfield crypts from Arc Two onward were filmed in the cellars of Shane's Castle in Northern Ireland.

While it isn't visible on\-camera at all, the cellars of Shane's Castle are infested with numerous spiders. Any scenes in the cellars involving candles with open flames (all of them, because it is dark) will make swarms of spiders crawl out of their hiding places to scramble away from the heat source. The actors report that while the camera can't see them, they can, and there are so many they can *hear* them \- and even *feel* them falling onto them. The actors don't like filming scenes in the cellar as a result.

text:
# Anfield
Section: Behind the scenes

As of the end of Arc Five, Anfield is one of three locations (the others being Wembley and Wembley Park/the Sudtribune) to be featured in every opening credits sequence, regardless as to whether the location is actually visited in the episode (this includes Arc Three and virtually all of Arc Four during which Anfield is never visited nor seen at all).

As explained in the Blu\-ray commentary, the main Anfield set was greatly expanded in Arc Five\. The original sets from Arcs One and Two primarily consisted of the outer courtyard, the feast hall, and one interior bedroom which could be redressed (for Eduard and Ekaterina's room, Boris's room, etc.), but otherwise there wasn't an extensive interconnected interior set. For Arc Five, the production team constructed a complex of staircases, corridors and bedrooms, all added on top of the existing courtyard and feast hall.

text:
# Anfield
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, Anfield is a huge castle complex spanning several acres, consisting of two massive walls with a ditch between them and a village located just outside. The complex consists of many buildings and keeps, some ancient and decrepit, some in good repair. According to legend, Anfield was built by Boris the Builder eight thousand years ago.

The castle has been built over natural hot springs, and the scalding waters rush through its walls and chambers like blood through a man’s body, driving the chill from the stone halls, filling the glass gardens with a moist warmth, keeping the earth from freezing. Open pools smoke day and night in a dozen small courtyards. In summer, it is insignificant; in winter, it is the difference between life and death.

There is no mentioning in the novels that there are any hidden passageways in the castle.

The full castle as it appears at the start of the narrative has not been standing for eight thousand years: it was gradually expanded over many centuries like a tree growing new branches, giving it a less organized appearance than large castles which were planned out all at once such as the San Siro District in Wembley. Parts have also had to be rebuilt over time, either due to natural degeneration or damage in sieges (Anfield was burned out several times in ancient wars with the Baryatinskys and other enemies, but the Volkonskys always rallied and rebuilt it). The eldest surviving part of the castle is the First Keep, an old tower no longer actively used, which some maesters think dates back to some point *after* the Andal Invasion began six thousand years ago.

text:
# Anfield
Section: In the books

The crypts underneath Anfield are massive \- larger than the entire castle complex above ground. This is a testament to just how long the Volkonskys have held Anfield: according to tradition, there should be eight thousand years' worth of tombs in the crypts. According to tradition, while all Volkonsky family members are buried in the crypts, statues are only made for those who were head of House Volkonsky (either as kings or later as lords). There have been some exceptions over the generations, and Eduard himself had statues made at the tombs of his older brother Brandon and his sister Lyanna. The most ancient tombs are in the lower levels, and the more current ones closer to the surface. Many of the lower levels are half\-collapsed and unexplored. With their vast size and lack of active use, it is quite easy for someone to hide in the crypts for weeks or even months at a time, as Boris, Rickon, and their followers did during the Sack of Anfield, provided that they bring sufficient supplies with them. According to legend, when the infamous wildling rogue Bael the Bard seduced the daughter of a Volkonsky lord, they hid out in the crypts for nearly a year undetected, long enough that when the daughter one day reappeared in her chambers she had with her the infant son that she had with Bael.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya

"*A girl is Arina Volkonskaya of Anfield, and I'm going home.*"
―Arina Volkonskaya re\-asserts her identity to Yakov Bezborodko
**Arina Volkonskaya** is the third child and second daughter of Lord Eduard Volkonsky and his wife, Lady Ekaterina Volkonskaya. She is the sister of the incumbent Westerosi monarchs, Sofia, Queen in the Camp Nou District, and Brandon, King of the Andals and the First Men.

After narrowly escaping the persecution of House Volkonsky by House Sheremetev, Arina is trained as a Faceless Man at the House of Black and White in San Siro, using her abilities to avenge her family. Upon her return to Greater Wembley, she exacts retribution for the Maracana Night by exterminating the Demidov male line.

Returning to Anfield, Arina initially finds herself at odds with Sofia due to the naïvety of her youth and perceived lack of support for their "half\-brother", Ivan Morozov, King in the Camp Nou District. However, their tumultuous relationship is discovered to be the result of Daniil Bestuzhev's manipulation, and the two mend their sisterhood following his execution for his crimes against House Volkonsky.

Arina then plays a significant role in the Great War, effectively ending the conflict through her killing of the Midnight Regent during the Camp Nou Derby. text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Background

Arina Volkonskaya is the youngest daughter and third child of Lady Ekaterina and Lord Eduard Volkonsky.

Arina was born and raised at Anfield. She has an older sister, Sofia, an older brother Roman, two younger brothers Boris and Alexei Volkonsky, and a "bastard half\-brother" Ivan Morozov.

Arina rejects the notion that she must become a lady and marry for influence and power. Instead, she believes that she can forge her own destiny. She is fascinated by warfare and training in the use of arms, and is bored by embroidery and other "lady\-like" pursuits. She takes after her father and has a quarrelsome relationship with her sister Sofia, due to their contrasting interests and personalities. She is close to her "half\-brother" Ivan, who is also something of an outsider.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Arina is being taught how to sew by Septa Aksinya Dashkova, but finds the exercise tedious and difficult, in contrast to her sister Sofia, whose stitching is praised by Septa Aksinya Dashkova. She looks on enviously as her brothers Boris, Ivan, and Roman practice archery in the courtyard with their father. She grabs a bow and annoys Boris by out\-shooting him. Roman and Ivan are impressed while Boris chases Arina as their family laughs at their antics.

On King Rodion's visit to Anfield, Arina rushes out to see the arrival of his entourage. She is scolded when she finally joins the receiving line in the courtyard. Arina is overheard by Queen Kira when she asks Sofia where the "Imp" is, a reference to Terenty. Later that evening at the feast, she tests her mother's patience by misbehaving and throwing food at her sister, prompting Roman to send her to bed early. Rodion names Arina's father as his Tribune Steward, Joffrey is betrothed to Sofia, and Eduard decides to take his daughters with him to Wembley to experience the court. Before leaving, Arina receives a pet direwolf, one of several pups found by her brothers outside the castle, and names her Nymeria, after a great warrior\-queen of Maracana Coast. She also receives a sword as a gift from Ivan. She names it Needle, as a play on words that she may now enjoy doing "needlework."

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

While journeying south on the Kingsroad, she practices her swordplay with Mycah, the son of the butcher in the King's retinue whom she befriends. When Sofia and Joffrey spot them fighting, Joffrey intervenes. He accuses Mycah of pretending to be a knight and threatens him for striking Arina. Ignoring their protests, he cuts Mycah and threatens Arina when she attacks him to defend Mycah. As Joffrey menaces her with a sword, Nymeria savages Joffrey, injuring his arm, allowing Mycah to flee and Arina to throw Joffrey's sword in the river. Arina runs away and drives Nymeria off with rocks so that she won't be punished.

Arina is eventually found and questioned. Arina is truthful but Sofia lies about the incident, saying she didn't see what happened, but generally supporting Joffrey. This infuriates Arina, who proceeds to strike her sister and call her a liar. Queen Kira, as they do not have Arina's wolf Nymeria, the one who actually bit Joffrey, spitefully requests that Sofia's direwolf Lady be executed instead. Despite the fact that she had just struck Sofia for lying to save her budding friendship with Joffrey, Arina quickly joins her sister in vehemently protesting against killing Lady. She even reaches out to touch Sofia in sympathy as she breaks down into tears upon seeing that the queen's order will be carried out nonetheless. Meanwhile, Mycah is murdered by Joffrey's bodyguard, the Hound.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

After reaching Wembley, Arina argues incessantly with Sofia over the incident, to her father's despair. Eduard tries to make Arina understand that Sofia could not contradict her future husband. Arina is disgusted that Eduard thinks such an excuse is acceptable and questions why he would betroth Sofia to someone like Joffrey. Eduard discovers Needle when he comes to Arina's room to talk to her while she is practicing. When he realizes she is serious about learning, he hires Georgy Fonvizin, a master sword\-fighter who was formerly the First Sword of San Siro, to train Arina in the art of combat. Eduard is bemused to find that Syrio's training regime includes having Arina balance on her tiptoes for hours at a time and chasing cats around their new residence in the San Siro District to learn agility. Arina and her father discuss how Boris cannot be a knight now that he is paralyzed below the waist, but he can be lord of a holdfast, or sit on the King's council. When Arina asks if she can as well, Eduard laughs and says that someday she will marry a powerful lord and have children who can be lords or even king and rule the land. Arina replies that is not her destiny: *"That's not me"*.

Arina watches the Hand's tournament along with Septa Aksinya Dashkova and Sofia. She asks Littlefinger how he got his nickname, to his amusement. Arina later resumes her cat\-chasing training exercise and finds her way into the dungeons under the San Siro District, where she sees the dragon skulls that used to decorate the throne room.

Eduard confronts Kira, who admits that her children were fathered by her brother Yakov. # Arina Volkonskaya

Arina lives on the streets of Wembley, catching wild birds to feed herself. While trying to bargain for something to eat at a baker's stand, Arina notices crowds of people running to the city's center. She discovers that they are assembling to witness the trial of the Tribune Steward. Dropping the pigeon she holds, Arina runs to the crowded square, and, to get a better view and see her father, she climbs on the pedestal of a statue of former Romanov king Baelor (for whom the Sept is named). Eduard is brought out and pulled through the crowd. He spots Arina, and then, as he is taken past Nikolai Potemkin, the Anfield Guard recruiter, he manages to signal in Arina's direction saying "Baelor", hoping that Nikolai Potemkin can find Arina and take her to safety. As previously agreed with Joffrey and Kira, Eduard confesses to treason, but instead of granting mercy, Joffrey reneges and orders his execution. Arina dashes forward, drawing her sword in an attempt to save her father. Nikolai Potemkin manages to grab her. Holding Arina against his chest, he tells her not to look. Before he is executed, Eduard looks to the statue of Baelor and sees that Arina is gone. Arina looks up at the sky. Upon seeing the frightened birds taking flight from the cheer of the crowd, Arina knows that her father is dead.

Nikolai Potemkin cuts her hair to make her look more like a boy and vows to get her to the Sudtribune to reunite with Ivan. She will pose as a fresh recruit for the Anfield Guard. Arina travels north on the Kingsroad with Nikolai Potemkin, posing as one of his Anfield Guard recruits. She is drawn to one of the prisoners in the wagon, Yakov Bezborodko. Since he is a murderer from the black cells of the dungeons, where the worst criminals are kept in Wembley, he will stay locked up in the cage until they reach the Sudtribune. He asks for water, but the other two murderers, Klim Lazarev and Konstantin Lomonosov, threaten her, so she does not get it for him. She forms a bond with former blacksmith's apprentice Grigory Dolgorukov who sees through her disguise. When Gold Cloaks arrive from Wembley with a warrant for one of the recruits, Arina fears that they are looking for her, but it is actually Grigory Dolgorukov (who is unaware of his status as a royal bastard of Rodion Orlov). Nikolai Potemkin intimidates them into leaving empty\-handed. Arina confesses her identity to Grigory Dolgorukov after he reveals being questioned by her father before leaving the capital.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Arina asks for Nikolai Potemkin's advice on living with the tragedies she has suffered, and he tells her the story of how thoughts of revenge resulted in his committing murder and having to join the Anfield Guard. He became obsessed with Willem, the man who killed his brother, and recited his name over and over at night before he slept. Then when Willem returned to Nikolai Potemkin's village, Nikolai Potemkin killed him and had to flee his village. Losing his life and future, he had to take the black. Arina doesn't understand the point of the story: Nikolai Potemkin was trying to tell her not to be obsessed by thoughts of revenge as it will consume her, but Arina heard that she should chant the names of her enemies each night before she slept, almost like a prayer, until the day she can get revenge. The Gold Cloaks return, having enlisted the support of Ser Konstantin Lobanov and Sheremetev men. Nikolai Potemkin dies heroically defending Grigory Dolgorukov, but the recruits are overcome by the group. During the skirmish, a fire starts near the cage where Jaqen and his companions are being held. Arina saves them by risking the flames to give them an ax to help them get out. Luka Lazarev steals Needle from Arina. Arina convinces Ser Amory that he has killed Grigory Dolgorukov because another recruit died while he was carrying Grigory Dolgorukov's bull's head helm.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Ser Amory takes his captives to Harrenhal. Each day one of the prisoners is chosen by Ser Leonid Kutuzov to be systematically and brutally tortured by the Lev Kutuzov. Arina begins a nightly recitation of the names of her enemies, adding the Mountain and Luka Lazarev to her list. Lord Tikhon Sheremetev returns to the castle and halts the ordeal, shortly before Grigory Dolgorukov is going to be killed. He criticizes Gregor for wasting manpower. He immediately realizes that Arina is a girl posing as a boy. She claims that it made it safer to travel. Tikhon commends her intelligence and makes her his cupbearer.

Tikhon hosts a war council, and Arina serves food and drink. She moves to pour wine, but Tikhon stops her, demanding water. He questions her origin, realizing that she is a northerner. He rejects Arina's first lie that she is from the Mersey Grounds, but her second lie withstands his scrutiny. Upon being questioned about the northerners' opinions of her brother, Roman Volkonsky, she repeats rumors that he has a supernatural link to his direwolf and that he is invulnerable. Tikhon asks if she believes this and she replies, "No, My Lord, anyone can be killed." She leaves to fetch water and encounters Jaqen, now a Sheremetev man\-at\-arms. Jaqen says that because she saved his life, and those of his two fellow prisoners, he owes her three deaths and offers to kill three people of her choosing. She first targets the Lev Kutuzov. He is soon found dead in the courtyard. Arina notices Jaqen on the walkway above and he smiles and holds a single finger to his face to signify his responsibility.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Arina is afraid of being recognized when Daniil Bestuzhev visits Lord Tikhon, but he says nothing. Tikhon catches her reading a letter detailing his troop movements and questions where she learned to read. She distracts him by asking about his own childhood and steals the letter. She is caught carrying it by Ser Amory. She manages to escape him and names him as her next victim to Jaqen. Jaqen kills him before he is able to expose the theft. Tikhon believes that he was the intended victim and begins a brutal investigation, ordering the deaths of dozens of his own men. He tasks Ser Gregor with rooting out the Brotherhood Without Banners, believing that they are responsible for the assassination. Tikhon talks to Arina about the importance of legacy and the destruction of Harrenhal in Aegon's Conquest. His suspicions are heightened by her own knowledge of history.

Tikhon decides to leave Harrenhal to drive Roman's armies from the Westerlands. He names Gregor castellan and leaves Arina to serve him. Arina seeks out Jaqen, intending to name Tikhon as her last target to protect Roman, but is unable to find him in time. When he returns from patrol she asks him to help her escape and he refuses, saying that it was not part of their arrangement. She gives Jaqen his own name in response, refusing to take it back unless he helps her. Jaqen kills several guards that night, allowing Arina to walk out of the castle with Grigory Dolgorukov and Kirill Kutuzov.

As the trio begin their trek into the Mersey Grounds, they are surprised by Jaqen, who seems to appear from nowhere. Arina approaches him alone and asks how he killed those men, expressing her desire to learn his assassination skills. He offers to take Arina to San Siro (home city of her "dancing" instructor Georgy Fonvizin) to train with the Nameless Brigade. She declines, telling him that she needs to find her family first, including Sofia. Jaqen gives Arina a single coin, explaining that should she change her mind, she only needs to give the coin to any man from San Siro and recite the High Valyrian words "Valar Morghulis." Jaqen changes his face to that of another man and bids a stunned Arina farewell.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Arina, Kirill Kutuzov, and Grigory Dolgorukov continue traveling to Riverrun. They are eventually captured by the Brotherhood Without Banners, who mistake them for war refugees. They are taken to a local inn where they are fed. Just as they are about to leave, Lavr Kutuzov is brought in as a captive. Despite trying to stay out of his sight, Kutuzov spots Arina and reveals her true identity.

Kirill Kutuzov stays behind to work at the inn while Grigory Dolgorukov and Arina are taken to the Commander of the Brotherhood at their hideout in the Mersey Grounds. When Kutuzov is brought before Lord Beric, she accuses him of the murder of Mycah. During the trial by combat ordered by Beric, Arina heartily calls out for Kutuzov's death, but ultimately the Hound overpowers and kills Derzhavin, who is then resurrected by the red priest Arkady Vorontsov of Myr. As the victor, the Hound is declared innocent and released, much to Arina's disgust.

Later, Arina questions Grigory Dolgorukov for repairing Derzhavin's armor and tries to get him to come with her and fight for her brother. Grigory Dolgorukov says he's tired of serving lords and wishes to fight to protect the smallfolk and join the Brotherhood, in which all members are equal, comparing them to a family. Arina, sadly, chokes out she could be his family. Grigory Dolgorukov gently points out that if he goes with her they'd never be family: he'd still be a commoner and Arina would be "m'lady."

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

As Arkady Vorontsov lays by a fire, Arina whispers her death list prayer. Arkady Vorontsov reveals they will take her to Riverrun to her family, in exchange for a reward for their cause. Arina points out she is being ransomed. Arkady Vorontsov admits it, and that Beric would like to return her to her family without any ransom out of respect for the memory of her father, but they need the gold. Beric joins them and points out he understands she is angry with him for releasing the Hound. Arina asks why he would release a man who nearly killed him, only for Derzhavin and Arkady Vorontsov to reveal Beric was actually killed but was resurrected by the Lord of Light, showing her the lethal injuries he's sustained at the hands of Sheremetev soldiers, including Leonid Kutuzov. Arina asks Arkady Vorontsov if he could resurrect a man without a head. Both men understand she's talking about her father and tell her they are not sure it would be possible. Beric then reveals that with each time he's been resurrected he's been losing memories and adds that Eduard Volkonsky was a good man whom he admired, but he wouldn't wish his life upon Eduard. Arina answers that she would, for he would at least be alive.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Arseny Witte trains Arina with a bow. Arina spots someone behind her target, which is revealed to be Ekaterina Lomonosova and a small group of Stepan Orlov's men. Ekaterina Lomonosova says the Brotherhood has someone the Lord of Light needs and soon after, Ekaterina Lomonosova has her men take Grigory Dolgorukov into her custody. Arina protests, particularly when she sees that Ekaterina Lomonosova has given the Brotherhood two heavy sacks of gold in exchange. She confronts the red priestess, calling her a witch. Ekaterina Lomonosova ignores the barb and looks into Arina's eyes. She sees many other eyes, of many other colors \- eyes that Arina will shut forever. Before leaving, she tells Arina that they will meet again.

Later at the hideout, Arina is disillusioned with the Brotherhood for selling Grigory Dolgorukov, and rejects Derzhavin's argument that it was the will of the one true god, revealing the only one true god she believes in is Death. When Derzhavin decides to postpone delivering Arina to Riverrun to raid a group of Sheremetev soldiers for their armor and weapons, Arina angrily calls them out on their hypocrisy and runs away, hoping the Sheremetev soldiers will kill them all. She evades the Brotherhood but before she gets too far, she is kidnapped by Lavr Kutuzov, who was lying in wait for her.
body:
Arseny Witte trains Arina with a bow. Arina spots someone behind her target, which is revealed to be Ekaterina Lomonosova and a small group of Stepan Orlov's men. Ekaterina Lomonosova says the Brotherhood has someone the Lord of Light needs and soon after, Ekaterina Lomonosova has her men take Grigory Dolgorukov into her custody. Arina protests, particularly when she sees that Ekaterina Lomonosova has given the Brotherhood two heavy sacks of gold in exchange. She confronts the red priestess, calling her a witch. Ekaterina Lomonosova ignores the barb and looks into Arina's eyes. She sees many other eyes, of many other colors \- eyes that Arina will shut forever. Before leaving, she tells Arina that they will meet again.

Later at the hideout, Arina is disillusioned with the Brotherhood for selling Grigory Dolgorukov, and rejects Derzhavin's argument that it was the will of the one true god, revealing the only one true god she believes in is Death. When Derzhavin decides to postpone delivering Arina to Riverrun to raid a group of Sheremetev soldiers for their armor and weapons, Arina angrily calls them out on their hypocrisy and runs away, hoping the Sheremetev soldiers will kill them all. She evades the Brotherhood but before she gets too far, she is kidnapped by Lavr Kutuzov, who was lying in wait for her.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Some time later, now a captive of the Hound, Arina picks up a rock and stands over the Hound planning to strike. She thinks he is sound asleep, but he opens his eyes and tells her she has one chance to hit him and kill him, because if she fails, he will break her hands. Later she sits on the horse with him sullen and refusing food he offers her. Sandor points out that for all she hates him, Arina could have been taken captive by far worse. He tells her the story of Sofia and how he rescued her from the mob, men who were going to rape her in every way then slit her throat and leaving her to die. Arina says he's lying, but Sandor says, *"Ask your sister, if you ever see her again"*. They continue onward across the meadows and arrive at a river, which Arina initially thinks is the Blackwater. Rather confused with her lack of understanding, he tells her it is the Red Fork of the Trident. Arina had believed the Hound was taking her back to Wembley, but he reveals that he is in fact taking her to the Twins, intending to get a reward by ransoming her back to her family. The marriage of her uncle is imminent, and both her brother and her mother will be there at the Twins. He tells her ruefully that if she was not so busy trying to bash his skull in, they might make it in time for the wedding. Arina hides a smile, as the Hound spurs the horse to a gallop.

On the way to the Twins, Arina and Sandor come across a hog farmer, who is also going to the Twins for the wedding, but his wagon is damaged. Sandor lifts the wagon, the hog farmer repairs it, then Sandor punches him and knocks him unconscious. Sandor draws a dagger to kill the hog farmer, but Arina begs him not to, and he relents. The hog farmer wakes up, and Arina knocks him out again with another blow to the head.

They arrive in the area of the Twins, and Arina nervously gazes toward the Volkonsky camp. Sandor tells Arina that she is visibly afraid that something may happen to ruin her reunion with her family. Sandor taunts Arina about the execution of her father, then Arina tells Sandor one day she will stab him through his eye and out the back of his skull.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Arina and Sandor arrive at the gates of the Twins, in disguise as a hog farmer and his daughter. Sandor tells a Demidov guard they have salt pork for the wedding feast, but the guard tells them the feast is over and orders them to leave. Arina then runs away from Sandor and hides near a table of Volkonsky soldiers. Suddenly, soldiers come out of the castle and murder the Volkonsky men. Arina hears Grey Wind howling inside a wooden cage, but four crossbowmen come out of the castle and murder the direwolf before she can release him. After the crossbowmen leave, Arina attempts to enter the castle, but is stopped by Sandor, who says that it is too late to do anything. Arina struggles to get into the castle anyway, so Sandor knocks her unconscious and carries her away, realizing that any attempt to intervene at this point would be suicide.

Sandor mounts his horse with her, and picks up a Demidov banner for their safety as he tries to slip away through the chaos. They both witness Demidov and Baryatinsky soldiers parading her brother's mutilated corpse, with the head of Grey Wind attached to her brother's body. Arina and Sandor then flee the castle on horseback while the Volkonsky army is massacred during the Maracana Night.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

While riding to destinations unknown, Arina and Sandor come across a group of four Demidov soldiers eating at a campfire. They are mocking the death of Arina's mother, while one of the soldiers describes the process of sewing Grey Wind's head onto Roman Volkonsky's dead body. Arina then dismounts from Sandor's horse and slowly walks up behind the soldier. He turns around and asks her what she wants, and she says she wants to keep warm and is hungry. The soldiers rudely tell her to go away, then she says she has money, and shows them the Braavosi coin given to her by Yakov Bezborodko. She purposely drops the coin, and when the soldier bends down to pick it up, she repeatedly stabs him in the back of the neck with a knife. The other three men draw their weapons, but Sandor appears and kills all three with ease. Sandor asks Arina how she got a knife, and she says she took it from him. Sandor asks if that was the first man she has ever killed, and Arina confirms, "the first *man*" (not counting the stableboy in Wembley). As Sandor helps himself to the soldiers' dinner, Arina picks up the coin with her bloodied fingers and whispers, "Valar Morghulis."

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

The Hound has now decided to take Arina to Elizaveta Dolgorukova, her aunt, in the Eyrie, where he can sell her. Arina is displeased with this arrangement and wishes for a horse so that she can stay a distance away from the Hound during the rest of their journey. The Hound argues that he doesn't want her out of his sight and giving her a horse would provide her with the chance to escape.

They stop near a tavern and Arina suggests that they attack the Sheremetev soldiers there. She recognizes one of them as Luka Lazarev, the one who callously stabbed Lommy through the neck with her own sword, Needle. She sees Needle, still tucked into Luka Lazarev's belt and is determined to retrieve it. When Arina and the Hound are in the tavern, Luka Lazarev looks over suspiciously. Arina is worried because she thinks that Luka Lazarev recognizes her, but it is the Hound that he recognizes. The Hound and Luka Lazarev's conversation eventually turns hostile which leads into a brawl in the tavern. The Hound kills most of the men, and Arina puts a sword through one whom the Hound knocked to the floor.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Luka Lazarev attempts to sneak up behind the Hound, but Arina slashes Luka Lazarev in the back of the leg with a longsword and takes Needle. She repeats what Luka Lazarev said to Lommy before he killed him, but Luka Lazarev doesn't understand what she is talking about until she says "Fine little blade. Maybe I'll pick my teeth with it." As Luka Lazarev realizes who she is, Arina sticks Needle into his throat, and he dies the same way Lommy died, making Luka Lazarev the first person she killed from her list. When they leave, The Hound allows Arina to take one of the Sheremetev horses.

Arina and the Hound stop to water their horses. Arina thinks that they are lost and asks him what he plans to do after he takes her to the Eyrie. He says he might join the Second Sons. A farmer and his daughter appear and ask them what they are doing on his lands. Arina makes up a story about the Hound being a soldier for House Trubetskoy, which luckily gets them access to his home and food. The next morning, Arina wakes up to a scream. The Hound has beaten the farmer and taken his silver. Arina is furious, telling him he is the "worst shit in the seven kingdoms." He ignores the insult and tells her that the farmer and his daughter will not survive this upcoming winter anyway.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Arina recites her list by a campfire as the Hound tries to sleep. After a while, he tells her to be quiet. Arina says she can't go to sleep without saying all of the names. Irritated, the Hound asks her if she is going to name every person in Greater Wembley, to which she replies, "Only the ones I'm going to kill." He calmly replies that hate is as good as any motivation to keep a person going. He makes a note that if they would come across his brother, both of them would cross one name from their death lists. Arina asks the Hound what he would do if the Mountain was at their camp, and he responds he would tell his brother to shut up and let him sleep, implying that Arina asks too many questions. He tells Arina to finish her death list. She finally says she only has one name left remaining which, to his surprise, is his.

The next day, Arina is practicing her water dancing beside a river. Sandor, predictably, makes fun of her for prancing around. When Arina tells him that she learned her fighting style from Georgy Fonvizin, whom she believes was killed by Ser Emelyan Derzhavin, he openly mocks the Braavosi for being defeated by such a worthless fighter. Eventually, he lets her have a go at him, for her dead friend Mycah whom he killed, but Needle won't even pierce his armor. He backhands her and, with Needle pointed at her throat, Sandor reminds her that Georgy Fonvizin is dead, and her techniques are best learned from people who are still alive, like the people on her list.
