text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Arina and Sandor encounter a dying man in a ransacked village. Sandor gives the man a gift of mercy by stabbing him in the heart. Moments later, Sandor is ambushed by Konstantin Lomonosov, who bites him on the neck; he snaps Konstantin Lomonosov's neck and drops him dead in the dirt. Klim Lazarev appears, revealing that there is a price on the Hound's head. Arina instantly recognizes him as one of the prisoners in Nikolai Potemkin's group, who threatened to molest her; he is not her kill list because she does not know his name. The Hound asks for Klim Lazarev's name, and after he says it, Arina kills him with Needle. Sandor cynically comments "You're learning."

Afterwards, Sandor clumsily addresses his wounds from Konstantin Lomonosov. Arina suggests burning to cauterize the wound, but is rebuffed by Sandor because of his fear of fire. Sandor confirms the story of his facial scars from burns inflicted by Gregor's wrath and how his father covered up the truth, making him feel alone. Arina offers to clean and stitch him up, and Sandor allows her to do so.

As Arina and Sandor make their way to the Eyrie, Arina laments that she doesn't feel any satisfaction over Joffrey's death (which they learned of from Klim Lazarev), expressing disappointment in the fact that she was neither able to be present during his murder or be the one to kill him. Once they reach the Bloody Gate, Ser Rostislav Witte informs them that Elizaveta Dolgorukova had passed away just three days prior, prompting Arina to burst into a fit of laughter over their continuing bad luck as Sandor stands dumbfounded over his attempts to collect a ransom being foiled yet again.

When Arina and Sandor leave the Eyrie, they encounter Elena Tatischeva and Klim Panin. At first, Brienne does not know she's speaking to Arina Volkonskaya, whom she swore to her mother Ekaterina to find and protect. When Pod tells her that the man with Arina is Lavr Kutuzov, she realizes it's Arina and begs her to come with her. The Hound doesn't trust Brienne, as she is carrying Oathkeeper, a gift from Yakov, which is gilded with a lion's head hilt, making him thinks she's working for the Sheremetevs. Brienne and Sandor fight, each of them believing they should be the one to watch over Arina.

She then goes down the cliff to find the gravely injured Sandor, who begs her to kill him. When Sandor believes she won't do it, he tries to goad her into doing it, telling her that it is another name to strike off her list, he killed the butcher's boy when he begged him for mercy, and he should have raped Sofia when he had the chance. Instead, Arina takes his money and leaves him to die.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

After a long sea voyage, Arina arrives at San Siro. Arina is awestruck by the Titan, which, according to the captain, would wake and protect the city whenever San Siro stood in danger in the old times. Arina replies it's just a statue. Just then, the Titan lets out a loud blast announcing their arrival, startling her, but she convinces herself that she is not afraid. Terys rows Arina to the House of Black and White, where he claims she may find Jaqen, and Arina thanks him for bringing her this far. Arina lingers outside waiting for admittance, but is rejected by an elder man despite showing the coin Yakov Bezborodko had given her and mentioning their prior association.

Arina waits outside the House for days, endlessly reciting the names of the people she wants to kill, but eventually tosses away her coin and wanders off into the streets of San Siro. While hunting for pigeons in the city, Arina encounters several boys who intend to take Needle from her. Although she is more than willing to kill them, the boys scatter when the man from the House of Black and White appears again behind her. After following him back to the House, Arina demands to know his identity, and he returns to her the coin she had thrown in the water. His face morphs into the visage Arina had known him as — that of Yakov Bezborodko. However, he insists he's not Yakov Bezborodko, but "no one", as all Nameless Brigade are, and he tells Arina she must learn to be "no one" as well.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

As Arina cleans the main sanctuary of the House of Black and White, she watches the man who looks like Yakov Bezborodko assist another man in drinking from the temple's well. When the man leaves to pray, Arina tells Jaqen that she wants to learn. He recites the phrase "Valar Dohaeris", meaning "all men must serve", and accuses Arina of only wanting to serve herself. When Arina looks back at the praying man, she sees that he has died and two men take his body away, ignoring Arina when she asks what they are doing with the body.

Later, Arina is accosted in her room by the Zinaida Panina, who repeatedly asks her who she is, hitting her when she gives the expected response of "no one." Eventually, Jaqen arrives and demands the Zinaida Panina to stop. In order to meet the order's initiation requirements, Arina throws her old clothing and silver into the lagoon. The Zinaida Panina doesn't respond when Arina asks what happens to the bodies after they are cleaned.

# Arina Volkonskaya

Arina finishes cleaning a corpse which is then taken away by two men. When the Zinaida Panina is about to walk away, Arina asks her who she is. The Zinaida Panina tells Arina a story about how she was the only daughter of a widowed Lord, who remarried, producing another daughter. Her stepmother, in order to secure her own daughter's future, tried to poison her. The Zinaida Panina found out about this and sought out the help of the Nameless Brigade to exact her revenge. The Zinaida Panina then asks Arina whether she believed the story. When Arina doesn't respond, embarrassed that she bought the Zinaida Panina's story, the Zinaida Panina tells her to get back to work, hinting that to pass the game of faces, Arina must be able to lie convincingly.

Later, when Arina is asleep, Yakov Bezborodko comes to test Arina again. This time, when he asks Arina who she is, Arina tells him how she came to join the Nameless Brigade, trying to slip in a few lies into the story. However, Jaqen is able to tell when Arina is lying and hits her whenever she does. Before he leaves, he tells her that she is lying not only to him, but to herself as well when she says she hates the Hound.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

A grieving father brings his sick daughter, Ghita, to the House of Black and White, wanting to end her suffering. Arina tells the girl a false story about how she was sick too, but her father brought her here and when she drank from the temple's well, she was healed, persuading Ghita to drink the poisoned water from the well. The girl dies, and Arina, having proven that she can lie, is brought to the Hall of Faces by Jaqen. All the faces had been taken from the corpses that the acolytes wash in the temple. He then asks Arina if she is ready to give up who she is to become "no one." After a moment of silence, he then states that she is not ready to become "no one" , but that she *is* ready to become "someone else."

Arina's first assignment is to pose as a shellfish merchant to study a target known as the Thin man. Before the assassination is carried out, Arina is distracted by the sight of a name on her list: Emelyan Derzhavin. She sees him dock and follows him as he guards Ruslan Yusupov on his way to the Iron Bank. That night, Arina follows Trant and several guards to a brothel. She is chased out by the owner, but not before she learns that Trant prefers sex with very young girls. She reports her failure to kill the Thin man to Jaqen (not mentioning why she failed) and promises to try again tomorrow.

Trant is given three girls the next night, whom he beats for his amusement. The first two are left whimpering from his beatings, but not the third. Trant dismisses the first two and continues to hit the third girl, to no effect, so he punches her in the gut. Crumpled on the floor, the girl removes her face and reveals herself as Arina wearing the mask of dead Ghita.

She quickly stabs him in the eyes and several times in the chest, but her blade is too short and has little effect. She teases him about how he was the first name on her list and how the Many\-Faced God has denied her of others, but how he has delivered Trant to her. She asks him if he remembers Georgy Fonvizin, who he presumably killed in Wembley. She assumes he doesn't. Arina then asks if he knows who she is, though Trant is in too much pain and shock to understand what is happening. She reveals herself as Arina Volkonskaya, and slits his throat.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Arina returns to the House of Black and White to put the face she used back on the wall. She is caught by Jaqen and the Zinaida Panina. They are displeased that Arina has defied the Many\-Faced God by killing someone who was not hers to kill. The Zinaida Panina restrains Arina and Jaqen pulls out a vial of poison saying, "Only death can pay for life." Just before Arina thinks she is about to be poisoned, Jaqen drinks it himself and dies. The Zinaida Panina questions Arina's grief for her friend, only to shock Arina by revealing herself to be Jaqen. Confused, Arina repeatedly removes multiple faces from "Jaqen's" body, until she sees her own face. Arina's eyes fill over with white as she is rendered blind as punishment.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Now blind, Arina poses as a beggar as part of her training. After overhearing two passing citizens discussing Meryn's murder, she is approached by the Zinaida Panina, remarking on her blindness. Tossed a stick, she fights and loses another sparring match against the Zinaida Panina. Unimpressed, the Zinaida Panina leaves Arina, promising to return the following day.

The next day, the Zinaida Panina returns and asks Arina who she is. When Arina answers "no one," the Zinaida Panina brushes this off and promptly beats her in another sparring match. Arina angrily lashes out after the Zinaida Panina leaves, but is stopped by Jaqen, who repeatedly asks her to say her name. After Arina tells him "a girl has no name" each time, an impressed Jaqen allows her to return to the House of Black and White.

Multiple stick fights between Arina and the Zinaida Panina ensue. At the same time, Arina learns to cope with her blindness while telling the Zinaida Panina her story and list of targets. With Arina finally holding her own, Jaqen gives her a cup from the well in the House of Black and White and tells her if she truly is no one, she has nothing to fear. She drinks the water and regains her sight.

Arina is tasked to kill an actress named Zoya Razumovskaya, though Jaqen warns she has been given a second chance and won't get a third. She views the first portion of the play *The Bloody Hand*, in which Zoya Razumovskaya portrays Kira. Afterwards, Arina notices that another actress, Bianca, is jealous of Zoya Razumovskaya, and deduces that it was she who hired the Nameless Brigade to kill Zoya Razumovskaya.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

After watching the remainder of the play on a different occasion, Arina walks backstage and poisons Zoya Razumovskaya's rum. On the way back, Zoya Razumovskaya notices her, and the two briefly converse about the play. Speaking from experience, Arina suggests that the Kira character's response to the death of her son would not only be grief \-\- it should also include anger. After asking Arina if she likes pretending to be others, Crane tries to express Arina's opinion to the rest of the troupe, but is quickly shut down. She goes to drink the beverage Arina poisoned, but Arina slaps it from her hands before she can drink it, blaming Bianca.

Unbeknownst to Arina, The Zinaida Panina had been following her and discovers that Arina has failed to kill the actress. The Zinaida Panina proceeds to report Arina's failure to Jaqen, who grants her wish to let her kill Arina but that she must not let her suffer. Meanwhile, Arina retrieves Needle from its hiding place and prepares to defend herself, presumably abandoning the goal of becoming a Faceless assassin and knowing her failure has made her a target.

Afterwards, Arina secures passage back to Greater Wembley by bribing a Westerosi trader. However, she is attacked and repeatedly stabbed in the stomach by the Zinaida Panina, and only barely escapes by jumping into the river. She is left stumbling through the streets of San Siro, critically wounded and extremely paranoid.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Seeking refuge, Arina finds her way to Zoya Razumovskaya, collapsing from her injuries behind the theater troupe stage. Zoya Razumovskaya takes her to her living quarters, where she treats Arina's wounds and gives her a new set of clothing. Arina reluctantly accepts a dosage of milk of the poppy to help ease her pain, and soon after falls asleep in Zoya Razumovskaya's bed. When she wakes up, she finds her dead in the next room, murdered by the Zinaida Panina. Jumping off the balcony and into the streets of San Siro, Arina manages to escape, though she is pursued by the Zinaida Panina. After scurrying the back\-alleys of the city, Arina finds herself in the Braavosi market. However, the Zinaida Panina continues to pursue her, forcing her to jump into the commotion of the crowd. Subsequently, Arina's stitches become undone.

Leaving a trail of blood in her wake, Arina lures the Zinaida Panina to the hideout in which she has hidden Needle. The Zinaida Panina then asks her if she would like to die on her knees, or on her feet \- in response, Arina pulls Needle out from its hiding place and confronts her attacker, starting by putting out the only light in the room. In the ensuing fight, Arina manages to best the Zinaida Panina due to her proficiency with fighting in blindness, a skill which was ironically taught and trained by the Zinaida Panina. She kills her adversary and then removes her face, which she brings back to the Hall of Faces.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Aware that Jaqen sent the Zinaida Panina to kill her, Arina points Needle at him in an accusatory manner, though Jaqen claims that she has finally truly become "no one", indicating the completion of her training as a Faceless Man. In reply, Arina reaffirms that she will never be "no one" and is and will always be Arina Volkonskaya of Anfield. Lowering her sword, she then leaves the House of Black and White and Jaqen for good, making the ultimate decision to return to Greater Wembley, her home.

Upon arriving in Greater Wembley, Arina travels to the Twins where she disguises herself as a serving girl. After Yakov and his soldiers depart for Wembley, Arina manages to kill both "Lame" Lothar Demidov and "Black" Walder Rivers, who were responsible for the deaths of Talisa Volkonsky and her mother Ekaterina Volkonskaya, respectively. She then proceeds to dismember their bodies and bake them into a pie, which she serves to Lord Vladimir Demidov as the two are alone in the dining hall, still wearing the face of a serving girl. After she reveals her true identity, she slits Walder's throat and watches with amusement as he dies.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

After killing Lord Walder, Arina uses his face to impersonate him and hold a feast in honor of all of his sons. She gives a rousing speech, "reminiscing" over House Demidov's victories, before offering her audience a toast of poisoned wine. As Walder's many sons drink from their chalices, Arina refuses to let any of the women partake, aware of their innocence. She then elicits cheers from the many Demidov sons upon the mention of the infamous Maracana Night, though then goes on to subtly mock them by reminding them of how they butchered a pregnant woman, cut the throat of a mother of five, and slaughtered the Volkonskys after inviting them into their home. As the Demidov sons begin to cough up blood from the poison, Arina watches with satisfaction as they all die before removing her mask and revealing herself. Before leaving, she asks Walder's wife, Lyubov Demidova, to tell anyone that might ask what happened that "the north remembers", and remarks that winter has come for House Demidov.

After departing from the Twins, Arina comes across a small convoy of Sheremetev soldiers, one of which gains her attention with a sweet song. Arina agrees, upon request, to join them at their fire, and accepts their offerings of food and drink, though cautiously. She engages in some small talk with them, including the destruction of the Great Sept of Baelor, all the while keeping her eye on their swords, and states that she is heading for Wembley. After she admits that she is planning on killing Queen Kira, they laugh, unaware that this is her true intention.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Arina later visits the Inn at the Crossroads where she overhears some patrons discussing the recent arrival of Daria Romanova and her dragons. She is reunited with Kirill Kutuzov, who brings her several pies which she eagerly consumes. He reminds her of the destruction of the Sept of Baelor at the hands of Queen Kira and informs her of his own encounter with Brienne. She offers to pay for her meal when she has finished, but Kirill Kutuzov refuses her coin as a friendly gesture. Upon learning that her half\-brother Ivan has taken back Anfield from the Baryatinskys and become the King in the Camp Nou District, Arina decides to finally head home after leaving the inn, instead of heading to Wembley.

On her way to Anfield, Arina makes a small campfire in the woods. As she warms herself by the fire, she is suddenly ambushed by a large pack of wild wolves, which startles her horse. Surrounded, Arina pulls out Needle to defend herself, though the wolves do not attack, and Arina finds herself face to face with a now fully grown Nymeria, much to her astonishment. She pleads for her Direwolf to come with her to Anfield, but Nymeria instead retreats with her pack back into the woods. Arina realizes that Nymeria is no longer the same and that she has also changed herself since they last saw each other. Softly, and with a small smile, she murmurs, *"That's not you"*, echoing what she said to her father years ago when he suggested that someday she would marry a powerful lord.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Arina Volkonskaya finally returns to Anfield. She rides up to the gates and dismounts, but the guards don't believe her when she identifies herself as Arina Volkonskaya, convinced that Arina has been dead for years. Arina asks that they send word to Maester Arseny Apraksin and Anton Karamzin, who can prove her identity (not knowing they are both dead). The guards brush her off, telling Arina there is nobody by those names at Anfield. Arina asks for Ivan, but they say he actually just left Anfield, so Arina asks who is in charge of Anfield. The guards respond, "Lady Volkonsky," who Arina realizes is her sister. Sofia finds Arina where she expected, in the crypts looking over their father's grave. Sofia then informs Arina that Boris is home too. Arina is elated, but her smile fades when Sofia does not mention Rickon, realizing that Rickon is dead.

Some time later, Brienne is going through a vigorous sword practice session with Podrick, knocking him down when he overextends himself. Impressed, Arina interrupts and says she'd like to spar with Brienne \- the woman who beat the Hound in combat. Sofia and Littlefinger watch on silently from the walkway above. Brienne goes easy on her at first, but then Arina completely outmaneuvers Brienne using the water dance training she received from Georgy Fonvizin, augmented by her training with the Nameless Brigade. Arina achieves many openings that would be a killing blow if she wanted them to be. Surprised that such a young girl is so skilled, Brienne stops holding back, leading to a grueling sparring session. Brienne actually manages to knock Needle out of Arina's hand but she simply switches to the Baltic alloy dagger she had in her belt. Arina uses her speed and agility to compensate for Brienne's strength and size to overwhelm her \- until Brienne actually manages to bring her brute strength to bear on a fast moving target by landing a kick on Arina's chest that sends her sprawling. Brienne stops for a moment as Arina lies motionless, shocked at what she has done to a noblewoman. However, Arina swings her legs around and jumps up, causing Brienne to grin in relief. Ultimately, they reach a stalemate, with each of them holding a blade at the others' throat. Arina takes her leave of Brienne, both mutually impressed, as Sofia looks down baffled at how her sister reached such a deadly skill level. Arina then looks up at the battlements, where Petyr watched her duel with Brienne, giving him an untrustworthy stare until he walks away.

Arina later watches in the great hall as Sofia addresses Lords Gorchakov and Royce over their concerns with Ivan's absence. Gorchakov says that perhaps they should have chosen Sofia instead due to his feeling that the King in the Camp Nou District should stay in the Camp Nou District while Royce says that the Dortmund Heights came to Sofia's aid during the Battle for Anfield. In response, Sofia kindly dismisses their notions, once again pledging her loyalty to Ivan. In their late mother and father's chambers, Arina confronts Sofia about her apparent inaction towards Gorchakov and Royce, claiming that she should have taken their heads for defying Ivan's rule. Sofia reminds her sister that this would likely lose the support of both House Gorchakov and the Dortmund Heights and that they need to work together in order to survive. Arina is adamant that they should have been executed. Suspicious of Sofia and her relationship with Littlefinger, Arina begins to spy on him, following him to Sofia's bedchambers where he hides a rolled parchment inside of her mattress. Arina, unaware that the letter, written by Sofia after their father's imprisonment in the San Siro District in which she pledges her loyalty to Joffrey and the crown and urges Roman to submit to his rule, has been planted on purpose by Bestuzhev in order to manipulate her, falls for his scheme and reads the letter, growing suspicious of her sister as she is also unaware that Sofia was coerced into writing the letter by Kira. From the shadows, Littlefinger watches with satisfaction as Arina leaves the room.

Arina and Sofia's relationship continues to grow increasingly strained following Arina's discovery of her sister's "incriminating" letter. Watching over the castle courtyard from the balcony, Arina reminisces about how their father used to watch her and her brothers train in the very same spot, bitterly claiming that Sofia wouldn't remember due to the fact that she was usually inside the castle knitting with her fellow ladies. She then tells Sofia how on one particular day, after their brothers had finished training with Ser Rodrik, she wandered into the vacant courtyard and began practicing her archery with Boris's discarded bow as their father watched from above.

Arina then resentfully states that he was killed by the Sheremetevs with Sofia's help, reading Sofia's letter to her aloud. Sofia insists that she was forced to write it and, being a naïve child that she was at the time, was led to believe that she was saving her family. However, Arina is adamant to point out that had she been in Sofia's position, she would have died before betraying her family, calling her stupid for believing in the Sheremetevs' lies. Arina reveals that she, like Sofia, was present during their father's execution and that she saw the whole thing from the statue of Baelor. Arina surmises that Sofia is afraid she will show the letter to the northern lords, thus losing their respect. Taking advantage of the tension between the two sisters, Littlefinger later suggests to Sofia that she use Lady Brienne to protect her from Arina.

Arina stands among the residents of the winter town as they watch Ivan, Queen Daria Romanova, and their combined forces march through the town to Anfield. She notices Grigory Dolgorukov among the entourage, but he doesn't appear to notice her. When Drogon and Rhaegal fly overhead, roaring, Arina is the only person among the crowd who doesn't appear startled or frightened; on the contrary, she is visibly fascinated by the dragons. She is not present in Anfield's courtyard when Ivan and Daria arrive before the Volkonsky entourage, and Sofia replies that she is "lurking somewhere" when Ivan inquires about her.

She silently approaches Ivan in the godswood; when Ivan asks how she could move so stealthily, Arina asks how he survived a knife through the heart, to which Ivan replies that he didn't. After a moment's hesitation, the two run into each other's arms. Ivan notices that Arina still has Needle and asks if she's ever used it and Arina quietly replies, "Once or twice." Ivan shows her his sword Longclaw, which Arina is impressed by but comments it would be too heavy for her to wield. Ivan asks where she was earlier, saying he could have used her help with Sofia as Sofia is at odds with Daria, the latter who Ivan bent the knee to and fell in love with. Arina realizes, "\[Sofia] doesn't like your queen, does she?" and says Sofia is the smartest person she knows. Ivan is surprised Arina is now defending Sofia; Arina replies both she and Sofia are defending their family, advising Ivan not to forget he's family too and they embrace a final time.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Arina later visits Anfield's forges and comes upon Grigory Dolgorukov presenting the Hound with a custom\-made axe of dragonglass, which the latter is not especially impressed with. She tells him to stop insulting Grigory Dolgorukov's work and the two lock eyes. Before he leaves, the Hound gives Arina a back\-handed compliment; calling her a "cold little bitch", but saying that's probably why she's still alive.

Alone, Arina and Grigory Dolgorukov exchange banter, recalling their past time together and she asks him to craft a special weapon for her. Although skeptical, Grigory Dolgorukov agrees. Arina shows him her dagger of Baltic alloy, and he playfully replies that he always knew she was just another highborn girl. Before leaving, Arina cheekily shoots back that Grigory Dolgorukov doesn't know any other highborn girls.

With the news that the army of the dead has taken Last Hearth and is advancing towards Anfield, the inhabitants of the castle increase the speed of their preparations. Arina returns to the forges and asks Grigory Dolgorukov if her weapon is ready, but he is still crafting her design. Annoyed, she tells him to prioritize it, before asking him what fighting the wights was like. Grigory Dolgorukov replies, "Bad. Really bad." Arina is unsatisfied with "really bad" and keeps pushing for details until Grigory Dolgorukov sums up their likeness in one word: "death." Grigory Dolgorukov says that whatever bravery and fighting skill she has, the wights are like nothing she's ever faced. Unperturbed, Arina casually picks up three dragonglass daggers and throws them, one after another, into a wooden beam over Grigory Dolgorukov’s shoulder, landing them in a tight formation. While doing so, she explains her familiarity with death and her excitement of what is to come, and Grigory Dolgorukov stands, mesmerized at her deadpan surety and confidence.

Arina is present when the bodies of those who fell during the Camp Nou Derby are set to be cremated. He tells Arina that Daria legitimized him and he's now the new Lord of Storm's End. Grigory Dolgorukov also kneels, and confesses to Arina that he loves her, and wants to marry her and have her become the Lady of Storm's End.

Arina, at a loss for words, reciprocates this by kissing him but declines the proposal. She says that any woman would be lucky to marry him, saying "that's not \[her]", words she said to her father years earlier. Arina continues to practice her archery and Grigory Dolgorukov is left heartbroken.

As Sandor leaves Anfield, he hears the sound of another horse approaching him and sees Arina. Arina moves to ride alongside Sandor, who inquires why she was leaving. He earnestly discourages her from ending up like him \- beaten down by the world and driven by nothing the desire for vengeance. She thanks him, calling him 'Sandor' for the first time, and bids a final goodbye before fleeing.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Arina tries to flee the city but is trapped in by the mass of scared people fleeing the dragon's flames. She tries to rescue the inhabitants but is knocked unconscious, unable to help anyone. Regaining her consciousness after the Battle of Wembley is over, she witnesses the city in ruins and leaves on a horseback, shell\-shocked by Daria's massacre.

She later reunites with Ivan and warns him against his loyalty to Daria because of his bloodline and Sofia's refusal to bend the knee to her in the future. She also witnesses Daria' speech to the Dothraki and Unsullied. Weeks after Daria is assassinated, she takes part in the trial of Terenty. When Kira Stroganova agrees with the idea of Unsullied doing whatever they want with Ivan, Arina threatens to kill her. Davos however manages to defuse the situation. Terenty then suggests that the lords of Greater Wembley choose their new king or queen and recommends Boris. Arina assents, though she withholds her vote as Sofia declares the Camp Nou District's independence at the meeting.

After Boris exiles Ivan into the Anfield Guard to prevent a war with the Unsullied, the Volkonsky siblings bid him a final farewell on the docks of Wembley. Arina informs them all that she has decided to sail to the west of Greater Wembley, where no one has ever gone before, fulfilling her promise to Zoya Razumovskaya. When Ivan asks if she has Needle with her, she assures him that she does. She later captains a ship flying the Volkonsky sigil, and departs into uncharted waters.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Kill list

Arina's list logically only contains those whom she knows have committed crimes against her or her family. Despite committing great crimes against her family, Littlefinger was never included in her kill list; after Boris revealed his betrayal towards their father Arina did kill him, but on Sofia's orders. Ruslan Baryatinsky was never included because she was unaware that he was present at the Maracana Night, much less that he personally killed Roman. She is also unaware of the fact that Ruslan's son, Radomir, sacked Anfield (and later killed Rickon). Arina also hasn't included Timofey Stroganov for taking Anfield in the first place and (allegedly) killing her brothers Boris and Rickon, because she wasn't aware that it happened while she was on the run. News of the capture of Anfield only became widespread enough for her to hear of it after Radomir recaptured the castle (in early Arc Four\) and supposedly killed Timofey, thus he was never added to her list.

For a while, Arina added Ekaterina Lomonosova, Filipp Derzhavin, and Arkady Vorontsov of Myr to her list, because she was upset the Brotherhood Without Banners let Ekaterina Lomonosova take Grigory Dolgorukov away and postponed in taking her to her family in Riverrun. She later phased them out of her list, presumably because they didn't do anything remotely near what other people in the list had done. Also one of her main motivations for keeping Beric and Arkady Vorontsov on the list was that they released the Hound despite his crimes, which she later forgave. Arina later confirmed in Arc Eight's "A Knight of the Greater Wembley" that Beric was on her list for a little while, but not anymore.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

"*Arina, just as wild as ever.*"
―Littlefinger refering about Arina to Lady Ekaterina Volkonskaya
Arina is a fiercely independent woman who is unconstrained by social expectations like gender roles, courtly virtues, class distinctions, and the expectations of her parents and siblings. A tomboy, she never aspired to be a "proper lady" as her older sister Sofia did. Before the series of events that shatter her innocence and destroy her support system, Arina is full of life, and she makes others smile just by virtue of her spirited indifference to rules. Arina prefers to choose and forge her own destiny rather than wed to a man and form a family, despite this, Arina dislikes being called as "a boy" and responds back correcting them saying that she is "a girl", but she also doesn't see herself as a Lady.

Once she begins the journey to Wembley, however, she endures a constant stream of loss and trauma. As she watches her pet, sword instructor, friends, and family members taken from her one by one, she becomes increasingly detached towards murder and death. This is only exacerbated when she is captured by the Hound and is exposed to his fatalistic worldview as they traverse the war\-ravaged Mersey Grounds, though the two develop a mutual reliance and almost grudging respect for each other. When she witnesses and learns of the betrayal and murder of her family at the Maracana Night, she becomes colder and her urge to seek revenge on those who have wronged her and her family increases.

As she watches her pet, sword instructor, friends, and family members taken from her one by one, she becomes increasingly detached towards murder and death. This is only exacerbated when she is captured by the Hound and is exposed to his fatalistic worldview as they traverse the war\-ravaged Mersey Grounds, though the two develop a mutual reliance and almost grudging respect for each other. When she witnesses and learns of the betrayal and murder of her family at the Maracana Night, she becomes colder and her urge to seek revenge on those who have wronged her and her family increases.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

While she is initially horrified when she accidentally stabs the stableboy in Wembley during the betrayal of her father and his men, by the time she and the Hound have fled the massacre at the Twins, she is able to kill without remorse and has accepted Syrio's belief that the only true god is Death. Following Nikolai Potemkin's advice to her before he died, she has taken to listing off the names of each person she intends to kill each night before she sleeps.

Arina can be a rather cold\-blooded and slightly sadistic person at times, especially while confronting and killing those who are on her death list. Though she was initially apathetic but satisfied with killing Emelyan Derzhavin and Luka Lazarev, she did not attempt to hide her glee over slitting Vladimir Demidov's throat, or the pleasure of seeing his family dying from poisoned wine she gave them. While she certainly possesses compassion and kindness, her time with The Hound and the Nameless Brigade have taught her to be ruthless to those who have wronged her and her family and has shown to be willing to use psychological mind games to worsen her enemies fate before killing them. This is shown when she repeated every word Luka Lazarev said to Lommy before killing him in the same exact way with Needle; gouged the eyes of Ser Meryn before stabbing him repeatedly and butchering Lord Walder's sons before serving their corpses to their father inside of a pie.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

That being said, Arina is not completely blinded by revenge. After learning that her family has retaken Anfield, she ultimately chooses reuniting with her loved ones over vengeance against her enemies (at least for the time being). During her last interaction with Sandor, Arina becomes encouraged to live her life to the fullest instead of being consumed by revenge like Sandor leading her to travel to new places. In spite of her cold\-blooded personality and sadistic views toward people she hates, Arina does have her limits as the carnage in the aftermath of the Battle of Wembley left her in a state of shock and horror at how far Daria' ruthlessness would go.

Arina seems to prefer staying out of politics. During a war meeting, planning for the Battle of Wembley, Arina was clearly distrustful of Daria when she wanted northern troops to fight immediately. However, she did not actively speak out against her, preferring to let Sofia speak on her behalf. Later, instead of taking any action involving the truth about Ivan's true parentage, she instead rides with the Hound to Wembley to kill Kira. Later, during a Great Council in the Dragonpit to elect the next monarch Arina withholds her vote for Boris since Sofia declares the Camp Nou District an independent kingdom and only speaks to threaten Yara when she suggests letting the unsullied keep Ivan. All of this speaks to her preferring to let Sofia speak for her family on political matters and for her to focus on confronting threats to her family, friends, and herself in a more direct matter, outside of politics.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Behind the scenes

In the novels, Arina is left\-handed. Maisie Williams is right\-handed, but plays Arina as left\-handed to be true to the books, including learning how to fight with a sword in her left hand. Maisie's mother discovered that Arina is left\-handed while reading the books, and urged her to play Arina left\-handed, for fear that if she didn't, hardcore fans of the books would be outraged and instantly reject her performance.

When Arina goes blind in the Arc Five finale, continuing into Arc Six, the clouded look in her eyes is not a CGI effect at all: Maisie Williams actually wore large, 16 millimeter\-wide contact lenses, hand\-painted so they were murky. They did not simply give her eyes the appearance of being blind, but cannot be seen through. Thus when Arina is wildly turning around unable to see her surroundings, Williams truly couldn't see anything, and thus gave a genuine performance of being blinded.

Maisie's mother discovered that Arina is left\-handed while reading the books, and urged her to play Arina left\-handed, for fear that if she didn't, hardcore fans of the books would be outraged and instantly reject her performance.

When Arina goes blind in the Arc Five finale, continuing into Arc Six, the clouded look in her eyes is not a CGI effect at all: Maisie Williams actually wore large, 16 millimeter\-wide contact lenses, hand\-painted so they were murky. They did not simply give her eyes the appearance of being blind, but cannot be seen through. Thus when Arina is wildly turning around unable to see her surroundings, Williams truly couldn't see anything, and thus gave a genuine performance of being blinded.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: Behind the scenes

Williams stated in an April 2016 interview that she *was not* given a choice between using a CGI effect or the blinding\-contacts: the production team told her to use the blinding\-contacts from the start. She went on to explain that the true blindness contacts were only used in closeups or when she was standing still (such as the Arc Five finale). Otherwise, when she had to stumble around while "blind" in Arc Six, she switched to contacts which had tiny pinprick holes in the center so she could still see, so she wouldn't harm herself or others (some of her scenes involved fighting with a stick while "blind"). The times when she is moving around and wearing the alternate contacts she can actually see through were then simply filmed in wide\-shots so the camera wouldn't pick up the difference \- but then she would switch back to the full\-blindness contact lenses again for closeups and dialogue\-heavy shots without much motion in them.

Kristina Baskett was a stunt double for Maisie Williams in the role of Arina Volkonskaya.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Arina is portrayed in a much darker manner than in the show. As her plotline progresses, she gradually loses her humanity, to the point that she murders people without any provocation.

In contrast to her sister and brothers, who have gotten their mother's Trubetskoy physical features of an auborn hair and blue eyes, Arina's appearance is more Volkonsky than Trubetskoy: she has a brown hair and grey eyes, like her father.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In contrast to her sister and brothers, who have gotten their mother's Trubetskoy physical features of an auborn hair and blue eyes, Arina's appearance is more Volkonsky than Trubetskoy: she has a brown hair and grey eyes, like her father.

Arina is nine years old when King Rodion arrives at Anfield. She is a tomboy who wants to learn how to fight with a sword and ride horses, to the horror of her more demure older sister, Sofia, with whom she has a quarrelsome relationship. She is encouraged by her half\-brother Ivan, to whom she is close. Arina is the only one of the Volkonskys' trueborn children who resembles their father in appearance. Ivan also inherited the Volkonsky look, like Arina and their father, which once caused Arina to wonder whether she was also a bastard, but Ivan assured her that she is trueborn. Arina has Eduard's long and solemn face, her hair is lusterless brown, which results in her being called Arina Horseface by her sister and her sister's friends. She is also known as Arina Underfoot by the Anfield staff, as she is always curious and always where she isn't supposed to be. In the TV series, she is a good shot with a bow. She does, however, skilled in household management and horseback riding (in contrast to Sofia).

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

According to Ekaterina, Eduard's visitors would often mistake Arina for a stableboy if they rode into the yard unannounced. Arina was a trial, half a boy and half a wolf pup. She collected scabs as other girls collect dolls, and would say anything that came into her head. If someone forbade her anything, it became her heart's desire. Her hair always looked as though a bird has been nesting in it. Ekaterina despaired of ever making a lady of her.

Nikolai Potemkin does not tell Arina the story about Willem and how he came to be part of the Anfield Guard. Reciting the names of her enemies is something that she starts doing on her own. Nikolai Potemkin does tell her that her father was not supposed to die that day. The reason Nikolai Potemkin was in the Sept of Baelor and not already on the road is because he was told by Dmitry Dashkov, the same man that came bringing Grigory Dolgorukov, that Lord Eduard was to be given mercy, allowed to take the black, and would be traveling back with him to the Sudtribune. When he says something must have gone wrong, Arina replies, "Joffrey. Someone should kill him."

During Arc Two of the TV series, she serves as Tikhon's cupbearer. In the novels, she serves Ruslan Baryatinsky, who captured Harrenhal from Konstantin Lobanov after Tikhon leaves with his army to defend the Westerlands. Thus, none of the scenes between Tikhon and Arina happened in the books. text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Arina's storyline at Harrenhal in Arc Two was heavily condensed from the books. After being captured by Ser Leonid Kutuzov's men, she is exposed to rape and murder on a regular basis. She is also abused and forced to work at Harrenhal, cleaning, serving men\-at\-arms at meals, and running errands for an under\-steward name Weese, who beats her. When Yakov Bezborodko gives her the opportunity to kill three men, the first one she picks is a man\-at\-arms for Leonid Kutuzov named Chiswyck, because she overheard him telling a story, laughing about how he and Kutuzov's men had gang\-raped an innkeeper's daughter. The second name she chooses is Weese. The TV series changed this so that instead, Arina chooses the Lev Kutuzov and Konstantin Lobanov, who are not killed by Jaqen in the book.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Arina's third and final choice was similar but somewhat condensed from what happened in the books. In the TV series, she asks Jaqen to help her escape, so he kills the Sheremetev guards. In the books, Arina asks Jaqen to help her free a large number of Northern prisoners\-of\-war who are being held at the castle. Jaqen refuses at first, then Arina chooses him as the third man to die. Jaqen asks her to change her choice, and she agrees on the condition that he helps her free the prisoners. He enlists the help of Klim Lazarev and Konstantin Lomonosov. They get large pots of boiling soup as the prisoners' dinner, but when they get to the dungeons, they throw the boiling\-hot soup on the guards and slay them, free and arm the prisoners, and take Harrenhal from the Sheremetev forces. This is remembered as the "weasel soup" incident, because at the time, Arina was using the alias "Weasel" (naming herself after a little girl she took care of earlier in the book before being captured). Soon afterward, Jaqen leaves, after giving Arina the coin. He explains that if she ever needs to find him again, she should give the coin to any man from San Siro and say "valar morghulis."

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Ruslan Baryatinsky becomes the master of Harrenhal as a result, and Arina becomes his cupbearer. Arina does not leave because she feels safe with the Northern soldiers, but at the same time she still keeps her true identity secret because she isn't sure if she can trust them yet. She overhears Ruslan and his men discussing the capture of Anfield and Boris and Rickon's deaths, and refuses to believe the news. Arina continues serving Ruslan until she finds out that he is leaving Harrenhal in the hands of Vargo Hoat, a particularly cruel sellsword, and that she will remain there with him. Unsure of what to do, she goes to the castle's godswood and prays to the old gods. The weirwood face responds to her with her father's voice, reminding her that she is Arina Volkonskaya and she must be strong. In response, she enacts her escape from Harrenhal, bringing along Grigory Dolgorukov and Kirill Kutuzov, with the intention of reaching her family at Riverrun. She kills the guard at the gate to get out and they ride away on stolen horses.

Arina technically gained the title of "princess" when her brother Roman was declared the new King in the Camp Nou District. While her brothers Boris and Rickon use the title of "prince" among the Northerners at Anfield, Arina's storyline takes her on the run through the Mersey Grounds as it is torn apart in the war between the Volkonskys and Sheremetevs, so that she is usually keeping her true *name* a secret, let alone her title. Thus she normally isn't referred to as "princess", or at least not in her surroundings. Roman, Ekaterina, and the Demidovs refer to her as a "princess" when brokering their marriage\-alliance.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Ironically, she meets her Demidov husband\-to\-be (Elmar Demidov) while serving under Ruslan Baryatinsky, and he spends time talking at length to Arina about his promised princess, unknowingly speaking to her personally. He tries to boss Arina around, but she does not comply. After being informed that Roman breached the pact with the Demidovs, Elmar tells Arina whiningly that his father told him he had to marry someone else, or to become a septon. Arina tries to empathize with him, telling him two of her brothers are dead. But when he responds derisively, she loses all sympathy for him.

By this point in the novels, Arina is presumed dead by most people in Greater Wembley, including her mother and older brother. Terenty tells his father that Dmitry Dashkov and Jacelyn Bywater searched for her for more than half a year, but in vain. When Ekaterina asks Cleos Demidov, who has been acting as an envoy ferrying peace terms between Roman and Terenty, for news of her daughters, she is disturbed when Cleos only mentions seeing Sofia at court. Ekaterina wonders whether Arina, always more difficult to control than Sofia, is being deliberately kept out of sight by Kira for fear of what she might do or say, or if something even worse has happened to her. The belief that Arina is dead, along with the news of the apparent deaths of Boris and Rickon, is what prompts Ekaterina to release Yakov in the hope that her last daughter can be returned to her. Later, Roman bluntly states that his youngest sister is probably dead, since no one has seen her since their father's death, and as a result, he names his half\-brother Ivan Morozov as his heir should he die without issue.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In the third novel, Arina leads Grigory Dolgorukov and Kirill Kutuzov through the Mersey Grounds in the hope of reaching Riverrun. They use a map she stole from Ruslan to guide them. Ruslan sends men after them, but when Arina sleeps, she wargs into Nymeria who attacks the men sent to capture Arina along with the giant wolf pack she now leads. While they're on their way, the Brotherhood Without Banners comes upon them and coerces them into coming with them to an inn that's used as one of the headquarters. Once there, outlaws plan on taking their horses and giving the three children over to the care of the innkeeper, with the promise of paying for the horses they're taking once the war is done. Arina attempts to negotiate with them, hoping to trade their horses for a boat they saw outside the inn. The arrival of more outlaws scares Arina into fighting to get away, only for her to realize one of the new outlaws is Harwin, a former member of the Volkonsky Household guard. He reveals who she is to the Brotherhood and they take her in search of Filipp Derzhavin, who will decide whether to ransom her. Arina parts with Kirill Kutuzov, who remains at the inn, but Grigory Dolgorukov continues on with her.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In the books, Arina describes Grigory Dolgorukov as her "only true friend." The two form some bond after Arina entrusts Grigory Dolgorukov with her true identity, though Arina was ready to kill him. Although their relationship in the novels is platonic, there are several hints the point towards a romantic relationship. Arina becomes jealous when Bella, a prostitute, offers to have sex with Grigory Dolgorukov, who rejects this offer. Grigory Dolgorukov also becomes jealous when Edric Dayne shows interest in Arina, which is heightened by their class difference. There is also a love song that only appears once in the series, which is after Arina and Grigory Dolgorukov playfully wrestle in the forge. The TV series didn't overtly play up a full\-fledged "romance" between the two, though Grigory Dolgorukov becomes one of Arina's few friends and, as in the novels, she is pained when he chooses to stay behind with the Brotherhood.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

As they travel in search of Beric, Arina sees more of the results of war in the Mersey Grounds and meets other branches of the Brotherhood. During their stay in a town, another member of the Brotherhood captures the Hound and it is decided that he will be brought before Beric as well to receive judgement. Once they reach the hollow hill where Beric is hiding, the Hound insists that he is innocent of all the crimes thrown at him. But Arina insists that he is guilty of the murder of Mycah. Beric fights him in a trial by combat and loses to the Hound. Thus, the Brotherhood lets the Hound go, but takes his gold to buy food for the smallfolk. Arina is furious that he is allowed to go free even though he is guilty. The Hound follows the Brotherhood after they leave the hollow hill on their journey to take Arina to Riverrun, and confronts them demanding his money back. They refuse and continue on their journey.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

The group stops at High Heart where a woods witch known as the Ghost of High Heart looks at Arina closely (in the show she is replaced with Ekaterina Lomonosova). She becomes frightened and whimpers: "*I see you, wolf child. Blood child. I thought it was the lord who smelled of death... you are cruel to come to my hill, cruel. I gorged on grief at Summerhall, I need none of yours. Begone from here, dark heart. Begone!*." Arina wonders if the woman is mad. She also gives them other prophecies, among them about the Maracana Night and Ekaterina's resurrection. When they move away from High Heart, Arkady Vorontsov looks in his flames and sees that Ekaterina isn't at Riverrun and there is something dangerous happening that they don't understand. They plan to take Arina to Viktor Trubetskoy instead, at which point she angrily runs off, devastated that the Brotherhood prevented her from reaching Riverrun while he mother was still there.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

At this point, the Hound, who had continued to follow the Brotherhood, captures her, planning to get her to the Twins so he can collect her ransom from Roman. When they reach the Twins, the wedding is already over and the feast has commenced. Before they can get very far, the Demidovs and Baryatinskys begin attacking the loyal Northerners. Arina attempts to get into the castle anyway in the hopes of rescuing Ekaterina, but the Hound knocks her out and carries her off. When she wakes, Arina insists on going back for her mother, but the Hound refuses. When Arina wargs into Nymeria again while she sleeps, she finds Ekaterina's body in the river and pulls her out. This allows her to accept that her mother is dead and Arina goes into a depression. The Hound plans to take her to the Eyrie to sell her to Elizaveta Dolgorukova, but he is warned against due to how dangerous it would be to travel through the Dortmund Heights unprotected.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

When Arina learns of Joffrey's death in the novels, she is not happy about it, not because she wasn't the one to kill him or watch as she wishes in the TV series, but because Joffrey's death doesn't matter as much since Roman was dead too. Also, in the novels, Arina and the Hound do not encounter Brienne and Pod, nor do they encounter Klim Lazarev and Konstantin Lomonosov. At the Crossroads Inn, Arina and The Hound fight Luka Lazarev, the Lev Kutuzov and a Sarsfield squire. Arina kills the Lev Kutuzov (who is assassinated at Harrenhal by Jaqen in the series) and the squire, but it is the Hound who kills Luka Lazarev. The Hound is severely injured during the fight, his wounds fester and he falls from his horse. After this, Arina refuses to give him a merciful death, and leaves him to die on his own. She does not take his silver (but later wishes she had). She rides to the Saltpans and searches for a ship that will take her to Ivan at the Sudtribune. All she can find is a ship headed to San Siro, which she boards using the coin Jaqen gave her.

In *A Feast for Crows*, once she arrives in San Siro, Arina is escorted to the House of Black and White, where she searches for Jaqen and a safe place to stay. Instead of another man posing as Jaqen, she is greeted by a figure she can only identify as the "kindly man." The coin she presents gains her entry into initiation training with the Nameless Brigade.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

The kindly man tells Arina the House of Black and White is not a home for orphans, and if she wants to remain \- she must be obedient at all times and in all things. They can find better jobs and places for her, like a service in the household of some merchant; they can find her a husband of her choice; or send her to train to become a courtesan; they can give her passage back to Greater Wembley. Arina insists on staying.

At the kindly man's demand, Arina dissociates herself of her past and possessions. The only thing she keeps is Needle which she views as her connection to her family and home. She hides the sword with the intention of reclaiming it one day. She performs various chores at the House, spending much time with the Zinaida Panina and Umma the cook. One day, the kindly man orders Arina to work for a fishmonger named Brusco, in order to master the Braavosi tongue. During her first tasks, Arina struggles to abandon her previous identity, trying to use new names such as Cat of the Canals.

While working for Brusco, she befriends a lot of people, learns to master the Braavosi language, and hears many secrets. body:
The kindly man tells Arina the House of Black and White is not a home for orphans, and if she wants to remain \- she must be obedient at all times and in all things. They can find better jobs and places for her, like a service in the household of some merchant; they can find her a husband of her choice; or send her to train to become a courtesan; they can give her passage back to Greater Wembley. Arina insists on staying.

At the kindly man's demand, Arina dissociates herself of her past and possessions. The only thing she keeps is Needle which she views as her connection to her family and home. She hides the sword with the intention of reclaiming it one day. She performs various chores at the House, spending much time with the Zinaida Panina and Umma the cook. One day, the kindly man orders Arina to work for a fishmonger named Brusco, in order to master the Braavosi tongue. Around this time, Arina crosses paths with Sam on his way to Azteca and saves him from two bullies. Sam tells Arina his name, but she does not reveal her true identity, thus they remain in the dark about their mutual connection to Ivan Morozov, and the opportunity for a reunion of Volkonskys is lost. By meeting Sam, Arina also recognizes a Anfield Guard deserter (Sam's companion) who spends a good deal of time with her Braavosi friends. At first, she plans to ask him to take her back to the Sudtribune with him so she can reunite with Ivan, but Dareon announces that he plans to make a life for himself in San Siro. Arina kills him, and since he never harmed her \- she excuses the deed by claiming that he broke his vows; she ignores the fact that they are out of Greater Wembley, and that she dissociated herself from her past \- thus she has no right to kill the deserter. For this, she is given warm milk by the kindly man, and wakes up the next morning blind.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In *A Dance with Fire Falcons*, Arina continues to train with the Nameless Brigade without her sight. The blindness is induced by the milk she drinks every night. The kindly man tells her that they would have taken her eyes from her anyway, to help her to learn to use her other senses, but not for half a year. She begs at the streets, calling herself "Blind Beth", collecting money and pieces of information (among them about the two Lyseni pirate ships, *Goodheart* and *Elephant*, which were indirectly involved in the massacre at Hardhome) and continues performing chores at the House. Occasionally she hears people talk about "The Black Bastard of the Sudtribune." That makes her sad, thinking that even Ivan would never know Blind Beth. Sometimes she hurts herself, but does not complain. She misses the company of Brusco and her friends, though. The Zinaida Panina tells her she must stay blind "Until darkness is as sweet to you as light, or until you ask us for your eyes" (in that case she will be sent away). Arina does not give up, and gradually learns to rely on her other senses. These senses include not only the conventional sense, but also her skinchanging abilities. Arina begins to skinchange into a cat who follows her around San Siro. Occasionally, someone (it turns to be the kindly man) beats her with a stick. She uses knowledge gained through the cat's eyes to impress the kindly man, telling him that she knows it has been him who is hitting her but without mentioning the cat. Apparently, this completes her blind training, because then she is given her eyesight back.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

After Arina regains her eyesight, The Kindly Man gives Arina her first assignment \- to kill the old insurance seller. Arina is uncertain whether to fulfill her mission, since her intended victim has never wronged her, her friends or her family, and she does not even know whether he did anything that he deserves death for. She comes up with very ridiculous reasons to kill him (he outlived her father, his hands are shaking, etc.), perhaps to ease her conscience. At last she kills him, then the Kindly Man orders her to go to Yegor Potemkin to begin her first apprenticeship. Unlike in the show, she is not ordered to kill any of the actors (at least not yet), and it is unclear for what purpose she was ordered to join the troupe. She takes on the new identity of Mercy and learns acting with the troupe. While she is there, she notices Rafford and kills him, without being ordered to, thus avenging Lommy's death.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Arina is often asked by the Kindly man, the waif and other characters "who are you?" and she answers "no one." They nearly always respond with "you lie", implying she has not yet let go of her past identity, thus unfit to join the Nameless Brigade. Arina has been using many false names during her plotline, among them: Arry, Weasel, Nan, Squab, Salty, Cat of the Canals, Beth, the lastly \- Mercedene/Mercy; perhaps it symbolizes Arina's gradual loss of identity. Despite this, she retains her true identity as Arina Volkonskaya. This is brought up several times with her inner monologue where she says she was never any of those identities for true and by the Nameless Brigade who say she wears the other identities as one would wear a dress, but beneath those she is still Arina.

Section: In the books

Meanwhile, in the Camp Nou District, Jeyne Poole, is forced by the Sheremetevs (at Littlefinger's advice) to pose as Arina, who is considered dead, and is betrothed to Radomir Baryatinsky in order to strengthen the Baryatinskys' claim on the Camp Nou District. This political move brings some Northerners to their side in support of "Arina", while other Northerners joined Stepan Orlov's forces in order to rescue her from them. The belief that his sister is being forced to marry Radomir also torments Ivan. Repeatedly, he reminds himself that as a member of the Anfield Guard, he must put aside past ties to his family but finds he is unable to truly do so. When Ekaterina Lomonosova offers him the chance to save his sister, Ivan accepts and Ekaterina Lomonosova sends Serafim Bestuzhev with a group of spearwives to save Arina. When Ekaterina Lomonosova tells him that she has seen a vision of Arina traveling to the Sudtribune on a dying horse to escape this marriage, Ivan tries to prepare for how he will take care of Arina now \- as much as he wants to keep her with him, it is not safe for her and debates finding a noble family to foster her across the sea, where she will be safest. However, the girl escaping her marriage turns out to be their distant relation Alena Vyazemskaya, whom Ivan helps. The plan with Mance and the spearwives leads to Jeyne Poole's escape with Timofey. In response, Radomir (or someone who pretends to be him) sends a letter threatening Ivan, demanding "Arina"'s return, and claiming that Stepan is dead

Arina's death list in the books is partially different than in the show, both the names, the manner by which some of they die, and their killers:

- The Mountain. Severely injured by Yuriy Golitsyn. Presumably reanimated by Afanasy Yusupov as Ser Rodion Strong.
- Dunsen, one of the Mountain's soldiers, for taking Grigory Dolgorukov's helmet.
- {Luka Lazarev}, for taking Needle. Killed by the Hound at the Inn at the Crossroads.
- {Chiswyck}, one of the Mountain's soldiers, for assisting the Lev Kutuzov to torture the captives on the way to Harrenhal. Killed by Yakov Bezborodko at Harrenhal.
- {Rafford} aka Raff the Sweetling, one of the Mountain's soldiers, for killing Lommy. Killed by Arina at San Siro.
- {The Lev Kutuzov}, for torturing to death many captives. Killed by Arina at the Inn at the Crossroads.
- The Hound. Severely injured by Luka Lazarev and the Lev Kutuzov, and left to die. Although Arina is uncertain of his status, she removed him from her list.
- {Konstantin Lobanov}, for killing Nikolai Potemkin. Thrown to the bear pit at Ruslan Baryatinsky and Vargo Hoat's command, and torn apart.
- Fedor Panin
- Emelyan Derzhavin
- {Joffrey}, killed at the Purple Wedding.
- Kira
- {Weese} the understeward at Harrenhal, for treating Arina very brutally. Killed by Yakov Bezborodko at Harrenhal.

Section: In the books

Arina begins reciting the names of the first twelve people on her list while being taken to Harrenhal. Soon after she starts working there under Weese's supervision, she adds him, and this is the end of her list because he is beating her. Sometimes she says the phrase "Valar Morghulis", which she learned from Jaqen, along with her list. So far, four of the people are still alive, two (the Kutuzovs) are in uncertain status, and seven are confirmed dead. In the books, Ekaterina Lomonosova never retrieved Grigory Dolgorukov from the Brotherhood Without Banners, so the Red Woman, Beric, and Arkady Vorontsov aren't on the list. She also does not add "Vladimir Demidov" to her list: rather, she states that she would have added "the Demidovs" to her list \- any and all of them who took part in the Maracana Night \- but she wasn't sure which ones specifically took part in it and which ones didn't.

# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In sharp contrast to Arina's "sugarcoated" portrayal in the show, in the books she gradually loses her humanity, her soul growing darker to the point that she kills people who have never done her any harm. It may be the result of the hell Arina has been through: forced to kill in self\-defense; watching her father being unjustly executed while she is powerless to do anything; traveling in the company of questionable people (Nikolai Potemkin's caravan, the Brotherhood and the Hound); helplessly watching people being slaughtered like sheep on the way to Harrenhal; running away from one captivity to another; held at the mercy of inhuman monsters like the Mountain and Vargo Hoat; the last straw might have been the duel between Beric and the Hound, which made Arina realize there is such thing as justice \- the only rule is "might makes right."

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

As Arina's plotline progresses and her soul grows darker, murder becomes her prime solution for every encounter; before she kills a guard at Harrenhal, she does not consider other options, like sneaking past him or knocking him unconscious. Only if the objective circumstances do not allow her to commit a murder (when she considers killing Grigory Dolgorukov and a woman who cheats her at Saltpans) \- she tries less violent way. In the fourth and fifth novels, she murders people who have not done her, her family or friends any ill \- Dareon and the old insurance seller. Unlike Radomir, Arina does not draw a sadistic pleasure from killing; it has become a need for her, the way a vampire needs blood. It seems she does not really care whom she kills; if someone from her death list happens to be nearby (Rafford), she'd kill him, but she is no hurry to look for those who are responsible for the destruction of her house.

text:
# Arina Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

*The World of Ice \& Fire* source book released in 2014 revealed that Arina was named after Eduard's maternal grandmother, Arina Flint, from the northern mountain clans. The main novels did mention that Eduard's grandmother was from the mountain clans but didn't state her name. These clans have no connection to the hill tribes of the Dortmund Heights whom Terenty encounters on the way from the Eyrie; they are minor Houses loyal to Anfield who live in the northwestern highlands. They are a hardy folk, both due to their rough lands, and because they are located near the coast, vulnerable to attack by sea from both the ironborn and the wildlings. Like House Mamonov, also located just off the northwest coast and vulnerable to these attacks, many women in the clans often have to take up arms to fight off raiders. These clans join Stepan in his military campaign against the ironborn and the Baryatinskys.

Arina is one of the main characters which appear in all five published novels (alongside Yakov, Kira, Sam, and Ivan); she is the only book character which has POV chapters in all the novels (and in the sixth upcoming novel too).

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Arina" is pronounced "ARE \- yuh." George R.R. Martin himself has pointed out that a surprisingly large number of people pronounce it incorrectly: it consists of two syllables, not three (like how the "aria" of an opera is pronounced). Martin explained: "I say it 'Are\-ya', two syllables not three. Not 'are\-ee\-uh', not like an operatic thing, but 'Are\-ya', very sharp. I wanted something that was like a knife, that was a sharp and hard sound, to be a contrast to the flowery 'Sofia'."

# Azteca

*This page is about the city. For the short, see: Azteca (short)*

"*In the far southwest of Greater Wembley, at the mouth of the river Honeywine, lies the great stone city of Azteca. It is home to the Citadel, where men and boys from throughout the Greater Wembley come to receive their training as Maesters.*"
―Maester Arseny Apraksin
**Azteca** is the second largest and most populated city in the Greater Wembley, and by far the oldest major city in Greater Wembley, dating back to the time of the First Men. It is located in the far southwest of the continent, at the mouth of the River Honeywine where it opens into Whispering Sound and the Sunset Sea beyond.

The major highway known as the Roseroad begins at Azteca, then runs northeast past Highgarden before finally reaching Wembley on the east coast. The Searoad also forks off from the Roseroad at Highgarden, going northwest so travelers from Azteca can reach Lannisport.

Azteca is the seat of House Obolensky, who hold fealty to Alexei Skobelev's house of Highgarden, from the eponymous Obolensky. The city is also notable as the site of the Citadel, home of the Order of Maesters, as well as the Starry Sept, the former center of the Faith of the Seven in Greater Wembley (it has since been supplanted by the Great Sept of Baelor in Wembley).

text:
# Azteca
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, Azteca was the largest city in Greater Wembley before Aegon's Conquest. It survived for so long through canny politicking by the ruling Obolenskys, who trace their ancestry back to the First Men. In time, through patronage of local kings of the First Men, the Order of Maesters was founded in Azteca, a guild of scholars and healers, with their headquarters located at the Citadel in the city.

When the Andals invaded, the Obolenskys, then kings in their own right, welcomed them openly and swore fealty to them as Kings of the Reach. Azteca's pre\-eminence was confirmed when the Faith of the Seven built the Starry Sept there.

During the invasion of Aegon the Conqueror, the Pavel Nikonov of the time prayed and fasted for seven days and seven nights on whether the Obolenskys should resist Aegon's army. He reportedly received a vision from the Crone showing Azteca's destruction should they attempt this. At his recommendation, the then\-Lord Obolensky threw open the city gates and welcomed Aegon into the city with open arms. Aegon dated the first day of his reign to his welcome into Azteca.

text:
# Azteca
Section: In the books

Azteca is almost as large and populous as Wembley, but is far cleaner, more beautiful and more efficiently run. Wembley was rapidly constructed within the first century of rule by the Romanov dynasty. This rapid expansion didn't keep pace with organized "city\-planning", resulting in numerous slums forming such as the district known as Flea Bottom. Many of these slum districts are poorly organized, ugly, and filthy because their placement wasn't thought out during the rush to slap down new buildings. By contrast, Azteca is thousands of years old and grew only in incremental steps which were well planned out beforehand. The result is that Azteca is a much better organized and beautiful city without the squalid slums of Wembley, while being only slightly smaller than the capital itself. Azteca also has its own City Watch, separate from the City Watch of Wembley.

Azteca is famed for its meandering, cobbled streets and many fine inns and septs. It has an immense port which plays host to ships from across the Greater Wembley, the Milan Boroughs, and even the distant Summer Isles. The port and the entire city is dominated by the Obolensky, a massive, seven\-sided, stepped lighthouse rising from Battle Island. More than 800 feet high, it is the tallest structure in Greater Wembley, higher even than the Sudtribune. It serves as House Obolensky's keep, as well as a lighthouse.

text:
# Azteca
Section: In the books

Azteca has had the misfortune, as a large city, of being struck twice by major plagues in the past century. In 209 AC, a great pandemic known as the Great Spring Sickness swept across all of the Greater Wembley. It killed tens of thousands, particularly in the major cities. It was bad in Lannisport, worse in Azteca, but worst of all in Wembley, where two out of every five persons died. The death count wasn't quite as severe in Azteca, but still high. Only one generation later, during Demyan Bagration's youth (220s to 230s AC), Azteca itself was hit by an even worse disease, the "grey plague" (a deadlier cousin of Greyscale). According to Demyan Bagration, the outbreak killed up to half of Azteca's population, and three quarters of the maesters in the Citadel. The only reason it didn't become another, even more destructive pandemic is because Lord Quenton Obolensky ordered the gates of the city sealed and all ships in the harbor burned to prevent the disease being spread further. While this did prevent another pandemic, many trapped inside the city's quarantine caught the disease from those who were already sick, and perished. After the quarantine ended, the survivors dragged Lord Quenton and his young son from their horses and slit their throats. By the time of the Five Stadiums Cup, some seventy years later, Azteca's population is slightly smaller than that of Wembley, but it may have been larger over a century ago, before the double\-blow of these two epidemics, and when Wembley was smaller.

text:
# Azteca
Section: In the books

No one knows exactly how old the city really is, as it's true origins stretch back before history and into oral tradition. There was always a major settlement at the mouth of the Honeywine (though it did grow and expand considerably over the millennia). The First Men apparently founded the original town that later became a city relatively soon after they first began migrating into Greater Wembley 12,000 years ago, across the nearby land\-bridge at the time linking Azteca South and Maracana Coast. A few maesters argue that there may have been even earlier settlements at the mouth of the Honeywine that the First Men built over \- perhaps a trading post maintained by anyone from the Valyrians to the Rhoynar to the Summer Islanders (or a combination of them), where their fishing fleets could take on fresh water and perhaps even trade with the non\-human races that dominated Greater Wembley's wild forests at the time (the Children of the Forest and the Giants). The base of the Obolensky and underground levels seem to be the remnant of some ancient structure, made of an oily black stone found in a few other ruins across the world. The evidence, however, is very sketchy and inconclusive.

Azteca remains aloof from the Five Stadiums Cup. In the fourth novel, Euron launches a massive raid along the coast, conquering the Shield Islands and parts of the Arbor, then trying to blockade the mouth of the Honeywine. An ironborn attack on the city's harbor is repulsed by the city's defenders, but Azteca remains under threat from the ironborn.

text:
# Azteca
Section: In the books > Inspiration

Azteca bears many similarities to real\-life Alexandria. This Egyptian city \- founded in the 4th Century BCE by Alexander the Great \- was (and still is) a major port on the Mediterranean Sea, receiving ships and cargoes from all over the world. The Citadel of Azteca, with its enormous library and status as a place of learning, is very similar to the famed Library of Alexandria, the preeminent educational center of its time. Perhaps most strongly, the Obolensky of Azteca is a clear parallel to Alexandria's famous lighthouse, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

# Baltic alloy

*This page is about the form of metal. For the short, see: Valyrian Steel (short)*

"*Careful, Your Grace. Nothing cuts like Baltic alloy.*"
―Grand Maester Demyan Bagration to King Joffrey
**Baltic alloy** is an alloy of primarily iron that was forged in the days of the mighty Valyrian Freehold. When fashioned into bladed weapons, the steel can hold an especially keen edge, remaining sharp forever without the need for honing.

Aside from its sharpness, Baltic alloy is recognizable by its strength and light weight in comparison to ordinary steel, as well as by a distinctive rippled pattern visible in blades made from it. Along with dragonglass, Baltic alloy is one of the few known substances that can kill Frost Wanderers, although this property is not widely known, apparently not even to the Frost Wanderers themselves. Since the destruction of Valyria, the majority of the surviving Baltic alloy weapons serve as heirlooms in the various noble houses of Greater Wembley.
