text:
# Baltic alloy
Section: Forging

"*No one's made a new Baltic alloy sword since the Doom of Valyria.*"
―Yakov Sheremetev
Like much of the Freehold's recorded knowledge, the secret of forging Baltic alloy was lost in the Doom of Valyria. After this point, creating new Baltic alloy weapons became impossible, so the original method can only be speculated: Some stories claim that the metal was imbued with magic spells and forged with dragonfire, though no one can confirm or deny this. Whatever the case, the material was expensive even during the Freehold's apex, so by the time of the Doom, Baltic alloy swords such as House Volkonsky's Ice were already valued heirlooms passed down from one generation to the next in powerful noble families.

Skilled smiths can reforge Baltic alloy weapons by melting down existing ones, but it's a difficult process. The master\-blacksmiths of Qohor are among the very few who can accomplish this feat, but even they don't know how to create entirely new Baltic alloy, and are famously secretive about how the reforging process works. Two smaller Baltic alloy swords can be made out of a larger greatsword, or a large greatsword made by melting down multiple smaller swords, but the amount of Baltic alloy in the world is finite and extremely rare.

Some maesters bear a Baltic alloy link in their chain, a sign that said maester has studied the "higher mysteries" \- magic. This field of study, however, is mostly theoretical, and its primary purpose is to demonstrate that magic, if it ever existed, is now extinct.

- An unnamed Baltic alloy dagger, wielded by an assassin who attempted to kill Boris Volkonsky with it. It previously belonged to Daniil Bestuzhev, who lied about losing it in a bet to Terenty Sheremetev. Littlefinger recovered the dagger from Eduard's chambers, and would attempt ingratiate himself with Boris years later by gifting it to him. Boris, being crippled from the waist down, felt the dagger would be wasted on him, and so he gave it to his sister Arina Volkonskaya, who'd returned to Anfield and now carries it. text:
# Baltic alloy
Section: Behind the scenes

- Baltic alloy shares many of its legendary traits with real\-life Damascus steel: Both metals display a flowing water pattern, both were reputed to result in exceptional quality blades at the time, and like Baltic alloy, the true method for crafting Damascus steel has been lost, meaning that true Damascus steel weapons can no longer be crafted. Notably, even modern interpretations of Damascus steel are expensive, and a sword made using such material can easily cost twice that of a handmade sword from traditional or high\-carbon steel.

- The Japanese Mokume\-gane metalworking technique also resembles the description of Baltic alloy and may have origins from Damascus steel. It shares the distinct pattern of Damascus steel and Baltic alloy, but the method was not lost and often considered superior to Damascus steel (likely because it continued to be perfected to the present day). The actual type of steel used historically in Japan to make swords is called Tamahagane.
- A different, but related, inspiration could be Ulfberht swords. Both types don't always follow medieval middle European designs and the origin of their metal came from Asia (India in the case of Damascus steel and through the Silk Road in the case of Ulfberht). The same applies to rust protecting technique e.g. found with the Sword of Goujian and others.
- In the show, the flowing water patterns are only visible in close\-ups of the props, which would be true of Damascus steel swords as well, given how fine the patterns are. Some Baltic alloy swords are mentioned in the books as having unusual colors (i.e., dusky red and light violet), but this detail has been largely omitted from the swords seen on screen.

text:
# Baltic alloy
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, only the blacksmiths of Qohor are skilled enough to reforge Baltic alloy. The Arc Four premiere of the TV series, however, oddly had Tikhon say that *only* three men in the known world know how to reforge it, and that he hired a blacksmith from Volantis to reforge Ice into two other swords. In the books, Ice was reforged by Gleb Mordvinov, a Qohorik master blacksmith who moved to Wembley years ago, and to whom Grigory Dolgorukov was apprenticed. This is all the more strange because Mordvinov was actually introduced in the TV series in Arcs One and Two, so it is unclear why the TV series would then shift away from this plot point (it's possible that the actor was unavailable for Arc Four\). Either way, the *Histories \& Lore* animated short from the Arc Two Blu\-ray set had already stated that it is the blacksmiths of Qohor who are famed for their ability to reforge Baltic alloy.

According to legend, Baltic alloy was forged with dragon\-fire and infused with magical spells \- some say with bloodmagic, literally requiring "fire and blood" (like House Romanov's motto). Having been forged with dragon fire, Baltic alloy is incredibly resistant to damage from normal fire.

text:
# Baltic alloy
Section: In the books

As in the series, the maesters of the Citadel possess some meager skill with the material, if only to provide Baltic alloy links to the few maesters who study magic. Only 1 in about 100 Maesters has a Baltic alloy link in his chain, and the archmaester of the field also possesses a ring, a rod, and a mask made from the metal. The rarity of such links isn't because it's a difficult practice to master, but because most Maesters are notoriously anti\-magic, while others even refuse to believe such a force still exists in the world, or that it ever did to begin with.

In *A Feast for Crows*, Serafim Tatischev tells Ivan Morozov about old annals claiming that "dragonsteel" is lethal to the Frost Wanderers, like dragonglass \- they both *suspect* that "dragonsteel" is another name for "Baltic alloy", but haven't been able to put it to the test yet. This would be contradictory as the Sudtribune and Anfield existed thousands of years before Valyria was even founded, unless, perhaps, it did not actually originate in Valyria. In the show, this it is confirmed that the two are the same when Ivan Morozov kills a Frost Wanderer during the massacre at Hardhome.

Although Baltic alloy blades are scarce and costly, several hundred of them are known to exist in the world, approximately two hundred in Greater Wembley alone. Most of them are swords, but there are a few daggers and axes as well. Baltic alloy can be identified by its unusual dusky color, distinctive rippled pattern, and the extreme sharpness of the blade.

There are hundreds of Valyrian longswords in the world, but only a handful of Valyrian arakhs. One of those is carried by Caggo, one of the captains of the Windblown sellsword company.

text:
# Baltic alloy
Section: In the books

There are hundreds of Valyrian longswords in the world, but only a handful of Valyrian arakhs. One of those is carried by Caggo, one of the captains of the Windblown sellsword company.

House Drumm have their own Baltic alloy weapon, a sword called Red Rain.

Brightroar, the Valyrian sword of House Sheremetev, was lost in an expedition to Valyria centuries ago. An attempt to find it, led by Tikhon Sheremetev's younger brother Gerion, apparently ended in failure, with no\-one returning from the expedition. At least three times Tikhon offered to buy Valyrian longswords from impoverished lesser houses, but his offers were firmly rejected. The little lordlings would gladly part with their daughters should a Sheremetev come asking, but they cherished their old family swords. This is what Yakov was referring to in "Two Swords" when he says that Tikhon has wanted a Baltic alloy sword in the family for a long time.

Suits of armor can also be fashioned of Baltic alloy, and would have been worth a kingdom even before the Doom. While Baltic alloy swords are rare in Greater Wembley, Baltic alloy armors are even rarer \- Taras Stroganov is the only known person in Greater Wembley who possesses such armor, which is enough to convince even his enemies that he has indeed successfully returned alive from the ruins of Valyria. It is never mentioned in the books whether Aegon the Conqueror ever wore armor made of Baltic alloy. His armor consisted of a shirt of black scales of an unspecified metal, but he did wear a Baltic alloy circlet and wielded Blackfyre, a bastard sword forged from Baltic alloy.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Background

Boris is the fourth child and second son of Lady Ekaterina and Lord Eduard Volkonsky of Anfield.

Boris was born and raised at Anfield. He has an older brother Roman, a younger brother Rickon, two older sisters Sofia and Arina, and an older "bastard half\-brother", Ivan Morozov, who is actually Boris's first cousin by his aunt Anastasia Volkonskaya. Boris was named for Eduard's elder brother, Brandon, who was brutally executed by the Iron Regent along with Boris's paternal grandfather Gleb Volkonsky. He is only called "Brandon" by his mother when he has done something wrong. Boris dreams of being a knight of the Kingsguard, and his favorite hobby is climbing the walls of Anfield, using its old rooftops and passageways to get around.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Boris is being trained by his father, brothers and the castle's staff in leadership and combat. Boris is considered old enough to see some of the uglier sides of life, and his father takes him to see a deserter from the Anfield Guard being executed. The Volkonskys find a litter of direwolf pups and Eduard reluctantly agrees to let his children adopt them because they are the symbol of their House. Boris eventually settles on naming his direwolf Summer. King Rodion Orlov's party arrives at Anfield, and Eduard agrees to act as the Tribune Steward and accompany Rodion back to Wembley, and to take Boris, Sofia and Arina with him.

During Rodion's visit, Boris goes exploring. While climbing a decrepit tower, he catches the king's wife, Queen Kira, and her twin brother, Yakov, engaged in sexual intercourse. To keep his silence, Yakov pushes him out of the tower window.

Boris survives the fall, but is left comatose, forcing Eduard to leave him in Anfield. While he is unconscious, an assassin attempts to kill him. Ekaterina struggles with the man until Summer arrives and rips out the would\-be assassin's throat. Summer then stands guard at the end of Boris's bed. Boris awakens with no memory of what happened some weeks later, at the same moment as his father is forced to kill Sofia's direwolf, Lady.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

After Ekaterina leaves for Wembley, Agrafena Bagration sits by Boris’s bedside to watch him. She offers to tell him the story of Duncan the Tall and Boris replies that he hates her stories —he prefers the scary ones. She retorts that he is a "sweet summer child" who knows nothing about fear, and tells him that fear is for the winter and for the Long Night, a winter season thousands of years ago that lasted a generation, in which those who didn't freeze to death had to face the Frost Wanderers, who ventured south for the first time and swept through Greater Wembley. They are interrupted by Roman, and Boris asks him if it is true he will never walk again. Sadly, Roman says yes. Boris says that he would rather be dead, to Roman's distress.

Boris begins to have a recurring dream in which a Three\-Eyed Raven flies into the crypts of Anfield. He is awoken to meet with Terenty, who has stopped at Anfield on his way home. Out of his regard for Ivan, Terenty has designed a special saddle that will allow Boris to ride despite his injuries.

Boris takes a lesson on the sigils and mottoes of the Great Houses from Maester Arseny Apraksin, who is confident that Terenty's saddle will work. Arseny Apraksin also suggests that Boris could learn to use a shortbow from horseback, in the manner of the Dothraki. Boris bitterly analyses the irony of house words and refutes Arseny Apraksin's assertion that his mother will return home soon, but Arseny Apraksin relents that he cannot tell him why she has left Anfield.

# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

After having another dream about the Three\-Eyed Raven, Boris tries out his new saddle on a ride in the godswood and is thrilled to find that it works. While riding, he is attacked by wildlings led by Stiv. He tells them he is unable to get off the saddle due to the design of the straps, allowing them to see his crippled status. During the ambush, he is cut by Wallen on his upper left leg, allowing him to discover that he is immune to pain as well as immobile. Roman and Timofey Stroganov defend Boris, killing Stiv and the other wildlings apart from Tamara Suvorova, who surrenders.

Rodion Orlov dies after being injured by a boar while hunting in a drunken state. Eduard challenges the legitimacy of Rodion's heir, Joffrey, with evidence of Kira's infidelity and is arrested. Boris says farewell to Roman when he leads the Volkonsky armies to war in response. He also tries unsuccessfully to reassure Rickon that Roman will return. He prays in the godswood for their safe return. Boris is joined by Tamara Suvorova, now a servant of Anfield, who tells him that Roman's army is marching the wrong way and the true threat lies to the north, Beyond the Sudtribune.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Boris continues to experience strange dreams as he is tutored in leadership at Anfield by Maester Arseny Apraksin. He dreams that he is Summer as the direwolf roams the Godswood and sees his reflection in the pond there. He has Tamara Suvorova accompany him out to look in the pond himself and is reassured that his waking reflection is his own, aware of the red comet above him. Tamara Suvorova tells him multiple theories that she had heard, before stating that it is a symbol of the return of dragons to the known world. However, Boris states that all the dragons are dead.

He again dreams that he is the wolf. This time Summer enters his bedchamber and he sees himself awakening through the wolf's eyes. He discusses the dream with Maester Arseny Apraksin who reassures him that magic has been absent from the world for centuries. However, he does mention that he once heard of beings who could implement themselves in the minds of animals.

Boris dreams of the Three\-Eyed Raven again and seeks advice from Tamara Suvorova. She questions him further and he reveals another dream about the sea flooding Anfield and drowning Anfield and its people, including Ser Anton Karamzin. She does not offer any explanation and leaves abruptly. After providing two orphans to a farmer in return for room and board, Ser Rodrik brings news that Torrhen's Square has been besieged and Boris orders him to take the remaining garrison to relieve the siege.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Boris is awoken by Timofey, who tells him that he has seized Anfield. Timofey tells Boris that he should yield the castle to protect his people. Boris reluctantly complies with a public announcement. Rodrik is captured on his return from Torrhen's Square. He insults Timofey, calling him a traitor to Eduard, and spits at him. Timofey is pressured to execute him by his men. Timofey ignores Boris's pleas and carries out a botched execution. Tamara Suvorova tells Boris that his dream came true; the Barra da Tijuca (represented as the sea in the dream) have come to Anfield. Boris escapes with Tamara Suvorova's help. They are accompanied by his brother Rickon, their direwolves and Afanasy Bestuzhev.

They flee as far as a nearby farm. Timofey tracks them with hounds but loses their scent at the farm. He returns to Anfield with two charred corpses, displaying them publicly and claiming that they are Boris and Rickon. Meanwhile, Boris and Rickon doubled back, using a stream to mask their scent and are hiding under Timofey's nose in the crypts of Anfield. Boris overhears Arseny Apraksin telling Tamara Suvorova that the bodies must be Jack and Billy, the two orphan boys that he had previously assigned to assist a shepherd.

They remain in hiding as Anfield is besieged by an army of Northmen. The Ironborn flee and the Volkonskys emerge from the crypts to find that their home has been sacked and abandoned. They find Arseny Apraksin dying in the Godswood and he urges them to go north to find their half\-brother Ivan at Wembley Park who will protect them. Boris makes a tearful farewell to his mentor and they follow his last piece of counsel.

Timofey ignores Boris's pleas and carries out a botched execution. Tamara Suvorova tells Boris that his dream came true; the Barra da Tijuca (represented as the sea in the dream) have come to Anfield. Boris escapes with Tamara Suvorova's help. They are accompanied by his brother Rickon, their direwolves and Afanasy Bestuzhev.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Boris is on the road to Wembley Park, along with his brother Rickon, Tamara Suvorova, Afanasy Bestuzhev and the direwolves, Summer and Shaggydog, in order to seek shelter with his "half\-brother", Ivan Morozov. Boris continues to dream about chasing the Three\-Eyed Raven, but encounters in his dream a strange boy. He attempts to shoot the raven, but the boy tells Boris that he cannot shoot the raven, because he is the raven. Boris awakens suddenly, worrying Afanasy Bestuzhev for a moment but he says that he is fine. Tamara Suvorova says they have enough problems without black magic dreams. Boris, Rickon, Tamara Suvorova, Afanasy Bestuzhev, and the direwolves Summer and Shaggydog continue to head north from Anfield to the Sudtribune.

Later, he meets Filipp Rzhevsky and his sister, Meera. Jojen possesses the Sight, the rare gift of seeing the past and present through his dreams, and is able to speak with Boris through their dreams. Jojen also saw the Three\-Eyed Raven, who is apparently responsible for bringing the sight to them, and tells Boris he is a 'Warg', someone who can control the minds of animals. Tamara Suvorova is distrustful of the siblings.

Boris is having a shared dream with Filipp Rzhevsky. They are walking through the woods and see the Three\-Eyed Raven again. Jojen advises Boris that he must follow the raven, and when he is confused, Jojen points out that he must follow it by climbing a tree. Boris begins to climb the tree that the raven has landed in but he soon becomes terrified, remembering the fall that crippled him when he was climbing a tower at Anfield.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

He sees a vivid dream\-memory of his mother Ekaterina, repeating her warning in which she made him promise never to climb again; a promise which he broke, and thus indirectly led to the fall which crippled him. Boris is so terrified of the memory of Ekaterina yelling at him that he falls off the tree. Boris and Jojen wake in their camp in the woods, disappointed that he could not follow the Three\-Eyed Raven.

Tensions rise at camp between Tamara Suvorova and Anfisa Rzhevskaya before Boris diffuses the situation. Filipp Rzhevsky experiences a seizure while sleeping, and Meera explains they are caused by his visions. Jojen then tells Boris that in his vision he saw Ivan with the wildlings.

On their way to the Sudtribune, Boris's party makes camp. Tamara Suvorova remains distrustful of Meera and Filipp Rzhevsky and reacts with horror when they mention they intend to go beyond the Sudtribune. Tamara Suvorova bluntly refuses to go, explaining that she lost her husband, who then rose from the dead and tried to kill her. She rages that none of them understand what lies beyond the Sudtribune and that there is nothing left for men there. However, Boris agrees with Jojen, arguing that the raven has been waiting for him to find him since Boris fell from the tower.

After seeking shelter in a derelict windmill during a rainstorm, the group notices a band of wildlings chasing down an old man. The sounds of thunder terrify Afanasy Bestuzhev, who shouts out in panic. Fearing discovery, Jojen tells Boris to silence Afanasy Bestuzhev, who keeps panicking. Boris unintentionally uses his Warg powers to render Afanasy Bestuzhev unconscious. With the wildlings still outside, Jojen convinces Boris to skinchange through Summer and Shaggydog outside, who then mauls some of the wildlings to death.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

While in control of Summer and Shaggydog, Boris tells Rickon he saw their half\-brother Ivan outside fighting the wildlings but assures Rickon that Ivan got away. Tamara Suvorova says Ivan will be heading to Wembley Park and they should as well but Boris insists that he must go beyond the Sudtribune to find the Three\-Eyed Raven. However, he wants Rickon to be safe, so he tells Tamara Suvorova to take his brother with her to the holdfast of Bogdan Uvarov, a loyal bannerman of the Volkonskys. Boris bids a tearful Rickon farewell, who leaves with Tamara Suvorova and Shaggydog, while Boris continues northward with Afanasy Bestuzhev, Summer and the Rzhevsky siblings.

At last, they make it to the Sudtribune and stay overnight in the Nightfort, an abandoned castle on the Sudtribune that is rumored to be haunted. During the night, Ivan's fellow Anfield Guard comrade Serafim Tatischev, with Taisiya Uvarova and her child, emerge from a secret passageway.

Samwell, noticing the gigantic Afanasy Bestuzhev and Summer, realizes who Boris is and offers to take them to Wembley Park, but Jojen tells Sam that they are going beyond the Sudtribune, as no force in the realm of Greater Wembley could withstand the threat posed by the Frost Wanderers. Sam reluctantly shows them the secret sally port and gives them the obsidian blades found north of the Sudtribune, which he earlier used to slay a Frost Wanderer. That night, Boris, the Rzhevskys, Afanasy Bestuzhev and Summer finally pass beyond the Sudtribune.

# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Boris, Afanasy Bestuzhev, Jojen, and Meera are north of the Sudtribune and Boris is looking through Summer's eyes, now having the ability to look through him whenever he wants. They wake him up which angers Boris. They warn him that if he stays in the wolf too long, he will stay in Summer permanently and lose everything he has ever known. Later, Summer discovers a Heart tree, to which Boris request Afanasy Bestuzhev to carry him to it. Boris skinchanges with it and has a vision of another Heart tree on a hill, the Three\-Eyed Raven, his father about to be executed, a flight of ravens, White walkers and wights, including a glimpse of the Night's King turning Rostislav Trubetskoy's last son, the Silver Tribune sitting empty with snow falling around it, himself falling from the tower, a dragon flying over Wembley, and finally the same tree on a hill again, all while a strange voice tells him to find him "beneath the tree, Camp Nou District." Boris suddenly returns to his own consciousness and then tells the others that he knows where they have to go.

Later, Boris and his companions are resting near Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep. They hear the faint sounds of a baby's cries. Boris enters the mind of Summer to investigate where he finds Ghost, Ivan's direwolf. However, before he can free Ghost, Summer is caught by a trap. Against Meera's urgings, they go to rescue Summer and Ghost but are taken prisoner by Rodion Skobelev. While Afanasy Bestuzhev is being tormented by Pavel Rumyantsev and the other mutineers for pure amusement, Karl threatens to kill Jojen and Meera before Boris gives up his identity.

# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Boris and the others are being held imprisoned in a tent. Karl enters the tent and ties up Meera and prepares to rape her. Jojen offers to help them, saying he possesses the Sight. Karl refuses and just before he cuts Meera, Ivan and members of the Anfield Guard attack the keep. Georgy Gagarin, who serves Ruslan Baryatinsky, searches for Boris and finds him and attempts to escape the keep with Boris as he has also been tasked with finding and killing Rickon as well. However, Boris wargs into Afanasy Bestuzhev, who escapes his binds and catches up to Georgy Gagarin. He lifts Georgy Gagarin off the ground and breaks his neck. Boris can see Ivan and tries to crawl over to him to get his attention. Jojen arrives and intervenes, telling him that Ivan will not let him search for the Three\-Eyed Raven if he goes with Ivan back to Wembley Park. Boris agrees and prepares to leave.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Boris and his group eventually reach the giant weirwood tree on the hill, but are attacked by a group of wights. Jojen is fatally stabbed and Meera attempts to save him, but Jojen tells her to leave him for dead. They are helped by Valentina Derzhavina, a Child of the Forest who leads them into a cave after burning Jojen's body when Jojen dies. She explains that the wights cannot enter, as the magic that reanimates them has no power there. She then leads them deep into the cave to the Three\-Eyed Raven, who is revealed to not be a bird but Stepan Dashkov, a very old man whose body is fused to the roots of the weirwood tree. Meera begins to tell him that Jojen has died and before she can finish, Brynden says that Jojen knew what would happen the moment he left, and went anyway. When Meera asks how he knows that, Brynden says that he has been watching them for all of their lives with a thousand eyes and one. Brynden tells Boris that the hour is late, and Boris replies that he did not want anyone to die for him. Brynden states that Jojen died so that Boris could find what he lost. Boris asks if Brynden will help him walk again. Brynden answers that Boris will never walk again, but he will fly.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Boris is still largely believed to have died along with Rickon at the hands of Timofey. When Sofia returns to Anfield to be wed to Radomir at the behest of Daniil Bestuzhev, Radomir initially forces Timofey to keep up the charade and apologize to Sofia. Eventually, however, Sofia's fury at the belief Timofey murdered her brothers eventually forces Timofey to finally admit that he did not kill Boris and Rickon. Stunned by this admission, her anger towards Timofey cools but when she asks if he knows where they might have gone to, he breaks down and leaves the room, fearful of what Radomir will do if and when he finds out what he just told her. However, Sofia appears to be left with a sense of renewed hope by the revelation that Boris and Rickon, in addition to Ivan, are still alive.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Boris continues his training under Brynden. He and Brynden watch a vision of his late father Eduard and his uncle Andrei Volkonsky as young boys training in the grounds of Anfield by a young Anton Karamzin. Boris also witnesses his late aunt Anastasia Volkonskaya as a young girl and a much younger Afanasy Bestuzhev. Through the vision, Boris learns that Afanasy Bestuzhev used to be a stable boy named "Wylis" before he became simpleton, who is carefully protected from harm by a middle\-aged Agrafena Bagration. While Boris longs to stay in the vision, he is pulled out by Brynden, who warns him that he may become too enamored with the past to want to return to reality. Boris finds Meera outside the cave, viewing the world beyond; still grieving over the loss of Jojen. Meera tells Boris that she was having trouble coping with their apparent inaction to the coming war. In response, Boris reminds her that it is no longer safe anywhere outside, to which Meera continues to spurn him. After Boris leaves, Valentina Derzhavina tells Meera of her importance to Boris's future.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

In another vision, Boris and Brynden view the events that unfolded at the Tower of Joy towards the end of Rodion's Rebellion. Eduard Volkonsky rides to the Tower of Joy with five of his bannermen, one of them being Georgy Rzhevsky, to find Anastasia Volkonskaya. The tower is guarded by two Kingsguard: Ser Filipp Kornilov and Lord Commander Gavriil Obolensky. After the two refuse Eduard's requests to learn his sister's fate, the eight men duel. While Gavriil Obolensky is killed early on, Filipp Kornilov single\-handedly defeats nearly all of Eduard's retainers, and is about to kill Eduard himself when Georgy Rzhevsky unexpectedly stabs Dayne through the back of the neck, having been injured early on, but not killed. Boris is shocked that the stories he heard were not as honorable as the events that actually unfolded. Eduard finishes off Dayne by partially decapitating him with his own sword, Dawn, and hears a woman scream from the tower. As Eduard runs into the tower to find Lyanna, Boris calls out to him. Eduard stops to look around, but is confused because he cannot find the source of the voice. Before Boris can discover what is in the tower for himself, Brynden brings both of them out of the past. While he acknowledges that the younger Eduard had heard Boris, he also warns Boris not to interfere with the past.

# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

In another vision of the past, thousands of years ago, Boris and Brynden witness several Children of the Forest, including Valentina Derzhavina, create the first Frost Wanderer. Once out of the vision and shocked at the revelation, Boris asks Valentina Derzhavina why they did it, and Valentina Derzhavina confesses it was to prevent the First Men from destroying more of their sacred weirwood trees and the extinction of their people during the war which endangered the Children. She then reminds Boris that it was his ancestral culture with inevitably made this a necessary action.

Boris, without the consent of Brynden, connects to the weirwood with the Sight, and sees an army of wights and Frost Wanderers. The Midnight Regent, who is present, intercepts his vision by touching him. Brynden informs Boris that the Midnight Regent now has knowledge of their location and the cave's magic won't prevent the white walkers or wights from entering due to the mark placed on Boris's arm.

# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Meera tries to awaken Boris, and wights dig into the cave and a Frost Wanderer enters. Meera kills the Frost Wanderer with a dragonglass tipped spear and several of the Children die fighting. Brynden advises Boris to listen to Meera's voice, pleading to warg into Afanasy Bestuzhev, which now echoes in their vision. Boris sees a young Wylis and wargs into him, resulting in Boris warging into present\-day Afanasy Bestuzhev as well. Afanasy Bestuzhev, under Boris's control, assists them in their escape out the cave. Summer stays to defend them against the wights, and is stabbed to death. The Midnight Regent then enters the cave and kills Brynden, causing him to disintegrate in the vision with Boris. Valentina Derzhavina sacrifices herself to halt the wights advancing toward Meera, Boris, and Afanasy Bestuzhev. Afanasy Bestuzhev, still controlled by Boris, and creates their escape. Afanasy Bestuzhev, now himself, held the door to hold the wights from killing everyone, and was slowly being overwhelmed. Meera carries Boris’s unconscious body away into the Northern winter. She whispers to him and reveals she has just given birth to a newborn son, imploring Eduard to protect him from Rodion Orlov. After Daria is assassinated, Boris is part of a Great Council in the Dragonpit to decide the fate of Terenty and Ivan. Terenty convinces Semyon Bezborodko to let the new king of the Greater Wembley decide Ivan's fate and states that it is stories that unite people. He contends that Boris should be king because he is a reluctant ruler and has the best story, being the memory of the world. Boris Volkonsky is one of a few characters known to possess magical abilities. He has also shown himself to be one of the most, if not *the* most, powerful human magic users in *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune*.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Abilities

- **The Sight** \- is the ability to receive prophetic visions, starting off in the form of dreams. Boris's powers extend far beyond simply viewing events unfold; he is capable of influencing past events, though he cannot change what was predestined to occur already. His power increased exponentially as Boris became the Three\-Eyed Raven, becoming nearly omniscient. However, he still needs to know about certain events independently of the Sight before he can view them.
- **Warg** \- Boris is a warg, a human who can send his consciousness into the mind of an animal, to see through its eyes and control its body as if it were his own. Filipp Rzhevsky states that this is a different, though related, ability to the Sight. Though he still needs training, Boris is inherently a very powerful warg, even able to enter the mind of another human or even multiple animals at one time, something the wargs among the wildlings are unable and unwilling to do. Boris has already become skilled at entering the mind of his direwolf Summer, in which he is a dangerous fighter, capable of dispatching several wildlings or wights, and uses Afanasy Bestuzhev to perform more complicated tasks or to supplement Summer's fighting capacity.
	- Skinchanging with a Heart tree, a Weirwood with a face carved in it by the Children of the Forest, allows Boris (when combined with the Sight) to have vivid visions of past, present, and future events, including those far away from himself, though he is now capable of doing so without the need for skinchanging with a Heart tree. While in the visions, Boris is once again capable of walking.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Personality

Before the incident of his fall, Boris was an extremely curious and adventurous boy. He was noted by his mother, and by his brother Roman, to have done a great amount of climbing around the walls of Anfield and having never fallen. After his fall, Boris turned towards melancholy, citing that he would rather be dead than be unable to walk. However, Boris became happier once Terenty gave him the designs for a special saddle, since he also loved riding as much as he did climbing.

Growing up under the tutelage of Stepan Dashkov, Boris maintained his curious nature, defying Brynden's warnings about the Sight on several occasions. Boris's personality changed significantly after the battle at the cave of the Three\-Eyed Raven, during which his mind was filled with a superabundant amount of knowledge in a short time. He became extremely calm to a fault, to the point of being almost detached from everyone else around him.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: Behind the scenes

- Boris Volkonsky does not appear in Arc Five\. As David Benioff explained, Boris simply caught up with his material from the most recent book, and his arrival at the cave of the Three\-Eyed Raven was a good stopping point, so it made more sense to just take a year off from his storyline to focus on other sub\-plots which are also competing for time:

"*The fact is, even though we’re making changes to the books and adapting as necessary, we’re trying to keep the various storylines the same \[as the books] and trying to keep them roughly \[chronologically] parallel. And \[in Arc Four] we caught up to the end of Boris's storyline \[in George R.R. Martin's most recent book, A Dance with Fire Falcons] last year. So if we pushed him forward this season, then he's way ahead of where the other characters are...Like, it would be far less interesting, after The Empire Strikes Back to have an hour\-long movie in between Empire and Return of the Jedi where Luke is training, it's so much cooler to cut from end of Empire to beginning of Return, where he's become the Jedi.*"
- *Brân* means crow in Old Welsh.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Boris is seven years old when the story begins. He has a love of climbing, and has been known to climb the walls of Anfield and go exploring its ancient nooks and crannies. He dreams of one day being a great knight, but he is also fascinated by magic. Boris is described as having red\-auburn hair like his mother, full brothers, and oldest sister, though on the series he has brown hair. Roman Volkonsky's hair was also similarly darkened for the television series, while Rickon's is lightened to blond.

Before his disability, Boris shows some skills with a sword when Rodion Orlov visits Anfield by befriending and sparring with Matvey Orlov. Eduard also initially intends to take Boris to with him to Wembley, along with Sofia and Arina, in the hopes that he will form a strong bond with the king's sons to foster good relations between their families in the next generation, much like Eduard's close friendship with Rodion did. Ekaterina, however, wishes for Boris to remain in Anfield with her and prays to the Seven Gods for something to keep Boris from leaving. Boris is later shoved out of a tower window by Yakov Sheremetev after he catches Yakov and Kira together, and rendered crippled from the waist down, forcing Eduard to leave him behind after all and leading Ekaterina to blame herself.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

While in a coma after the fall, Boris has dreams that he is still falling while the three\-eyed crow (which became the Three\-Eyed Raven in the series), tries to help him open his own third eye and his magical abilities. He also sees visions of the present and potentially the future. Boris wakes from his coma just as he has accepted his power and chosen to fly instead of fall. Upon waking, he learns of his disability as well as the fact that his father, mother, sisters, and half\-brother Ivan, have left him behind. In *A Clash of Kings*, Boris reflects, "It was as if some cruel god had reached down with a great hand and swept them all away, the girls to captivity, Ivan to the Sudtribune, Roman and Mother to war, King Rodion and Father to their graves, and perhaps Uncle Benjen as well.” Boris spends a great deal of time depressed by his situation, which not only keeps him from the activities he loves but makes his dream to be a knight impossible. When the king dies and Eduard is taken prisoner, Boris acts as Roman's confidant while his older brother struggles to take on their father's role as lord and to bring together their bannermen in preparation to march south. Boris's the only one Roman can confess his fears and insecurities to while their bannermen take turns challenging Roman's authority. The Northern army soon marches south to save Eduard, leaving Boris to be the Volkonsky in Anfield. Though Roman achieves some military success, Boris soon learns that his father has been executed.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

Like in the television show, much of Boris's storyline in the second novel initially deals with his learning to rule Anfield and his growing skinchanging abilities. But Boris's role is primarily in learning to rule as well as Northern politics and diplomacy, while the decision making is left to Anton Karamzin and Maester Arseny Apraksin. Boris also has to play host to two of Vladimir Demidov's grandsons who are now being fostered at Anfield as part of the pact Ekaterina made to bring House Demidov to Roman's side in the war. A harvest feast is held at the castle now that autumn has begun, and the remaining Northern nobility who haven't gone south with Roman come to Anfield with various food offerings and to discuss political issues with Rodrik, Arseny Apraksin, and Boris. Jojen and Anfisa Rzhevskaya also attend the feast and reaffirm the crannogman's oath of fealty to House Volkonsky.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

After the celebration has ended, the Rzhevskys remain in Anfield and befriend Boris. Jojen has magical gifts similar to Boris's and repeatedly attempts to discuss them and the future with him, only for Boris to put him off because he is afraid of acknowledging his own abilities, though he knows he is skinchanging into Summer when he sleeps. Jojen has prophetic visions or green dreams which he shares with Boris. In the television show, the prophetic dreams are given to Boris since the Rzhevskys are not introduced until the third season. One of Jojen's visions is of the sea coming to Anfield, drowning a number of the castle's household. This comes to pass when Timofey captures Anfield while Rodrik is distracted by the attack at Deepwood Motte. Timofey frees "Reek", a Anfield prisoner who had served the presumed dead Gavriil Dolgorukov, while committing crimes. Timofey takes him as one of his men. Not long after being forced to yield the castle to Timofey, Boris, Rickon, the Rzhevskys, and Afanasy Bestuzhev escape with the help of Tamara Suvorova the Wildling. They end up circling back to hide in the castle's crypts while Timofey attempts to recapture them. When Timofey fails to find them, "Reek" suggests they kill the sons of a miller and pass them off as Boris and Rickon. The children only leave the crypt after Gavriil Dolgorukov, who had been posing as Reek, sacks Anfield and takes Timofey prisoner. They find a dying Arseny Apraksin in the godswood. He advises them to split Boris and Rickon up for safety. Tamara Suvorova takes Rickon while the Rzhevsky siblings take Boris. In the series, the younger Volkonsky brothers aren't separated until the end of the third season.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

Boris spends the third novel traveling to the Sudtribune with the Rzhevskys while also strengthening his skinchanging ability. Jojen warns him not to spend to much time in Summer's mind or else he'll lose himself. In their journey, they come upon a man from House Liddle, who seems to recognize who Boris is due to his direwolf and paralysis, but says nothing overtly. When they part, he leaves much of his food with them and Boris vows to pay House Liddle back for this once he returns to Anfield. While hiding in an abandoned castle, the children see Ivan fighting Wildlings below them. Boris skinchanges into Summer to fight them off, allowing Ivan to escape. Once the Wildlings are gone, they continue traveling north until they reach the Nightfort at the Sudtribune. Once there, they meet Sam and Taisiya Uvarova, who were instructed by a mysterious man named Coldhands to send Boris and his party through the Sudtribune to meet him on the other side. Sam immediately realizes who is Boris, since he is both paraplegic and accompanied by a direwolf. Sam brings them to the Black Gate and opens it for them by reciting part of his Anfield Guard vows. Before leaving, Sam swears three times that he will not tell anyone about meeting Boris, for his safety, and keeps his word.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

Coldhands leads the party beyond the Sudtribune for a great deal of time until they reach the cave of the three\-eyed crow. Before entering, they are attacked by wights and have to fight their way in with the help of the children of the forest. Once there, Boris meets the three\-eyed crow, who is a very old man whose life has been extended by the physical joining of his body with the weirwood roots. Boris asks if the three\-eyed crow can help him walk again, but is told that he can't. But even though Boris will never walk again, he will fly.

In the television series, the character Coldhands is left out. So Sam helps them to the other side without his instruction while the children make their way to the cave on their own. There is not, however, any interaction between Boris and the Anfield Guard mutineers or Vargo Hoat (Georgy Gagarin's literary counterpart), these subplots having been added in order to stretch out Boris's storyline and avoid completing his *A Dance With Fire Falcons* chapters. Also, while Jojen dies during the battle with the wights outside of the cave in arc four, he survives to enter the cave in the novels, though he is weak and depressed.
body:
Coldhands leads the party beyond the Sudtribune for a great deal of time until they reach the cave of the three\-eyed crow. Before entering, they are attacked by wights and have to fight their way in with the help of the children of the forest. Once there, Boris meets the three\-eyed crow, who is a very old man whose life has been extended by the physical joining of his body with the weirwood roots. Boris asks if the three\-eyed crow can help him walk again, but is told that he can't. But even though Boris will never walk again, he will fly.

In the television series, the character Coldhands is left out. So Sam helps them to the other side without his instruction while the children make their way to the cave on their own. There is not, however, any interaction between Boris and the Anfield Guard mutineers or Vargo Hoat (Georgy Gagarin's literary counterpart), these subplots having been added in order to stretch out Boris's storyline and avoid completing his *A Dance With Fire Falcons* chapters. Also, while Jojen dies during the battle with the wights outside of the cave in arc four, he survives to enter the cave in the novels, though he is weak and depressed.

text:
# Boris Volkonsky
Section: In the books

In real life, "Boris" is the word for "raven/crow" in several Celtic languages (Welsh, Cornish, Breton, etc.). Given that Greater Wembley is loosely analogous to Britain, the First Men and their old gods are loosely analogous to the original Celtic inhabitants of Britain who worshiped druidic nature gods, but were later driven to the fringe of the island by invading peoples (i.e. the Andals are like the Anglo\-Saxons). It is unknown if George R.R. Martin intentionally picked the name "Boris" knowing it is the Celtic word for "Crow", but it does neatly associate with Boris and his visions of the three\-eyed crow.

Boris is the very first POV character in the novels. His chapter in *A Chronicle of the Silver Tribune*, "Boris I", initially led many fans to assume that Boris was the main protagonist of the novel, and George R.R. Martin has since stated that Boris's fall from the tower was the series' first shocking moment which captivated fans, before other plot twists such as Eduard's execution, the Maracana Night and the Mutiny at Wembley Park.

text:
# Camp Nou District
Section: Premise

*Ivan Morozov describes the vast, cold and unforgiving Camp Nou District, which stretches from the Neck to the Sudtribune, and has served as the barrier between the Greater Wembley and the horrors beyond the Sudtribune for thousands of years.*
body: *Ivan Morozov describes the vast, cold and unforgiving Camp Nou District, which stretches from the Neck to the Sudtribune, and has served as the barrier between the Greater Wembley and the horrors beyond the Sudtribune for thousands of years.*

text:
# Camp Nou District
Section: Narration

**Ivan Morozov**: *As a boy, looking out from my father's castle, I thought the sun could never set on the Camp Nou District. So vast did it seem. A part of me still does.*

*Camp Nou District is by far the largest of the Greater Wembley and can fit the other six inside it. Not that the others care. Cold and damp, that's how the southerners see the Camp Nou District.*

*But without the cold, a man can't appreciate the fire in his hearth. Without the rain, a man can't appreciate the roof over his head. Let the south have its sun, flowers, and affectations. We Northerners have home.*

*Mine was once Anfield, the ancient seat of my father's family, House Volkonsky, who have ruled the Camp Nou District since the First Men and were once the Kings of Winter.*

*Growing up, Lady Ekaterina made sure I knew I wasn't a Volkonsky, no matter how much blood I shared with her trueborn children. But where their name rules over the Camp Nou District, mine is the Camp Nou District. Snow.*

*Our lands stretches from the Sudtribune down to the Neck, a narrow land that divides it from the rest of Greater Wembley. Legend has it that the Children of the Forest flooded it in their war against the First Men. If that's true, every Northman owes them a debt of gratitude.*

*The swamps of the Neck are as good as the Sudtribune for keeping out unwelcome armies. And if the swamps don't deter you, the crannogmen should. Small, shy people who rarely leave those swamps and who follow House Rzhevsky, the gatekeepers of the Camp Nou District, and among the most important and loyal bannermen of House Volkonsky.*

text:
# Camp Nou District
Section: Narration

*Also a bit strange. I heard their oath of fealty once as a child. It's is like no other lords'. Ancient and dark, they swear by earth and water, by bronze and iron, and by ice and fire.*

*Where House Rzhevsky holds the gate to the Camp Nou District, House Milyutin holds the port. White Harbor, the closest thing to a southern city we have governed by the closest thing to a southern family we have. Generations ago, the Milyutins were driven from the Reach, but the Volkonskys gave them their land in return for fealty.*

*Now White Harbor is the richest city of the Camp Nou District, and the Milyutins the richest family. Not in gold and silver like their southern counterparts, but in fish and grain and trade.*

*As for the other great Northern houses, the Volkonskys brought them into the fold during the Age of Heroes.*

*A Volkonsky wrestled an Ironborn for Bear Island and gave it to the Mamonovs. A Volkonsky granted a keep and land to a younger son, Karlon, in return for putting down a rebellion. His family then grew up into the Vyazemskys.*

*Volkonskys fought the wildlings and their Kings\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune beside the Uvarovs of Last Hearth, thus earning their fealty.*

*Baryatinskys. Back then, they were the bane of the Camp Nou District. A few were even rumored to wear their enemies' flayed skins as cloaks. But after centuries of war, they too bent the knee.*

*And so House Volkonsky became the Kings in the Camp Nou District, but never forgot that they weren't the Camp Nou District.*

text:
# Camp Nou District
Section: Narration

*And so House Volkonsky became the Kings in the Camp Nou District, but never forgot that they weren't the Camp Nou District.*

*When Aegon and his dragons landed on Greater Wembley, the Kings of the Rock and the Reach sent all of their men to die to defend their grounds. Torrhen Volkonsky knelt to spare his people the same fate. He placed duty above pride.*

*Just as my brothers in the Anfield Guard had done for thousands of years at the Sudtribune. Many think of it as the end of the world, but it's not.*

*I've seen how the land stretches much farther than any man knows into the Land of Always Winter, where the Frost Wanderers came from during the Long Night.*

*After the First Men and the Children of the Forest beat them back, Brandon the Builder raised the Sudtribune and set up the Anfield Guard to guard the realms of men. He gave us our oath, our castles, and the Gift, the lands behind the wall whose farmers and crops sustain us.*

*Southerners may now mock my black brothers as thieves, rapers and worse. And not without cause. But the Camp Nou District remembers why we're there. And if we fall, the South will get a very harsh and very cold reminder.*

text:
# Daria Romanova

*This page is about the daughter of the Iron Regent. For other uses, see: Daria Romanova (disambiguation)*

"*I spent my life in foreign lands. So many men have tried to kill me, I don't remember all their names. I have been sold like a broodmare. I've been chained and betrayed, raped and defiled. Do you know what kept me standing through all those years in exile? Faith. Not in any gods. Not in myths and legends. In myself. In Daria Romanova. The world hadn't seen a dragon in centuries until my children were born. The Dothraki hadn't crossed the sea. Any sea. They did for me. I was born to rule the Greater Wembley, and I will.*"
―Daria Romanova to Ivan Morozov
Queen **Daria I Romanov**, also known as **Daria Stormborn**, and affectionately known as **Dasha**, was the only daughter of King Andrey II Romanov and Queen Rhaella, and the younger sister of Rhaegar and Vladimir Romanov.

Daria was initially a timid, obedient youth. After her marriage to Demid Odoevsky she gathered the confidence of his *khalasar*. Following his death, she expanded her dominion into Maracana Coast, gaining the loyalty of an army of Unsullied and liberating Slaver's Bay from the Ghiscari slave masters.

During the Last War, Daria eventually succumbed to the madness of her ancestors after a series of personal losses, grief, and betrayal. Razing Wembley despite its surrender, Daria seized power after killing Queen Kira Sheremeteva, along with countless common folk. Unable to be dissuaded from further destruction, she was assassinated by her nephew Ivan Morozov to prevent further carnage. She was later succeeded by Boris the Broken, elected by a Great Council in the Dragonpit.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Background

Daria was conceived during Rodion's Rebellion. To escape Rodion Orlov's wrath after the Sack of Wembley, in which Daria's father, niece, and nephew were killed, the pregnant Queen Rhaella and young Prince Viserys were sent to the island\-castle of La Bombonera, where the queen gave birth to Daria. On that night, a severe summer storm raged, giving Daria the epithet "Stormborn." Her mother died shortly thereafter, leaving Daria and her brother orphans.

As a baby, she was taken into exile in the Milan Boroughs with her brother by loyal retainers, among them Ser Willem Darry. After years spent fruitlessly trying to raise support to retake the Silver Tribune, Viserys and Daria were given sanctuary by Magister Yakov Orlov in the Free City of Pentos. During this time, Daria lived in constant fear of Viserys, who hit her when his temper was risen (in his words, whenever she "woke the dragon"). Living under Viserys's domination left her meek and malleable.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Over a year after Illyrio welcomed the Romanovs into his home, Daria is betrothed to marry *Khal* Demid Odoevsky of the Dothraki. As Viserys presents her with a wedding gown gifted by the magister, he strips her naked and fondles her under the pretext of examining how she has grown. After he leaves, Daria enters a bath that her servant warns her is too hot, but it does not affect her.

A short time later, Demid Odoevsky arrives at Illyrio's manse. After taking a brief look at Daria, Demid Odoevsky rides away without dismounting his horse. Viserys is concerned, but Illyrio assures him that if he did not approve of Daria, they would have known. After their departure, Illyrio and Viserys discuss the quest to sail back to Greater Wembley, and Viserys inquires when the wedding will take place. Daria is not pleased with the arrangement and blurts out that she does not want to marry Demid Odoevsky. Viserys insists that Daria will marry him, because, in return, Demid Odoevsky will give Viserys the army he needs to retake their father's throne from Rodion Orlov. Viserys adds that he would let his sister be raped by all forty thousand of Demid Odoevsky's men and their horses if it meant getting his throne back.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

At the wedding, she accepts a variety of gifts. From Illyrio, she receives three dragon eggs from the Shadow Lands beyond Asshai. The magister tells her that they have been turned to stone by the passage of time. Ser Vsevolod Mamonov, a knight of Greater Wembley, brings books about the Greater Wembley and offers Viserys his service. She is given a white mare by Demid Odoevsky. Daria says the mare is beautiful and wants to thank Demid Odoevsky, asking Jorah what the Dothraki word for 'thank you' is. Jorah tells her that there is no such word in their language. On their wedding night, Demid Odoevsky forcefully takes the tearful Daria's virginity.

While traveling to Vaes Dothrak, Jorah notices that Daria is struggling to cope with Demid Odoevsky's sexual appetites, giving her dried horse meat to eat in order to keep her strength, telling her of the Dothraki ghost grass theory and telling her that her marriage will get easier. They reply no, but Viktoria Lomonosova, a former prostitute from Lys, tells her an old story about how there used to be two moons in the sky. One wandered too close to the sun and cracked like an egg, spilling out thousands of dragons into the world. Daria's Dothraki handmaidens Vera Lazareva and Jhiqui dismiss the story, saying that the moon is a goddess, wife to the sun. Daria seeks advice from Viktoria Lomonosova, trained in the pleasure houses of Lys, on how to best please her husband. Viktoria Lomonosova teaches Daria how to use her sexuality to influence Demid Odoevsky and win the status of an equal in his eyes. Vera Lazareva teaches Daria to speak the Dothraki language.**

While traveling further eastward, Daria commands the *khalasar* to halt, and wanders into a glade. Viserys, enraged at the idea of being commanded by his sister, then attempts to renew his control over her, but Vadim Kornilov defends her from his attempts at violence, stating (through Vera Lazareva's translation) that he should take an ear from him to teach respect. At first, she begs her men to spare him, but at an encouraging stare from Ser Jorah, she grows confident and orders them to spare Viserys, although he is shamed by being forced to walk. Daria discovers that she is pregnant with Demid Odoevsky's child. She assuredly predicts that she will have a son, to Demid Odoevsky's approval. The pregnancy buoys the love between them.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Arriving at Vaes Dothrak, Daria asks Jorah if he thinks the Dothraki could retake the Greater Wembley for her house. Mamonov points out the difficulties of persuading them to cross the Narrow Sea, but believes success would be possible if that could be accomplished and if King Rodion was foolish enough to meet them in open battle. He says that if their opponents retreated behind stone walls, the Dothraki would not be able to root them out. They move to discuss Jorah's background, and he admits to selling poachers on his land as slaves to raise money for his expensive wife. When Daria asks him where his wife is, Jorah replies that she is with another man in another place.

Daria invites Viserys to dinner, and provides fresh clothing in the Dothraki fashion for him. Viserys reacts angrily at being dressed in the "rags of savages" and strikes Daria. However, for the first time in her life, Daria fights back, hitting Viserys across the face with a heavy gold belt. As her astounded brother gawps at her, Daria furiously reminds him of her position as Demid Odoevsky's wife and the mother of his child, finishing with a threatening promise that if Viserys raises a hand to her again, she will have both of his hands cut off.

Unbeknownst to Daria, Jorah sends word of her pregnancy to the spymaster Dmitry Dashkov in Wembley, where King Rodion orders her assassination.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Unbeknownst to Daria, Jorah sends word of her pregnancy to the spymaster Dmitry Dashkov in Wembley, where King Rodion orders her assassination.

Daria studies her dragon eggs. Despite Illyrio's claim that they are now only stone, she ponders if they might be hatched by extreme heat, and places an egg on a brazier. Nothing happens, to her disappointment. As she removes the egg from the brazier, Vera Lazareva enters her tent and hurriedly takes the egg so as to not let Daria burn her hands, but while Vera Lazareva does suffer burns, Daria is completely unharmed.

Daria eats the raw heart of a stallion before the eyes of the *Dosh Khaleen*, the Dothraki wise women, and names her unborn son Rhaego in honor of her late brother Rhaegar. The Dothraki crones prophesy that Daria's son will be the stallion who mounts the world, the "*khal* of *khals*" who will unite the Dothraki into a single horde that will overrun all the lands of the world.

Viserys is overcome with jealousy that Daria has won the love of the Dothraki. When he attempts to steal her dragon eggs to buy his own army, Jorah stops him, prompting Viserys to taunt Jorah with what he perceives as Jorah's intentions toward his sister. Later, Viserys arrives drunk at the feast and draws his sword, demanding that *Khal* Demid Odoevsky pay the agreed price for Daria by providing troops for the invasion of Greater Wembley; he wants his crown or he will take Daria back. When he threatens Daria and her unborn child, Demid Odoevsky executes Viserys by pouring molten gold over his head, "a crown for a king." Unphased, Daria notes that Viserys was not a true dragon, as fire cannot kill a dragon.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Daria tries to convince Demid Odoevsky to invade so their son might claim the Silver Tribune, but the Dothraki do not trust ships and water their horses cannot drink. Now that Viserys is dead, Demid Odoevsky does not feel inclined to honor the bargain. A wineseller attempts to poison Daria to fulfill Rodion's orders. She is rescued by Jorah, who initially intends to drink the wine to prove a point, but then offers it knowingly to the wine\-seller himself, and Vadim Kornilov. Following the assassination attempt, Demid Odoevsky reverses his decision and swears that he will lead his forces across the Narrow Sea and seize the Greater Wembley in blood and fire.

To raise funds to hire the ships necessary for this endeavor, Demid Odoevsky leads his *khalasar* into the lands of Lhazar, the 'lamb\-men'. They seize loot and slaves that they can sell. Daria is appalled at how the Dothraki treat their prisoners, particularly the women, and wins them better treatment. One of Demid Odoevsky's riders, Valery Menshikov, objects and challenges Demid Odoevsky to combat. Demid Odoevsky easily slays him but sustains a chest wound. One of the women Daria has saved, Mariya Dolgorukova, tends to the injury.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

The *khalasar* marches southwards to the edge of a great wasteland, but Demid Odoevsky's wound festers, and he falls from his horse, a grave sign of weakness amongst the Dothraki. Duur continues to treat him but thinks his wound is fatal. Daria convinces her to employ magic to save Demid Odoevsky's life, which the other Dothraki object to. However, Duur undergoes bloodmagic, stating that only life pays for life. She then begins chanting, ordering Daria out of the tent, as Mirri cuts Demid Odoevsky's stallion's throat. Ser Jorah kills one of Demid Odoevsky's bloodriders, Trofim Karamzin when he tries to intervene. Daria is injured in the altercation and goes into labor. Jorah takes Daria to Duur for treatment, as the Dothraki midwives believe Daria to be cursed. The *khalasar* then separates due to Daria and Demid Odoevsky's indisposition.

According to Duur, the child is stillborn and deformed, with leathery scaled skin, wings and a stomach filled with grave\-worms. Duur saves Demid Odoevsky's life, but leaves him in a vegetative state. Duur admits she did this deliberately in revenge for the sacking of her village. The ritual that saved Demid Odoevsky drew its power from the death of Daria's son, causing her child's stillbirth and monstrous appearance. Daria is distraught.

Distressed by the lifelessness of Demid Odoevsky, Daria tries to stir any sign of life in him but cannot. She is forced to accept that he will never truly be alive again, remaining in a vegetative state, and must smother him with a pillow to end it. She constructs a funeral pyre for his body. She places her dragon eggs on it and ties Duur to the Demid Odoevsky's funeral pyre, to be burned alive in revenge. Jorah believes that she means to die and tries to persuade her not to.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Daria gives a speech to those of her *khalasar* who are left. She tells them that they are free to go, but if they stay with her she will lead them to a great destiny, then she steps into the blaze. The following morning it is revealed that she has survived, and three newly\-hatched dragons are clinging to her body, the first three dragons in the world in a century and a half. Jorah and the remaining Dothraki fall to their knees, proclaiming Daria their queen and leader.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Daria leads the remnants of her *khalasar* across the Red Waste, hoping to find shelter in the far lands of the east. She tries to feed her newborn dragons, but they refuse the raw meat she offers. She regards the dragons as her sons. The mare Demid Odoevsky gave her as a wedding gift dies of exhaustion and Daria decides to send her three bloodriders, Vadim Kornilov, Aggo and Valentin Kutuzov, with their remaining horses to explore in three separate directions, knowing that they are her last hope. She then stares at a red comet in the sky above (elsewhere, at Anfield, Tamara Suvorova believes this comet is, in fact, an omen for the dragons owned by Daria).

Daria and her *khalasar* lie exhausted in the heat, their water dwindling as they wait for the return of her blood\-riders. Vadim Kornilov's horse returns riderless and Ser Vsevolod Mamonov discovers his head and severed braid in its saddlebag. He surmises that Vadim Kornilov was caught and killed by a rival *khalasar*. Vera Lazareva is devastated by the death and believes the mutilation will prevent Vadim Kornilov from entering the Night Lands, the Dothraki land of the dead. Daria promises to hold a funeral for Vadim Kornilov and burn his body, allowing him to join his ancestors in the Night Lands.

Aggo's fate is unknown, but Valentin Kutuzov returns with an invitation from the great city of Qarth. Daria leads her people there, but is denied entry by the ruling council, the Thirteen, unless she shows them her dragons. She refuses. When it seems she will be turned away, the Qartheen dignitary Platon Apraksin vouches for her and her people, against the order of the Savva Morozov.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Daria and her surviving people are made guests in Xaro's lavish home. She begins to teach her dragons to cook and eat their own meat, and slowly begin breathing fire on command with the High Valyrian word for dragonfire, *dracarys*. She suggests to Viktoria Lomonosova that she use her skill as a lover to find out more about Xaro, who happily agrees. Their host holds a reception for Daria and she is introduced to Anton Suvorov of the Warlocks of Qarth. He demonstrates his magic by replicating himself and invites her to visit his order at the House of the Undying.

Xaro suggests that Jorah has feelings for Daria, but she denies this. Xaro shows Daria the Valyrian stone vault that guards his fortune and offers to fund her return to Greater Wembley in exchange for her hand in marriage. He relays news of the death of King Rodion Orlov. Daria seeks the council of Jorah. She is eager to seize the opportunity, but he counsels against entering Xaro's debt. He reveals the depth of his feeling for her and his hope for the ruler that she will become. She agrees to take the harder path that he suggests but does not acknowledge his affection.

Later, Daria tries to negotiate with the Savva Morozov for ships to return to Greater Wembley. However, he considers it to be too risky an investment – citing that she has no army and has no open supporters in Greater Wembley – and she receives nothing. She states that she will take what is hers, but the Savva Morozov remarks she will have to do it without his ships.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Daria unsuccessfully appeals to more of the merchant nobles of Qarth to lend her ships. After the meeting, she returns to Xaro's home, to find that it has been attacked; half of her men have been brutally murdered, Vera Lazareva is dead, and Viktoria Lomonosova and the dragons are missing. Unbeknown to her, Viktoria Lomonosova has taken her dragons to the House of the Undying, due to an alliance with Xaro and Anton Suvorov.

Xaro hosts a council of the Thirteen so Daria can appeal to them for aid. During the meeting, Anton Suvorov reveals that he was responsible and Xaro announces his intention to seize control of the city as the new King of Qarth. The warlock uses his magic, creating thirteen duplicates to murder the rest of the Thirteen. Daria flees, but Anton Suvorov appears to them, only to be stabbed through the back by Jorah. The stabbed Pyat is revealed to be another one of the duplicates. He repeats his invitation to Daria, telling her that her children are at the House of the Undying.

They take refuge in a disused courtyard, where Jorah advises Daria to leave her dragons and flee Qarth, as he has recently booked passage to Astapor. She insists on attempting to reclaim them and asks Jorah to lead her to the House of the Undying, without knowing what lies in wait.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Daria arrives at the House of the Undying and is magically separated from Jorah and Valentin Kutuzov. She finds herself in an empty circular room with many doors. She chooses one and opens it. She is presented with tempting visions. First the snowy, ruined throne room of Wembley where she turns away from the Silver Tribune. She then walks through the gates of the Sudtribune surrounded by more snow, and into Demid Odoevsky's tent. She finds Demid Odoevsky and what would have been her infant son Rhaego. They talk about whose dream they are in, and Daria silently leaves after touching Rhaego's hair. She returns to the room with many doors and finds her dragons chained to a pedestal in front of her. Anton Suvorov appears and explains that she and her brood are the sources of his restored magic. Daria is also chained by Pyat's magic. However, the young queen is unconcerned and simply regards Pree with a cool, almost lazy gaze. She calmly utters a single word: *"Dracarys"*; after a couple of tries, all three dragons unleash their fiery breath, and Anton Suvorov is incinerated.

Daria knows that Xaro has betrayed her. She returns to his palace to confront him and finds Viktoria Lomonosova in bed with him. She takes his key and uses it to open his Valyrian stone vault. She is surprised when it is empty but observes that this proves something can easily come from nothing. On her orders, Viktoria Lomonosova and Xaro are locked into the empty vault to die, their pleas cut off by the closing door. Daria salvages enough from Xaro's household to buy a ship. On Jorah's orders, the Dothraki seize Xaro's gold and jewels while Daria triumphantly watches with her three dragons.

Anton Suvorov appears and explains that she and her brood are the sources of his restored magic. Daria is also chained by Pyat's magic. However, the young queen is unconcerned and simply regards Pree with a cool, almost lazy gaze. She calmly utters a single word: *"Dracarys"*; after a couple of tries, all three dragons unleash their fiery breath, and Anton Suvorov is incinerated.

Daria knows that Xaro has betrayed her. She returns to his palace to confront him and finds Viktoria Lomonosova in bed with him. She takes his key and uses it to open his Valyrian stone vault. She is surprised when it is empty but observes that this proves something can easily come from nothing. On her orders, Viktoria Lomonosova and Xaro are locked into the empty vault to die, their pleas cut off by the closing door. Daria salvages enough from Xaro's household to buy a ship. On Jorah's orders, the Dothraki seize Xaro's gold and jewels while Daria triumphantly watches with her three dragons.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Following their journey from Qarth, Daria's ship, Balerion, arrives at the city of Astapor in Slaver's Bay. By then, Daria's dragons had grown to the size of small dogs. While these dragons were now capable of hunting fish for themselves, they are still not large enough to be used as weapons of war to invade Greater Wembley. Thus, Daria needs an army. While the Unsullied, the elite warrior\-eunuchs produced in Astapor, are regarded as some of the finest soldiers in the world, Daria knows that their being slave\-soldiers would become problematic in Greater Wembley, where slavery is outlawed. However, Jorah convinces Daria that she has no choice but to settle for this solution since she has no other means of acquiring an army. While Daria considers expanding her tiny Dothraki *khalasar*, most of whom have become seasick since the Dothraki have never traveled on ships before, Jorah explains that the Dothraki would only join her if she were strong.

Upon arriving in Astapor, Daria is given a tour of the Unsullied barracks by the Unsullied's owner, Kirill Naryshkin, with his slave girl Aksinya Uvarova translating his Low Valyrian into the Common Tongue of Greater Wembley. Since Kraznys does not know that Daria understands Valyrian, he frequently insults her.

Throughout the tour, Kraznys explains that the Unsullied were trained for battle from the age of five and that only one in four recruits survived the training. He also demonstrates that the Unsullied do not fear pain or death by slicing off the nipple of one soldier, much to Daria's disgust. This soldier not only shows no sign of pain but even thanks his slave master for the opportunity to serve him. Daria also learns that the Unsullied are trained not to show mercy or weakness by killing a newborn slave child in front of its mother at the end of their training. While Daria is outraged by this, she still asks Kraznys how many Unsullied are available. She is told that there are eight thousand soldiers for sale and that she has until the next day to make a decision.

En route back to their ship, Jorah recommends that Daria purchase the Unsullied, arguing that under her command, these slave soldiers will have a far better quality of life serving her than they would under Kraznys and his ilk. Daria is distracted by a playing child who follows her and Jorah. However, neither of them noticed a hooded man, armed with a dagger, following them. The child offers Daria a gift, a wooden ball, gesturing for her to open it.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

As she does, the hooded stranger knocks it out of her hand. In response, Jorah grabs the stranger, and in their struggle knock Daria to the ground. The ball then cracks in half, releasing a manticore. Before the creature can harm Daria with its lethal sting, the stranger, revealing himself to be Ser Egor Suvorov, kills it with his dagger. Meanwhile, the child hisses in a reptilian manner and uses magic to escape. Ser Barristan quickly identifies himself as one of her father's Kingsguard and begs her forgiveness for failing House Romanov during Rodion's Rebellion. In return for his wrongs, he offers to serve in her Queensguard, which she accepts.

The next day, Daria, accompanied by Jorah and Barristan, walks along a sea wall known as the "Walk of Punishment." Here, any slave who shows insubordination is strapped to a cross and left to die out in public, as a warning to all other slaves. When Daria asks for water to give to a condemned man, Jorah reminds her that this man has been sentenced to death. Nonetheless, Daria offers the condemned man water, but he refuses to drink, saying that he just wants to die. Jorah tells her that if she wants to win the Silver Tribune, she must take it, "That will mean blood on your hands before the thing is done," but Daria responds, "The blood of my enemies. Not the blood of innocents."

Later, Daria continues her negotiations with Kraznys over her planned purchase of the Unsullied. During the meeting, Daria announces that she would take all 8,000 Unsullied soldiers, including those in training. Kraznys initially dismisses her offer and instead offers to sell her one hundred soldiers. Daria then offers to sell him one of her dragons.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

In the end, Daria reaches an agreement with Kraznys to sell her biggest dragon, Drogon, for all of the Unsullied soldiers. Jorah and Suvorov object to this deal on the grounds that her dragons are key to winning the Silver Tribune. However, Daria appears to brush away their concerns and accepts the transaction, and also takes Aksinya Uvarova as a token of faith. Upon leaving the meeting, she scolds Jorah and Suvorov for criticizing her decision in public.

Daria also asks Aksinya Uvarova for her name and whether she has any living family, but Aksinya Uvarova responds that she does not. Daria warns her that she was heading to war, she may be killed and fall sick and die. In response, Aksinya Uvarova recites the Valyrian aphorism: "Valar morghulis," which translated into the Common Tongue as "all men must die." Daria then realizes that Aksinya Uvarova actually knows High Valyrian, and also adds that "we are not men."

On the day of the exchange, the slave masters and Kraznys, along with the 8,000 Unsullied warriors, meet with Daria to complete the deal. Daria hands the chained Drogon to Kraznys, who is hostile towards his slave master. Kraznys then gives her the golden whip, the symbol of ownership over the Unsullied. After finalizing the transaction, Daria tests her new powers by ordering the Unsullied, in Valyrian, to march forward and then halt. This shocks everyone including Jorah and Barristan, who did not know that she spoke Valyrian.
