text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Kraznys then complains that Drogon did not obey his command, to which Daria angrily retorts that "a dragon is not a slave". Kraznys is both stunned to learn she speaks fluent Valyrian and horrified to realize Daria understood his derogatory comments and insults about her the whole time, merely feigning ignorance to lull the masters into a false sense of security. She then orders the Unsullied to kill all the slave masters and free all the slaves in Astapor, but to harm no innocents. When a panicking Kraznys desperately shouts for someone to kill her, asserting that he is the master of the Unsullied, Daria tells Drogon, *"dracarys."* Kraznys is burned to death.

With the Unsullied under her command, Daria sacks Astapor with little resistance. Once it is done, she addresses all of her Unsullied warriors and tells them they are now free. She also gives them the option of leaving unharmed or fighting under her command as free men. At first, the Unsullied remain quiet, not knowing what to do with their newfound freedom. However, one Unsullied soldier begins to beat his spear against the ground, signifying his allegiance to her. The rest of the Unsullied follow suit shortly thereafter. Now in command of an army of free men, Daria marches forward with her new army while her dragons fly overhead and roar triumphantly.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Daria and her new army make for Yunkai, the next great city of Slaver's Bay, as Daria becomes determined to free all the slaves she can now that she has the power to. Daria orders the Unsullied to elect a commander from their own ranks. The officers ultimately choose Semyon Bezborodko who, like all Unsullied, was given the name of a type of vermin. When Daria instructs the Unsullied to go back to their own names or pick new ones they like, Semyon Bezborodko elects to keep his, as it was the name he had when Daria Stormborn set him free.

While Daria and Barristan are confident that they can conquer Yunkai since the city has only ever bred sex slaves, Jorah expresses his concerns that the city's defenders will not fight them on the battlefield, but will rather strengthen their position behind the walls and utilize guerrilla tactics against her army. He also views the Yunkai campaign as a distraction from their main goal of taking Greater Wembley. Despite the little she has to gain, Daria is adamant on freeing the slaves of Yunkai, who number in the hundreds of thousands.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

She orders Semyon Bezborodko to send a messenger to the city, and inform Yunkai's slaver rulers that they must either surrender or suffer the same fate as Astapor. Daria holds an audience with the Yunkish herald, Ratmir Rumyantsev, who is one of the ruling "Wise Masters" of Yunkai. Razdal attempts to discourage Daria from attacking his city by claiming that numerous armies throughout history had tried and failed to conquer it. However, Daria is undaunted and comments that a hard\-fought battle will give her Unsullied some practice, referring to Kraznys' words. Razdal then attempts to bribe her by providing her with the gold and ships needed to transport her army to Greater Wembley. In exchange, Daria will have to leave Yunkai in peace.

In response, Daria makes a counter\-offer: she will spare the lives of Razdal and the slave\-masters of Yunkai if every slave (men, women, and children) in the city were set free, and given as much food, clothing, and property as they could carry in payment for their services. She threatens to show no mercy if Yunkai rejects her offer. Razdal is offended by Daria's demands and threatens to use Yunkai's "powerful friends" to destroy her.

As a result of Razdal's actions, Daria's dragons scream at him. When Razdal protests that he had been promised safe conduct, Daria responds that her dragons made no such promise and they take offense to him threatening their mother. Razdal is also unable to reclaim the chests of gold he had brought with him. Following his departure, Daria orders her knights to find out more about Yunkai's "powerful friends" before she decided to attack the city.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

They eventually discover that these "powerful friends" are the Second Sons, a professional mercenary company. While there are only 2,000 of them, the Second Sons are armored and mounted, enough to cause trouble for the Unsullied. Daria tells Barristan to organize a meeting with the Second Sons' captains, saying that men who fight for gold "can't afford to lose to a girl."

Daria meets with the Captains Demyan Dashkov, a Braavosi who is also known as the Titan's Bastard, and Prokhor Gagarin, a Ghiscari, and Prendahl's underling Daniil Bagration. During the proceedings, Demyan Dashkov insults Daria by likening her to a whore and touches Aksinya Uvarova inappropriately. Prendahl and Demyan Dashkov refuse Daria's offer of an alliance, pointing out they will not get their rewards until she reclaims the Silver Tribune. In response, Daria replies that she had no army a fortnight ago and that she had no dragons a year ago. Daria gives them two days to make up their mind and sends them away with the barrel of wine which Demyan Dashkov had departed.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

After the Second Sons depart, Daria instructs Barristan to kill Demyan Dashkov in the event that she had to fight with them. Barristan replies that he would be glad to do so. Later that night, Daria takes a bath and is surprised to learn that Aksinya Uvarova speaks nineteen languages. In response, Aksinya Uvarova comments that this shouldn't be that odd since it only took Daria a year to gain a reasonable grasp of Dothraki. The *khaleesi* bristles at the idea she speaks only *reasonable* Dothraki and switches to the language to teach Aksinya Uvarova a lesson, only to have her pronunciation corrected. Suddenly, an Unsullied enters and holds a knife to Aksinya Uvarova's throat, advising the women not to scream. He removes his helmet, revealing himself as Daario. He confesses that his captains want to kill Daria, but he disagreed with them. Instead, he beheaded them and shows their severed heads to Daria. Shortly after, Daario swears fealty to Daria. Thus, Daria gains a new ally in her conquest.

For their assault on Yunkai, the new captain Daario suggested attacking the city through its lightly defended back gate. Their plan was to infiltrate the city and open the main gates for the rest of the army to invade. While Ser Jorah was skeptical of the plan, Daria and Semyon Bezborodko were willing to trust Daario. During the war meeting, Daario attempted to flirt with her. When the battle began, Ser Barristan remained behind to guard Daria, fulfilling his duty as a Queensguard. During that night, Jorah, Daario, and Semyon Bezborodko infiltrated the city and fought their way through the slave soldiers guarding the city. Within a few hours, Romanov forces had captured Yunkai.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Daria sits near the sea with her three dragons, each one about the size of a small horse. Daria strokes Drogon's head, while Rhaegal and Viserion fight over a dead lamb and Drogon joins the fight. As Daria tries to calm him down, Drogon, without warning, snaps at her with a hiss as a warning to not interfere. He then roars and goes to contest the kill. Drogon snarls a warning at his mother. This act, that her own children would threaten her, and that they are outgrowing her influence and ability to control them, leaves Daria visibly shaken.

Daria returns to her Unsullied army to resume the march to Maracana. She notices Semyon Bezborodko and Daniil Bagration are absent and sets out to find them after being told they are "gambling." Daario explains they are deciding on which of them will ride up front with her in the vanguard. Frustrated, Daria states that the honor goes to Jorah and Barristan as they did not keep her waiting all morning. She orders the two men to ride at the back with the livestock. She also adds that the last man holding his sword shall find a new queen to fight for. Both Daario and Semyon Bezborodko instantly drop their swords.

On the road to Maracana, Daria speaks with Aksinya Uvarova, who tells her queen that Maracana would be wise to fear her approach. Daario meets them on the cliffside, and Daria expresses her annoyance when he shows her flowers he has picked. He reveals that the flowers represent a portrait of the landscape, and serve various purposes, chiefly that knowing her surroundings is important to her strategy.

Some weeks later, Daria is irritated to discover Daario in her private quarters. The mercenary tries to give her flowers, but the queen demands to know what he wants. Jorah enters the throne room in Maracana. In an audience before her, a seething Daria demands an explanation, and Jorah says it is a plot by Tikhon Sheremetev to divide them. Daria counters that the pardon was signed the year they met. Asking him whether he claims the pardon was forged, Jorah admits that it was not. He soon confesses to giving Dmitry Dashkov information on Daria's activities in Maracana Coast. Daria angrily says that Jorah revealing her pregnancy by *Khal* Demid Odoevsky to them led to her near\-poisoning at the hands of a wine merchant. Jorah protests that his actions stopped her from being poisoned, but Daria retorts this was only because he knew it might be coming. Jorah begs for her forgiveness, but Daria rebuffs him, saying he betrayed her, selling her secrets to the man she holds responsible for the death of her family. She spares his life, however, and gives him a day to leave Maracana. She warns that if he is seen in the city after that, his head will be thrown into Slaver's Bay. Jorah is last seen leaving Maracana on a horse.

Daria sits in her throne room where she is receiving another day's supplicants. An old man named Fennesz approaches the throne. Fennesz explains that he was not one of the slaves who toiled away at manual labor, but a well\-educated teacher and servant to Master Mighdal, who employed him as a teacher for his own children. He tells Daria that Master Mighdal's seven\-year\-old daughter Calla admires Daria, having learned of the Romanov dynasty through Fennesz's teachings. As a servant of Master Mighdal, Fennesz was well\-treated and even well\-respected in the household, but when Daria forcibly freed all of the slaves in the city she did not understand the full\-scale complications of suddenly having to care for so many people. Fennesz originally stayed in Master Mighdal's house after she took the city. Mighdal's children begged him to stay, but Mighdal and Fennesz agreed that he must leave rather than face reprisals, forcing Fennesz to become homeless. Daria insists that she had established mess halls to feed the freed slaves and barracks to house them. Fennesz says that he has visited these refugee centers and they are not very safe: the young prey on the old, harassing and robbing them. Daria insists that her Unsullied will restore order, but Fennesz points out that even assuming that they are able to ensure his physical safety, he has lost his livelihood and his purpose and is too old to start anew. Therefore, he has come to Daria to beg her permission to sell himself back to Mighdal. She is shocked that he would *want* to be owned as a slave again, as a man might own a goat or a chair.

He implores her that the young who can adapt rejoice in her new world, but for those too old to change, there is only fear and squalor. Nor, he says, is he alone: there are many supplicants waiting outside lining up to make similar requests. Daria is crestfallen and says she did not liberate the slaves of Maracana only to preside over the very injustice she sought to destroy, but surprisingly relents and admits that freedom means making one's own choices. Therefore she allowed Fennesz to enter into a labor contract with Mighdal, but lasting no more than one year. He earnestly thanks her and leaves. The next supplicant then enters, a shepherd carrying a bundle in his arms. The shepherd timidly approaches and states that he is unable to speak in the common tongue and requires Aksinya Uvarova to translate. Distraught, he tells Daria that the "winged shadow" came, placing the bundle on the ground and opening it to reveal charred bones \- of a *human child*. Daria's largest dragon, the pitch\-black Drogon, has roasted the man's three\-year\-old daughter Zalla until this is all that was left of her.

Horrified, Daria meets with Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko in private to discuss the details of Zalla's death and how to deal with the growing threat the dragons are posing to the people of Maracana. Semyon Bezborodko reports that Drogon was last seen flying over the Black Cliffs three days ago, but he can no longer be found. Realizing that she can no longer control her dragons, Daria tells them to head with her to the catacombs under the city. Later, she leads her remaining two dragons, Rhaegal and Viserion, into the catacombs, where they are distracted by sheep carcasses. As they are feeding, Daria personally locks huge iron collars around their necks, which are secured by heavy chains. She weeps as she does so, as it is symbolically reducing her remaining "children" to chained\-up slaves themselves. Daria wordlessly leaves and closes the huge stone door to the catacombs behind her as her dragons grow distressed and pathetically call after her when they attempt to follow and realize they are chained in place.

Following the removal of the golden harpy from the top of the Great Pyramid and the subsequent murder of White Rat, Daria is furious. She orders that he be buried with full honors in the Temple of the Graces as a statement to the Sons of the Harpy, and orders that the Unsullied patrol the streets of Maracana. She later receives Gleb Bagration's report on the situation in Yunkai. Daria is pleased that the Wise Masters will share their rule with the former slaves but refuses to support Hizdahr's concession of allowing the fighting pits to reopen.

Later that night, Daario tries to convince her to reconsider, explaining that he was once a slave who earned his freedom in the pits. The skills he learned ultimately led him to the Second Sons and thence to Daria. Upon learning that Drogon hasn't been seen in weeks, Daario muses on the possibilities of a dragon queen with no dragons. In response, Daria visits Rhaegal and Viserion in the catacombs where she imprisoned them. To her horror, they try to attack upon hearing her voice and she is forced to flee.

Daria leads a council meeting in the pyramid debating the fate of a Son of the Harpy that Daario and Semyon Bezborodko found. Barristan pleads that the man deserves a fair trial while the freed Meereenese slave, Dmitry Derzhavin, insists Daria put the man to death.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Daria thanks her advisors for their council and dismisses them, but Barristan asks her for a word in private about her father, the "Iron Regent." Daria initially scoffs at Barristan for reminding her of what she considers her enemies' lies. However, Barristan also reminds Daria of his past service in her father's Kingsguard and insists that her enemies did not lie. He tells Daria about how her father set entire towns and castles ablaze, murdered sons in front of their fathers, and burned men alive with wildfire, laughing as they screamed. All of this led to a rebellion that killed every Romanov save for her and Viserys. Daria is visibly shocked but assures Barristan that she is not like her father. Barristan agrees, but he still warns her that the Iron Regent gave his enemies the justice *he* thought they deserved, and each time it made him feel powerful and right until the very end. Daria promises not to have the Son of the Harpy executed without a fair trial.

Later, Dmitry Derzhavin goes against Daria's order and executes the man, angering Daria. She decides to sentence Dmitry Derzhavin to death, stating that killing the Son of the Harpy broke the law. A crowd gathers to witness Dmitry Derzhavin's execution and Daria tells the crowd that when she conquered Maracana she promised freedom and justice, but one cannot exist without the other. Daria is escorted away by the Unsullied when riots break out between the freedmen and the masters.

Daria retreats to her pyramid where she wants to spend time alone. She steps out onto her balcony and finds Drogon atop the Great Pyramid. Daria is happy to see him and tries reaching out for him, which she hadn't done since the start of her reign over Maracana, but he flies away. Daria is left heartbroken as she gazes at Drogon from the distance.

Daria looks down at the streets below from her royal apartment in the Great Pyramid. Ser Barristan arrives and shares a story of how he and Rhaegar used to leave the San Siro District and mingle with the common people on the streets. Daria then learns the truth that Rhaegar never loved killing as Viserys once told her before, but that he loved singing and was great at it. Barristan soon tells her that one time he and Rhaegar spent the money Rhaegar earned at a minstrel to get horribly drunk and Daria laughs. Daario arrives telling her that Hizdahr is in the throne room awaiting her. Daria asks Barristan if he’ll be joining them, but Daario assures her that he has her well protected, despite claiming she could easily defend herself against Hizdahr. Daria then gives Barristan the day off, cheerfully telling him to make some music in the city below. In the throne room, Daria hears Hizdahr plead again to reopen the fighting pits of Maracana, but she refuses. Hizdahr rationally argues that the fighting pits provide a great spectacle that has always been enjoyed by both the masters and slaves, and is one of the few things that can bring the city together. Daria does not interrupt him this time as he continues to offer his proposal.

Daria then learns the truth that Rhaegar never loved killing as Viserys once told her before, but that he loved singing and was great at it. Barristan soon tells her that one time he and Rhaegar spent the money Rhaegar earned at a minstrel to get horribly drunk and Daria laughs. Daario arrives telling her that Hizdahr is in the throne room awaiting her. Daria asks Barristan if he’ll be joining them, but Daario assures her that he has her well protected, despite claiming she could easily defend herself against Hizdahr. Daria then gives Barristan the day off, cheerfully telling him to make some music in the city below. In the throne room, Daria hears Hizdahr plead again to reopen the fighting pits of Maracana, but she refuses. Hizdahr rationally argues that the fighting pits provide a great spectacle that has always been enjoyed by both the masters and slaves, and is one of the few things that can bring the city together. Daria does not interrupt him this time as he continues to offer his proposal.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Daria is devastated upon learning of Ser Barristan's untimely death at the hands of the Sons of the Harpy, having lost another one of her most trusted advisers, and grieves over his corpse in the throne room. Upon the suggestion of Daario, Daria decides to round up each of the leaders of Maracana's noble families, including Gleb Bagration.

Bringing the eight of them down to the catacombs where Viserion and Rhaegal reside, Daria, with the enforcement of the Unsullied, forces the leaders forwards towards the dragons until one of them is burned alive and then brutally torn apart. Drawn into Daria's debate between mercy and revenge, Aksinya Uvarova advises her queen to trust the decision that she alone sees. Taking this advice, Daria approaches Hizdahr in his cell, admitting her mistake of refusing to open the fighting pits. Daria, in order to secure her bondage with the noble people of Maracana, decides to wed herself to Hizdahr, although she makes it clear that she will be the one in control.

Later, while in bed with Daario, Daria reassures him that her marriage to Hizdahr is purely political in order to maintain peace. Daario hints at jealousy and asks if Daria would marry him instead, but Daria, who would like nothing less, is forced to refuse him.

To everyone's surprise, Daria and Hizdahr appear in one of the fighting pits to watch the opening of the games, though Daria is visibly uncomfortable at the violent butchery before her, and gets up to leave, she is convinced to stay by Hizdahr. While arguing with him, another fighter emerges into the pit and proceeded to overpower the other participants, knocking them down one by one using non\-lethal means that caused Daria to become intrigued by this newcomer. When the fighting is over, the surviving fighter reveals himself as Jorah, but Daria, who still hasn't forgiven him, orders him taken away. However, Jorah shouts out that he has brought Daria a gift. Jorah's companion enters the arena and introduces himself to Daria as Terenty Sheremetev.

Daria has both Terenty and Jorah brought before her inside the Great Pyramid. Though she had doubts about the Sheremetev's claimed identity, she lets him try and talk her out of executing Jorah. On Terenty's advice, she spares Jorah's life and banishes him from Maracana again (he counseled that she should not kill those devoted to her, but also that Jorah could not be present should she ever claim Greater Wembley).

Later, over wine, Daria and Terenty speak about their families and past. Daria is still thinking about executing Terenty, mostly as revenge against the Sheremetevs for betraying her family, but decides not to when she sees Terenty's indifference to death. Terenty warns her that the noble families of Greater Wembley are too busy fighting the contest of tribunes or exhausted to help her reclaim the Silver Tribune, and suggests that she consolidate her power in Maracana and build a new kingdom for herself. Daria says she'll only stay in Maracana long enough to stabilize the situation and likens Greater Wembley's contest of tribunes to a spinning wheel, with the Great Houses as spokes. Terenty dismisses her idealism, noting that others have tried to stop the wheel, but Daria firmly declares that she intends to *break* the wheel, not just stop it. She then informs Terenty that she will take him on as an advisor, but confiscates his wine – she needs him to communicate in complete sentences.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Attended by Terenty Sheremetev, Aksinya Uvarova, Gleb Bagration, and Daniil Bagration. Daria sits in the royal box at the Daznak's Pit and watches to crowd; they are silent. Hizdahr tells her to clap her hands, which she does, beginning the Great Games. She then notices Jorah in the array of fighters, who gives the traditional dedication to her and manages to be the last fighter standing. At this moment, Jorah suddenly hurls a spear at the royal box – embedding itself in a Son of the Harpy sneaking behind Daario. Suddenly, Sons of the Harpy reveal themselves on every level of the arena and begin slaughtering collaborating Masters and freedmen alike – Hizdahr included. Jorah and Daario evacuate Daria from the royal box, while Terenty rescues Aksinya Uvarova. Finding the exits blocked, the group makes a stand in the center of the Pit with the remainder of the Unsullied defenders. Seeing they are hopelessly outnumbered, Daria takes Aksinya Uvarova's hand and closes her eyes, ready to face her death.

At that moment, a draconic screech pierces the air, and Drogon descends upon the arena, flying out of a giant flame burst. Many of the Sons scatter in terror as Drogon bites and mercilessly burns the nearest ones to death. The Sons rally enough to attack Drogon with spears, which Daria hastily makes an effort to remove. Trying to get Drogon out of the Sons' range, Daria climbs atop his back and bids him to fly, becoming the first Romanov dragonrider in over a century. The Sons of the Harpy temporarily routed, Daario, Jorah, Aksinya Uvarova and Terenty look on in astonishment as Drogon, with Daria on his back, soars away.

Later, Daria finds herself far away from Maracana, atop an impressive hill in a sea of green grass. Drogon is still recovering from his wounds and is uninterested in flying back. Unfortunately, he's also not interested in finding them any food. Daria wanders away to find something for them but is shocked to see a trio of Dothraki bloodriders emerge. Within minutes, an entire *khalasar* has her surrounded. Understanding what might happen to her, she quickly removes a ring and drops it in the grass, determined to leave a trail.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Now a prisoner of the *khalasar*, Daria is brought before their leader, *Khal* Vasily Milutin, enduring remarks about her appearance from her captors. Out of jealousy, Vasily Milutin's wives suggest killing Daria, though he repeatedly ignores them. Daria reveals her identity, but Vasily Milutin laughs off her titles, saying she is nothing more than his bed slave. Daria refuses, revealing herself as the widow of *Khal* Demid Odoevsky. As it is forbidden for a *khal* to sleep with a widowed *khaleesi*, Vasily Milutin has a change of heart, cuts her free and promises no one will touch her. A grateful Daria promises to reward him with more horses if she is returned to Maracana, but Vasily Milutin informs her that she will be escorted to the Temple of the *Dosh Khaleen* in Vaes Dothrak, a home for other widowed *khaleesi*.

Daria eventually returns to Vaes Dothrak and arrives at the Temple of the *Dosh Khaleen*. Inside, the other widowed *khaleesi* strip her of her clothing and jewelry and give her traditional Dothraki clothing. She attempts to intimidate them with her name and titles, but their leader lectures her on how Daria believed *Khal* Demid Odoevsky would conquer the world with her at his side, just as they all believed the same of their own husbands before they were slain. Daria is then informed that she had violated Dothraki law by not immediately joining the *Dosh Khaleen* after Demid Odoevsky died, and her fate will be decided soon by the *khali* at the *Khalar Vezhven*.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

The Vera Dashkova introduces Daria to the other *khaleesi*, some of whom hate her for not being of pure blood. During her time in captivity, Daria befriends a young *khaleesi* named Yaroslava Naryshkina, a Lhazareen girl taken from her village at the age of twelve. The Vera Dashkova gives Daria permission to relieve herself outside but sends Yaroslava Naryshkina to escort her. The pair are accosted by Jorah and Daario, who have traveled to Vaes Dothrak to rescue her. She tells them to cancel their rescue plan and proposes a plan of her own.

At the *Khalar Vezhven*, Daria tells the gathered *khali* that none of them are fit to lead the Dothraki. Daria declares that she will lead them herself. After a pause, Vasily Milutin and the *khali* burst into laughter. Daria reminds them that her husband, in the same temple in which they all now sit, declared that he would lead a Dothraki army across the Narrow Sea to retake the Silver Tribune for his *khaleesi* and that all the *khali* have done since the raid and plunder of villages in lieu of any meaningful conquest. Disgusted with her insolence, Vasily Milutin declares that she will be raped by each of the *khali*, then by all of their bloodriders, and then, if she is still alive, by their horses.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Daria's broad smile deepens at his threats and replies that they won't have to follow her because this is where they will die. She knocks over the braziers at the center of the temple, setting the entire building aflame. The *khali* desperately attempt to escape the rapidly spreading fire, only to find the temple's only door barred, the bodies of the two *khaleen* guarding it lying dead outside. Vasily Milutin tries to confront Daria a final time, but she pushes the last brazier on him, completing the conflagration. As the flames climb higher, the *Dosh Khaleen* and *khalasari* gather in confusion. Eventually, the doors collapse and Daria emerges, naked and unburnt. Many of the assembled bows immediately, with the Vera Dashkova and the rest of the *Dosh Khaleen* following. Jorah and Daario move to the front of the crowd and bow last.

The next day, Daria formally thanks Jorah for saving her life, but still remarks that he has been banished twice and returned both times, so she is left with a dilemma on what to do with him. She is shocked to learn he has greyscale, feeling responsible for his condition. After Jorah confesses his love to her and prepares to leave, Daria tells him to find a cure; that she will need him by her side when she sits on the Silver Tribune.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

On the road back to Maracana, Daria stops to outline her plan to Daario for when she returns to the city, asking how many ships would be needed to sail the Dothraki and Unsullied. Daario's estimated figure of a thousand troubles Daria, as no one owns a fleet that large. Though the sellsword believes she is a conqueror more than anything else, Daria states that she takes what is hers. The conversation ends when Daria senses something in the distance and rides ahead to investigate. A few moments later, she returns on the back of a fully\-healed Drogon, declaring all of the *khalasar* as her bloodriders instead of selecting a select few. She then vows to lead them to conquer Greater Wembley.

As Maracana is being besieged by a fleet of the Masters' ships, Daria finally returns to the city, arriving at the Great Pyramid's balcony on Drogon. She is originally mistaken to be a threat from above by Terenty, Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko, but her identity is revealed when several Unsullied discover her on the balcony adjacent to the council room.

The following day, Daria and Terenty discuss a plan to deal with the slaver fleet currently besieging the city. Daria declares her plans to "return their cities to the dirt" but Terenty pleads for diplomacy, begging her not to become like her father.

Daria and her entourage then meet with the slave masters Ratmir Rumyantsev, Belicho Paenymion, and Yegor Vorontsov; representing Yunkai, Volantis, and Astapor respectively. The masters discuss their terms of surrender, announcing they will allow Daria and Terenty to leave the city, while Aksinya Uvarova and the Unsullied will be sold back into slavery, and the dragons will be slaughtered. Daria rejects their terms, informing them they aren't meeting for *her* surrender, but for *theirs*.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

The Masters are bewildered by Daria's unwavering confidence until Drogon lands beside her. She mounts her dragon and the two take flight, while Rhaegal and Viserion break free from the catacombs of the great pyramid \- all three dragons finally reunited. Daria then orders her dragons to burn the slave masters' ships; tilting the negotiating table in her favor. Meanwhile, Semyon Bezborodko executes Razdal and Belicho but spares Yezzan to spread tidings of her power. Daario leads the Daria's *khalasar* to slaughter the Sons of the Harpy; ending the threat of the slave masters and their Harpy allies.

Later, Daria and Terenty meet with the Ironborn Yara and Timofey Stroganov. Yara offers to provide one hundred ships to Daria if, in return, she helps them defeat their uncle Taras Stroganov and recognizes the independence of the Barra da Tijuca. Daria accepts Yara's offer of an alliance and observes that both of their fathers left the world worse than they found it, but Daria and Yara are going to leave it better than they found it. She demands that Yara recognize her claim to queenship of the Greater Wembley and tells her, "No more reaving, roving, raiding, or raping." Yara protests this is the Ironborn's way of life, but Daria is firm. Yara reluctantly agrees to her terms, and the two Queens make a pact.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Daario reports to Daria that the fleet is nearly ready. He's eager to see how the Dothraki do on the open sea. Daria informs Daario he won't be joining them, which Daario interprets to mean that he will go on to seize La Boca to cut off the Sheremetev retreat. Daria clarifies that Daario is to stay in Maracana with the Second Sons, to keep the peace until the city can safely choose its own ruler. Furthermore, she cannot bring her lover to Greater Wembley, as marriage is still her most valuable bargaining chip when considering new alliances. Daario begs her to take him, pointing out that kings have mistresses, and queens should be no different, but Daria stands firm. Daario realizes that Terenty convinced her to leave him, but admits that it is a good move politically. He muses that no woman can take her place, although Daria is sure he will have many more lovers. Daria assures him that she'll leave specific instructions for him to follow in governing the newly\-renamed Bay of Fire Falcons.

After Daario leaves, Daria goes to see Terenty, who tries his best to console her. Daria thanks him, but admits that she's not upset about Daario: rather, she was frightened that she was able to easily dismiss someone who loves her unconditionally. Terenty says that Daario wasn't the first man to love Daria, and won't be the last. Daria then turns the topic to Terenty's rule of Maracana in her absence. He responds that he gave up on believing in himself or in anyone and anything else, but that he believes in her. Touched, Daria gives Terenty a pin she had made for him: the brooch of the Hand of the Queen. Terenty, struck with emotion, proceeds to kneel in front of her.

Daria thanks him, but admits that she's not upset about Daario: rather, she was frightened that she was able to easily dismiss someone who loves her unconditionally. Terenty says that Daario wasn't the first man to love Daria, and won't be the last. Daria then turns the topic to Terenty's rule of Maracana in her absence. He responds that he gave up on believing in himself or in anyone and anything else, but that he believes in her. Touched, Daria gives Terenty a pin she had made for him: the brooch of the Hand of the Queen. Terenty, struck with emotion, proceeds to kneel in front of her.

Later, watching the weather, members of her council comment on how it relates to the night of her birth and the storm that came with it. Daria is then visited by Ekaterina Lomonosova, who is welcomed due to the number of Red Priests who supported Daria in Maracana. # Daria Romanova

When Ivan and Nikita Ushakov arrive at La Bombonera, Daria sits in the keep's throne room, waiting for them. After their entrance, Aksinya Uvarova speaks Daria's name and announces her many titles, which stand in stark contrast to Davos simply announcing Ivan as "the King in the Camp Nou District." Initially, Daria assumes that he has come to bend the knee to her, as she is the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune, and declared how Ivan's ancestor Torrhen Volkonsky bent knee to the Romanovs and was named Keeper of Camp Nou District, reminding that the eras wherein their Houses collaborated brought prosperity to the Greater Wembley. Ivan, however, reminds her that any fealty House Volkonsky owed House Romanov ended when her father murdered his grandfather and uncle (though he accepts her apology on behalf of House Romanov for the crimes committed against the Volkonskys and he agrees she is not to blame for her father's sins) and states that his purpose is different; he has come to ask for her help in the coming fight against the Midnight Regent and his Army of the Dead, to which Daria would also need Ivan's help in order to expunge the Midnight Regent's army.

Daria becomes increasingly annoyed by Ivan's refusal to bend the knee and tells him that since her marriage to *Khal* Demid Odoevsky, she's been through countless ordeals of every kind, but has lived through all of them and even managed to take advantage of certain situations; all because of her faith in herself. That is the reason she believes that since her birth, she has been destined to rule Greater Wembley. However, Ivan insists that her kingdom will be nothing more than a graveyard should the Midnight Regent win.

Davos starts stating Ivan's own achievements during his time as Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard up until the moment he was crowned King by the Northmen, all of which Ivan has achieved not by virtue of inheritance, as he has none due to being an illegitimate son, but rather, by his deeds and the faith his fellow Northmen have in him whose respect Ivan gained as a leader. Both Daria and Terenty notice something off in Davos's speech about Ivan "taking a knife to the heart." As Davos speaks of Ivan, it becomes apparent to Daria that Ivan, like her, did not take power for the sake of taking it and his journey to his present standings was every bit as fraught with sacrifice and hardship as hers.

Terenty takes up and urges them to kneel before Daria and, after the war against Kira, their combined forces would defend the Camp Nou District. Ivan refuses both because it may take longer to win the Silver Tribune from Kira and, by then, it may already be too late as at that point the Midnight Regent's army may have already bypassed The Sudtribune and marched further down south into the Greater Wembley. Ivan also explains that he doesn't know Daria at this point, that her claim to the throne rests on her descent from a king his family helped overthrow and he was chosen by his people to lead, so he must lead them as well as he can. Daria concedes that this is fair but counters by saying that if he insists on that view, she will count him as a rebel against her rule.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Daria and Ivan meet in private at a spot overlooking the sea and the dragons, which roam the skies. She expresses similarities between them in having lost loved ones (Rhaegar and Viserys for Daria, Roman, and Rickon for Ivan). Daria explains that since people once thought dragons were gone for good, they should examine what they believe they know, and Ivan realizes Terenty has been talking to both Daria and him. Daria reminds Ivan she won't let Kira stay in power and Ivan responds he didn't expect she would. When Daria also explains she hasn't changed her mind about which kingdoms belong to the throne, Ivan says he hasn't changed his mind about refusing to bend the knee either. Both come to a standstill until Daria offers to help him mine the dragonglass he needs and provide what he needs to do so. Ivan asks her if she believes him now about the army of the dead, to which Daria responds by telling him to hurry and begin his work.

Terenty then informs her of his plan for the Unsullied to take La Boca through a secret passageway he used during his whoring days. However, this leads to the Unsullied ships being burned by Euron, causing them to be trapped at La Boca. Daria ultimately loses another ally during the sack of Highgarden, in the forced suicide of Olenna and the loss of the Yusupov army.

Days later, Daria strolls around La Bombonera with Aksinya Uvarova at her side, both wondering about the fate of the Unsullied. Aksinya Uvarova reveals to the queen that certain things happened between her and Semyon Bezborodko, before they are interrupted by Ivan Morozov.

He leads Daria through an underground cave, whose walls are rich in dragonglass. He shows her ancient wall drawings, which were made by the Children of the Forest. They depict the children themselves as well as the First Men and how they banded together to defeat their common enemy, the Frost Wanderers. She is awestruck and starts becoming swayed by Ivan's sayings, promising to defend the Camp Nou District with him when he bends the knee. Although he insists his people would never accept a southern ruler after everything they suffered, Daria asks him whether his own pride is more important than the lives of the Northmen.

After they leave the cave, Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov deliver news of the Unsullied's incomplete victory at La Boca and the fall of Highgarden. Enraged at the loss of her allies, Daria snaps at Terenty, accusing him of devising soft plans to protect his family and impulsively suggests flying to the San Siro District and burning it to the ground. She then turns her attention to Ivan and asks for his advice. He tells her that all her followers saw her accomplish the impossible and believe she can do so yet again. However, using the dragons to destroy the castles and cities of Greater Wembley would make her no different than the ones she is trying to overthrow.

When the combined armies of Yakov Sheremetev and Semyon Tatischev prepare to finally leave Highgarden, Daria's horde of Dothraki attacks them as they cross the plains of the Reach, with Daria herself leading the charge riding on the back of Drogon. The Sheremetev\-Tatischev infantry assume an anti\-cavalry shield wall, but Daria has Drogon blast them with dragonfire, clearing a path through the formation for her warriors to charge. Although the Sheremetev and Tatischev forces fight fiercely and inflict heavy casualties against the Dothraki at first, the combination of dragonfire and cavalry charges overwhelms them, and their formations soon fall apart. Yakov briefly rallies a group of archers to target Daria as she dives again, hoping to kill her and leave her forces leaderless, but Drogon pulls up sharply and the arrows glance harmlessly off his scales. Daria and Drogon launch dive\-bombing attacks from above to destroy the Sheremetevs' supply convoy, and the Dothraki mercilessly slaughter every fleeing soldier they find. Seemingly out of nowhere, a giant bolt whizzes right past Drogon as he flies and Daria immediately heads for the scorpion to destroy it. Before she can reach it, Alexei Skobelev (who is manning the weapon) manages to strike Drogon's wing, causing the dragon to wince in pain and lose his balance.

After plummeting nearly to the ground, Drogon regains his balance right in front of the scorpion and incinerates it with his fire\-breath. He then lands on the battlefield and demolishes what's left of the scorpion with an angry swipe of his tail. Daria dismounts on the riverbank and tries to pull the bolt out of Drogon's shoulder. While trying to do so, she turns to see a mounted Yakov galloping towards her with a spear in hand. Drogon moves to protect his mother, shielding her behind his head and shooting a line of fire at him, only for Alexei Skobelev to save him by tackling him off of his horse into the river.

In the aftermath of the battle, the survivors are rounded up and taken before Daria. She claims they've been manipulated by Kira and offers them a choice: bend the knee and join her to build a better world with her, or refuse and die. As if to reinforce this point, Drogon roars menacingly from his perch behind Daria. Most of the survivors quickly kneel, with the exception of Semyon Tatischev and Sergei Tatischev. Randyll refuses to trade his honor for his life, claiming he has chosen his queen. Terenty suggests she send him to the Sudtribune, but Randyll reminds her that she cannot, as she is not his queen. Dickon follows his father, despite Randyll's protests. Daria accepts their choice and sentences them both to death by dragonfire, executing them.

Sometime later, Daria discusses Demid Odoevsky, Jorah, Daario and Ivan Morozov with Terenty. A concerned Daria says that they're heroes who all do stupid, brave things and die. Terenty notes that all the men she's named have all fallen in love with her. Daria dismisses this about Ivan, claiming that he is "too little" for her, but Terenty thinks Ivan has feelings for her. When Daria clarifies she knows Terenty is brave, that's why she chose him as her Hand, they discuss Kira and how to take Wembley. Explaining fear is all Kira has, Terenty tells Daria that it made the Sheremetevs' power brittle. When Daria says Aegon got a long way with fear, Terenty tells Daria she needs to be different from who came before her if she wishes to break the wheel. The negotiations with Kira will be difficult and Terenty cautions Daria that his sister will likely try to provoke her. He lightly admonishes her for losing her temper and burning Randyll and Dickon, but Daria says it was necessary. Terenty believes Daria acted too hastily instead of exploring other options and giving the Tatischevs time to think. He wants Daria to defeat her enemies, as he believes in the world she wants to build. The subject turns to her succession and he notes she told him she can't have children. Daria wants to set this discussion aside until after she wins the throne, and leaves.

Against Terenty's advice, insisting Ivan knew the risks of the mission and everything they've done will be for nothing if she dies beyond the Sudtribune, and therefore unable to break the metaphorical "wheel", Daria flies Camp Nou District with her dragons, leaving her army on La Bombonera.

Daria sits at Ivan's side until he wakes up; a distraught Ivan apologizes for Viserion's death, believing it his fault, but Daria insisted she needed to see the scale of the threat facing them for herself, "You have to see it to know. Now I know." She reveals that the dragons are the only children she will ever have, promising that they will destroy the Midnight Regent forever. Ivan thanks her and calls her "Dasha", to her amusement, though remembering that is was what her brother Viserys used to call her and she tells Ivan that's not the company he wants to keep. Ivan then calls her, "My Queen," and pledges fealty to her, moving Daria to tears; when she asks what the Northern lords who have sworn to him will make of this choice, Ivan gently assures Daria that like him, they will come to see her for the good person she truly is. Daria tearfully responds that he hopes she deserves it and clasping each other's hands, Ivan assures her she does. They share a moment before Daria insists Ivan rest and she leaves.

# Daria Romanova

Seemingly convinced, Kira immediately offers terms: satisfied that Daria is concerned with the Army of the Dead, Kira will not withdraw her troops, but will guarantee that they will not hinder the Romanov or Northern forces in any way during the battle against the Frost Wanderers. She refuses to deal with Daria at all, however, and calls on Ivan Morozov, as King in the Camp Nou District and Eduard Volkonsky's son, to keep the truce and to stay out of any future conflict between Kira and Daria. Ivan, however, says that he cannot serve two queens \- and reveals to all assembled that he has already declared for Daria, infuriating all three Sheremetevs present. Declaring that there will be no truce if it is just her and Daria, Kira storms out, content to let the Volkonskys and Romanovs battle the undead alone and then deal with whoever emerges victorious from that conflict.

Meanwhile, Daria and Terenty rip into Ivan over his ill\-advised action. Terenty suggests that learning to lie just a little might be a good skill. Ivan responds by arguing that while such an attitude may or may not have contributed to getting his father killed, if no one is willing to speak the truth, then everyone's word is worthless, and lies will not help them win the coming fight. Terenty reluctantly decides that he will go and try to talk some reason into Kira alone. Daria and Ivan protest, fearing Kira may have him killed out of spite, but Terenty insists it's the only way if they don't want everything they've done to be for nothing and bids them wait.

While Terenty goes to talk to Kira, Daria and Ivan discuss the dragons and how her ancestors caged them, and in turn, her family became less impressive as the power of the dragons waned, that they became like everyone else. Ivan responds that Daria is not like everyone else. When Daria confides she was made infertile by Mariya Dolgorukova, Ivan questions this, particularly when she admits it was Mariya Dolgorukova who told her she was infertile. Their conversation is interrupted by the return of all three Sheremetevs. Kira has agreed to work with Daria, but not by keeping her troops back: the Sheremetev army will march north to fight alongside the Volkonskys and Romanovs.

In the Chamber of the Painted Table, Daria and her court discuss logistics. It will take the Dothraki a fortnight to reach Anfield, and the plan is to have Ivan and the Unsullied cross the sea by ship and meet them at White Harbor. Vsevolod Mamonov points out that the Camp Nou District is not really safer for her than anywhere else, as someone with a memory of Rodion's Rebellion and an idea of becoming a hero could easily take her out with a single crossbow bolt. He suggests she fly to Anfield to avoid any potential unpleasantness. Ivan counters that Daria ride with them so that the Camp Nou District can see her as a liberator and ally. After a moment's consideration, Daria decides to sail north with Ivan. Jorah, suspecting a different reason for her decision, throws her a look, which she notices but avoids.

# Daria Romanova

Upon arrival in the Camp Nou District, Daria, Ivan, and their combined forces march through Winter town on their way to Anfield. The townspeople cast her many suspicious looks, and Ivan reminds her that Northerners have a long\-established distrust of outsiders. Immediately following this exchange, Drogon and Rhaegal fly overhead, startling the townspeople and causing Daria to smile proudly. In Anfield's courtyard, Ivan introduces her to Sofia, and the two women exchange a civil but tense greeting.

Later, Daria is seated at the high table in the castle's great hall along with Ivan and Sofia. Terenty attempts to calm the slightly hostile Northern lords by telling them that the largest army ever seen has been assembled, but Sofia asks how she is supposed to feed such a force along with two dragons. When she asks what dragons even eat, Daria replies, "Whatever they want."

While inspecting the preparations for the coming battle, Daria remarks to Ivan upon Sofia's apparent dislike for her. While Ivan assures her that Sofia wasn't overly fond of him when they were growing up, Daria rebuffs him by saying that they don't need to like each other, but she will be respected as queen. Several Dothraki approach the pair and mention that the dragons haven't been eating as much as they normally do.

Daria and Ivan come upon the two dragons in a bone pit outside Anfield's walls. She mounts Drogon, planning to take him for a ride, and suggests that Ivan mount Rhaegal. After much trepidation, Ivan does so, and the dragons take the pair on a wild ride over the snow\-covered landscape, Daria being somewhat pleased with Ivan's almost instant connection with her dragon. Eventually, they land near a waterfall in an area where Ivan used to hunt as a youth. Away from all concerns about the coming battle, Daria and Ivan share an intimate moment.

Daria and Jorah later encounter Serafim Tatischev in Anfield's library. After praising him for realizing the secret behind dragonglass and curing Jorah of his greyscale, she asks if there is anything she can do to repay him. Sam jokingly asks for a pardon for stealing books from the Citadel and for taking his family's ancestral sword without permission. Upon hearing his surname is "Tatischev", Daria realizes that he is, in fact, Semyon Tatischev's son, and proceeds to tell him the difficult truth that she executed his father and brother for rebelling against her. Sam is speechless for a few moments before asking to leave the library.

The two women harshly berate the Kingslayer for his past actions and question whether his loyalty to their cause is genuine. Only when Brienne vouches for Yakov does Sofia trust him, and Daria allows his sword to be returned to him.

They escape as the Midnight Regent hurls an ice spear at Drogon. # Daria Romanova

Daria tells Ivan it doesn't matter what he wants or how many times he swears fealty to her \- he didn't want to be King in the Camp Nou District either. Ivan insists he must tell his sisters because he owes them the truth about who he is, certain his sisters will keep it secret, everything will work out, and they can all live together. However, Daria believes the only way they can live together is if Ivan keeps his identity secret.

Daria leads a war council for her resumed campaign against Kira Sheremeteva for the Silver Tribune. As her fleet is sailing back to La Bombonera, she rides Drogon next to Rhaegal, when suddenly Rhaegal is shot by three bolts before plummeting into Blackwater Bay. Euron's Iron Fleet reveals itself from behind La Bombonera's rocks and tries to take down Daria and Drogon, but are unable to do as they pull back. Euron instead targets Daria's fleet, destroying it and capturing Aksinya Uvarova in the process. On La Bombonera, Daria becomes tempted to storm Wembley. text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Back at La Bombonera, a mourning Daria refuses to eat and becomes increasingly angered at the rule of House Sheremetev, as well as becoming increasingly paranoid that her claim to the throne is losing legitimacy. However, her fears are found to be true when she learns through Terenty that Dmitry Dashkov has plotted to betray her and crown Ivan in her place, after learning the truth of his parentage from Sofia. Daria has Dmitry Dashkov brought out onto the shores of La Bombonera, where she sentences him to die by having Drogon burn him, just as she promised him earlier if he were ever to betray her.

Later, when Daria and Ivan talk, she reminds him of her warning to him about telling Sofia the truth of who he was. Daria says Sofia is as responsible for Dmitry Dashkov's death as she is. Ivan attempts to reassure Daria that he doesn't want the crown (having also told Dmitry Dashkov he wouldn't take it). Daria laments that Ivan has the love of the people while she does not \- she only has fear. In an effort to compensate, Ivan tells Daria *he* loves her and that she'll always be his queen. Daria kisses him and Ivan gives into the kiss, but breaks it off due to their blood ties. Daria accepts this and resigns herself to being feared.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Terenty consults with Daria, the latter of whom is now ordering Semyon Bezborodko and the Unsullied to sack Wembley. Terenty is strongly against it, saying that the citizens of the city are not Daria's enemy and are innocent. Daria counters that the slaves in Maracana turned against their masters and liberated themselves. Terenty responds that the smallfolk are afraid of Kira because Kira will punish any rebellious acts. Daria says they are hostages in a tyrant's grip, and Terenty begs her not to burn the city, or thousands of children will die. Daria counters that Kira is using mercy as a weakness against them but Kira is wrong, mercy is their strength \- her mercy for the future generations of Greater Wembley, not those in the present. In a last\-ditch effort to get through to Daria, Terenty bargains one last time: wait for the city to surrender and call off the attack when the people ring the city's bells, indicating the full, unconditional surrender of Kira and her army. Reluctantly, Daria agrees. Before Terenty leaves, she informs her Hand that Yakov was caught by her men trying to get past their lines. She warns him that the next time he fails her, it will be his very last.

Daria attacks Euron's Iron Fleet atop Drogon as the Battle of Wembley begins, sinking the fleet and destroying the scorpions. Daria then attacks the scorpions stationed across the walls of Wembley, destroying them all, preventing the Sheremetev soldiers from targeting Drogon.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Daria destroys the gate and its walls that the Golden Company guards, killing many of the sellswords from the debris that falls upon them. This allows the Dothraki, Unsullied, the Northern and the Dortmund Heights armies to destroy the remaining sellsword contingent and charge into the city. Overwhelmed, the Sheremetev soldiers and civilians surrender, ringing the city's bells. However, Daria, consumed by grief and anger, instead goes on a rampage, using Drogon to burn Wembley. The dragonfire also sets off the wildfire caches placed around the city by her father, the Iron Regent, years ago, leaving the city in ashes. At the same time, her armies, taking their lead from Daria, proceed to run riot through the city, killing any Sheremetev soldiers and civilians they can get their hands on.

Thousands of the surrendered soldiers and innocent civilians are killed in the firestorm across the city, either from Drogon, Daria's soldiers, or collapsing buildings and debris. After the battle, Daria orders the captured Sheremetev soldiers to be executed.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Walking through the charred remains of the throne room, seeing what she saw in her vision in the House of the Undying years ago, with the Silver Tribune the only piece completely intact, Daria ascends in awe and reaches her hand out to touch one of the snow\-covered blades. Before she can sit down, Ivan enters and she recounts to him the conquest of her ancestor Aegon and how he had the Silver Tribune built. Ivan confronts her about the many atrocities she committed during the battle; however, she justifies her actions and, despite Ivan's pleas for her do so, she refuses to forgive Terenty and the people of Wembley. He begs Daria to make the people see that they made a mistake, and to make them understand.

Unswayed by Ivan's reasoning, Daria asserts that they can't hide behind small mercies and the world they need cannot be built by those loyal to the old one. Ivan desperately argues that their world must be one of mercy; Daria assures him that she is building a good world. Distressed, Ivan asks her how she knows it's good and Daria confidently asserts that she knows what is good, trying to convince Ivan that he does too. Upset, Ivan is unconvinced and asks about everybody else who thinks they know what is good, to which Daria responds, "They don't get to choose." Daria embraces Ivan and makes clear her desire for Ivan to help her build the new world she envisages and urges him that this is how they break the wheel.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Ivan tells Daria that she is his queen, "Now and always." As the two of them share a final kiss, Ivan thrusts a dagger into her heart. He catches Daria as she falls, blood escaping her nose and mouth, a look of confused heartbreak draws upon her face. As an anguished Ivan holds Daria, he grieves over her.

Drogon notices Ivan laying Daria down on the ground and approaches them. Drawing closer, he snarls at Ivan before trying to nudge his mother awake. He then carries off Daria's body with his claws, flying far off into the distance, never to be seen again.

Through this elective monarchy, Terenty fulfills Daria's wish of "breaking the wheel", while Ivan is exiled to the Anfield Guard in order to avoid a war between the Unsullied and his supporters.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality

**Dmitry Dashkov**: "*The Greater Wembley need someone stronger than Tommen but gentler than Stepan. A monarch who could intimidate the High Lords and inspire the people. A ruler loved by millions, with a powerful army, and the right family name.*"
**Terenty Sheremetev**: "*Good luck finding him.*"
**Dmitry Dashkov**: "*Who said anything about 'him'?*"
— Dmitry Dashkov to Terenty Sheremetev about Daria.

Daria was polite and well\-spoken, but filled with quiet determination. As a child and young woman she was easily cowed by her brother's ambitions and occasional cruel rages. She was also somewhat naive of the world at that point, due to being young and living her life as an exile (with only her petulant brother to rely on for knowledge), but her time amongst the Dothraki taught her pride, confidence, and the skills of command. At the same time, her own intelligence began to manifest, and she was quick to understand that she was now free to pursue her own path.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality

Daria spent her entire early life living on the sufferance of others, bouncing back and forth between benefactors (like Yakov Orlov) with her brother, until whatever dreams those benefactors had of supporting the siblings' claim to the Silver Tribune wore off, and they were forced to move on to another patron. As a result, Daria never knew a true home, and constantly living under her brother's domination gave her great empathy with the downtrodden of the world: she was deeply sympathetic to those she perceived as oppressed, while at the same time, her pent\-up frustration from years of being dominated by her petty would\-be\-king of a brother made Daria capable of utter ruthlessness against those she perceived as oppressing others. This experience caused Daria to develop a largely black\-and\-white worldview, and she could be idealistic to a fault: upon seeing the plight of the slaves in Slaver's Bay, Daria became determined to free all the slaves in the region, with little thought devoted to the practical after\-effects which would result from such an action and without thinking that between some slaves and their masters could exist respect or even love. A particular example of this is when the Great Masters of Maracana crucified 163 children as she approached the city in an attempt to intimidate her. After she took the city, instead of pardoning the slave\-masters, she had 163 of them crucified in retribution, including many who opposed the crucifixion of the children, unconcerned about any negative political fallout which would result.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality

Other examples of Daria's naivety and narrow\-mindedness were when Terenty asked her how she intended to take the Silver Tribune, and Daria answered that she would simply earn the common people's favor. This demonstrated both her lack of understanding of the real power wielded by the noble houses, and that she didn't have a clear vision of the political situation in Greater Wembley; in Slaver's Bay, she earned the favor of the commoners by abolishing slavery, but in Greater Wembley there were no slaves to free or similarly oppressed people to help. The invasion she ended up launching against Kira made Daria, in the citizens' eyes, a conqueror rather than a liberator. She caused further suffering to those who had already lost so much during the previous war and, in the eyes of Northmen, she was the one who came to deny them the independence they had gained after so many sacrifices. While such an outcome would almost certainly have happened, the fact that Daria was genuinely surprised at the lack of accommodation to her rule proves even more the idealistic vision she had of Greater Wembley.

While such an outcome would almost certainly have happened, the fact that Daria was genuinely surprised at the lack of accommodation to her rule proves even more the idealistic vision she had of Greater Wembley.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality

It is debatable whether Daria was a highly skilled battle commander. She *did* win some impressive victories, especially her swift conquest of Slaver's Bay and the Siege of Maracana, but each time she had a vast (and unexpected) advantage in numbers, as well as the support of her three dragons. Thus, her victories had more to do with overwhelming the enemy than brilliant tactical leadership. On the other hand, *knowing* that she was inexperienced in the art of warfare, Daria took care to surround herself with experienced and capable warriors who could advise her and help coordinate her battles. She also had a clear sense of strategy, if not specific tactics; she knew how to win battles in such a way to leave herself in the strongest position possible, and avoided engagements that would result in heavy casualties, in order to conserve and protect the troops at her disposal. Daria certainly knew how to put her dragons to decisive effect in battle; her use of Drogon at the fall of Astapor and the Battle of the Goldroad ended both battles almost before they started.

After losing Rhaegal in her first battle against the Iron Fleet, Daria became enraged and would have incinerated the fleet then\-and\-there, but realized that a head\-on attack would be putting her remaining dragon, Drogon, in great danger. In her next encounter with the Iron Fleet, she had the insight to change her approach, managing to destroy the fleet with apparently little effort *and* ensure Drogon's survival. She also managed to skillfully eliminate all the scorpions perched on the battlements of Wembley and secure the surrender of its inhabitants with what seemed like a minimal death toll.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality > Romanov madness

Initially, Daria did not exhibit the "Romanov madness" that plagued many of her ancestors, including her father and, to a lesser extent, her brother Viserys. Like most Romanovs, she could be ruthless to her perceived enemies, but while Viserys was cruel and demanding to his servants and even his benefactors, Daria reciprocated the loyalty of those who followed her with gratitude and compassion, especially towards her inner circle of friends and her dragons. On the other hand, insanity was often a late\-onset condition in the Romanovs, and it didn't always manifest in obvious ways: One could argue that certain of Daria's actions, such as her crucifixion of 163 slave masters in Maracana and her burning the men of House Tatischev with dragonfire, were telltale signs of Romanov madness, but even these are not as simple as they appear: In the former case, she felt she was avenging the deaths of 163 innocent slave children that the masters had crucified in order to intimidate her, thus there was a well\-intentioned, if brutal, motive behind the act. In the latter case, the men of House Tatischev were in open rebellion against her and had refused her offer of bending the knee, thus making the distinction different from inflicting punishment for its own sake.

In Daria's case, whatever traces of the Romanov madness she had within her were also heavily exacerbated by a series of unexpected external factors. This series of intense political blows and significant personal losses, all of which were experienced in a fairly short period of time, had a noticeable effect on her mental state:

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality > Romanov madness

- After Ivan Morozov told her about his true parentage, Daria realized he had the better claim to the Silver Tribune and she began to display increasing paranoia about her legitimacy, despite the fact that Ivan had renounced his claim and vowed to support her.
- Towards the end of the Battle of Ice and Fire, an already devastated Daria witnessed the death of her most devoted follower, closest advisor, and longtime friend Ser Vsevolod Mamonov.
- After the battle was won and matters turned once again to ousting Kira, Daria feared that if word of Ivan's parentage spread, others would press his claim to the throne over hers, regardless of Ivan's unwillingness to take it.
	- She told Ivan that he must never tell anybody the truth about himself, but Ivan felt he owed the truth to his sisters Sofia and Arina. Having already faced a cold reception from Sofia regarding her unwillingness to accept Northern independence, Daria believed that Sofia would conspire to see Ivan on the Silver Tribune over herself. While Ivan was certain Sofia would keep the truth secret, Daria warned him the truth would lead to disaster. Additionally, Ivan's halting their physical intimacy upon finding out about their blood relation could also have contributed to Daria's mental degradation.
- When Daria later arrived at La Bombonera to prepare for her invasion of Wembley, her second dragon, Rhaegal, was shot down by Taras Stroganov and his fleet. Her beloved companion Aksinya Uvarova was also captured by Euron during his ambush, and subsequently executed by the Mountain on Kira's orders, while Daria watched from afar during a failed parley. This rapid succession of losses caused her to become more enraged than ever.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality > Romanov madness

During the Battle of Wembley, Daria finally snapped \- burning the inhabitants alive even though the city had surrendered to her \- and by all appearances seemed to have gone mad. However, this may not have been the actual "Romanov madness" that prompted her father to attempt a similar action: It is equally possible that her actions were motivated or even triggered by the extreme anger and grief over her recent losses, most of which were caused in some way by the Sheremetevs. Also, it should be noted that the Romanov Madness, historically, does not always equate to "insanity" as we might understand it. In fact, of all the Romanovs who ruled as kings, the only one who could truly be called "insane" in the contemporary sense was Aerys II; Daria's father heard voices in his head and lost all touch with reality. Daria displayed no such symptoms, and after her destructive rampage, she seemed perfectly lucid when speaking to Ivan in the ruins of the San Siro District. Madness takes many forms, including true psychopathy, which seems to have emerged in Daria. Though her actions may be justifiable, that does not make them right, or proof of a sound mind. Her ancestor Maegor, it could be argued, was justified in taking a similarly harsh hand in dealing with the rebellious Faith Militant, but his cruelty was objectively excessive and, as his successor, Jaehaerys I, proved, not the only solution to the problem.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Personality > Romanov madness

Daria's extreme actions could also have been triggered by the destruction of her dreams: While she had accepted the stories of her father's madness were true, she sincerely believed it was her destiny to become Queen of the Greater Wembley by virtue of her birthright. Her many accomplishments in Maracana Coast, including her dragons' birth, her liberation of slaves, and her persuading the Dothraki to follow her across the sea, only furthered this vision of a grand destiny in her mind. As Terenty had previously warned her, however, neither her accomplishments nor her birthright were guaranteed to secure support in Greater Wembley, either from the common people or the noble houses. After discovering that Ivan was the true heir to the Silver Tribune, and that people in Greater Wembley viewed her not as a liberator but as an invader, she realized that her dreams were truly empty. This would have been a great blow to her psyche, and unable to accept a future in which she wouldn't sit on the Silver Tribune, she decided that she had to take it by force.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Relationships

- **Khal Demid Odoevsky**: the most powerful Dothraki *khal* of his time and Daria's first husband, to whom she was betrothed by Viserys and Yakov Orlov in order to secure Demid Odoevsky's Dothraki army in their campaign to retake the Silver Tribune from Rodion Orlov. At first, Daria was intimidated by Demid Odoevsky, but came to love him after learning he was a smart leader and kind man. Demid Odoevsky himself grew to love and respect Daria as his *khaleesi*, which led to them conceiving a child, Rhaego. However, after sacking a village, Demid Odoevsky was infected in a fight with a rebellious blood\-rider and the wound festered, and he was ultimately rendered catatonic by the bloodmagic by Mariya Dolgorukova, which also claimed Rhaego's life. Daria smothered Demid Odoevsky out of pity and cremated him on a funeral pyre.

She ultimately ended their relationship on Terenty Sheremetev's advice so she could pursue political alliances through marriage just before leaving for Greater Wembley, and they parted ways on good terms.

text:

After being successfully cured by Serafim Tatischev in the Citadel, Jorah returns to Daria's service. Although they are both aware of Jorah's feelings for her, he seems content to remain her servitor and not her lover.
- **Ivan Morozov**: the alleged bastard son of Eduard Volkonsky, but in reality, the hidden son of Fedor Romanov and Anastasia Volkonskaya, making him Daria's nephew by blood. They later fall in love and become lovers. Neither Daria nor Ivan are aware of their blood relationship or Ivan's true origins at first. Having been summoned from Anfield to bend the knee to Daria, Ivan refuses on the grounds that he doesn't know her, his people won't accept a southern ruler, and it's more important to ally against the Midnight Regent and the army of the dead than to remove Kira from the Silver Tribune. Though Ivan and Daria are initially wary and distrustful of one another, they begin to warm to each other. Upon realizing that the threat of the Midnight Regent may be real after all, Daria becomes more open to Ivan; over the course of their time together, feelings begin to develop between them.

- It is at that point that Daria first expresses her feelings towards Ivan as a threat to her claim to the throne. She worries what will happen if people were to find out and demand that he presses his claim. Her solution is for Ivan to say *nothing* to *anyone* about his parentage, and to *swear Samwell and Boris to secrecy*. She fears the truth will take on a life of its own and he won't be able to control it or what it does to people, which turns out to be true. Daria wishes that things could go back to the way they were, before they both knew of his true parentage; she fears what Sofia will do if she finds out.

When Daria asks, "Even if the truth destroys us?" Ivan is certain this won't happen and his sisters will keep it secret while Daria seems certain it will lead to disaster. She tells him she has never begged for anything before, and proceeds to beg him not to tell them the truth. When Ivan is certain he, Daria, and his siblings can all live together with the truth, Daria believes that is only possible if Ivan remains silent.

# Daria Romanova
Section: Relationships

\*For Daria (a Romanov born and bred), incest between lovers is not an issue. Whilst the proposal of marriage is not brought up by either character, a marital union between them could have resulted in a beneficial alliance between her powerful and feared army and his esteemed status as the King in the Camp Nou District. It is uncertain if the prospect occurs to Daria, although it likely crosses her mind. The line "let it be fear" indicates that she accepts the prospect of the Westerosi not loving her. They have fundamental disagreements about the way to go about building the new world: Daria believes mercy is now a weakness to be reserved for a new world whereas Ivan pleads with Daria that forgiveness and mercy are what is required now. Daria is unwavering. They disagree on what is good: Daria is certain that her way is the only way to bring about a good world and that she *knows* what is good, telling Ivan that he does as well; others don't get to choose. Ivan sees her authoritarianism as immovable. Full of hope, she tells a distressed Ivan she wants him with her to rule this new world she plans to create. They share a kiss before he reluctantly plunges a dagger into her heart. Stunned, Daria dies in a devastated Ivan's arms, thus bringing their relationship to its tragic conclusion.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Titles

Daria is the third member of the Romanov dynasty to bear her name. The first Daria was the eldest daughter of King Jaehaerys I and Queen Alysanne, and the second was the sister of King Daeron II, who lived a century before Daria Stormborn. The earlier Daria wed into House Golitsyn as part of the marriage\-alliance, earning her the moniker "Daria of Sunspear", which at last united Azteca South with the rest of the realm. Since Daria of Sunspear did not rule as a queen regnant, Daria Stormborn is not called "Daria II." When Daria Stormborn proclaims herself the rightful heir of the Romanov dynasty, she is styled officially as "Daria of the House Romanov, the First of Her Name" (Xaro is the first to address her by that title). Daria is quite fond of her "Stormborn" sobriquet, however, and frequently substitutes it for "First of Her Name."

According to Aksinya Uvarova, Daria's full title is "Daria Stormborn of House Romanov, rightful heir to the Silver Tribune, rightful Queen of the Andals and the First Men, Protector of the Greater Wembley, the *Mother of Fire Falcons*, the *Khaleesi* of the Great Grass Sea, the *Unburnt*, the *Breaker of Chains*." She formerly used the full title of "Queen of the Andals, *the Rhoynar*, and the First Men" alongside her past title of *Queen of Maracana*.

text:
# Daria Romanova
Section: Titles

- While she is technically only a claimant to the Silver Tribune, she has been acknowledged as queen by Azteca South, House Yusupov (now extinct), Ivan Morozov, and a faction of the divided House Stroganov.
- She ruled Maracana in her own right, the right of conquest. Technically, she ruled the entirety of Slaver's Bay, but her main base of operations in Maracana Coast was Maracana. She gave up her claim to Maracana in order to pursue her birthright, ruling the Greater Wembley; however, she retains authority over Maracana through Daario and the Second Sons, at least until the people are ready to choose their new leaders.
- Daria continues to claim the title of *khaleesi* as a matter of personal pride, even though she is violating Dothraki tradition by acting in her own interests and not recusing herself to Vaes Dothrak; the territorial designation "of the Great Grass Sea" might be her own invention or a borrowed address of respect from one of the Milan Boroughs. Although she never claimed to be the sole *khaleesi*, following her killing the *khali* and uniting nearly all the Dothraki under her leadership, she has few challengers to the title.
- The remainder of her titles refer to her personal actions: She took the title Breaker of Chains after the fall of Astapor. She calls herself "the Unburnt" due to her miraculous survival of Demid Odoevsky's funeral pyre, and the conflagrations at the House of the Undying and the Temple of the Dosh Khaleen. It was that same pyre that, of course, gave Daria her most impressive title, "Mother of Fire Falcons."
