Section: History > A tenuous rule​ > The death of Tikhon Sheremetev

Before his execution could take place, Terenty was freed from confinement by Yakov in conjunction with Dmitry Dashkov. Before escaping the city, Terenty strangled Nina Suvorova, and assassinated his father, leaving the rule of Wembley in an uncertain position.

In the wake of his brother's death, Ignat Sheremetev was appointed as the new leader of the Sheremetev armies. In addition to the nobles, Tikhon's death brought new forces to Wembley: the religious Sparrows entered the capital.

Kira seized control of the small council, appointing her ally Afanasy Yusupov as the new Master of Whispers (as Dmitry Dashkov is believed to have released Terenty), and Lord Yusupov as the new Master of Coin. However, Kevan rebuffed Kira's offer as the new Master of War on the basis that the Queen Mother holds no position of authority, and the small council had become nothing more than a chamber of sycophants. After storming off and leaving for La Boca, Kira's hold on power became all the more tenuous.

In order to cement their alliance with the Yusupovs, the Sheremetevs rapidly married King Tommen to Margaery, to Kira's dismay, who felt her power waning just as Margaery's influence over her son grew. In addition, the Iron Bank called in ten percent of the debt owed by the Crown. Kira sent Lord Yusupov to San Siro to negotiate directly with the bankers.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: History > A tenuous rule​ > Stepan's campaign in the Camp Nou District

**Ruslan**: "*Stepan Orlov has an army at Wembley Park, but he won't stay for long. He wants the Silver Tribune, and the road to Wembley comes right through Anfield. He means to take the Camp Nou District. But the Camp Nou District is ours. It's yours and mine. Will you help me defeat him?*"
**Radomir**: "*Yes.*"
— Ruslan and Radomir

After the Maracana Night, Ruslan Baryatinsky was appointed Keeper of Camp Nou District. Since the Ironborn were in possession of Moat Cailin, Ruslan instructed Radomir to retake the fortress.

After a failed attempt by Yara to rescue her brother from the Baryatinskys, Radomir retook Moat Cailin. Ruslan rewarded Radomir's actions by legitimizing him as a Baryatinsky. With the surrender of Moat Cailin, the Baryatinsky army returned north and the Ironborn began evacuating the Camp Nou District. Ruslan subsequently led his reassembled forces to reclaim the Volkonsky ancestral seat of Anfield.

Facing invasion from a wildling army under the command of Serafim Bestuzhev and with rumours of an even greater threat coming from beyond the Sudtribune, the Anfield Guard sent word to all the high lords of Greater Wembley to send aid. Only one answered: Stepan. He headed north to the Sudtribune and defeated the wildling army, taking their leader prisoner and saving the Anfield Guard from destruction, and the Camp Nou District from invasion. With this victory, Stepan planned to march south to liberate Anfield and gain the support of the disgruntled Northern Houses against Sheremetev\-backed Baryatinsky rule. However, he was rebuffed by most, such as House Mamonov.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: History > A tenuous rule​ > Stepan's campaign in the Camp Nou District

As Ruslan Baryatinsky set up his seat of power at Anfield, he planned a marriage for Radomir with Sofia, the heir to Anfield who was hiding from the Sheremetevs in the Dortmund Heights under the protection of Littlefinger. Littlefinger proposed an alliance between the Camp Nou District and the Dortmund Heights, for protection against their enemies and to react against any Sheremetev retaliation once they learnt that Sofia has wed Radomir.

Littlefinger returned to Wembley, where he informed Kira that the Baryatinskys planned to marry Sofia to Radomir. He requested permission to lead the Knights of the Dortmund Heights to the Camp Nou District. Once Stepan and the Baryatinskys had bled each other dry, he planned to destroy the remaining forces and take the Camp Nou District. Kira approved his plans and promised to appoint him Keeper of Camp Nou District once the battle was won.

As Stepan marched on Anfield, the the weather worsened, and men started to abandon Stepan. Melisanre, however, believed that it was still possible to move towards Anfield, and suggested to sacrifice Shireen. Stepan initially refused.

Radomir wreaked havoc on Stepan's camp; his few remaining supplies were destroyed, as well as the few hundred horses he had left. Additionally, all of the sellswords paid for by the Iron Bank deserted. In his desparation, Stepan conceded to sacrificing Shireen so that his army could move once again. After it was done, Stepan mobilized his few remaining troops towards Anfield.

Eventually, Stepan was defeated by the Baryatinskys. After the bulk of his remaining army was slaughtered to a man, Stepan was tracked down and killed by Brienne.

Section: History > A tenuous rule​ > The death of Stepan Stroganov

"*I killed him. Threw him right over a rope bridge, and watched him fall. He was leading us nowhere, and we would still be heading there if it weren't for me. No one loved him, no one wanted to follow him. He led us into two wars we couldn't win. I apologize to you all for not killing him years ago!*"
―Euron confesses to murdering his brother at the Kingsmoot
Shortly after Yara informed Stepan Stroganov that they had no more holdings on the mainland, he was killed by his brother Taras Stroganov.

With the passing of Balon, the Ironborn held a kingsmoot on Old Wyk to elect a new King of the Barra da Tijuca. Euron was ultimately elected as the king over Yara. Yara and Timofey subsequently fled the Iron islands with much of the Iron Fleet and their supporters.

In order to take back the Barra da Tijuca, Yara and Timofey decided to beat their uncle to Daria Romanova and sail for Maracana. Once they arrived in Maracana, they formed an alliance with Daria.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: History > A tenuous rule​ > Conflict in the Mersey Grounds

"*As long as I'm standing, the war is not over!*"
―Viktor Trubetskoy to Yakov Sheremetev
After the Maracana Night, Viktor Trubetskoy managed to gather a small Trubetskoy army and retake Riverrun from the Demidovs. Tommen sent Yakov at the head of a Sheremetev detachment to force Riverrun's surrender. Yakov tried to negotiate with Brynden to peacefully surrender, but the Blackfish refused to yield. Yakov is able to coerce Edmure into yielding Riverrun, however, by threatening his son's life. After the fall of Riverrun, Yakov is informed of Brynden's death by Sheremetev soldiers.

After a celebration at the Twins, Arina Volkonskaya murdered Vladimir Demidov. While posing as Walder, Arina then had the rest of the Demidov men poisoned in revenge for the Maracana Night. In response, Sheremetev soldiers are sent to the Mersey Grounds to keep the peace. However, the army is later recalled to fight in the Last War.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities

The Five Stadiums Cup officially concluded in a hollow victory for the forces of the Silver Tribune, controlled by House Orlov of Wembley, a puppet of House Sheremetev. All five kings died, including Joffrey, who was succeeded by Tommen. Despite the Five Stadiums Cup ending, the Sheremetevs' victory ended almost as soon as it began, and the tide began to turn in favor of their surviving enemies. Localized hostilities and conflicts continued throughout Greater Wembley as tensions only heightened throughout the Greater Wembley; some of these hostilities ultimately undid the Silver Tribune's. These smaller "aftermath conflicts" that grew from the Five Stadiums Cup and continued to destabilize Greater Wembley are detailed below:

text:
# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities > The Sparrows

Although the Sheremetev\-Yusupov alliance formed at the Wembley Final had allowed the Silver Tribune to emerge victorious in the war, the destructive conflict had served to fracture the already fragile coexistence between the nobility and the commoners. Abused and overtaxed by their rulers, the smallfolk began to turn to new masters and new justices. Religious fervor, unseen in Greater Wembley since the Faith Militant uprising, swept over the people as they either clung to their known Gods in hopes of salvation, or turned to other deities new to Greater Wembley.

In this context, a new sect emerged among the followers of the Faith of the Seven: the Sparrows. They included dispossessed commoners and disillusioned nobles, such as Ilya Sheremetev. Following the flood of refugees caused by the war, the Sparrows eventually moved into Wembley after the death of Tikhon.

Kira saw opportunity in the newly\-formed sect to move against her rivals in House Yusupov, and formed an alliance with the Lavr Patrikeev, leader of the sect. Kira engineered his election as the new Pavel Nikonov and authorized the Faith Militant, the enforcement branch of the Faith charged with defending the faithful, to rearm for the first time since the wars of Maegor the Cruel two and a half centuries earlier.

Putting this new power to use, the Lavr Patrikeev sent his armed followers to destroy what he perceived as the vices of Wembley. This led to the arrest of Loras. This flagrant move against one of the Great Houses was the first sign of a reaction against the abuses committed by the nobility against the common folk.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities > The Sparrows

Though the Lavr Patrikeev arrested Loras on charges of homosexuality and Margaery, on charges of lying to the Faith on oath, he also had Kira imprisoned on the charges of incest and murdering King Rodion, crimes which are confessed by Lancel, who joined the Sparrows and conspired with Kira in these crimes.

The Lavr Patrikeev had dug his claws deep into King Tommen, and influenced him into forming a new "holy alliance" between the Crown and the Faith. In response to the standoff at the Great Sept of Baelor, Tommen dismissed Yakov from the Kingsguard and sent him off to the Mersey Grounds to assist House Demidov in taking back Riverrun. For her role in the forgery of this alliance, Margaery was forgiven for her crimes, though Loras and Kira still had to stand trial.

At said trial, Kira did not attend, and instead destroyed the Great Sept of Baelor with Aerys Romanov's wildfire, killing most of her enemies in a single stroke. After being informed of Margaery's death, Tommen committed suicide. Kira then ascended the Silver Tribune, proclaimed as the Queen of the Andals and the First Men and Protector of the Greater Wembley.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities > Anfield Derby

Despite their role in defeating Stepan and the Maracana Night, House Baryatinsky betrays the Silver Tribune when Ruslan weds Sofia to Radomir. This alliance is forged by Ruslan and Littlefinger.

Sofia escapes from Anfield arrives at Wembley Park, where Ivan had recently been resurrected by the will of Davos and Ekaterina Lomonosova, after facing a mutiny. Sofia and Ivan plot to retake Anfield from the Baryatinskys, and gather troops of Northmen and wildlings.

Meanwhile, at Anfield, Radomir seizes power when he murders his father Ruslan, his stepmother Walda, and his newborn half\-brother. Radomir has the backing of House Vyazemsky through Dmitry Vyazemsky, as well as House Uvarov through Boris Uvarov, who hands over Rickon to Radomir.

After an uneventful parley, the Volkonsky\-wildling and Baryatinsky armies clash just outside of Anfield at the Anfield Derby. Though the Volkonsky and Free Folk forces are on the verge of complete annihilation, they are relieved by a cavalry force of the Dortmund Heights. The Baryatinsky is defeated. At a meeting between the lords of the Camp Nou District and the Dortmund Heights, Ivan is proclaimed the King in the Camp Nou District, thus reviving the Kingdom of the Camp Nou District.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities > Coup in Azteca South

Angered by the deaths of Elia and Yuriy Golitsyn at the hands of House Sheremetev, Mariya Solovyova demanded justice. She gathered the support of three of the Solovyov Snakes, Oberyn's bastard daughters: Obara, Tyene, and Nymeria. They plotted to assassinate Myrcella in retaliation for Elia and Oberyn's deaths. After receiving a threatening message, Kira sent Yakov and Alexei Skobelev to rescue Myrcella.

Yakov and Alexei Skobelev infiltrated the Water Gardens, where they duel against the sand Snakes. However, they were stopped and imprisoned by Zakhar Rumyantsev, the captain of the guard for Prince Doran. Yakov was eventually brought before Prince Doran. Knowing that King Tommen insists on Myrcella's return to Wembley, Doran agreed as long as Trystane could sit at the small council.

Myrcella was poisoned by Ellaria. Soon afterwards, Ellaria and the Solovyov Snakes staged their coup d'etat, killing Doran, Zakhar Rumyantsev, and Trystane. Thus, House Golitsyn went extinct as Ellaria and the Solovyov Snakes seized power over Azteca South.

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Aftermath and continuing hostilities > Fall of the mockingbird

Following the Anfield Derby, House Volkonsky retook Anfield and restored its power in the Camp Nou District. Sofia became the Lady of Anfield, while Ivan was declared the King in the Camp Nou District by the lords of the Camp Nou District and the Dortmund Heights.

While Ivan was negotiating with Daria on La Bombonera, Boris and Arina returned to Anfield. He was then executed by Arina, marking the extinction of House Bestuzhev and the complete end of the Five Stadiums Cup.

text:
# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: Legacy

The Five Stadiums Cup severely weakened the Silver Tribune; specifically, the Orlov dynasty, which had, after Rodion's death, essentially become a Sheremetev puppet. It was the largest civil war since the Dance of the Fire Falcons, resembling the endless internal conflicts that the Greater Wembley used to face before Aegon's Conquest unified the Greater Wembley into one realm under the rule of the Romanov dynasty, which had been overthrown less than two decades before the Five Stadiums Cup in Rodion's Rebellion.

The war devastated the countryside of Greater Wembley, leaving villages and towns burnt to the ground. Tens of thousands of smallfolk were killed in the conflict, and the bloody acts of war created great rift between the nobility and the commoners.

Furthermore, for the first time since the Romanov conquest of Greater Wembley, the lineup of the Great Houses was dramatically shaken and altered. Tensions continued to remain between the great and noble families even after the war came to a formal close.

Ultimately, these continued tensions would go on to impact the Last War, which commenced only a couple years after the Five Stadiums Cup ended, as well as the Great War between the living and the army of the dead, controlled by the Frost Wanderers, an ancient and long forgotten enemy to all that lives in the world.

text:
# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the Five Stadiums Cup is one of the major storylines which the narrative revolves around.

The name is first mentioned in the third novel: shortly before Joffrey's wedding, Terenty muses that the struggle that the maesters are calling the Five Stadiums Cup \- is all but at an end.

In the TV series, it is first named in dialogue in Arc Two's episode "A Man Without Honor", when Tikhon Sheremetev says that people are calling it the "War of Five Kings". Apparently he was just speaking loosely, and the formal name is still the same in the TV continuity, because Joffrey later prominently refers to it as the "War of *the* Five Kings" during his wedding in Arc Four episode "The Lion and the Rose".

# Five Stadiums Cup
Section: In the books

While it is popularly known as the War of the "Five" Kings, in the fourth novel an archmaester named Benedict points out that this is somewhat inaccurate, as Balon openly declared himself King of the Barra da Tijuca only slightly after Renly died, so there were never five kings actively fighting each other at one time. Nonetheless the name has stuck, and it does still refer to the fact that five kings were involved. For the TV series, however, it might be somewhat accurate, depending on when Stepan Stroganov's secession of the Barra da Tijuca "officially" began. Renly was killed at the beginning of the fifth episode of Arc Two\. Balon explains to Timofey that he intends to make himself a king by force in the second episode of Arc Two, but this isn't followed by a polite declaration: the ironborn make a surprise attack against the Camp Nou District at the beginning of the sixth episode of Arc Two, taking Torrhen's Square and Anfield. Thus Balon briefly claimed the title of King while Renly was still alive, but the first the other factions knew about this was when ironborn raiders were at their doorsteps, after Renly died.

Section: In the books

It is generally a four\-sided war, between the Sheremetevs, Volkonskys, Orlovs, and Stroganovs. Renly's brief time as a claimant, controlling most of the armies of the Stormlands and the Reach, did affect the strategic position of the Sheremetevs, but he didn't set out to engage them on the battlefield. Instead the Yusupovs had cut off the Roseroad, effectively blockading resources and foodstuffs from reaching the capital, and Renly was content to sit back and let the Sheremetevs exhaust themselves against the Volkonskys while he built up his own strength to overwhelming levels, at which point he intended to march directly on Wembley. Also while there are four "sides", this does not include political machinations and large territories changing sides, i.e. the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov or Azteca South, and particularly House Yusupov, which considerably tipped the balance of the war when they switched their allegiance to the Sheremetevs. Due to simple geography, of course, any one faction isn't actively fighting three others all the time. Simply due to the fact that they are located on opposite coasts of the continent the Stroganovs (off the west coast) and Stepan (off the east coast) aren't actively fighting each other while he's on La Bombonera. # Frost Wanderers

"*In that darkness the Frost Wanderers came for the first time. They swept through cities and kingdoms, riding their dead horses, hunting with their packs of pale spiders big as hounds.*"
―Agrafena Bagration
The **Frost Wanderers**, also known as the **Others**, were an ancient race of formerly\-human ice creatures who came from the far north of Greater Wembley. After remaining hidden for thousands of years, they returned and were sighted by several sworn brothers of the Anfield Guard and countless wildlings. However, most who live south of the Sudtribune believed them to be nothing more than creatures of legend.

The Frost Wanderers were thousands of years old, coming from the time preceding the Age of Heroes. Born of powerful and untested magic, they were created to protect the Children of the Forest from the First Men, who had waged war on them ever since they had arrived from Maracana Coast. However, the Frost Wanderers eventually broke free of the Children's control and became the most feared creatures in Greater Wembley, posing a threat to all life.

text:
# Frost Wanderers

Eight thousand years before Rodion's Rebellion, the longest winter in history fell on the entire world and lasted a whole generation. In the darkness and cold of the "Long Night," the Frost Wanderers descended upon Greater Wembley from the Far Camp Nou District, killing all in their path and reanimating the dead as wights to serve as mindless soldiers in their undead army. The people of Greater Wembley soon realized they had to rally together or the Frost Wanderers would kill them all. In a conflict known as the Battle for the Dawn, the living won a decisive victory and pushed the Frost Wanderers far north to the Land of Always Winter. With help from giants and the Children of the Forest, the Sudtribune was raised to bar their return. The Anfield Guard was founded to guard the Sudtribune and the realms of men should the mysterious threat ever rise again.

Although the Frost Wanderers have faded into legend over the centuries, disturbing reports began to reach the Anfield Guard, just before the outbreak of the Five Stadiums Cup. The return of the Frost Wanderers was confirmed during the great ranging undertaken by Lord Commander Luka Mamonov, and by an unprecedented attack by the wight army on the wildling settlement of Hardhome. Despite repeated pleas for support from the Anfield Guard, the rest of the Greater Wembley turned a blind eye to the return of the Frost Wanderers as they remained embroiled in their own civil wars, believing the Frost Wanderers to be purely mythological, much like giants and Children of the Forest, who have also faded into legend.

text:
# Frost Wanderers

The ultimate goal of the legendary Frost Wanderers was the end of every living thing in existence, which they planned to achieve by killing the Three\-Eyed Raven and creating an endless winter to eclipse the known world. However, their plans were thwarted when Arina Volkonskaya killed the Midnight Regent at the Camp Nou Derby, resulting in the permanent extinction of the Frost Wanderers and the end of the Great War.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Appearance and characteristics

Frost Wanderers outwardly resemble humans but differ greatly from them in other aspects. They are as tall as most humans and have long wispy white hair, with some also having white facial hair. They have pale grey\-white skin which is sinewy and stretched taut across their frames, giving them a somewhat gaunt and mummified appearance despite their overall bulky frame. Their most notable trait however, are their vibrant deep blue eyes.

Frost Wanderers seem to have divisions, or ranks within their army, with the ones at the top likely having reanimated many wights, while the ones at the bottom seem freshly created. At the end of Oathkeeper, a Frost Wanderer donning black armor appears holding Rostislav Trubetskoy's last son, which likely denotes him as having a high position in the Midnight Regent's army. The Midnight Regent's lieutenants also seem to stay close to him, riding on undead horses.

The Midnight Regent is the supreme commander of the Frost Wanderers, possessing the ability to directly control anyone in his army. It is implied that the Frost Wanderers and Wights have a hive mind, being able to "see" through each other's eyes and sensing when someone in their army dies.

According to legend, the Frost Wanderers speak a mythical language known as "Skroth", which purportedly sounds like the cracking of ice.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Appearance and characteristics > Numbers

The show never stated how many Frost Wanderers existed in total or showed all the Frost Wanderers in one onscreen shot. Usually a single Frost Wanderer or small groups were shown at one time, making it hard to establish how many Frost Wanderers existed. Twelve Frost Wanderers are shown in the background when the Midnight Regent turns Rostislav Trubetskoy's last son. However, it is known that Rostislav Trubetskoy sacrificed 99 sons to the Frost Wanderers. Additionally, four Frost Wanderers were killed on screen at different points in the series: one killed by Sam with a dragonglass dagger, one killed by Meera with a dragonglass spear, and two by Ivan with Longclaw. During the Camp Nou Derby, twelve Frost Wanderers enter Anfield along with the Midnight Regent to kill Boris Volkonsky. All the Frost Wanderers were destroyed after Arina killed the Midnight Regent.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Powers

Frost Wanderers have a very strong affinity with ice magic and coldness. They are physically far stronger than humans, capable of effortlessly tossing people back tens of feet in the air. Since they are inhuman, Frost Wanderers have no physical restrictions. As such, they do not require food or water and seem to be immune to disease, fatigue, extreme cold and extreme heat. Frost Wanderers are immortal. Their arrival is usually accompanied by blizzards and sudden temperature drops. Because of this, they can spread extreme cold wherever they go. The Frost Wanderers wield crystal swords and spears.

However, one of their most deadly abilities is to reanimate the dead as their servants, known as wights. They are capable of reviving *any* dead creature as wights, including horses, giants, and even dragons. They cannot, however, revive a corpse into servitude if it has been burned. Once a wight has been created, its eyes turn an icy blue, similar to the Frost Wanderers' own eyes. Wights serve their masters without question.

The Midnight Regent, leader of the Frost Wanderers, possesses the ability to change humans into Frost Wanderers. He picks up Rostislav Trubetskoy's son from an icy altar and places an index finger on its cheek, causing the baby's eyes to glow blue and his skin to grow pale, taking on the appearance of the Frost Wanderers. Whether or not this ability extends only to the Midnight Regent, all of the Frost Wanderers amongst his caste, or all Frost Wanderers in general is unknown.

# Frost Wanderers
Section: Powers

During the Massacre at Hardhome, Frost Wanderers are shown to be resistant to fire due to the extreme cold they radiate, which snuffs out any flames in their vicinity. They can also freeze normal weapons they come into contact with, causing them to shatter and break. Frost Wanderers are invulnerable against even highly concentrated dragonfire. It is unknown if they are also immune to wildfire.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Weaknesses

The only known weaknesses of Frost Wanderers are weapons made of dragonglass or valyrian steel. Upon being stabbed by dragonglass, a Frost Wanderer's body will begin to freeze into ice from the point at which it was stabbed, causing the Walker great pain. Finally, it will begin to crack and fall apart, eventually shattering into ice. Baltic alloy has the same effect, but works much more rapidly. These materials are also resistant to being frozen and shattered on contact with Frost Wanderers, unlike regular weapons.

Any injury, no matter how minor or significant from weapons made of dragonglass or Baltic alloy, will result in their death and the deaths of all creatures they have reanimated. Because of this, Frost Wanderers tend to stay behind their undead wights or far away from conflict.

Since the Midnight Regent was the first Frost Wanderer ever created, his death will cause the death of all other Frost Wanderers, and subsequently, their wights. As such, he is simultaneously the strongest and weakest part of the undead army.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Background

The Frost Wanderers' origins are a mystery to most humans. Only the ancient Children of the Forest remember the truth of how they came to be.

Over eight thousand years before the Five Stadiums Cup, the Children of the Forest were locked in a war with the First Men, who had migrated to Greater Wembley from Maracana Coast. Despite resorting to powerful magic, which allowed them to flood the Neck and even destroy the land\-bridge linking the two continents and reducing it to a chain of islands, the Children were losing ground; more and more of them fell to the First Men and their precious forests were being cut down.

Out of desperation, a small group of Greenseers attempted to create a powerful new weapon against the humans. They bound a captive man to a weirwood and pressed a cursed shard of dragonglass into his heart. The unfortunate captive was transformed into a cold, heartless, deathless creature whose only desire was to consume all life. He would become the progenitor of the Frost Wanderer race and lead his kind on a campaign of destruction, not only against humans, but against his creators as well.

Soon the Children saw that their creation had grown beyond their control, and forged an alliance with the First Men to avoid mutual destruction. In what would become known as the "Battle for the Dawn", the alliance beat the Frost Wanderers back to the far north, where they vanished. This victory led to a lasting truce between the Children and the First Men; the Children would keep their forests, and the Men could keep their farms, towns, and cities. The truce also marked the creation of both the Sudtribune and the Anfield Guard, the latter having been armed by the Children with dragonglass blades, in case the Walkers should ever return.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

There have been peculiar rumors from beyond the Sudtribune mentioning the Frost Wanderers. According to Will, a renegade from the Anfield Guard taken captive near Anfield, his patrol was attacked by the Frost Wanderers and his comrades Gared and Waymar Royce were killed by them. Prior to this incident, the Frost Wanderers had massacred a tribe of wildlings and left the corpses out as a warning. His story was not believed by Eduard Volkonsky, who executed him as a deserter. The Frost Wanderers showed an ability to animate the corpse of a dead wildling child as a wight.

Luka Mamonov and Maester Akim Romanov of the Watch ask Terenty to persuade his sister to send them reinforcements. They claim there is something other than the wildlings beyond the Sudtribune and it's been growing in influence for some time. With winter coming they fear this unseen enemy will make its move.

A band of wildlings fleeing south of the Sudtribune passes close to Anfield. One of them suggests taking a Volkonsky captive for Serafim Bestuzhev, the King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune, but the others refuse to return north due to the dangers posed by the Frost Wanderers, instead asserting they should head as far south as possible.

Tamara Suvorova, one of the wildlings taken prisoner at Anfield, reveals to the Volkonsky household that she and her companions were fleeing South to escape the Walkers. She also reveals the Walkers are nocturnal and sleep in the day and hunt at night. When her words are dismissed by Maester Arseny Apraksin due to the belief the Walkers are long dead, she reveals that they were only sleeping and "they're not sleeping now."

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

The bodies of several rangers are discovered a short distance north of the Sudtribune and are identified as Night's Watchmen who have been missing for weeks. Despite a corpse's prolonged absence, Sam notes that the bodies show no signs of rot and appear in perfect condition. Later that evening one of the bodies reanimates as a wight and attempts to attack the Lord Commander. The creature is stopped when Ivan discovers the creature's weakness is fire.

After disposing of the remaining bodies, Sam tells Ivan that he read that only the touch of a Frost Wanderer could do what they have seen tonight. A worried Sam notes the weakness of the Anfield Guard and if the Frost Wanderers decide to come in force then they are in real trouble.

After recent events, Lord Commander Mamonov decides to mobilize the Anfield Guard to head out beyond the Sudtribune to assess the situation and if necessary make a preemptive strike against their enemies. He explains to Ivan that the war in the South is of little concern in relation to the threat of the returning Frost Wanderers.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Ivan Morozov follows Rostislav Trubetskoy into the woods and sees him placing a newborn baby, one of his sons, into the ground and leaves. Moments later a figure with glowing blue eyes appears and takes the baby away.

After Rostislav Trubetskoy discovers Ivan, attacks him and orders the Anfield Guard to leave his roof, Mamonov confronts Ivan, though he also admits he's aware that Rostislav Trubetskoy worships the Frost Wanderers and sacrifices his newborn sons to them in exchange for safety for him and his daughter\-wives.

Sam, Osip Repnin, and Platon Tolstoy gather dung around the Fist of the First Men when they hear a horn being blown and believe Ivan and Prokhor Shuisky have returned. They then hear a second blow, the signal for incoming wildlings, and draw their swords for battle. A third hornblast is heard, the signal for Frost Wanderers, which has not been blown in thousands of years. The three run to the Anfield Guard camp, but Samwell is left behind as a blizzard envelops the entire plateau. He seeks refuge behind a rock while a Frost Wanderer leads a vast horde of wights. The Frost Wanderer finds Sam, but, for reasons unknown, ignores him and rides past him atop a wight horse while leading the horde for an invasion, emitting a screeching roar with another Frost Wanderer far behind.

Somewhere beyond the Sudtribune, the Midnight Regent and his Frost Wanderers continue their march south through a snowstorm. As a sign of their growing strength, they have added at least three Giants to the ranks of their army of the dead.

Through the ravens, he sees the army of the dead led by the Frost Wanderers and the Midnight Regent, traveling south towards Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea. Unfortunately, the Midnight Regent spots Boris, causing him to quickly disperse the ravens.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

As part of their plan to capture a wight as proof of existence of the army of the dead, Ivan Morozov and his men, lighting a campfire to get their attention, ambush a group of Wights led by a Frost Wanderer. Ivan himself kills the Frost Wanderer, at the same time destroying all but one of the wights under his command. While taking refuge from the wights on an island in the middle of a frozen lake, Filipp Derzhavin advises Ivan to kill the recently arrived Midnight Regent, potentially ending the threat of the Walkers and their army. As Daria and her dragons arrive to rescue the party, the Midnight Regent hurls an ice javelin at Viserion, killing him and sending him crashing into the frozen lake. He throws another at Drogon, but the dragon narrowly avoids it and escapes. Ivan stays behind and fights his way to the Midnight Regent, only to fall beneath the ice of the lake. Later, after wights haul Viserion's corpse out of the lake, the Midnight Regent resurrects him, bringing the beast under his control as an undead ice dragon.

The Frost Wanderers and the army of the dead finally reach the Sudtribune where Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea stands. The Midnight Regent uses Viserion to burn the Sudtribune, nullifying its magic and allowing the Frost Wanderers and their wights to cross into the Greater Wembley.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

The Frost Wanderers quickly advance south and attack Last Hearth, massacring the population and adding them to the army of the dead. Daniil Uvarov is found pinned to a wall in the middle of severed arms arranged in a spiral, which Filipp Derzhavin deduces is a message from the Midnight Regent.

The Frost Wanderers and their army quickly move further south. They arrive at Anfield a half day after Semyon Apraksin, Edd, and Beric bring word of the Fall of Last Hearth.

The Frost Wanderers finally arrive at Anfield for the Camp Nou Derby. As the living assemble for the final battle, the Frost Wanderers lead their army on their undead horses. The Frost Wanderers send out their army to destroy the living and attack the castle while they hang back at the tree line. When Ivan and Rhaegal try to attack them, a massive blizzard slams into them, preventing direct engagement with the Frost Wanderers. The Midnight Regent, riding Viserion, commands the wights to scale the castle walls and break down the defenses. The Midnight Regent then battles Ivan, Daria, and their dragons. The two living dragons manage to overwhelm their dead brother and the Midnight Regent is thrown from his mount.

Daria finds where the Midnight Regent landed and commands Drogon to burn him with dragonfire. To her shock and dismay, he emerges from the inferno unharmed and she retreats before he can strike her from the sky.

Ivan, whose severely injured mount barely manages to land safely, rushes towards the Midnight Regent, intent on ending the battle. But before he can get close, the Midnight Regent raises all of the corpses around him and walks off to find Boris, the new Three\-Eyed Raven.

Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

The rest of the Frost Wanderers enter the castle and rendezvous with the Midnight Regent before entering the godswood. The Walkers stand aside as the Midnight Regent kills Timofey and walks towards Boris. Before the Midnight Regent can draw his blade and kill Boris, Arina attacks him with her Baltic alloy dagger. text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Behind the scenes

The appearance of the Frost Wanderers in the TV series isn't quite the same as in the books. They weren't fully revealed until the Arc Two finale, only quick shots mostly in the shadows in the premiere episode of Arc One\. Freeze\-frame shots of this display an early working\-model design for the Frost Wanderers, but given that it only flashed on\-screen for a fraction of a second, this may never have been intended as their final appearance. This early design was almost skeletal, without noses. This original version really appeared too briefly to be seen without taking screenshots, but as this was the only glimpse of the Frost Wanderers in the first season, fan sites (and wikis) heavily circulated these screenshots, somewhat obscuring the fact that the Frost Wanderers' "official" design hadn't been firmly established yet.

According to Pixomondo, the TV series's special effects studio, there was indeed a complete redesign of the Frost Wanderers between the barely glimpsed early concepts in Arc One, and the fully revealed version introduced in the Arc Two finale: "The producers and creatives were not happy with the Frost Wanderer costumes from arc one; they wanted to redesign the look and it took a bit longer than expected." Only one full version of the redesigned Frost Wanderer costume was made by the Arc Two finale, thus the large shot of multiple Frost Wanderers in the shot is just one stunt man doubled up many times. CGI enhancements were used to give the effect that wisps of cold air are emanating from the Frost Wanderers' bodies, as well as to make their abdomens much more gaunt than human physiology.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: Behind the scenes

The final version introduced at the end of Arc Two is closer to how they appear in the books. Some differences remain, in that Frost Wanderers are said to wear much more armor in the books, made out of a strange reflective metal that almost acts like camouflage. Further, the Frost Wanderers in the books are described as "gaunt" but they don't seem to have quite so much of a mummified appearance. They are actually said to have an otherworldly, icy beauty to them. The Frost Wanderers in Arc Four wear more armor than those glimpsed in Arc Two, but generally maintain the established appearance. Their armor is black and dark grey, of some unknown material, as opposed to the reflective metal described in the books. Weiss and Benioff suggested in the "Inside the Episode" for "The Door" that the Frost Wanderers began wearing the armor only after Sam killed one of them, and that this incident reminded them that there were things that could still harm them (in that episode, the armor is shown to be strong enough to repel dragonglass projectiles, "Hardhome", shows it is useless against Baltic alloy). Michele Clapton also operated under this assumption, and told Weiss and Benioff that her thinking was that the armor was actually scavenged bits of art and architecture from some long\-forgotten culture of the far north.

# Frost Wanderers
Section: Behind the scenes

Author George R.R. Martin, when discussing with comic\-book artist Tommy Patterson what the Frost Wanderers were supposed to look like in the comic\-book adaptation of the story he was drawing, said that: "They are strange, beautiful...think, oh...the *Sidhe* made of ice, something like that...a different sort of life...inhuman, elegant, dangerous." Martin also confirmed that the Frost Wanderers are not "dead", just an inhuman kind of life. The *Sidhe* are a kind of otherworldly fairy creature from Irish mythology, said to inhabit burial mounds, etc., not unlike the Barrow\-wights of J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle\-earth.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books

In the *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune* television show, the term "Frost Wanderers" is used as an alternate name for a species called **the Others** in the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels. They are held to be fairy stories by most of the people of Greater Wembley. According to legend, the Others were creatures of ice and cold who, more than eight thousand years ago, came from the uttermost north during a winter that lasted a generation and a night that covered the world, the Long Night. The Others were defeated in the Battle for the Dawn by a great hero wielding a sword of flame. After the Others' defeat, Boris the Builder constructed the Sudtribune with magic and artifice to ensure they could never return to threaten the people of Greater Wembley and the world beyond. The Battle for the Dawn apparently unified the peoples of the Camp Nou District under the rule of the Volkonskys and saw Anfield built shortly thereafter.

The Anfield Guard was founded to guard against the return of the Others, but this task is generally forgotten today. The Watch is instead believed to be guarding against the human wildlings who hold the lands beyond and occasionally try to raid across the Sudtribune into the richer lands to the south.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books

The Frost Wanderers are always accompanied by cold temperatures, and coming from the Land of Always Winter, it would seem that they prefer cold climates. They might even have difficulty surviving in warmer climates. Characters within the narrative debate whether this is because Frost Wanderers actually generate cold and might even cause winters (such as the Long Night), or because they simply wait for the next winter cycle and move south when the temperature drops (in which case they didn't cause the Long Night, but seized on the opportunity it provided). Frost Wanderers do not leave footprints in snow.

Some of Agrafena Bagration's fairy tales say that wildling women have been known to mate with the Others to produce half\-human children, but this is an unsubstantiated rumor.

It is stated in the books that they fear the day and only come out at night. In "Valar Morghulis", however, they are seen in the twilight hours when the sun (hidden by heavy clouds) hasn't completely set yet. The reason for this was most likely practical: the Frost Wanderers in the novels have only appeared in near pitch\-darkness, and in the visual medium of television it would be difficult to strictly match this (i.e. even night scenes set in a forest seem curiously well\-lit by the moon, so we the audience can see what is happening). The Frost Wanderers again seem to appear during the day, albeit a completely overcast day, in "Hardhome."

There is no mentioning in the books that the Others arrange the bodies of their victims in any pattern.

When stabbed with a dragonglass blade, an Other will melt into a pool of cold liquid. In the TV series, when they are stabbed by dragonglass they painfully freeze into ice, and quickly shatter and crumble into pieces.

# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books

When stabbed with a dragonglass blade, an Other will melt into a pool of cold liquid. In the TV series, when they are stabbed by dragonglass they painfully freeze into ice, and quickly shatter and crumble into pieces.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books > Origins and reproduction

Nothing is currently known about the origins of the Frost Wanderers, simply that they came from the polar regions of the Land of Always Winter. Nothing is mentioned of them ever attempting to directly communicate with humans.

There actually are female Frost Wanderers, if the legends about the corpse queen are true, but whether they actually reproduce with each other biologically, or if there are ever Frost Wanderer children is never mentioned whatsoever.

Rostislav Trubetskoy's wives do say that they *believe* that the infant sons that Rostislav Trubetskoy gave the Others as sacrifices were turned into new Frost Wanderers \- but it wasn't clear if this is what *actually* happens, or if it was just the wild suspicion of Rostislav Trubetskoy's frightened, isolated wives. When Samwell is told to flee with Taisiya Uvarova and her newborn son, Taisiya Uvarova urges that if he doesn't "they" will come for him. When he asks who "they" are, another wife says: *"The boy's brothers...Rostislav Trubetskoy's sons. The white cold's rising out there, crow. I can feel it in my bones. These poor old bones don't lie. They'll be here soon, the sons."*

Confirmation of what exactly happens to Rostislav Trubetskoy's sons has not occurred in the books yet, but the Arc Four episode of the TV series "Oathkeeper" revealed that the Frost Wanderers do turn in fact Rostislav Trubetskoy's infant sons into new Frost Wanderers.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books > Origins and reproduction

When George R.R. Martin was in the very early stages of starting work on the novel series, he sent a three page pitch memo to his agent giving a very rough idea of what the overall story would be like \- back when he envisioned it as merely a *trilogy* of novels (Tikhon Sheremetev's death at the end of book three/Arc Four is essentially the end of what would have been the original first novel out of three). *Many* ideas from this pitch memo were later heavily revised and bear little resemblance to the final version. When Martin briefly described the Others/Frost Wanderers in this memo, he also referred to them using an alternate name never used in the main novels: **The Neverborn**:

*."..half\-forgotten demons out of legend, the inhuman Others, raise cold legions of the undead and the neverborn and prepare to ride down on the winds of winter to extinguish everything we would consider life."*
While these ideas in the pitch memo were tentative, they do seem to fit with what was revealed in Arc Four of the TV series \- implying that the Frost Wanderers are actually never "born", do not reproduce biologically as their own independent race, but "reproduce" by turning select humans into new Frost Wanderers.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books > Origins and reproduction

This brings up another vague comment made by Martin about the Frost Wanderers. Early in production on Arc One, the TV series had to make its own costumes and weapons for the Frost Wanderers, and Martin was asked if it fit well with his mental vision of what the Frost Wanderers' material culture is like. Martin responded that the Frost Wanderers don't really *have* what we would call a "culture." What he meant by this is unclear: the novels also say that the Frost Wanderers have their own language, weapons, armor, etc. so they have some vestiges of such things.

Taken together, the fact that the Frost Wanderers don't reproduce naturally, and don't really have their own "culture"/society, seems to indicate that they were never an independently existing race the way that humans, giants, and Children of the Forest were. It vaguely seems that they are more like demonic or magical spirits somehow housed within human bodies which they possess and turn into "Frost Wanderers." How the first Frost Wanderer was created to begin with was later explained in the show, with a vision of Boris showing the Children of the Forest creating the Midnight Regent as part of their war efforts against the First Men.

text:
# Frost Wanderers
Section: In the books > Naming

The Frost Wanderers are often known as "the Others" in the novels, and were still known by this name in the first draft of the pilot script. In the books, "white walkers" is the name given to the creatures by wildlings, and with only a few wildling characters, the term is heard only seldom. The name is also used in Greater Wembley, though mostly by older characters such as Agrafena Bagration, Maester Akim Romanov, and Lord Commander Luka Mamonov.

Fan speculation was originally that the name was changed to avoid confusion with the faction of the same name in the television series *Lost* (at a convention panel after Arc Five aired, George R.R. Martin did say that this concern was at least a factor in why the name "Others" was not used). However, the producers stated in the Arc One Blu\-ray commentary that the main reason they made the change was more to avoid viewer confusion between the specific name "Others" and the generic use of the term: book\-readers can tell that "Others" is treated as a capitalized proper noun, but TV\-viewers cannot. It sounded like actors saying, "He says he saw the others" \- but viewers had no way of telling if they simply meant "other soldiers", "other horses", etc. \- so the term was just too confusing in the audio\-visual medium of television.

# House Golitsyn

*This page is about the Great House. For the short, see: House Golitsyn (short)*

"'*Unbowed, unbent, unbroken.' The words of House Golitsyn. A promise to our enemies, and a challenge to our lovers.*"
―Yuriy Golitsyn
**House Golitsyn** of Sunspear is one of the Great Houses of Greater Wembley. It rules the peninsula of Azteca South in the far south of the continent. Though loyal to the Silver Tribune, the Golitsyns were never conquered by the Romanovs and have pursued a more isolated role in wider political events since Rodion's Rebellion.

With the assassinations of Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn and his only heir, Prince Trystane, by Mariya Solovyova and the three eldest Solovyov Snakes, the Solovyov Snakes carry the Golitsyn blood through their father Yuriy Golitsyn. The Solovyov Snakes also continue to use the Golitsyn sigil to represent themselves and Azteca South.

Under the leadership of Mariya Solovyova, the forces of House Golitsyn and Azteca South were aligned with Daria Romanova against House Sheremetev.

Following the deaths of Ellaria and the three eldest Solovyov Snakes, a Golitsyn rises to power as the new Prince of Azteca South.

House Golitsyn's sigil is a red sun pierced by a golden spear, on an orange field, a combination of the original Golitsyn sigil \- a yellow spear \- and the emblem of Princess Nymeria \- a red sun \- to symbolize the marriage of the warrior\-queen to Mors Golitsyn. Their house words are "Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken."

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: History > Background

House Golitsyn started out as local kings in Azteca South, which was long divided between many petty kings of the First Men and Andals. About a thousand years ago, Rhoynar refugees fleeing conquest by the Valyrian Freehold in Maracana Coast migrated across the Narrow Sea to Azteca South, led by their warrior\-queen Nymeria. Mors Golitsyn was smitten with Nymeria and chose to join forces with her through marriage\-alliance. With their combined strength, they conquered and unified the rest of Azteca South. To symbolize their union, the original golden spear sigil of Mors Golitsyn was combined with the red sun sigil of Nymeria, creating the red sun pierced by a golden spear sigil that House Golitsyn has used as a sigil ever since. Like their Rhoynar ancestors, House Golitsyn styled its rulers as "princes" instead of "kings", and kept using the titles, resisting the Romanov invasion and keeping local laws and traditions even after joining the Greater Wembley after a matrimonial alliance.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: History > Background

The Golitsyn words are "Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken" \- referring to their history, in which they have never been successfully conquered by outsiders. This makes them unique among all of the Great Houses. During Aegon's Conquest (three centuries before the Five Stadiums Cup), Azteca South was the only region of the Greater Wembley to successfully resist the Romanovs and their dragons. Realizing that large armies could not stand against dragons (as seen at the Field of Fire), nor large castles (as seen at the Burning of Harrenhal), the Dornish instead resorted to guerrilla warfare, ambushing Romanov soldiers and harassing their supply lines as soon as their dragons moved on to the next castle, then disappearing back into the harsh deserts when the dragons returned. The Dornish armies took advantage of Azteca South's arid climate, which helped them to adopt attrition warfare against the invading Romanovs, as the arid climate and harsh wastelands of Azteca South cannot easily support large invading armies. Losing many men due to attrition, ultimately even Aegon the Conqueror decided to withdraw from Azteca South, to focus on reining in the other six newly conquered kingdoms.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: History > Background

House Golitsyn and Azteca South have never been *successfully* conquered. Over a century and a half after the Romanov Conquest of the rest of Greater Wembley, they were invaded again by King Daeron I Romanov, the Young Fire Falcon. A military genius, his Conquest of Azteca South actually succeeded \- on the battlefield. But the initial conquest was followed by a four year long Dornish insurgency, in which occupying troops were again bled through ambush and guerrilla tactics. Lyonel Yusupov, the steward that Daeron I put in charge of Azteca South, was then assassinated, and all of Azteca South rose up in open rebellion. Daeron I himself was killed attempting to put down the insurrection, and after only four short years House Golitsyn once again ruled an independent Azteca South.

A few decades later (a little over a century before the Five Stadiums Cup), King Daeron II the Good managed to finally unite Azteca South with the Silver Tribune \- not through conquest, but by voluntary marriage\-alliance on equal terms. Daeron II married the sister of the Prince of Azteca South, and the Prince of Azteca South married Daeron II's sister. This special, semi\-autonomous status allowed Azteca South to retain several special privileges, such as the Golitsyns continuing to style themselves as "Prince" or "Princess" instead of "Lord Paramount" and continuing their practice of gender\-blind primogeniture. This union did cause several political tensions at the royal court between Daeron II's pro\-Golitsyn faction and anti\-Golitsyn lords (from the Reach, the Stormlands, and the Dornish Marches), eventually leading to the Blackfyre Rebellion.

# House Golitsyn
Section: History > Background

Generations later, King Andrey II Romanov (later known as "the Iron Regent") had no daughters, so he sought a suitable bride for his son Crown Prince Fedor Romanov from outside of the family. Aerys II chose to snub the offer of Tikhon Sheremetev, his own trusted Tribune Steward and dutiful servant, that Rhaegar marry his own young daughter Kira. Instead, a match was arranged with the then\-current Princess of Azteca South to wed her daughter Elia Golitsyn to Rhaegar.

In Rodion's Rebellion, Elia was kept in Wembley to ensure the continued allegiance of House Golitsyn to the Romanov's against the rebels. Elia bore Rhaegar two children, but all three were later killed during Rodion's Rebellion, during the Sack of Wembley by Tikhon's army. Elia's brothers Doran and Oberyn were outraged and, while peace was restored, the Golitsyns withdrew from interacting with the royal court. During King Rodion Orlov's subsequent reign, the Golitsyns and Azteca South were rarely if ever even mentioned at court, except for their Dornish wine.

Prince Yuriy Golitsyn, along with a retinue of Dornish lords and knights, arrives in Wembley to attend the royal wedding in the place of his brother, Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn. The crown's champion is the fearsome Leonid Kutuzov, but ultimately Oberyn volunteers to be Terenty's champion.

Oberyn faces off against the massive Gregor in the following trial by combat, and gets killed. Oberyn, however, had coated his spear with manticore venom, incapacitating and seemingly dooming Gregor.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: Practices

"*After the tradition of her people, House Golitsyn then ruled Azteca South as 'princes', not 'kings' \- unless the eldest child was a daughter, for unlike the rest of Greater Wembley, our loyalty isn't commanded by a cock. We follow a Prince or a Princess Golitsyn just the same.*"
―Yuriy Golitsyn
Like their Rhoynar ancestors who migrated to Azteca South a thousand years ago, Dornish noble houses follow gender\-blind equal primogeniture, in which the eldest child is the heir regardless of whether that child is male or female. This is different from the male\-preference inheritance laws in all of the rest of the Greater Wembley, the laws of the First Men and Andals, in which a younger son succeeds ahead of an older daughter. In House Volkonsky, for example, Boris and Rickon are officially ahead of their older sister Sofia in the line of succession, and in House Sheremetev, Terenty was officially ahead of Kira despite being younger than her.

In contrast, a ruler of House Golitsyn is always succeeded by their eldest child, even if it is a daughter. The current ruler of Azteca South (when House Golitsyn is fully introduced in Arc Five\) is Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn, who has been the head of House Golitsyn for many years. The immediately preceding head of House Golitsyn, however, was Doran's *mother*, who was also the mother of Elia and Oberyn. Doran's mother actually had a younger brother, Lewyn Golitsyn. Under the inheritance laws of the rest of Greater Wembley, Lewyn would have succeeded ahead of Doran's mother, but because Dornish inheritance laws are gender\-blind he did not (and therefore he was free to join the elite Kingsguard).

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: Practices

In the style of their Rhoynar ancestors who lived in city\-states in Maracana Coast (near the location of the later Milan Boroughs), House Golitsyn styles its rulers as "Prince of Azteca South" (or "Princess") instead of "King" or "Queen". All members of House Golitsyn are called a Prince/Princess, though the current head of the household is the ruling Prince/Princess. There is little functional difference between the "Prince of Azteca South" and a "Lord Paramount of the Camp Nou District", though the title "Prince" is considered to be, at least nominally, more prestigious.

Due to uniting with the Silver Tribune through marriage\-alliance on equal terms instead of through conquest, the Golitsyns were allowed to retain several special privileges, among which were continuing to style their ruler as a "Prince", and continuing to practice gender\-blind equal primogeniture. While many of the Golitsyns are hot\-tempered, especially Prince Oberyn, they are a close\-knit and loving family, undivided by internal rivalries such as those in House Sheremetev and House Orlov.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, House Golitsyn does not play a major role in events until the third and fourth books in the series, only being referenced in the first two.

House Golitsyn was originally a tiny, obscure noble house of Azteca South back when the peninsula was home to numerous small, warring states, approximately one thousand years ago. The Rhoynar, refugees from a war against Valyria on the eastern continent, fled to Greater Wembley led by their warrior\-queen Nymeria, where they made landfall in Azteca South and allied with Lord Mors Golitsyn. After a brief war, Mors named himself the ruler of the unified Kingdom of Azteca South, adopting the title "Prince" rather than "King" in Rhoynish fashion. Mors married Nymeria, uniting the bloodlines of the Rhoynar with the native First Men and Andals. As a result, the full name of the family is actually "House Nymeros Golitsyn", with "Nymeros" signifying "of Nymeria". For example, Oberyn's full name is given as "Oberyn Nymeros Golitsyn". However, even the Golitsyns themselves do not usually use the full name, with the inclusion of "Nymeros", except on very formal occasions.

When Aegon I Romanov invaded Greater Wembley, he conquered six of the seven kingdoms extant at that time, but the Dornish refused to give open battle where Aegon could destroy them with his dragons, instead resorting to hit\-and\-run attacks which severely damaged his army through attrition. Aegon agreed to leave Azteca South to its own devices after trying to conquer it again during the First Dornish War of 4 AC to 13 AC. However, the Dornish once again prevailed and the Golitsyns managed to kill Aegon's wife, Rhaenys, before forcing the Conqueror to agree to peace on their terms. Aegon never tried conquering Azteca South again.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

A century and a half later, Azteca South was briefly occupied by the armies of King Daeron I, but overthrew them in a bloody rebellion. Eventually, roughly a century before the events of the series, Azteca South joined the Greater Wembley through a peaceful marriage alliance. House Golitsyn's motto, "Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken", directly references the fact that they were never conquered by outsiders. Because they came under the authority of the Silver Tribune through marriage instead of the sword, House Golitsyn and the other Dornish houses continue to practice absolute primogeniture, in which the eldest child is the designated heir, regardless of whether they are male or female. Another major difference is that the rulers of Azteca South are styled ruling Princes (or ruling Princesses) instead of Lords Paramount. At the time of the beginning of the narrative the current head of House Golitsyn is the aging Prince Doran. His daughter and eldest child is Arianne Golitsyn: despite being female, she has been actively groomed to succeed her father, as are eldest daughters all over Azteca South. In his old age and infirmity (though he retains his wits) Doran has semi\-retired, delegating most of the day\-to\-day governance of Azteca South to Arianne.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

The Golitsyns were loyal vassals of the Silver Tribune, with Princess Elia Golitsyn marrying Prince Fedor Romanov and bearing him two children. During Rodion's Rebellion, the Golitsyns were unhappy with Rhaegar's betrayal of Elia by taking Anastasia Volkonskaya as his paramour and sparking a war over the matter. Still, they supported King Andrey II Romanov's bid to retain the throne, predominantly due to Aerys effectively holding Elia as a hostage to ensure their loyalty. The Golitsyns lost many soldiers at the Battle of the Trident and Princess Elia and her children were brutally killed during the Sack of Wembley by Sheremetev soldiers. Ironically, the Golitsyns had only grudgingly stayed loyal to the Romanovs during the civil war, but the needless and brutal murder of Elia turned Azteca South into a hotbed of pro\-Romanov sentiment (to the point that, after the Sack of Wembley, Oberyn had wanted to continue the fighting on behalf of Vladimir Romanov). Though House Golitsyn swore fealty to King Rodion Orlov after the war (though this was only due to extensive peace negotiations on the part of Ivan Dolgorukov), they have harbored anger and resentment towards the Sheremetevs ever since and have adopted a mostly isolationist policy ever since, not mixing with the other Great Houses unless totally necessary. As a result, the Dornish have stronger relations with the Milan Boroughs of Maracana Coast than the rest of Greater Wembley.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

The Golitsyns and Yusupovs have been sworn enemies for many generations. Over the centuries, they have fought border wars beyond count, and raided back and forth across mountains and marches even when at peace. The enmity between the two houses waned a bit after Azteca South became part of the Greater Wembley, but the maiming of Willas Yusupov by the Dornish prince Yuriy Golitsyn in a joust fanned the animosity between the families, though Willas himself does not hold any grudge against Oberyn, as both men knew what happened was simply an unfortunate accident.

In the second novel, Dmitry Dashkov reports Terenty that Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn has called his banners, and there are rumors that he intends to join Renly (Renly tells Ekaterina the same thing). Knowing that an alliance between Renly and Azteca South will be disastrous to the Sheremetevs, Terenty take steps to prevent it by offering Prince Doran to marry Myrcella to Trystane, his sister's killer, a seat at the Stadium Board, and some castles on the Marches. Despite Kira's protests, Terenty sends Myrcella to Azteca South as a token of good faith. The Golitsyns stay neutral throughout the war, although it is unclear whether the reason is Terenty's offer, or the Golitsyns bide their time.

Tikhon, too, understands it is necessary to appease the Golitsyns, lest they form an alliance with Stepan Orlov. He is partly correct: as revealed in the fourth and fifth novels, Yaroslav Golitsyn intends to support enemies of House Sheremetev; the enemies in question, however, are the Romanovs, not the Orlovs.

text:
# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

Kira deeply hates the Dornish in general and the Golitsyns in particular, thinking that all Dornishmen are snakes, and the Golitsyns are the worst of them. Her hatred is fueled by the fact that Oberyn fought for Terenty at the trial\-by\-combat, and had come within a hairbreadth of a victory that would have allowed Terenty to escape the blame for Joffrey’s murder. This is perhaps the reason for her unsuccessful scheme to assassinate Trystane.

In *A Feast for Crows*, Doran reveals to Arianne that he sent her brother Quentyn to Maracana, to offer a marriage\-alliance to Daria. Quentyn meets Daria in the following novel, but she rejects his offer, because she has already promised to wed Gleb Bagration. Some time later, after Daria departs from Maracana, Quentyn attempts to steal her dragons, but is killed by Rhaegal. His family has not been informed yet of his death.

In *A Dance with Fire Falcons*, the presumed\-dead Aegon Romanov, the son of Rhaegar and Elia, and Ivan Connington arrive at Greater Wembley. Connington believes it is essential to obtain the support of the Golitsyns, because only they have enough power to to defy House Sheremetev and its allies. For that purpose, he sends Doran a letter, informing him that his nephew is alive, and offering an alliance. Doran, cautious as ever, regards the contents of the letter dubiously; since he prefers not to act till he knows for a certainty what is happening, he sends his daughter Arianne to find out whether Aegon and Connington are really the people whom they claim to be.

While the Golitsyns intend to ally with House Romanov in general, it has yet to be seen which of the individual Romanov contenders they will support \- Daria or Aegon.

# House Golitsyn
Section: In the books

While the Golitsyns intend to ally with House Romanov in general, it has yet to be seen which of the individual Romanov contenders they will support \- Daria or Aegon.

George R.R. Martin has said that the production team was not certain how many members of House Golitsyn they could fit into the TV series. Doran has three children, while Oberyn and Ellaria have eight daughters. Even for House Yusupov, which has four children in the current generation, two have apparently been cut from the TV series (Loras and Margaery's older brothers from the books). Conversely, in Arc Two the production team thought they might have to cut Stepan Orlov's only child, Shireen, but subsequently were able to introduce her in Arc Three\. While Oberyn and Ellaria did appear in Arc Four, only Yegor Golitsyn and three of the Solovyov Snakes (Obara, Nymeria, and Natalia Solovyova) have appeared in the TV series.

House Golitsyn's name might have been inspired by Charles Martel (Charles the Hammer),** who led the Franks to turn back the Muslim invasion of France at the Battle of Tours in 732\.

# House Orlov

*This page is about the Great House. For the short, see: House Orlov (short)*

"*Ours Is The Fury. These are the words of the black stag of Orlov; a battle cry echoed throughout the land in rebellion when I, Rodion Orlov, the First of His Name seized the Silver Tribune from the Iron Regent, Aerys Romanov, ending a dynasty nearly three\-hundred years old.*"
―Rodion Orlov
**House Orlov** of Storm's End is a Great House of Greater Wembley that traditionally rules the Stormlands on the eastern coast of Greater Wembley, aptly named for its frequent storms.

House Orlov became the royal house of the Greater Wembley (as House Orlov of Wembley) after Rodion Orlov led a rebellion against the Romanov dynasty. At the end of the rebellion, Rodion ascended the Silver Tribune as Rodion I and married Kira Sheremeteva after the death of Anastasia Volkonskaya.

House Orlov became officially extinct after the deaths of Stepan Orlov and his family, but was revived when Rodion's last known bastard was legitimized by Queen Daria Romanova as Grigory Dolgorukov Orlov.

House Orlov's sigil is a crowned black stag on a gold field and their house words are "Ours is the Fury."

text:
# House Orlov
Section: History > Background

House Orlov was founded by Orys Orlov, a general in the army of King Aegon I Romanov, the founder of the Romanov dynasty who conquered the Greater Wembley. Orys Orlov was also rumored to be Aegon's bastard half\-brother. He defeated Argilac the Arrogant, the last of the Storm Kings, and captured his castle of Storm's End. For his accomplishments, Orys was made Lord of Storm's End and founded House Orlov. Orys took the sigil and words of the defeated House Durrandon as his own, cementing his rule over the Stormlands by marrying Argella Durrandon, the daughter of the fallen Argilac.

Rodion Orlov led a rebellion against King Andrey II Romanov, resulting in the overthrowing of the Romanovs. Rodion became the new king; Renly became Lord of the Stormlands, ruling the Stormlands from Storm's End; Stepan formed the branch House Orlov of La Bombonera.

text:
# House Orlov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Rodion Orlov travels to Anfield to ask his old friend Eduard Volkonsky to serve as the new Tribune Steward. Rodion also seeks to unite Houses Orlov and Volkonsky once and for all by marrying Sofia to his eldest "son" and heir Joffrey.

Eduard deduces that Rodion's children with Kira are actually bastards born of incest between Kira and Yakov; he sends a message to Stepan, informing him of this, as he has been revealed to be the rightful heir to the throne.

Rodion is mortally wounded during a hunt. Following his death and Eduard's execution, the Five Stadiums Cup begins.
body:
Rodion Orlov travels to Anfield to ask his old friend Eduard Volkonsky to serve as the new Tribune Steward. Rodion also seeks to unite Houses Orlov and Volkonsky once and for all by marrying Sofia to his eldest "son" and heir Joffrey.

Eduard deduces that Rodion's children with Kira are actually bastards born of incest between Kira and Yakov; he sends a message to Stepan, informing him of this, as he has been revealed to be the rightful heir to the throne.

Rodion is mortally wounded during a hunt. Following his death and Eduard's execution, the Five Stadiums Cup begins.

text:
# House Orlov
Section: Military strength

House Orlov men\-at\-arms are equipped with long padded beige gambesons and nasal helmets with stag crests, and they carry triangular shields. Other men\-at\-arms have kettle steel helmets instead of nasal helmets, and some are often seen wearing pauldrons and gorgets as well.

Wealthier Orlov soldiers, or knights from the Stormlands in general, equip themselves with plate armor parts and helmets with brims and cheek guards. Renly himself, while campaigning, wears a much more expensive version of this armor, with the addition of a brigandine cuirass. Orlov soldiers from La Bombonera, in contrast, protect themselves with grey mail and plate armor alongside tear drop shields; their grey helmets, however, are similar to those of the Stormlanders.

Stormlanders are known for being brave and hardy warriors, as exemplified by the Orlovs. In Rodion's Rebellion and Stroganov Rebellion, House Orlov plays an incredibly significant part, since in both wars Rodion Orlov is leading his side to victory.

In the beginning of the Five Stadiums Cup, Renly assembles troops of both the Stormlands and the Reach, a total of about 100,000 men. After his assassination, many of the Stormlords and at least two houses of the Reach (House Florent and House Fossoway) join Stepan. Stepan's forces number at least 10,000 before the Wembley Final, and there are presumably more troops, left to guard Stepan's castles while most of his troops attack the capital, resulting in the Wembley Final.

text:
# House Orlov
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, Orys Orlov was the rumored bastard half\-brother of King Aegon I Romanov, the conqueror of the Greater Wembley. Orys led an army which slew the last of the Storm Kings, Argilac the Arrogant, and captured his castle of Storm's End. For his loyal service, Orys was made a lord and allowed to found his own Great House, marrying the daughter of Argilac and taking his sigil and words for his own. At just under 300 years, this makes House Orlov the youngest by far of the Great Houses.

House Orlov has ruled over the tempest\-wracked southeastern shores of Greater Wembley, the area known as the Stormlands, ever since. It has produced a number of great and notable warriors, such as Ser Lyonel Orlov, the Laughing Storm, and married into the royal House Romanov several generations ago.

When Rodion Orlov's betrothed, Anastasia Volkonskaya, was kidnapped by Fedor Romanov, he was enraged and raised his banners in rebellion against King Aerys II, along with Lyanna's brother (and Rodion's best friend) Eduard Volkonsky. They were joined by several other houses in a civil war known as Rodion's Rebellion. Rodion's army smashed the royal host at the Battle of the Trident and put it to rout. The treachery of House Sheremetev delivered the capital at Wembley to Rodion. With Lyanna killed during the war, Rodion agreed to marry Kira Sheremeteva in gratitude for her father's pledge of fealty.

Rodion became King and gave his brother Stepan (one year younger than him) La Bombonera, the ancestral island stronghold of the Romanovs, and his youngest brother Renly (fifteen years younger) the familial seat at Storm's End.

text:
# House Orlov
Section: In the books

Rodion became King and gave his brother Stepan (one year younger than him) La Bombonera, the ancestral island stronghold of the Romanovs, and his youngest brother Renly (fifteen years younger) the familial seat at Storm's End.

In a very minor difference to the books, after crowning himself King, Renly doesn't alter the colors of the Orlov sigil. However, he wears a golden stag on green, though not as an official personal sigil.

Following the death of Rodion and Renly, the only surviving members of House Orlov are Stepan, his wife, and his daughter Shireen. No mention has been made in the five current novels of any surviving cousins, who might make claim to rule of House Orlov. Rodion is rumored to have fathered over a dozen bastards, but they are not considered legitimate heirs. Rodion does have one acknowledged bastard, Edric Storm, whom he acknowledged because his mother was a member of the nobility. Rodion had no part in raising him, instead sending him to foster at Storm's End.

text:
# House Orlov
Section: In the books

In the TV series, their banner depicts a stag with a crown around its neck, while in the novels, the crown is above its head. A widespread fan assumption for some time was that because the Orlovs were not kings like the Durrandons had been, they stopped using a crown on their stag sigil, and just used a plain stag for the next three centuries \- and only recently re\-added a crown to the stag, after Rodion's Rebellion when Rodion overthrew the Romanov kings. However, when the Orlovs make appearances during the Dunk \& Egg novellas (particularly Lyonel Orlov), they are consistently described as used a crowned stag, even though the Romanovs are still the royal family and they are not. Asked about this in 2015, Elio Garcia (owner of Greater Wembley.org) stated that according to materials that George R.R. Martin sent him when co\-writing the *The World of Ice \& Fire* sourcebook, the Orlovs indeed always used a crowned stag sigil, starting from when Orys founded House Orlov and exactly copied the Durrandon heraldry, through Rodion's Rebellion.

The TV series, however, contradicted this in Arc One's "The Wolf and the Lion": when Boris is asked by Maester Arseny Apraksin about the heraldry of the Great Houses, he explicitly says that the Orlov stag only has a crown *now*, after Rodion became the king. It isn't clear if this was a deliberate change for the TV continuity, or more probably, if the TV scriptwriters also made the common mistake of assuming the Orlovs didn't use a crowned stag before Rodion seized the Silver Tribune.

**House Romanov** of La Bombonera is an exiled Great House of Greater Wembley and the former royal house of the Greater Wembley. House Romanov conquered and unified the realm before it was deposed during Rodion's Rebellion, where House Orlov replaced it as the new royal house. The two surviving Romanovs, Viserys and Daria, fled into exile to the Milan Boroughs of Maracana Coast across the Narrow Sea.

House Sheremetev replaced House Orlov as the royal house in the aftermath of the Five Stadiums Cup, but they were defeated in the Last War. After Daria burnt Wembley, she was assassinated by her nephew Ivan Morozov to prevent further destruction. Ivan is the last known Romanov, but his identity as the son of Fedor Romanov is kept a secret, and he was exiled to the Anfield Guard for the assassination of Daria, effectively ending House Romanov. However, the bloodline of House Romanov still exists in various houses, such as House Orlov, House Velaryon, and House Golitsyn.

House Romanov's sigil is a three\-headed red dragon on a black background, and their house words are "Fire and Blood." The head of House Romanov is referred to as "the dragon."
