text:
# House Romanov
Section: History > Background

House Romanov was one of the forty dragonlord families of the Valyrian Freehold, an empire that rose in Maracana Coast and dominated much of the known world. Due to their mastery of dragons, and thus sorcery, they had no real opposition to contend with. Using dragonfire and magic, they built their grand capital city of Valyria, which was unmatched in quality in the east.

The Valyrian Freehold's reign would continue until the Doom of Valyria, a cataclysmic event that ultimately fractured the mighty empire and left the Romanovs as the last surviving dragonlords, due to Daenys the Dreamer having foreseen the disaster and convincing her father to leave their capital and take their family to La Bombonera, in spite of their rivals' sneers (another reason could be that Aenar met with some mishap at court and chose exile over execution). La Bombonera would become the seat of their power, due to its importance in their survival, and Aegon Romanov would end the Century of Blood after Valyria's fall by joining the Milan Boroughs' side against Volantis.

After a century of isolation, Aegon, disinterested in the eastern lands of his ancestors, which he saw as old and withered, looked west to the Greater Wembley of Greater Wembley, which he sought to conquer and unify into one realm, with the aid of his dragons and his sister\-wives Rhaenys and Visenya.

In the Romanov era there were periods of peace and prosperity during the reign of benevolent kings like Jaehaerys the Conciliator, but also periods of terror and distress when evil tyrants like Maegor the Cruel ruled. The civil population of Greater Wembley suffered a lot especially during the bloody conflicts between opposing branches of House Romanov, like the Dance of the Fire Falcons and the Blackfyre Rebellions.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: History > Background

During the increasingly erratic reign of King Aerys II, his son Rhaegar was said to have kidnapped Anastasia Volkonskaya for unknown reasons; this led to a massive uprising led by Eduard Volkonsky, Rodion Orlov, and Ivan Dolgorukov. At the end of this war, Aerys and Rhaegar were dead and the Romanov power\-base in Greater Wembley destroyed. Aerys's youngest children, Viserys and Daria, were taken by Romanov loyalists into exile in the Milan Boroughs of the East. Unknown to most, however, Rhaegar had his marriage with Elia Golitsyn annulled and remarried Lyanna, with whom he also had a son, Ivan Morozov. As Lyanna lay dying after giving birth to her son, she pleaded with her brother Eduard to keep her baby safe from Rodion, who surely would want her baby dead due to Rodion's immense hatred for Rhaegar and promise to wipe out the Romanov bloodline. She reveals her son's name is 'Aegon Romanov'. To protect his sister's son from Rodion, Eduard takes his infant nephew back with him to Anfield, names him 'Ivan', and claims him as his illegitimate son, raising Ivan as his own child alongside his trueborn children. The child would become Ivan Morozov and grows up with the maternal side of his family.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: History > Background

Generations of compound inbreeding have preserved in the Romanov bloodline the classic Valyrian features of silver\-white (platinum blonde) hair, and very fair, pale skin. Allegedly, this also preserved in their bloodline the ability to successfully bond with and ride dragons. They also seem to be somewhat more tolerant of extreme heat and high temperatures than other people, though they are by no means invulnerable to fire – or at least, not all of them. Unfortunately, some believe that this practice of inbreeding has also caused the trait of insanity to plague House Romanov; though some members are known to be perfectly normal psychologically\-speaking, other Romanovs throughout history have displayed bizarre, erratic and sometimes violent behavior, succumbing to the so\-called 'Romanov madness'.

# House Romanov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Daria and her retainers flee Qarth by ship, heading for Astapor to purchase an army. Daria is nearly assassinated, but is rescued by Ser Egor Suvorov, who has tracked her down to pledge fealty to House Romanov once again. Daria double\-crosses the Good Masters, seizing their elite Unsullied and burning the slave\-owning elite. Daria thus becomes the first Romanov in generations to march at the head of her own conquering army. Daria heads to Yunkai, where she manages to win over the Second Sons and liberate that city from the Wise Masters.

# House Romanov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Daria has been captured and brought before Khal Vasily Milutin, but manages to get free with the help of Daniil Bagration and Jorah. The Dothraki immediately show their allegiance to Daria, thus making her the leader of all the Dothraki present, including at least 100,000 Dothraki warriors. Daria returns to Maracana, which is besieged, and defeats her enemies.

Daria meets Timofey and Kira Stroganova, who have arrived to pledge their fleet to the Romanov cause. Back in Greater Wembley, Dmitry Dashkov secures the assistance of Azteca South and House Yusupov. Daria and her army sail to Greater Wembley.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Daria arrives at La Bombonera, her birthplace and the ancestral stronghold of House Romanov.

Daria suffers several major setbacks: her ironborn fleet is destroyed by Taras Stroganov; the Unsullied capture La Boca, but end up stranded at the castle; Yakov leads an army to Highgarden, sacking the castle and knocking the Yusupovs out of the war.

Daria gains a potential ally in Ivan Morozov, now King in the Camp Nou District. Daria later leads the Dothraki against the Sheremetev army, defeating the army and cutting them off from Wembley.

In the Citadel, Taisiya Uvarova and Sam find out that Ivan is actually a trueborn Romanov, thus he is the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune.

Ivan gives up his crown to Daria and pledges allegiance to her as his queen.

At the Dragonpit in Wembley, Daria offers a truce to Kira Sheremeteva, but in vain.

Daria sails with Ivan to Anfield, and they become lovers.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Daria and Ivan arrive at Anfield.

Sam informs Ivan of his true parentage and calls him the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune, Aegon of House Romanov, the Sixth of His Name. Ivan says that pressing his claim is treason, expressing no interest in the Silver Tribune and reinforcing his loyalty towards his queen.

The Romanov and Volkonsky forces fight and defeat the army of the dead at the Camp Nou Derby.

The Romanov fleet is suddenly ambushed and destroyed by Euron.

The Romanov, Volkonsky, and Dolgorukov forces attack Wembley. Even after the Sheremetevs surrender, the Romanov, Volkonsky, and Dolgorukov forces sack the city, while a mad Daria burns the city.

House Romanov is restored to royalty. Daria intends to conquer the world and put an end to the rule of all tyrants. Ivan reluctantly kills her.

Drogon unleashes his fire across the throne room, melting the Silver Tribune, destroying what Aegon the Conqueror built and "breaking the wheel" that have plagued Greater Wembley for over 300 years. He picks up Daria's body and flies away, leaving a grieved Ivan behind.

Ivan is sent to the Sudtribune by the new king, Brandon I Volkonsky. As a member of the Anfield Guard, Ivan is prohibited from fathering children and House Romanov will become extinct with Ivan's death.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Maracana Coast

House Romanov's military strength has fluctuated over the last few years under Daria Romanova's leadership. Since the death of her husband *Khal* Demid Odoevsky, Daria has commanded a khalasar containing only a few dozen riders, less than half of whom are warriors, as well as a single trained knight, Vsevolod Mamonov. During her time in the Red Waste and Qarth, Daria's dragons were not large enough to provide combat assistance.

By the time Daria reached Astapor in Slaver's Bay, her dragons had grown enough to provide limited air support in certain engagements, and she had gained the loyalty of an additional knight, Ser Egor Suvorov. It should be pointed out that although limited, the dragons at this time are capable of providing the only air support in the known world.

Following the fall of Astapor, Daria gained an army of 8,000 fully trained Unsullied, elite warrior\-eunuchs who fight in large, disciplined phalanx formations, as well as several hundred Unsullied\-in\-training who serve as auxiliaries.

Shortly after arriving at Yunkai, Daria is able to secure the affection of Daniil Bagration, a lieutenant in the Second Sons. During a parley between Daria and the captains of the Second Sons, Daario points out that Daria's Unsullied are impressive infantry, but she still possesses no cavalry, siege weapons, or ships. Later that night, Daario slays the captains of the Second Sons, makes himself captain, and pledges the company to Daria. The Second Sons add 2,000 armored cavalry to the growing Romanov army.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Maracana Coast

During Daria's rule of Maracana, the Unsullied and the Second Sons take light, but constant losses, most of them assassinated by the Sons of the Harpy. The greatest losses of this time were both of her knights: Daria banished Ser Jorah upon learning that he had once spied on her for Rodion Orlov, and Ser Barristan was killed by the Sons of the Harpy. During her time in Maracana, her forces took control of the Meereenese naval fleet that consisted of 93 ships, although the fleet was later destroyed in the harbor.

After burning the Dothraki khals in Vaes Dothrak, Daria emerges unburnt from the flames, and all the people in the city bow down to her. In perhaps her greatest turnaround yet, Daria secured the loyalty of the roughly 100,000 Dothraki assembled at the time, finally gaining the numbers – though not the means – to retake Greater Wembley.

By this point, all three dragons had grown significantly larger, with Drogon, in particular, becoming larger than a carriage due to his continued freedom. He is now large enough for Daria to sit comfortably across his back, and has begun to obey her commands while riding. Should they be tamed and ridden, all three dragons are now large enough to coordinate aerial assaults should the need arise. During the second siege of Maracana, all three dragons were deployed to devastating effect, even though Drogon was the only one being ridden.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Greater Wembley

There are no official allies or vassals of House Romanov left in Greater Wembley. In truth, Dmitry Dashkov is a Romanov loyalist and possesses a vast spy network, but by himself, Dmitry Dashkov commands no military forces and cannot be considered a military asset. He eventually relocated to Maracana and began openly serving Daria, again mostly through coordinating his spy network.

King Rodion Orlov expressed fear that even after all these years, there are still a sizable number of noble houses in Greater Wembley who are either secret Romanov loyalists or who later developed some grievance with Rodion's rule and would flock to the Romanov banner if they attempted to retake the Silver Tribune in open war. It is not clear what influence his opinions since Ser Jorah stressed to Dasha that the number of Romanov loyalists remaining in Greater Wembley is far lower than Viserys liked to believe. Viserys believed that because House Yusupov of the Reach and House Golitsyn of Azteca South fought on the Romanov side during Rodion's Rebellion, the prospects were good that they'd be willing to join his cause and rebel against Rodion. Nonetheless, for much of Rodion's reign, and most of the Five Stadiums Cup that followed, it was unknown and remained to be seen if the dissatisfied houses would support a Romanov return, while House Yusupov had become closely aligned with the Sheremetev\-backed House Orlov.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Greater Wembley

However, following the Assassination of Stepan Stroganov, the Coup in Azteca South and the Destruction of the Great Sept of Baelor, the attitudes of several major factions changed dramatically. Fleeing their uncle upon his success at the kingsmoot on Old Wyk, Yara and Timofey Stroganov made for Maracana, where they agreed to support Daria's claim and provide transport for Daria's army, as well as support at sea, in exchange for Yara's accession to the Salt Throne, independent of the Greater Wembley. Daria accepted the independence of the Barra da Tijuca, provided that the independent Ironborn give up all reaving, raping and pillaging, to which Yara reluctantly acquiesced. Meanwhile, Ellaria, in desperate need of allies, agreed to support Daria's invasion. At Dmitry Dashkov's urging, she also reached out to Feodora Yusupova, who was out for revenge against Kira Sheremeteva.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Greater Wembley

As a result, House Romanov gained the support of the largely intact forces of the Reach, Azteca South, and the Barra da Tijuca. After the recent events of her invasion of Greater Wembley, Daria's army had already taken several heavy blows. Yara's Ironborn fleet was destroyed by her uncle, Taras Stroganov. The Solovyov Snakes, along with Yara, were captured by Euron, effectively knocking Azteca South out of the war. Yakov Sheremetev then led an army into the Reach to sack Highgarden, also knocking House Yusupov out of the war. The Unsullied took moderate casualties at the Fall of La Boca, which was likewise the case with the Dothraki at the Battle of the Goldroad. When Ivan Morozov, King in the Camp Nou District, sought an alliance with Daria for her help in defeating the Army of the Dead threatening all of humanity, he initially refused her condition that he bend the knee as he did not know her yet. However, when Daria came to rescue Ivan's party Beyond the Sudtribune and the Midnight Regent managed to kill Viserion with an ice spear, upon which Daria vowed to fight the Midnight Regent at Ivan's side, Ivan bent the knee to Daria as queen and agreed to pledge his Northern forces to her. The Midnight Regent reanimated Viserion as a wight, leaving Drogon and Rhaegal as Daria's living dragons.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: Military strength > Greater Wembley

Half of the Dothraki and Unsullied troops were killed during the Great War. The remainder were forced to scatter and retreat behind the walls of Anfield. Although both Drogon and Rhaegal survived, they were injured during the battle against the dead. After the Great War, Romanov forces still maintained roughly a dozen ships in the royal fleet and a contingent of Unsullied forces. After Euron shot down and killed Rhaegal with scorpion bolts, Drogon became Daria’s only living dragon.

Daria had Dmitry Dashkov burned alive by Drogon for treason shortly before the Battle of Wembley. The Romanov\-Northern forces suffered light casualties in the battle, but they emerged victorious when the city surrendered to Daria, allowing her to take the Silver Tribune. However, Daria laid waste to a surrendered Wembley, killing thousands of civilians in the process. She declared to her assembled Dothraki and Unsullied forces that they "liberated" the people of Wembley and will do so all over the world. Daria had Terenty Sheremetev arrested for treason upon finding out Terenty tried to save his brother Yakov. Ivan pleaded with Daria to stop this path of destruction but Daria believed her actions were necessary to build her ideal world. Unable to dissuade her, an agonized Ivan assassinated her to prevent more carnage upon the world. Drogon was anguished to discover his mother’s lifeless body, but he did not blame Ivan for her death. Instead, he used his fiery breath to melt the Silver Tribune before carrying Daria across the Narrow Sea.

After Daria’s death, Semyon Bezborodko and the Unsullied sailed to Naath to protect its people as Semyon Bezborodko had promised Aksinya Uvarova. Meanwhile, the Dothraki either returned to Maracana Coast or integrated themselves into Westerosi society.

After Daria’s death, Semyon Bezborodko and the Unsullied sailed to Naath to protect its people as Semyon Bezborodko had promised Aksinya Uvarova. Meanwhile, the Dothraki either returned to Maracana Coast or integrated themselves into Westerosi society.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the Romanov family (they were not a formal House, as this was a Westerosi concept not found in the Freehold) moved from Valyria to La Bombonera, then the most far\-flung outpost of the Valyrian Freehold, apparently in fear of a prophecy predicting the destruction of Valyria a century before it happened. Both before and after their relocation, the Romanovs were counted among the dragonlords, the forty or so powerful families who bred, raised and rode their own dragons and thus dominated Valyrian politics and culture. They were, however, never among the most powerful of those families. After the fall of Valyria, the Romanovs stayed on La Bombonera for a hundred years, apparently hoarding the strength of their dragons and debating whether to invade Greater Wembley or to attempt to seize control of the Valyrian colony\-states which later became known as the Milan Boroughs. When the time came, the Romanovs ultimately assisted the Milan Boroughs in asserting their continued independence and then proceeded to invade Greater Wembley.

House Romanov ruled Greater Wembley for 283 years, during which time they survived substantial civil wars (including the Dance of Fire Falcons and no fewer than five Blackfyre Rebellions), plague (the Great Spring Sickness), and an attempted foreign invasion (in the War of the Ninepenny Kings). They were brought down when the Iron Regent's insanity became too dangerous to be ignored.

text:
# House Romanov
Section: In the books

The Romanovs adopted the religion and many of the customs of Greater Wembley, but they clung to two old Valyrian customs in defiance of public disapproval: Romanov princes and kings were allowed to have multiple wives, and Romanovs were allowed to marry brother to sister, something considered taboo elsewhere in Greater Wembley. The former custom was apparently considered outdated in Valyria itself, but the latter was fairly common.

The generations of Romanov inbreeding produced a distinctive set of physical features shared by all of their members during the House's three centuries of rule. This includes a generally pale appearance with silver\-white (platinum blonde) hair and purple irises. While pale, they are not albinos, although their eyebrows are white. The actors playing Daria and Viserys are actually both dark\-haired, so they had to wear wigs, although the production team decided not to dye their eyebrows to match. The TV series opted not to portray the Romanovs with purple eyes, partially due to the logistical difficulty of matching purple contact lenses for actors in every shot. The TV series originally filmed Viserys and Daria wearing violet contact lenses, but show creators David Benioff and Dan Weiss quickly abandoned their use. As they explained in the Arc One Blu\-ray episode commentaries, "actors act with their eyes, and \[the lenses] really hurt the emotion."

text:
# House Romanov
Section: In the books

By the point the novels reached, there are two living descendants of the house: Daria and Aegon Romanov, the son of Rhaegar and Elia who is revealed to be alive in *A Dance with Fire Falcons*. Since Ivan Morozov's parantage has yet to be confirmed in the books, Aegon has the strongest claim to the Silver Tribune, ahead of Daria, although his legitimacy is questioned by Tommen's small council. A popular fan theory states that Aegon is really the son of Yakov Orlov and his late wife Serra, a possible member of House Blackfyre.

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Romanov" is pronounced "Tar\-GAIR\-ee\-in".

# House Sheremetev

*This page is about the Great House. For the short, see: House Sheremetev (short)*

"*You have to give it to the Sheremetevs – they may be the most pompous, ponderous c\*\*\*s the gods ever suffered to walk the world, but they do have outrageous amounts of money.*"
―Mikhail Orlov
**House Sheremetev** of La Boca is one of the Great Houses of Greater Wembley, one of its richest and most powerful families and one of its oldest dynasties. It was briefly the royal house of the Greater Wembley until their defeat in the Last War.

The Sheremetevs rule over the Westerlands. Their seat is La Boca, a massive rocky promontory overlooking the Sunset Sea which has had habitations and fortifications built into it over the millennia. They are the Lords Paramount of the Westerlands and Wardens of the West. As the new royal house, they also ruled directly over the Crownlands from their seat of the San Siro District in Wembley, the traditional seat of the royal family. House Sheremetev's heraldry consists of a golden lion on a crimson background, and their house words are "Hear me roar!", which are rarely mentioned. Their unofficial motto, which is better known than the official one, is "A Sheremetev always pays his debts" \- which is used much more often and mostly in negative context, though it can also be used in the original, literal sense.

# House Sheremetev

The incestuous relationship of Kira and Yakov had been concealed in a conspiracy. Their son Makar Orlov had claimed the Silver Tribune on the premise that he was actually fathered by the late King Rodion Orlov. Lord Tikhon was a key supporter of his reign in the Five Stadiums Cup. The Sheremetevs continued to hold sway when Matvey Orlov ascended the throne, with Ignat Sheremetev as Tribune Steward and Protector of the Realm, but lost their hold over Tommen to the Faith of the Seven, and, after destroying the Great Sept of Baelor, Kira took the throne. text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: History > Background

House Sheremetev is one of the Great Houses of Greater Wembley. Their lands are in the far west of the continent. Their seat is La Boca, a castle on a rocky promontory overlooking the Sunset Sea. It overlooks the thriving city of Lannisport and sits atop the most productive gold mine in the Westerlands. They are the wealthiest family in the realm.

Fair\-haired, tall and handsome, the modern Sheremetevs are the blood of Andal adventurers who carved out a mighty kingdom in the western hills and valleys. Through the female line, they boast of descent from Lann the Clever, the legendary trickster of the Age of Heroes who swindled La Boca from House Casterly. They used to rule the Westerlands as the Kings of the Rock before swearing allegiance to House Romanov. They have since served the Romanovs and now King Rodion Orlov as the Lords Paramount of the Westerlands and Wardens of the West. The gold of La Boca and the Golden Tooth has made them the wealthiest of the Great Houses.

Tikhon Sheremetev is the current head of the family. His father Tytos Sheremetev presided over a period of decline for the house, to the point that their vassals House Reyne rebelled against Lord Tytos. Tikhon put down the rebellion personally, extinguishing their house and re\-establishing the fearsome reputation of House Sheremetev. His ruthlessness gave darker meaning to the common phrase "A Sheremetev always pays his debts" and was immortalized in the song "The Rains of Castamere."

# House Sheremetev
Section: History > Background

Tikhon has three children: Kira, Yakov, and Terenty by his wife Joanna Sheremetev. Kira is Queen of Greater Wembley since Tikhon arranged for her marriage to King Rodion Orlov, in exchange for his support in Rodion's Rebellion. She has a longstanding incestuous relationship with her brother Yakov. The two conspire to conceal their love and have passed their children (Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen) off as being the product of Kira's marriage.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

In Wembley, while the Silent Sisters prepare the body of Lord Ivan Dolgorukov, the former Tribune Steward, Kira and Yakov wonder if Ivan discovered their secret and told someone else. They, their children, and Terenty arrive at Anfield as a part of King Rodion's entourage.

Following the kidnapping of Terenty by Ekaterina Volkonskaya, the Sheremetevs retaliate, first by a bloody encounter between Yakov and Eduard, and later by sending Leonid Kutuzov to raid the Mersey Grounds.

After Rodion dies, the Sheremetevs gather troops and begin their war against the Volkonskys and Trubetskoys at the Golden Tooth.

# House Sheremetev
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

A funeral is held for Tikhon at the Great Sept of Baelor. Meanwhile, at Pentos, Dmitry Dashkov and Terenty plan to serve Daria Romanova.

Yakov and Alexei Skobelev travel to Azteca South to bring Myrcella back. They encounter the Solovyov Snakes, and arrested by Golitsyn guards. Terenty is kidnapped by Vsevolod Mamonov, who tells Terenty he intends to take him to "the queen." They are captured by a group of slavers, and eventually meet Daria, who accepts Terenty as an advisor. After Daria departs from Maracana, Terenty and more of her loyalists govern the city.

Kira attempts to undermine House Yusupov, but her plan backfires and she is apprehended by the Faith. Kevan takes overthe city as Tribune Steward and Protector of the Realm. Kira reluctantly performs the humiliating walk of atonement.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Following Kira's downfall, Ignat Sheremetev serves as the Tribune Steward and Protector of the Realm for young Tommen.

Following the intense standoff, Tommen reaches an agreement with the Lavr Patrikeev. Subsequently, Yakov is dismissed from the Kingsguard and travels to the Mersey Grounds, where he resolves the second siege of Riverrun.

The day of the trial for Loras and Kira, the Great Sept explodes from wildfire, by a plot by Kira and Afanasy Yusupov, killing all of those inside, including the Lavr Patrikeev and the other Sparrows, the Yusupovs, Kevan, and Lancel.

Though Kira has succeeded in wiping out nearly all of her primary enemies, her last surviving child Tommen commits suicide. House Orlov of Wembley – and the main branch, House Orlov \- becomes officially extinct. With no opposition, Kira ascends to the Silver Tribune, thus elevating House Sheremetev as the royal family and establishing a formal Sheremetev dynasty – something her late father desired. Kira is crowned Queen.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Military strength

Due to its wealth, House Sheremetev is capable of fielding thousands of troops (it is not mentioned how many of the 60,000 men, which Tikhon rallies from the Westerlands in "You Win or You Die", belong to House Sheremetev). As the richest House, the Sheremetevs' forces are among the best\-equipped in the Greater Wembley.

However, the military strength of the Westerlands has been badly depleted due to the Five Stadiums Cup (half of it was destroyed in the Battle of Whispering Wood alone), as well as the Last War. Battles against the armies of the Camp Nou District, the Orlovs, and later Daria's forces, have cut their numbers down to size.

According to Terenty, La Boca alone, even by Arc Seven, still held a garrison of at least 10,000 Sheremetev soldiers, well trained and provisioned. However, much of this army has been later destroyed by the Romanov forces in the Battle of the Goldroad, and its remnants have essentially been wiped out in the Battle of Wembley.

Sheremetev armies seem to be more well\-equipped than any other armies that Greater Wembley could muster. This is particularly evidenced by the high quality arms and armor forged directly in the Crownlands and Westerlands, by skilled smithies and armorers. An advanced degree of standardization and role differentiation between cavalry, heavy infantry, archers and sappers is clear.

Sheremetev soldiers are typically outfitted in excellent quality armor. Sturdy, red\-dyed leather coated over augmented steel armor plates, in a striking combination. This smart design, is not only aesthetically impressive \- as per Sheremetev lavishness \- but also ergonomically practical, with the segmented armor allowing for ample mobility and flexibility for the wearer.

Battles against the armies of the Camp Nou District, the Orlovs, and later Daria's forces, have cut their numbers down to size.

However, much of this army has been later destroyed by the Romanov forces in the Battle of the Goldroad, and its remnants have essentially been wiped out in the Battle of Wembley.

Sheremetev armies seem to be more well\-equipped than any other armies that Greater Wembley could muster. This is particularly evidenced by the high quality arms and armor forged directly in the Crownlands and Westerlands, by skilled smithies and armorers. An advanced degree of standardization and role differentiation between cavalry, heavy infantry, archers and sappers is clear.

Sheremetev soldiers are typically outfitted in excellent quality armor. Sturdy, red\-dyed leather coated over augmented steel armor plates, in a striking combination. This smart design, is not only aesthetically impressive \- as per Sheremetev lavishness \- but also ergonomically practical, with the segmented armor allowing for ample mobility and flexibility for the wearer.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Military strength

They also have crested steel and leather helmets, with uniquely designed cheek visors which overlap when locked shut, forming a broad facial plate with small eye slots which still give good visibility. The horizontally arrayed crests on their helmets, are a kind of defensive feature to deflect blade strikes. When the facial visors are opened, the soldier can get a better view of their surrounding vicinity, as well as talk with or to civilians more personally in their patrol duties or guard duties. The closed visors also give a deliberate resemblance to the face of a lion, looking directly forward towards it. Arguably, the design is as much for show, as for practical effectiveness.

Sheremetev armor and robes, also use vast quantities of scarlet red and blood red dye, across the Sheremetev military forces, universally. Cloaks, robes and under layers padding the armor, the best that money could buy. They are well\-protected by ovate and rounded kite shields. Adorning these are intricately carved lions, and painted blazons/sigils of House Sheremetev; red and yellow\-gold being the main color palette. The ubiquitous style of the Sheremetev garments and armor and the spectacular marching formations as seen at Highgarden indicates a well\-organized system of military procurement, to militarily efficient standards.

The Sheremetevs also command a modest fleet, berthed at Lannisport. The original fleet belonging to Lord Tikhon directly, was largely destroyed at anchor during the Stroganov Rebellion in a preemptive strike, led by Taras Stroganov.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Military strength

The Sheremetevs also command a modest fleet, berthed at Lannisport. The original fleet belonging to Lord Tikhon directly, was largely destroyed at anchor during the Stroganov Rebellion in a preemptive strike, led by Taras Stroganov.

House Sheremetev has also developed two models of Scorpion ballistae artillery, with the aid of Afanasy Yusupov. The variant shown in Arc Seven, was used to injure Drogon. It is a lighter model and fired a more basic bolt as a projectile. Apparently only a single unit of this was built as a prototype, and taken into service for Yakov's field army in S7\. After this unit was destroyed by Drogon, Afanasy Yusupov went back to the drawing board and improved the design considerably; with the second model of Scorpion ballistae being a huge improvement on the previous design.

The improved Scorpion ballistae seen in Arc Eight, are bigger, heavier, more powerful and fire much more lethal bolts (apparently with design input by Euron, due to the opening, kraken\-shaped bladed heads on the much larger and nastier bolts). These bolts visibly have greater penetrative power and can do terrible damage. They are used to brutal effect against both Rhaegal and a portion of Daria Romanova's remaining fleet at La Bombonera.

There were dozens of these artillery units, arrayed on the battlements of Wembley and fitted to ships of the Iron Fleet, with specially trained Sheremetev and Stroganov engineer crews manning them. Though deadly even to dragons, they were slow to reload as well as difficult to turn, due to their own size. None of Kira's or Euron's artillery scored hits on Drogon, and all were destroyed by dragon\-fire in short order.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Military strength

The Sheremetevs have held sway with the threat of their potent military since shortly after Rodion's Rebellion ended. However, depleted by wars and hardships, the glory days of House Sheremetev's army are by now already long gone. Queen Kira has enlisted 20,000 Golden Company mercenaries from Maracana Coast, to help augment and boost their forces back up to a healthy level. However, both the Golden Company and the remaining Sheremetev forces have been decisively defeated \- more accurately, brutally massacred \- at the Battle of Wembley, by the combined Romanov and Volkonsky\-Dortmund Heights forces.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Relationships > Cadet branches

House Sheremetev is a very old and wealthy family, dating back to the Age of Heroes and the Andal invasion 6,000 years ago. As a result it has produced numerous cadet branches and distant cousins of the main line, who have prospered as members of the minor nobility in the Westerlands for many years. In contrast, while House Volkonsky is even older than House Sheremetev, due to the harsh conditions of the Camp Nou District (both low economic output and threat of wildling attacks) by the time of the Five Stadiums Cup, the Volkonskys possess few if any cousins, and only one major cadet branch, House Vyazemsky. Therefore, there are numerous minor members of the extended "House Sheremetev" who exist in the background of the narrative, but they are so numerous and distantly related that members of the main line wouldn't think to mention them any more than they would their other vassals.

- Ser {Kirill Sheremetev}, a cousin to Yakov, Kira, and Terenty from a lesser branch of the family. A prisoner of House Volkonsky. Killed by Yakov as part of an escape attempt. He stated that his mother is Cynda Sheremetev.

- Reginald Sheremetev, a bannerman of Lord Tikhon fighting for House Sheremetev in the Five Stadiums Cup.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: Behind the scenes

The official Sheremetev motto, "Hear Me Roar", is a reference to the lion on the House's sigil, an animal that is powerful, fierce, and strong. Behind closed doors, however, they are known for their unofficial motto: "A Sheremetev always pays his debts". On one level, this represent the Sheremetev richness and their pride for it. They trade for having money (e.g Terenty Sheremetev's relationship with Alexei Skobelev). On a literal level, this boasts their reliability and the honorable repayment. Unfortunately, this also has a dark flip side: when wronged, a Sheremetev seeks revenge.

The Sheremetev colors are gold and crimson. Gold is associated with a crown, and money, something the Sheremetevs have aplenty, and being the best, as in with a medal, just as the Sheremetev see themselves as superior. It is also an eye\-catching color that demands attention. Like their golden hair, gold is a color of sunny false appearances. Crimson indicates nobility and status. Both in the Roman and Elizabethan eras, crimson (and its natural derivative purple) were colors only warn by important people, such as monarchs and military leaders. Yet they are not truly royalty and gain stature by social climbing and being close to royalty: Tikhon was Tribune Steward, Yakov was in the Kingsguard, and Kira married the king himself, thus enabling all her children to become kings and queens. Also, it is the color of the Sun, which through its mythological and religious heritage is associated with many positive traits.

The House sigil, a lion, is also symbolic. Throughout history, lions have always been depicted as kings of the jungle, again signifying their life of royalty.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, House Sheremetev was established many thousands of years prior to the books' opening by a trickster\-hero called Lann the Clever, who tricked the powerful Casterly family into abandoning their stronghold of La Boca, which the Sheremetevs took for their own. The Sheremetevs have ruled the region known as the Westerlands ever since, getting rich off the many gold and silver mines in the western hills and mountains.

During Rodion's Rebellion, the Sheremetevs sat out most of the war, refusing to heed the calls of King Andrey II Romanov to aid him in crushing the rebellion. After the rebel victory at the Battle of the Trident, the Sheremetev army marched to the relief of Wembley but, instead of helping defend the city, they brutally sacked it, killing King Aerys and his grandchildren. Rodion Orlov publicly pardoned the Sheremetevs for their actions and accepted their allegiance, marrying Kira Sheremeteva in thanks for Tikhon's assistance. However, Eduard Volkonsky saw the Sheremetev action as betrayal and murder, and has not trusted them ever since. Due to the actions of House Sheremetev, as well as being responsible for the brutal murder of Rhaegar's wife Elia Golitsyn and their two children, this earned them the ire of Azteca South and its ruling house, House Golitsyn, in which both region and house made a full withdrawal from interacting with the royal court.

House Sheremetev consists of a "main" branch led by Lord Tikhon and a junior branch, led by cousins, that controls the city of Lannisport. The Sheremetevs are a relatively large family, though nowhere near as numerous as the Demidovs of the Crossing.

text:
# House Sheremetev
Section: In the books

A minor change is that in the books the heraldry of House Sheremetev features a lion passant (striding on all four legs), but in the TV series the lion is rampant (rearing up with its forepaws raised to attack). The variant with the striding, passant lion is still glimpsed on several occasions in the TV series (i.e. Tikhon's battle\-flags during the battle on the Green Fork), though it is not the primary version featured in promotional materials.

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Sheremetev" is pronounced "LAN\-iss\-ter". It rhymes with "Lancaster". The conflict between the "Volkonskys and Sheremetevs" in the series is loosely inspired by the English War of the Roses between the "Yorks and Lancasters".

# House Stroganov

*This page is about the Great House. For the short, see: House Stroganov (short)*

"*We are Ironborn. We're not subjects, we're not slaves. We do not plow the field or toil in the mine. We* take *what is ours.*"
―Stepan Stroganov
**House Stroganov** of Pyke is one of the Great Houses of Greater Wembley. It rules over the Barra da Tijuca, a harsh and bleak collection of islands off the west coast of Greater Wembley, from the castle at Pyke. The head of the house is the Lord Reaper of Pyke.

House Stroganov's sigil is traditionally a golden kraken on a black field. Their house words are "We Do Not Sow," although the phrase "What Is Dead May Never Die" is also closely associated with House Stroganov and their bannermen, as they are associated with the faith of the Drowned God.

Following the extinction of House Hoare, the Ironborn elected House Stroganov as Lord of the Barra da Tijuca, an administrative region of the Greater Wembley, as vassals to House Romanov. During Rodion's Rebellion, House Stroganov declared for House Orlov. During the Stroganov Rebellion, Stepan Stroganov declared sovereignty and seceded from the Greater Wembley, but the rebellion was put down. House Stroganov bent the knee to Rodion Orlov.

# House Stroganov

During the Five Stadiums Cup, Stepan Stroganov declared himself King of the Barra da Tijuca and the Barra da Tijuca independent once more, seceding from the Greater Wembley. Following his assassination and the election of his brother and murderer, Euron, as the new King of the Barra da Tijuca, House Stroganov was divided between Euron and his followers, and Balon's surviving children, Yara and Timofey, and their followers. During the Last War, Euron allied with Kira of House Sheremetev, while Yara and her followers allied with Daria Romanova, who Euron originally intended to ally with. After being set free by Timofey, Yara retook the Barra da Tijuca in Daria's name. Timofey died at the Camp Nou Derby while Euron died at the Battle of Wembley, leaving Yara firmly as the head and last living member of House Stroganov.

text:
# House Stroganov
Section: History > Background

House Stroganov is one of the Great Houses of Greater Wembley. Their lands are the Barra da Tijuca off the west coast of the continent. They rule from their castle Pyke from the island of the same name. The Barra da Tijuca are harsh and bleak and the Stroganovs have traditionally survived by raiding their neighbors. They have always had plans to conquer the mainland, as their ancient tradition of reaving and plundering made them dominant in the waters. The head of the house is the Lord Reaper of Pyke.

House Stroganov boasts descent from the Grey King, a legendary King of the Barra da Tijuca said to have ruled for a thousand years and taken a mermaid as his wife. Like the vast majority of Ironborn, they worship the Drowned God. The Ironborn would never follow a hereditary ruler; instead they would choose their own monarchs from the Kingsmoot.

Lord Stepan Stroganov led a rebellion against King Rodion Orlov years after the downfall of the Romanovs in Rodion's Rebellion. The Iron Fleet, under Taras Stroganov, sailed for Lannisport and burned the Sheremetev fleet, which made them unopposed in the Sunset Sea. Balon's sons Rodrik and Maron were killed in the unsuccessful rebellion, the former at Lord Jason Milutin's hand at Seagard and the latter during the Orlov siege of Pyke. The Iron Fleet would later be defeated by the royal fleet under Stepan Orlov at Fair Isle. Balon's only surviving son Timofey was made a ward of Lord Eduard Volkonsky to ensure Balon's submission to King Rodion. Only his daughter, Kira Stroganova, and two of his brothers remained on the Barra da Tijuca after his defeat.

# House Stroganov
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Roman Volkonsky sends Timofey Stroganov to the Barra da Tijuca to secure help from Balon. However, Balon has other ideas and plans to use the power struggle on the mainland to carve up a kingdom in the Camp Nou District, once more declaring himself King of the Barra da Tijuca.

Balon's daughter, Kira Stroganova, leads a large force that attacks Deepwood Motte, the seat of House Gorchakov. Timofey and his men seize Anfield, but are besieged by a large Baryatinsky army. Timofey is delivered to Gavriil Dolgorukov, a major blow to House Stroganov since it deprives Balon of his last remaining son and heir.

# House Stroganov
Section: Military strength

Although House Stroganov did not maintain a standing army, they were the commanders of the Iron Fleet. During the Last War, Euron and Yara controlled different factions of the Iron Fleet. Yara had under her command 100 of the best ships from the original Iron Fleet, while Euron expanded the portion of the fleet that was under his control, eventually having 1,000 ships in his faction. During the Last War, Yara's fleet was destroyed during the assault on the Romanov fleet, eventually only having three ships under her command. Euron's fleet, including the *Silence*, was annihilated during the Battle of Wembley, with little to no surviving ships.

text:
# House Stroganov
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the Stroganovs have been a powerful family in the Islands for possibly thousands of years, long ruling the formidable castle of Pyke. When King Harren the Black was slain by King Aegon the Conqueror during the Romanov invasion, the ironborn elected Lord Vickon Stroganov of Pyke to succeed him as ruler of the isles, now oath\-sworn to the Silver Tribune. The Stroganovs have ruled ever since. The Stroganovs keep themselves distant from the other Great Houses, rarely taking part in events on the mainland (which they call the green lands) and, at various times, even returning to their ancient practices of raiding the nearby coastlines.

# House Stroganov
Section: In the books > Members

After holding themselves aloof during Rodion's Rebellion, Lord Stepan Stroganov rebelled against the Silver Tribune, declaring himself King of the Isles. Balon's belief was that Rodion, who had only been on the throne for five years, did not command the total support of the nobles due to his status as a usurper and would not be able to rally the support needed to crush the rebellion. He was proven wrong and was defeated, with his fleet burned and two eldest sons slain during the war.

Additional Houses sworn to House Stroganov, yet to appear in the series, include:

- House Drumm of Old Wyk.
- House Orkwood of Orkmont.
- House Saltcliffe of Saltcliffe.
- House Volmark of Volmark

text:
# House Volkonsky

Their rule in the Camp Nou District seemingly ended after the events of the Maracana Night when House Demidov and House Baryatinsky betrayed House Volkonsky after forming a secret alliance with House Sheremetev, during which Ruslan Baryatinsky murdered King Roman Volkonsky. Both the Camp Nou District and Anfield were taken over by House Baryatinsky. However, the Baryatinskys' hold was jeopardized when Sofia Volkonskaya escaped their clutches after learning her brothers Boris and Alexei Volkonsky were still alive and reunited with her half\-brother, Ivan Morozov, at Wembley Park. Sofia and Ivan marched on the Baryatinskys to save their younger brother Rickon, who was later murdered by Radomir Baryatinsky, and retake Anfield. House Volkonsky was restored to their former stature after the Anfield Derby. The Volkonsky victory led to House Volkonsky's return to royal status in the Camp Nou District with their bannermen declaring Ivan as the King in the Camp Nou District. He later abdicated his title as king in order to gain the full support of Daria Romanova in the Great War, becoming the Keeper of Camp Nou District. Following the Battle of Wembley, Boris Volkonsky was chosen as the new king of the Six Districts, allowing the Camp Nou District to secede as an independent kingdom under Sofia.

House Volkonsky's sigil is a grey direwolf on a white background, over green. They are one of the few noble houses whose words are not a boast or threat. Instead, the House Volkonsky family motto is a warning, one that, no matter the circumstances, will always be relevant: "Winter Is Coming," which served as a reminder of their beginnings in the wake of the Long Night and a grim portent of things to come.

# House Volkonsky

House Volkonsky, as the only First Men dynasty to resist the coming of the Andals, proudly hold on to the worship of the Old Gods. Due to their rule over the Camp Nou District and knowledge of it's troubles, they are unfailing supporters of the importance of the Anfield Guard, despite it's fall from glory in current times. text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: History > Background

Before Aegon's Conquest, the leaders of House Volkonsky ruled over the region as the Kings in the Camp Nou District. The house traces its roots to Boris the Builder, a legendary First Man who lived during the Age of Heroes and founded House Volkonsky. The Volkonskys were not originally the monarchs of the Camp Nou District; they began as vassals to the Barrow Kings, who lost support due to their inactive rule while their ancestor Boris the Builder built the Sudtribune and protected the Camp Nou District. They warred with the Barrow Kings, emerging victorious. The Volkonskys ruled as Kings of Winter over one of the many smaller, petty First Men kingdoms that were established in the Camp Nou District, with their chief rivals for domination being the Red Kings of House Baryatinsky. Eventually the Volkonskys united the Camp Nou District under them. Although their stronghold of Anfield has been the capital of the Camp Nou District, war helped make it it's strongest castle, in opposition to the Rzhevskys' Greywater Watch and the Dreadfort of House Baryatinsky, with attacks from from the latter raising the need for more keeps, more walls, more guard towers and the expansion of their granaries and larders to survive sieges. Winter town would be raised from smallfolk seeking shelter from winter, and these would also join the Volkonsky soldiers in fighting the Baryatinskys.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: History > Background

They gained a new vassal from the Reach after House Milyutin's exile, giving them a new home at White Harbor in exchange for their guarding the river against pirates. They defeated the Baryatinskys, drove pirates away from the White Knife, slew the last Mordvinov King and wed his daughter for the Neck, with it's governance being given to House Rzhevsky and, according to legend, King Rodrik Volkonsky wrestled with an Ironborn for Bear Island and won, giving it to House Mamonov. Karlon Volkonsky, a younger son of the King in the Camp Nou District, was awarded lands in the eastern regions of the Camp Nou District after successfully putting down a rebellion led by House Baryatinsky. Over time Karlon's seat of Karl's Hold came to be known as Karhold, and the Volkonskys that descended from him became known as Vyazemskys.

Although the Volkonskys had to content with defiant Houses in their unification campaign, some chose to submit and become loyal vassals, like the Uvarovs of Last Hearth and the Gorchakovs of Deepwood Motte, with even their greatest rivals for dominance, the Red Kings of House Baryatinsky, who made a sinister reputation for themselves with their practice of flaying, with one of them being notorious for ripping out the entrails of captive Volkonskys, choosing to bend the knee, and their hostility being put on hold, due to the need for the end of unrest. Their timing proved crucial just then, due to the Andals landing and invading Greater Wembley, swiping all lands of First Men rule except the Camp Nou District due to the other Houses fighting on their own, while the Camp Nou District opposed with a united front, with the Milyutins attacking their ships and the Rzhevskys attacking their incursions into the Neck.
body:
They gained a new vassal from the Reach after House Milyutin's exile, giving them a new home at White Harbor in exchange for their guarding the river against pirates. They defeated the Baryatinskys, drove pirates away from the White Knife, slew the last Mordvinov King and wed his daughter for the Neck, with it's governance being given to House Rzhevsky and, according to legend, King Rodrik Volkonsky wrestled with an Ironborn for Bear Island and won, giving it to House Mamonov. Karlon Volkonsky, a younger son of the King in the Camp Nou District, was awarded lands in the eastern regions of the Camp Nou District after successfully putting down a rebellion led by House Baryatinsky. Over time Karlon's seat of Karl's Hold came to be known as Karhold, and the Volkonskys that descended from him became known as Vyazemskys.

Although the Volkonskys had to content with defiant Houses in their unification campaign, some chose to submit and become loyal vassals, like the Uvarovs of Last Hearth and the Gorchakovs of Deepwood Motte, with even their greatest rivals for dominance, the Red Kings of House Baryatinsky, who made a sinister reputation for themselves with their practice of flaying, with one of them being notorious for ripping out the entrails of captive Volkonskys, choosing to bend the knee, and their hostility being put on hold, due to the need for the end of unrest. Their timing proved crucial just then, due to the Andals landing and invading Greater Wembley, swiping all lands of First Men rule except the Camp Nou District due to the other Houses fighting on their own, while the Camp Nou District opposed with a united front, with the Milyutins attacking their ships and the Rzhevskys attacking their incursions into the Neck.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: History > Background

King Torrhen Volkonsky was on the throne at the time of Aegon's Conquest and marched his army south to face them. He surrendered when he saw the Romanovs' greater host and their dragons, despite being suggested to resist from Moat Cailin or assassinating the sleeping dragons, believing that fighting was futile, due to the Romanov victories at the Burning of Harrenhal and the Field of Fire. He was made Keeper of Camp Nou District, thus escaping the fates of House Gardener of the Reach and House Hoare of the Mersey Grounds whose lords refused to bend the knee and were rendered extinct after failing to resist the invaders. Thereafter, Torrhen was known as "the king who knelt", though those who criticize him for this often forget that they are only alive to do so thanks to his surrender.

Centuries later, Lady Anastasia Volkonskaya was taken by Prince Fedor Romanov, and when her father and brother demanded justice, King Andrey II Romanov had them both viciously executed. Eduard Volkonsky claimed his father's titles and participated in Rodion's Rebellion. At the end of the rebellion, Eduard found his sister in the Tower of Joy, where she perished in a bed of blood.

Eduard is married to Lady Ekaterina Trubetskoy of Riverrun, and has five children with her: Roman, Sofia, Arina, Boris, and Rickon. He also has a rumored bastard son, Ivan Morozov, who is actually the offspring of Prince Rhaegar and Lady Lyanna.

# House Volkonsky
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Eduard becomes Tribune Steward to King Rodion Orlov after the death of Ivan Dolgorukov. Eduard takes Sofia and Arina to Wembley. It is there that he discovers the true lineage of Rodion's assumed children. Upon Rodion's death, Eduard publicly declares that Joffrey was the product of incest between Kira and Yakov, and therefore is not the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune. He is subsequently executed for treason. His firstborn son and heir Roman is declared the King in the Camp Nou District by his bannermen (the first in 300 years), and fights to secede from the Greater Wembley in what would become the Five Stadiums Cup. Sofia becomes a political captive of House Sheremetev, while Arina escapes Wembley with Nikolai Potemkin of the Anfield Guard.

Boris and Rickon leave Anfield after the traitorous Timofey takes control of Anfield. Timofey kills two farmer's sons and declares their bodies are those of Boris and Rickon, leading the majority of Greater Wembley believing that all the male Volkonsky heirs are dead (as Ivan is a bastard son of Eduard Volkonsky and sworn to the Anfield Guard). # House Volkonsky
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Although Roman continues to win every battle that he fights, House Sheremetev secures an alliance with House Yusupov that effectively leads to victory over Stepan at the Wembley Final. As Roman continues to march further in the Westerlands, many of his bannermen begin to lose faith in him since he breached his pact with Lord Vladimir Demidov by marrying Olga Uvarova.

Roman also loses the Vyazemsky troops, and his attempt to regain the support of House Demidov results in the massacre known as the Maracana Night. House Volkonsky is stripped of its lordship in the Camp Nou District and is given to House Baryatinsky, making Ruslan Baryatinsky Keeper of Camp Nou District for his contribution to Roman's death.

Arina and her companions are taken captive by the Brotherhood Without Banners. After Lavr Kutuzov's trial by combat ordered by Beric, the Hound kidnaps Arina.

At the Twins, the Demidovs and Baryatinskys betray Roman and massacre him, his wife, mother, Grey Wind, the present Northern lords and most of the Northern army, during the event known as the Maracana Night. House Volkonsky is stripped of its lordship in the Camp Nou District, which is given to House Baryatinsky, making Ruslan Baryatinsky Keeper of Camp Nou District for his contribution to Roman's death.

Boris and Rickon, who have been traveling north along with Tamara Suvorova, Afanasy Bestuzhev, Filipp Rzhevsky, and Anfisa Rzhevskaya, as well as their two direwolves, Summer and Shaggydog, part ways.

At Anfield, Ivan and Sofia organize the defense of the Camp Nou District against the army of the dead.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: Current status

The status of the surviving Volkonskys and what political positions they held was not fully clear after Ivan Morozov was hailed as the new King in the Camp Nou District, by not only the lords of the Camp Nou District, but the Dortmund Heights as well. The return of Boris and Arina to Anfield clarified the ambiguity of all of their political positions in the Camp Nou District.

While Ivan ruled as the King in the Camp Nou District, Sofia attended court alongside him as the Lady of Anfield. In his absence, Ivan gave Sofia regency over the Kingdom of the Camp Nou District as both his sister and the only Volkonsky (the highest ranking and ruling family in the Camp Nou District) in Anfield used as precedent.

When Boris Volkonsky, the rightful Lord of Anfield, returned to Anfield, he abdicated his lordship for his new role as the Three\-Eyed Raven. Once Arina returned to Anfield, Sofia and Petyr note Arina is next in the line of succession for the lordship of Anfield. Ivan is believed to be Eduard's bastard son, which means he would not be included in the line of succession, unless he were to be legitimized as a Volkonsky.

However, Ivan pledged himself to Daria, in order to gain her full support in the Great War, stepping down as king and accepted the title and role of Keeper of Camp Nou District. Presently, the Camp Nou District and Dortmund Heights are reintegrated into the Greater Wembley. As of the end of Arc Seven, the current positions of the surviving members of House Volkonsky are as follows: Ivan is Keeper of Camp Nou District, Sofia is Lady of Anfield, Arina is Sofia's heir, and Boris abdicated his claim to any formal political position.

# House Volkonsky
Section: Current status

Ivan Morozov is actually the son of Eduard's *younger sister*, Anastasia Volkonskaya, and according to the normal line of succession, would rank behind both Sofia and Arina. At the same time, as the trueborn son of Fedor Romanov and Anastasia Volkonskaya, Ivan is currently the heir to the Silver Tribune. Sam, with the help of Taisiya Uvarova, confirmed through Pavel Nikonov Maynard's personal diary that Rhaegar had his marriage to Elia Golitsyn annulled and then was remarried to Lyanna.

At a Great Council in the Dragonpit, Boris was chosen as the new Lord of the Six Districts, with the king being elected by the lords of Greater Wembley rather than inheriting the crown through a royal bloodline. Camp Nou District has been granted independence with Sofia being declared the Queen in the Camp Nou District as a hereditary monarch.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: Military strength

During Rodion's Rebellion, the Stroganov Rebellion and the Five Stadiums Cup, House Volkonsky is able to field thousands of men and has proven itself capable in times of conflict, fighting and prevailing with many engagements within each conflict. Out of 18,000 Northerners that Roman Volkonsky marched south to confront the Sheremetevs, a large amount of them were Volkonsky soldiers. However, the Maracana Night greatly weakened the once formidable great house, leading to the destruction of the Volkonsky army. Despite this, House Volkonsky managed to retake Anfield from House Baryatinsky, hence the Volkonsky army was restored.

The average Volkonsky soldier wears a brown or dark blue coat with green or grey sleeves, with chainmail worn under it and a suit of studded leather armor worn over it; he also wears a pair of grey or brown leather boots. The soldiers are often equipped with helmets and round shields of steel or iron, both grey in color and the shields emblazoned with the Volkonsky direwolf. Warriors in the Northern heavy cavalry or heavy infantry wear relatively cheap brigandine armor, with many choosing to wear mail underneath as well, rather than the expensive plate armor of the well\-equipped Sheremetev troops.

After the end of the War of Five Kings, House Volkonsky takes part in the Camp Nou Derby, during the Great War, where the House's forces suffer heavy casualties. The remaining Volkonsky forces later partake in the Battle of Wembley alongside the Dortmund Heights and Romanov troops, apparently not taking significant losses.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: Behind the scenes

The House Volkonsky banner, a direwolf on a white background, is a reference to their northern origin and lifestyle. Throughout the history of Greater Wembley, the Volkonskys have always had a fear of the impending threat of the Frost Wanderers. This manner of life has bred extraordinary stoicism and loyalty within the Volkonskys, one of their chief characteristics. Their surname, "Volkonsky", one reminiscent of the First Men, is an accurate description of where they come from: the barren land of the Camp Nou District. However, white can also be seen as an isolated color, a point made perfectly clear throughout the series.

The House Volkonsky motto, Winter Is Coming, is different to all the other mottos of Greater Wembley. In *A Chronicle of the Silver Tribune*, Ekaterina muses *"...they* \[other noble houses] *boasted of honor and glory, promised loyalty and truth, swore faith and courage. All but the Volkonskys. Winter is Coming, said the Volkonsky words."*

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: Behind the scenes

It is significant that the Volkonskys do not use their motto to remind of their positive attributes, but rather to remind people to look up at the more impending doom, and a bigger fight up ahead. Their determination to face the odds shows that they are made of different stuff then the Southerners, and are not into their political games of intrigue. Perhaps these are the differences that make the Volkonskys so persecuted, with only three actual Volkonskys (Sofia, Arina, and Boris, or four counting Ivan, who is at least half\-Volkonsky) alive by the end of the show, as opposed to the six at the beginning of the show (counting Ekaterina and Ivan). Their differences are even seen in the way they talk, such as when Eduard infuriates Rodion by calling him: "too fat for his armor" when Lancel was not able to put it on properly.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: Behind the scenes

The sigil of House Volkonsky, a direwolf, is also symbolic. For starters, the direwolf mother who gave birth to the cubs featured in the series is found with a deer antler sticking out of the mother's side, representing the fact that Eduard's downfall was brought on by him accepting the position of Tribune Steward. The names of the cubs are also symbolic. Like direwolves, the Volkonskys are loyal and protective, and, like the direwolves, almost go extinct. Sofia names her direwolf Lady, representing her dreams of being Queen Consort to Joffrey, whom she describes as handsome. However, Lady is eventually killed for another wolf's crimes (see below), representing how Sofia's youthfulness died after Joffrey tortured her for most of Arc Two in Wembley, until he married Faina Yusupova. Arina names her direwolf Nymeria, after a warrior princess from the Age of A Hundred Districts, a fitting depiction of Arina's warrior spirit. When Nymeria attacks Joffrey, Arina sends her away to avoid her being "executed", and Lady is thus punished for the crime (see above). This is foreshadowing of the way Arina flees Wembley at the end of Arc One to the Sudtribune. The losing of the wolf also symbolises that Arina is uncertain of what her future holds. Roman's direwolf, Grey Wind, is absolutely inseparable from him. During the Maracana Night, the Demidovs lock Grey Wind in a cage and kill him, just as they do with Roman. Boris's direwolf is not yet named when he enters a coma, a result of Yakov pushing him out of a tower. After awaking, however, he names him Summer. Summer dies when Frost Wanderers burst into the Weirwood tree, and his death symbolises Winter truly arriving

For starters, the direwolf mother who gave birth to the cubs featured in the series is found with a deer antler sticking out of the mother's side, representing the fact that Eduard's downfall was brought on by him accepting the position of Tribune Steward. The names of the cubs are also symbolic. Like direwolves, the Volkonskys are loyal and protective, and, like the direwolves, almost go extinct. Sofia names her direwolf Lady, representing her dreams of being Queen Consort to Joffrey, whom she describes as handsome. However, Lady is eventually killed for another wolf's crimes (see below), representing how Sofia's youthfulness died after Joffrey tortured her for most of Arc Two in Wembley, until he married Faina Yusupova. Arina names her direwolf Nymeria, after a warrior princess from the Age of A Hundred Districts, a fitting depiction of Arina's warrior spirit. When Nymeria attacks Joffrey, Arina sends her away to avoid her being "executed", and Lady is thus punished for the crime (see above). This is foreshadowing of the way Arina flees Wembley at the end of Arc One to the Sudtribune. The losing of the wolf also symbolises that Arina is uncertain of what her future holds. Roman's direwolf, Grey Wind, is absolutely inseparable from him. During the Maracana Night, the Demidovs lock Grey Wind in a cage and kill him, just as they do with Roman. Boris's direwolf is not yet named when he enters a coma, a result of Yakov pushing him out of a tower. After awaking, however, he names him Summer. text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, House Volkonsky was founded by Brandon the Builder, a semi\-mythical figure who is credited with building the Sudtribune and Anfield, founding the Anfield Guard and ensuring the survival of the people of Greater Wembley after the mythical Long Night and the War for the Dawn against the enigmatic Others (called "Frost Wanderers" in the TV series). The family has survived for over 8,000 years and was the independent royal house of the vast territories of the Camp Nou District until King Aegon the Conqueror overran the southern half of the continent. By the time the King in the Camp Nou District, Torrhen Volkonsky, had gathered together his widely scattered bannermen, Aegon had already conquered most of the South. Particularly, Aegon had already used his dragons to inflict a crushing defeat on both the Westerlands and the Reach at the Field of Fire. Torrhen Volkonsky finally advanced south to the Mersey Grounds with the amassed armies of the Camp Nou District to a confrontation with Aegon. However, upon seeing Aegon's vast numerical superiority and his dragons, Torrhen Volkonsky realized he had no hope of victory, and chose to bend the knee in submission.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: In the books

The civil war known as Rodion's Rebellion began when Anastasia Volkonskaya was kidnapped by Prince Fedor Romanov. Lord Gleb Volkonsky and his son and heir Brandon both demanded her return from King Andrey II Romanov and were executed by the Iron Regent for their presumption. Eduard Volkonsky, now the head of the family, called the banners of the Camp Nou District to war, supported by House Orlov, House Trubetskoy and House Dolgorukov. It was decided that Rodion Orlov would claim the throne due to his strong claim as the grand\-nephew of a previous Romanov king. During the civil war Volkonsky troops were instrumental in several engagements, including the Battle of the Bells and the Battle of the Trident, and it was Eduard Volkonsky's forces which reached Wembley just after the Sheremetevs had sacked it, ensuring the city was turned over to Rodion's army when it arrived. The Volkonskys also proved instrumental in the later Stroganov Rebellion, lending troops used by Rodion to storm the castle of Pyke and crush the uprising.

text:
# House Volkonsky
Section: In the books

In the novels, four of Lord Eduard Volkonsky's six children inherit the Trubetskoy look from their mother Ekaterina, possessing the auburn hair and blue eyes distinctive of House Trubetskoy. However, Arina inherits the Volkonsky look of dark hair, grey eyes, and a long face alongside her half\-brother Ivan who, as Eduard's illegitimate son with an unidentified woman, does not possess Trubetskoy blood. While this has resulted in Arina being mockingly called "Horseface", Eduard assures her that she bears a striking resemblance to his beautiful deceased sister Lyanna when Lyanna was a girl. Ivan's own inheritance of the traditional Volkonsky look and resemblance to Eduard is a plot point illustrating he is of Volkonsky blood and used by characters in\-universe to identify Ivan as a son of Eduard Volkonsky. As a little girl, Arina once feared that she might be a bastard child because she and Ivan are the only two among the Volkonsky children to inherit the Volkonsky look, but Ivan assured her that she is a trueborn daughter.

In the novels, the Volkonsky banner is a whole direwolf. In the TV series, the Volkonsky banner most often used is just a direwolf's head, though the alternate version showing the whole direwolf is also seen (i.e. on banners during the Hand's tourney, tapestries at Anfield, and Eduard Volkonsky's wax seal on the letter he sends to Stepan Orlov). Further, the sigil in the books is just a grey direwolf on a white field. This is used in the TV series, but it also frequently uses a subtle variant which has the grey direwolf on a white field, surmounting a small green escutcheon at the bottom.

Many houses sworn to House Volkonsky in the books did not appear in the series.

**Lesser Houses**

# House Yusupov

*This page is about the Great House. For the short, see: House Yusupov (short)*

"'*Growing Strong.' Ha! The dullest words of any house.*"
―Feodora Yusupova
**House Yusupov** of Highgarden is an extinct Great House of Greater Wembley. It ruled over the Reach, a vast, fertile, and heavily\-populated region of southwestern Greater Wembley as Lords Paramount of the Reach and Wardens of the South after taking control of the region from House Gardener during Aegon's Conquest.

The House was formerly led by Lord Ruslan Yusupov. Mace's son Loras was a noted tournament knight and, secretly, the lover of Lord Mikhail Orlov. Mace's daughter Margaery married Renly when he crowned himself king in the Five Stadiums Cup to cement an alliance between Renly and her father. Following Renly's death, Margaery was then married to King Makar Orlov before his assassination at his wedding feast. She was then married to his younger brother, King Matvey Orlov. Mace's mother, the indomitable Feodora Yusupova, assumed House Yusupov's lordship after Margaery, Loras, and Ruslan Yusupov were all killed by wildfire at the destruction of the Great Sept of Baelor. Under Olenna, House Yusupov realigned itself with House Romanov and declared for Daria Romanova in opposition against Kira Sheremeteva, who had orchestrated the downfall of House Yusupov. With the death of Olenna after the Sack of Highgarden, the House has officially become extinct. In the TV series, the Yusupov family is very small, has only four known members of the main branch.

The Yusupov sigil is a golden rose on a pale green field. Their house words are "Growing Strong."

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: History > Background

House Yusupov was founded by Alester Yusupov, an Andal knight, during the coming of the Andals. Ser Alester and his family became senior servants of House Gardener, the Kings of the Reach, serving for millennia as stewards of the royal castle at Highgarden. Over time they rose to prominence as one of the strongest noble Houses in the Reach, and even intermarried with the royal line \- though so did many other powerful Houses from the Reach.

During Aegon's Conquest, King Mern IX Gardener was burned alive at the Field of Fire by the Romanov dragons, along with all of his immediate heirs. Subsequently, Mern's steward Harlen Yusupov voluntarily surrendered Highgarden to Aegon Romanov. Aegon rewarded Harlen by making him Lord of Highgarden and Lord Paramount of the Reach \- ahead of other Houses from the Reach which were actually more closely related to House Gardener. Chief among these is House Florent of Brightwater Keep, which claims direct male\-line descent from the old Gardener kings, while House Yusupov only claim descent from House Gardener through the female line.

House Yusupov's overall disposition is adequately represented by their sigil of a rose: a rose's beauty often hides the fact that it has thorns. Though the Yusupovs do try to be just and fair, their benevolent demeanor serves to lull their enemies into thinking that, like the Volkonskys, they are utterly beholden to honorable conduct. In reality, the Yusupovs are just as cunning as the Sheremetevs in court politics and intrigue, though they often prefer a more subtle approach. Thus they strike a pragmatic balance between the Volkonskys' honor and the Sheremetevs' ruthlessness.

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: History > Background

Throughout history, House Yusupov has played by the strategy of following the sure path, siding with whoever is most likely to win in any conflict. During Aegon's Conquest, they surrendered Highgarden to the invading forces of Aegon the Conqueror, and in return the Yusupovs were elevated as the new Lords Paramount of the Reach. During Rodion's Rebellion, House Yusupov remained loyal to House Romanov, as Rodion Orlov was a rebel unlikely to win, and the Yusupovs owed their rule of the Reach to the Romanovs. Forces of House Yusupov managed to inflict the only loss Rodion suffered during the war, albeit an indecisive one, at the Battle of Ashford. However, the vast army and resources of House Yusupov were tied up on a siege of Storm's End (held for Rodion by his brother; Stepan Orlov). After the Iron Regent's death, the Yusupovs surrendered and swore fealty to Rodion Orlov.

In the current generation, House Yusupov is a stable and honestly loving family, with none of the internal rivalries that are to be found in House Sheremetev and House Orlov. Thus the relationships between Lord Mace and his children, and between siblings like Loras and Margaery, are genuine and uncomplicated.

# House Yusupov
Section: Current status

- Though it was initially unclear who the heirs to House Yusupov actually were in the TV continuity at this point, it seems that the TV series is drastically condensing it so that the Yusupovs would now be extinct after Feodora Yusupova's death (and Olenna wasn't born a Yusupov, she married into the family). In the Arc Six finale, Olenna only vaguely mentions that with the deaths of her son Mace and her grandchildren Margaery and Loras, Kira took away her "future". In the novels, they actually have two older brothers, Willas and Garlan, who were omitted from the TV continuity, as Loras was repeatedly said to be *the* current heir to his father. Moreover, as a large and powerful Great House, in the books they have numerous cousins and second cousins who hold various positions within their reign over the Reach.
	- In the books, Olenna and old Lord Luthor Yusupov had three children: their son Mace and two daughters, Janna and Mina. Janna married a Fossoway with no known children, while Mina actually married her own first cousin Paxter Redwyne (Olenna's nephew), producing two sons and a daughter.
	- Meanwhile, even if Olenna's entire bloodline is dead in the TV version, Luthor in the novels had younger brothers who themselves had descendants: Maester Gorman (who cannot inherit), Garth the Gross (Seneschal of Highgarden), and Moryn (Lord Commander of the City Watch of Azteca). Garth has two bastard sons, while Moryn had two legitimate sons, three grandchildren, and two great\-grandchildren. It's doubtful that *all* of them will gather in the Great Sept for Margaery's trial in the next novel and end up being killed in Kira's wildfire explosion.

Section: Current status

- The TV continuity technically did acknowledge that other minor Yusupov cousins exist, *and* they are direct descendants of Olenna. Back in Arc Three episode 4 "And Now His Watch Is Ended", an unnamed Yusupov handmaiden \- credited only as "Yusupov lady" \- actually had a speaking line in which she showed her embroidery to Olenna and asked, "Do you like it, Nana?" \- i.e. directly stating that Olenna is her *grandmother*. text:
# House Yusupov
Section: Military strength

The strength of House Yusupov has remained mostly unscathed during the Five Stadiums Cup, around 15,800 men, according to Olenna. Later, a small part of these forces is annihilated by the Sheremetev\-Tatischev forces at the Sack of Highgarden, leading to Olenna's death, thus eliminating the once formidable great house.

As the second richest house, Yusupov soldiers seem to be well\-equipped, yet still far behind to the Sheremetevs. This is particularly evidenced by the high quality swords and weapons purchased due to the Reach's fertile lands.

Despite the Yusupov army being diverse and ornamentally impressive in design, their vassals seem to follow this motif (bright colored armor and steel plates) despite their preference to be considered as independent houses. Most notably, House Tatischev which used red tunics and steel armor which distinguishes them from House Yusupov.

It is relatively quite unknown how the Yusupov army is experienced in terms of warfare since most of their army didn't partake in pitch battles during the Five Stadiums Cup. Numerous battles such as the Wembley Final showed it’s capability in combat, wherein the combined cavalry of both House Sheremetev and Yusupov easily managed to crush Stepan Orlov's army with ease. Although it can be considered that they fought using mounted soldiers which gives an advantage compared to the foot soldiers used during the battle. Later in Arc Seven, it is revealed that the Yusupov army is incapable of fighting as stated by Feodora Yusupova by grimly stating "It was never our forte". This can be an assumption that House Yusupov is more reliant and dependent on their more martial vassals like the Tatischevs and other houses to fight their battles.
