- According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Yusupov" is pronounced "TI\-rul", as opposed to "Tie\-rell", etc. In spite of this, several characters, including Lady Olenna, have inconsistently alternated with pronouncing it "TIE\-rell". Even *within the same scene* in Arc Three's "Walk of Punishment," Kira says "Tie\-rell" while Tikhon says "Tih\-rul" (although since this different works to underscore their disagreement, it may be intentional for that one scene). When asked about this, official *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune* linguist David J. Peterson (creator of the Dothraki and Valyrian languages, who did not create the pronunciation guide) said that he personally pronounces it as "Tie\-rell", but has heard it both ways on the TV show \- given that he doesn't himself decide how to pronounce basic character names. He did offer that maybe, just as in real life, there are simply multiple ways to pronounce the same name.

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, House Yusupov is a powerful noble house. The Reach is the most populous region of the Greater Wembley, and the Yusupovs can field the largest army on the continent, although the Sheremetevs, being richer, can better equip their troops. This makes the Yusupovs formidable enemies but excellent allies.

House Yusupov never ruled as "kings and queens", as opposed to the Volkonskys, Sheremetevs, or Dolgorukovs. Before King Aegon I Romanov's invasion and unification of the Greater Wembley, the Yusupovs were stewards to House Gardener, the Kings of the Reach. The Yusupovs had responsibility for maintaining the castle of Highgarden, the seat of royal power in the Reach. In the battle known as the Field of Fire, King Mern IX Gardener and all of his issue were burned alive by Aegon's dragons. Harlen Yusupov, King Mern's steward, surrendered Obolensky to King Aegon and was rewarded with the title of Lord Paramount of the Reach and Warden of the South.

House Florent of Brightwater Keep has long disputed the suitability of the Yusupovs to the rule of the Reach because they can claim a closer blood\-relationship to the old kings of House Gardener. House Florent is a cadet branch of House Gardener, founded by a younger son of the main Gardener line, while House Yusupov can only claim descent from House Gardener through the female line.

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: In the books

As a result, the Florents have often bucked the authority of the Yusupovs in the past three centuries since the Romanov conquest. It came as little surprise when after Renly died and House Yusupov led their vassals in switching to support King Joffrey and the Sheremetevs, House Florent was the only major House from the Reach to switch allegiance to Stepan instead. Indeed, Stepan's wife, Selyse, is herself a Florent.

Thus the Yusupovs, while always maintaining firm control of the Reach, have always feared they have an uneasy grip on their rule. While the Yusupovs possess very fertile lands from which they can raise large armies, there are other powerful noble families in the Reach, such as House Florent, which don't particularly respect them the way the vassals of the Volkonskys and Sheremetevs respect them because they used to be their kings. A great deal of skill at court politics has thus been needed to keep the Yusupovs' powerful vassals in check, though Yusupovs like Lady Olenna possess this in abundance. Therefore, House Yusupov is always on the lookout to secure a marriage into a royal line, strengthen their prestige and cement their rule over the Reach.

The Golitsyns and Yusupovs have been sworn enemies for many generations. Over the centuries, they have fought border wars beyond count and raided back and forth across mountains and marches even when at peace. The enmity between the two houses waned a bit after Azteca South became part of the Greater Wembley, but the maiming of Willas Yusupov by the Dornish prince Yuriy Golitsyn in a joust fanned the animosity between the families, though Willas himself does not hold any grudge against Oberyn, as both men knew what happened was simply an unfortunate accident.
body:
As a result, the Florents have often bucked the authority of the Yusupovs in the past three centuries since the Romanov conquest. It came as little surprise when after Renly died and House Yusupov led their vassals in switching to support King Joffrey and the Sheremetevs, House Florent was the only major House from the Reach to switch allegiance to Stepan instead. Indeed, Stepan's wife, Selyse, is herself a Florent.

Thus the Yusupovs, while always maintaining firm control of the Reach, have always feared they have an uneasy grip on their rule. While the Yusupovs possess very fertile lands from which they can raise large armies, there are other powerful noble families in the Reach, such as House Florent, which don't particularly respect them the way the vassals of the Volkonskys and Sheremetevs respect them because they used to be their kings. A great deal of skill at court politics has thus been needed to keep the Yusupovs' powerful vassals in check, though Yusupovs like Lady Olenna possess this in abundance. Therefore, House Yusupov is always on the lookout to secure a marriage into a royal line, strengthen their prestige and cement their rule over the Reach.

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: In the books

As D.B. Weiss summed it up in a Arc Two featurette, in the current generation House Yusupov is a closet matriarchy of sorts. While dependable, honorable, and loyal, the men of House Yusupov aren't particularly intelligent or adept at politics. Instead, the female members of House Yusupov (such as Margaery and her father's mother, Olenna) are the intelligent ones who actively plan out the political course that House Yusupov will take. An exception to this is Lord Mace's eldest son, Willas, who, unlike his father and two younger brothers (Garlan and Loras), is said to be quite well\-educated.

Since being elevated to rule of the Reach, during any major Greater Wembley\-wide conflict, the Yusupovs have frequently judged a conflict and then followed the strategy of pragmatically siding with whoever seems most likely to win, rather than fighting for abstract principles of law or honor. During the Romanov Conquest, they surrendered to the Romanovs willingly in return for their favor. In Rodion's Rebellion, they sided with the Iron Regent because they owed the Romanovs everything, and didn't think Rodion Orlov could defeat him. During the civil war known as the Dance of the Fire Falcons, however, the Yusupovs judged that the faction of Rhaenyra Romanov and the faction of Aegon II Romanov were so evenly matched that it was not obvious at the outset which side would win. With neither side having a clear advantage over the other, to the surprise of both, the Yusupovs declared neutrality and took no part in the war (though their bannermen were heavily divided between the two sides).

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: In the books

In the books, as in the series, the Sheremetevs grow increasingly concerned with how much power the Yusupovs managed to gain. Ever since the second novel, the Yusupovs become the Sheremetevs' most important allies, and they take full advantage of that to increase their (and their bannermen) political power, slowly but surely.

Following the battle of the Blackwater, the Yusupovs are greatly rewarded for reinforcing the Sheremetev troops: Margaery is betrothed to Joffrey; Loras becomes a member of the Kingsguard; Mace is given a seat at the Stadium Board as Master of Ships; Garlan is granted the lands of House Florent. Two of the Yusupovs' bannermen, Paxter Rewyne, and Mathis Rowan, are also granted seats in the Stadium Board.

During the third book, Tikhon Sheremetev decides to restore Demyan Bagration (whom Terenty had previously sent to the black cells beneath the San Siro District) to the position of Grand Maester after he received word that the Citadel planned on naming Maester Gormon, born Gormon Yusupov, his replacement.

Following Tikhon's death, the Yusupovs grow bolder with their demands, among them to wed Margaery to Tommen shortly after his brother's death, much to Kira's annoyance. Kira's resentment toward the Yusupovs soon turns into mistrust, and then to paranoia, based on several items:

- Shortly after Terenty's escape, Afanasy Yusupov informs Kira that an ancient Yusupov coin was found in the cell of a jailer named Rugen (who is Dmitry Dashkov in disguise).
- Lady Taena Merryweather of Myr, wife of the newly\-appointed master of laws, tells Kira that her handmaiden Senelle is spying for Margaery and that Olenna pays merchants in Wembley with old coins which are only half the weight of newly minted gold dragons.

text:
# House Yusupov
Section: In the books

At first, Kira suspects that someone is seeking to drive a wedge between the Sheremetevs and Yusupovs; this may be the truth (in view of Dmitry Dashkov's statement at the end of the fifth novel), but Kira's paranoia soon overcomes her logic.

As Margaery's popularity and influence over Tommen grow, Kira suddenly realizes (correctly) that the Yusupovs had a motive to dispose of Joffrey. She becomes convinced that the Yusupovs plot to undermine the Sheremetevs; they conspired with Terenty to murder Joffrey, maybe to murder Tikhon too; they helped Terenty escape from jail; lastly, Margaery is the queen whom Maggy referred to. Driven by her paranoia, Kira plots to have Margaery charged with adultery and shamed in public. However, similarly to each and every scheme Kira comes up with, this one goes wrong too: the witnesses against Margaery prove to be false, and Kira finds herself in a much worse position than Margaery. Ironically, as a result of the scheme, the Yusupovs grow more in power.

Kevan, like his niece, is wary of the Yusupovs' power greed; however, he acknowledges that alienating the Yusupovs is a much worse option than complying with their demands. He chides Kira for rejecting Mace's request to become the King's Hand, reasoning that although Mace is hardly suitable for that office \- it is even more foolish to make him a foe.

text:
# Ivan Morozov

"*You've got the Camp Nou District in you. The real Camp Nou District.*"
―Semyon Apraksin
**Ivan Morozov**, born **Aegon Romanov**, is the son of Anastasia Volkonskaya and Fedor Romanov, the late Prince of La Bombonera. From infancy, Ivan is presented as the bastard son of Lord Eduard Volkonsky, Lyanna's brother, and raised alongside Eduard's lawful children at Anfield. Ivan's true parentage is kept secret from everyone, including Ivan himself, in order to protect him from those that sought the complete annihilation of House Romanov.

Ivan joins the Anfield Guard and is later elected as Lord Commander. As a result of several controversial decisions, such as allowing the wildlings to settle south of the Sudtribune, Ivan is murdered in a mutiny, but is resurrected by the red priestess Ekaterina Lomonosova.

Freed from his Anfield Guard vows, Ivan and his half\-sister Sofia Volkonskaya retake Anfield from House Baryatinsky, restoring House Volkonsky's dominion over the Camp Nou District. Ivan is declared King in the Camp Nou District.

Ivan negotiates with Daria Romanova for an alliance against the Frost Wanderers in the imminent Great War. Later he pledges himself and his army to Daria, with whom he falls in love, subsequently abdicating his throne and being named Keeper of Camp Nou District.

Later, Ivan learns his true lineage from Serafim Tatischev, revealing Daria is his aunt. A dragonrider whose dragon was Rhaegal, he fights in the Camp Nou Derby, during which the Midnight Regent is defeated and the return of the Long Night is prevented. Afterwards, Ivan aids Daria in her resumed campaign to take the Silver Tribune and participates in the Battle of Wembley. However, when Daria lays waste to a surrendered Wembley, Ivan tries but is unable to dissuade her from more destruction and assassinates her to prevent further carnage.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Background

"*His name is Aegon Romanov. If Rodion finds out, he'll kill him. You know he will. You have to protect him. Promise me, Eduard. Promise me.*"
―Anastasia Volkonskaya to her brother Eduard, speaking of her son Ivan Morozov.
Seventeen years before the Five Stadiums Cup, Fedor Romanov allegedly abducted Anastasia Volkonskaya in a scandal that led to the outbreak of Rodion's Rebellion. Rhaegar eventually returned to fight in the war, but not before leaving Lyanna behind at the Tower of Joy, guarded by Lord Commander Gavriil Obolensky and Ser Filipp Kornilov of the Kingsguard. Eduard Volkonsky rode to war along with her betrothed, Rodion Orlov, to rescue his sister and avenge the deaths of their father and brother at the orders of Aerys II, the Iron Regent.

Rodion ultimately killed Rhaegar at the Battle of the Trident, effectively ensuring their victory in the war. After the Sack of Wembley, Eduard continued south in search of his sister and ultimately found her at the Tower of Joy in the Red Mountains at the border of Azteca South. Eduard and his companions engaged in a final fierce melee with the remaining Kingsguard, which resulted in the deaths of all combatants save Eduard himself and Georgy Rzhevsky.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Background

After defeating the last of the Kingsguard, Eduard rushed into the tower to save his sister \- only to find Lyanna dying from childbirth, having just given birth to Rhaegar's own son. Desperate to protect the life of her newborn child, a fading Lyanna pleaded with Eduard to promise her that he would keep her son safe, and his true heritage hidden from Rodion as he had been Rhaegar's most bitter enemy. Furthermore, the boy's existence was a potential threat to Rodion's claim to the Silver Tribune after the deaths of Rhaegar's other children, Rhaenys and Aegon, by his wife Elia Golitsyn, who also perished, during the Sack of Wembley. In accordance with her last wish, Eduard resolved to pass Lyanna's son off as his own bastard and raise him in his home castle \- a great blow to his honor as he knew that his decision would shame both himself and his wife, Ekaterina Trubetskoy.

Rather than using his nephew's birth name of Aegon, which would have given away his real parentage, Eduard gave the baby the name "Ivan" after his great friend and mentor Ivan Dolgorukov, Lord of the Dortmund Heights, whom he loved like a second father. The boy also grew up using the surname "Snow", as is customary for acknowledged bastards in the Camp Nou District. In truth, however, "Ivan" is not a bastard at all, as Rhaegar apparently had his marriage to Elia annulled and married Lyanna.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Background

Ivan spent the next seventeen years being raised in Anfield as Eduard's illegitimate son, alongside his trueborn children with his wife. Understandably, Eduard never told anyone, including Ekaterina or Ivan himself, who his mother was or even if she was still alive. When pressed by Rodion, whom he couldn't deny an answer, Eduard vaguely claimed that Ivan's mother was a lowborn woman named "Wylla" that he met during the war. Eduard never treated Ivan much differently from his trueborn children.

Despite sharing a happy marriage, Ivan's presence at Anfield would serve as a constant source of friction between Eduard and Ekaterina. Ekaterina never mistreated Ivan, but she was cold towards him and avoided him whenever possible, viewing him only as a living reminder of the one time that Eduard had dishonored her. Ekaterina would later confess to her daughter\-in\-law Talisa about how Ivan caught the pox when he was a child, and she stayed with him through the night and prayed to the gods to let him live out of guilt for previously praying for his death, accepting that the boy was not to blame for her husband's sin, though it was still not enough to make her love Ivan, something she would eventually come to regret.

Ekaterina would later confess to her daughter\-in\-law Talisa about how Ivan caught the pox when he was a child, and she stayed with him through the night and prayed to the gods to let him live out of guilt for previously praying for his death, accepting that the boy was not to blame for her husband's sin, though it was still not enough to make her love Ivan, something she would eventually come to regret.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Background

Due to his bastard status, Ivan grew up feeling like an outsider at Anfield. Although Eduard would see that he was well\-treated, Ivan's attendance at Anfield's more "formal" occasions was restricted and he would even be barred from sitting inside at the Lord's table with his family so as not to offend important guests. Otherwise, Ivan still lived better than many bastard\-born children and was well\-raised by Eduard as his own. He was loved by his father and siblings, was never hungry or poor, lived in his father's castle, and had a noble's upbringing. Ivan received a highborn education from Maester Arseny Apraksin and a young lord's martial training from Anfield's master\-at\-arms, Ser Anton Karamzin.

Of the Volkonsky children, Ivan was very close friends with Roman \- given that they were roughly the same age, being regular companions in training and riding. He was also close with both Boris and Rickon, and was friendly rival to Lord Eduard's ward, Timofey Stroganov. However, Ivan's closest relationship was with Arina, who, as an adventurous tomboy prone to un\-ladylike pursuits, also felt like a social outsider. In contrast, Ivan's early relationship with Sofia was unpleasant; very much her mother's daughter, she was aloof and cold to him as well.

# Ivan Morozov

Ivan and Roman instruct Boris in archery, when their father receives word about a captured deserter from the Anfield Guard, for which the penalty is death. Ivan accompanies his father, Roman, Boris, Timofey, Rodrik, and Arkady Karamzin, Rodrik's nephew. out to the holdfast where the deserter, Will, is being held. It is Boris's first time watching his father carry out an execution, but as the deserter is brought into position outside, Ivan warns Boris not to look away, as their father will know. Ivan praises Boris afterwards for keeping his composure. On their way back to Anfield, they find a dead direwolf \- a species not seen south of the Sudtribune in centuries \- and her newborn pups.

Ivan talks Eduard into allowing the young Volkonskys to adopt them, pointing out that a direwolf is the sigil of House Volkonsky: given that there are five direwolves and five trueborn Volkonsky children, it must be a sign that the Volkonsky children are meant to have the pups. In order to make this point, Ivan intentionally leaves himself out of the count of Volkonsky children, and when Boris asks about this, Ivan responds that he is not a Volkonsky. Just as they are about to leave, however, he finds the runt of the litter, an albino, which crawled away from its mother's corpse. Timofey remarks, "The runt of the litter, that one's yours, Snow." Ivan takes this direwolf as his own, naming him Ghost.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Ekaterina ensures that Ivan, Roman, and Timofey are groomed for the arrival of Rodion and Queen Kira Sheremeteva. Ivan, in particular, is set against the altering of his appearance, as well as expressing antipathy against the royal family. When the Orlov entourage arrives, Ivan is present, but is not allowed to attend the subsequent banquet for fear of offending the royal guests (on Ekaterina's suggestion). He waits outside in the courtyard venting his frustrations against a practice dummy. When Ivan's uncle, Andrei Volkonsky, arrives, Ivan tells him he has been thinking about it, and before his father leaves for the south he wants to join the Anfield Guard.

Since they don't care about recruits' pasts and even a bastard can rise to positions of high honor in it, the Watch provides an easy escape from his life in Anfield. He later meets Terenty Sheremetev. As a dwarf, Terenty knows what it is like to be an outcast, so he gives the young man some advice: never try to hide what he is, for the world will not forget. Instead, he should wear the name "bastard" openly, like armor, and then it can never be used to hurt him. When Ivan angrily asks Terenty what he knows about it, Terenty replies that "all dwarfs are bastards in their father's eyes."

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Before departing, Ivan has a run\-in with Yakov Sheremetev, who infamously killed his grandfather, the Iron Regent. Yakov sarcastically thanks him for protecting all of them from the mythical monsters that allegedly exist beyond the Sudtribune, in order to taunt him. Before Ivan departs for the Sudtribune, he says goodbye to the unconscious Boris, who has been injured in a fall. He gives Arina a sword named Needle that he had made especially for her, advising her to "stick them with the pointy end." Ivan says he will miss her, and they both hug.

As he prepares his saddle, Roman asks if Ivan said goodbye to Boris and is sure Boris will survive. Ivan says Volkonskys are hard to kill, and Roman asks about his mother, and Ivan assures him she was kind. Roman offers to visit him at the Sudtribune sometime, and they bid farewell with a hug. At their parting on the Kingsroad, Eduard vows to tell Ivan the truth about his mother the next time they meet. Ivan is accompanied by his uncle Benjen and Terenty, who has expressed a desire to see the Sudtribune (and urinate from the top of it) before he dies. Ghost also accompanies Ivan to the Sudtribune.

At Wembley Park, Ivan's expectations of the Anfield Guard are soon disappointed. Instead of a brotherhood of noble warriors sworn to defend the realm from wildlings and Frost Wanderers, he realizes the Watch is a dumping ground for criminals and wastrels. He earns the enmity of Ser Makar Tchaadayev, the master\-at\-arms in charge of training new recruits. He humiliates his fellow recruits with his superior fighting skills, learned from Anfield's master\-at\-arms over the course of many years.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Benjen stands with Ivan on his first watch and tells him that he is going ranging Camp Nou District of the Sudtribune. Ivan is keen to accompany him, but Benjen insists that he complete his training. Terenty helps Ivan see that he is no better than the recruits, but has been afforded more advantages than them due to his highborn upbringing. Ivan offers to train some of his new brothers and Oleg Razumovsky and Osip Repnin accept. He also befriends the fat and bookish coward Serafim Tatischev when he arrives at Wembley Park, and helps to protect him from the cruelty of Tchaadayev. Tchaadayev angrily tells Ivan that going easy on Sam won't help him, and will risk getting him killed during the next winter.

After completing his training, Ivan is inducted into the Anfield Guard and swears his oath before a weirwood Heart tree on the north side of the Sudtribune. He is assigned to the stewards rather than the rangers, and at first, thinks it is due to his ongoing feud with Tchaadayev. However, Sam points out that Lord Commander Luka Mamonov has asked for Ivan as his personal steward, and may be grooming him for command. Ivan is concerned when Benjen's horse returns to the Sudtribune riderless. Later, Ghost finds the corpses of two rangers assigned to Benjen, Othor and Jafer Flowers. Learning of Eduard's imprisonment, Tchaadayev taunts Ivan about being a traitor's bastard, causing Ivan to draw a knife in anger. He is restricted to quarters.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Later, Othor's corpse becomes a wight and attacks Mamonov. Ivan saves Mamonov's life by burning the wight, earning a pardon for his earlier misdemeanor. Mamonov also gives Ivan his Baltic alloy sword, Longclaw \- given that his own son Jorah fled into exile and left it behind. Ivan ponders abandoning the Watch to join Roman's army when it marches against the Sheremetevs, but Akim Romanov tells him that he chose to stay with the Watch when he was similarly tested \- as he is secretly a long\-forgotten great uncle of the Iron Regent, and was once known as Akim Romanov *Romanov*, but his entire family was killed at the end of Rodion's Rebellion.

News of Eduard's execution reach Wembley Park. Ivan immediately leaves, meaning to join Roman and seek vengeance for his father's death. Samwell, Oleg Razumovsky, and Osip Repnin intercept him and convince him to stay. Mamonov tells Ivan their war against the Frost Wanderers is more important than the contest of tribunes in Wembley. He tells Ivan that the Watch is marching beyond the Sudtribune in force, to find Benjen and learn the truth about the threat. Ivan swears to him not to attempt to desert again and accompanies the troops as they set out.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Mamonov prepares Ivan for a command role as the great ranging travels Camp Nou District seeking Benjen and an explanation for the wight attack. They pass through several abandoned wildling villages before arriving at the home of their unsavory ally Rostislav Trubetskoy.

Ivan is perplexed when he learns that Rostislav Trubetskoy incestuously marries his own daughters, but apparently has no sons. He takes an instant dislike to Rostislav Trubetskoy when they meet with him. Rostislav Trubetskoy reveals to Jeor that he has not seen Benjen, and that the wildlings are gathering with their leader, King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune Serafim Bestuzhev. Jeor reprimands Ivan for failing to follow his lead with Rostislav Trubetskoy \- the man disgusts him as well, but unfortunately, he's one of the few wildlings who is willing to give them shelter and supplies which mean the difference between life and death for many black brothers in the wild.

Sam appeals to Ivan to aid Rostislav Trubetskoy's pregnant daughter\-wife Taisiya Uvarova. She is afraid of having a son, but will not say why. Ivan is frustrated and refuses to disobey Jeor's order to leave Rostislav Trubetskoy's wives alone. Ivan sees Rostislav Trubetskoy carrying a newborn into the woods and follows him. He sees Rostislav Trubetskoy leave the child for a Frost Wanderer but does not recognize the creature hidden in the shadows. Rostislav Trubetskoy spots him and knocks him out. Rostislav Trubetskoy disarms Ivan and drags him back to his keep. He expels the rangers from his home. Jeor reveals that he knew that Rostislav Trubetskoy was sacrificing his sons, but chose to ignore it because of his usefulness as an ally of the Anfield Guard.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

The rangers reach the ancient fortified peak known as the Fist of the First Men and await Prokhor Shuisky and his party from the Shadow Tower. When Prokhor Shuisky arrives, he suggests altering their tactics and using small groups to overcome Mance's lookouts in the Skirling Pass. Ivan asks to join Prokhor Shuisky's raiders and Jeor lets him go.

Prokhor Shuisky leads his men into the pass, and they locate and ambush the wildling watchers. Ivan realizes his opponent is a young woman and hesitates to kill her. She introduces herself as Uliana Vorontsova, but does not give away details of Mance's plans. Prokhor Shuisky leaves Ivan alone to execute Uliana Vorontsova. Ivan is unable to do it and she escapes. He pursues and recaptures her, but they become separated from Prokhor Shuisky's group. Ivan decides they cannot regroup with Prokhor Shuisky due to the approaching night. Uliana Vorontsova convinces Ivan to sleep next to her to share body heat and keep warm, and then makes sexual advances towards him. Ivan rejects the temptation to break his oath.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Ivan unties Uliana Vorontsova's legs, while keeping her hands bound, as he continues his search for the rest of the raiders. She tells him that she knows that he is a virgin. As they walk, Uliana Vorontsova questions Ivan as to why the men of the Anfield Guard hate the wildlings. She explains that both the Free Folk and the Northmen like the Volkonskys are descendants of the First Men, and the wildlings just happened to be on the wrong side of the Sudtribune when it was built. She urges him to forget about his oath and live free. Another sexual advance from Uliana Vorontsova prompts him to reach for his sword. She backs away and trips him with the rope, when he is caught off guard.

He pursues her but is ambushed and taken captive. Uliana Vorontsova tells him that he should have taken her when he had the chance. Uliana Vorontsova brings Ivan to the Klim Kostomarov, and convinces him that Mance will want to question Ivan. The Klim Kostomarov has a prisoner of his own; Prokhor Shuisky. The Halfhand tells Ivan that the rest of the men were killed while they searched for him. He urges Ivan to make their deaths meaningful and become a spy within the wildling ranks. He then feigns anger with Ivan until he is restrained after managing to knock Ivan over.

In Anfield, after Timofey betrays House Volkonsky and takes the castle, he refuses to flee and join the Anfield Guard when he is surrounded by Gavriil Dolgorukov's men, claiming that Ivan will likely kill him for betraying the Volkonskys and apparently burning Boris and Rickon alive (in actuality, Timofey faked their deaths).

As they make their way to Mance, Uliana Vorontsova continues to playfully mock Ivan by tapping him on the head with the flat of Longclaw. Prokhor Shuisky uses the distraction to advance his plan to portray Ivan as a traitor to the Anfield Guard. He attacks Ivan, and the Klim Kostomarov allows them to fight. text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

As Ivan is led by Uliana Vorontsova and the Klim Kostomarov into the main wildling camp in the Frostfang mountains, he discovers that almost all of wildling society is on the move to escape the Frost Wanderers, including the women and children. As they enter the camp, Ivan is shocked to see a real\-life giant walk past. Many of the wildlings are surprised to see Ivan in his all\-black Anfield Guard clothing and shout "crow!" at his approach. Several young boys pelt Ivan with ice and small stones but Uliana Vorontsova shoos them away.

Ivan is led into the tent of the King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune, Serafim Bestuzhev, where the Klim Kostomarov explains that he is Eduard Volkonsky's bastard son to a large man with a heavy beard who is eating chicken by the fire. He says he doesn't care, but his interest is piqued on hearing that Ivan killed Prokhor Shuisky Halfhand. As they talk Ivan kneels before the man, whom he assumes to be Serafim Bestuzhev, and calls him "your Grace." This causes all of the wildlings to burst out laughing. As it turns out this isn't Mance, but his lieutenant Semyon Apraksin Giantsbane. The real Mance is an unassuming man sitting in a corner, who then introduces himself and tells Ivan to stand, as no man kneels before another among the Free Folk, since they do not recognize a class of nobility in their culture.

Mance says he is glad that Ivan killed Prokhor Shuisky, as he had killed many of Mance's wildlings. Ivan says that he wants to leave the Anfield Guard, because he is disgusted that Mamonov already knew what Rostislav Trubetskoy was doing but did nothing to stop it. Ivan states that the First Men he is descended from defeated the Frost Wanderers once during the Long Night, and that now he wants "to fight for the side who fights for the living." Mance is satisfied and advises Ivan to get a new cloak, his black one clearly attracting malignity.

Ivan then marches south with the Free Folk army. Mance explains that his army is a diverse force, formed of about ninety different groups or clans of wildlings, who speak seven different languages, and have numerous internal rivalries. However, he managed to unite them all by telling them the truth: that they will all die if they remain north of the Sudtribune. Mance brings Ivan to one of his scouts, Ruslan Witte. He is sitting silently with his eyes rolled back as an eagle circles above him. Mance says that he is a "warg."

Mance orders Semyon Apraksin to take a force of twenty men to scale the Sudtribune to attack Wembley Park from its exposed rear. Mance's plan is for Semyon Apraksin's small band to distract Wembley Park by attacking their exposed southern side, at which point Mance's main army will assault it from the north. Semyon Apraksin will know that Mance is in position when his army makes a massive signal fire. Mance orders Semyon Apraksin to take Ivan with him, as Ivan knows the layout of Wembley Park, and it will prove a key test of his loyalty: if it turns out that he won't really betray the Anfield Guard, Semyon Apraksin can easily throw him off the Sudtribune to his death.

On their way to the Sudtribune and Wembley Park, Ivan and Uliana Vorontsova are gathering firewood, when the warg Ruslan Witte asks him about the defenses of the Anfield Guard. Ruslan Witte has seen through the eyes of his eagle that there are patrols on top of the Sudtribune and he wants to know how frequent they are. Ivan says they usually sent out patrols in teams of four, two builders to inspect for structural damage and two rangers to protect them, but that the frequency of their patrols often changes. Ruslan Witte says the wildlings know there are nineteen castles along the south side of the Sudtribune, but he wants to know how many are currently manned.

Ivan finds this very unpleasant, but reluctantly says that only three are currently manned. Apart from Wembley Park, there is also Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea at the extreme eastern end, and the Shadow Tower at the western end. Ivan is then asked how many men currently garrison Wembley Park. Ivan is very reluctant to answer, but after being threatened by Ruslan Witte, he gives an exaggerated number, saying there are one thousand men (this is a lie, as Wembley Park only had six hundred men before the great ranging, and the garrison now is closer to three hundred). Semyon Apraksin tells Ivan that he likes him, but if he is lying to them, he will rip his guts out through his throat. Despite this, Ivan remains steadfast to the lie.

Ivan and Uliana Vorontsova then walk away, but she steals his sword Longclaw, making him chase her to get it back. She leads him into a nearby cave. Uliana Vorontsova starts disrobing, and says that she wants to make sure Ivan has truly come over to the wildlings' side and broken his Anfield Guard vows \- by making him break his oath of celibacy with her. She quickly shucks off all of her clothes and walks up to him naked. Ivan is very hesitant at first, but they soon end up having sex in the cave. Afterwards, Ivan and Uliana Vorontsova lay together in a naked embrace, and Uliana Vorontsova tells Ivan she wishes they could stay in this cave forever.

# Ivan Morozov

He joins a wildling party led by Semyon Apraksin Giantsbane to climb the Sudtribune. Beforehand, he is questioned by Uliana Vorontsova about their relationship and his allegiance to the Anfield Guard, saying that he must be loyal to her instead. During the climb, Uliana Vorontsova causes part of the ice to break, leaving them hanging in the air by the rope. Ruslan Witte, believing them to be lost, cuts it. Ivan manages to save himself and Uliana Vorontsova by climbing back to the ice. The two return to the climb and reach the top, where Uliana Vorontsova gazes at the north side and the south side, before they kiss.

After surviving the perilous climb of the Sudtribune, Ivan, Uliana Vorontsova and the wildlings led by Semyon Apraksin Giantsbane advance through the Gift \- the strip of land immediately south of the Sudtribune which the Watch draws supplies from \- and continue on towards Wembley Park, to await Serafim Bestuzhev's signal to begin the attack. Afterwards, Ivan confronts Ruslan Witte about cutting his and Uliana Vorontsova's rope loose on the Sudtribune, nearly killing both of them in the process. Ruslan Witte tells Ivan that he doesn't see Uliana Vorontsova complaining about what happened, because she is a wildling and understood what needed to be done in a pressure situation, also telling Ivan that this is the reason he will never be able to keep her.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

During the journey through the woods, a jealous Ruslan Witte confronts Uliana Vorontsova and says that he would be a better man for her than Ivan, while continuing to express his distrust in him. Later, Ivan tries to persuade Uliana Vorontsova that the wildlings can't win an attack against the realms but she refuses to listen and points out that Ivan is now one of them; if it fails, so does he. She restates her passion for him and tells him bluntly that if they die, they die, but before they die, they will live.

Ivan and the wildling party prepare to raid an elderly horse breeder's home for his horses and gold; Ivan insists that the old man is no threat to them, but Ruslan Witte and Semyon Apraksin Giantsbane intend to kill the man so as to stop him from alerting the Anfield Guard to their presence. However, when the party attacks the farmstead, Ivan surreptitiously hits a rock with his sword, alerting the old man who flees; Ivan also distracts Uliana Vorontsova when she tries to shoot the fleeing man with an arrow. Outside, Semyon Apraksin moves to kill the old man, but Ruslan Witte tells him to have Ivan do it instead to prove his loyalty. Ivan is ultimately unable to kill the innocent man, and instead, Uliana Vorontsova kills the man with an arrow.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Realizing that Ivan is still loyal to the Anfield Guard, Semyon Apraksin orders his men to kill Ivan; Semyon Apraksin restrains Uliana Vorontsova to stop her trying to help Ivan, and soon after Ivan battles with Ruslan Witte. In the nearby Queenscrown, a hidden Boris enters the mind of Summer to aid Ivan. as he battles to the death with Ruslan Witte and finally kills him. With the last of his strength Ruslan Witte wargs into the mind of his pet eagle, which swoops down and attacks Ivan, clawing him badly about the face before he fights the bird off. Ivan then steals a horse and escapes, leaving a heartbroken Uliana Vorontsova and heading back to the Sudtribune.

Stopping to rest and tend to his injury, Ivan is confronted by a furious Uliana Vorontsova, who has an arrow ready to shoot him. Ivan tries to talk Uliana Vorontsova out of shooting him, insisting that he still loves her. Though his feelings are clearly reciprocated Uliana Vorontsova is still angered by his betrayal and shoots Ivan three times with her bow as he flees from her. Ivan is badly injured, but his horse manages to carry him the rest of the way to Wembley Park, as he hovers in and out of consciousness. Having reached safety, Ivan is brought inside the castle by the guards, where he encounters Sam and Oleg Razumovsky, who are overjoyed to see him and insist that his injuries be taken care of.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Ivan survives the injuries inflicted by Uliana Vorontsova and has largely recovered, though he still grimaces while getting dressed. At some point, Ivan has been told about his half\-brother Roman's death at the Maracana Night and wanting vengeance for his family, but decides to stay at the wall. He shares with Sam that he had always been jealous of Roman for having more of their father's affection and for being better than him at riding, fighting, and winning the affection of other girls. Still, he says he could never bring himself to hate Roman, as he was also always a good friend and honorable person. Sam responds by saying he has felt the same way about Ivan, that Ivan is better than him at everything (except reading).

It turns out that Sam had been sent to retrieve Ivan, who has been summoned to testify before a panel of five sworn brothers, including Maester Akim Romanov, acting Lord Commander Makar Tchaadayev, and Gavriil Stolypin (who was exiled to the Sudtribune by Terenty). At the hearing, Ivan admits to killing Prokhor Shuisky, living amongst the wildlings, and sleeping with one. He also states that Mance intends to attack and gives intel on his plans and strength. Both Stolypin and Tchaadayev are openly hostile to Ivan, disbelieving much of what he says and call for his execution. Akim Romanov, however, realizes that Ivan is speaking the truth, and the hearing ends with Ivan being allowed to keep his head.

Meanwhile, at the Dreadfort, when Timofey is pressed by Ruslan Baryatinsky for information on the whereabouts of Boris and Rickon, he reluctantly guesses that they may try to head to Ivan at Wembley Park. At Radomir's suggestion, Ivan becomes a target of the Baryatinskys, since Radomir reasons that even though Ivan may be a bastard, he is still a son of Eduard Volkonsky, and may pose a threat to the Baryatinskys' future hold on the Camp Nou District, either because the Northerners who are still furious at the Baryatinskys for betraying the Volkonskys may rally behind him even though he is a bastard in the Anfield Guard, or because Ivan may simply seek revenge on both Ruslan and Radomir for their role in the Volkonskys' downfall at Maracana Night. Ruslan subsequently sends his hunter, Georgy Gagarin, to the Sudtribune in order to infiltrate the Watch, use Ivan to find Boris and Rickon and then kill them all, promising a lordship as a reward.

The orphan Roman Stolypin then arrives at Wembley Park, telling them how the wildling raiding parties south of the Sudtribune killed his entire village. Tchaadayev asks for Ivan's opinion on protecting the smallfolk living in the Gift, thinking Ivan will disagree with his decision not to send help. Instead, Ivan regretfully says that he knows from his time with the wildlings that this exactly what they want \- to lure as many of them out of Wembley Park as possible to weaken its defenses for the massive attack about to come from the north side of the Sudtribune, which would allow them to move over a thousand miles southward before they reached an army that could stop them.

Therefore, Ivan agrees with Tchaadayev that they should do nothing, and concentrate every available man in Wembley Park itself to brace for the assault. Ivan gives a speech about avenging Mamonov's death at the hands of the mutineers and this convinces a number of his brothers to join him in his attack, including Osip Repnin, Edd, and Georgy Gagarin (who secretly intends to kill Ivan during the mission and blame it on the mutineers).

The group attacks at night, taking the mutineers by surprise. Ivan personally enters the main building to deal with Rodion Skobelev. The two of them are evenly matched, though Karl manages to get the upper hand by spitting in Ivan's face and then kicking him to the floor. Before he can land the finishing blow, Karl is stabbed in the back by Sissy. Karl attempts to kill her, though it's a fatal mistake as Ivan doesn't miss the opportunity to thrust Longclaw through the back of Karl's head and out of his mouth.

After the fight, Ivan and the others count five dead amongst the Watch, including Georgy Gagarin, whose neck was snapped in a way that terrifies Ivan (Ivan being completely unaware that Georgy Gagarin had been killed by a Boris\-possessed Afanasy Bestuzhev). He then reunites with Ghost, before turning to Rostislav Trubetskoy's wives and offering them refuge at Wembley Park. They decline, saying that after the abuse they took at other members of the Anfield Guard they can't trust them and will go their own way. Before leaving, they set a torch to Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep, burning it to the ground.

Before he can land the finishing blow, Karl is stabbed in the back by Sissy. Karl attempts to kill her, though it's a fatal mistake as Ivan doesn't miss the opportunity to thrust Longclaw through the back of Karl's head and out of his mouth.

After the fight, Ivan and the others count five dead amongst the Watch, including Georgy Gagarin, whose neck was snapped in a way that terrifies Ivan (Ivan being completely unaware that Georgy Gagarin had been killed by a Boris\-possessed Afanasy Bestuzhev). He then reunites with Ghost, before turning to Rostislav Trubetskoy's wives and offering them refuge at Wembley Park. They decline, saying that after the abuse they took at other members of the Anfield Guard they can't trust them and will go their own way. Before leaving, they set a torch to Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep, burning it to the ground.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Ivan and his fellow black brothers return to Wembley Park, much to the annoyance of Tchaadayev and Stolypin. Once Alliser spots Ghost, he orders Ivan to lock up Ghost or his direwolf will become food for the Anfield Guard. Later, Ivan reports that Serafim Bestuzhev's army was closing in on Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep and will reach the Sudtribune before the next full moon. Ivan states that defending the tunnel is hopeless since the gates will not stop the giants in Serafim Bestuzhev's army. He proposes they seal the tunnel, but Makar Tchaadayev refuses to listen. Alliser then assigns Ivan and Sam to night duties atop the Sudtribune until the next new moon.

News of the wildling attack on Mole's Town, the largest village in the Gift, reaches Wembley Park. Ivan, Oleg Razumovsky, and Platon Tolstoy try to comfort a distraught Sam, who believes that Taisiya Uvarova and her baby are dead. Osip Repnin is furious that the wildlings slaughtered the inhabitants of Mole's Town, which included brothers of the Anfield Guard. Ivan concludes that if Mole's Town has been attacked, then Serafim Bestuzhev's assault on Wembley Park is imminent.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Atop the Sudtribune, Ivan and Sam are staring out into the darkness of the north and awaiting the imminent wildling invasion. Sam attempts to interrogate Ivan about what it was like to be with a woman, stating that as their deaths are likely imminent, it may be his last chance to find out. Sam brings up that the vows of the Anfield Guard only explicitly forbid members from taking wives or producing children, and that other "activities" are open to interpretation. Ivan replies glumly that Alliser most likely does not care about their interpretations. When further pressed by Sam to describe lying down with Uliana Vorontsova, Ivan attempts to explain but is unable to properly express it, proclaiming exasperatedly that he is "not a bleeding poet." Ivan offers to take the watch up alone so Sam can go below.

Later that night, Ivan hears the horn blowing and looks north, witnessing a tremendous conflagration north of the Sudtribune, just as Mance had promised him. Ivan approaches Tchaadayev, who finally relents and admits that they should have heeded his advice and sealed the tunnel, but grimly muses that leadership means not second\-guessing oneself because of "clever little twats" like him. While they start to prepare for the massive wildling army that is emerging from the woods, another horn blows from down below at Wembley Park, signaling the unanticipated appearance of Semyon Apraksin's band of wildlings at Wembley Park.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Alliser decides to go down and defend the keep, leaving Stolypin in charge of the Sudtribune's defenses. Even though a wildling strike force led by two giants, one of which is riding a mammoth, charge towards Wembley Park's outer gate, Stolypin does nothing and breaks down, demoralizing the troops. Osip Repnin steps in by falsely claiming that Alliser needs Janos back down in Wembley Park, allowing Ivan to take command of the Sudtribune's defenses, silently thanking Osip Repnin. The black brothers continue to rain down arrows on the advancing wildlings, even killing ones that are attempting to scale the Sudtribune.

Dongo, armed with a massive bow, manages to fire a huge arrow at one of the bunkers atop the Sudtribune, and Ivan is unable to warn his brothers fast enough before the giant fires again, violently killing one of his black brothers. Although Ivan manages to repel most of the wildlings attacking the outer gate, including the mammoth, one giant manages to single\-handedly lift the gate. Ivan, knowing the inner gate won't hold against him, sends a group of black brothers led by Osip Repnin to hold it at any cost. Ivan decides to give Edd control of the top of the Sudtribune, and tasks Sam with releasing Ghost from his pen to assist in the fighting, then orders half a dozen other men to descend with him and finally enter the fray.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Ivan quickly dispatches many wildlings with Longclaw, catching the attention of Sergei Bagration, Magnar of the Thenns, and so the two meet in single combat. Sergei Bagration eventually gets the upper hand by knocking Longclaw away, then Ivan disarms Sergei Bagration of his axe using some chains, and the fighting goes hand to hand. Sergei Bagration brutally smashes his face into an anvil and tosses him into the blacksmith's forge. However, when Sergei Bagration picks Ivan up and begins to strangle him, Ivan spits blood in Sergei Bagration's face, distracting him long enough for him to grab the blacksmith's hammer lying next to him and bury it into Sergei Bagration's skull.

Upon killing him, Ivan turns around to find Uliana Vorontsova pointing her bow at him with an arrow drawn. He smiles at her, causing her to hesitate. Before either can say anything, Uliana Vorontsova is shot through the heart by Roman Stolypin. Ivan holds her in his arms as she tells him that they should have never left the cave, and they lament circumstances that prevented them from being together as she succumbs to her wound.

Later, while Edd forces the wildling army to retreat for the night, down below Ivan deals with a heavily wounded Semyon Apraksin, who continues to fight despite being the only wildling left alive in the castle. Ivan subdues him with a crossbow and orders his brothers to take him prisoner and interrogate him. The following morning, Ivan discusses with Sam his suicidal solution to end the wildling threat: he plans to assassinate Serafim Bestuzhev, noting that he is the only thing binding the disparate wildling clans that make up the army, and his death will rob them of that purpose and leadership.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Sam tries to stop him, but to no avail. As Ivan prepares to leave via Wembley Park's tunnel, they discover the bodies of the black brothers who held the inner gate against the giant. Osip Repnin is amongst the casualties, and Ivan tells Sam that all bodies must be burned. Before Ivan leaves, he remembers the promise he made to Luka Mamonov and decides to leave Longclaw with Sam. Sam tells Ivan to come back, and Ivan looks and Sam and gives him an unsure smile before stepping out into the wilderness on the other side of the gate. Ivan finds Mance in a wildling camp north of the Sudtribune, and claims he wants to negotiate with him.

Despite Mance expressing disappointment at Ivan's betrayal, they drink a toast to some of their fallen friends, such as Osip Repnin, Uliana Vorontsova, and Mag the giant. Mance then notices that Ivan is eyeing a cooking knife, and quickly deduces that Ivan came to parley with Mance simply so he could assassinate him. Before anyone can make a move, they are interrupted by the sound of war horns. Outside, hundreds of mounted knights led by Stepan Orlov and Nikita Ushakov arrives and slaughter many of the wildlings, scattering the rest.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Ivan introduces himself to Stepan as Eduard Volkonsky's son, and suggests that Stepan arrest Mance instead of executing him, reasoning that Mance had the chance to kill him, but chose not to. Out of respect for Eduard, Stepan accepts, and Ivan also advises Stepan to burn the bodies of the dead in order to prevent them from returning as wights. During the funeral, Ivan notices Ekaterina Lomonosova staring at him through the flames. Later, Ivan visits Semyon Apraksin, who tells Ivan that Uliana Vorontsova truly loved him, and asks him to lay Uliana Vorontsova to rest north of the Sudtribune. Ivan later takes his love's body into the woods and burns it, weeping as he walks away.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Ivan spars with Roman Stolypin, along with other new recruits before being summoned by Ekaterina Lomonosova to see Stepan atop the Sudtribune. He questions the Red Woman if she is cold, as she is dressed in unusually light clothing for the local climate, but she states that "the Lord's fire" lives within her. Ekaterina Lomonosova asks if Ivan is a virgin. Ivan replies he is not, which she approves. Ivan meets with Stepan and Davos, kneeling before the king. With Ruslan Baryatinsky ruling Anfield, Stepan asks Ivan if he wants to avenge his fallen half\-brother.

Ivan reaffirms that he is a sworn brother of the Anfield Guard. Davos states that his loyalty to the Watch is considered dubious because of his time spent with the wildlings. Nevertheless, Stepan wants Ivan to retake the Camp Nou District with the help of the wildlings, stating that he will pardon them and declare them citizens of the realm once the war is won. Stepan will give the wildlings their lives and freedom if Mance bends the knee and swears his loyalty. He gives Ivan until nightfall to convince Mance, or the King\-Beyond\-the\-Sudtribune will be burned as a sacrifice to the Lord of Light.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Ivan does his best to convince Mance to save his life as well as all the wildlings, but fails: the wildlings only follow him because he kneels to no one, so if he did kneel to Stepan, they would lose all respect for him and ignore his commands anyway, so he might as well die with his honor intact by refusing. As Mance is led to the pyre, Stepan gives him one last chance to save his life. Mance politely refuses and is led to the stake and Ekaterina Lomonosova lights the pyre. Unable to watch Mance suffer, Ivan storms off. Just as the fire begins to fully consume Mance, he is mercifully shot through the heart with an arrow by Ivan.

Stepan and Davos summon Ivan to discuss his future. Stepan shows him a letter delivered by messenger\-raven from Anastasia Mamonova saying she would only pledge her House to a member of House Volkonsky. Stepan offers a simple solution: as king, he will officially legitimize Ivan and make him Lord of Anfield. Later that day, the choosing for the new Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard has begun, and many brothers of the Anfield Guard have assembled to vote for either Tchaadayev (who is fervently supported by Janos) or Ser Ratmir Milutin commander of the Shadow Tower.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

After hearing from Ivan that he intends to refuse Stepan's offer and stay true to his vows, Sam nominates Ivan as the third candidate and recounts how he took command of the defense of Wembley Park (including the fact that Tchaadayev fought bravely and Stolypin was cowering in the pantry with Taisiya Uvarova) and was willing to sacrifice himself to stop Mance. With the votes cast, Akim Romanov and his aide tally the tokens and a tie is declared between Ivan and Tchaadayev. Akim Romanov feels around in his hands for his voting chip and produces a circle token and adds it to Ivan's stack amidst cheers and laughter, as Ivan has been chosen as the 998th Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard.

Ivan is approached by Stepan and Davos about the offer of legitimization. As the new Lord Commander, Ivan reminds the king that his place is with the Anfield Guard, even though his dream was to be a Volkonsky. Stepan, a man of duty, respects his decision to keep his vow and tells Ivan he intends to march on Anfield within a fortnight since the Anfield Guard cannot afford to feed both his army and the wildling prisoners. He also recommends sending Tchaadayev to command Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea], and that executing the wildling prisoners would be the safest choice. Stepan then leaves, but Davos stays behind and tries to further persuade Ivan to help Stepan retake the Camp Nou District. Davos iterates that the Anfield Guard is "the shield that guards the realms of men", telling Ivan that it may not just mean protecting the Greater Wembley from beyond the Sudtribune, but possibly taking part in battles in order to prevent the Greater Wembley from suffering, such as the Camp Nou District will under Baryatinsky rule.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

During Ivan's first general meeting of the garrison in the main hall as Lord Commander, he starts with some levity by assigning a black brother to oversee the digging of a new latrine pit. He also acknowledges Ser Makar Tchaadayev as an experienced and valuable member of the Anfield Guard by naming him First Ranger. Ivan then orders Stolypin to man and repair Greyguard, a ruined castle. Janos refuses to obey and Ivan reminds him that this is a direct order. Janos then refuses him a third time and Ivan asks Janos if he's refusing to obey the order. Janos publicly insults him, telling Ivan, "You can stick your order up your bastard ass." Ivan orders Janos to be taken outside, and calls for Roman Stolypin to fetch him Longclaw, while Janos insists Ivan is mistaken if he thinks he can frighten him.

Obedience to the laws of his "father" \- that the man who passes the sentence must swing the sword \- Ivan makes ready to personally behead Janos. While on the chopping block, Janos begins to plead for mercy. After a moment of hesitation, Ivan executes the cowardly former Commander of the City Watch with a single blow. From across the courtyard, Stepan sees Ivan behead Janos for refusing his orders, and slightly nods in approval.

Ivan continues to train new recruits, with Stepan, Selyse, Shireen, and Ekaterina Lomonosova observing him, with Stepan implying that he does not believe Ivan to be Eduard's bastard son \- saying that Eduard was always an honorable man and it wasn't in his character to randomly have sex with some tavern whore. Later, Sam presents him with requests to the Northern Lords for men for the Anfield Guard.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

He is reluctant to send one to Ruslan Baryatinsky, his brother's killer, until Sam convinces him that they must stay neutral and ask for as many men as they can for the Watch, and right now the Baryatinskys rule the Camp Nou District and have the most men \- leading Ivan to sign the request angrily. Ekaterina Lomonosova enters his office and again tries to persuade him to chase the rats out of his home, but he claims that Wembley Park is now his home. She attempts to seduce him, sensing a power inside his blood, but Ivan rebuffs her, remembering his love for Uliana Vorontsova. As Ekaterina Lomonosova leaves, she tells him, "You know nothing, Ivan Morozov."

Later on, Ivan consults Akim Romanov for advice on a hard decision he is about to make, noting that half the men in the Anfield Guard despise him for his sympathy for the wildlings, but Akim Romanov tells him to "Kill the boy, and let the man be born," in other words, just make the hard choice and do what he believes is best. Indeed, Ivan's plan is to allow the wildlings to pass the Sudtribune and settle in the Camp Nou District as subjects of the Greater Wembley or even let them join the Watch. Ivan's idea is met with harsh criticism, even from his closest friends such as Edd and Roman Stolypin, but Ivan's goal is actually to keep the wildlings from falling into the hands of the coming Frost Wanderer army. Ivan points out that every single wildling left on the north side of the Sudtribune will be killed, then resurrected and added to the Frost Wanderers ever\-growing army of the undead.

Ivan speaks alone with Semyon Apraksin, who reveals that the remainder of Mance's army probably fled back to Hardhome, a large fishing village on the coast. Ivan requests that Semyon Apraksin go there and negotiate with the remaining wildling chieftains, to let them pass through the Sudtribune on Ivan's terms. Semyon Apraksin agrees, so long as Ivan accompanies him so that the wildlings will know it is not a trap. Ivan borrows several of Stepan's ships for the journey (as he is marching inland and won't be using them). Later, as Stepan prepares to leave Wembley Park for Anfield with his army, Ivan thanks him for his help, promises him he will have his ships back, and watches Stepan depart for Anfield to take his childhood home back from the Baryatinskys.

Ivan later prepares to leave Wembley Park with Semyon Apraksin and a group of black brothers including Edd. He entrusts the care of the Anfield Guard to Tchaadayev, who criticizes his mission, and says his farewells to Sam, who gives him a bag of dragonglass daggers in case he should run into Frost Wanderers on the way. He hugs Sam for what might be the last time and leaves Wembley Park on his mission.

Later at Anfield, Radomir mentions to Sofia that Ivan has been made the new Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard, citing Ivan as an example of a bastard who rose high in the world, claiming that if Ivan did it, then so can he.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Ivan reaches Hardhome with his companions. After Semyon Apraksin kills the Klim Kostomarov for challenging him, he and Ivan go inside a hut to speak with the leaders of the clans. Though the wildlings are prepared to kill Ivan for murdering Mance, Semyon Apraksin stands up for him and reveals that Ivan killed Mance out of mercy. Ivan offers to share the dragonglass weapons with the wildlings and allow them to settle on land south of the Sudtribune if they promise to aid the Anfield Guard in the coming battle against the Frost Wanderers: even if they and all the men of the Greater Wembley are not enough to stop them, they can at least die fighting. Five thousand wildlings agree while the rest decide to stay, though Semyon Apraksin hopes more will come around with time.

However, as they are preparing to leave, they are all attacked by an army of wights. Ivan fights his way to the hut to retrieve the dragonglass daggers, but he is ambushed by a Frost Wanderer. They fight for a while and Ivan is almost killed until he retrieves Longclaw. To the surprise of both Ivan and the Frost Wanderer, Longclaw doesn't shatter from the cold of the Walker's weapon when he uses it to parry his attack \- because it is made of Baltic alloy, forged with dragon\-fire and spells. Ivan quickly regains his ground and slashes the Frost Wanderer with it, making it shatter into a cloud of ice particles, and revealing that the Frost Wanderers can also be killed by Baltic alloy.

Edd helps Ivan to his feet and they make it back to the boats to Stepan's ships, with the wights refusing to follow them in the water. But as they leave, the Midnight Regent himself appears at thousands of e wharf and shares a long glance with Ivan, at the same time using his magic to raise all of the dead as wights before Ivan's eyes. Ivan looks on in obvious terror, as he knows the slaughter he just witnessed is merely a prelude to what is coming for all of Greater Wembley.

Ivan and the others make it back to the north side of Wembley Park on foot, and he makes himself seen by Tchaadayev so that they will be let inside. Tchaadayev hesitates but ultimately relents and orders the gates to be opened. As the wildlings are let through Wembley Park into the Greater Wembley, Ivan laments not being able to save the rest, while Sam comforts him, reminding him that he at least saved a few, who would have died too if he did nothing. Tchaadayev, however, warns Ivan, telling him that his kind heart will get him killed. Indeed, as Ivan looks around, he sees almost all of his brothers looking at him scornfully, among them Roman Stolypin, Nikita Panin, and Matvey Mordvinov.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Ivan discusses with Sam the war against the Frost Wanderers, and his increasingly strained relationship with the rest of the Anfield Guard. Sam asks for leave to take Taisiya Uvarova and her baby with him to Azteca, where he will train to become a maester. Sam reasons that he is better suited to the life of a maester than a warrior, and that the Anfield Guard needs to fill the gap left by the late Akim Romanov Romanov. Ivan is reluctant, as he has few friends nowadays, and also points out that as a maester, Sam's vow of chastity will be doubly prevalent, before finding out that Sam and Taisiya Uvarova have had sex already (to Ivan's amusement). Ivan eventually agrees to Sam's request and sees him off.

Davos returns to Wembley Park to beg Ivan for soldiers \- though this was really just a ruse to get Davos out of Stepan's camp, because he had become so desperate that he gave in to Ekaterina Lomonosova's request to burn Shireen as a sacrifice.

Ivan points out that the Anfield Guard, even if they do ally with Stepan, will not be enough, and the wildlings will not fight for Stepan as it isn't their fight. Their argument is broken up by the arrival of a wearied and addled Ekaterina Lomonosova \- who abandoned Stepan when it became apparent he would lose the battle in the ice. When Davos questions her about Stepan and Shireen, she says nothing yet her sorrow is manifest, all but confirming the demise of his king and princess. Still forlorn and at a loss for words, Ekaterina Lomonosova heads inside the castle, leaving both Ivan and Davos horrified at the news.

That night while reading messages, Roman Stolypin comes to Ivan and tells him one of the wildlings knows of the whereabouts of his uncle Benjen, who has been missing since before the great ranging. Ivan quickly follows Tchaadayev to a gathering of his Watch brothers, only to find a sign marked "Traitor." Tchaadayev, Yarwyck, Mordvinov and two other black brothers proceed to stab Ivan while uttering, "For the Watch." As the wounded Ivan kneels, gasping for breath, Roman Stolypin tearfully comes forward and after a few moments of pause, stabs Ivan in the heart and declares, "For the Watch." Ivan collapses and dies from his wounds before the mutineers leave him out in the cold to bleed out.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Upon seeing the body of his dead master, Ghost howls in mourning from his pen. His cries summon Davos, Edd and a handful of other black brothers who quickly move Ivan's body to his quarters. They quickly realize that Tchaadayev was most likely the orchestrator of Ivan's demise, and free Ghost to help them protect Ivan's body while Edd leaves to find Semyon Apraksin and the Wildlings. Ekaterina Lomonosova also looks at Ivan's body and claims that she had seen a vision of him fighting at Anfield, though Davos remains adamant that Ivan is gone for good. Tchaadayev later approaches Davos and the loyal brothers with a promise of amnesty if they throw their weapons down and surrender, though they refuse to back down, despite Tchaadayev's threats of death if they don't.

After being rescued by Edd and the wildlings, Davos goes to Ekaterina Lomonosova and asks if there's any magic she knows of that can resurrect Ivan. Shaken by Stepan's death, she says all she believed in was a lie. Davos states that he wasn't asking the Lord of Light for help, but Ekaterina Lomonosova herself. Ekaterina Lomonosova then performs a ritual with Ivan's body: cleaning his wounds, cutting some of his hair, trimming his beard, and burning it in the fire, all while chanting in High Valyrian. Her attempts seem to be in vain. Semyon Apraksin storms out in frustration, those remaining leave the room one by one, and after a few moments alone with Ghost, Ivan awakens, gasping for air.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Coming back to his senses, Ivan is accosted by Davos and Ekaterina Lomonosova. He reflects on his perceived failure in spite of doing the right thing, but after some encouragement from Davos, Ivan gets dressed and enters the courtyard to the surprise of everyone present, reuniting with Semyon Apraksin and Edd. Later, the leaders of the mutiny are rounded up for execution. After hearing last words from each (with the exception of Roman Stolypin), Ivan once again acts in accordance with his father's law that "the man who passes the sentence should swing the sword" and personally cuts the trapdoor rope, hanging them simultaneously.

Technically free from his vows, Ivan then passes his cloak and command to Edd, declaring his intent to leave the Anfield Guard.

A day later, Ivan packs his belongings. Edd chastises him for abandoning the Anfield Guard despite the threat of the Frost Wanderers looming, and reminds Ivan of the oath he swore. Ivan retorts by saying that he already died, and that he couldn't stay after what was done to him. His half\-sister, Sofia arrives after escaping Radomir with help from Timofey, along with Elena Tatischeva and Klim Panin. Ivan is initially stunned when he sees Sofia but they tearfully embrace. Shortly thereafter, Ivan and Sofia talk inside while Sofia eats. The two share their lives since leaving Anfield, and reminisce about their childhoods. Sofia regretfully mentions how awful she was to Ivan during their youth, and that she felt guilty about it for years. Ivan shrugs it off as childhood mischief, though he forgives Sofia after she presses the issue. The pair acknowledge that their last haven is Anfield, and even then, the Baryatinskys are currently occupying it, but Ivan is reluctant to fight again after everything he's been through.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Later, as Ivan eats with Sofia, Brienne, Podrick, Semyon Apraksin, and Edd, he receives a letter from Radomir, informing him that he is holding Rickon prisoner and furiously demanding the return of Sofia on threat of massacring Ivan's allies, raping Sofia and murdering Rickon and Ivan. Ivan notes Radomir's signature and Sofia deduces that Ruslan Baryatinsky is dead. Ivan asks Semyon Apraksin how many men he has; Semyon Apraksin says 2,000, not enough to fight Radomir's 5,000 by themselves. With some urging from Sofia to rally the Northern Houses still loyal to the Volkonskys, Ivan resolves to take Radomir down.

While discussing strategy with Davos, Ekaterina Lomonosova, Sofia, Brienne, Edd, and Semyon Apraksin, Ivan bitterly notes that they simply don't have the numbers to challenge the Baryatinskys at present. Even though the three most powerful houses are already backing the Baryatinskys, Ivan suggests rallying the weaker houses, as their combined strength would give them a numerical advantage when combined with his current forces. When Sofia mentions Viktor Trubetskoy's recapture of Riverrun and the virtual guarantee of support from the Trubetskoys, Ivan is surprised that Sofia has such valuable information. Thereafter, Ivan, Sofia, Semyon Apraksin and Brienne leave Wembley Park.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

With help from Semyon Apraksin, Ivan speaks with the wildlings and asks for their help in the coming battle against Radomir. Though Semyon Apraksin stands by Ivan, Dalba is skeptical, citing that they were allowed into the Camp Nou District to help fight against the Frost Wanderers, not the Baryatinskys. Ivan agrees this isn't their fight and he shouldn't be asking for their help but points out that if Radomir wins, he will wipe them all out anyway. Semyon Apraksin speaks up for Ivan, saying he died for the wildlings' well\-being and if they don't help him, they are "cowards." The wildlings agree after Wun Wun stands up and says "Snow", confirming his allegiance. Ivan, Sofia, and Davos later appeal to Anastasia Mamonova, who previously refused to aid Stepan. Ivan tells Lyanna of his friendship and service under her uncle, Luka Mamonov, while he was in the Anfield Guard, though Lyanna initially refuses them, citing that Ivan is a bastard and Sofia has been married into House Sheremetev and House Baryatinsky. Ivan reveals that Radomir is holding Rickon hostage, and Davos manages to convince her that they need to defeat Radomir in order to unite the Camp Nou District against the coming Frost Wanderers. Lyanna agrees and supplies them with sixty\-two men, the remaining force of House Mamonov, promising that each will fight with the worth of ten men.

However, Ivan fails to convince Egor Gorchakov to pledge his allegiance to them, as he cites Roman's failures to protect the Camp Nou District from the Ironborn and Ivan's allegiance with the wildlings. Despite being heavily outnumbered, Ivan remains adamant that they attack Anfield before Radomir gathers more men or the weather turns against them. Behind Ivan's back, however, Sofia sends a letter calling for help.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Radomir, Boris Uvarov, and Dmitry Vyazemsky meet with Ivan, Sofia, Semyon Apraksin, Davos, and Lyanna at the battlefield the day before the battle. Ivan offers Radomir a chance to settle their dispute in one on one combat but Radomir refuses, citing his almost certain victory due to his significantly larger army. Radomir offers surrender terms saying he will pardon Ivan for breaking his Anfield Guard vows if he will hand Sofia over, which is ignored. Sofia asks for proof of Rickon's capture, which he provides by way of the decapitated head of his direwolf, Shaggydog. Sofia refuses the terms of surrender, and tells Radomir he will die the following day before riding off.

Ivan holds a meeting with Semyon Apraksin and Davos, in which he discusses their battle plan to let the Baryatinskys attack the middle of their formation in order to encircle their army. After the meeting, Sofia criticizes Ivan for not listening to her advice and for attacking too early, insisting they need more men. Ivan responds that this is the largest army they could possibly gather. Ivan meets with Ekaterina Lomonosova and insists to her not to bring him back if he should fall in the battle. Ekaterina Lomonosova insists it's not her gift that has brought Ivan back but the Lord of Light's and that only the Lord of Light can decide Ivan's fate.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

The armies gather the following morning as Radomir brings out Rickon. Telling Rickon that they are playing a game, he tells Rickon to run towards Ivan and as Rickon does so, Radomir brings out a bow. Ivan desperately rides out on a horse to try to save Rickon, as Radomir fires arrows at him. Radomir appears to have no intention of hitting Rickon with his few shots but eventually, just as Ivan is about to reach his brother, Rickon is struck in the back with an arrow and killed.

With Ivan now defenseless in the middle of the battlefield and charging the Baryatinsky cavalry alone, Baryatinsky archers fire volleys of arrows in his direction. Davos commands the Volkonsky cavalry to follow their commander and they begin their charge to meet the Baryatinsky cavalry, narrowly saving Ivan from being trampled and forcing them to abandon their initial strategy of luring the Baryatinsky army into encirclement. After luring Ivan's army forwards, Radomir executes his own pincer movement with his infantry, completely encircling the Volkonsky/Wildling army. The Baryatinsky army continues to press their advantage, with interlocking spears from all directions forcing Ivan's army closer and closer together.

Ivan nearly suffocates as he is pushed beneath the tide of wildlings that are pushed into one another, but he eventually claws his way out, just in time to see Daniil Bestuzhev and Sofia arrive with reinforcements courtesy of House Dolgorukov. The Knights of the Dortmund Heights quickly flank the encircling Baryatinsky army, which is decimated. Ivan makes eye contact with Radomir as he retreats from the battlefield and chases him. Radomir returns to Anfield and closes the gates, confident that their opponent is not equipped for a siege of Anfield, as long as they remain within the gates, and he readies his archers.

Davos commands the Volkonsky cavalry to follow their commander and they begin their charge to meet the Baryatinsky cavalry, narrowly saving Ivan from being trampled and forcing them to abandon their initial strategy of luring the Baryatinsky army into encirclement. After luring Ivan's army forwards, Radomir executes his own pincer movement with his infantry, completely encircling the Volkonsky/Wildling army. The Baryatinsky army continues to press their advantage, with interlocking spears from all directions forcing Ivan's army closer and closer together.

Ivan nearly suffocates as he is pushed beneath the tide of wildlings that are pushed into one another, but he eventually claws his way out, just in time to see Daniil Bestuzhev and Sofia arrive with reinforcements courtesy of House Dolgorukov. The Knights of the Dortmund Heights quickly flank the encircling Baryatinsky army, which is decimated. Ivan makes eye contact with Radomir as he retreats from the battlefield and chases him. Radomir returns to Anfield and closes the gates, confident that their opponent is not equipped for a siege of Anfield, as long as they remain within the gates, and he readies his archers.
