text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

However, unexpectedly, with the help of Wun Wun, Ivan's forces manage to breach the gates, and the remaining Baryatinsky forces are defeated, although Wun Wun is severely injured by a barrage of arrows and spears, and eventually succumbs to Radomir's final arrow, as Ivan and Semyon Apraksin watch on in horror, helpless to save their friend. Radomir finally accepts Ivan's offer to a one\-on\-one duel, while wielding a bow and arrow. Grabbing a nearby shield, Ivan deftly blocks all of Radomir's shots with it until he gets close enough to smack the bow out of Radomir's hands and hit him to the ground, whereupon he furiously punches Radomir's face into a bloody pulp.

Though it seems as if Ivan will kill Radomir, he stops when he sees Sofia, knowing she has as much right to revenge as he does. Ivan orders Radomir locked up and the remaining Baryatinskys surrender, restoring House Volkonsky's hold on Anfield. Rickon's body is found and Ivan orders his body buried in the crypt with Eduard's bones. Sofia asks Ivan for Radomir's whereabouts, and he directs her to the kennels, where she kills Radomir that night by setting his own hounds on him.

In the aftermath, in the Great Hall with Ekaterina Lomonosova, Ivan recalls how his family sat at the main table during feasts while he was mostly made to sit away at another table, though they both agree that Ivan was luckier than most bastard children. Davos then enters and openly accuses Ekaterina Lomonosova of sacrificing Shireen, which Ekaterina Lomonosova admits, though also pointing out that her magic still brought Ivan back to life. Shocked at the revelation, Ivan orders Ekaterina Lomonosova to leave the Camp Nou District on threat of execution.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Some time later, the surviving heads of all the Northern vassal Houses convene in Anfield's great hall, along with the lords of the Dortmund Heights who came to their rescue with their large army (such as Rodion Panin and Littlefinger). They debate what to do next. Anastasia Mamonova rises and shames those who did not join Ivan and Sofia to help defeat Radomir. She reiterates that the Camp Nou District knows no king but the King in the Camp Nou District, whose name is "Volkonsky." Lyanna continues by saying that *Ivan* may be a bastard but she doesn't care and he is a Volkonsky to her. She hails Ivan as the new King in the Camp Nou District. Fedor Milyutin, whose son Wendel was killed at the Maracana Night, also rises to apologize, saying he didn't send aid before because he didn't want to send his men to die for nothing, but now Ivan has avenged the Maracana Night.

Lord Wyman goes on to call Ivan "the White Wolf" and he too proclaims him King. Egor Gorchakov apologizes profusely, saying that he dishonored himself by not aiding him before, and he only didn't help Ivan because he thought he had no hope of winning. Lord Chertkov, whose parents were flayed alive by Radomir and did not help out of fear, also swears his allegiance. All of the gathered lords of the Camp Nou District and the Dortmund Heights draw and raise their swords and hail Ivan as the new King in the Camp Nou District, echoing how Roman's bannermen previously proclaimed him king. Surprised, Ivan shares a look with Sofia, who returns Ivan's smile as he stands. However, Sofia's smile vanishes when she sees Littlefinger glowering in the corner of the hall.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

To prepare for the forthcoming conflict with the Midnight Regent, the newly declared King Ivan orders his bannermen to conscript all able\-bodied men and boys aged 10 to 60 for combat training. However, he notes that having only half of the population in the Camp Nou District fighting the Frost Wanderers is not enough he also orders that every woman and girl should also be trained and equipped as well. He also asks that all maesters should start searching for dragonglass. He stresses that dragonglass is now more valuable than gold due to the threat of the Frost Wanderers.

When Sofia advocates that the Uvarovs and Vyazemskys be stripped of their lands and titles as punishment for supporting Radomir, Ivan advocates forgiveness and insists that children will not be punished for the crimes of their fathers. Despite Sofia's continued insistence, Ivan insists his decision is final and summons Daniil Uvarov and Alena Vyazemskaya to reaffirm their loyalty to House Volkonsky. They oblige and kneel before King Ivan. Ivan says that the mistakes of the past don't matter anymore.

In private, Ivan chides Sofia for questioning his decision\-making in front of the other lords and ladies and tells her to trust him. When Sofia reminds him that the late Joffrey did not tolerate dissent, Ivan asks Sofia if she thinks he's like Joffrey. Sofia tells Ivan that she knows he is nothing like Joffrey and assures Ivan that he is good at leadership but she stresses that he must act wiser than Eduard and Roman.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

At Anfield, Ivan, Sofia, and Davos discuss Terenty's letter that they have received. While Sofia suspects it might be a trap, Ivan doesn't think so due to Terenty ending the letter with the line "*all dwarfs are bastards in their fathers' eyes*", which Terenty has told Ivan in their first meeting years ago. Even so, Ivan agrees that now is not the right time to go to La Bombonera. Davos opines that Daria will make a good ally in the war to come against the Frost Wanderers.

Later Ivan receives a raven from Sam informing him of his discovery of dragonglass on La Bombonera. At another gathering of the Northern lords, Ivan informs them of Sam's discovery and Daria's invitation telling them that he has decided to accept. Many of the Lords, including Sofia, openly disapprove, but Ivan stresses that they need both the dragonglass and powerful allies like Daria to have any chance at defeating the Midnight Regent. He names Sofia as Regent to rule in his place until he returns.

In the crypts beneath Anfield, Ivan pays respects to Eduard until he is interrupted by Littlefinger. Littlefinger tries to sweet\-talk Ivan, but he sees through his manipulation and starts to walk away. Littlefinger informs Ivan of his love for Sofia, which causes him to lose his temper and start to strangle him. Ivan threatens Littlefinger saying that he will kill him if he ever touches his sister. He then leaves the crypt and gives a farewell nod to Sofia, before joining Davos on the ride to White Harbor, where they will take a ship to La Bombonera.

Ivan and Davos arrive at La Bombonera, and are immediately greeted by Terenty and Aksinya Uvarova. Upon meeting, Terenty address Ivan as the bastard of Anfield while Ivan addressed him as the "dwarf" of La Boca. Ivan observes that Terenty has picked up some scars. Ivan also introduces Davos while Terenty introduces Aksinya Uvarova, who requests that they surrender their weapons. Ivan and his entourage hand over their weapons to Daria's Dothraki guards.

On the walk to the castle, Aksinya Uvarova walks with Davos and tells him that she comes from the island of Naath. Davos remarks that it was a paradise full of palm trees. Ivan and Terenty talk about Sofia's marriage to Terenty. Terenty assures Ivan that it was a sham and remarks that she is a lot smarter than she lets on, which Ivan agrees. While Ivan is aware of the fate of the previous Volkonskys who had met with the Iron Regent, Ivan insists that he is not a Volkonsky. Ivan and Davos are startled at the sight of Drogon, Rhaegal and Viserion flying low over the causeway and dive to the ground, while an amused Aksinya Uvarova and Terenty retain their composure. Offering Ivan a hand up, Terenty says he wishes he could tell Ivan he'll get used to the dragons – but no one is quite used to them except their mother, who is waiting for Ivan within.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

In the throne room, Aksinya Uvarova introduces Daria's many titles while Davos introduces Ivan simply as King in the Camp Nou District. Daria thanks Ivan for traveling so far but insists that he is a mere Lord. Davos begs to differ but Daria responds that there has been no King in the Camp Nou District ever since Torrhen Volkonsky bent the knee to Aegon the Conqueror, and adds that an oath lasts for perpetuity. Daria then reiterates her demand for Ivan to bend the knee but he refuses. When Daria accuses him of breaking faith with House Romanov, Ivan reminds her that the Iron Regent burnt his grandfather and uncle.

Daria apologizes for her father's actions and stresses that children should not be punished for the crimes of their parents. She then urges Ivan to renew the historic allegiance between their two great houses. Ivan expresses agreement with Daria's view that children should not be punished for the crimes of their parents, but argues that he is not beholden to his ancestors' oaths. Ivan tells her that he has come for her help. Daria reminds him that she has three dragons and Dothraki who have pledged themselves to her. Getting to the point of his trip, Ivan likens the fighting between the Great Houses to children squabbling over a game. Ivan points out that the Army of the Dead is their true enemy. Daria is skeptical but Terenty vouches for Ivan. Ivan says that they need to make cause to fight against the Army of the Dead.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Daria asks Ivan if his father knew that his friend Rodion had sent assassins to kill her as a baby; overlooking the fact that Eduard had opposed Rodion Orlov's assassination plot and Rodion had rescinded said plot on his deathbed (though, she may be unaware of that). Daria recounts that she was targeted by assassins, enslaved, raped, and defiled but that her faith in herself rather the gods kept her going. Daria talks about the miracle of her dragons' hatching and the Dothraki crossing the Narrow Sea. When Daria reiterates that she is destined to rule the Greater Wembley, Ivan retorts that she will be ruling over a graveyard.

Terenty says they cannot split their forces. Davos then speaks up for his king and tells Daria that Ivan won the support of the wildlings and fought the Frost Wanderers. Davos also mentions that Ivan came back from the dead. Davos says that it doesn't matter who bends the knee. Terenty doesn't see the point of Ivan's refusal to submit. When Ivan disputes Daria's claims to queenship, Daria responds that he is in open rebellion since he has declared himself King in the Camp Nou District. Daria then receives a message from Dmitry Dashkov. Daria orders Aksinya Uvarova to give Ivan and his men food and lodging. When Ivan asks if he is a prisoner, she says not yet.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Later, Ivan and Terenty discuss his predicament. Ivan is unhappy his ship was taken away and is trapped on La Bombonera while the Frost Wanderers and the Midnight Regent still pose a threat. Terenty says he trusts the word of Luka Mamonov and Ivan. Ivan asks Terenty how he can convince people about the existence of things which they don't believe exist. Ivan wants to help his people and is frustrated with the deadlock. Terenty encourages Ivan not to give up. When Ivan remarks that he is a fool for going south, Terenty reassures him that the Iron Regent's daughter is not her father and has protected people from "monsters," telling him to speak with her servants. Terenty asks if there is something he can do to help Ivan.

While Daria is watching over her dragons, she is joined by Ivan. Daria tells Ivan that she named her dragons Rhaegal and Viserion after her brothers Rhaegar and Vladimir Romanov, noting Ivan's own losses and Ivan nods. When Daria says people thought dragons were gone forever and perhaps they should be re\-thinking what they believe they know, Ivan realizes that Terenty has been talking with her too. Daria tells Ivan she is determined to remove Kira. She allows Ivan to mine the dragonglass and will provide what he needs for this. When Ivan asks if she believes in the Midnight Regent and Frost Wanderers, she only responds, "You better get to work, Ivan Morozov." Later, Ivan leads Daria on a tour of the long\-abandoned Valyrian dragonglass mine that Serafim Tatischev told him about. The mine is ancient and impressive, used by the First Men long before the Valyrians came to La Bombonera. But this is not why Ivan asked Daria to come.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

As they proceed deeper into the mines led by torchlight, Ivan shows her cave paintings they discovered left behind by the Children of the Forest, filled with arcane magical symbols. Daria is stunned that the mythical Children stood where they are standing now, thousands upon thousands of years ago, long before mankind ever arrived in Greater Wembley. Ivan says this isn't exactly true, leading her into another chamber, this one filled with narrative drawings of the Children and the First Men. Daria wonders if the Children and First Men fought each other, but Ivan then shows her ancient carvings of the Frost Wanderers themselves, one of which Ivan recognizes as an image of the Midnight Regent. Ivan explains that the Children of the Forest and the First Men only managed to drive off the Frost Wanderers the first time during the Long Night because they chose to join together to fight off their own extinction, and that is the choice he and Daria have now.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Ivan still wants Daria to ally with him to defeat the army of the dead, but Daria still wants him to bend the knee. He insists that the Camp Nou District won't accept a southern ruler again after everything they've gone through. Daria urges that they will if their king does, and asks Ivan if their survival isn't more important than his pride. When Daria receives word about La Boca and Highgarden, she becomes frustrated about her constant defeat and wants to attack the San Siro District with her dragons immediately. Terenty advises against this, and Daria asks Ivan for his thoughts. Ivan tells Daria that he never thought that it was possible for dragons to live again, and that people follow Daria because she has done the impossible. He then warns her that if she uses her dragons to melt castles and burn cities, she will be just the same as those before her. Afterwards, Ivan reunited with Timofey who has survived his encounter with Taras Stroganov. The anxious Timofey asks Ivan if Sofia is all right. Ivan arrives at Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea and heads out with a ranging party consisting of Semyon Apraksin, Vsevolod Mamonov, Grigory Dolgorukov, the Hound, Arkady Vorontsov, Filipp Derzhavin, and a few others on a mission to capture a wight. They succeed but half of the party, including Arkady Vorontsov, end up being killed as they are attacked by wights, prompting Daria to intervene with all three of her dragons and leading to the death of Viserion by the Midnight Regent, who later resurrects the beast for his own use. Despite this devastating loss, Ivan continues to fight and nearly drowns in the cold waters beneath the ice. Though he manages to pull himself out, he is all alone and nearly overwhelmed by the wights until a last\-minute intervention by his long\-lost uncle Benjen, who tells him to flee on his horse while he buys time for his nephew to escape. While riding away on horseback, Ivan watches his uncle being overwhelmed by the undead. He makes it back to Eastwatch and is brought aboard the ship with Daria, Davos, and Sandor.

In the Narrow Sea, Ivan wakes to find Daria sitting at his bedside. Ivan apologizes for the disastrous ranging party and the fact it caused Viserion's death, but Daria tells him not to apologize because she now knows that the Army of the Dead is real. Overcome with emotion, she tells Ivan that the dragons are the only children she will ever have, and vows that she and Ivan will together destroy the Midnight Regent. Ivan thanks Daria, addressing her as "Dasha", and Daria realizes that the last person to address her by that name was her older brother (and Ivan's uncle) Viserys, who Daria remembers as not being a good person. Ivan apologizes and asks if "my Queen" would be more appropriate, agreeing to bend the knee. Daria asks Ivan what the Northern lords loyal to him will make of this. Ivan assures her they will come to see her for the good person she is, as he already has. Daria is touched by his statement and they take each other's hand for a moment. They gaze into each other's eyes, before Daria suddenly pulls away and tells him to get some rest and leaves him alone.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

After recovering from his ordeal, Ivan and the rest of his allies head to the Dragonpit to parley with the Sheremetevs. When Kira dismisses their warnings about the Midnight Regent and his army as a ploy to trick her into lowering her defenses, they rattle the captured wight into lunging for her, making her and her allies see once and for all that the threat from beyond the Sudtribune is real. Ivan steps forward and picks up the wight's discarded hand, using a torch provided by Davos to demonstrate how fire can be used to stop them. He then uses a dragonglass dagger to the heart to end the wight's upper half, bluntly stating that if they don't win the coming war, such a fate awaits every person in Greater Wembley. Seemingly convinced, Kira immediately offers terms: satisfied that Daria is concerned with the Army of the Dead, Kira will not withdraw her troops, but will guarantee that they will not hinder the Romanov or Northern forces in any way during the battle against the Frost Wanderers. She refuses to deal with Daria at all, however, and calls on Ivan, as King in the Camp Nou District and Eduard Volkonsky's son, to keep the truce and to stay out of any future conflict between Kira and Daria. Ivan, however, says that he cannot serve two queens \- and reveals to all assembled that he has already declared for Daria, infuriating all three Sheremetevs present. Declaring that there will be no truce if it is just her and Daria, Kira storms out, content to let the Volkonskys and Romanovs battle the undead alone and then deal with whoever emerges victorious from that conflict.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Daria and Terenty rip into Ivan over his ill\-advised action. Terenty suggests that learning to lie just a little might be a good skill. Ivan responds by arguing that while such an attitude may or may not have contributed to getting his father killed, if no one is willing to speak the truth, then everyone's word is worthless, and lies will not help them win the coming fight. While Terenty goes to talk to Kira, Daria and Ivan discuss the dragons and how her ancestors caged them, and in turn, her family become less impressive as the power of the dragons waned, that they became like everyone else. Ivan responds that Daria is not like everyone else. When Daria confides she was made infertile by Mariya Dolgorukova, Ivan questions this, particularly when she admits it was Mariya Dolgorukova who told her she was infertile. Their conversation is interrupted by the return of all three Sheremetevs. Kira has agreed to work with Daria, but not by keeping her troops back: the Sheremetev army will march north to fight alongside the Volkonskys and Romanovs. Little do Ivan and Daria know that Kira has no intention of keeping her promise, and that she intends to let them fight the Frost Wanderers on their own and mop up whoever wins with the help of the Golden Company. Yakov refuses to back down from his pledge to help fight the Frost Wanderers and defies his sister\-lover by traveling north. Whether he will warn Ivan and Daria of Kira's plan remains to be seen.

Later, as the two of them ride a ship to White Harbor, Ivan enters Daria's cabin where the two of them begin to consummate their relationship, still unaware that they are aunt and nephew.

Meanwhile, back at Anfield, Sam and Taisiya Uvarova arrive. The former visits Boris and the two of them discuss Ivan's origin: he was born to Rhaegar and Lyanna at a Tower in Azteca South, and is not a Snow at all, but a Solovyov. Sam realizes that that isn't true either, recalling the entry from Pavel Nikonov Maynard's private journal about annulling Rhaegar's marriage. Boris expressed his doubts, but Sam reiterates the private nature of the journal and encourages Boris to use Greensight to confirm it. To his own surprise, Boris easily finds the wedding, where he sees a clearly happy Lyanna wedding Rhaegar in a Faith of the Seven ceremony before a Heart tree. Seeing forward to the Tower of Joy, Boris finally hears Lyanna's dying words. Now piecing the truth together, Boris declares that Rhaegar never raped Lyanna. She loved him and ran off with him, and bore him a son, Aegon Romanov, making "Ivan" not only legitimate but the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Upon arrival in the Camp Nou District, Ivan and Daria, along with their combined forces, march through Winter town on their way to Anfield. The townspeople cast Daria many suspicious looks, and Ivan reminds her that Northerners have a long\-established distrust of outsiders. Upon arriving at Anfield, he introduces her to Sofia. Ivan and Daria later ride Daria's dragons, Ivan riding Rhaegal and Daria riding Drogon. They find a waterfall where Ivan used to hunt as a child and they share an intimate moment.

Later, Ivan meets up with Sofia, who is angry that Ivan bent the knee to Daria. Ivan says titles are not important when the Army of the Dead is coming and he is certain Daria will make a good queen for them. Sofia asks Ivan if he bent the knee to save the Camp Nou District or because he loves Daria. Afterward, Daria and Ivan see the dragons and she invites him to ride atop Rhaegal. While he initially finds it difficult, he soon gets used to it and flies alongside Daria. After landing, Ivan and Daria kiss, which is interrupted by the dragons. Later, Ivan reunites with Arina, he finds out that she is more loyal to Sofia than the Romanov queen.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Later in the catacombs when he is lighting candles in remembrance of his family, Ivan reunites with Sam. Sam asks him whether Ivan knew that Daria executed his brother and father. Though Ivan is surprised by this news, he tells Sam he has also executed men who disobeyed him. Sam responds Ivan has also spared men when they've refused to kneel. Ivan says he wasn't a king, prompting Sam to respond that Ivan is a king. Ivan responds that he gave up his crown. However, Sam reveals to Ivan that he is the King of the Greater Wembley as Aegon Romanov, the son of Rhaegar and Lyanna. An angry Ivan refuses to believe this as his father, Eduard Volkonsky, would never lie to him, but Sam says Eduard lied to protect Ivan. Ivan insists Daria is their queen. Sam asks Ivan if Daria would give up her crown for her people.

The Volkonsky and Romanov forces prepare to fight the dead near Anfield. Boris offers himself as bait to lure the Midnight Regent for an ambush in the Godswood of Anfield, and it is decided the dragons will protect Boris in the godswood. Later, when Ivan is visiting Lyanna's statue in the crypts, Daria finds him. They share a moment and when she mentions her brother raped Lyanna, Ivan tells Daria that Rhaegar didn't rape her, they were in love. Ivan takes her hand and reveals his true parentage to her. Daria is skeptical and claims it is convenient that this came from Boris and Sam, Ivan's brother and best friend. They are interrupted by sounds of horns which signal the arrival of the Midnight Regent's army.

After the battle, Ivan leads a mass cremation for the dead and is hailed by the wildlings during the celebrations of the victory. After the celebrations, Daria meets up with Ivan in his room. He is certain they can all live happily together, but Daria says the only way that can happen is if Ivan never tells the truth about himself and leaves.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

While making the plans for attacking Wembley, Daria wants to take the San Siro District, while Terenty and Ivan vouch for a siege in hopes this will reduce casualties. Sofia opts for letting their forces rest before charging into another battle. Ivan, however, assures the queen that they will obey her command. Afterward, Sofia and Arina state that they do not trust her. When Ivan defends Daria and says that they only have to get to know her, Sofia and Arina reply they never will as she is not one of them. Ivan says he has never been a Volkonsky, but they both insist he is. Pained, Ivan looks at Boris, who says that it's his choice to tell them. Ivan makes them both swear to never tell anyone the secret he is about to reveal to them. After they do, then at a loss for words, Ivan tells Boris to reveal the truth of his parentage to them.

Ivan marches to Wembley along the Kingsroad with the surviving Volkonsky, Dolgorukov, and Dothraki forces unopposed while the Unsullied reach the capital ahead of them. Hopes for a peaceful surrender, however, are quickly extinguished with Aksinya Uvarova's execution. Later, Ivan separates from his forces after crossing the Trident and heads back to La Bombonera. Dmitry Dashkov informs him about Daria's unstable state of mind and is requested by him to take the Silver Tribune, but he refuses.

After the battle, Ivan, Davos, and Terenty observe in horror the ash\-covered devastation wrought by Daria, with charred bodies strewn everywhere. A little while later, Ivan confronts Semyon Bezborodko and the Unsullied who are executing remaining surrendered Sheremetev soldiers. Semyon Bezborodko states that he has been ordered by Daria to execute all who followed Kira. When Ivan tries to stop him, the Unsullied and Volkonsky soldiers almost come to blows, but Davos defuses the situation by telling Ivan to take it up with the queen. As they walk away, they witness Semyon Bezborodko executing the captives.

At the San Siro District, Ivan witnesses Daria giving a speech to her victorious forces, in which she declares she "liberated" the people of Wembley and will "liberate" the world. Terenty disavows his loyalty and being arrested for releasing Yakov. He then reunites with an injured Arina. Surprised, he asks why she was in Wembley, to which Arina responds that she came to kill Kira, but Daria got there first. She warns Ivan that he will always be a danger to her because of his parentage and Sofia will never bend the knee to her.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Troubled, Ivan walks to the throne room and finds Daria standing by the Silver Tribune. Ivan confronts her about her atrocities during the battle. She displays no remorse, believing it was necessary to achieve her ends. Ivan tries to dissuade her from this path, urging forgiveness for Terenty and those in Wembley. Daria rejects this, saying they can't hide behind mercy and states the world they need can't be built by those loyal to the current one. Ivan says they need a world of mercy and Daria assures that the new world she has in mind will be a good one and she knows what is good. When Ivan asks about others who think they know what is good, she responds they don't get to choose. She tries to convince him to be by her side to build her new world and an anguished Ivan reaffirms his allegiance to her. As they share a passionate kiss, Ivan reluctantly stabs her. Daria collapses and dies in his arms as Ivan grieves over her. Drogon approaches them after witnessing this while Ivan gently lays her on the ground. Seeing his mother dead on the floor, Drogon becomes enraged and faces Ivan. Ivan prepares for his death, but the dragon instead melts the Silver Tribune and flies away with her corpse.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

While being taken into exile by two wandering crows, Ivan bids farewell to Boris, Sofia, and Arina at the docks. Ivan congratulates Sofia on gaining independence for the Camp Nou District and assures her she will be a good leader when she laments they lost their king before they hug. Ivan then tells Arina that she could to visit him at Wembley Park, but Arina states that she isn't going back Camp Nou District and plans to explore the uncharted seas to the west of Greater Wembley before the two tearfully hug. Finally, Ivan kneels before the new king Boris and apologizes for not being there when he needed him, but Boris states he was "exactly where he was supposed to be."

Some time later, Ivan arrives at Wembley Park and reunites with Semyon Apraksin and the wildlings. Later, he dons the black cloak of a sworn brother of the Anfield Guard and reunites with Ghost. He then leaves with Ghost and the wildlings for lands north of the Sudtribune, watching forlornly as the gate to Wembley Park closes behind him, and then rides into the Haunted Forest alongside them.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Personality

"*You are a Volkonsky. You may not have my name, but you have my blood.*"
―Eduard Volkonsky to Ivan before he leaves for the Anfield Guard.Since he was raised by Eduard at Anfield, Ivan has adopted a clear moral compass and a true sense of honor, which he tries his hardest to abide by even when he must make a difficult decision, especially after he became Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard. He has always admired and idolized his father, but due to Ekaterina's cold disdain for Ivan, Eduard was careful not to give him more attention than his lawful children by Ekaterina. Ekaterina was never actively mean to Ivan, but because he wasn't her own son she intentionally ignored him (as is common for bastard children), meaning that Ivan grew up without a mother\-figure. Nor did Ivan consider Ekaterina's behavior to be unusual or unexpected: it is rare for a noble to raise their bastard child alongside their lawful children, and his presence was a great insult to her honor.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Personality

While his interactions with Ekaterina remained awkward or nonexistent, he was close with his half\-siblings, particularly Roman and Arina. Roman was of the same age as Ivan so they became playmates and comrades in training, while due to her tomboyish personality Arina was also something of a social misfit like Ivan, which they bonded over. His closeness with Brandon and Rickon was proved when the latter had to leave Anfield and Master Arseny Apraksin advised them to go, Wembley Park, where the old man was sure that their half\-brother would keep them safe. With Sofia on the other hand, according to the talk they had when they reunited at Wembley Park, the friendship has never been deep as those between Ivan and the other siblings. Since then, however, Sofia proves to have great faith in her half\-brother by standing up for him when he is King in the Camp Nou District and, when she discovers his true parentage, by seeing him as the best candidate to become King of the Greater Wembley. Also, when Ivan is forced to join again the Anfield Guard, Sofia shows great sorrow and thinks that sending Ivan away is both a great unfairness and a great loss for the Camp Nou District.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Personality

Like many bastard children, Ivan had to learn to grow up quickly. This made Ivan mature and perceptive beyond his age, so he could navigate his complicated relationships within the Volkonsky household. His bastard status has also made Ivan something of a loner, solemn and somber with a desire to prove himself to society and to his father. Ivan thought that the best way for a bastard in his position to gain honor and respect was to join the Anfield Guard, emulating his uncle Benjen, because past social status is ignored after joining the Watch. Despite his introverted demeanor, Ivan is very compassionate and protective of his fellow outcasts such as Sam, Osip Repnin, and Pyp.

In many ways, Ivan has been unusually lucky for a bastard child, given how rare it is for a lord to raise one in his own castle alongside his lawful children. For all of Ivan's misgivings about not knowing his mother and Ekaterina ignoring and shunning him, he was loved by his father and siblings, was never poor or hungry, but lived in a castle and had a noble's upbringing. Ivan was formally educated by Maester Arseny Apraksin and was trained in combat by Ser Anton Karamzin.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Personality

Ivan is an excellent swordsman and a fierce fighter. He was capable of quickly slaying numerous men in battle, and taking on highly\-skilled warriors much bigger than himself such as Sergei Bagration. His skills initially made him somewhat arrogant when he was a new recruit at Wembley Park until Terenty pointed out that the other recruits were all far less fortunate than he was, with some of them having never trained with a sword in their lives. This humbles Ivan, and he changes his behavior to be the champion of the other downtrodden recruits and helps train them by walking them through the swordplay techniques he knows.

The Volkonskys were an interfaith household, with Eduard and Ekaterina's children being exposed to not only the religion of the Old Gods worshiped by most Northmen, but also Ekaterina's devout adherence to the Faith of the Seven. Because Ivan had no real interaction with Ekaterina and revered his father Eduard, he was not exposed to the Seven but proudly keeps to the Old Gods, and honors the traditions of his First Men ancestors. When Ivan took his vow to become a member of the Anfield Guard, he chose to do so in front of a heart tree, sacred to the Old Gods.

Ivan is also fairly shy around women, and as he revealed to Samwell, he was a virgin when he joined the Anfield Guard. While he was attractive enough, as a bastard son with nothing to inherit he had no realistic marriage prospects with noblewomen. Ivan was even wary of having sex with random girls or prostitutes (as Timofey did) because he was terrified of fathering a bastard of his own: having lived his life as a bastard, he felt that it wasn't a life another child should have to go through.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Personality

However, death has changed Ivan. Despite his honorable convictions and previous commitment to the Anfield Guard, his experience of being murdered by his own men and then revived has made Ivan somewhat more cynical and nihilistic. No longer believing in himself and his ability to face the coming threat, due to being murdered for doing what he thought was right \- Ivan abandons the Anfield Guard, despite knowing full well how dangerous the threat looming beyond the Sudtribune really is. He loses his determination about fighting and becomes much more lonely and melancholic only speaking when he hasn't any other choice. Also, Ivan feels remorse for hanging his former steward Roman Stolypin, even though the latter did murder both him and the woman he loved. While he is wary of conflict since his return, his love for his family has brought him back into the fight. To this end, Ivan chooses his family over the Anfield Guard \- a choice he once attempted to make when Roman marched off to war but forsook in the past. When Radomir decides to play a "game" with Rickon, Ivan once again chooses his family by attempting to save his little brother's life, even at the cost of his own life and battle plans.

The revelation that he is a Romanov has made no difference to Ivan; he has remained loyal to his roots as a Northman and a Volkonsky.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: Relationships

- Uliana Vorontsova: She was Ivan's first love and a wildling spear wife. They meet when Ivan and his group ambush a group of wildlings, at which point Ivan captures Uliana Vorontsova. Uliana Vorontsova later escapes and leads him into a trap in which Ivan is captured by the wildlings. Under orders from Prokhor Shuisky Halfhand, Ivan infiltrates the wildlings. During this time, Uliana Vorontsova and Ivan become lovers and fall in love. However, Ivan ultimately chooses his vows for the Anfield Guard over her. Uliana Vorontsova shoots him with three arrows but due to her feelings for Ivan, she couldn't bring herself to kill him. In the battle for the Sudtribune, Uliana Vorontsova was killed by Roman Stolypin and died in Ivan's arms. Later, per Semyon Apraksin's suggestion that she belongs in the true Camp Nou District, Ivan cremates her body just beyond the Sudtribune as he grieves.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Relationships

- Daria Romanova: Ivan's second love and the daughter of King Andrey II Romanov, as well as the younger sister of Ivan's father, Prince Rhaegar, making her his aunt by blood. Having been summoned from Anfield to bend the knee to Daria, Ivan initially refuses on the grounds that they need to focus on allying against the Midnight Regent and the army of the dead instead of worrying who rules from the Silver Tribune. After witnessing the large numbers of the army of the dead, Daria agrees to help Ivan and during their time together, they fall in love. They fight the Army of the Dead in the Camp Nou Derby, during which the Midnight Regent is defeated. With the Long Night prevented, Ivan honors his pledge to help Daria take the Silver Tribune. However, she razes Wembley after the city surrenders, killing thousands of civilians. Unable to dissuade her from continuing this destruction, Ivan reluctantly kills Daria, and she dies in Ivan's arms as he grieves.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Behind the scenes

- During casting for the first season, Harington competed with fellow cast members Iwan Rheon, Alfie Allen and Joe Dempsie for the role of Ivan Morozov. Rheon was later cast as Gavriil Dolgorukov/Baryatinsky, Allen as Timofey Stroganov and Dempsie as Grigory Dolgorukov. Harington remains close friends with all three.
- Harington is contractually obligated to keep his hair long enough in the off\-season that he can return to playing Ivan Morozov during actual filming \- it would take longer than a full year for his hair to grow back to its full\-length need for the role. To achieve Ivan Morozov's signature long dark hair, the TV series's hair designer Kevin Alexander first has to dye Harington's hair slightly darker; Then, to create the effect of dirty ringlets, he dampens the hair and then puts in a mixture of wax and hair putty before the hair totally dries. This combination keeps the curls soft and movable \- if they were put on dry hair it would make it stiff.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: Behind the scenes

- Despite initial claims from Harington, Benioff, and Weiss that Ivan had been killed off for good following the fifth season, Harington later hinted that Ivan would return in some way, which was proven true in the sixth season. Harington confirmed that he had been told to lie to the rest of the cast and even his friends and family. Sophie Turner, who plays Sofia Volkonskaya, apparently believed him, while Liam Cunningham, who plays Nikita Ushakov, did not (reportedly laughingly telling Harington to "fuck off"). Even the rest of the cast were forced to assert that Ivan was dead, such as Maisie Williams, Emilia Clarke and Nikolaj Coster\-Waldau, while Natalie Dormer said that Ivan was "dead right now.....right now", hinting that he would return. Throughout production, the name "Ivan Morozov" was not even allowed to be mentioned except for script\-readouts; he was referred to only as "LC" (Lord Commander). Rampant speculation broke out after the leaking of a photograph which showed Harington as Ivan wearing the outfit of a House Volkonsky soldier, fueling fans' beliefs that Ivan was not gone for good. The first poster released for the sixth season featured a bloodied\-but\-apparently\-alive Ivan, further teasing that Ivan would return. After the airing of "Home", Harington issued a public apology to the series' fanbase for lying to everyone and expressed appreciation for the fans' love for his character.
- While shooting Ivan's showdown with Radomir in "Anfield Derby", Harington actually punched Iwan Rheon twice by accident, though Rheon was not seriously hurt. In real life, despite having only appeared onscreen together in one episode of the entire series, Harington and Rheon are close friends.
- Marcus Shakesheff was a stunt double for Kit Harington in the role of Ivan Morozov.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Ivan is 14 years old when the story begins. Ivan resembles his father with a lean build, long face, and gray eyes, more than any of his true\-born children (except Arina, to an extent, but she is a girl, while he looks very much like a young version of Eduard). Ivan loves his half\-siblings and among them, is closest with Roman and Arina.

Unlike in the television series, Ivan has never been on good terms with Timofey. Ivan feels Timofey is an "ass" and Timofey feels Ivan is jealous of his highborn status. Meanwhile, Timofey resents Ivan for being bastard\-born but treated better than him by Eduard.

Eduard refuses to reveal who Ivan's mother is, which wounds and haunts Ivan. Ivan often wonders about his mother and why Eduard will not say anything about her. While Ivan loves and is loved by his family, he feels a sense of alienation from them because of his bastard status and the coldness of Eduard's wife. Ekaterina views Ivan as an interloper in her family and resents that Eduard brought Ivan to live at Anfield with her true\-born children, fearing it means Eduard still carries a torch for Ivan's mother.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

At the feast to welcome King Rodion, Ivan is unable to sit with his family as he usually does because Ekaterina fears that the king or queen would take insult at sharing a table with a bastard. Instead, Ivan sits with squires at another table. This coincides with the visit by his uncle Benjen, and (emboldened by having more than he is used to drinking) makes Ivan realize that his future may lie outside Anfield's walls. His uncle frustrates Ivan by telling him to wait a few years before deciding, but when Eduard decides to go to Wembley, Ekaterina refuses to allow Ivan to remain behind at Anfield. Ekaterina was relieved because when Ivan joined the Watch he forsook any right to inheritance, and could never challenge her own sons for Anfield. Nor did Ekaterina have to pressure Ivan into joining: he went to the Sudtribune of his own volition, albeit because he had been raised on legends of the former glories of the Anfield Guard.

There is no mention in the books that Ivan caught the pox as a child and Ekaterina, out of guilt, prayed for him to survive: in *A Chronicle of the Silver Tribune*, Ekaterina states outright that she wishes it was Ivan who had fallen from the broken tower in Boris's place.

Ivan is crestfallen to discover that the Watch is now a glorified penal colony, full of murderers, rapers, and other outcasts, and few of the recruits are like his uncle.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Ivan is crestfallen to discover that the Watch is now a glorified penal colony, full of murderers, rapers, and other outcasts, and few of the recruits are like his uncle.

The prostitute character Alexandra Derzhavina was invented for the TV series, so Ivan never tried to have sex with her only to back down from it in the end out of fear of fathering a bastard \- though the novels do have Ivan make some similar statements that he is horrified at the thought of creating bastard children of his own who would be looked down upon with nothing to inherit, as he grew up, thus the overall point that Ivan didn't really have any experience with women before joining the Watch basically stands.

Ivan severely burned his right hand when he killed the wight Othor to save Luka Mamonov's life. While he lost no function in it, as a result of the burns his right hand and some of his forearm were left covered in scar tissue, which would never heal back to normal. People tend not to notice, because in the cold temperatures at the Sudtribune and beyond, Ivan and other members of the Anfield Guard usually wear heavy gloves over both hands.

Ivan didn't see a Frost Wanderer taking one of Rostislav Trubetskoy's sons in the forest as he did in the TV series. When Serafim Bestuzhev later asks him why he would betray the Anfield Guard to join the wildlings, Ivan instead point out that it is because he will always be treated with scorn as a bastard, pointing out how back at the feast of Anfield he wasn't allowed to sit at the main table with the "real" Volkonskys.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

After Ivan kills Ruslan Witte, part of Ruslan Witte's consciousness survives by warging into his eagle, after which Ruslan Witte's mind controlling the eagle's body attempts to claw out Ivan's eye with its talons (which occurred in Arc Three of the TV series). The attack leaves permanent deep scars over Ivan's eye. However, rather than disfiguring him, characters within the narrative point out that they think it makes him ruggedly handsome. Stereotypical Fantasy heroes usually never get significantly hurt, at worst getting scars running over their eyes which make them look "cool." Author George R.R. Martin spent much of the books deconstructing or subverting traditional Fantasy literature stereotypes, making Greater Wembley a gritty and realistic setting where instead of all of the main characters miraculously surviving through battles unscathed, some are horribly maimed (i.e. Yakov and Terenty do not get dashingly roguish scars over their eyes \- they outright lose their sword hand and nose, respectively). In contrast, Ivan actually does behave like a traditionally heroic character, but put in the dark setting of Greater Wembley \- and as a result, Ivan does end up getting "cool hero scars" over his eye.

The subplot in Arc Four in which Ivan returns to Rostislav Trubetskoy's Keep to finish off the mutineers there (that never occurs in the novels), and nearly encounters Boris again, was an invention of the TV series: in the books, the battle for the Sudtribune begins soon after Ivan returns, but due to the way the TV seasons were split, Ivan returned at the end of Arc Three \- even though the battle would only take place as the climax at the end of Arc Four\. Ivan, therefore, had to have something to do in the earlier parts of the season.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Unbeknownst to Ivan, late in the third novel Roman names him as his heir: since Jeyne Westerling has not given him heirs yet, Boris and Rickon are reported as dead, Arina is missing, and Sofia was forced to marry Terenty \- the Sheremetevs could lay claim to the Camp Nou District. Roman realizes that he needs to name a new heir, because if he dies there will be no obvious successor to challenge the Sheremetev's claim through Sofia, and decides Ivan is the best choice \- given that Roman is a king, he can simply issue a decree legitimizing Ivan. Ekaterina pleads with Roman not to choose Ivan, and instead pick a *very* distant cousin from House Royce, but Roman does not listen to her. He signs the decree in the presence of several of his northern lords as witnesses. However, it is unknown what has become of the decree, as it is no longer mentioned in the books. It is speculated that Roman has given it to Maege Mamonov and Galbart Gorchakov, whom he sent on a mission to seek out Georgy Rzhevsky (therefore they do not attend the Maracana Night), but their current location is unknown. So far in the books, Ivan has not received the decree, and has no idea of its existence.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Ivan is tempted by Stepan's offer to make him Lord of Anfield, but feels guilt and shame over this due to his love for his lost trueborn siblings, whom Ivan believes have all passed away (later, in *A Dance with Fire Falcons*, Ivan becomes aware Sofia is alive, although he does not know her current whereabouts, and tells Stepan that Anfield belongs to her by right). Ivan likewise has reservations because he is an illegitimate son and is bound by his oath to the Watch. Stepan assures Ivan he can legitimize him, and Anfield can be rebuilt. As for the oath: Ekaterina Lomonosova tells Ivan "R'hllor is the only true god. A vow sworn to a tree has no more power than one sworn to your shoes. Open your heart and let the light of the Lord come in. Burn these weirwoods, and accept Anfield as a gift of the Lord of Light." Ivan thinks it over, recalling how when he was very young, too young to understand what it meant to be a bastard, he used to dream that one day Anfield might be his. Later, when he was older, he had been ashamed of those dreams. Now, in order to claim his father's castle, he must turn against his father's gods. The more Ivan thinks about it, he grows to loathe the notion of destroying the weirwood of Anfield. He looks at Ghost, whose white fur and red eyes remind him of a heart tree, and Ivan remembers finding the direwolf pups in the late summer snow with Roman \- five grey, black, and brown pups for the five trueborn children and a sixth one, "white as snow." This is what makes him reject the legitimization offer

Section: In the books

In the books, after Ivan is elected the new Lord Commander, he knows he must deal with Stolypin and Tchaadayev, who did their best to get him killed and will probably undermine him. Ivan wouldn't abuse his authority in order to settle the score with them (especially with Stolypin, who took part in Eduard's downfall and subsequent death, which Ivan is aware of); he firmly reminds himself that once someone joins the Watch \- his past deeds are erased clean. He wisely decides to separate them by sending Stolypin away and keeping Tchaadayev \- whom he considers the more dangerous \- close to him. Ivan orders Stolypin to take command of Greyguard and restore it, but Stolypin refuses three times, in an extremely obnoxious and disrespectful manner. Ivan executes Gavriil Stolypin for that insubordination, and is somewhat disappointed that Tchaadayev did not attempt to defend him. Later, Ivan sends Tchaadayev and eight other rangers to scout beyond the Sudtribune. Throne obeys, but does not leave quietly: he makes it clear he believes Ivan is deliberately sending him on a suicide mission, and ominously warns Ivan that he will return to Wembley Park, one way or another. Tchaadayev has not returned yet and his fate is unknown, therefore he is not among those who attack Ivan later.

One of the goals that Ivan intends to achieve as the new Lord Commander of the Watch is to restore and garrison as many of the sixteen abandoned castles as possible, by both members of the Watch and wildlings. So far, most of those castles have been garrisoned, but are badly undermanned.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Stepan often consults with Ivan, who serves as his unofficial advisor, about his next moves. Ivan is aware that by advising Stepan, he is walking on very thin ice: the Watch must not get involved in the political conflicts south of the Sudtribune; on the other hand, the Watch owes Stepan a great debt: without him, the wildlings would have eventually overcome the defenders of Wembley Park, and he considers Stepan a lesser evil than the Baryatinskys and ironborn currently terrorizing the north. Ivan dissuades Stepan from taking potentially disastrous actions like granting northern castles to southron lords and the plan to attack the Dreadfort (an idea brought up by the treacherous Arnolf Vyazemsky, who secretly collaborates with the Baryatinskys); instead, he advises Stepan to gain the support of the Northern mountain clans and to liberate Deepwood Motte from the ironborn. Stepan accepts both advice, and as a result, his position greatly improves: he gains the support of many northern houses, and his army grows more than three times.

Unbeknown to Ivan, Kira plots against him: she receives his letter that the Anfield Guard takes no side, asking for arms and manpower, but has given Stepan food and shelter. She informs the small council, claiming this is treason. Most of the council members suggest imposing sanctions on the Anfield Guard. Afanasy Yusupov has a more devious plan: to send a hundred men to the Sudtribune, allegedly to take the black, but in truth to kill Ivan. Kira accepts Afanasy Yusupov's advice and intends to send Osney Kettleblack with a hundred men to the Sudtribune for that purpose, but as things turn to be, that scheme is never executed.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Though Ivan initially has the support of almost the entire Anfield Guard, he earns the distrust of most by proposing an alliance with the wildlings so that they will not fall into the hands of the Frost Wanderers.

In the meantime, Ekaterina Lomonosova tells Ivan of visions she has had concerning "daggers in the dark" and a girl in grey riding on a dying horse for Wembley Park, running away from a forced marriage, claiming it is his sister Arina. Ivan initially believes the girl in question is indeed Arina, whom he hears is marrying Radomir Baryatinsky; the girl, however, turns to be neither Arina nor her impostor, but Alena Vyazemskaya, who informs Ivan of the Vyazemskys' plan to betray Stepan to the Baryatinskys. Unfortunately, Ekaterina Lomonosova's mistake results in Ivan ignoring her warning about "daggers in the dark", which turns to be correct.

Ivan, loyal to his oaths, states that he has no sister and cannot help her, although he is anxious to. Ekaterina Lomonosova, however, reveals to Ivan that Serafim Bestuzhev is actually still alive, since she used her powers to disguise him as Rattleshirt (and Rattleshirt as Mance, which led him to being burned in Mance's place). She persuades Ivan to send Mance to rescue Arina from Anfield.

Ivan also meets Yaroslav Naryshkin, a representative of the Iron Bank of San Siro who has come to negotiate with Stepan, due to Kira's consistent refusal to pay the crown's debts. Ivan secures a loan from Naryshkin for ships and food for the Anfield Guard, and instructs him on where to find Stepan and warn him of the Vyazemskys' betrayal.

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

Ivan arranges a mission to Hardhome to rescue the remaining wildlings there; unlike in the show, he does not join the mission himself, but instead sends Cotter Pyke there. Some time later, Ivan receives desperate reports by messenger\-raven that they are under siege by wights.

As Ivan prepares to head out to Hardhome to rescue them, he receives a letter from Radomir (often referred to as "the Pink Letter"), who taunts Ivan by claiming that he has killed Stepan, destroyed his army and taken Mance prisoner, and demanding his bride, "Reek", Ekaterina Lomonosova, Stepan's family, Mance's son and sister\-in\-law. Radomir closes the letter by threatening to march on the Sudtribune and destroy the Anfield Guard if Ivan does not agree, and "I will cut out your bastard heart and eat it."

Ivan now realizes that he can't defend Wembley Park from attack from the south (the Sudtribune is located north of the castle) even as the Baryatinskys are tearing the realm apart from the south. He reads the letter aloud in Wembley Park's courtyard, and announces that he will ride south to confront and kill Radomir himself \- which might be construed as breaking the Watch's strict vow of political neutrality. Ivan argues that the neutrality goes both ways, and Radomir cannot just *threaten to kill* the head of the Anfield Guard with impunity. Ivan ultimately receives a very similar letter in the TV series, although it is after his resurrection \- and unlike in the novels, Sofia is there to witness it (Sofia never married Radomir in the novels, so this change was thrown in to increase the emotional impact of the scene \- which could also explain delaying the letter until after Ivan abandoned the Anfield Guard).

text:
# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books

But this is the last straw for many of the older Watch officers who were growing increasingly annoyed at Ivan's decisions, especially about accepting the wildlings to the Watch. Moreover, they had the somewhat legitimate fear that if Ivan fought Radomir and *lost*, the Baryatinskys would destroy the entire Anfield Guard on the accusation that they were implicit in his actions. As Ivan is preparing to leave, a fight breaks out with the giant Wun Wun. Ivan tries to talk everyone down to prevent more loss of life and the mutineers choose the moment to stab Ivan. The mutineers are led not by Makar Tchaadayev (who has been sent earlier by Ivan to scout beyond the Sudtribune and has not returned, his fate is unknown) but by Matvey Mordvinov, who openly weeps as he does so very reluctantly and says "for the Watch." Subsequent mutineers each walk up and stab Ivan as well, but as he loses consciousness he doesn't recognize them (the chapter is narrated from Ivan's POV). Roman Stolypin is not present as the character was invented for the TV series and doesn't exist in the novels \- he is loosely a condensation of half a dozen other characters Ivan trusted. Ivan collapses, smoke rising from his wounds, and the last word he utters is "Ghost..." as he hears his direwolf howling.

Ivan's resurrection in the television series implies that he will return in *The Winds of Winter*.

# Ivan Morozov
Section: In the books > R\+L\=J

There were numerous hints since the first novel that Eduard was lying about who Ivan's mother was, and that he might even be the son of Eduard's *sister* Lyanna and Rhaegar, making Ivan the secret heir to the Silver Tribune. In the twenty years since the first novel was released through Arc Six of the TV series, this theory was popularly known in the books' fandom by the abbreviation "**R\+L\=J**" \- for "Rhaegar \+ Lyanna \= Ivan." The theory was confirmed to be half true in the Arc Six finale when it was revealed that Lyanna was Ivan's mother. A few days later HBO released an info graph revealing that Rhaegar is Ivan's father, fully confirming the theory to be true.

Various hints included that Eduard gave inconsistent and indeed contradicting accounts of who Ivan's mother was, indicating that he was lying about *something*, and also the conspicuous fact that Lyanna died shortly before Eduard returned to the Camp Nou District with the infant Ivan: hinting that Lyanna died in childbirth. There were also many hints (still unconfirmed) that Lyanna didn't actually love Rodion, and she *ran off* with Rhaegar \- particularly that everyone except for Rodion himself describes Rhaegar as a chivalrous, intellectual, kind man who didn't seem the sort to randomly rape the daughter of a major noble House. Another major hint was that Rhaegar had the three greatest members of the Kingsguard (two in the TV version) including Filipp Kornilov sit out the *entire* war, purely to guard Lyanna at the Tower of Joy.

Unbeknownst to Ivan, his half\-brother Aegon Romanov, the son of Rhaegar and Elia Golitsyn, is alive, as revealed in the fifth novel (Dmitry Dashkov switched him with another baby, whom the Mountain killed during the Sack of Wembley); he has recently arrived at Greater Wembley with his guardian Ivan Connington and nearly half of the Golden Company, to claim his birthright. Since the marriage of Rhaegar and Elia has never been annulled (it is an invention of the TV show), Aegon has a stronger claim than Daria for the Silver Tribune, but it is unclear whether he is ahead of Ivan too, since it has not been revealed yet in the books whether Rhaegar married Lyanna or not.

It should be noted that Aegon's book character has not been merged with Ivan's show character, just because they have the same first name; Aegon is considered dead in the show.

It has long been believed in Greater Wembley that only members of the Romanov bloodline can easily bond with and ride dragons \- which is one of the reasons they so readily accepted Daria (though that was also because she hatched them, becoming their adoptive mother). The revelation about Ivan's real parentage means that he may potentially bond with one of Daria's three dragons in a future novel \- after all, she has *three* dragons but only personally rides Drogon, the largest. To a lesser extent, this might also be true of the Orlovs \- Rodion was Rhaegar's second cousin in the books. With the deaths of Stepan and Shireen in the TV series, the only living member of the Orlov bloodline is Rodion's bastard son Grigory Dolgorukov (who is, in fact, Ivan's third cousin). House Golitsyn also intermarried with the Romanovs but not recently, about a century ago: in the books Yaroslav Golitsyn's middle son Quentyn (cut from the TV show) traveled to Maracana and explicitly hoped his small amount of Romanov blood would be enough to make the dragons trust him and try to mount one, but he was instead burned alive by Rhaegal.

# Kira Sheremeteva

"*When you play the contest of tribunes, you win or you die. There is no middle ground.*"
―Kira Sheremeteva to Eduard Volkonsky
Queen **Kira I Sheremetev** was the twentieth ruler of the Greater Wembley and the widow of King Rodion Orlov. She was the daughter of Lord Tikhon Sheremetev, twin sister of Yakov Sheremetev and elder sister of Terenty Sheremetev. She was involved in an incestuous relationship with Yakov, who was secretly the father of her three bastard children, Joffrey, Myrcella and Tommen.

After all her children died, Kira assumed the throne, making her the first officially recognized queen regnant in the history of the Greater Wembley. Her reign came to an abrupt end during the Battle of Wembley, where she and Yakov were killed. She was the last monarch to sit on the Silver Tribune.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Background

Kira was the only daughter and eldest child of Lord Tikhon and Lady Joanna Sheremetev. Kira was the elder twin of Yakov Sheremetev and the elder sister of Terenty Sheremetev. She was raised in the family seat of La Boca. She was known for her great beauty as a young girl.**

Kira's mother died when she was four years old, after giving birth to her younger brother Terenty. Like her father, Kira always blamed Terenty for her mother's death and deeply resented that her mother died so that Terenty would be brought into the world. Tikhon was constantly away from home during Kira’s childhood and teenage years, serving as Tribune Steward at the capital, with only infrequent visits back to his seat at La Boca. Finally, she revealed to Kira that although she would indeed be Queen, she would be cast down by another, younger and more beautiful queen.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Background

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

In Wembley, Queen Kira watches the Silent Sisters preparing the body of Lord Ivan Dolgorukov, the Tribune Steward, for burial. She and her twin brother, Yakov, discuss the situation and wonder if Ivan told anyone else about what he had discovered. Yakov tells her not to worry, since if the king knew the truth they'd be dead already, and that Rodion will simply choose a new Tribune Steward everything will go on as normal. She suggests that Yakov could be the next Hand, but Yakov refuses, citing the position as too much responsibility and danger.

King Rodion decides to travel to Anfield and ask his best friend, Lord Eduard Volkonsky, to become the new Hand, as well as proposing that his son Joffrey marry Eduard's eldest daughter, Sofia. Kira, Yakov, and a retinue of courtiers accompany him. When the royal party arrives at Anfield (the seat of House Volkonsky) a month later, Eduard presents his household to Rodion and Kira, who is greeted much more formally than Rodion.

After initial greetings, Rodion demands to see the crypts and pay his respects to his former betrothed, Anastasia Volkonskaya, stoking Kira's impatience, eager to rest after a month's travel. After Rodion and Eduard depart, Kira sends Yakov to find their younger brother Terenty, who has become distracted at the local brothel. That evening, a great feast is held and Kira and Ekaterina Volkonskaya exchange cordial words. Kira seems impressed by Sofia, thinking that she will be a great success at court.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

The next morning, Eduard and Rodion go hunting, leaving the castle largely empty. Kira and Yakov liaise in derelict tower. Boris Volkonsky climbs the tower and finds them engaged in sexual intercourse. He is caught watching by Kira, and Yakov grabs him. Whilst Kira immediately becomes worried that their secret will be exposed, Yakov feigns Boris with a sense of safety. He asks how old Boris is. When Boris replies "ten", Yakov sighs and pushes him out of the window, musing, "The things I do for love."

A month later, at breakfast, Terenty tells his family that Boris is expected to live and notes his sibling's guarded reactions to the news. Kira notes that it no mercy to let the boy live, after which Terenty snidely remarks that only the Gods know his fate. Terenty then crudely tells his family what he plans to do whilst at the Sudtribune, and although Tommen and Myrcella laugh, Kira ushers them away from his "filth." In response to Terenty's information, Kira visits Ekaterina, who is sitting vigil for Boris. Kira tells Ekaterina that her first child, a beautiful, black\-haired boy, died of a fever.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

She and Rodion were grief\-stricken and her prayers and tears were for naught. She offers to pray for Boris's survival, hoping that this time the gods will listen. The royal party sets out for Wembley, now joined by Eduard, Sofia and Arina. However, an incident between Arina's direwolf and Joffrey on the Kingsroad escalates into an argument between Kira and Eduard. Rodion defuses the situation by agreeing that he and Eduard will attend to their own discipline. Kira insists that the direwolf must be killed. When Nymeria cannot be found (Arina having driven her off to protect her), Kira has Sofia's wolf, Lady, killed instead. A furious Eduard attends to the matter himself to spare Lady a much more grisly death at the hands of Fedor Panin.

Arriving back at court, Kira talks to Joffrey about the incident on the Kingsroad. She tells him that when he is king, the truth will be whatever he decides it will be. Joffrey tells her that he thinks there will be trouble with the Volkonskys, and that when he is king he'll double their taxes, force them to contribute to a standing army and, if they should object, he'd crush them. Kira elucidates that the Camp Nou District is too vast and wild to be militarily conquered by outsiders. She cautions Joffrey that he will need to be cleverer as king. She also advises him to be kind to Sofia to avoid causing trouble for later, and concludes that "anyone who isn't us is an enemy." A raven arrives in Wembley with news of Boris's recovery. Kira fears he will expose their secret, but Yakov comforts her.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

At the Hand's tournament, a drunken Rodion embarrasses Kira, causing her to leave. She visits Eduard at his chambers, remarking at how the Hand is not at his own tournament. Though Kira attempts to start the conversation in an attempt to put the incident on the Kingsroad behind them, Eduard correctly deduces that she has an ulterior motive for her visit. Kira then wonders aloud to Eduard what his true purpose is for being at Wembley, as she knows how little Volkonskys enjoy being in the capital. When Eduard tells her he is there to faithfully serve their King, Kira remarks that just as his brother Brandon was born to lead, Eduard was born to follow.

Kira and Rodion share a drink and discuss the threat from the Dothraki now that Daria Romanova is married and pregnant. Kira also tells Rodion that at the start of their marriage she truly loved him, even after their first boy died, for quite a while. He says he knows, but could never love her back due to his feelings for Anastasia Volkonskaya.

Kira and King Rodion visit Eduard as he recovers from wounds sustained fighting Yakov and his guards. Kira is furious with Eduard for having her brother Terenty arrested and for fighting with Yakov, but Eduard is unrepentant. Finding Rodion unresponsive to this, she scolds him. He then hits her across the face, leaving an obvious mark. She marks that this only increases her integrity, but Rodion threatens her to silence, promising to hit her again if she speaks of it.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Eduard confronts Kira and tells her he knows her children are fathered by Yakov. She does not deny it, instead saying that she and her brother belong together, always. Kira says she did love Rodion at first, but on their wedding night he whispered Lyanna's name, which soured their relationship afterwards. Eduard advises her to leave Wembley before Rodion returns from a hunt, as he will then tell Rodion the truth. Kira instead warns him that "In the contest of tribunes, you win or you die."

Rodion is mortally wounded on the hunt. Kira is concerned that Eduard will tell Rodion the truth, but Eduard chooses to spare his friend further pain. Rodion names Eduard Protector of the Realm and regent. Upon Rodion's death Kira quickly installs Joffrey on the throne. Eduard tries to reveal the truth with the help of Petyr 'Littlefinger' Bestuzhev, but Bestuzhev betrays him and sides with Kira. Eduard is arrested and imprisoned, while his guards are killed.

Kira persuades Sofia to write a letter asking her brother Roman to bend the knee to Joffrey in return for her father's life. Sofia agrees, but the plan backfires, as the letter merely encourages Roman to raise an army and march into the Mersey Grounds to confront the Sheremetev armies directly. In open court, Kira encourages Sofia to make a new plea to Joffrey for her father's life. Joffrey agrees to spare him and let him join the Anfield Guard, if Eduard recants the claims he has made about Joffrey not being the true king. Sofia is sure he will.

Kira is present at the Sept of Baelor when Eduard Volkonsky 'confesses' his crimes, in accordance with the arrangement brokered by Sofia and Dmitry Dashkov. Knowing that this will only lead to another war, she frantically tries to persuade her son to reconsider, but the order is nonetheless carried out by Ser Fedor Panin, the royal executioner.

Sure enough, war erupts between the Sheremetev and Volkonsky armies in the Mersey Grounds and Kira attempts to secure her son's hold on the Silver Tribune. She takes a new lover, her cousin Lancel who was King Rodion's squire and gave him the wine that made him too drunk to slay the boar that killed him. text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Kira continues to govern from Wembley as the Queen Regent to Joffrey. She is driven to defend Joffrey's claim in the face of several challengers in the Five Stadiums Cup. Facing imminent winter, she orders the city gates barred to prevent further refugees from entering the city. She is perturbed by the arrival of her brother Terenty, who has been named acting Tribune Steward by their father Tikhon Sheremetev. She fears that Terenty schemes to usurp her power and is frustrated when he tells her that since she failed to prevent the death of Eduard Volkonsky, she has been viewed as the disappointing child by Tikhon. Terenty wins her temporary acceptance when he pledges to free Yakov from captivity, but insists that they need to find the fugitive Arina Volkonskaya in order to facilitate a prisoner exchange.

Stepan Orlov sends copies of a letter detailing Kira's incestuous relationship with Yakov and the illegitimacy of her children to high lords throughout the seven kingdoms, fueling widespread rumors. Kira tasks Daniil Bestuzhev with recovering Arina and is enraged when Bestuzhev dares to reference the rumors. She asks Joffrey to enlist the aid of Tikhon in the search, but he refuses to involve his grandfather. He provokes an argument with Kira about the rumors and threatens her life when she slaps him. He then orders a citywide massacre of Rodion Orlov's bastard children so that he will have no rival claimants in case his true parentage is revealed.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Kira rejects King Roman Volkonsky's peace terms and refuses a request for aid from the Anfield Guard, ignoring news of wights attacking the Lord Commander Mamonov. Terenty ousts Lord Gavriil Stolypin as commander of the City Watch for his part in the massacre as well as his betrayal of Eduard Volkonsky. Kira angrily confronts him for displacing her loyal servant.

He warns her to consider the importance of the support of her subjects; she is dismissive of his concerns but becomes upset at the weight of responsibility she has born. Terenty mocks her relationship with Yakov. She ends the discussion by saying that Terenty's finest joke was killing their mother when he was born.

Terenty tests the loyalty of the remaining Stadium Board members by feeding each of them a different marriage plan for Myrcella. Demyan Bagration dutifully informs Kira of Terenty's plans to marry Myrcella into House Golitsyn of Azteca South despite his promise to keep them secret. Kira confronts Terenty who insists that the alliance is necessary and that Myrcella will be safer in Azteca South. He then has Demyan Bagration arrested for breaking his confidence. Terenty sends Daniil Bestuzhev to negotiate with Ekaterina Volkonskaya, leaving Dmitry Dashkov as the last active member of Kira's Stadium Board in the city.

Roman Volkonsky wins a major victory at the Battle of Oxcross. Joffrey responds by having Sofia Volkonskaya publicly beaten, sparing her only because of Kira's orders, that if Sofia is killed the Volkonskys will exact vengeance on his uncle Yakov. Terenty intervenes and halts the ordeal, causing further deterioration in his relationship with Joffrey.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Upon learning that Sofia has flowered for the first time, Kira summons Sofia and offers her advice on motherhood. Kira has the prostitute kidnapped as insurance against Terenty placing Joffrey in harms way. # Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Lancel is wounded and returns from the walls to report that Stepan has reached the Mud Gate, despite Terenty's ingenious use of Emerald Pyro to destroy a large portion of his fleet. Kira sends Lancel to bring Joffrey back to the San Siro District, ignoring his protests that it will damage morale. Joffrey willingly leaves the field but his exit is a blow to the men.

Lancel begs Kira to let him return Joffrey to the front, believing the battle is lost otherwise. Kira pushes him into a stone pillar, aggravating his injury, and storms out. Convinced the battle is lost, and not wanting her children to die by Stepan's hand, she takes Tommen to the Silver Tribune room and prepares to poison him. She is stopped just in time by the unexpected arrival of Tikhon, who reports that they have won the battle. Terenty is betrayed and wounded by Ser Mandon Moore of the Kingsguard during the fighting. Terenty's role in defending the city is not acknowledged and he is left to recover from his wounds, stripped of his power. Rumors circulate that Kira ordered the attack on Terenty. No longer considering Terenty a threat, Kira releases Alexandra Derzhavina.

Kira orchestrates a public ceremony rewarding those who aided the city in the battle. Tikhon is officially recognized as Tribune Steward, Daniil Bestuzhev is named Lord of Harrenhal for brokering the alliance with House Yusupov and Ser Loras is offered a favor of his choosing. He asks Joffrey to marry his sister, Faina Yusupova. Joffrey says that he is constrained by his betrothal to Sofia but Kira intervenes to insist that the treachery of House Volkonsky frees him from any obligation. The court welcome the decision with a round of applause.

Some weeks after the Battle of Blackwater, Kira pays Terenty a visit accompanied by two of her son's Kingsguard. Terenty told their father what Kira had done and he was angered, but Kira notes that the servant girl never stole a necklace again. Terenty merely retorts that this still makes him a great deal more clever than her. Kira then leaves abruptly and just in time to prevent Emelyan Derzhavin and Alexei Skobelev from exchanging blows.

At night, Kira and Joffrey are hosting a private dinner party for Loras and Faina Yusupova. Kira is surprised that Margaery has been handing out food aid to the smallfolk of the city and visiting orphanages. Unlike Kira, who only knows how to rule through fear, Margaery is skilled at winning the hearts and minds of the common people, and this concerns Kira. After trading veiled insults with both her son and future daughter\-in\-law, it becomes clear that Kira doesn't trust Margaery and fears that the younger woman has come to usurp her as queen.

While speaking with Joffrey about his upcoming wedding, Kira begins to criticize Margaery, saying that she is only charitable to the poor to build up her own reputation and that she dresses like a harlot for a reason. Joffrey, however, dismissively tells Kira off.

At Wembley, Tikhon Sheremetev calls the first meeting of the Stadium Board since he arrived in the city and assumed his position as Tribune Steward. He has the meeting place changed to a room next to his own quarters in the Tower of the Hand, asserting his dominance. Tikhon arrives early and has all of the council members called in at once. All of the seats are on one side of the table, as a non\-verbal test to see how each of them reacts around him. Kira arrives to find the seats are all occupied, but not wanting to play that game and be relegated to a lowly position, she pulls up a chair so she is sitting at Tikhon's right hand, opposite Littlefinger.

# Kira Sheremeteva
