While Joffrey is giving Margaery a tour of the Sept of Baelor, Kira speaks with Lady Olenna, exchanging stories about their deceased husbands. When Margaery takes Joffrey with her to greet the common people, Kira realizes that she has lost control of Joffrey to the Yusupovs. Later, Kira meets with Tikhon to discuss the Yusupovs and informs him how Margaery has begun to manipulate Joffrey. Tikhon is satisfied, as Kira has only let Joffrey do whatever he pleased. He also tells her that she is not as smart as she thinks she is and that undermining the Yusupovs would be irrational considering how they helped defeat Stepan. When Margaery and Joffrey wave to the crowd outside the Sept, Kira initially fears for Joffrey's safety. Upon realizing that the crowd is hailing the two, Kira then realizes that Margaery has a control over Joffrey.

Kira encounters Lord Bestuzhev and informs him that she fears the Yusupovs do not have the Sheremetevs' best interest at heart. Littlefinger agrees that he will use his spies to uncover their plans, one of which turns out to be marrying Loras to Sofia. Initially, Kira is delighted when her father decides to "kill this union in its crib" by instead having Terenty marry Sofia to secure the Camp Nou District. However, her smug attitude towards Terenty when this is revealed to him quickly evaporates when Tikhon reveals that he intends to have her marry Loras to secure the Reach.

Kira protests against this, saying she is Queen Regent and not some broodmare, but Tikhon angrily asserts that she is his daughter and she will do what he tells her and put an end to the "rumors" about her. Kira begs her father not to make her enter another loveless marriage but Tikhon refuses to hear another word from either of his children, saying they have disgraced the family name for far too long. As Tikhon leaves the room, Kira hesitantly opens her eyes and shifts her gaze toward Terenty, expecting to see him laughing at her but Terenty is too glum about his own awkward predicament.

Kira and Terenty Sheremetev observe Loras and Sofia from Kira's chambers overlooking the garden. Terenty sarcastically asks which of the four of them has it the worst. He then finally accuses his sister of trying to have him killed during the Wembley Final. Kira, tired of fighting him, remains quiet while he deduces that only two people can command the Kingsguard. Terenty realizes that while Kira certainly has the authority to command a Kingsguard, she isn't stupid enough to command Ser Mandon Moore to kill him in public. Terenty realizes that it was in fact Joffrey who ordered Ser Mandon Moore to kill him, because Terenty was the only one who stood up to him. Kira tells him his life is not in danger from Joffrey, as he dare not try anything like that now that Tikhon is the Hand. They discuss about Yakov's possible return to Wembley, with Kira wondering where he could possibly be. She asks Terenty which one of them should be the one to break the news to Sofia. Terenty decides he might as well dash Sofia's hopes sooner rather than later.

As the court gathers for Terenty's wedding, Kira finally snaps when Margaery says she looks radiant. At the end of the meeting, she leads Joffrey to bed after he calls out Tikhon's cowardice during the Rebellion.

Kira questions his loyalty to their enemies, but Yakov states that he only did it so he could return to her. She then asks if he could track down and kill Sofia Volkonskaya, believing that she schemed with Terenty to murder Joffrey. Yakov remains silent. He then tries to convince Kira that Terenty is innocent, but she refutes that he has always pitied their little brother and firmly believes that Terenty is the monster that killed their son. Kira tells Yakov that she wants four men at Tommen's door and abruptly dismisses him, referring to him only as "Lord Commander", showing that their relationship has almost completely deteriorated.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Kira is present at the coronation of her son, Tommen. Seeing Margaery at the coronation, Kira tells her that she understands that Joffrey was a monster, but as her first child, Kira still loved him.

She also believes the newly crowned Tommen will make a good and decent king, but he needs guidance. Kira asks Margaery if she is still interested in being queen. Margaery says she will need to speak to her father about the matter.

Kira is present at a Stadium Board that discusses the threat of Daria Romanova, who they learn has recently conquered Maracana. Kira doubts that Daria is a credible threat to the Silver Tribune, a view not shared by the rest of the council. When Dmitry Dashkov mentions that Lavr Kutuzov has been spotted in the Mersey Grounds, Kira recounts him as being both a coward and a traitor to the crown.

At Terenty's trial, Kira is verbally confronted by Terenty, who angrily declares his innocence, but tells her how he wishes he could have been the one to murder Joffrey and that he felt the boy deserved it.

Kira bribes Alexei Skobelev to sway him from being Terenty's champion in his trial by combat by arranging for him to marry Praskovya Skobeleva, and later she approaches Leonid Kutuzov and enlists him as her champion.

Initially worried for the possibility of Kutuzov's failure, as Terenty's champion, Yuriy Golitsyn, has more passion throughout the fight, as Kutuzov killed his sister, Elia Golitsyn. However, this ultimately proves to be Oberyn's downfall, as Gregor manages to maneuver him to the ground and crush his skull. She watches proudly as the Mountain defeats him and smiles as their father sentences Terenty to death. She later sees to the treatment of Ser Gregor's wounds.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Escorted by Ser Meryn, Kira walks to the Great Sept of Baelor for Tikhon's funeral, surrounded by numerous lords and ladies, including Margaery, who she glances at suspiciously. Kira is stopped by the Pavel Nikonov, who suggests to her that they start soon, since lords and ladies have come from all over Greater Wembley, but she says they will wait a little longer while she has a moment alone with Yakov and their father's corpse.

Inside, Yakov warns that all the power and prestige their father built for House Sheremetev belongs to them now, and that once everyone sees that Tikhon is truly dead, their enemies will do everything they can to take it away from them. Kira bluntly states that their true enemy is Terenty and that Yakov is partly responsible for Tikhon's death since he was the one who released their father's murderer, and then she leaves him.

Later, during Tikhon's wake, Kira is approached by Loras, who babbles on and on, but she ignores him, as she is intently watching Tommen and Margaery sharing a few words and holding hands. Demyan Bagration offers his condolences, yet she completely ignores him as well. She is then approached by Lancel, who has recovered from his wounds at the Blackwater and become extremely pious and joined the Sparrows. Kevan apologizes for the appearance of his son, but Kira comforts him by saying Lancel will grow out of this phase. While she is having a private moment, Lancel approaches her again and asks for her forgiveness for their "unnatural" relationship, and for serving Rodion the wine that led to his death. Kira brushes off Lancel's request, and his prayers for Tikhon's soul.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Kira summons Yakov to show him a box she's received. Inside, a stuffed Red Viper holds Myrcella's necklace in its jaws. Kira is both unnerved and unsurprised by the threat as Azteca South blames the Sheremetevs for the deaths of Oberyn and Elia Golitsyn. Acknowledging Kira's distress, Yakov makes a promise: "I'm going to Azteca South. And I'm bringing our daughter home." When Yakov asks Alexei Skobelev to join him in this quest, he reveals that Kira has arranged for Wyllis Bracken to wed Praskovya Skobeleva instead of Alexei Skobelev, breaking their agreement.

Later, two men bring Kira the head of a dwarf. She's disappointed it's not her brother, but donates the head to Afanasy Yusupov's lab. Kira presides over the Stadium Board and doles out new titles on Tommen's behalf: Afanasy Yusupov is named Master of Whisperers, and Ruslan Yusupov takes on the additional title of Master of Coin. When Kira appoints her uncle Kevan as Master of War, he rejects the offer. "I did not return to the capital to serve as your puppet," he says, emphasizing that Tommen should attend the meetings himself. Kevan reminds Kira she's nothing more than Queen Mother, and he decides to return to La Boca. Kira is left dissatisfied with Kevan's departure.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

On the way to the Sept of Baelor, Kira is incensed to find the crowd cheering Margaery's name. She remains stone\-faced throughout the ceremony. The following morning, Kira walks with Tommen along the battlements and tries to subtly turn him against his wife, but Tommen scares her by asking her if she'd prefer to go back to La Boca. Kira goes to confront Margaery, finding her bragging about Tommen's libido to her handmaidens. Kira tries to verbally spar with Margaery as she used to, but the younger queen is in her prime, and assaults Kira with backhanded compliments and subtle barbs. Realizing that she is losing, Kira departs.

Later on, Kira and the Stadium Board are visited by the Pavel Nikonov, who has recently been abducted from Littlefinger's brothel and forced to walk naked through the streets of Wembley. Kira is mildly amused and not particularly sympathetic to the man's plight. She later pays a visit to the so\-called Lavr Patrikeev. Assuming a much more conciliatory and humble tone than she ever has before, Kira talks with him about the relationship between the Faith and the Crown, and also mentions that she's had the Pavel Nikonov thrown in the Black Cells.

Kira meets with the Lavr Patrikeev again and names him as the new Pavel Nikonov, allowing him to reinstate the Faith Militant, a military order dedicated to defending the Faith of the Seven which was abolished two centuries ago. Savva Yusupov is arrested during the ensuing rampage for his homosexuality, which Margaery believes is part of Kira's plan to divide her and Tommen.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Tommen confronts his mother and demands that Loras be released, but she calmly tells him that she didn't order his arrest, although her tone of voice seems to imply that she knew beforehand that Loras would be arrested and allowed it to happen in order to interfere with Margaery and Tommen's relationship.

During her meetings with Littlefinger, Kira again feigns ignorance about Loras' arrest and seems unconcerned about what repercussions this might have. The Queen Regent is about to dismiss Bestuzhev when he admits that even though he lost track of Arina, he has discovered Sofia Volkonskaya's whereabouts.

She's finally back at Anfield 'allying' herself with House Baryatinsky. Kira is naturally livid that the Baryatinskys have betrayed her and vows that they'll end up being flayed for their crimes. Petyr then suggests that Kira could just wait a while until Stepan has dealt with the Baryatinskys or vice versa. The Dortmund Heights army (under his command) could later easily mop up the remains. The only boon Littlefinger wants for his service is to be named Keeper of Camp Nou District. Kira readily agrees on the condition that Bestuzhev brings her Sofia's head.

After a brief but tense meeting with Olenna in which mutual insults are exchanged, Kira takes part in the trial of Savva Yusupov. Though she appears incredulous towards the accusations, it is clear that she has played a part in engineering the entire process. She plays the same trump card that she once did with Terenty and Nina Suvorova by making a deal with Ignat Gagarin, Loras's lover, to testify against Loras in exchange for being spared from persecution. As a result of her schemes, Loras is to be put on trial, and Margaery is imprisoned for giving false testimony.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

When Tommen loses his appetite over his wife's arrest, Kira attempts to calm him down, and gives him a long speech about how as King, he will be faced with many circumstantial situations in which he will be powerless to act, as Rodion Orlov sometimes was, though she proclaims her love for him by claiming that she will do anything it takes to protect him, even if it means burning down entire cities, and weeps as she cuddles her son. She later visits Margaery in her cell, bringing her food and trying to convince her that she will do her utmost to get her out, but Margaery angrily counters that she knows Kira engineered both her arrest and Loras's in order to retain control over her son, and shouts at her to get out, throwing the bowl of stew at her and calling her a "hateful bitch." Kira leaves and finds the Lavr Patrikeev beneath the Sept of Baelor, who tells her that both Loras and Margaery will be put on trial, and certain septons, including himself, will stand as judges.

Kira thanks the Lavr Patrikeev for his actions, and he proceeds to give her a speech about the history of the Sept. He tells her that the Yusupovs' falsehoods will be revealed for all the world to see, as in the case of everyone, including Kira herself. The Lavr Patrikeev reveals that Lancel confessed his adulterous affair with Kira following Yakov's capture by Roman Volkonsky, and orders Kira arrested, to her horror. She is taken to a cell by a group of septas, but threatens them that her face is the last thing they will see before they die for what they are doing to her.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Kira remains in custody for the next few days, visited only by Septa Raisa Milutina, who offers her water in return for a confession, but she repeatedly refuses. She is later visited by Afanasy Yusupov, who informs her that the charges against her are treason, incest and regicide, which she dismisses as lies, though Afanasy Yusupov reminds her that the Faith will not depend on physical proof as much as the Crown does in her upcoming trial. She asks about Yakov, but Afanasy Yusupov claims there has been no response, and further tells her that Demyan Bagration has summoned Kevan back to the capital and Tommen has fallen into a depression.

Afanasy Yusupov, however, tells Kira that she can still confess, but she refuses. Before he leaves, Afanasy Yusupov tells her that his work is progressing. Later, when Raisa Milutina visits her again, Kira offers to make her a Lady of the capital or have her killed, depending on whether or not she will help her. Raisa Milutina pours her water on the floor and leaves. Kira finally abandons her pride and licks the water from the dungeon floor, breaking into tears.

Sometime later, Kira is brought before the Lavr Patrikeev to confess her sins. She confesses of adultery with Ser Ilya Sheremetev, but denies her incestuous relationship with her brother Yakov. She begs to be allowed to go to the San Siro District to see her son Tommen. The Lavr Patrikeev accepts, but states that she has to stand trial.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Kira is brought to a cell where she is stripped naked and washed, and her long blonde hair is cut short. She is then brought outside, where she is forced to walk completely naked through the streets of Wembley, from the Great Sept of Baelor to the San Siro District as punishment. She is escorted through an angry mob, who hurl filth and vicious insults at her.

With bloody feet, Kira makes it to the San Siro District. Upon entering the gates, Kira finds her uncle Ignat Sheremetev, Grand Maester Demyan Bagration and Afanasy Yusupov waiting for her. Afanasy Yusupov attempts to comfort her by covering her body with a cloak. Heavy footsteps are heard, and Afanasy Yusupov introduces Kira to the newest member of the Kingsguard: a seven foot tall man in golden armor, the Mountain, who has his face hidden constantly due to Afanasy Yusupov's experimentation and the effects of manticore venom. Afanasy Yusupov suggests Kira to go inside to have a look at her feet, which are badly injured, when the huge knight lifts her up and carries her away.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Once again residing in the San Siro District, Kira is alerted to Yakov's return and runs excitedly to the port to meet Myrcella for the first time in the space of almost 4 years, but her worst fears are realized when she sees a despondent Yakov standing alone on the boat, with a corpse behind him she immediately realizes is Myrcella's.

Later, Kira is comforted by Yakov in her quarters. Kira finally admits to Yakov that she believes their children's deaths truly are destined according to Maggy's prophecy, since both Joffrey and Myrcella are gone and the only one left is Tommen. Yakov scoffs it off and promises Kira revenge for all that their enemies have taken from them.

A man in Wembley brags about revealing himself to Kira during her walk of shame. When the man leaves the crowd to urinate, the gigantic Kingsguard knight walks up behind him and brutally kills him by smashing his head against the wall before reporting back to Kira.

When Kira attempts to leave for Myrcella's funeral with the Kingsguard knight in tow, a squad of guards blocks her path; their leader informs her that by order of the king, she is prohibited from leaving the castle, in the interest of her own protection. Kira demands that they move, but the guards do not budge, even when Kira's Kingsguard places a hand on his sword. Eventually, Kira acquiesces and retreats to her chambers. Tommen later visits his mother to apologize for doing nothing when she was arrested and forced to walk through the streets naked, then asks her to teach him to rule. Moved, Kira tearfully embraces her son.

Once alone, Kira wishes to speak with Tommen in private, having missed the past several Stadium Board meetings. Tommen is anxious to fight the Lavr Patrikeev, since Margaery is still a prisoner, though Kira reminds him of what the Sparrow forced her to do. Although Tommen knows his mother has always hated Margaery, Kira claims the rivalry is unimportant, explaining that kings and queens must command respect, and the Lavr Patrikeev is little more than an idealistic anarchist using the Faith to achieve his goals. After Tommen reveals his conversation with the Lavr Patrikeev and knowledge of something important, Kira presses him for information.
body:

When Yakov asks Afanasy Yusupov to order Leonid Kutuzov to slaughter the Lavr Patrikeev and the Faith Militant, Kira claims it will not be necessary, since she has opted for a trial by combat and again named Gregor as her champion.

She then orders Afanasy Yusupov to place his spies all over Greater Wembley to prevent any other Great Houses from benefiting from the Sheremetevs' disgrace. Kira, Yakov and Gregor attend a Stadium Board meeting, but Kevan, Demyan Bagration, Olenna and Ruslan Yusupov refuse to accept them, with Olenna coldly reminding Kira that she is no longer Queen. When they defy the council and sit down, Kevan leads the council out, leaving Kira alone with Yakov and Gregor.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Kira and Yakov attend another Stadium Board meeting, this time presided over by Kevan and Olenna. Though Olenna reminds Kira she is not welcome, adding her repeated humiliations, Yakov defends his sister, revealing that Tommen has been talking to the Lavr Patrikeev about Margaery and Loras. Kira points out the Lavr Patrikeev was expecting them to fight among each other, and before the trial, Margaery will perform her own walk of atonement, which Olenna agrees must not happen. Although Kira promises to destroy the Sparrows for corrupting Lancel, Kevan warns them the Lavr Patrikeev has many supporters, and more lives could be lost in the ensuing battle.

After his failure at the Sept of Baelor and forced removal from the Kingsguard, Yakov informs Kira he is being sent to Riverrun to help the Demidovs deal with Viktor Trubetskoy. Despite her brother's protests and anger over Tommen's decision to join the Lavr Patrikeev, Kira advises him to lead the Sheremetev army as their father intended, confident that the Mountain will win her trial by combat. She kisses Yakov goodbye, reminding him they are the only ones who matter.

Kira visits Feodora Yusupova in an attempt to convince her to stay in Wembley. She uses Margaery and Loras as an excuse for Olenna to stay, but Olenna angrily reminds Kira that all this is happening because of Kira herself. Olenna reminds her of the smug look she gave her when Loras and Margaery were being dragged away by the Faith Militant. She tells Kira that the universally hated Queen Mother has no support in Wembley, and has lost.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Afanasy Yusupov enters Kira's chamber to inform her that the Faith Militant have entered the San Siro District. Accompanied by Afanasy Yusupov and the Mountain, Kira confronts the group. Lancel tells her that the Lavr Patrikeev wishes to speak with her at the Sept of Baelor. When she refuses, Lancel tells her that it is not a request.

Kira retorts that the Lavr Patrikeev promised that she could stay in the San Siro District until her trial, which Lancel replies that no such promise was made. When Ser Leonid Kutuzov threatens the Faith Militant, Lancel tells Kira to order him aside or there would be violence. Kira says that she chooses violence. One of the Faith Militant attacks the Kingsguard, leaving several visible holes in his armor but drawing no blood. In response, the Mountain rips the man's head off and tosses it aside and Lancel and his men back down.

Later, Kira, Afanasy Yusupov and Ser Gregor enter the Great Hall to find a large crowd gathered for a royal announcement. The ladies in court look at the Queen Mother in detest. Kira asks Ignat Sheremetev why she was not informed. Kevan bars her from standing beside her son and tells her that her place was in the gallery "with the other ladies of the court." Kira reluctantly takes her place there while the other women stand aside, not wanting to be near her or Gregor.

King Matvey Orlov starts by saying that the Crown and the Faith are the two pillars that hold up this world, and should one collapse, so does the other. He also says that The Father judges them all, and if they break his laws, they shall be punished. He announces that Savva Yusupov and Kira's trial will be held in the Sept of Baelor on the first day of the festival of The Mother. After much prayer and reflection, he also announces that trial by combat will be forbidden in the Greater Wembley, stating that it is a scheme made by those who wants to escape true judgement from the Gods, and that Loras and Kira would stand trial before seven septons as it was in the earlier days of the Faith.

As the king leaves, Afanasy Yusupov tells a shocked Kira, who had been planning on calling a trial by combat with Gregor as her champion, that his little birds have been investigating an old rumor that she had told him about, and that it appears to be much more than a rumor.

On the day of her trial, Kira dresses incredibly ornately. She is adorned with fine clothes and all manners of jewelry. However, she does not show up at the Great Sept for her trial, instead viewing the city in the distance from the San Siro District. Unknown to those present at the trial, there is a large cache of wildfire underneath the Sept, placed there by Aerys II at the height of his insanity. Kira has Afanasy Yusupov's little birds light candles which eventually shrink to a size in which the cache can be ignited. Shortly before, Kira has Afanasy Yusupov and his little birds assassinate Demyan Bagration, so as to consolidate all power to her.

The explosion kills Margaery, Mace, and Savva Yusupov, Ignat Sheremetev, all of the Sparrows including Lancel and the Lavr Patrikeev, and a number of Wembley citizens. Through right of conquest, she has Afanasy Yusupov crown her Queen of the Greater Wembley. During the coronation, she sees Yakov from afar, who gives her a grim look.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Following her coronation, Kira shows Yakov a giant map of Greater Wembley and discusses the multiple foes they now face. While Kira has dreams of ushering in a long dynasty, Yakov reminds her that they are losing the war, and with all their children dead, there is no Sheremetev line to inherit the Silver Tribune. When Yakov asks Kira about Tommen, she responds angrily that he betrayed them by committing suicide. Kira adds that they are the only living Sheremetevs who count. Yakov tells her that they need allies and reports that House Demidov has been exterminated. Kira angrily reminds him that she has been listening to their father's counsel for the past forty years and has learnt some things.

They later meet with Taras Stroganov to discuss a possible alliance. Though Kira declines his offer of marriage, Euron graciously departs, promising to return with a gift that will win her heart. Later, Kira gives a speech urging several nobles from the Reach, including Lord Semyon Tatischev, to reaffirm their allegiance to the Silver Tribune and not follow House Yusupov in supporting Daria. Kira warns that the Romanov's Dothraki and Unsullied hordes would pillage their lands and homes, and rape their women. When Lord Tatischev points out that Daria has three dragons, Afanasy Yusupov replies that he is "at work on a solution."

Later, Afanasy Yusupov leads Kira to the dragon skulls beneath the San Siro District. He tells Kira that his spies have reported that one of Daria' dragons was wounded by a spear at Maracana, showing that the dragons are not invincible. Afanasy Yusupov then displays a ballista and reassures her that they can hurt dragons. Kira tests the ballista on the nearby skull of Balerion the Black Dread (the dragon of Aegon the Conqueror) and is pleased when the bolt pierces through the massive, hard skull.

Euron returns to the capital with Ellaria and Natalia Solovyova, the women who poisoned her daughter Myrcella. In recognition of Euron's gesture of good faith, Kira agrees to Euron's marriage proposal, though only after the war is won, and names him commander of the Silver Tribune's naval forces. She is cheered by the attendants in the Throne Room following her success, propagandising her defence as being compromised of the "sons and daughters of Greater Wembley."

Kira has Ellaria and Tyene both chained and gagged in one of the black cells. She tells Ellaria that even though they are enemies, she understands her captive's fury. She calls to mind how skillful a fighter Oberyn was up to the point when he got killed, taunting Ellaria by insinuating Oberyn brought his own death upon himself by taunting Gregor instead of just leaving him to die. She then reveals her own grief at losing her only daughter, and walks over to Tyene, complimenting her beauty before ungagging her and kissing her full on the lips with the very same poison that Ellaria used on Myrcella. Afanasy Yusupov puts the gag back on Tyene and gives Kira the antidote.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

After the Sack of Highgarden, Kira meets with Tycho, who is pleased that Kira will use the captured gold to pay off the Silver Tribune's massive debts to the bank, and he engages in open flattery by saying that she is as cunning at military strategy as her father Tikhon was, if not more so. Now that the Sheremetevs' old debts will be mostly paid off, and the Iron Bank's faith in them somewhat reassured by their recent military victories, Kira wants to take out new loans to strengthen her position in the war, so she can finish securing control over the rest of the continent. They discuss that Kira wants to use the money to hire foreign sellsword companies to bolster the depleted Sheremetev military ranks. Specifically, she reveals that she has had Afanasy Yusupov make overtures to hire the best and largest private mercenary army in all of the Milan Boroughs: the Golden Company. Tycho assures her that the Iron Bank will be delighted to help her with these future endeavors, once it receives the gold she is bringing them.

Yakov returns to Wembley to inform Kira of their defeat in the Battle of the Goldroad. He flatly insists that the Sheremetevs have no chance of defeating Daria, even if Kira were able to buy enough mercenaries to replace their huge losses; Afanasy Yusupov's scorpion did little more than anger Drogon, and neither the Sheremetev soldiers nor any mercenaries will be able to match the huge horde of Dothraki, who Yakov notes killed their men as if it were sport to them, not war. Kira snidely asks Yakov if they are expected to surrender to a Queen whose throne Kira occupies and whose father Yakov betrayed and murdered, mockingly remarking that Terenty could intercede for them with Daria.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Yakov reveals to Kira that Terenty is innocent of Joffrey's murder, telling her Feodora Yusupova confessed to it. Kira is dismissive, so Yakov talks her through it, asking her rhetorically if Olenna would prefer Margaery to marry the strong willed and sadistic Joffrey or the emotionally pliable and good\-natured Tommen. Effectively, Olenna would have become the true ruler of the Seven kingdoms behind the scenes \- in the same way that their father Tikhon Sheremetev became the true ruler of Greater Wembley through his grandsons.

Feeling cheated of yet another vengeance, Kira can barely contain her fury as she laments listening to Yakov, saying Olenna ought to have died screaming. Yakov then points out that such vengence is pointless, with House Yusupov now being extinct, as well as their isolation from anybody else of significance. Kira then surmises to say that she will fight to the bitter end rather than surrender.

Later, at the San Siro District, Afanasy Yusupov is visiting Kira when Yakov enters her chambers. Yakov tells Kira that he met with Terenty. When Kira asks if Daria wants to negotiate a surrender, Yakov tells her that Dasha is seeking an armistice due to the threat posed by the Army of the Dead. Kira knows that Alexei Skobelev secretly organized the meeting between Terenty and Yakov. Kira says that perhaps an alliance with Daria may be a wiser move, but she still retains her determination to destroy any force that stands against her. She also asks if Yakov plans to punish Alexei Skobelev for arranging the clandestine meeting with Terenty. She also reveals that she is pregnant with another of Yakov's children, one who she believes will someday be the heir to the Silver Tribune. After reflecting on their late father's advice that "the lion does not concern himself with the opinions of the sheep", Kira hugs Yakov and whispers in his ear that he is never to betray her again.

As the Dragonpit Summit comes into fruition, Afanasy Yusupov tells Kira from her chambers that Daria's forces are en route to the Dragonpit. Kira then warns Gregor that if anything should go wrong, he should kill Daria first, followed by Ivan and then Terenty, following then in any order she sees fit, before departing herself.

# Kira Sheremeteva

At the Dragonpit, the various factions meet: Kira, Yakov, Afanasy Yusupov and Euron representing the Silver Tribune, Ivan, Davos and Brienne representing the Camp Nou District, and Daria' court. When Kira demands to know where her rival is, the Fire Falcon Queen makes a suitably dramatic entrance on Drogon's back, with Rhaegal flying overhead. Euron tries to posture, threatening to kill Yara unless Timofey yields to him and deriding Terenty's dwarfism; when Terenty and Timofey retort to his taunts with their own, Euron remarks that Terenty would have been killed at birth in the Barra da Tijuca.

A furious Yakov orders Euron to sit down, and when he disregards the warning, Kira reiterates it; a subdued Euron returns to his seat. Getting the meeting on track, Terenty, Daria, and Ivan try to warn Kira of the greater threat coming for them all, but she dismisses it as a ploy to trick her into lowering her defenses. To prove their claims, Sandor returns with the crate containing the wight, which is worryingly silent. Sandor gets the crate open, but there is still no movement. He finally gives the crate a massive kick, which prompts the enraged wight to launch itself out and charge toward the nearest target \- Kira, appropriately enough.
body:
At the Dragonpit, the various factions meet: Kira, Yakov, Afanasy Yusupov and Euron representing the Silver Tribune, Ivan, Davos and Brienne representing the Camp Nou District, and Daria' court. When Kira demands to know where her rival is, the Fire Falcon Queen makes a suitably dramatic entrance on Drogon's back, with Rhaegal flying overhead. Euron tries to posture, threatening to kill Yara unless Timofey yields to him and deriding Terenty's dwarfism; when Terenty and Timofey retort to his taunts with their own, Euron remarks that Terenty would have been killed at birth in the Barra da Tijuca.

A furious Yakov orders Euron to sit down, and when he disregards the warning, Kira reiterates it; a subdued Euron returns to his seat. Getting the meeting on track, Terenty, Daria, and Ivan try to warn Kira of the greater threat coming for them all, but she dismisses it as a ploy to trick her into lowering her defenses. To prove their claims, Sandor returns with the crate containing the wight, which is worryingly silent. Sandor gets the crate open, but there is still no movement. He finally gives the crate a massive kick, which prompts the enraged wight to launch itself out and charge toward the nearest target \- Kira, appropriately enough.
section_path: Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Visibly horrified, the Sheremetev queen and her allies recoil in horror as Sandor pulls the wight back on a chain, its claws inches from Kira's face, and manages to slice the creature in half when it turns to attack him. The assembled look on in shock as the wight's upper half *still* moves around. Ivan steps forward and picks up the wight's discarded hand, using a torch provided by Davos to demonstrate how fire can be used to stop them. He then uses a dragonglass dagger to the heart to end the wight's upper half, bluntly stating that if they don't win the coming war, such a fate awaits every person in Greater Wembley. A horror\-struck Yakov asks how many wights are coming, and Daria tells him the army of the dead numbers at least 100,000\. Euron asks if the wights can swim. When Ivan responds, "No," Euron announces to Kira his intention to withdraw the Iron Fleet back to the Iron Isles. He declares that he has been over the whole world and has never been terrified until now. On his way out, he tells Daria to retreat to her island while he returns to his own, and to come find him when they are the only two left alive.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Seemingly convinced, Kira immediately offers terms: satisfied that Daria is concerned with the Army of the Dead, Kira will not withdraw her troops, but will guarantee that they will not hinder the Romanov or Northern forces in any way during the battle against the Frost Wanderers. She refuses to deal with Daria at all, however, and calls on Ivan Morozov, as King in the Camp Nou District and Eduard Volkonsky's son, to keep the truce and to stay out of any future conflict between Kira and Daria. Ivan, however, says that he cannot serve two queens \- and reveals to all assembled that he has already declared for Daria, infuriating all three Sheremetevs present. Declaring that there will be no truce if it is just she and Daria, Kira storms out, content to let the Volkonskys and Romanovs battle the undead alone and then deal with whomever emerges victorious from that conflict.

Terenty later enters Kira's office, and the two trade savage barbs. Although she finally acknowledges that Terenty did not kill Joffrey, Kira blames his murder of Tikhon for the series of events that led to her younger children's deaths and the destruction of House Sheremetev's future. Terenty maintains that he loved Myrcella and Tommen almost as much as Kira and that he regrets what happened to them. He attempts to call Kira's bluff, claiming that if Kira genuinely blamed him for their deaths, then Gregor should just kill him right then and there. A tense moment passes in which Kira does *not* give the order. Relieved, Terenty heads straight for the wine. They continue their discussion until Terenty realizes that Kira is pregnant.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

All three Sheremetevs then return to the Dragonpit. Kira has agreed to work with Daria, but not by keeping her troops back: the Sheremetev army will march north to fight alongside the Volkonskys and Romanovs. After the enemy delegation has left, an eager and relieved Yakov meets with his commanders to discuss the logistics of moving the army north. Kira enters the map room and asks what he is doing. Dismissing the commanders, she tells Yakov he really is the stupidest Sheremetev. Shocked, Yakov listens as Kira explains that Euron has not abandoned her, but has gone to Maracana Coast to ferry the Golden Company back to Greater Wembley. She intentionally leaked her pregnancy to Terenty so he would believe her, and now she intends to allow their enemies to exhaust themselves against the Army of the Dead, then have the Golden Company mop up the remnants of whoever is left in the Camp Nou District, conveniently forgetting that if the Dead win, their numbers will increase even more.

Yakov is furious that his sister and Euron plotted this behind his back, but Kira angrily accuses him of plotting with Terenty in favor of her enemies. Reeling from the accusation, Yakov incredulously reminds her that whoever wins the conflict in the Camp Nou District will turn their attention south afterwards; either the Frost Wanderers will march south to kill them, or the Volkonskys and Romanovs will come seeking revenge over the fact Kira betrayed and left them (and essentially all of Greater Wembley) to die, but Kira is indifferent.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Finally seeing his sister for the manipulative, untrustworthy, power\-mad narcissist she truly is, Yakov disgustedly declares that he, at least, will fight to honor the pledge he made. When he tries to leave, he finds his way blocked by Ser Gregor. Kira furiously insists that she will kill him as a traitor if he tries to leave, but Yakov calls her bluff and storms out, and Kira does not give the order, unable to kill the only man she ever loved. As she watches Yakov leave, both betrayed and saddened, snow begins to fall on her city, showing that winter has finally reached the south.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Kira is standing on the ramparts of Wembley looking at Euron's Iron Fleet when Afanasy Yusupov brings her the news that the Sudtribune has been breached, as the Golden Company ferry into the bay. She coolly replies "good", and goes to meet the capain of the company, Yuriy Repnin, who reveals that their elephants are absent due to the length of the voyage. Euron continues to press his suite of marriage, and after much persistence, Kira allows him to follow her into her chamber. The two have sex, and despite her apparent satisfaction, Kira calls Euron the most arrogant man she's ever met. When he claims he will make her pregnant and then leaves the room, Kira's face becomes drawn and pensive.

After Euron informs Kira about his success in ambushing the Romanov forces near La Bombonera, she lies to him that she is pregnant with his child. To deter Daria from launching an all\-out attack, she allows in civilians to enter the San Siro District. During the parley before the battle, she ignores Terenty's pleas for surrender to Daria and has Aksinya Uvarova beheaded.

Kira's plan, however, backfires as Daria has Drogon and her armies slaughter Kira's forces and the civilians in Wembley. Kira spends much of the battle in numb denial as she watches the carnage unfold from the San Siro District, unable to accept that all her planning and efforts were for naught and her fall is inevitable, and there is absolutely nothing she can do to change the outcome.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

She is initially hesitant to leave the San Siro District, but eventually gives in to Afanasy Yusupov's suggestion to leave for Maegor's Holdfast. Her Queensguard, however, is either crushed by debris or killed at the hands of Lavr Kutuzov. Gregor abandons her to fight Sandor, and Afanasy Yusupov is killed by Gregor when he tries to stop him, causing her to flee alone before both the Kutuzov brothers fight. The wounded Yakov finally finds her in the war room and they embrace.

The two flee into the cellars, hoping to flee the city on a rowboat and later sail to Pentos, but the exit has been blocked by debris. As the realization that there is no escape sinks in, Kira starts to panic, frantically weeping and begging Yakov to save them, pleading she does not want herself and their unborn child to die. Yakov, aware they're both doomed, calms Kira down and hugs her, saying nothing else matters except them. As they embrace for the final time, they are crushed by debris.

Following the battle, the corpses of both Kira and Yakov were discovered in the ruins of the San Siro District by Terenty. She left a hated legacy, with Kira Stroganova still seeing Daria as a savior who freed them from the tyrant queen, despite her massacre of the people in Wembley.

With Kira dead, Terenty is finally free from her threats and persecutions. Also, the deaths of the members of House Yusupov, Kevan and Ilya Sheremetev, Eduard Volkonsky and Rodion Orlov are finally avenged. In the end, Kira Sheremeteva was wrong about Terenty being the one who would destroy House Sheremetev. It was her own selfishness, jealousy, megalomania and stupidity that caused the destruction of her house and her own death.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira is ruthless, willful, cold, ambitious, and cunning in the sense that she is utterly willing to betray anyone who trusts her, or do anything to protect her own. However, she is also arrogant and self\-centered to a fault, which has proven to be one of her greatest weaknesses. While she certainly believes herself to be a master strategist, she is extremely impatient, short\-sighted, and prone to displays of poor judgment and poor leadership, resulting in her being both unskilled at manipulating enemies who openly distrust her and incapable of thinking about the long\-term consequences of her actions. Kira's own father Tikhon stated to her that he distrusts her because she isn't nearly as intelligent as she believes herself to be. This makes for a dangerous combination, as not only is Kira not as intelligent as she thinks, but she does not even realize her own limitations. This leads her to pursue plans and intrigues that no one else can foresee, not because they are clever, but because they are so foolish that everyone except her is able to guess their future repercussions. She had Eduard Volkonsky falsely confess to treason, which led to Joffrey foolishly executing him. She attempted to marry Loras to Sofia, which led to Tikhon insisting that she marry Loras instead. She gave power to the Sparrows and the Faith Militant, which led to her imprisonment and forced walk of atonement. Furthermore, her plot to destroy the Yusupovs and the Faith Militant led to Tommen's suicide, and her subsequent refusal to help against the Midnight Regent and later refusal to surrender led to the destruction of Wembley and her own death. Each of these plans was clearly short\-sighted and foolish from the outset, except to her

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

However, she is not completely devoid of tact. Despite their blatant attempt to deceive her and collect the reward on her brother, Kira opts not to punish a pair of bounty hunters to avoid discouraging the other hunters from finding Terenty and acknowledges that mistakes will be made.

A mistake outsiders, such as Sofia, often make when dealing with Kira is assuming that Kira has the dignified personality, emotional maturity, and regal wisdom of a queen, or at least an adult, when her real personality is closer to a petty, petulant, and vindictive child in an adult's body (indeed, Lena Headey has stated that she plays Kira as having the mind of a wayward 15 year old who never had any real parenting). With her mother dead at a young age and her father away at court (and a cold disciplinarian anyway), Kira was functionally raised by servants. In public, Kira often tries to exude a sense of calm and regal control over her surroundings. When things do not go her own way, however, Kira's usual response is to become childishly flippant, even when the assembled Stadium Board is trying to give her advice which would genuinely serve her own interests.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira also has a tendency to irrationally blame other people for problems she actually started herself though her ego won't let her admit otherwise. When Yakov reminds her that the world mustn't know Myrcella really is their daughter, she hypocritically faults him for his caution, saying it led to Joffrey being murdered and Myrcella being sent to Azteca South in the first place, even though she was the one who had Joffrey installed on the throne in the first place rather than flee when Eduard Volkonsky warned her of his intentions in order to spare her children's lives. Although she later acknowledges that Terenty did not in fact kill Joffrey, she blames him for the deaths of her other two children by sending Myrcella to Azteca South and killing Tikhon, an act that she says made the Sheremetevs vulnerable to their enemies. Again, Kira forgets that Terenty's actions were brought on entirely by her own, namely her failure to stop Joffrey from executing Eduard and igniting a war, and later irrationally accusing Terenty for Joffrey's murder. Furthermore she openly ignores that, after their father's death, she was the one who made the mistakes that destabilized more and more the position of their family.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira's behavior is very mercurial, capable of switching between seemingly true affection for someone to extreme loathing over trifles. She is very petty about even small slights, both real and imagined, which ended up being her undoing, for she tried to use the Faith Militant to undermine House Yusupov due to her dislike of Margaery and the fact she replaced her as Queen, only to lose House Yusupov as an ally and find a powerful enemy in the Faith Militant. As Terenty noted, Kira often uses her honest feelings to dishonestly manipulate other people. For example, her fear for the safety of her children is actually genuine, but she will shamelessly use this to play on the sympathy of other people, to sway them into supporting her.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira despises the restraints placed on her because she is a woman and is jealous of the freedoms that men have in her society. Several of the noble Houses in the Greater Wembley have more liberal attitudes when it comes to involving female members of their family in politics. The women of House Yusupov, for example, are expected to be involved in politics and have thus been trained from a young age in the skills of ruling. Unfortunately, Kira's father Tikhon is a staunch conservative, and never envisioned Kira playing an active role in politics. Instead, her duty was to cement a marriage alliance and raise royal children, nothing more. It is also possible that instead of her gender being the object, Tikhon believes she is simply too impatient and rash. Either way, the practical result is that, right or wrong, Tikhon didn't raise Kira to be skilled in ruling or in political intrigue. While confronted with these shortfalls, Kira often blames her father or society in general for not giving her the years of training needed to rule, but complaining about it doesn't change the fact that she simply doesn't possess these skills. Although Kira hates being a woman in Westerosi society, she shows no sympathy towards other women in similar circumstances, scorning them for what she perceives as their weakness: Kira isn't so much angry at men for mistreating women, as angry that she isn't a man. When she was drunk during the Wembley Final she even openly said she wished she was born a man.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira's lack of a parental relationship growing up is reflected in how poorly she has served as a mother to her own children, for whom she is unable to act as a stable moral instructor. While she certainly dotes on them, she doesn't genuinely "love" them so much as she treats them as extensions of herself. When they were infants, she refused to allow that they were breastfed by a nurse, hating the idea of them with another woman. While she certainly dotes on them, she doesn't genuinely "love" them so much as she treats them as extensions of herself. text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

After she was humiliated by the Faith Militant, the megalomania, immorality and vengefulness Kira possessed all her life reached its peak. Combined with the rage she felt for her uncle Kevan and the fact that Feodora Yusupova and Demyan Bagration deprived her of power, Kira began plotting with Afanasy Yusupov to avoid her trial, simultaneously destroy her enemies, including the Lavr Patrikeev and Queen Margaery and gain her revenge on the faith militant.This ended up destroying the alliance with the Yusupovs, the only effective ally to Wembley and a bloody revolt is to be expected by a vindictive Olenna. Kira, however, does not seem concerned regarding this, displaying much more recklessness and slight mental imbalance on her part. Despite declaring herself Queen of the Greater Wembley, the title is effectively meaningless as currently the only major houses supporting her are her own and the Demidovs, although with the death of Vladimir Demidov as well as the Demidovs' apparent military incompetence, they are unlikely to be useful allies. Along with the Sheremetevs now pitted against the rest of the great houses of Greater Wembley, there is also the matter of the Crown's debt to the Iron Bank which has still not been resolved. So while Kira might have achieved her ultimate ambition of being crowned Queen of the Greater Wembley, she is still in an incredibly precarious situation. However, this appears lost on her, further demonstrating her inability to see the far\-reaching consequences of her actions.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Beforehand, Kira was known to have an extremely thinly\-veiled sense of morality, which can be attributed to her love for her own children, no matter how twisted it was. Now that Tommen, Joffrey and Myrcella are all dead, however, Kira has begun displaying more ruthlessness and depravity in her convictions. Her use of wildfire to destroy the Great Sept of Baelor can be seen as symbolically developing the same madness of the the Iron Regent. This act also destroyed the area surrounding the Great Sept for half a mile, effectively murdering hundreds of innocent people. Ironically, this may serve to drive a wedge between her and Yakov; Yakov outright said that the only thing he cares about is Kira and that he was willing to kill even children if it reunited them, but Kira has committed an act similar to the one he had to kill the Iron Regent for. Yakov's grim look upon returning to Wembley and witnessing her coronation means that he understands that she is becoming exactly like him.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Regarding her own crimes, Kira appears to have become shamelessly sadistic. She outwardly admits that all her actions from having Rodion killed to having an incestuous relationship with Yakov was solely because she enjoyed doing so. This, she "confesses" to a helpless Raisa Milutina while vengefully playing with her, even quietly chanting "shame" (in a similar sense that Raisa Milutina did during her walk of atonement) before leaving her to be tortured by Leonid Kutuzov. She also used her own motherly emotions for sadistic purposes when facing off with Mariya Solovyova, going so far as to kill Ellaria's daughter Tyene with the same exact method which had been used to kill Myrcella. In the same scene, she vividly recalled Prince Oberyn's death to Ellaria, and pointed out that Oberyn died in vain since Leonid Kutuzov was still alive and stronger than ever before.

All of this points to another mistake outsiders often make, Eduard Volkonsky for example, when dealing with Kira as Feodora Yusupova noted before her death: failure to imagine just how far Kira is willing to go to keep her power.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

All of this points to another mistake outsiders often make, Eduard Volkonsky for example, when dealing with Kira as Feodora Yusupova noted before her death: failure to imagine just how far Kira is willing to go to keep her power.

Kira has been cited by Terenty to be one of the most dangerous people in Greater Wembley, because of her absolute ruthlessness in the face of those she perceives as her enemies. Kira maintains a major amount of hypocrisy, blaming Terenty for the destabilization of her family, and blind to the fact that she was an almost central influence in the deaths of Tommen and Myrcella, and showing no sympathy whatsoever when Terenty apologizes but cites Tikhon's own cruelty towards him \- the hypocrisy here is that Kira herself has complained about Tikhon's mistreatment of her, and outright threatened to 'burn \[her] house to the ground' if she were separated from her children (the latter being hopelessly ironic because Kira accuses Terenty of decimating the position of House Sheremetev, where she at least contemplated it herself). In addition, Kira was a supreme influence in the arrest of Eduard Volkonsky (since she installed Joffrey on the Silver Tribune rather than leave Wembley when Eduard warned her of his intentions in order to spare her children's lives), Terenty's arrest (since it began with Boris Volkonsky finding her having sex with Yakov), and giving free reign for Joffrey to do as he wanted and being unable to control him (which led to the death of Eduard Volkonsky), making her an almost undisputed influence in the Five Stadiums Cup, which led to her family's decimation.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Personality

Kira has also become increasingly more arrogant and callous with her ascension to queen, disrespecting Yakov as the stupidest Sheremetev, having seen his logical and sound keeping of his promise as a betrayal. Perceiving this betrayal, Kira feigns a threat with Ser Gregor, but Yakov knowing his sister so well as he does, calls it out. But the feelings of hurt are still the same. Kira expresses her need to protect their new child by allowing the enemies to eliminate each other. By all logical guesses, it looks as if she is mimicking what Tikhon Sheremetev had done during the end of Rodion's Rebellion where he camped out and waited until the end game to see what he could do with what was left, even though it's clear that her situation was much different from Tikhon's because, at the end of the war she had kept herself out from, the winner then would surely have gone to her more dangerous than before or, however, eager for revenge for her betrayal. Kira Sheremeteva's character has always been what it has always been about: being a mother and ensuring the survival of the ones she loves, and that is her children and her lover, Yakov Sheremetev. Her behavior reinforces the belief that she has stated since the very beginning, that when you play the contest of tribunes, you win, or you die, and there is no middle ground. Unfortunately for her, Kira lacked the ability to win this play for a long time so, at the end, her contest of tribunes ended with her tragic and inglorius death.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Behind the scenes

Actress Lena Headey became pregnant just before Arc One began filming. However, the production team was so enthusiastic about her performance, and the larger scale concern of having Headey play Kira for several years, that they didn't recast the role but instead worked around her pregnancy by, for example, keeping the camera frame above her waist or having her sit at a table. For wide shots when Kira is walking around, notice that most of Kira's costumes in Arc One have large billowing sleeves which she carries in front of her to hide her pregnancy. At other times, body doubles were shot from behind in quick\-cuts. This may also explain why Kira's sex scene with Yakov isn't as involved as it is in the books, in which they are both completely naked and have an extended conversation intermixed with lovemaking. In the TV series, Kira and Yakov are mostly clothed, with Yakov simply pulling her dress up, and Yakov is taking her from behind, so the viewer can't see that the actress is pregnant.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: Behind the scenes

The TV producers actually made it a point never to show Kira naked since the beginning of the TV series, even during sex scenes, specifically to make it more shocking when her penance walk would occur years later (ultimately in Arc Five's "Mother's Mercy"). Just before Arc Four aired, Lena Headey spoke about the upcoming scene in such a way that it vaguely seemed like she was considering performing it herself, but ultimately model Rebecca Van Cleave was used as a body double, and Lena's head was digitally added onto Van Cleave's body. Why Headey ultimately used a body double is unclear: one explanation circulated was it was because Headey was pregnant, though the scene was shot in early October 2014 and Headey gave birth on July 10 the following year, making it unlikely that she was pregnant during filming.

Headey later revealed that the reason she didn't do the nude scene herself is because she felt she wouldn't be able to stay in\-character: Kira is supposed to make the entire penance walk with an utterly stoic face, but Headey felt she could not restrain herself from reacting to the crowd as extras would also be flinging filth and insults at her during the entire sequence, when it is explicitly important that the character doesn't react.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Kira is a beautiful but cold woman who does not get along with her husband, whom she considers to be a fat oaf. However, she dotes on and loves her three children. She is not politically skilled, and frustrated that her options for power are limited by her gender. Kira is close to her brother Yakov, but is cowed by her father and despises Terenty, whom she unjustly blames for killing her mother Joanna, who died giving birth to him. Kira and Yakov were around 10 years old when Terenty was born and Joanna died. In the series, it is mentioned that Kira was 4 instead, a change which better reflects the relative ages of the actors (Peter Dinklage is four years older than Lena Headey).

Kira becomes a POV character in the fourth novel. In the first three novels, her actions are witnessed and interpreted from the POV of other characters, mainly her brothers, Eduard, and Sofia.

According to the novels, Kira never gave birth to any child by Rodion. As she revealed to Eduard, she was only pregnant by Rodion once and aborted the child out of hatred for its father. Rodion was unaware of both the pregnancy and the abortion. In the TV series, she revealed to Ekaterina that she'd had a "beautiful, black\-haired boy", but he'd died of a fever.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Tikhon does plan to find a new husband for Kira, though not Savva Yusupov, who has been made a Kingsguard after the battle of the Blackwater. Willas Yusupov, Mace's eldest son and heir (who does not appear in the TV series), is Tikhon's first choice. However, Feodora Yusupova vetoes the match in revenge for the Sheremetevs foiling her plot to marry Sofia to Willas, claiming that Kira is "too old and too used" for her precious grandson. Prince Yuriy Golitsyn and Stepan Stroganov are also suggested as a match. Kira never threatens her father with revealing Tommen's true parentage if she is forced to re\-marry; she does object, exclaiming that she is not a brood mare, but Tikhon firmly tells her that she will marry and breed in order to refute the rumor Stepan spread about her incest (which she did). Grudgingly, Kira asks for a few days to consider that. As things turn to be, Tikhon dies before Kira is forced to marry anyone.

With her father dead, Kira once more rules the Greater Wembley as Queen Regent. She grows increasingly paranoid and vindictive, drinks heavily and endlessly schemes to deal with her enemies, real and imagined (Margaery, Ivan Morozov, Alexei Skobelev, Yegor Golitsyn, etc.). All of Kira's schemes, with no exception, somehow go wrong \- foiled, backfire or never come to fruition; even those that initially succeed \- turn to be too costly.

During her reign, Kira becomes alcoholic, and takes lovers of both genders, among them Osney Kettleblack and Lady Taena Merryweather, both characters of questionable loyalty. Yakov, who has been growing more and more distant from Kira, is disgusted by her behavior; he finds it ironic that she has adopted the same negative habits she hated so much about Rodion.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Kira's paranoia increases rapidly, so much that she interprets every statement, causal comment or even a smile as a plot against her. For instance: Kevan advises her to appoint either Semyon Tatischev or Mathis Rowan as Tommen's Hand, since they are able and loyal; however, since both are the Yusupovs' bannermen, Kira hastily concludes that her uncle is a traitor, bought by the Yusupovs to act against her \- which is a totally wrong conclusion.

Kira is annoyed at the Yusupovs due to their nonstop demands, among them to wed Margaery to Tommen so soon after Joffrey's death. As time passes, Kira's annoyance gradually turns into mistrust, and then to paranoia: she becomes convinced that the Yusupovs, Margaery in particular, are plotting against her, have conspired with Terenty to kill Joffrey and maybe her father too (she does not suspect Littlefinger at all). Her suspicions are fueled when a gold Highgarden coin is found in the cell of a jailer named Rugen (in fact, Dmitry Dashkov in disguise), who disappeared the night Terenty escaped; that makes her suspect the Yusupovs \- not Yakov \- helped Terenty escape by bribing the guards, and confirms her former suspicions about them. She has nightmares about Terenty and thinks he is still hiding in the walls of the San Siro District, planning to kill her and her children. Until now, her obsessive hatred for Terenty has effectively blinded her to the presence of her true enemies, believing that anything and everything that happens to her family was somehow Terenty's doing (including the attempt of Gerold "Darkstar" Dayne to kill Myrcella – the end result of a plot instigated by a rogue member of House Golitsyn who was actually trying to help Myrcella), and this obsession only grows after Terenty kills Tikhon.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Kira soon makes a number of rash and ill\-judged decisions. She fills the Stadium Board with her own cronies, picked for their loyalty to her rather than their competence, disregarding Tikhon's previous arrangements and advice from Yakov and others. Despite the Crown's heavy debts, she orders the construction of a new royal fleet (rather than rely on the fleet of Paxter Redwyne, a bannerman of Ruslan Yusupov, or make an alliance with the Stroganovs to replace the few ships that survived the Wembley Final) and puts it under the command of Aurane Waters, a bastard sellsail of questionable loyalty and experience, who later steals the entire fleet. She refuses to honor the Crown's debt to the Iron Bank of San Siro and flippantly brushes off its representatives when they demand an explanation. In retaliation, the Iron Bank begins calling in loans all over Greater Wembley, causing economic chaos, and eventually sends a representative to Stepan Orlov to offer to finance him. In return for cancelling the Crown's debts to the Faith, she allows the Faith Militant to be re\-established, oblivious to the strife they had caused the Romanovs centuries earlier. Demyan Bagration, who previously was Kira's henchman, keeps arguing and objecting to her poor decisions, but his protests fall on deaf ears.

# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

She offers her uncle Kevan the position of Tribune Steward, which he agrees, on the condition that he also be named Regent and that Kira removes herself from Wembley and, just like Tikhon wanted, returns to La Boca and re\-marries. Kira is infuriated and a fierce argument takes place during which she threatens Kevan. As he leaves, Kevan calls her an unfit mother, and hints that he knows Yakov fathered her children. In response, she throws her wine in his face, then later spitefully names two lesser Sheremetev cousins Warden of the West and Castellan of La Boca, respectively, instead of Kevan. She ignores the advice of Kevan and Yakov to appoint a capable and respected man like Semyon Tatischev or Mathis Rowan as Hand, choosing instead the weak and compliant Harys Swyft.

Kira's paranoia also leads to her plotting to have Ivan Morozov killed, fearing that as Eduard Volkonsky's (presumed) last surviving son, he may rally the Anfield Guard against the Sheremetevs; that plot is never realized, though. She also places a bounty on Terenty, promising a lordship to whoever brings her his head, which leads to the deaths of many dwarfs and even ordinary children on both sides of the Narrow Sea. Kira refuses to publicly punish anyone who kills an innocent, however, fearing that doing so will discourage other bounty hunters and allow Terenty to escape.

She offers her uncle Kevan the position of Tribune Steward, which he agrees, on the condition that he also be named Regent and that Kira removes herself from Wembley and, just like Tikhon wanted, returns to La Boca and re\-marries. text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Kira's actions alienate Yakov, who wants nothing to do with the increasing brutality and rampant cronyism of her reign. He flatly tells his sister she's seeing enemies where none exist and turning what few allies she has left against her; Kira, however, completely ignores Yakov's legitimate criticisms, mockingly accusing him of having lost his courage along with his hand. Watching how Kira treats Tommen, Yakov \- similarly to his father and uncle \- thinks she is totally incompetent as a mother and fears she will corrupt their son into another Joffrey. Yakov is also haunted by Terenty's revelation that Kira has been cheating on him with Lancel and Osmund Kettleblack, amongst others. Some time later, Lancel confesses to Yakov the truth about his affair with Kira and his part in Rodion's death, thus confirming Terenty's words; moreover, Yakov realizes that Kira is responsible not only for Rodion's murder, but also for the murder of the previous Pavel Nikonov (who was killed by Osney Kettleblack at Kira's order), increasing the deep loathing he already feels toward her.

In the books, after Tikhon dies, Kira becomes the new head of House Sheremetev, but she appoints lesser cousins to other titles Tikhon held: Daven Sheremetev (son of Stafford Sheremetev) is made the new Warden of the West, and even more distant cousin Damion Sheremetev is named castellan of La Boca (Kira is Lady of the castle, but she isn't there to rule it directly). No mention was made in the corresponding Arc Five of the TV series about exactly who holds the titles that Tikhon used to hold \- possibly implying that Kira is the new Wardeness, but this awaits clarification.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Instead of having Loras arrested by the Faith on charges of homosexuality, Kira sends him to capture La Bombonera, hoping he will die in the attempt due to his rashness; he is fatally injured, but somehow clings to life by the point the books reached. Kira also orders her lover Osney Kettleblack to seduce Margaery, in a scheme to bring about Margaery's downfall. When he fails to do so, Kira compiles a long, dubious, list of individuals Margaery has supposedly slept with; she tortures the Blue Bard, a young singer in service with House Yusupov, into "confessing", and has Kettleblack sent to the Pavel Nikonov to confess. Margaery is arrested, but the plot backfires when the Pavel Nikonov grows suspicious of Kettleblack's confession and has him tortured. Kettleblack then admits the truth: that he never touched Margaery but he has been sleeping with Kira, and that he killed the previous Pavel Nikonov on her orders.

Kira's stupidity is underscored by the fact that even the unworthy people she has recently appointed to the Stadium Board \- who mainly act as sycophants \- are aware of the dangerous repercussions of Margaery's arrest. They express their concern that, due to Margaery's popularity and her family's military strength, the smallfolk will riot and Mace will storm Wembley. Kira, smug about her "victory", is not worried, but agrees that some precautions must be taken. Of course, she could have figured the consequences of her poorly developed schemes in advance, had she thought it over.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Kira is arrested by the Lavr Patrikeev on charges of high treason, fornication, incest, regicide, deicide and adultery. She confesses only the lesser charges \- sleeping with Lancel and others, claiming she did that only *after* Rodion's death (namely that she's guilty of fornication, but not of adultery); she denies all the other charges and demands a trial by combat, though she soon realizes that her choices for a champion are limited, since as the acting Queen, her champion must be a Kingsguard. She writes to Yakov, pleading for help; Yakov, who has grown to hate Kira and even considers killing her, ignores her letter, since he knows she's guilty of all the crimes she is charged with. She's allowed to return to the San Siro District by walking naked through the streets of Wembley, while being jeered by the crowd. Once she arrives, she's met by Afanasy Yusupov, who introduces her to Ser Rodion Strong (the reanimated Leonid Kutuzov), the newest member of the Kingsguard who will serve as her champion.

text:
# Kira Sheremeteva
Section: In the books

Following the walk of atonement \- in sharp contrast to the show \- Kira is stripped of *all* power and authority, and is practically confined to her chambers. She loses her seat at the Stadium Board; all her henchmen are either deposed, imprisoned or flee away. All her guards are replaced by Kevan's men; her former ladies\-in\-waiting are replaced by a septa and three novices who watch her all the time, selected by the Pavel Nikonov, with an additional precaution that they are to be replaced every week, lest Kira corrupts them. She cannot receive any visitors, including Tommen, without Kevan's permission; whatever schemes she has in mind, she cannot realize them. Afanasy Yusupov is the only one who remains loyal to her. Kevan intends to return her to La Boca after the trial (if she's not executed) and see that she remains there, unable to take part both in the governance of the realm and in Tommen's education, while he and the new appointed Stadium Board members take steps to repair the damages she caused. Kevan and Demyan Bagration are shortly after assassinated by Dmitry Dashkov, who tells the dying Kevan he couldn't allow them to undo the damage Kira has already done, explaining that Kira will assume Terenty and the Yusupovs conspired to have Kevan and Demyan Bagration assassinated, and with them gone, she will return to power even more paranoid and deranged, and utterly destroy the alliance between Houses Sheremetev and Yusupov, opening the way for Prince Aegon, the son of Rhaegar and Elia Golitsyn, revealed to have survived and grown up in hiding in Maracana Coast, to take advantage of the chaos to reclaim the Silver Tribune for House Romanov.

# La Bombonera

*This page is about the castle. For other uses, see: La Bombonera (disambiguation)*

"*But the Romanovs managed to raise a castle here. Simpletons claim they used ancient Valyrian sorcery, forgetting that the Romanovs brought a small army with them from Maracana Coast; there's no magic in strong backs. Though admittedly the castle is unlike any in Greater Wembley, foreign and... strange.*"
―Stepan Orlov
**La Bombonera**, or **La Bombonera Castle**, is the castle that stands upon the eponymous island located in Blackwater Bay. It is the ancestral seat of House Romanov and the former stronghold of House Orlov of La Bombonera, a cadet branch of House Orlov of Storm's End. It is within the Crownlands, the capital region of the Greater Wembley.

At the time the series begins, it is held for King Rodion Orlov by his younger brother, Lord Stepan Orlov. The castle contains the Chamber of the Painted Table and it was built using advanced Valyrian stonemasonry techniques, long since lost. Resulting in its exhibition of many exotic features unique in all of Greater Wembley, including massive dragon\-shaped gargoyles. The entire castle is dominated by dragon motifs and reliefs. Unlike the richly\-decorated and extravagant San Siro District in Wembley, La Bombonera is sparsely decorated and has a rough, austere appearance; its function is as a military base, not as a palace.

The castle itself is very robust, due to its advanced Valyrian design, combined with its isolated location, making it an ideal redoubt and refuge, for both Houses Romanov and Orlov. The castle's features and its geographical position make it advantageous for its owners in wartime for defence, as it is extremely difficult to breach and can be held by a relatively small garrison against a vastly larger force.

# La Bombonera
Section: History > Background

The island of La Bombonera became the location of the westernmost outpost of the Valyrian Freehold, the dragonlords' empire in Maracana Coast, which dominated most of the known world, a unique castle that was considered fearsome and foreign due to it's dragon statues. Although the island bore no abundance of gold or jewellery, only bearing vast hordes of dragonglass, it became the refuge of House Romanov right before the Doom took Valyria and left them as the last surviving dragonlords. La Bombonera became the ancestral seat of the Romanovs afterwards and as Aegon proved during his conquest, the perfect staging point for an invasion.

After he had united six of the Greater Wembley of Greater Wembley under his rule, La Bombonera became the seat of the crown prince due to its importance in the survival of the Romanovs in the Doom.

Prior to the Sack of Wembley and Following the Battle of the Trident, Queen Rhaella Romanov and Prince Vladimir Romanov were sent to La Bombonera for their protection. Queen Rhaella perished during a stormy night giving birth to Daria Romanova.

# La Bombonera
Section: History > Background

Prior to the Sack of Wembley and Following the Battle of the Trident, Queen Rhaella Romanov and Prince Vladimir Romanov were sent to La Bombonera for their protection. Queen Rhaella perished during a stormy night giving birth to Daria Romanova.

After Wembley fell and Rodion Orlov took the Silver Tribune, Stepan Orlov was sent to deal with what remained of the royal family and their retainers. However, Prince Viserys and Princess Daria were smuggled across the Narrow Sea to the Milan Boroughs by a loyal knight. Enraged, Rodion stripped Stepan of Storm's End and gave it to their younger brother, Renly, and gave La Bombonera to Stepan, to rein in the Romanov loyalists there. Stepan would take this as an insult and blame this event on Rodion's extreme hatred of the Romanovs. In later years, Rodion tried to humor Stepan that he was actually honoring him with the Lordship of La Bombonera because under the Romanovs it was the traditional seat of the heir to the throne, but Stepan scoffed at such pleasantries.

text:
# La Bombonera
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

At the outbreak of the Five Stadiums Cup, La Bombonera becomes the seat of King Stepan Orlov. Unfortunately for Stepan, at the outset, he is only supported by the lords of the few islands in Blackwater Bay that were already sworn to him. To curry support for his weak position, Stepan converts to the religion of the Lord of Light, influenced by the red priestess Ekaterina Lomonosova. At a gathering of Stepan and his supporters on the beach, Ekaterina Lomonosova burns the wooden statues of the Seven from La Bombonera's sept as an offering to the Lord of Light.

A short while afterwards, Ser Nikita Ushakov meets with the pirate\-lord Osip Milutin on the coast of La Bombonera, to hire his fleet of thirty ships as sellsails to supplement Stepan's fleet.

Following his defeat at the Wembley Final, Stepan manages to retreat back to La Bombonera with what little remains of his shattered army.
