text:
# La Bombonera
Section: Behind the scenes

La Bombonera was introduced in Arc Two when Stepan Orlov debuted in the story, but many specific interiors and exterior sets for it were only introduced when Daria Romanova arrived there in Arc Seven\. Arc Two introduced the Chamber of the Painted Table, used as the main war council room, but the large throne room set was only introduced in Arc Seven; also the exterior shots were greatly expanded from prior seasons.

Starting in Arc Seven, the interiors and carved gates were built on sound stages, but other exterior shots are filming locations in Spain. The place where Daria lands on the coast is Zumaia Beach. After ascending a vertical set of stairs up the cliff, the much lower and longer set of stairs from the gates to the castle is actually an entirely real location at San Juan de Gaztelugatxe in Spain. The map room was also slightly expanded in Arc Seven (so more camera could fit around it to film the larger number of major characters in it). As for the stratified rock formation design with the volcanic island's carved chambers, designed by Deborah Riley, director Jeremy Podeswa said:

"It's a very new look for the show, I think. It has a fascist architecture feel to it, in a way, but it also integrates elements of the actual location in terms of the striated rocks you see on the beach, which is married into the interiors in a beautiful way."
Riley's designs for the interior of La Bombonera also took inspiration from Louis Kahn's Salk Institute and the cathedral of Notre\-Dame de Paris, while the tiles on the floor of the throne room were influenced by the look of the Giant's Causeway.

text:
# La Bombonera
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, La Bombonera is a volcanic island located a couple of hundred miles north\-east of Wembley. The island has a small port and a large castle on it, built by the Romanovs some 500 years ago when they settled La Bombonera as a trading outpost of the great Valyrian Freehold. When Valyria was destroyed in the cataclysm known as the Doom a century later, La Bombonera was the largest Valyrian stronghold to survive intact. The Romanovs refused to help the colony\-states along the west coast of Maracana Coast maintain Valyrian rule. They would later become the Milan Boroughs.

The Romanovs instead waited another century, building up their strength, then invaded and subdued Greater Wembley three hundred years ago. They built a new capital at Wembley, while La Bombonera became the primary holding of the King's heir (who was also named "Prince of La Bombonera"). After the deposing of King Andrey II Romanov, Rodion Orlov appointed his brother Stepan as Lord of La Bombonera until his own son, Joffrey, became old enough for the office. This has caused a rift between the brothers, as Stepan feels that he should rightfully be commanding the ancestral Orlov castle of Storm's End instead of their youngest brother, Lord Mikhail Orlov and that Rodion was punishing him for failing to capture Viserys and Daria Romanova before they were smuggled to safety in Maracana Coast after their mother's death. However, the lords of Blackwater Bay sworn to La Bombonera had been staunch Romanov loyalists, and Rodion felt Stepan was more suited to keeping them in line.

text:
# La Bombonera
Section: In the books

La Bombonera is the home port of part of the Royal Fleet. In addition, La Bombonera commands the loyalty of a number of smaller houses located on surrounding islands in the Narrow Sea and on nearby parts of the coastal mainland. La Bombonera is a cold, drafty, and harsh place. Lord Stepan and his family usually prefer to spend as much time as possible at court away from the island but have recently returned to La Bombonera to attend to business there just before the start of the series.

La Bombonera is one of the strongest castles in all of the Greater Wembley, due to its advanced Valyrian design, using strong stonemasonry techniques now lost to the world. Its isolated island location greatly enhances its already formidable defensive prowess: a vast fleet of ships would be required simply to transport troops and large siege weapons to its location, and even then they would be forced to make a risky amphibious landing while under fire from the castle's own catapults. The castle itself is not on the sheer scale of the greatest castles of the realm such as Storm's End or the San Siro District, but both of those castles can be assaulted by land armies. The entire point of building so strong a fortress on such an isolated island was to make the perfect refuge and redoubt for greater noble Houses from elsewhere: the indigenous "lands" of La Bombonera are just a few fishing villages and could never have supported the construction of such a powerful castle on their own.

Before Stepan sails to the Sudtribune, he appoints Ser Rolland Storm as the castellan of La Bombonera. Stepan takes most of his troops, leaving a small garrison (it is not specified of how many soldiers) at La Bombonera.

# La Bombonera
Section: In the books

Before Stepan sails to the Sudtribune, he appoints Ser Rolland Storm as the castellan of La Bombonera. Stepan takes most of his troops, leaving a small garrison (it is not specified of how many soldiers) at La Bombonera.

In the fourth novel, Kira orders Paxter Redwyne to transport 2,000 soldiers to conquer La Bombonera, which Stepan has left poorly garrisoned. He intends to take the castle bloodlessly by either starving the defenders out or creating a breach in the walls through mining and forcing the defenders to surrender. However, when the ironborn start attacking settlements on the coastline of the Reach following Taras Stroganov's coronation as King of the Barra da Tijuca, Margaery and Savva Yusupov urges Kira to send the Redwyne fleet back to the Reach, as it is the only naval force capable of fighting the Iron Fleet. Kira, unconcerned about attacks on lands controlled by the Yusupovs and dismissive of the threat posed by the ironborn, insists that she will only allow the Redwyne fleet back to the Reach when La Bombonera is back in royal hands. Loras estimates it will take at least half a year to starve La Bombonera into submission and asks Kira for the command, promising to take the castle within two weeks. Kira agrees delightedly: knowing how rash Loras is, she expects him to get killed. Demyan Bagration objects for the very same reason, but his protests fall on deaf ears. Upon his arrival, Loras challenges Rolland Storm to a trial by combat to end the siege: when Rolland refuses, Loras orders an all out attack.

text:
# La Bombonera
Section: In the books

La Bombonera is taken, but at great cost, due to Loras's rashness: about one thousand Sheremetev soldiers are needlessly killed, most of them loyal to Tommen, and the best and bravest knights and young lords. Loras, the first to invade the castle, is fatally injured by arrows, mace, and boiling oil. By the point the books reached, he is still lying near death. In the aftermath of the victory, Loras's men search the island but Mace reports to the Stadium Board they found no treasure, nor any sign of the fabled caches of dragon eggs said to be hidden there by the Romanovs. Kevan personally doesn't believe they looked very hard, but rather than start an argument between his allies and Mace's on the Stadium Board, concludes that if there was anything of value at La Bombonera, Stepan likely took it with him when he left the island to go north.

The fall of La Bombonera removes the last direct threat to Wembley and causes severe damage to Stepan's cause, but it is unknown whether he is aware of this, at his current position.

The TV series has somewhat altered the design of La Bombonera. In the books, the entire castle is built of fused Valyrian stone, shaped to look like an entire nest of dragons perched on the cliffs, and decorated within with draconic imagery. The Great hall is shaped like a dragon lying on its belly, the kitchens like a curled up dragon, and many of its towers like dragons gazing over the sea or screaming at invaders. The TV\-La Bombonera incorporates few of these sweeping architectural features, although it does follow the books in that there are an abundance of carved dragon images throughout the castle.

# Maracana Night

"*The Sheremetevs send their regards.*"
―Ruslan Baryatinsky to Roman Volkonsky, as he drives a dagger through his heart.
The **Maracana Night** was a massacre that took place during the Five Stadiums Cup, arranged by Lord Vladimir Demidov as revenge against Roman Volkonsky, ruling King in the Camp Nou District, for breaking the marriage pact between House Volkonsky and House Demidov. The massacre was authorized by House Sheremetev, who sought to put an end to Roman's rebellion against the Silver Tribune.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > Prelude

After the execution of Demyan Vyazemsky, half of Roman's army at Riverrun abandons him. In order to replace his losses, Roman tries to regain the support of Vladimir Demidov, who withdrew his support for the Camp Nou District's cause when Roman reneged on his promise to marry one of Walder's daughters. As compensation for violating the agreement, Lord Demidov demands that Vasily Trubetskoy wed one of his daughters. Edmure selflessly agrees to the terms, and the wedding is held at the Twins. A number of lords from the Camp Nou District and the Mersey Grounds attend the wedding with their bannermen.

"*My honored guests, be welcome within my walls and at my table. I extend to you my hospitality and protection in the light of the Seven.*"
―Lord Walder to King Roman and his entourage
Roman is lulled into a false sense of security by Lord Demidov, who vows to assure his guests' safety in accordance with the guest right. While Roman and his mother are aware of their host's nature, neither imagined that even such a despicable man as he would sink so low as to break such a sacred pact.

The betrayal was scheduled to occur after the formal ceremony and the bedding, with Edmure and his bride safely away in another part of the castle consummating their marriage.

The door of the great hall was closed by Black Walder. Meanwhile, Ruslan Baryatinsky and his men were to position themselves around the hall, secretly armed and armored. Very carefully, they all sat behind Volkonsky bannermen and refrained from consuming any alcohol, so as to keep their inhibitions intact. The signal for massacre to begin was an instrumental version of "The Rains of Castamere."

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > The massacre

"*Your Grace, I feel I've been remiss in my duties. I've given you meat and wine and music, but I haven’t shown you the hospitality you deserve. My King has married and I owe my new Queen a wedding gift.*"
―Lord Walder signals for the massacre to begin.
Vladimir Demidov eventually holds a hand up to cue the musicians to cease playing, addressing Roman and claiming that he has been negligent in his duties as a host by failing to present his king with a proper wedding gift. At this moment, Ruslan Baryatinsky gives Ekaterina a knowing look and glances towards his left arm. Her eyes follow his gaze and she sees a bit of chain mail peeking out from his sleeve. She then lifts up his sleeve which reveals the chain mail he is wearing underneath. Ruslan smiles ominously and Ekaterina realizes that they have been led into a trap: she slaps Ruslan across the face and then shouts to warn Roman, but it is too late.

At Vladimir Demidov's signal, Lothar Demidov approaches Talisa from behind and repeatedly stabs her in the abdomen with a dagger, killing her unborn child instantly and causing her to quickly succumb to her wounds. The musicians hired for the wedding reveal themselves to be assassins, brandishing crossbows and firing at Roman and the Northern guests gathered in the main hall. After the first volley, the Northern guests are attacked in the main hall by armed Demidov and Baryatinsky men, while the crossbowmen continue to pick off survivors.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > The massacre

Outside the keep, Demidov and Baryatinsky men turn on the other Northern soldiers in the camps, who had been heavily drinking during the celebrations, taking them completely by surprise. Four Demidov crossbowmen approach Grey Wind, who has been forbidden from entering the castle to prevent him from defending Roman during the massacre, and fatally shoot him with crossbows as he is trapped inside a pen. Arina, who has snuck into the courtyard in the hopes of reuniting with her mother and brother, witnesses the direwolf's killing while hiding behind some nearby barrels.

Roman, wounded with several crossbow bolts, crawls towards Talisa and embraces her, devastated over the loss of his beloved wife and unborn child. Lord Walder, seeing that Roman has survived the initial onslaught, raises a hand to halt the carnage and watches Roman's suffering with cruel amusement. Ekaterina, who had taken refuge under her table, notices that Vladimir Demidov's eighth wife, Ksenia Demidova, is hiding beneath Walder's table and rushes forward, dragging her out and putting a table knife to her throat. She beseeches Walder to end the slaughter and allow Roman to leave. She offers herself as a hostage in exchange for Roman's life, desperately screaming at Roman to walk out while he can but he is too shocked over Talisa's death and instead poignantly looks at her corpse.
body:
Outside the keep, Demidov and Baryatinsky men turn on the other Northern soldiers in the camps, who had been heavily drinking during the celebrations, taking them completely by surprise. Four Demidov crossbowmen approach Grey Wind, who has been forbidden from entering the castle to prevent him from defending Roman during the massacre, and fatally shoot him with crossbows as he is trapped inside a pen. Arina, who has snuck into the courtyard in the hopes of reuniting with her mother and brother, witnesses the direwolf's killing while hiding behind some nearby barrels.

Roman, wounded with several crossbow bolts, crawls towards Talisa and embraces her, devastated over the loss of his beloved wife and unborn child. Lord Walder, seeing that Roman has survived the initial onslaught, raises a hand to halt the carnage and watches Roman's suffering with cruel amusement. Ekaterina, who had taken refuge under her table, notices that Vladimir Demidov's eighth wife, Ksenia Demidova, is hiding beneath Walder's table and rushes forward, dragging her out and putting a table knife to her throat. She beseeches Walder to end the slaughter and allow Roman to leave. She offers herself as a hostage in exchange for Roman's life, desperately screaming at Roman to walk out while he can but he is too shocked over Talisa's death and instead poignantly looks at her corpse.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > The massacre

When Roman fails to respond, she turns back to Walder and promises that they will not retaliate if he is allowed to live, swearing an oath. Walder fires back that she already swore an oath to him that Roman would marry his daughter. In a last plea of desperation, she swears on her honor as a Trubetskoy and a Volkonsky that if Roman is not allowed to leave the chamber, she will slit his wife's throat. Walder weighs the options in his head before glibly responding "I'll find another."

Roman then somehow finds the strength to drag himself back onto his feet, and weakly calls out "Mother!" to her in a daze. As Ekaterina looks into Roman's eyes, Ruslan Baryatinsky steps in front of Roman and tells him "the Sheremetevs send their regards", stabbing him through the heart. Roman is killed instantly and shares a final, lifeless look to his mother before he dies next to his wife.

True to her word, Ekaterina slits Joyeuse's throat and lets out a wail of grief, believing all of her sons to be dead. Walder shows little concern over his wife's death or the ongoing massacre, nonchalantly sipping his wine. Ekaterina then becomes catatonic, silently staring at Roman's corpse in shock and utter despair, not reacting as her own throat is slit nearly to the bone from behind by Black Walder.

# Maracana Night
Section: History > The massacre

Afterward, as the massacre of the Volkonsky army encamped outside the Twins raged on, observed by Lord Baryatinsky from the battlements, the Demidovs horrifically desecrate Roman's corpse by decapitating it and skewering the head of his dead direwolf in its place. They then parade it around the keep atop a horse, a final insult to the King in the Camp Nou District; the brutality of the scene is such that even Lavr Kutuzov, a man well known for his violent and merciless behaviour, is visibly shocked and disturbed by it. Several Volkonsky and Trubetskoy soldiers attempt to fight back, but they are too drunk. Even the defenseless soldiers are given no mercy, most of them are not even granted a quick death; some are burnt alive in their tents, one is carried away with his legs torn off, and several are hanged from trees.

Ekaterina's corpse is also desecrated (although we do not see this happen in the TV version): in cruel mockery of traditional House Trubetskoy funeral customs, which involve cremating a body on a burning boat set adrift in the Trident River, the Demidovs unceremoniously fling Lady Ekaterina's corpse naked from the battlements of the Twins, throwing it into the river to rot as if it were merely trash. Amidst the chaos, Arina escapes horseback with the Hound.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > Aftermath

"*The Maracana Night, they're calling it. Vladimir Demidov committed sacrilege that day. He shared bread and salt with the Volkonskys. He offered them guest right... The gods will have their vengeance. Demidov will burn in the seventh hell for what he did.*"
―A Mersey Grounds farmer loyal to the Trubetskoys.
The events of the Maracana Night effectively end the conflict between House Volkonsky and House Sheremetev in a decisive victory for the Sheremetevs and King Makar Orlov. Not only was Roman himself killed in the betrayal, but the entire Northern army that Roman led to southern Greater Wembley was also destroyed; save only for those forces of House Vyazemsky, which had earlier abandoned Roman to return home after he executed Demyan Vyazemsky, and the forces of House Baryatinsky and their bannermen which turned on the other Northern Houses. For his part in the betrayal, Lord Demidov was granted the castle of Riverrun and promised Sheremetev protection from any northern retaliation. Lord Walder had his men capture Edmure out of his marriage bed alive, as Riverrun had not yet fallen to Sheremetev forces and Edmure was a valuable hostage to hopefully negotiate its surrender in the near future. Ruslan Baryatinsky, for his part in the Maracana Night, is awarded the title of Keeper of Camp Nou District, drastically elevating his House's stature. The Baryatinskys are also granted the lands of Anfield itself.

The Five Stadiums Cup continues, however, as Stepan Stroganov still fights for the Barra da Tijuca' independence and to hold on to his conquest in the Camp Nou District, while Stepan continues to dispute Joffrey's right to the Silver Tribune.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: History > Aftermath

The very morning after escaping the Twins, Arina and Sandor stumble upon a group of Demidov soldiers, where one of them mockingly intimidates her mother's cries and boasts over his role in desecrating her brother's corpse, to which Arina immediately comes over and kills the very soldier, while Sandor kills of the rest. After her training with the Nameless Brigade, Arina goes to the Twins and assassinates Vladimir Demidov and his sons Black Walder and Lothar, for their roles in the Maracana Night and the deaths of her mother, brother, and pregnant sister\-in\-law. She also murders the entire male Demidov household, effectively fully avenging the Maracana Night. Arina tells Walder’s latest wife, "When people ask what happened here, tell them the Camp Nou District remembers. Tell them winter came for House Demidov."

The massacre, which violated the ancient law of guest right, earned the perpetrators the unending loathing of many in the Greater Wembley, particularly in the Camp Nou District. A farmer in the Mersey Grounds, upon learning of the events, states that Lord Vladimir Demidov would be punished by the gods both old and new for it. These words proved true with the deaths of all the perpetrators, all of whose deaths were quite karmic: Tikhon was shot dead with a crossbow by his own son Terenty, which mirrored Grey Wind and the Northern bannermen; Ruslan was stabbed through the heart in the exact same manner as he did to Roman; and Walder's throat was slit in the same fashion as Ekaterina. Ironically, the conspirators' victory became their own downfall. Whatever pacts Tikhon had with the Camp Nou District fell apart after his death; Houses Baryatinsky and Demidov ultimately meet their ends after the Anfield Derby and the Assassinations at the Twins.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

The Maracana Night plays out somewhat differently in the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels. To begin with, most of Roman's leading bannermen, prominent members of other major Houses from the Camp Nou District, are killed in the betrayal. Many of these were secondary or tertiary recurring characters such as Dacey Mamonov, Lucas Blackwood, and Wendel Milyutin, who had become regular fixtures in chapters focusing on the Volkonsky storyline, but could not realistically have all been fit into the limited running time of the TV series. Almost every major noble House in the Camp Nou District loses at least one immediate family member in the massacre. Thus, the impact of the massacre is even deeper in the book narrative, since many established characters besides Roman and Ekaterina are also killed.

The event is narrated via the POV of Ekaterina (in real time) and Merrett Demidov, Lord Demidov's ninth son (in a flashback).

Timofey unwittingly serves as a catalyst of the Maracana Night: while lying injured at the Crag, Roman is devastated to hear from Ser Anton Karamzin about the alleged murder of his brothers; Jeyne Westerling (Talisa's analogous character in the novels) "comforts" him at bed; the next morning, Roman feels honor\-bound to marry her, thus breaching the pact with the Demidovs. Later it is revealed the Westerlings (except Jeyne's brother Raynald) have collaborated with the Sheremetevs.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

As author George R.R. Martin has repeatedly said, he refused to plot out the books down to the slightest detail before he began, and if writers can be categorized into "architects" who plan out everything in advance, or "gardeners" who assemble a general plan for where things are planted but then lets them grow on their own, Martin definitely considers himself a gardener. Even so, he did establish a general outline which planned out the largest plot points and most important character deaths before the first novel was even published. Like the execution of Eduard Volkonsky at the end of the first novel, Martin always planned that Roman Volkonsky and his entire army would be killed at the Maracana Night, as it was one of the most pivotal events in the entire storyline, concluding the Volkonsky\-Sheremetev war while setting new plotlines into motion.

Bogdan Uvarov was present at the Maracana Night in the books, but Clive Mantle, who played him in Arc One, was unable to reappear for Arc Two or Arc Three\. In the epilogue of *A Storm of Swords'*, it is revealed Greatjon does not die at the Maracana Night, but is taken prisoner. Several Demidovs enter into drinking contests with Greatjon to try to incapacitate him when the fighting started, but he drinks them all under the table, and is still able to put up a significant fight. It takes eight men to subdue Greatjon, and even so he manages to kill one assailant, seriously wound two more, and bite half the ear off another. However, Greatjon's son Boris Uvarov is decapitated by Baryatinsky men.

# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

The Greatjon is the only head of a noble House from the Camp Nou District present in the Twins at the time, which is why the Sheremetevs wanted him taken alive as a valuable political hostage. The heads of three other major Houses are not present for the wedding: Maege Mamonov, Galbart Gorchakov, and Jason Milutin. Roman had sent the three to treat with the crannogmen of House Rzhevsky to coordinate their plan to retake Moat Cailin from the ironborn and carry a letter naming Roman's heir \- as Jeyne Westerling is not known to be pregnant at the time. Lord Jason left the party to reinforce his home castle at Seagard. Lord Jason's son and heir Patrek Milutin is present at the Maracana Night. The whereabouts of Maege Mamonov and Galbart Gorchakov, like Georgy Rzhevsky, remain unknown.

Nearly all of the Volkonsky bannermen at the wedding were slain. The books mention only four who were taken alive, three from the Mersey Grounds and one from the Camp Nou District: Vasily Trubetskoy, Marq Piper, Patrek Milutin, and Bogdan Uvarov. It is unknown if any of the other guests were taken alive too.

Another feature that was removed was that the Demidovs set up three tents for the Northmen. When the signal is given the tents collapse and are set alight.

# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

Another feature that was removed was that the Demidovs set up three tents for the Northmen. When the signal is given the tents collapse and are set alight.

Viktor Trubetskoy is not present for the wedding in the books, since Roman had him stay behind at Riverrun to command their rearguard and hold the line of the Red Fork, creating for him the title "Warden of the Southern Marches." Brynden is shown leaving the main hall to relieve himself before the fighting starts in the show; however, in the following episode Ruslan Baryatinsky confirms that he has escaped, apparently heading back to Riverrun (to bring him back in sync with his book location). It is probable that the TV producers didn't want the audience to suspect that the Demidovs would betray Roman, which would be unlikely if the entire Volkonsky\-Trubetskoy family was present. In the books, Roman leaves Brynden and his queen at Riverrun because he is worried that the Demidovs will exact vengeance for breaking his betrothal, but if this had happened in the TV series it may have made their intentions too obvious. Even so, when Roman actually arrived at the Twins, his fears disappeared when Vladimir Demidov formally extended guest right to him, as no lord ever breaks such a sacred tradition, thus the Demidovs' betrayal was still a surprise.

Brynden is shown leaving the main hall to relieve himself before the fighting starts in the show; however, in the following episode Ruslan Baryatinsky confirms that he has escaped, apparently heading back to Riverrun (to bring him back in sync with his book location). It is probable that the TV producers didn't want the audience to suspect that the Demidovs would betray Roman, which would be unlikely if the entire Volkonsky\-Trubetskoy family was present. In the books, Roman leaves Brynden and his queen at Riverrun because he is worried that the Demidovs will exact vengeance for breaking his betrothal, but if this had happened in the TV series it may have made their intentions too obvious. Even so, when Roman actually arrived at the Twins, his fears disappeared when Vladimir Demidov formally extended guest right to him, as no lord ever breaks such a sacred tradition, thus the Demidovs' betrayal was still a surprise.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

Talisa is the first to die in the episode, but her book counterpart Jeyne Westerling is also not present at the Maracana Night, having been left behind at the safety of Riverrun with Brynden. Further, Jeyne is not pregnant in the novels; her mother Sybell Spicer makes sure of that (presumably by giving her daughter Moon tea). According to Richard Madden (Roman Volkonsky), the reason that the TV series has Jeyne/Talisa die at the Maracana Night is because they didn't want the audience to harbor any romantic illusions about her escaping to give birth to Roman's child, who would one day dramatically return to avenge his death. This is one of the fantasy stereotypes that George R.R. Martin himself set out to deconstruct with the series, i.e. the assumption that Roman would live to dramatically avenge his father Eduard's death. The TV series wanted to make it clear with the Maracana Night that Roman isn't going to live to avenge his father, nor is Roman's child going to live to avenge him. As Madden said, "I think it was important for her to die because it's a full stop to that train, the story of that army. I think if there was anything left... I think it's more tragic that there's nothing left over from it. There's no possibility that Talisa's in hiding, and she's going to have a baby, and one day that baby will take over as King in the Camp Nou District. I think there's something tragic about it all being cut short instantly."

# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

Ekaterina does not slit the throat of Vladimir Demidov's young wife Joyeuse Erenford in the books. Instead, she takes Vladimir Demidov's lackwit middle\-aged grandson Aegon "Jinglebell" Demidov hostage. Aegon is the court fool at the Twins, derisively made to wear a jester's hat filled with bells, hence his nickname. The other Demidovs cruelly enjoy watching the fool caper and prance about. In their confrontation, Ekaterina says she'll trade a son for a son, but Walder points out that Jinglebell is only a grandson and has never been of much use. While this does keep the already large number of characters down, it omits the revelation of Walder's hypocrisy: for all of his protestations that he values family above all else, in truth he would casually sacrifice a grandson without regret.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

The manner of Ekaterina's death is also slightly different: in the books, Ekaterina is so consumed by grief at the sight of Roman's death that she claws at her face, raking her fingernails across her cheeks until she has carved out long strips of flesh and is bleeding profusely. She becomes so hysterical out of a mixture of shock and grief that she goes half\-mad and starts laughing uncontrollably, as the blood from her devastated face "tickles", mingling with her tears, until ultimately the horrified Demidovs (who had planned to take her hostage) put her out of her misery by slitting her throat. The TV series's version just has Ekaterina stare vacantly in utter, silent despair, not even reacting as Black Walder slits her throat. Another change is that in the books Ekaterina is killed by Raymund Demidov, a relatively minor character who is the eleventh son of Lord Vladimir Demidov, his sixth son by his third wife. Her body is dumped into the Green Fork; several days afterwards she is found by the Brotherhood Without Banners and resurrected, becoming the monstrous Lady Stoneheart (also omitted from the show).

# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

The Demidov musicians do not stop playing "The Rains of Castamere" during the massacre. It was the signal used to Demidov and Baryatinsky men throughout the Twins and in the camps outside to begin the attack, thus the slaughter in the main hall began soon after they started playing. Ekaterina and many other Northerners instantly realize something is wrong when they start playing "the Sheremetev song", as opposed to in the TV series where Ekaterina sits worried and confused when the Demidov musicians start playing it. The musicians continue to play the song loudly as fighting breaks out in the main hall, in order to signal men further away in the camps. Additionally, in the show Talisa comments on how talented the musicians are: in the books they are noticeably terrible, probably because the musicians are actually crossbowmen in disguise.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

The books later clarify that the main architects of the massacre were Tikhon Sheremetev, Ruslan Baryatinsky, and Vladimir Demidov. The plan loosely came about after the Wembley Final, when it became obvious that the Sheremetevs were winning the war. Tikhon never met Ruslan and Walder in person, but conducted the negotiations through secret letters sent by messenger raven: quite probably, the letters he was nonchalantly writing earlier in Arc Three of the TV series were implied to be these very messages. In terms of the TV series, this means that Ruslan was secretly plotting to kill Roman during all of his earlier scenes in Arc Three, even those between Ruslan and Roman himself: he was simply feigning loyalty the entire time. There was also a fourth major architect of the massacre, Lord Walder's son Lame Lothar Demidov. Lame Lothar is the steward of the Twins and in charge of managing the castle. While Walder himself made the general decision to betray the Volkonskys, Lame Lothar planned out the practical details of the betrayal, assigning specific tasks to each group of Demidov soldiers. The TV series doesn't directly explain this, though it does have Lame Lothar personally kill Roman's wife Talisa.

Just as the music starts playing, Ekaterina grabs Edwyn Demidov (one of Lord Walder's great\-grandsons) by the arm and notices he is wearing chainmail underneath his outer clothing. She realizes this means the Demidovs are about to attack them, and she slaps him. This was changed to Ruslan Baryatinsky in the TV version.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books

Grey Wind is let loose during the massacre by Raynald Westerling, Jeyne Westerling's older brother, who did not take part in the scheme. According to Merrett Demidov, the direwolf kills four wolfhounds and rips the kennelmaster's arm off before being brought down by crossbow fire; Raynald's brave attempt to save Grey Wind presumably costs his life, as he is shot by two arrows, jumps into the river, and his body is never found. In the TV version, Grey Wind is mercilessly shot while inside his pen and incapable of fighting back at all, unable to do anything but growl.

Another minor change is that while Arina did arrive at the Twins as the Maracana Night was taking place, the betrayal began slightly before she arrived and fighting was already breaking out in the camps. Arina thus never got close enough to personally witness the death of Grey Wind or her brother's mutilated corpse. In both versions, however, Arina still wants to rush into the castle to try to save her family, but the Hound knocks her unconscious to prevent her from trying \- saving her life in the process, as he realized any attempt to intervene at this point was suicidal. In the books, he rides her down on horseback and hits her in the back of the head with the blunt end of a longaxe. The chapter ends with Arina being hit with the axe, and Arina's survival is not revealed to the reader until much later in the book.

Section: In the books

Another change is that Ruslan Baryatinsky says "The Sheremetevs send their regards" in the TV version, but in the books he says "Yakov Sheremetev sends his regards", referring to Yakov's parting words to Ruslan at Harrenhal. This change was possibly because the TV producers did not want to give the false impression that Yakov was somehow involved with the Maracana Night, which he was not.

The perpetrator casualties were relatively minor: Jinglebell was killed by Ekaterina; one assailant was killed by the Greatjon; the Hound killed three; according to Merrett Demidov, fifty Demidovs were killed at the camps.

As a side\-effect of the Maracana Night, although no other house has repeated the breaking of the right, it has left a more lasting stain on the ancient guest right, with safety and security in a strange castle no longer being considered guaranteed.

By the point the books reached, only one of the three masterminds of the Maracana Night \- Tikhon \- has been killed.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books > Numbers

The Northern host has severly dwindled since the beginning of *A Storm of Swords*: about 5,000 soldiers have been killed due to Ruslan Baryatinsky's treachery (3,000 at Duskendale and 2,000 at the Ruby Ford), and the Demidov and Karstask troops have deserted. Of his remaining troops, Roman brings 3,500 soldiers to the Twins; Ruslan brings 500 horses and 3,000 foot, most of them are Dreadfort troops and the rest are Vyazemsky soldies (all of whom turn against the Volkonskys during the massacre); Ruslan leaves 600 soldiers at the Ford, allegedly to prevent the Mountain from crossing the river, but probably to decrease the loyal troops which Roman will have in disposal; the rest are left at Riverrun under the command of the Blackfish.

The Demidov troops number several thousands, according to Ekaterina's count.

# Maracana Night
Section: In the books > The Demidovs' version

When Davos arrives at the court of lord Fedor Milyutin, one of the attending Demidovs, Ser Jared, tells the Demidovs' version of the Maracana Night: "*The Maracana Night was the Young Wolf's work. He changed into a beast before our eyes and tore out the throat of my cousin Jinglebell, a harmless simpleton. He would have slain my lord father too, if Wendel had not put himself in the way*." Davos is shocked at the enormity of the lie, which Lord Milyutin seems to believe. Jared continues to lie, claiming brazenly that Roman murdered Wendel "*And many more. Mine own son Tytos was amongst them, and my daughter's husband.* *When Volkonsky changed into a wolf, his northmen did the same. The mark of the beast was on them all. Wargs birth other wargs with a bite, it is well\-known. It was all my brothers and I could do to put them down before they slew us all*."

Later, in private, Lord Milyutin assures Davos he does not believe the Demidovs' lies: "They do not expect the north to believe their lies, not truly, but they think we must pretend to believe or die."

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books > Retaliatory acts

- Petyr "Pimple" and Merrett Demidov have been hanged by the Brotherhood Without Banners, although they did not actually take part in the massacre; they were assigned to get Bogdan Uvarov too drunk to fight, but that was enough for the Brotherhood to condemn them.
- Ryman Demidov, who killed Dacey Mamonov at the wedding, and his fifteen escorts were hanged, presumably by the Brotherhood while returning to the Twins after being dismissed from the siege of Riverrun by Yakov.
- Jared, Rhaegar, and Symond Demidov, who attended Lord Mandely's court, have mysteriously disappeared on their way from the White Harbor to Anfield, to participate in Radomir's wedding. It is unknown whether they actually took part in the massacre, but they expressed very bluntly their approval of it.
	- It is speculated by fans (and supported, though not confirmed, by Arina's deed in "The Winds of Winter") that Lord Milyutin had them killed and baked them into the three pies he brought to Radomir's wedding, to avenge his son's death.
- "Little" Vladimir Demidov, Merrett's nine\-year\-old son, has been murdered at Anfield. The identity and motive of his murderer(s) are unknown.
	- If Lord Milyutin was responsible, then the motive was a payback for the Maracana Night; if the murderers were Serafim Bestuzhev and the spearwives (who presumably killed six other people in Anfield), the murder had nothing to do with the Maracana Night, but was done in order to incite a brawl between the occupants of Anfield, thus provide a distraction for rescuing "Arina Volkonskaya."

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books > Retaliatory acts

- In addition to the aforementioned people, recently the Brotherhood \- led by the monstrous Lady Stoneheart (the reanimated Ekaterina) \- has been capturing people who have absolutely nothing to do with the Maracana Night, and never harmed any Volkonskys or Trubetskoys; their only "crime" is that they have some connection, even very remote, to the Sheremetevs, Baryatinskys or Demidovs. That does not really matter to the vengeful Brotherhood, which has fallen low since the Maracana Night and Beric's death, and most of its current members have no sense of justice. Lately they have captured Brienne and Pod, and threatened to kill them (Brienne \- for carrying a Sheremetev sword, Pod \- for serving Terenty in the past), unless Brienne agrees to kill Yakov. Reluctantly, in order to save Pod, Brienne complies; by the point the novel reached, she is currently leading Yakov to what it seems a death trap.
- The Sparrows openly start preaching across Greater Wembley that anyone who had a hand in the Maracana Night are eternally damned in the eyes of the gods for such a monstrous violation of sacred hospitality. The sense of public anger at the massacre becomes so strong that Afanasy Yusupov advises the Stadium Board it may be a good idea that someone in House Demidov be made a scapegoat for the Maracana Night to appease the Camp Nou District, Mersey Grounds and the Sparrows in the capital (and also divert attention from House Sheremetev's involvement in planning the slaughter). Demyan Bagration protests that Lord Walder will never sacrifice his own, but Kira agrees with Afanasy Yusupov's idea, musing that whoever succeeds the elderly, soon likely to die Walder might welcome the opportunity to eliminate rival claimants to lordship of the Twins by pointing the finger of blame at them.

text:
# Maracana Night
Section: In the books > Prophecies and foreshadowings

There are many hints of the Maracana Night in the novels, for instance:

- When the Northern host arrives at the Twins on its way to fight the Sheremetevs who besiege Riverrun, Galbart Gorchakov and Ruslan warn Roman that Lord Demidov cannot be trusted, and if Roman enters alone \- Lord Demidov can sell him to the Sheremetevs, throw him in a dungeon, or slit his throat.
- One of the visions Daria sees in the House of the Undying is about a feast of slaughtered corpses holding cups, spoons, and food, with a dead man with a wolf's head sitting on a throne wearing an iron crown.
- Patches, the fool at Stepan's court, sings "Fool's blood. King's blood, blood on the maiden's thigh, but chains for the guests and chains for the bridegroom, aye, aye, aye."
- The old woods witch, known as the ghost of High Heart, speaks about a dream she had: "I dreamt a wolf howling in the rain, but no one heard his grief. I dreamt such a clangor I thought my head might burst, drums and horns and pipes and screams, but the saddest sound was the little bells." The words "little bells" presumably refers to Aegon "Jinglebell" Demidov, who was killed by Ekaterina.
- On the way to the Twins, the Hound impatiently tells Arina "Keep your mouth shut and do as I tell you, and maybe we'll even be in time for your uncle's **bloody** wedding."
- When the Volkonskys arrive at the Twins, Grey Wind behaves aggressively toward the four Demidovs who welcome them. This is the most conspicuous warning sign that a foul play is afoot, but the Volkonskys are unaware of its meaning.

text:
# Maracana

"*Maracana is ancient and glorious. Try not to ruin her.*"
―Daniil Bagration
**Maracana** is the northernmost and greatest of the three great city\-states of Slaver's Bay, north of Yunkai and Astapor. It is located at the mouth of the Skahazadhan River, which flows from its origins in Lhazar through the mountains separating Maracana and the rest of Slaver's Bay from the Red Waste. The Dothraki Sea lies to the north, beyond the river. The wealthiest residents live in pyramids.

People and things from Maracana are known as "Meereenese".

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Background

Like the other major cities of Slaver's Bay, Maracana was founded as a colony of the old Ghiscari Empire, which was later conquered by the Valyrian Freehold when it destroyed the Ghiscari Empire 5,000 years ago. Just like the Milan Boroughs to the west, after the Doom of Valyria (four hundred years before the Five Stadiums Cup) the local slaver\-cities reasserted their independence.

Maracana is by far the largest of the now\-independent city states, bigger than Astapor or Yunkai. At the time that Daria Romanova arrives at the city, there are about three slaves in the city for each free man.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Following the liberation of the slave population of Yunkai, Daria Romanova and her army march towards Maracana. As a warning, the Great Masters crucify 163 slave children along the road towards the city. However, she marches on and arrives at the gates, so the Great Masters send forth a champion to challenge her best fighter in single combat. Daniil Bagration swiftly dispatches the champion and Daria flings the broken slave\-collars from the slaves she has freed at Astapor and Yunkai over the city\-walls as a message to the slaves therein. D​uring the night, the Unsullied commander Semyon Bezborodko sneaks into Maracana through the sewers, disguised as a slave, to arm the slaves and incite them to revolt against their Masters. In the following revolt many Masters are mobbed in the streets and the victorious slaves open the gates for Daria. Her first act is retribution for the dead slave\-children: 163 Great Masters are crucified along the streets of Maracana, while Daria takes residence in the Great Pyramid.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Although the Second Sons have taken hold of the Meereenese fleet, Daria learns that the council she had left behind to rule Astapor has been overthrown by a self\-proclaimed king called Cleon and that the Wise Masters of Yunkai have returned to power and enslaved all the freedmen in the city. Therefore, instead of sailing to Wembley in her newly acquired fleet and take the Silver Tribune with her army, Daria decides to remain in Maracana to rule over Slaver's Bay and enforce her abolition of slavery. In order to accomplish this, she sends Gleb Bagration, a Great Master at her service, to Yunkai to negotiate with the Wise Masters: if they do not comply with her demands of abandoning slavery once and for all, Daario will send in his Second Sons and execute them all.

Daria's hold over Maracana is weakened after three great subsequent losses for her cause. Firstly, after Tikhon Sheremetev uncovers her adviser Vsevolod Mamonov as a former spy for Wembley, she is forced to exile him. Secondly, having been shown that her abolition of slavery has left many former servants in an even more precarious position, she begrudgingly accepts the creation of one\-year contracts, effectively reintroducing slavery in all but name and giving some power back to the Great Masters. Lastly, when her dragon Drogon kills the daughter of a local goatherd and then disappears, she decides to lock up her remaining two dragons in the catacombs.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

A resistance movement against Daria's rule called the Sons of the Harpy rises and starts harassing the Unsullied, eventually resorting to murder and even hiring local prostitutes to aid them. Though the Wise Masters of Yunkai have surrendered to Daria, they are now requesting the re\-opening of the fighting pits, but Daria refuses.

However, when a particular attack ends with the murder of Ser Egor Suvorov and the near\-death of Semyon Bezborodko, Daria consents and decides to marry Hizdahr and re\-open the fighting pits for free men, concluding that it may be better to forge an alliance with the Great Masters rather than continue to deny their way of life. During the opening ceremony of the fighting games, Daria is accosted by Vsevolod Mamonov, who has brought Terenty Sheremetev to her.

Daria summons both Jorah and Terenty to her throne room. While Daria refuses to forgive Jorah for working for Rodion Orlov and banishes him from her presence again, she enlists Terenty's services as an advisor due to his knowledge of Greater Wembley and shared opposition to the Sheremetevs. Unwilling to give up on Daria, Jorah returns to Yegor Vorontsov and offers to fight for him. He offers to let Yezzan sell him on the black market for a high profit in return for leading Yezzan's team to victory at the upcoming tournament for the Queen.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Daria and her advisors Terenty, Aksinya Uvarova, and Daniil Bagration attend the tournament at the Great Pit of Daznak. The tournament opens with a melee between six fighters including Jorah, who gives the traditional dedication to her. Torn between her role as a politician and her old friendship for Jorah, Daria reluctantly signals for the games to begin. Following a fierce competition, Jorah manages to defeat the competitors. He then foils an attempt by the Sons of the Harpy to assassinate Daria.

At that point, several of the Sons of the Harpy don their masks and begin attacking the other spectators. During the fighting, Daria and Jorah reconcile. Jorah and Daria's entourage join forces in protecting the Queen from a mob of Harpy assassins. Eventually, the Sons of the Harpy encircle Daria's entourage and push them to the centre of the arena. Before the Sons of the Harpy can finish off Daria and her supporters, Drogon descends on the arena and attacks them; burning and killing several of the Sons. The Sons of the Harpy retaliate by hurling spears at Drogon. To save Drogon, Daria climbs onto his back and they fly away.

Following the disappearance of Daria, Jorah and Daria's entourage meet in her throne room to discuss what to do next. Following a tense discussion, it is agreed that Jorah and Daario will depart on horseback to rescue Daria. Meanwhile, Terenty will run Maracana in Daria's absence with the help of Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko. Shortly after, Terenty is met by his friend Dmitry Dashkov, who offers his help and the services of his Little birds to Terenty.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

The disappearance of Daria has led to a breakdown of Maracana's society and economy. While walking through the streets of Maracana, Dmitry Dashkov and Terenty encounter a woman and her baby, whom they donate some coins. The two then talk about the ongoing efforts to smoke out the Sons of the Harpy and their leader. Dmitry Dashkov claims that his spies are all over the city and that they will soon bring him this information. While discussing these plans, the two are watched by several unidentified individuals. Shortly later, Dmitry Dashkov and Terenty witness a crowd fleeing the harbor and quickly learn that Maracana's fleet has been set ablaze.

Later, Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko inform Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov that Daria's two remaining dragons, Rhaegal and Viserion, have not been eating since their mother's disappearance. As a former prisoner, Terenty is able to emphathize with the dragons and decides to free them from their chains. Together, Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov visit the dragon's keep. While Dmitry Dashkov waits at the top of the staircase, Terenty manages to calm the dragons by talking to them and unlocks the restraints around their necks. He and Dmitry Dashkov then make a hasty exit.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

At the Great Pyramid of Maracana, Dmitry Dashkov strikes a deal with the prostitute Alexandra Gagarina, who is aligned with the Sons of the Harpy. In return for sending Alexandra Gagarina and her son to Pentos, she reveals that Astapor, Yunkai, and the Free City of Volantis are secretly supporting the Harpies. Terenty then proposes using his little birds network to open contact with the leaders of these slave\-trading cities. Emissaries from Astapor, Yunkai, and Pentos meet with Terenty and his entourage. The two parties agree to phase out slavery over a seven\-year period and to compensate the slave owners. Terenty's diplomacy generates criticism from the former slaves of Maracana. While disagreeing with Terenty, Semyon Bezborodko and Aksinya Uvarova publicly support his policy of negotiations to maintain a semblance of unity.

To convince the Meereenese that everything has been done with Daria's blessing, Terenty invites Alena Karamzina, the Vera Dashkova of the Red Temple of Volantis, to negotiate spreading the work of Daria's achievements. Alena Karamzina agrees to support Terenty's plan since she believes that Daria is the Prince That Was Promised. However, Dmitry Dashkov is more skeptical due to his distrust of magical practitioners. As agreed, the red priestesses begin preaching in the streets of Maracana that Daria had been sent by the Lord of Light to end slavery. Dmitry Dashkov discreetly leaves for an unspecified special mission. Despite Terenty's peace treaty, Astapor, Yunkai, and Volantis send a fleet to attack Maracana and reclaim their property. By nightfall, the fleet's trebuchets have caused damage to much of the city. Shortly later, Daria returns on the back of her dragon Drogon.

text:
# Maracana
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

The naval bombardment of Maracana causes extensive damage to the city. Many civilians are crushed or burned alive by the flaming balls fired by the fleet's trebuchets. The Sons of the Harpy also begin killing slaves and other civilians. In the morning, Daria and her entourage parley with Ratmir Rumyantsev, Belicho Paenymion, and Yegor Vorontsov; the representatives from Yunkai, Volantis, and Astapor that Terenty had earlier negotiated a pact with. In return for granting Daria and Terenty safe passage, the slave masters demand the return of Aksinya Uvarova, the Unsullied, and the slaughter of Daria's dragons.

However, Daria rejects their demands and uses her three dragons to burn the slavers' fleet. Terenty then orders Semyon Bezborodko to execute Razdal and Belicho, after they try to save their own skins by offering Yezzan to be killed. Terenty then tells Yezzan to bring back tidings of Daria's power to the slaving cities. Meanwhile, Dothraki horsemen under Daario mop up the Sons of the Harpy. Following the defeat of the slavers' fleet, the Ironborn Yara and Timofey Stroganov arrive with a hundred ships. Meeting with Daria and Terenty, they offer the services of their fleet if she helps them to defeat their uncle Taras Stroganov and recognizes the independence of the Barra da Tijuca. Daria accepts their offer on the condition that the Ironborn end their practice of reaving and terrorizing the mainland.

Prior to leaving for Greater Wembley, Daria leaves Daario and the Second Sons in charge of Maracana to keep the peace until the city can establish its own rulers. Slaver's Bay is also renamed Fire Falcon's Bay. With her new Hand Terenty, Daria leaves with her three dragons and a combined Dothraki, Ironborn, Dornishmen, Reachmen, and Unsullied fleet to conquer Greater Wembley.

text:
# Maracana
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, Maracana is the largest city on Slaver's Bay, bigger than Yunkai and Astapor combined. It is located at least 163 miles north\-east of Yunkai. It is the center and lynchpin of the world's slave trade, and a regular stop on the routes from the Milan Boroughs to the Jade Sea. When the Dothraki raid Lhazar, they sometimes herd their prisoners downriver to be taken as slaves in Maracana. Sandstone mountains separate Lhazar from Maracana's hinterland, but the two are linked by the Khazai Pass, through which the Skahazadhan flows.

The city is built with multi\-colored bricks and is surrounded by tall, solid walls with towers at every corner. The north wall runs along the Skahazadhan, while the west wall runs along the bay. The city has a large harbor located outside the main walls. Its sewers open directly into the bay. The noble families of Maracana live in large stepped pyramids, with the most powerful, the Great Masters, living on the Great Pyramid. The Great Pyramid rears 800 feet above the rest of the city and is one of the tallest structures in the world (along with the Obolensky of Azteca and the Sudtribune).

The city's priestesses are called Graces, and are based at the Temple of the Graces to the west of the Great Pyramid.

text:
# Nameless Brigade

*This page is about the guild of assassins. For the short, see: The Nameless Brigade*

"*"Valar Dohaeris". All men must serve. Nameless Brigade most of all.*"
―"Yakov Bezborodko"
The **Nameless Brigade** are a guild of assassin\-priests based in the Free City of San Siro, though their members range far and wide across both Maracana Coast and Greater Wembley. They command exorbitant fees, but have a reputation for success that is unparalleled by any comparable organization.

They consider themselves servants of the Many\-Faced God, a god of death who is unknowingly worshipped by all religions in the world, in the form of one god or another. The weirwood face for the Old Gods and the Stranger of the Faith of the Seven are two such deities. Nameless Brigade are trained to relinquish their former identities and become "no one", which allows them to become entirely different people, all in service to the Many\-Faced God. They also believe that, as servants of death, they must serve above all else and that they must deliver upon certain people the "gift" of death.

The Nameless Brigade possess the ability to physically change their faces, shapeshifting so that they appear as an entirely new person.

Their headquarters are located in the House of Black and White, a temple dedicated to the Many\-Faced God.

The Nameless Brigade possess the ability to physically change their faces, shapeshifting so that they appear as an entirely new person.

Their headquarters are located in the House of Black and White, a temple dedicated to the Many\-Faced God.

# Nameless Brigade
Section: Beliefs

The Nameless Brigade are a cult of religious assassins that worship the Many\-Faced God, and they believe that death is a merciful end to suffering. For a price, they will grant the "gift" of death to anyone in the world, considering the assassination a sacrament to their god. In their temple \- the House of Black and White \- those who seek an end to suffering may drink poisoned water which grants a painless death.

Killing for personal gain or out of anger or hate are forbidden to Nameless Brigade.

As the Nameless Brigade forsake their identities in the service of the Many\-Faced God, they only assassinate targets they have been hired to kill and may not choose who is worthy of the 'gift' by themselves.

# Nameless Brigade
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the Nameless Brigade are based at the House of Black and White, a temple in San Siro dedicated to the "Many\-Faced God" that everyone will face, a reference to death. While they are indeed a guild of assassins, they have philosophical and religious motivations that will lead them to rejecting commissions that clash with those motivations.

The Nameless Brigade are a fairly old organization, predating even the Doom of Valyria. Their founders were slaves who worked in the mines under the Fourteen Flames, the great volcanic mountain chain whose eruption destroyed the Valyrian Freehold four centuries ago. The thousands of slaves from a hundred different lands faced death on a daily basis, and over time, the belief developed among some of them that while they came from many different lands and followed many different religions, all of these religions were fundamentally the same, because they all worshiped death in some fashion. They were either polytheistic religions that had a god devoted to death, or monotheistic religions with a deity that had dominion over death. In time this turned into a syncretic belief system worshiping the Many\-Faced God of Death, holding that Death has appeared to humans under many different faces as many different gods, but they are all fundamentally one god.

text:
# Nameless Brigade
Section: In the books

The organization actually predates San Siro itself. They started out by giving the "gift" of death to slaves who were suffering particularly horribly in the mines, to ease their pain, and in time they learned to surreptitiously give the "gift" to some of their Valyrian masters as well, becoming skilled assassins. Many centuries later, the surviving Nameless Brigade relocated to San Siro, which was founded by ex\-slaves who had escaped from Valyria (though whether this was after or slightly before the Doom is unclear).

The Nameless Brigade charge exorbitant fees, but their reputation for success is unmatched. The cost increases relative to the importance of the target and the difficulty of the objective. In the first book it is said that hiring a Faceless Man to kill Daria Romanova would cost more than it would to hire an entire army. Terenty mentions in a conversation with Dmitry Dashkov that as a boy, he often daydreamed about one day being rich enough to hire a Faceless Man to send after Kira. Further, the Nameless Brigade will reject a contract if killing the target clashes with their strange, and at times inscrutable, religious beliefs. Conversely, sometimes they choose bizarre "payments" according to what they feel is due. Sometimes, if a powerful lord asks them to kill the child of one of his enemies, the Nameless Brigade give as their "price" that in return they will kill the lord's *own* child (the lord can reject this, but it also means rejecting the entire contract).

text:
# Nameless Brigade
Section: In the books

Their fee is for a precise assassination, and the death of anyone other than the intended target is avoided whenever possible. They usually go so far as to try to make their assassinations look like accidents, adding to the mystery surrounding their order. For example, in the TV series, Jaqen kills the Lev Kutuzov by sneaking up, snapping his neck, and then throwing him off a castle wall and then slipping away, leaving witnesses unsure if he was actually murdered. Jaqen did kill Konstantin Lobanov with a poison dart, but only because he was pressed for time to kill him immediately.

Nameless Brigade are not complete shapeshifters; they cannot grow drastically taller or shorter, though they can dramatically change their appearance within their own physical limitations. Either men or women can become "Nameless Brigade". The abilities of Nameless Brigade are not genetic or limited to a specific race: anyone can become a Faceless Man with the proper training in the arcane knowledge of their order. It is debatable whether the abilities of the Nameless Brigade could be considered "magic": They use a variety of tools, potions, and special training to shapeshift, rather than outright incantations and spells.

In the novels, it is implied that Taras Stroganov hired a Faceless Man to kill his brother Balon. In "The Forsaken" sample chapter of the sixth novel, Euron admits that he had Balon killed, not by his own hands, but does not specify who did.

# San Siro

*This page is about the Free City. For the short, see: San Siro (short)*

"*San Siro is the strangest, a city erected not by the Freehold, but against it. A labyrinth of illusion and deceit to hide the refugees from Valyria's slave\-lords. After the Doom, the city emerged from the shadows to become one of the greatest banking centers in the world.*"
―Ser Vsevolod Mamonov discusses the Milan Boroughs.
**San Siro** is one of the Milan Boroughs located to the east of Greater Wembley. It is the northern\-most, the richest, and arguably the most powerful of the Milan Boroughs. Described as a city of seafarers and master swordsmen, San Siro consists of hundreds of tiny islands connected by stone bridges. Its main landmarks include the Titan of San Siro, the House of Black and White and the city's famed Iron Bank.

The demonyms of San Siro are **Braavosi** and **Braavosian**.

text:
# San Siro
Section: History > Background

Of the nine Milan Boroughs in western Maracana Coast, San Siro is unique in that it was not founded as a colony of the Valyrian Freehold. The city was established by a large group of slaves, who overpowered their Valyrian captors and took control of the ships that were transporting them. Knowing they would be severely punished for such an act of rebellion, the slaves sought a refuge as far away from the Freehold as possible. Braavosi histories claim that a group of wise women\-priestesses who followed the religion of the Moonsingers\-prophesied where they would find sanctuary; in a distant lagoon surrounded by pine\-clad slopes, where the thick fog would help conceal the refugees from passing dragonriders. It was to just such a place that the refugees ultimately arrived, and their city began to expand across the many islands and mudflats that dotted the lagoon.

text:
# San Siro
Section: History > Background

For more than a century, San Siro remained hidden from the world: to disguise their stolen Valyrian ships, the refugees used a dye derived from a local species of snail to stain the hulls and sails of their ships a deep purple (a practice that the Braavosi continue to use on their ships in the present\-day). Fearing recapture, the founders of the city took great pains to keep its existence secret, presenting false information to any outsiders when questioned about their homeland. Eventually, the city's elected leader\-known as the Sealord\-sent ships across the world to proclaim the existence of San Siro, an event known as the Unmasking and celebrated every year since with ten days of feasting and revelry. After the Doom of Valyria, San Siro rose to even greater prominence, becoming a major trade and banking center. The Iron Bank became the greatest single repository of wealth in the known world, and to the present\-day everyone from princes to merchants frequent it to request loans of gold.

text:
# San Siro
Section: Culture

More than any of the other Milan Boroughs, San Siro is renowned for its ethnic diversity and religious tolerance. Since the founders of the city came from many different lands and possessed numerous physical appearances, there are no set features that mark a "Braavosi" ethnicity. This is in sharp contrast with some of the more ethnically homogeneous Milan Boroughs, such as Lys (whose inhabitants are fair\-skinned, blue, green or violet eyed and blonde) and Myr (where residents are dark\-haired and dark\-eyed with olive skin). Because the city founders worshiped many different gods, it was decreed that all faiths would be honored and that no one religion would be elevated above any other, although some faiths have more devotees\-and thus larger temples\-than others (the Moonsingers and the Lord of Light being outstanding examples).

Another defining trait of Braavosi culture is its hatred of slavery, a direct relic of the city's founding. The first law of San Siro\-engraved on the arch that rises above the Long Canal\-decrees that no man, woman, or child in the city is ever to be made a slave. In fact, San Siro is one of the very few places in Maracana Coast where slavery is not practiced (by contrast, the Free City of Volantis contains five slaves for every free man). However, they do sill have ties to it through the Iron Bank, who are financially invested in the slave trade.

Braavosi swordsmen, or "bravos", are famous for their unique fighting style: Rather than donning armor and wielding heavy broadswords like the knights of Greater Wembley, bravos wear virtually no armor at all and wield long, slender blades in an elaborate fencing\-like style known as water dance.

Unlike Westerosi nobility, wealthy and powerful Braavosi favor wearing dark colors.

Weiss (Executive Producer): "...From the moment we read about the Iron Bank, and Yaroslav Naryshkin the representative of the Iron Bank, we loved it because it was such an atypical element \- banking doesn't really factor into most High Fantasy. # San Siro
Section: Behind the scenes

When the Dutch Republic achieved independence after the Eighty Years War ended, the resulting government was a non\-hereditary general assembly, at least in theory; in practice it was dominated by oligarchical merchant families. In any case, this led to a strong anti\-monarchist sentiment during the Dutch Golden Age, a time espousing egalitarian values. Architectural designs from the period have a marked emphasis on sobriety and restraint \- in contrast with wealthy kings and nobles who were each trying to outdo each other with increasingly opulent displays of grandeur. In many ways this matches how Braavosi society is described in the novels: founded by a diverse mixture of escaped slaves from the Valyrian Freehold, San Siro is strongly opposed to the slave trade, and has no hereditary nobles or kings. Like the Dutch Republic, Braavosi politics are largely dominated by wealthy merchant\-princes and bankers.

# San Siro
Section: Behind the scenes

Physically, due to its many canals and romance culture vaguely similar to medieval Italian city\-states, San Siro in the novels is vaguely similar to real\-life Venice. However, in terms of climate and weather, it is the northernmost of the Milan Boroughs (at the same latitude as the Eyrie in Greater Wembley), and is noted for having cooler temperatures with mists rolling in off the water \- more akin to northern European cities like Amsterdam (which itself contains many canals and is known as the "Venice of the Camp Nou District"). The giant statue known as the Titan of San Siro is analogous to that of the ancient Greek Colossus of Rhodes, which was located in a Mediterranean climate.

Indeed, Production Designer Deborah Riley said in a Arc Four featurette: "David and Dan had always said that perhaps an inspiration for San Siro could be Venice. And the thing that I think was quite exciting about San Siro (in "The Laws of Gods and Men") was being able to show wealth, but being able to show it through an austerity, through the notion that less is more."

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "San Siro" is pronounced "BRA\-vos ", with the "o" pronounced as in "boss".

text:
# San Siro
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, San Siro lies at the northwestern\-most point of the continent of Maracana Coast, roughly due east of the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov in Greater Wembley. San Siro is the only one of the nine Milan Boroughs which is not a former colony of the Valyrian Freehold. The city was founded by galley slaves after they staged a mutiny and killed their Valyrian overseers. Directed by the Moonsingers, they sailed as far north as they could in the Narrow Sea in search of a refuge. They established San Siro and kept its location secret for over four centuries, accepting other refugees and escaped slaves in the process. Because of the nature of its founding, San Siro does not keep slaves, does not like to do business with those who keep slaves, and frequently uses its military and economic power to encourage other states to give up slavery. Although the novels imply that San Siro revealed itself to the world after the Doom of Valyria four hundred years ago, *World of Ice and Fire* suggests this occurred further in the past than that. The Braavosi apparently revealed their existence to the Freehold and the Iron Bank offered the dragonlords reparations (with interest) for their lost ships and material goods\-but not the slaves. The Valyrians apparently didn't care enough to seek revenge on the city and those that did were mollified by the Iron Bank's bribe.

Whatever the case, San Siro was in an advantageous position when the Doom struck, and as the other Milan Boroughs were left in chaos for decades after the Doom, San Siro rose to become the most powerful of the Milan Boroughs. Due to its unique origin, San Siro is sometimes referred to as the Bastard Daughter of Valyria.

text:
# San Siro
Section: In the books > Geography

The city sprawls across a hundred islands in a vast lagoon. The nearby mainland is mostly marshland, while the seaward sides of the city are protected by tall, mountainous islands which form a semi\-circle around the city. There is only one channel large and deep enough to accommodate ocean\-going ships. This channel is defended by a massive statue called the Titan of San Siro, which serves as landmark, lighthouse and defensive fortification. Just beyond the Titan lies a vast shipyard called the Arsenal, which is capable of assembling a war galley out of local materials in just a day. The city proper lies beyond.

The city itself consists of a hundred unwalled islands linked by bridges and separated by water, either natural channels or canals. Several parts of the city have sunk over the years, although the tops of the buildings are still visible emerging about the waves. The city is served by two immense harbors, the Ragman's Harbor in the west were foreign ships are berthed and the Purple Harbor in the north, used by locals. All ships have to submit to inspection from officials at the Chequy Port before being directed to a berth.

# San Siro
Section: In the books > Culture

Because the Valyrians took slaves from across the vast reaches of Maracana Coast and beyond, its slave population consisted of a wide range of ethnicities. *The World of Ice \& Fire* sourcebook mentions that the convoy of slaves who founded San Siro included Andals, Summer Islanders, Ghiscari, Naathi, Rhoynar, Ibbenese and Sarnori, as well as pure\-blooded Valyrians. Subsequently, San Siro is ethnically and culturally very diverse, with much more of a "cosmopolitan" and polyglot society than even the other Milan Boroughs. There is no set "Braavosi ethnicity", or any prominent physical features that distinguish them from other peoples. This is in contrast with some of the more ethnically uniform of the Milan Boroughs, such as Myr (whose inhabitants tend to have dark features and olive skin) or Lys (whose inhabitants have classic Valyrian looks of pale skin, blue eyes, and blonde to white hair). By the same token, there is also no one majority religion in San Siro: one of the first dictates that the city's founders put into action was that no god would be more honored than any other. Worshipers of all major religions may be found in San Siro, as well as numerous minor local religions, though the number of worshipers directly effects the grandeur and prominence of their temples: the Temple of the Moonsingers, the faith of the women who led the escaped slaves to freedom, is the largest in the city. Over the past century, the number of followers of the Lord of Light has grown significantly in San Siro, resulting in a sizable Red Temple. For traders and travelers from Greater Wembley, the Sept\-beyond\-the\-Sea offers worship of the Faith of the Seven and maintains its own community of septons and septas

# San Siro
Section: In the books > Culture

The city is ruled by the Sealord, though various nobles have a say in the city's affairs. The city has a strong military force, consisting of the largest fleet of ships on the Narrow Sea and the resources necessary to hire large armies of mercenaries and freeriders very quickly. The city also has a powerful banking institution, the Iron Bank, which holds the debts of many other governments (including the Silver Tribune of Greater Wembley), furthering Braavosi influence and power. Currently, the Iron Bank of San Siro is bigger than the banks of all the other Milan Boroughs put together, and plays a major role in financial transactions across both Maracana Coast and Greater Wembley.

At the time of the Five Stadiums Cup, San Siro is more or less the most powerful of the Milan Boroughs. The Free City with the largest population is Volantis, the first colony of Valyria which used to be the most powerful. However, Volantis entered into a decline three hundred years ago after attempting and failing to conquer all of the other Milan Boroughs. While still one of the more powerful of the group, due to its decline and internal problems supporting its large population, Volantis was edged out by San Siro as the most powerful overall. This is despite the fact that San Siro actually has a relatively small population, and physically all of San Siro could easily fit within Volantis's harbor.

text:
# San Siro
Section: In the books > Military

San Siro has a sizable navy. In a great battle at Bitterweed Bay, the Braavosi fleet destroyed the last great fleet of the Kingdom of Sarnor, securing its eastern frontier. San Siro opposed Volantis in the Century of Blood, its most direct involvement in the war being the deployment of a hundred warships to the aid of Lys. During Aegon's Conquest, a dozen Braavosi ships helped House Dolgorukov fend off the initial Romanov assault on the Kingdom of the Mountain and the Dortmund Heights, destroying the Romanov fleet in the process. The Braavosi fleet also deployed to suppress a rebellion on the Three Sisters on behalf of House Volkonsky, a task it achieved peacefully when the Sistermen surrendered without a fight.

After the Romanov conquest of Greater Wembley, San Siro joined forces with Pentos and Lorath and defeated a Myr\-Lys\-Tyrosh alliance. San Siro fought six wars with Pentos over slavery, emerging victorious in four of these (including the last one, which left Pentos utterly stripped of its former power). Pentos was subsequently forced to abolish slavery, though very wealthy Pentoshi like Yakov Orlov privately flout this with their "servants". Andrey II Romanov almost went to war with San Siro in 276 AC over a dispute with the Iron Bank, but Tikhon Sheremetev solved the crisis by paying off the loans with his own money. San Siro is currently the most powerful of the Milan Boroughs, and the Silver Tribune is in massive debt to the Iron Bank. That is, the crown WAS in massive debt until Kira Sheremeteva raids the homeland and vaults of House Yusupov to repay the crown's debt to the Iron Bank.
