text:
# San Siro
Section: In the books > Locations

San Siro sprawls across a hundred small islands in the lagoon, connected by numerous bridges, while the larger islands are criss\-crossed by networks of smaller canals. For this reason horses are a rare sight in the city, and small boats are the fastest means of travel from one point in the city to another. There are also few trees in the city (except in gardens of the wealthy), nor is there brush and thatch to weave into roof coverings, so buildings in San Siro are typically made entirely of stone.

The only opening in the lagoon large enough for sea\-going ships to enter is defended by the Titan of San Siro, to the northwest of the city. Ships that sail under the Titan and continue in a straight line will reach the main waterway through San Siro, the Long Canal, which roughly divides the city in half. The Long Canal widens out when it reaches the heart of the city, forming its own interior artificial harbor, dotted with a few smaller islands which numerous temples are located on (due to their central location), among them the House of Black and White. Large ocean\-going ships cannot sail onto the Long Canal itself, due to the shallow water and numerous bridges.

Instead, two major harbors along the outer edges of San Siro service ocean\-going ships: the Purple Harbor on the northern side (proceeding left after passing the Titan), and Ragman's Harbor on the western side (to the right side after passing the Titan). Only Braavosi ships are allowed to use the Purple Harbor, while foreign ships have to use Ragman's Harbor (making the latter a much more rough and dirty neighborhood).

# San Siro
Section: In the books > Locations

- One large district runs along the entire western side of the Long Canal, with Ragman's Harbor on its outer western edge. The large number of foreign sailors trafficking here make it a more rough and working class section of the city \- though still prosperous and bustling with activity \- San Siro has its rich and poor sections, but not a truly massive slum district comparable to Flea Bottom in Wembley. The parts that actually border the central harbor are grander and inhabited by wealthier merchants. Arina Volkonskaya spends much of her time in this district around Ragman's Harbor (in part because she is still learning to speak Braavosi and more people in this section know the Common Tongue of Greater Wembley).
- The eastern side of the city from the Long Canal is itself roughly bisected by the smaller Green Canal, which also leads into the central harbor. The northeastern district is the most splendid part of the city, where most of the rich and powerful live: the Purple Harbor, the Sealord's Palace, the Iron Bank of San Siro, and the Hall of Justice are all located here. Accordingly, the northeast district is noted to have the best inns, taverns, and brothels in the entire city.
- Across the Green Canal, the southeastern district of the city is less noteworthy. Like the northwestern district, the parts of this section near the inner harbor itself are inhabited by several powerful families, but south of that, the region called the "Silty Town" is described as having small and unimportant buildings.

Section: In the books > Locations

The large aqueduct known as the Sweetwater River enters the city at the western side of the southern exit to the Long Canal. However, it only runs over the southernmost tip of the large western district, before crossing over the Long Canal into the southeastern district, then makes a long curve northwards along almost the entire length of the eastern side of the city. In the southeast district, it forms the divide between the Silty Town and more well\-to\-do area bordering the central harbor to the north. The aqueduct then crosses over the Green Canal, and continues all the way to near the Iron Bank itself, where it terminates at the Moon Pool.

- San Siro is heavily inspired by some Renaissance Europe's mercantile republics, of which Venice is the most famous. Due to its northern climate, it also has several parallels with Antwerp or Bruges (see "Behind the Scenes" above). Martin mentioned Amsterdam as a particular inspiration for San Siro' many canals after first visiting the city in 1990\.

text:
# San Siro
Section: In the books > Inspiration

- In spite of this, the historical development of San Siro has some loose parallels with ancient Athens. San Siro is actually located on very poor swamp lands, and does not actually produce many of its own products for export: the Braavosi economy is based on banking, and maintaining a large merchant fleet which transports goods between the different Milan Boroughs and Greater Wembley. The ancient Athenian historian Thucydides, writing in the fifth century B.C., pointed out that Athens was also located on lands which were actually poor relative to other parts of Greece, yet it rose to dominate much of the rest of Greece. Thucydides theorized that because Athens started out on poor lands, it wasn't a frequent target of foreign invasions, while other more wealthy cities were constantly being invaded or fighting trade wars. Thus while these other cities may have been physically richer, they could not capitalize on this raw wealth, while poor Athens enjoyed enough long\-term political stability that it eventually became a major hub for the development of regional commerce. Similarly, San Siro is relatively small, and has few natural resources, but because it wasn't reliant on Valyria it enjoyed political and economic stability during the Century of Blood, the hundred years of constant civil wars between the Milan Boroughs following the Doom of Valyria. Because San Siro was so stable, its banks and shipping became the most reliable, until it dominated commerce throughout the rest of the Milan Boroughs.

# Silver Tribune

*This page is about the throne. For the episode, see: The Silver Tribune*

"*The breath of the greatest dragon forged the Silver Tribune...the swords of the vanquished, a thousand of them, melted together like so many candles...*"
―Vladimir Romanov
The **Silver Tribune** was the throne upon which the King of the Andals and the Rhoynar and the First Men sat, located in the throne room of the San Siro District in the city of Wembley. Besides the monarchs themselves, only their Hand could sit on the Silver Tribune. *This page is about the throne. For the episode, see: The Silver Tribune*

"*The breath of the greatest dragon forged the Silver Tribune...the swords of the vanquished, a thousand of them, melted together like so many candles...*"
―Vladimir Romanov
The **Silver Tribune** was the throne upon which the King of the Andals and the Rhoynar and the First Men sat, located in the throne room of the San Siro District in the city of Wembley. Besides the monarchs themselves, only their Hand could sit on the Silver Tribune. The Silver Tribune was also a metonym, along with "the crown," referring to the monarchy that rules the Greater Wembley and the authority of the monarchy (e.g. "rebellion against the Silver Tribune").

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Background

The Silver Tribune was forged at the order of Aegon the Conqueror, the first of the Romanov Kings, who conquered six of the seven independent kingdoms of Greater Wembley and unified them under his rule \- the seventh kingdom of Azteca South was later joined through a marriage alliance. The throne was allegedly forged from the 1,000 swords that had been surrendered to Aegon in his conquest by the lords who had offered their fealty, though the actual number of the swords in 300 AC is fewer than two hundred. These were subsequently melted down by the fiery breath of Aegon's dragon, Balerion the Black Dread, then beaten and bent into a throne of imposing appearance, asymmetrical and surrounded by swords protruding from the ground, the steps being decorated with twisted steel. At some point during or prior to the reign of the Iron Regent, many of the swords that made up the Silver Tribune were removed and the throne was given a safer and more symmetrical design.

At some point during or prior to the reign of the Iron Regent, many of the swords that made up the Silver Tribune were removed and the throne was given a safer and more symmetrical design.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Background

At the end of Rodion's Rebellion, during the Sack of Wembley, as the Sheremetev army overran the city outside of the San Siro District, Aerys refused to surrender, and secretly ordered the city to be burned to the ground with hidden caches of wildfire. To prevent this, Yakov killed the Iron Regent in front of the Silver Tribune itself. Greatly disturbed at having killed the king he had taken the most sacred oaths to defend, Yakov then sat down on the Silver Tribune and gave no thought to the carnage going on outside. Hours later, the main rebel army arrived in the city, and Eduard Volkonsky came to the throne room, where he found Yakov sitting on the throne. Years later, Kira chided Eduard that he could have tried to seize the throne then and there, instead of letting Rodion take it, but he did nothing. Eduard never knew why Yakov really killed Aerys, and seeing him seated on the Silver Tribune like that gave Eduard the incorrect belief that Yakov hoped to seize the throne himself some day.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > House of the Fire Falcon : Arc One

After a Stadium Board concludes, Rhaenyra and Ser Harrold head to the throne room, where they find Prince Daemon sitting on the Silver Tribune. Ser Harrold is shocked by such disrespect, but Rhaenyra, used to her uncle's flippancy, is more amused. Rhaenyra and Daemon converse in High Valyrian, with Daemon, in his own words, noting the irony of Viserys throwing a tournament for his benefit (since until Viserys actually has a son, Daemon is his heir by law) before gifting his niece a bejeweled necklace of Baltic alloy.

King Viserys I Romanov confronts Daemon in the throne room, seated upon the Silver Tribune, the Romanov sword Blackfyre in his hand, surrounded by his Kingsguard. Viserys angrily demands to know if Daemon truly mocked his nephew as the "Heir for a Day". Outraged by the insult, Viserys declares his intention to publicly name his heir. When Daemon insists he is his brother's heir, Viserys retorts "*Not anymore"* and orders Daemon to return to his wife's seat in the Dortmund Heights. When Daemon steps forward to protest, the Kingsguard draw their swords and block his path, and Daemon grudgingly withdraws.

Before a gathering of the realm's nobility, including the lords of Velaryon, Obolensky, Volkonsky, and Orlov, Viserys bears witness as the nobles declare oaths of fealty to him and to Rhaenyra as his named heir.

# Silver Tribune
Section: History > House of the Fire Falcon : Arc One

Four years later, a full courtroom of nobles assemble before the Silver Tribune, as Viserys puts on his full regalia to formally receive his wayward younger brother. Daemon jauntily enters the throne room, not only still carrying Dark Sister sheathed at his hip, but playfully tossing the war hammer of Craghas Crabfeeder in his hand \- and wearing his own crown, made of bone and driftwood. As he reaches the base of the throne, Lord Commander Harrold Westerling draws his own sword and points it slowly into Daemon's chest plate to ward him off. The tension breaks when Daemon throws the war hammer on the ground in front of the Silver Tribune and says to add it to the chair (made from the melted weapons of their defeated enemies). Harrold sheathes his own sword, and Viserys points out that Daemon is wearing a crown, inquiring if he also calls himself king. Daemon says that his men hailed him as "King of the Narrow Sea" after he led them to smash the Triarchy's forces and conquer the Stepstones, but he quickly adds that he knows that there is only one true king. Daemon then kneels and offers up both his crown and the Stepstones to his older brother. Viserys asks what became of Corlys Velaryon, and Daemon says he sailed back home to Driftmark (not bothering to present himself at the royal court, due to his rift with Viserys). Viserys also asks who now holds the Stepstones, to which Daemon replies the tides, the crabs, and the corpses of 2000 Triarchy corsairs left staked on the shore as a warning to any who might follow Drahar's example

# Silver Tribune
Section: History > House of the Fire Falcon : Arc One

Still several hours later, a somewhat more sober Daemon stumbles through the gates of the San Siro District, only to be immediately seized by Harrold Westerling and two other Kingsguard, to bring him to an audience with the king. The guards roughly drop the still semi\-coherent Daemon onto the floor of the throne room. The guards leave, then Viserys appears from a side doorway. He accuses that Daemon defiled his daughter and gives him a swift kick in the ribs, asking if he will even attempt to deny it. Viserys bitterly accuses that it's not Rhaenyra that Daemon wants, but the Silver Tribune. Viserys rises, and dismissively tells Daemon to go back to the Dortmund Heights and his lawful wife, and to try to restore what scrap of honor he may have left; or not, it makes no difference to him, as he never wants to see Daemon again.

The feast is held in the throne room itself. Envoys from all the major noble houses of the realm are announced in turn by Ser Harrold Westerling as they enter, such as Lord Jason Sheremetev and Lord Hobert Obolensky (with the notable absence of Otto). Viserys and Rhaenyra sit at the middle of the high table set up in front of the throne's base and receive each in group, though Queen Alicent is noticeably late and has yet to arrive. By the end Joffrey has been beaten to death. Later that evening, Laenor and Rhaenyra are married in a private ceremony while Joffrey's blood is still warm.

# Silver Tribune
Section: History > House of the Fire Falcon : Arc One

During an audience in the throne room, with Otto Obolensky sitting on the Silver Tribune as Tribune Steward owing to King Viserys being bedridden, Vaemond makes the case that he is a true Velaryon and the closest kin of Corlys whereas Rhaenyra's sons are not. Before Rhaenyra has time to make her own case, Viserys enters the throne room to the surprise of everyone present and takes charge of the proceedings. Realizing that he has no chance of convincing the king to disinherit his own grandchildren, Vaemond becomes irate and aggressive, shouting that Rhaenyra's children are bastards and calling Rhaenyra herself a "whore." Vaemond's slander of the royal family is deemed to be treason and Viserys threatens to remove Vaemond's tongue himself. Before he is able to, Daemon decapitates him from behind using Dark Sister.

Otto has the nobles present at court herded into the throne room and informs them of Viserys's purported change of his successor, insisting they bend the knee and swear allegiance to Aegon. Lord Merryweather and Lady Fell refuse to break their oaths to Rhaenyra and are imprisoned. Lord Allun Caswell feigns allegiance.

# Silver Tribune
Section: History > House of the Fire Falcon : Arc Two

Aegon II formally sits on the Silver Tribune to hear the daily petitions from commoners of the city. He is flanked by his cronies Martyn Reyne, Leon Estermont, and Eduard Waters. Aegon is polite and even sympathetic to the petitioners, as he desperately wants approval as a good king, but he is inexperienced at rule and his grandfather Otto keeps correcting him. Later in the evening, Aegon is drinking with his cronies after a stressful day of petitions.

Later, Queen Helaena confronts Prince Aemond in front of the Silver Tribune asking if it was worth the price at the Battle at Rook's Rest.

# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Septa Aksinya Dashkova quizzes Sofia on her history lessons while walking through the throne room, asking her who built the Silver Tribune. Sofia correctly answers that it was Aegon the Conqueror.

Viserys tells Viktoria Lomonosova that the Silver Tribune was made of the swords of the vanquished.

Since the king is out hunting, Eduard sits on the Silver Tribune while listening to royal petitioners, in his capacity as Tribune Steward. He hears a report from a peasant refugee that the Mountain has been raiding villages in the Mersey Grounds.

Following Rodion's death, his alleged son Joffrey takes his place on the Silver Tribune.

Far away on the eastern continent in Vaes Dothrak, Daria urges her husband Demid Odoevsky to help her win back the Silver Tribune that her own father once sat upon, for her and Demid Odoevsky's unborn son that she carries inside her. At first, Demid Odoevsky is not very interested: Greater Wembley is very far away, across the ocean, and to the Dothraki it seems just like a literal chair (without all of the connotations of authority over the Greater Wembley associated with it). After a failed assassination attempt on Daria by one of Rodion's agents, however, Demid Odoevsky is deeply offended, and vows to attack Greater Wembley and take the Silver Tribune for Daria and their son, Rhaego.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Joffrey continues to jauntily sit on the Silver Tribune as the Five Stadiums Cup tears apart the realm. He gets up from the throne to menace the captive Sofia with a crossbow, idly considering shooting her, before relenting that his mother insists she remain alive \- so he simply orders his Kingsguard to beat and strip her in front of the entire court.

Meanwhile, at La Bombonera Island to the east, Stepan declares that the Silver Tribune is his by right, and all who deny that are his foes.

During the Wembley Final, just as the battle seems to be turning against the city's defenders, Kira goes to the throne room to sit on the Silver Tribune herself, while holding Tommen sitting on her lap. Together they await what she fears will be their end, and gets ready to give essence of nightshade to Tommen and herself to painlessly kill them both \- as if Stepan is victorious he will have them both tortured to death. In the nick of time, however, her father Tikhon enters the throne room along with Loras: the main Sheremetev army along with reinforcements from House Yusupov arrived at the last moment and repulsed Stepan's assault, winning the battle.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Feodora Yusupova, in typical fashion, has a low opinion of the throne itself, blithely referring to it as "that ugly iron chair."

Littlefinger remarks to Dmitry Dashkov that the Silver Tribune doesn't literally have thousands of swords in it, he has counted and the real number is under two hundred. He says that this is another inflated legend, part of the pageantry and propaganda that supports kings and dynasties but which is, in fact, illusory.

Joffrey later summons Tikhon to the throne room. Joffrey asks for a report of the Stadium Board meetings, and Tikhon invites him to attend the Stadium Board meetings. Joffrey squirms as Tikhon approaches the throne, and then asks for information on the rumors about Daria Romanova and her dragons. Tikhon confirms the rumors are true, and Joffrey demands to know what is being done about it. Tikhon tells him it is not his concern, and he should leave such matters to his advisers.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: History > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Euron presents Yuriy Repnin, the captain of the Golden Company, before Kira, who sits atop the Silver Tribune.

When she learns the truth of Ivan's parentage, Daria is upset to realize Ivan is the rightful heir to the Silver Tribune, having spent years believing it was her birthright and working toward it. Ivan tells Daria he doesn't want it and will refuse if anybody tries to press his claim.

After setting fire to most of Wembley and its people, Daria enters the throne room and touches the Silver Tribune, after years of seeking to claim it. Ivan tries to urge her off her path of destruction. Daria is resolved, sincerely believing she is justified in her actions and is certain this is the way they build a better world, by destroying the old one and those loyal to it. Ivan pleads with her to be merciful to the people but Daria is committed to her way of achieving her vision of a better world. To save Greater Wembley and its people, Ivan assassinates Daria and weeps as he holds her body in his arms. Following this, Drogon arrives and directs his flames not at Ivan, but the Throne, and melts it down. He bellows in grief as he flies away with Daria's body. All that remains of the Silver Tribune is a mound of melted debris.

After setting fire to most of Wembley and its people, Daria enters the throne room and touches the Silver Tribune, after years of seeking to claim it. Ivan tries to urge her off her path of destruction. Daria is resolved, sincerely believing she is justified in her actions and is certain this is the way they build a better world, by destroying the old one and those loyal to it. Ivan pleads with her to be merciful to the people but Daria is committed to her way of achieving her vision of a better world. To save Greater Wembley and its people, Ivan assassinates Daria and weeps as he holds her body in his arms. Following this, Drogon arrives and directs his flames not at Ivan, but the Throne, and melts it down. He bellows in grief as he flies away with Daria's body. All that remains of the Silver Tribune is a mound of melted debris.

# Silver Tribune
Section: Behind the scenes

George R.R. Martin expressed in his blog that the appearance of the Silver Tribune in *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune* isn't what the Silver Tribune looks like in the world of the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels.

In the TV series, the Silver Tribune is the size of a very large chair, is reasonably symmetrical, and Littlefinger remarks in Arc Three's "The Climb" that it doesn't literally contain thousands of swords, he has counted and there are under two hundred.

Martin explained that the physical proportions of the Silver Tribune in the books, as well as the throne room it is set in, are simply unfilmable due to their massive size. The throne room in the books is the size of St. Peter's Basilica at the Vatican, and the Silver Tribune itself towers over forty feet in height. The book version of the Silver Tribune *actually does* contain a thousand swords, taken from Aegon the Conqueror's fallen enemies, and the visual symbol of subsequent Romanov kings who sat atop that many swords of vanquished foes was a truly awesome sight to behold. Even the actual seat where the king sits is located over twenty feet off of the ground, and needs to be reached by an entire flight of stairs.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: Behind the scenes

The Silver Tribune is so large that it is *physically impossible* to move it. Aegon I eventually decided to raze the boomtown that had grown up around the site of his army's landing camp, a ramshackle town of wood and earth called "The Aegonfort", so that he could start over from scratch and construct a more permanent new capital city, Wembley. The San Siro District itself and the throne room had to be built *around* the preexisting Silver Tribune. The construction took many years and would continue long after his death, so in the meantime, he relocated the royal court to his ancestral castle on La Bombonera. It was impossible to move the Silver Tribune, however: when Aegon I died his son and successor Aenys had to travel to the unfinished construction site of Wembley to be crowned on the Silver Tribune, before then moving back to La Bombonera. This is also why no one ever tried to steal the Silver Tribune and take it elsewhere during civil wars, i.e. when one side or the other seized the capital during the Dance of the Fire Falcons, or during Rodion's Rebellion, no attempt was made by the defenders to sneak the throne out of the capital along with other royal emblems such as the king's crown.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: Behind the scenes

Moreover, Martin made the point that the Silver Tribune in the books was hammered together by blacksmiths, not sculptors and artisans, so it does not fit together neatly: rather, it is a sprawling and twisting asymmetrical stack of swords welded together into a vague throne\-shape and towering into the air. Aegon the Conqueror did "build" the Silver Tribune in that he commissioned it, and more specifically in that he used the fire of his dragon Balerion to melt down the swords and make them malleable, after which the blacksmiths would take them and add them to the growing construct.

Martin was nonetheless entirely sympathetic to the practical necessities faced by the TV production team: the throne room as he envisioned it may be the size of St. Peter's Basilica, but the TV series already films in the largest studio set in all of Europe, the Paint Hall in Belfast. He acknowledged that the book version of the Silver Tribune is so massive it would have difficulty fitting in any set, and even if it did, it might visually detract from the drama for the king to be holding conversations with people on the ground a full forty feet away from him. Martin also stated that he actually very much enjoys the design used for the Silver Tribune in the TV series \- it simply would have been physically impossible to replicate the towering edifice he described in the books.

In 2013, Martin pointed out a painting by Marc Simonetti (see at right) as coming closer than any previous artwork to what the Silver Tribune and the throne room look like as Martin envisions them in the books.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: Behind the scenes

In 2013, Martin pointed out a painting by Marc Simonetti (see at right) as coming closer than any previous artwork to what the Silver Tribune and the throne room look like as Martin envisions them in the books.

In 2014, a small replica of the TV series's Silver Tribune was given to Elizabeth II, Queen of the United Kingdom, on a visit to Paint Hall. The Queen declined an invitation to sit upon the actual Silver Tribune prop, although she was photographed inspecting it and other props from the series. As David Benioff later explained, she did not sit on the Silver Tribune prop because "Apparently the Queen of England is not allowed to sit on a foreign throne \- This is an esoteric rule we didn't know about until that moment." D.B. Weiss agreed that this seemed odd because the prop is a *fictional* throne for a fictional kingdom.

A Arc Four blooper reel revealed that during the trial scene in "The Laws of Gods and Men", Charles Dance (Tikhon) gripped the pommel of one of the swords making up the Silver Tribune so hard (because Tikhon is angry) that it accidentally snapped off \- he then looked down at it in his grip and swore, embarrassed that he had just broken the Silver Tribune prop.

For *House of the Fire Falcon*, the throne was redesigned to have a more menacing appearance and to be more true to George R.R. Martin's original vision. Designed by Jim Clay, the new throne stands 2 feet taller than the one in *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune* and is surrounded by approximately 2,000 swords, variously bent, melted, and protruding.

text:
# Silver Tribune
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, the Silver Tribune is reportedly uncomfortable to sit upon due to the blades that radiate out from it, occasionally cutting the incumbent. The moral lesson Aegon intended for his heirs was that no ruler should ever sit upon the throne carelessly, just as they must not rule carelessly. The Silver Tribune specifically contains the swords of those Aegon defeated in battle, but not of those who had surrendered honorably rather than give battle. As such, no swords from the Camp Nou District or the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov were included in the Silver Tribune thanks to Torrhen Volkonsky and Sharra Dolgorukov.

Aerys's increasing insanity over the years led him to absentmindedly sit upon the throne with his full weight, frequently cutting and injuring himself. Ultimately he cut and scraped himself so much upon the Silver Tribune that his personal enemies derisively referred to him as "King Scab", besides of his more common epithet, "the Iron Regent". This was seen by some as a sign of his unworthiness to rule.

At the end of Rodion's Rebellion, Aerys was slain by Yakov at the foot of the Silver Tribune itself. Yakov proceeded to wait out the rest of the sack of the city by Sheremetev soldiers, and waited in the throne room for the late arrival of Eduard Volkonsky and the main rebel army. Eduard's most powerful memory of the event was arriving in the throne room to find Yakov sitting on the Silver Tribune, his sword at his side still covered in Aerys' blood, with the Iron Regent's corpse lying in a pool of his own blood in front of the throne. On seeing Eduard, Yakov got off the Silver Tribune, joking that he was just keeping it warm for Rodion.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya

"*I did what I had to do to survive, my lady. But I am a Volkonsky. I will always be a Volkonsky.*"
―Sofia to Anastasia Mamonova
Queen **Sofia Volkonskaya** is the eldest daughter of Lord Eduard Volkonsky and his wife, Lady Ekaterina, sister of Roman, Arina, Boris, and Alexei Volkonsky, and "half\-sister" of Ivan Morozov; though truthfully he is her cousin.

Initially betrothed to Prince Makar Orlov, the heir to the Silver Tribune, Sofia travels to Wembley in preparation for her nuptials, but essentially becomes a hostage of House Sheremetev following the execution of her father on trumped\-up charges of treason. Under the (sometimes unwitting) tutelage of Kira Sheremeteva, Faina Yusupova, and Daniil Bestuzhev, Sofia becomes well\-versed in politics and court intrigue, but suffers all the same.

Even after escaping the capital and returning to her childhood home of Anfield, she endures further hardship at the hands of House Baryatinsky. After escaping from Anfield with the help of her father's former ward, Timofey Stroganov, and her sworn\-sword, Elena Tatischeva, Sofia reunites with Ivan at Wembley Park. Along with the support of the Free Folk, the knights of the Dortmund Heights, and certain Northern houses, the two of them retake Anfield from Radomir Baryatinsky, and Sofia becomes the Lady of Anfield, whilst Ivan is declared King in the Camp Nou District.

Displeased at Ivan for abdicating his title in favor of House Romanov, she finds enmity with Queen Daria, who refuses to accept Northern independence in her restoration and quest for the Silver Tribune. Following the Battle of Wembley and Daria's subsequent assassination, Sofia declares the Camp Nou District an independent kingdom and is later crowned Queen in the Camp Nou District.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Background

Sofia Volkonskaya is the eldest daughter and second child of Lady Ekaterina and Lord Eduard Volkonsky, the Keeper of Camp Nou District.

Sofia was born and raised at Anfield. She has an older brother, Roman, two younger brothers, Boris and Rickon, a younger sister, Arina, and a "bastard half\-brother" Ivan Morozov, with whom she had a distant relationship due to her mother's influence (which, like her mother, Sofia later regretted). Sofia enjoys proper "lady\-like" pursuits and is good at sewing, embroidering, poetry, singing, dancing, literature, etiquette, history, and music. When she was young she dreamed of being a queen like Kira Sheremeteva, and that just like in the epic songs she would meet her knight in shining armor. She has inherited her mother's Trubetskoy coloring, and Lady Ekaterina thought Sofia will be even more beautiful than she was when she was younger. She is often seen in contrast with her sister Arina, who has neither her looks nor her accomplishments in feminine activities and comportment.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

At the Inn at the Crossroads beside the Kingsroad, Joffrey offers to walk Sofia along the riverbank after the disquieting experience of meeting Ser Fedor Panin, the king's headsman. They find Arina practicing her swordsmanship with Mycah, a butcher's son, and Joffrey starts to hurt him for acting above his station and striking a girl of noble blood. Arina strikes Joffrey, and when the prince threatens her with his sword, Arina's direwolf, Nymeria, intervenes and bites Joffrey's arm. Arina and Mycah flee and Joffrey cries before snapping at Sofia to get him help. Sofia is taken before Rodion and his retainers and asked to corroborate Joffrey's claim, that he was the victim of an unprovoked attack. Arina tells her to tell the truth, but to Arina's fury, Sofia is worried about upsetting her betrothal with Joffrey, so she says that it happened too fast for her to know. Kira orders that Arina's direwolf be executed for harming Joffrey, but when the direwolf cannot be found, she suggests that Sofia's own direwolf Lady be substituted for Nymeria. Sofia and Arina are horrified Lady will be killed and protest. Eduard, furious with Rodion for agreeing to this, carries out the execution himself, to Sofia's anguish.

Arriving in Wembley, Sofia's enmity towards Arina and her father continues. Eduard fails to mollify Sofia by buying her a doll as she had outgrown dolls. Eduard explains to Arina that Sofia could not defy Joffrey or go against his version of events if Sofia wished to maintain his goodwill in marriage.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Sofia has a nightmare that she is being stabbed by her attackers from the riots. She wakes up to find her mattress bloodied by the onset of her first period. Nina Suvorova tries to help Sofia conceal the evidence as it means she is ready to bear Joffrey's children. The Hound catches them and (reluctantly) informs the Queen. Kira gives Sofia advice on motherhood, reassuring her that even if she never loves Joffrey, she will love her children with him. However, Kira tells Sofia not to love anybody except for her children, "The more people you love, the weaker you are."

Stepan Orlov sails his fleet into the bay outside Wembley, triggering the Wembley Final. Sofia is summoned to the throne room to say goodbye to Joffrey. He forces her to kiss his new sword and she subtly undermines his bravado. She then takes refuge in Maegor's Holdfast with Nina Suvorova where Kira is hosting the women of the court there. Kira mocks Sofia's faith and reveals Fedor Panin is present to kill them all if the walls are breached. She drunkenly advises Sofia to use her sexuality as a weapon. Eventually, Kira storms out, believing the battle lost. Sofia attempts to keep the morale of the women up with prayers and singing.

Later, Nina Suvorova tells Sofia to return to her chambers and bar her door to keep her safe should Stepan breach the keep. Sofia finds Sandor waiting for her inside. He tells her that he is going north and offers to take her with him. She is reluctant to leave the potential safety of being rescued by Stepan but he warns her that all men are killers. Stepan's force is ultimately defeated by a host of House Sheremetev and House Yusupov reinforcements led by Tikhon Sheremetev.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Sofia and Nina Suvorova sit on the docks watching ships arrive and depart. Sofia wants to play a game making up stories about where the ships are headed, but Nina Suvorova, in typical fashion, is uninterested. Sofia tells Nina Suvorova that she enjoys the game because the truth is either "terrible or boring." Bestuzhev arrives and tells Sofia of a new role that he has taken which will allow him to leave Wembley, and offers to smuggle her out of the city. She is hesitant about the idea.

 Sofia discusses the possibility of Littlefinger being in love with her, but Nina Suvorova warns her that Bestuzhev is manipulative and men usually want "one thing" from young ladies. Margaery and her grandmother Feodora Yusupova invite her to lunch in the gardens, where they ask her about Joffrey, after being escorted by her chambers by Loras. Sofia is initially too fearful to speak the truth, but eventually breaks down, her eyes blazing, and angrily recounts how Joffrey had said he would show her father mercy, only to behead him in front of her, and how he then took her up to the wall and forced her to look at her father's head on a spike. Sofia nervously attempts to backtrack, but Olenna tells her that they will never betray her confidence. Sofia admits that Joffrey is a "monster."

While the daughter and sister of traitors, Sofia is a very valuable hostage. If Roman Volkonsky dies, she becomes "the key to the Camp Nou District" as the Lady of Anfield, greatly increasing the power of whichever house she marries into. To prevent Littlefinger from gaining power, Dmitry Dashkov suggests to Olenna that a Yusupov marry Sofia.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

While she prays at the Red Keeps's godswood under guard, Margaery comes and talks to her, telling her that they should see Highgarden, the Yusupov home, together. Sofia replies that Kira would never allow her to leave Wembley. Margaery tells her that she could be wife to her brother, and this idea pleases Sofia.

In the castle gardens, Sofia and Margaery watch Loras spar with his squire. Sofia confidently remarks on his fighting ability, and inquires when she and Loras will wed, as per the Yusupov plot to keep her out of the hands of Bestuzhev and/or the Sheremetevs. Margaery replies that she will "plant the seed" of the idea after she and Joffrey are married. Sofia is skeptical Joffrey will let her go but Margaery is confident he will do it to please her, once she is his wife. However, Loras begins a sexual relationship with his squire, whom he tells of his engagement. Ignat Gagarin then passes that information on to his employer: Littlefinger. A short time later, Littlefinger meets with Sofia, offering her a place on his ship that will take him from the capital to the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov. Sofia practices lying for a change, and tells him that they should wait until after Joffrey's wedding, primarily because she fears for *his* safety if the plan fails. A master manipulator, Littlefinger is clearly suspicious of her motives, but doesn't press the matter for the moment. Instead, he says he is touched by her concern for his safety, and insists that she call him "Petyr."

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

The plan to wed Sofia to Loras fails when Kira grows increasingly suspicious of the Yusupovs and learns of the proposed marriage between Loras and Sofia through Daniil Bestuzhev. This news prompts Tikhon to arrange for Kira to marry Loras and Terenty to marry Sofia in order to curb the ambitions of House Yusupov and to bind two of the other great houses of the Greater Wembley closer to the Sheremetevs.

Still unaware of this plan, Loras and Sofia spend more time together in the following weeks, though Sofia is far more enthusiastic about their impending marriage than he is. Loras admits he's always wanted a big wedding with many guests, fancy food, and a good tournament, though he only seems to remember that there will be a bride when Sofia gives him an expectant look. One subject where they do find common ground is their shared hatred of Wembley, with Loras declaring the capital to be "the most terrible place there is."

Terenty decides he might as well dash Sofia's hopes sooner rather than later. He goes to Sofia's chamber and asks for a private word, but Sofia declines to dismiss Nina Suvorova. Terenty gives Nina Suvorova a carefully coded apology for not telling her in private before breaking the news to Sofia. As she watches Littlefinger's ship depart for the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov, Sofia is devastated to realize that both of her chances to leave Wembley have gone, and she has no choice but to marry into the family that killed her father and is keeping her hostage.

Sofia remains despondent over the deaths of her mother and brother. Despite encouragement from Nina Suvorova and Terenty, she refuses to eat, even declining her favorite lemon cakes. She tells Terenty that she lies awake all night thinking of how Ekaterina and Roman died, how Roman's body was desecrated, and how Ekaterina's body was dumped into the river. Sofia excuses herself from the table, saying she is going to the godswood. When Terenty offers that prayer can be helpful, Sofia reveals that she no longer prays \- the godswood is the only place she can go where nobody talks to her. While in the godswood, Sofia is watched by Yakov and Brienne, and later finds herself being followed by someone.

Sofia remains despondent over the deaths of her mother and brother. Despite encouragement from Nina Suvorova and Terenty, she refuses to eat, even declining her favorite lemon cakes. She tells Terenty that she lies awake all night thinking of how Ekaterina and Roman died, how Roman's body was desecrated, and how Ekaterina's body was dumped into the river. Sofia excuses herself from the table, saying she is going to the godswood. When Terenty offers that prayer can be helpful, Sofia reveals that she no longer prays \- the godswood is the only place she can go where nobody talks to her. While in the godswood, Sofia is watched by Yakov and Brienne, and later finds herself being followed by someone.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Sofia attends a breakfast held before the wedding of Joffrey and Margaery. There, Joffrey is presented with a gift from Tikhon: the second sword re\-forged from Ice, the recently\-destroyed ancestral sword of House Volkonsky and which had been used spitefully to kill her father. Sofia shoots the sword a grim look of understanding when this occurs, and is shocked when the sword is turned on Terenty's gift to Joffrey, a copy of *The Lives of Four Kings*. Joffrey names his new weapon Widow's Wail, commenting that he will be reminded of Eduard Volkonsky's beheading each time he uses it. Sofia looks on in obvious grief.

At the end of the wedding itself, Sofia comments bitterly that "we have a new queen." Terenty encourages her to look on the bright side: at least she isn't Queen. Later, at the wedding feast, Olenna walks up to Sofia to offer her condolences over the Maracana Night and invites her to visit Highgarden sometime when things settle down. During the exchange, Olenna toys with Sofia's hair and Homyakov's necklace in a grandmotherly fashion.

Meanwhile, Joffrey amuses himself with a farcical "reenactment" of the Five Stadiums Cup, with each king being played by a dwarf. The dwarf playing Roman wears a wolf's head that is eventually knocked off by the dwarf playing Joffrey. Sofia again looks on in grief. When Terenty makes a veiled reference to his nephew's cowardice during the Battle of Blackwater, a furious Joffrey pours wine over his uncle's head and orders him to be his cupbearer to humiliate him further. Joffrey drops his goblet on purpose and then kicks it under the table when Terenty tries to pick it up. Sofia, seemingly feeling pity for Terenty, picks up the goblet and hands it to him.

At Sofia's behest, she and Terenty try to leave, but Joffrey calls them back and demands Terenty bring him the cup again. Terenty grudgingly obliges but unbeknownst to everyone, Olenna had slipped some poison into Joffrey's cup. The poison had come from one of the stones on an unaware Sofia's necklace, which Dontos had given her and Olenna fiddled with earlier, allowing Olenna to retrieve the poison. Later, as Joffrey lies dying from being poisoned, Leonid Homyakov approaches Sofia and encourages her to leave in order to save her life, a suggestion Sofia takes to heart.

After the events of the Purple Wedding, Sofia and Dontos make a quick escape and get on a boat, leaving the city. Dontos takes Sofia to a ship which turns out to belong to Daniil Bestuzhev. Bestuzhev has Dontos killed to guarantee his silence and destroys the necklace Sofia was wearing. Sofia screams and asks why he killed Dontos. Bestuzhev simply states that Dontos was working solely for money and that now, she is safe.

Petyr visits Sofia in her cabin and Sofia deduces that he was involved in Joffrey's death. After he tries to deny it, he simply ends up telling her everything about the wedding. Sofia is confused because of everything that the Sheremetevs have done for him and tells him that she doesn't believe that he would risk his life just to confuse the Sheremetevs. In response, Bestuzhev states that he would risk anything to get what he wants. She asks him what he wants and he vaguely says "everything."

Sofia and Petyr are walking towards the Bloody Gate and Petyr educates Sofia on the Eyrie and its defenses. Sofia uses the disguise as Petyr's niece so no one knows who she is. When they enter the main hall, Sofia greets her aunt Lysa as Alayne, but Lysa interrupts her saying that she already knows who she is. However, Sofia cannot call Lysa 'Aunt' in front of anyone apart from Lysa, Petyr, and Sofia's cousin Robin, Lysa's son. Despite this, a joyful Robin offers Sofia a tour of the rest of the Eyrie.

Later that night, an annoyed Sofia can't sleep due to Lysa's constant screaming from consummating her marriage to Petyr. The next day, Lysa brings Sofia lemon cakes and tells her that Petyr brought three crates from the capital for Sofia. She tells Sofia a story about Ekaterina when she was young, getting fat off how much sweet food she had, which makes Sofia feel self\-conscious. She stops, but Lysa tells her to carry on. Lysa abruptly turns antagonistic, accusing her of having sex with Petyr. Sofia panics and tries to assure Lysa that she is a virgin. Lysa disregards this, grabbing her hand and squeezing hard. Sofia starts crying while saying that all Petyr says that she is a stupid little girl, with stupid dreams, who never learns and is a terrible liar. Lysa puts on a polite face again and assures her that it is all alright and after Terenty is executed she can marry her cousin Robin. Sofia is not sure what to make of this.

# Sofia Volkonskaya

After settling into the Eyrie, albeit with discomfort, Sofia wanders into the courtyards alone, as the snow falls around the Dortmund Heights. The snow, reminding her of home, prompts her to build a snow castle resembling Anfield. She has a short\-lived friendly conversation with Robin before she snaps at him for ruining her snow castle. This results in a heated confrontation between the cousins, which ends in Robin running back inside, crying after Sofia slaps him. Petyr presents himself shortly afterward, and Sofia questions him as to why he really had Joffrey killed. She allows herself to smile slightly when he claims that he did it for Ekaterina, the only woman he ever loved. Sofia is shocked when he kisses her on the lips, which Lysa witnesses. She summons Sofia to the High Hall, where she sits over the open Moon Door. Sofia begins to grow concerned when Lysa comments on how far the drop is to the ground. Lysa, enraged over Petyr's interest in Sofia, threatens to have her killed and nearly manages to push her out of the Moon Door to her death before Petyr intervenes. Sofia watches as he tells Lysa that he only ever loved Ekaterina, before pushing her to her death.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Sofia, as "Alayne," is called to testify before Lord Rodion Panin, Lady Evdokia Witte, and Ser Roman Kornilov before Bestuzhev can get to her, much to his chagrin. Sofia quickly reveals her true identity and relates the tale of her captivity and flight from Wembley. She then proceeds to truthfully tell of Lysa's mental instability, jealousy, and death, changing only a few small details (she kissed Littlefinger on the cheek and Lysa threw herself through the Moon Door). Sofia breaks down in tears and the lords are convinced, but while none of them are looking, she gives Littlefinger a stony, almost triumphant gaze; this indicates she is finally playing the ruthless contest of tribunes.

 Later, Bestuzhev visits Sofia and asks why she lied on his behalf. Sofia explains that she has no idea what Royce and Witte would want from her if Littlefinger were eliminated, but she knows exactly what he wants. Later on, as Littlefinger and Robin prepare to depart on a tour of the Dortmund Heights, Sofia accompanies them, appearing with noticeably darker reddish\-brown hair and garbed in a feathered black dress with a plunging neckline.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Sofia, still under the alias Alayne, attends a sword jousting session for Robin at Runestone, along with Littlefinger and Rodion Panin, visibly unimpressed with Robin's sub\-par skills at swordsmanship. Sofia notices that Littlefinger receives a raven message. Soon after, they leave Robin in the care of Lord Royce, for further training. On the carriage ride, Sofia questions Petyr as to why they are heading west when Lord Royce was told they would be traveling to the Fingers, unsure of his source of distrust. Petyr promises her that they are going somewhere far away, where Sofia will be safe from Queen Kira.

On their journey, Sofia and Bestuzhev stop for lunch at an inn, where she tries ale for the first time. Sofia can't see what all the fuss is about, although the entire episode is designed to catch Littlefinger off\-guard so she can ask about the raven\-message he received back at Runestone. Bestuzhev doesn't answer the question beyond indicating that the old saying "dark wings, dark words" doesn't apply in this instance. Shortly thereafter, Brienne appears unexpectedly and declares herself for Sofia. Bestuzhev doubts that Sofia would want a sworn shield who let both of her previous masters die, even when Brienne reveals the true, somewhat unbelievable circumstances of Renly's death. Sofia seems inclined to agree with Littlefinger, pointing out that Brienne was present at Joffrey's wedding, to which the warrior replies that neither of them wanted to be there. Sofia rejects Brienne's offer of service and watches as she quickly defeats the guards and escapes.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Sofia and Bestuzhev eventually arrive at the ruins of Moat Cailin, where Sofia learns that they are actually returning to Anfield and Bestuzhev's plan is to have her marry Radomir Baryatinsky, the recently legitimized son of Ruslan Baryatinsky, the current Keeper of Camp Nou District. Sofia is initially reluctant to marry into yet another family that betrayed hers, but Bestuzhev pacifies her by claiming it will be an opportunity for her to avenge her family.

They arrive at Anfield, where Bestuzhev introduces Sofia to the Baryatinskys. Ruslan and Radomir greet Sofia politely, and after a tense moment during which she is repulsed merely by looking at Ruslan, Sofia greets them with courtesy, while Anna Golitsyna, Radomir's secret mistress, eyes Sofia with jealousy. She is later brought back to her old room by a servant, who welcomes her home and tells her that "the Camp Nou District remembers." While walking through Anfield's courtyard, Sofia unknowingly passes Timofey Stroganov, who had been her father's ward she and her siblings grew up with at Anfield. Timofey hides his face from her as she passes.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Settling into life at Anfield, Sofia visits the Volkonsky family crypts, re\-lighting the votive candles and cleaning up the offerings left by visitors prior to Anfield's fall. Littlefinger finds her regarding the statue of her long\-dead aunt Anastasia Volkonskaya. Littlefinger, with minimal commentary, tells Sofia of the events at the tourney at Harrenhal, where Rhaegar unhorsed Ser Egor Suvorov, passed by his wife, and gave Lyanna a crown of flowers blue as frost, all to the shock of the crowd. He then tells Sofia that he's been recalled to Wembley and that keeping Kira waiting much longer would be unwise. Littlefinger explains parts of his master plan to Sofia: Stepan will inevitably take the Camp Nou District, and when he does, he will need a Volkonsky at Anfield. Littlefinger is certain Stepan will declare Sofia the Wardeness of the Camp Nou District. Even if Stepan fails, Radomir is already betrothed to Sofia, and thus Sofia, who has learned to manipulate from the very best, can take control of House Baryatinsky from within.

Sofia's maid brings a message to her. Consoling Sofia that she still has allies in the Camp Nou District, she tells Sofia to light a candle in the highest window of the Broken Tower if she's ever in trouble. As Sofia wanders around the castle, she runs into Anna Golitsyna. Anna Golitsyna puts on a friendly façade, talking to Sofia about her mother's demise. To help Sofia "remember" how things used to be while her family was still living in Anfield, Anna Golitsyna leads Sofia down to the kennels. In the kennels, Sofia finds "Reek" asleep in one of the cages. Awoken by Sofia's arrival, he just shakes his head when Sofia calls him Timofey. He warns her that she shouldn't be down there. Seeing Reek in such a pitiable condition, Sofia angrily storms away.

At dinner, Radomir is initially well\-behaved, toasting his wedding to Sofia, but is soon back to his old self as he forces Reek to apologize to Sofia for murdering Boris and Rickon. With much difficulty, Reek finally mutters an apology. Radomir suggests that Reek be the one to give Sofia away at the wedding since he is the closest thing Sofia has to kin; Ruslan accepts this suggestion. Ruslan and Walda announce Walda's pregnancy, upsetting Radomir, which in turn delights Sofia.

On the night of her wedding, Anna Golitsyna draws a bath for Sofia, during which she advises Sofia not to bore Radomir, and tells her about the fates of Violet, Tansy, and a third unseen girl named Kyra, examples of girls who Radomir murdered for sport. When Anna Golitsyna mentions that both she and Radomir killed Tansy by hunting her, Sofia becomes angry, asking Anna Golitsyna how long she has been in love with Radomir and if she really expected Radomir to marry her. She coolly tells Anna Golitsyna that she is a Volkonsky of Anfield and will not be intimidated so easily by her, and dismisses her to finish her bath herself, though she is visibly shaken by Anna Golitsyna's story.

Later, when Timofey comes to fetch Sofia for the wedding, she refuses to hold Timofey's arm. Timofey pleads for her to do so, revealing that Radomir will punish him if she doesn't. Sofia coldly asks if he thinks she cares what Radomir does to him, and strides past him. Reek then gives Sofia away to Radomir, and they wed in front of the Godswood, in a ceremony officiated by Ruslan and attended by many Northern lords. Sofia hesitantly takes Radomir as her husband, her eyes down, unable to look him in the eye.

Though Sofia addresses him as Timofey throughout this conversation, Reek keeps repeating his name is Reek, forcing Sofia to grab him by the face and look him directly in the eye. Sofia attempts to escape during the battle between the Baryatinskys and Stepan Orlov by picking the lock on her door with the corkscrew and lighting the candle in the tower. However, Brienne and Podrick don't see the candle due to being distracted by Stepan's army. In the process of trying to escape, Sofia runs into Anna Golitsyna and Timofey, with the former aiming a bow at her. Anna Golitsyna says that she has come to escort Sofia back to her chambers, and Timofey initially begs Sofia to go with her. Though Sofia is visibly frightened, she stands her ground and refuses to go with Anna Golitsyna, saying, "If I'm going to die, let it happen while there's still some of me left."

 A bemused Anna Golitsyna briefly lowers her arrow and admits Radomir needs her alive in order to secure his hold on the Camp Nou District. But Anna Golitsyna adds Radomir doesn't need Sofia in one piece to do that, just the "parts" that he needs to produce his heir. Anna Golitsyna maliciously nocks her arrow again and prepares to at least maim Sofia with it. Before she can release it, however, Timofey grabs Anna Golitsyna, making her fire and miss, and throws her off the battlement, killing her instantly on impact. Timofey and Sofia then escape Anfield by jumping off the side of Anfield's walls, hoping to survive the long fall by landing in the deep snow.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

After escaping from Anfield, Sofia and Timofey flee into the Wolfswood, with the Baryatinsky forces in hot pursuit. They cross a stream and briefly take shelter under an uprooted tree, where Timofey hugs Sofia to keep her warm. Shortly after, however, they are found by the Baryatinsky men and hounds. Timofey urges Sofia to flee to the safety of her half\-brother Ivan at Wembley Park. but Sofia refuses to leave Timofey behind to the Baryatinskys. Brienne and Podrick appear just in time and fight off the soldiers, killing them all. Brienne once again offers her service to Sofia, who this time readily accepts, reciting her vows.

On the way to Wembley Park, Brienne reveals to Sofia how she briefly met Arina near the Bloody Gate. Sofia is delighted to hear that her sister is still alive and well. Timofey decides to part with the group and head to the Barra da Tijuca. Sofia implores Timofey to come with them as Ivan will protect them from Radomir but Timofey refuses, fearing Ivan will have him executed as Timofey betrayed Roman, beheaded their master\-at\-arms Ser Rodrik, and killed those two boys. Sofia promises Timofey she will tell Ivan the truth about Boris and Rickon being alive, that Timofey didn't kill them, and wants him to join the Anfield Guard so all his crimes can be forgiven. Timofey responds he still killed two farm boys and reminds Sofia of his crimes against House Volkonsky, for which Ivan will never forgive him. He reveals he does not want to be forgiven as he can never make up for his crimes against Sofia and Ivan's family. When Sofia realizes that Timofey cannot be convinced to come with them, she bids him farewell, and the two share a tender hug.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Sofia, Brienne, and Podrick arrive soon at Wembley Park where they find Ivan. At first, both "siblings" are too stunned to even speak when they see each other, but quickly share a loving embrace after their long and tragic separation. As Ivan offers Sofia food, they reminisce about their happy childhood and how they both regret ever leaving Anfield. Sofia apologizes to Ivan for her dismissive treatment of him while growing up, to which Ivan responds that there is nothing to apologise for. When they resolve to stick together, Sofia says the only place they can go now is home. She then asks him to help her reclaim their home from the Baryatinskys. However, Ivan tells her that he is tired of fighting, that he had done nothing but fight since he left home, and that he was killed for it. Although Sofia appears to accept his choice, she tells him that she will reclaim Anfield and the Camp Nou District, with or without his help.

As Sofia and Ivan share a meal with Platon Tolstoy, Semyon Apraksin, Podrick, and Brienne, a messenger arrives from Anfield with a letter from Radomir. In the letter, Radomir states that he has Rickon prisoner at Anfield and if Sofia is not returned, he will slaughter every wildling under Ivan's protection, let his men rape Sofia, and feed Ivan and Rickon to his dogs. Radomir signs the letter 'Lord of Anfield and Keeper of Camp Nou District,' prompting Sofia to reveal Radomir killed his father.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

When Semyon Apraksin asks Sofia how many Radomir has in his army and Sofia recalls 5,000, Ivan asks Semyon Apraksin how many he has who are able to fight. Semyon Apraksin replies that they have only 2,000 men and women in shape to fight, not enough to match Radomir's five thousand. Sofia tells Ivan that the houses of the Camp Nou District will unite behind him as the son of the last true Keeper of Camp Nou District and they need to go back to Anfield to save it and their brother. Ivan agrees to take Radomir down so they save Rickon and take back their home.

Later, Sofia receives a letter from Petyr asking to meet in Mole's Town. Accompanied by Brienne, they meet in a ruined house, and Sofia angrily tells Bestuzhev the details of her wedding night, asking if he knew the truth about Radomir all along. Instead, Bestuzhev changes the subject, informing Sofia he has rallied the Knights of the Dortmund Heights to help her, along with news that her great\-uncle Brynden has recaptured Riverrun. Sofia takes an alliance with the Blackfish into consideration, but refuses help from Bestuzhev, warning him never to speak to her again. She says she has an army. Petyr responds it's her brother's army and adds, "Half\-brother."

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

At a war meeting at Wembley Park, Sofia and Ivan discuss which of the Northern houses they can rely on to support them. As the Vyazemskys and Uvarovs have already sided with House Baryatinsky, Ser Davos suggests asking House Milyutin. When Ivan decides to rally the two dozen houses still loyal to the Volkonskys, Sofia informs him they can add House Trubetskoy to the list, but lies about how she acquired the information. After the meeting, Sofia plans to send Brienne to Riverrun, as the Baryatinskys could intercept any raven sent there. Brienne is worried about leaving her and while Brienne feels Ivan is trustworthy, she is dubious about the other men. Sofia assures Brienne that Ivan will keep her safe, he is her brother and she trusts him. Brienne counters by asking Sofia why she lied to Ivan about meeting with Bestuzhev. Before riding south, Sofia gives Ivan a new cloak she had made for him styled after their father's.

Sofia and Ivan arrive at Bear Island and are summoned before Anastasia Mamonova. Ivan asks for the assistance of House Mamonov in the upcoming battle for Anfield to help them save their brother, as House Mamonov has pledged themselves to House Volkonsky. However, Lyanna tells him that he is a Snow and Sofia is a Baryatinsky. Sofia says that she did what she had to do, but she didn't want it. When Sofia attempts to flatter Lyanna and Ivan explains how he served under Lyanna's uncle Lord Commander Luka Mamonov, Lyanna wants them to get to the point. Ser Davos steps in and manages to convince Lyanna to pledge her allegiance, telling of the coming threat of the Frost Wanderers, however, a mere sixty\-two men are contributed.

Sofia and Ivan later travel to Deepwood Motte, to ask for the assistance of House Gorchakov. They receive a frosty reception from Egor Gorchakov, who has just reclaimed Deepwood Motte from the Ironborn. When Ivan fails to bring him around. Sofia tells Robett that the Gorchakovs are pledged to House Volkonsky, and sworn to fight when called upon. Robett responds he pledged to House Volkonsky and fought for Roman Volkonsky but it cost the Gorchakovs their home and many lives, due to Roman's lack of stability following his marriage to Talisa. Sofia and Ivan are only able to recruit a few Northern houses and only gain a few hundred men. Ivan says they should strike Anfield immediately before the coming storm and before Radomir can gather more men. Sofia says they don't have enough men and wants to go to Castle Chertkov to try and persuade Lord Chertkov, however, Ivan reflects on their lack of time. When Ivan refuses to change his mind, Sofia writes a letter to an unknown party (but does not tell Ivan) for reinforcements.

Sofia and Ivan meet with Radomir on the day before battle. Radomir tries to taunt Sofia, but she remains stoic. She asks Radomir how do they know if he truly has their younger brother Rickon. Smalljon answers her question by throwing the decapitated head of Rickon's direwolf Shaggydog into their view. As Radomir proceeds to tell the Volkonskys what to do if they want to save Rickon, Sofia cuts him off by telling him that he is going to die the next day and rides off.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

After a meeting where Ivan discusses battle plans with Semyon Apraksin and Davos, Sofia admonishes Ivan for attacking with too few men, saying that they need a larger force. Ivan agrees they don't have enough men but responds this is the largest army they could possibly gather, saying they have pleaded with every house who would have them and the Blackfish can't help. Sofia warns Ivan that Radomir won't fall into Ivan's trap, Radomir is the one who lays traps, and Radomir has been playing with people all his life. Ivan responds he has faced worse than Radomir Baryatinsky, to which she replies, "You *don't* know him!" When Ivan asks how do they get Rickon back, Sofia tells him will never get him back alive. Ivan refuses to give up on their brother and Sofia tells Ivan that Radomir wants him to make a mistake. Ivan asks Sofia what he should do differently but Sofia responds she doesn't know about battles and implores her brother not to do what Radomir wants him to do. When they finish arguing, Sofia tells Ivan that if Radomir wins, she will die before she goes back to him. Ivan vows to protect Sofia, to which she cynically replies that no one can keep anyone safe.

Sofia is not present during the premise of the Anfield Derby, in which Rickon is killed by Radomir. As the battle is nearing an end and all hope seems lost, a distant horn is heard sounding in the distance. Sofia and Daniil Bestuzhev (to whom Sofia had sent the raven) arrive with the Knights of the Dortmund Heights to help Ivan and his army reclaim Anfield. The Dortmund Heights forces run down the advancing Baryatinsky forces.

After Anfield is breached, Sofia enters the Anfield courtyard and witnesses Ivan defeat Radomir in single combat, though Ivan momentarily goes into a wild frenzy and begins to pummel Radomir, he spares Radomir out of respect for Sofia. With the Volkonsky banners hanging in Anfield once more, Sofia sees Rickon's dead body, concluding to ask Ivan where Radomir is. Sofia confronts a bloodied and bound Radomir in the kennels. He tries to goad her by telling her how she will never be rid of him because he is "part of \[her] now." Although Sofia does not deny his implication that she herself will always remember him, she calmly retorts that his house is about to become extinct and that all memory of Radomir to the rest of the world will soon disappear, just before an ominous growl from one of his hounds reveals his impending doom. Radomir responds that his dogs are loyal to him, but Sofia reminds her husband that he revealed he had been starving his dogs for seven days. The dogs approach Radomir and he desperately attempts to order them to heel but after a brief moment of hesitation, one of the hounds bites him. As they begin to tear Radomir apart while he screams, Sofia walks away with a small smile.

Two guards inform Sofia that someone claiming to be her sister Arina is trying to gain access to Anfield. They brush the girl off as an impostor, revealing she asked for Arseny Apraksin and Anton Karamzin. Sofia instantly realizes it must be Arina and knows where she has gone. Sofia finds Arina where she expected, in the crypts looking over their father Eduard's grave. They are happy to see each other but so much has happened to both of them in the past few years that they are at first awkward, unsure of what to say. Arina asks if she has to call Sofia "Lady Volkonsky" now, to which Sofia firmly insists "Yes" \- and then laughs. They smile and hug, though still a bit unsure. Arina notes that Ivan left her in charge and smiles when Sofia says that she hopes Ivan will be back soon \- he will be so happy to see Arina, remembering how happy Ivan was to see her when they were reunited.

The reunited sisters then look sadly on their father's grave statue. Arina says it doesn't really look like him. Sofia acknowledges that everyone who really knew his face is dead. Arina points out they're not. Arina tells Sofia that everyone says Sofia killed Joffrey. Sofia explains she actually didn't, though she wished she had. Arina remarks that he was always at the top of her "list." This confuses Sofia, and Arina explains that she'd been keeping a list of everyone she was going to kill \- at which they both laugh. Finally, Sofia asks how Arina got back, but Arina only says her road wasn't a pleasant one. Sofia says her own road wasn't either. They hug again, earnestly and warmly. Sofia then informs Arina that Boris is home too.

Sometime later, Sofia and Littlefinger watch on silently from the walkway above as Arina and Brienne. However, still unsure of Petyr's intentions, Sofia visits Boris. From this, she learns of the Sight, in which Boris proves Petyr's ultimate guilt in the Five Stadiums Cup. Sofia stands on Anfield's ramparts as the combined Volkonsky and Romanov forces march towards the castle, and stares in cautious awe as Drogon and Rhaegal fly overhead. She greets Ivan as he arrives in the courtyard, and mentions that Arina is "lurking somewhere" when Ivan notices her absence. He introduces her to Daria as the Lady of Anfield, and the two women exchange a civil but tense greeting.

Later, in the castle's great hall, Sofia sits at the high table along with Ivan, Daria, and Terenty. Terenty tries to calm those present who are displeased at Ivan bending the knee to Daria; he says that they have assembled the largest army ever seen. Sofia coolly undercuts Terenty by asking how she is supposed to feed an army that size, as well as two full\-grown dragons. When she sarcastically asks what dragons eat, Daria replies, "Whatever they want."

Sofia later converses with Terenty privately for the first time since they last saw each other at Joffrey's wedding; Terenty calls the wedding "a miserable affair," though Sofia sardonically remarks, "It had its moments." She also calls Terenty out for believing that Kira will honor the pledge to send the Sheremetev forces north. She is disappointed in Terenty, saying she used to think Terenty was the cleverest man she ever met.

Sofia shows Ivan the message that Egor Gorchakov will be remaining in Deepwood Mordvinov with his troops, as he never pledged to fight for a Romanov. She expresses her disapproval of Ivan giving up his crown to Daria. Ivan replies titles don't matter in the face of the Midnight Regent and the army of the dead and they don't stand a chance against them without Daria's help. Although Sofia assures Ivan that her faith in his judgement has not waivered, she bluntly asks him if he truly bent the knee to save the Camp Nou District, or because he loves Daria.

When Yakov arrives at Anfield, Sofia \- now clad in armor \- is once again seated at the high table with Ivan and Daria. The two women harshly berate Yakov for his past actions and question whether his loyalty to their cause is genuine. Only when Brienne vouches for Yakov does Sofia trust him, and Daria allows his sword to be returned to him.

Later, Daria speaks privately with Sofia, addressing some of the thorny political issues involved in their alliance. When Sofia notes Ivan's love for Daria and is concerned Daria is manipulating him, Daria openly confesses her love for Ivan, assuring Sofia she has no ulterior motives. Although a greater understanding appears to develop between the two women, Sofia remains firm in her conviction that the Northerners will never truly accept an outsider as their ruler again, and bluntly asks Daria what her plans for the Camp Nou District are once the dead have been defeated.

Impressed by her logic, Terenty sardonically remarks that they should have stayed married. Sofia humorously acknowledges that he was the best relationship she ever had, but his loyalties to Daria would mean that they could never remain together, which is taken as an offence to Daria by Aksinya Uvarova. As the army of the dead breaches Anfield's walls, the Midnight Regent reanimates all that have fallen in the battle so far, and his spell extends to the many Volkonsky bodies housed in Anfield's crypts. The two look desperately into each other's eyes, and Sofia pulls out the dragonglass dagger given to her by Arina.

Before she can act, however, Arina manages to slay the Midnight Regent in the godswood, causing the entire army and the remaining Frost Wanderers to shatter and collapse. Sofia and the other survivors make their way out of the crypt to survey what remains.

The survivors of the battle later gather in front of Anfield's walls to light the funeral pyres of all who gave their lives in defense of the living. Sofia tearfully places a pin bearing the House Volkonsky direwolf onto Timofey's body before lighting his pyre herself. During the celebration feast that follows, she makes her way to the table where the Hound is seated.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

When she lived at Anfield with her family, Sofia grew up as the eldest daughter of a Great House, trying to emulate her mother's example of a "proper lady" from the southern courts. Sofia's devotion to the traditional, refined "feminine virtues" caused friction between her and her blunt, tomboyish younger sister Arina, with whom she had a sibling rivalry. As a little girl, Sofia naively believed in the tales and epic romances in which every princess gets her honorable knight in shining armor to sweep her off her feet. Sofia was infatuated with the traditional romances about mythical figures like Jonquil, and historical figures like Duncan Romanov. Her greatest goal in life was to be married to a heroic and handsome prince, sitting around with other noblewomen eating lemon cakes while gossiping about the goings\-on at court.

Sofia's innocent, childhood infatuation with the ideals of princesses and knights made her tragically susceptible to the manipulations of the Sheremetevs. She held the blind belief that all queens and princes are kind and truthful, as if inherently a result of their titles, when Kira just happened to be a woman who married a king to secure a marriage alliance, and Joffrey just happened to be her son. Without real cause, she blindly loved Joffrey with all her heart and trusted and admired Kira, only for them to repay her love and trust with cruel abuse, with Joffrey having her father beheaded before her very eyes.

Sofia's innocent, childhood infatuation with the ideals of princesses and knights made her tragically susceptible to the manipulations of the Sheremetevs. She held the blind belief that all queens and princes are kind and truthful, as if inherently a result of their titles, when Kira just happened to be a woman who married a king to secure a marriage alliance, and Joffrey just happened to be her son. Without real cause, she blindly loved Joffrey with all her heart and trusted and admired Kira, only for them to repay her love and trust with cruel abuse, with Joffrey having her father beheaded before her very eyes.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

Afterwards, Sofia has a harrowing experience as a prisoner of the Sheremetevs, a plaything for the psychopathic Joffrey to have publicly beaten by his guards for petty amusement. Her shock at the death of her father was only later deepened at the news of how her mother and brother Roman were horrifically killed at the Maracana Night and their corpses desecrated. She was visibly elated upon hearing that Arina, Boris, and Rickon were actually still alive, and though she took mostly after her mother and had a somewhat distant relationship with Ivan, she loved him all the same. She was surprised to hear that Ivan had become Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard, and Ivan was the first person she turns to for shelter after escaping Anfield, aware that he would protect her from Radomir.

Sofia subsequently escapes Wembley to the Dortmund Heights with Littlefinger, and her experiences have clearly changed her personality. She had to learn from painful experience how to lie to survive at Joffrey's court, saying one thing but meaning another and manipulating people to her own ends as best she could. No longer under constant control by Joffrey and Kira's guards, she is in her own way beginning to mature into her own power and influence as a political force.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

The numerous tragedies she has suffered, and the crimes against herself and her family, have also darkened her personality turning her more ruthless, though not quite cruel. This shows when she refuses to take Timofey's arm when he comes to escort her to the Godswood to marry Radomir and coldly asks if he thinks she cares what Radomir will do to him if she doesn't. She also later expresses approval of what Radomir did to Timofey, now Reek, and declares she would do the same. Once reclaiming Anfield, Sofia feeds her abusive husband, Radomir to his own hounds, even smiling as it happened.

However, despite all the suffering that she has been through, Sofia appears to have retained a certain degree of compassion that is also demonstrated in her multiple attempts at reaching out to Timofey after Timofey admits that he did not kill Boris and Rickon and they are alive. After Timofey helps her escape from Anfield, Sofia once again sees Timofey as a surrogate brother and promises she will not let Ivan execute him when Timofey fears Ivan will have him killed for his crimes. Sofia also becomes more compassionate and a loyal sister to Ivan and apologizes for being "awful" when they were children. When she faces Anna Golitsyna for the last time prior to her escape from Anfield, Sofia was about to allow the psychopathic girl to shoot her so that she could die with as much of herself as was remaining. She has also become significantly more brave, courageous and is developing nerves of iron.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

Sofia's sufferings have made her stronger and more mature, but also more war\-like. Caring less for the traditional feminine virtues she used to praise as a child, Sofia moves against Radomir in order to take back Anfield and the Camp Nou District, and outright rejects his conditions for saving her brother Rickon, knowing full well he would never keep his word and instead tells him that he will die the next day. Her experiences with the Sheremetevs have enabled her to watch in grim satisfaction as Radomir is torn apart and eaten by his own hounds. This contrasts her visible horror in Arc One upon seeing the violence when she first arrived in Wembley, where she is distressed at Leonid Kutuzov's violence against Ser Hugh and Savva Yusupov and faints when her father is abruptly beheaded in front of her.
