text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Personality

Due to the harrowing experiences of the Volkonsky children, Sofia experiences a development in the relationships with her surviving siblings when they are reunited. Though she and Ivan were the least close of the Volkonsky children, they love one another as siblings and their relationship as brother and sister become stronger when they are reunited. While Sofia will argue with Ivan, she speaks to him as an equal, wants to see him safe, and Turner observes Sofia's relationship with Ivan has restored Sofia's faith in men. While Ivan remains a protective older brother to Sofia and likewise wants her safe, he also recognizes Sofia's intelligence and her adeptness as a leader, placing the Camp Nou District in her charge as his regent. Sofia and Arina did not get along as children and though they love each other, experience a rocky start after their reunion in Arc Seven due to their experiences. Nonetheless, they come to recognize new strengths in one another: Arina's skills as a combatant and Sofia's abilities as Lady of Anfield. By the end of Arc Seven, their relationship grows stronger and they develop a new closeness as sisters. Sofia is relieved and happy to be reunited with Boris but is unsettled by the changes he has undergone as a result of becoming the Three\-Eyed Raven. Regardless, she asks for Boris's help in using his powers to look into Littlefinger's past and upon learning the truth, decide to put Littlefinger on trial to answer for his crimes.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: Behind the scenes

- Sophie Turner has naturally baby blonde hair. So to get that Trubetskoy red, her hair had to be dyed for Sofia's auburn (reddish brown) hair. Kevin Alexander uses a mix of four different watercolor shades. Since Turner was only thirteen or fourteen when she started on the show, Alexander didn't want to use peroxide on her. The color lasts about ten days and needs to be touched up constantly.
- After the filming of the episode in which Sofia's direwolf, Lady, is executed, Turner adopted the dog that played Lady, a Northern Inuit named Zunni. Series author George R.R. Martin confirmed this on his blog.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Sofia enjoys conventional "ladylike" pursuits, with a keen interest in music, poetry, singing, literature, history, dancing and embroidery. She was taught to play the High harp by Lady Leonette. She has a romantic notion of handsome princes and knights fighting honorably for love and loyalty. She is sharply contrasted with her far less idealistic and tomboyish younger sister, Arina. She is described as traditionally beautiful, taking after her mother's family with her high cheekbones, deep blue eyes, and thick soft auburn hair.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Due to a time jump which was originally planned in the books but later dropped, Sofia is only 11 years old when the narrative begins. Author George R.R. Martin himself has said that he would have aged\-up the younger characters had he initially known he would abandon the time\-jump. Therefore, in the TV series' timeline, all of the younger characters including Sofia have been aged up two years from the books. Thus, Sofia is 13 years old in Arc One, and 14 years old in Arc Two\. Keeping in mind that in medieval times, the age of maturity was lower than it is today, this younger age in the books isn't quite as unusual as it sounds, but due to the abandoned time jump, this still causes some discrepancies. For example, in the books, Joffrey's torment of Sofia doesn't have quite the same inherent sexual tension to it because they're both two years younger. Sofia directly states that she is 13 years old in dialogue from the pilot episode of Arc One\. On her wedding night with Terenty Sheremetev, however, she says that she is 14 years old when she should be 15 years old because it's been two years since the pilot episode. It is possible that she either simply had not reached her nameday and turned exactly 15 yet, or that she was lying to try to shame Terenty before he took her virginity (though as it turned out, Terenty still refused to consummate the marriage, morally repulsed at being forced to marry such a young girl).

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

A subplot in the books which is only somewhat alluded to in the TV series is that in her desperation, Sofia starts latching onto the idea of Lavr Kutuzov as her protector from Joffrey or a potential source of an escape attempt.

In sharp contrast to Arina, Sofia is very timid, passive and submissive, waiting for things to happen rather than take active actions. She steps out of her passivity only on rare occasions, like the time she intervened to save Ser Dontos or her momentary intent to kill Joffrey, but these are exceptions; during the entire time she was held captive at the San Siro District, she did not make even the slightest effort to find a way to escape.

In the books, Sofia is shown to be partially responsible for her father's arrest by revealing to Kira his plan to have his daughters leave the capital city. Given that she is only a naive eleven\-year\-old, and that Eduard didn't give her any explanation for why he wanted to send her away from Wembley, she assumed he was simply fighting with Kira over some matter of state. Still enraptured with the idea of staying and marrying Joffrey, Sofia thought that if she told Kira she would then smooth over whatever disagreement they had. Yet the main fault is Eduard's, for foolishly revealing his cards to Kira, and even more foolishly \- putting his trust in Littlefinger and revealing his plan to him. Thus Littlefinger and Kira knew what Eduard planned to do and had time to prepare counter\-measures, regardless of what Sofia told Kira.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

When dealing with cruel or frightening people, Sofia uses her courtesy as an armor, as taught by septa Aksinya Dashkova, but it does not protect her from Joffrey's cruelty. She is often beaten by any of the Kingsguard (except the Hound), whenever Joffrey feels she needs to be taught a lesson. On one occasion, Joffrey decides that beating Sofia is not enough, and orders Emelyan Derzhavin and Boros Blount to strip her; only Terenty's intervention prevents something worse.

Sofia technically gained the title of "princess" when her brother Roman was declared the new King in the Camp Nou District. While her brothers Boris and Rickon use the title of "prince" among the Northerners at Anfield, Sofia's storyline involves her being held as a prisoner at King Joffrey's court in Wembley. The Sheremetevs refuse to acknowledge the Camp Nou District's claims of independence so they don't refer to Sofia as "princess." Meanwhile, Sofia is in fear for her life and is subjected to frequent beatings at the hands of the Kingsguard at Joffrey's whim, so she doesn't refer to herself as "princess" for fear of angering her captors. Thus her title is rarely, if ever, invoked (unless Roman and Ekaterina in the Northern camp are discussing her captivity).

Unlike in the show, Sofia does not befriend Nina Suvorova and does not trust her. Nina Suvorova does whatever Sofia tells her, but sometimes, she gives Sofia insolent looks. Sofia has no idea why Nina Suvorova looks at her this way, for Sofia does not know Nina Suvorova is her husband Terenty's lover.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Following Sofia's escape from Wembley, Littlefinger takes her first to his ancestral home at the Fingers. There he reveals Sofia part of the scheme to murder Joffrey; he does not reveal what his motive was, nor why it was necessary to involve her in the scheme.

As a precaution, Sofia's hair is dyed black (as her auburn hair would reveal her as a Trubetskoy) and is given the alias of "Alayne Stone", Littlefinger's bastard daughter who recently decided to seek him out after having been entrusted to the Faith of the Seven. Sofia keeps her true identity hidden whilst in the Dortmund Heights; starting from her second POV chapter of *A Feast for Crows*, she is no longer described as "Sofia" in the text but as "Alayne," even in her own thoughts. In the show, she is introduced simply as "Alayne", a niece of Petyr, who makes only a vague attempt to hide her hair; she later dyes it of her own volition.

Sofia has no idea that Littlefinger was involved in her father's downfall, but knows well that he is treacherous and cannot be trusted. She separates "Littlefinger" from "Petyr" in her mind: Petyr is the kind man who saved her from the Sheremetevs, and who loved her mother, but she knows Littlefinger exists within him, and he was never her friend: she remembers him smiling slyly and whispering in Kira's ear; she reminds herself that whenever she was in danger, Terenty and the Hound were the ones who saved her, not him; she knows about his part in Ivan Dolgorukov's death (Lysa reveals that in her presence); she saw him killing two people \- Ser Dontos and her aunt \- the latter by his own hands.

text:
# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Sofia's near\-death experience demonstrates her submissive personality very clearly: when Lysa accuses her of seducing Littlefinger, all the courage Sofia gathered prior to the confrontation instantly vanishes. Lysa orders her to open the Moon Door, and she complies, foolishly thinking that her deranged aunt would let her go, thus nearly getting herself killed (though she puts up some fight). Only Littlefinger's intervention saves her.

In sharp contrast to the show, Sofia does not become full of confidence overnight following her aunt's death. She does not lie to the lords about Lysa's death at her own behest, but under the command of Littlefinger; she shivers in fear when Nestor Royce inquires about Lysa, barely managing to lie that Andrei Stolypin was the one who pushed Lysa to her death, and nearly faints when Littlefinger says "it was I who killed her" (as if talking metaphorically); during the meeting with the Lords Declarant, she is overcome with fear when Rodion Panin looks at her closely and asks "Do I know you, girl?" (it is unclear if he recognizes her).
body:
Sofia's near\-death experience demonstrates her submissive personality very clearly: when Lysa accuses her of seducing Littlefinger, all the courage Sofia gathered prior to the confrontation instantly vanishes. Lysa orders her to open the Moon Door, and she complies, foolishly thinking that her deranged aunt would let her go, thus nearly getting herself killed (though she puts up some fight). Only Littlefinger's intervention saves her.

In sharp contrast to the show, Sofia does not become full of confidence overnight following her aunt's death. She does not lie to the lords about Lysa's death at her own behest, but under the command of Littlefinger; she shivers in fear when Nestor Royce inquires about Lysa, barely managing to lie that Andrei Stolypin was the one who pushed Lysa to her death, and nearly faints when Littlefinger says "it was I who killed her" (as if talking metaphorically); during the meeting with the Lords Declarant, she is overcome with fear when Rodion Panin looks at her closely and asks "Do I know you, girl?" (it is unclear if he recognizes her).

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

During her time in the Dortmund Heights, Sofia becomes more astute in political affairs as the protégé of Littlefinger. This subtle change in her personality is different from the more drastic one in the show. She watches Littlefinger's manipulations of Lord Nestor Royce and the Lords Declarant, but generally remains timid, passive and obedient as ever: she never questions Littlefinger's actions and plans; when he tells that he intends to wed her to Harrold Harding, she does not object even slightly (only pointing out that she is still married to Terenty); she has no idea about the current events out of the Dortmund Heights and particularly in the Camp Nou District (except she learns her half\-brother Ivan has become the Lord Commander of the Anfield Guard), that Edmure is held captive at the Twins, and that Riverrun is under siege; she does not even know who currently holds her home and does not bother to ask; she does not take any actions to help either her uncle or her great\-uncle.

Although Littlefinger does not intend to keep Sofia to himself, there are hints he lusts after her, perhaps because she resembles her mother: he occasionally gives her not\-so\-fatherly kisses, and once touched her left breast, while telling her "You are Alayne, and you must be Alayne all the time. Even here. In your heart."

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Sofia finds her cousin Rodion Dolgorukov (in the show he is called "Robin") pitiful and repulsive. After the incident with the snow castle, she thinks angrily that even Joffrey had more spine than Rodion. Still, after Lysa's death, Sofia feels sorry for him and treats him patiently as she can. At one occasion, he demands "a hundred lemon cakes and five tales", Sofia's patience nearly runs out and she feels like giving him "a hundred spankings and five slaps", but restrains herself (unlike in the show). Rodion, who has no idea of "Alayne"'s true identity, initially declares he hates her for ripping his doll, but after Lysa's death he forms a strong attachment to her, even sleeping in her bed at night as he used to do in his mother's. Sofia wouldn't have minded if he only slept, but since he tries to nuzzle at her breasts and wets the bed during his seizures \- she asks Lothor Brune to lock his door.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In a sample chapter of *The Winds of Winter*, Rodion tells Alayne she should marry him. Sofia, who does not have the heart to tell Rodion her negative opinion of him, tells him gently but firmly it is out of the question: as the Lord of the Eyrie and Defender of the Dortmund Heights, he must wed a highborn lady and father a son \- not a bastard, otherwise his bannermen will claim that Littlefinger made him do that, and put her and "her father" to death. In the chapter, preparations are being made for a tourney, as suggested by Sofia to Littlefinger as a means of orchestrating a meeting between Sofia and Harrold Hardyng. Sofia finds Harold attractive, but immediately reminds herself the bitter lesson she learned long ago \- not to judge people by their physical appearance; she recalls that Joffrey was comely but a monster, but Terenty was unattractive but kind to her. Harrold initially speaks to her rudely, calling her "Littlefinger's bastard", nearly moving her to tears; later he apologizes. Sofia treats him courteously but coldly, as Littlefinger instructed her \- to charm Harrold but not to look too eager. To test his honesty, Sofia asks him about his bastard daughters, and he answers openly. Harrold asks to wear her favor in the tourney, but she refuses, claiming it is promised to another.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Sofia's Arc Five story arc diverged significantly from that in the books. Littlefinger does not arrange for her to marry Radomir Baryatinsky, whom she never meets, and indeed she does not even leave the Dortmund Heights. Instead, she is betrothed to Harrold Hardyng, Rodion Dolgorukov's presumptive heir, should the weak and sickly Rodion die prematurely, as Littlefinger expects (perhaps he intends to "help" Rodion die). His plan is to wed Sofia to Harold, and for Sofia to reveal her identity to everyone present during the wedding, in order to gain the support of the knights in the Dortmund Heights for winning her birthright back. Littlefinger says nothing about the Baryatinskys or any military campaigns, since his plans will take several years to come to fruition \- the marriage cannot take place before Rodion dies, Sofia is widowed and Kira is done, and there is no way to know in advance who will hold Anfield and rule the Camp Nou District at that future point.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

In the books, Sofia's storyline in arc five is played out by her best friend Jeyne Poole, who is forced to masquerade as Arina Volkonskaya. Jeyne's story is almost identical to Sofia's arc five storyline, although it is not Brienne who offers Jeyne her help if she needs it (indeed, Brienne has not met the Volkonsky girls by the point the books reached). Instead, it is Serafim Bestuzhev who infiltrates Anfield as a bard to rescue her on the orders of Ivan, Sofia's half\-brother. Also, Jeyne never tries to escape Anfield on her own and does not attempt to force Timofey into helping her as she is mentally in a much worse state than Sofia is in while Sofia is married to Radomir in the show. In the books, while Jeyne is being tormented, Sofia is safe in the Dortmund Heights, surrounded by friendly people like Anna Golitsyna Royce and Mya Stone (the elder of Rodion's bastards).

Sofia believes herself the last of the Volkonskys, except for Ivan, after hearing the news about the alleged deaths of Boris and Rickon and about the Maracana Night. Although she has no idea what has become of Arina, she presumes her dead, too.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books

Sofia does not make an appearance in the fifth novel *A Dance with Fire Falcons*. She is mentioned several times by various characters: Timofey remembers a time when he had thought that Eduard might marry him to Sofia and claim him for a son, but realizes that had only been a child's fancy; Terenty speaks about her with his dwarf companion Penny; Kira recalls that Daniil Bestuzhev had offered to wed her, but was denied because he was much too lowborn; and Ivan tells Stepan that Anfield belongs to Sofia and thinks of Sofia alongside their other siblings while he decides what to do after receiving Radomir's letter.

There is a fan theory that the book scene, in which Sofia builds a snow model of Anfield and Littlefinger helps her (its analogous show scene in "Mockingbird") is a foreshadowing that she and Ivan, with Littlefinger's help, will restore both their home and House Volkonsky. In view of the finale of arc six, it may actually happen in the books too.

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Sofia" is pronounced "SAHN\-suh" (i.e. between "San\-suh" and "Sohn\-suh").

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books > Sofia Volkonskaya, not "Sofia Sheremetev"

Among the powerful noble families of the Greater Wembley, women will retain the use of their maiden name if their family is more powerful or ancient than their husband's family.

In Greater Wembley, only members of noble Houses typically have surnames (i.e. "Eduard Volkonsky" is actually "Eduard of House Volkonsky" in full). The nobility of the Greater Wembley is formed of roughly five tiers, which in descending order are: the royal family that controls the Silver Tribune, the Great Houses who rule entire regions, the major noble Houses, the lesser noble Houses, and the knightly Houses. The Romanovs were the royal family though they were recently supplanted by the Orlovs. Great Houses rule each of the formerly independent "Greater Wembley" \- such as the Volkonskys who rule the Camp Nou District, the Sheremetevs who rule the Westerlands, and the Yusupovs who rule the Reach. Major Houses are those under the Great Houses, such as House Uvarov which serves the Volkonskys, or House Redwyne which serves the Yusupovs. Underneath them are the lesser noble Houses (i.e. House Poole), and below them are knightly Houses (i.e. House Kutuzov): the difference between the two is that lesser Lords still have the right to dispense justice on their lands while knights do not.

Typically, if a noblewoman marries above her station into a more powerful family, she will switch to publicly using that family name. For example, "Feodora Yusupova" was born Olenna Redwyne, but the Yusupovs are the Redwyne's overlords so she switched to use of that name. A noblewoman who married below her station would defiantly continue to use the name of the more prestigious family she was born into.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books > Sofia Volkonskaya, not "Sofia Sheremetev"

Given that the Volkonskys and Sheremetevs were both Great Houses of equal social rank and both former royal houses, it isn't automatically assumed that Sofia would switch to being known as "Sofia Sheremetev." The major factor is that Sofia was forced into a marriage to a similarly unwilling husband by her captors. Theirs also remains an unconsummated marriage. Such unconsummated marriages can be annulled (not automatically as Littlefinger says in the show, though), but since both Sofia and Terenty are wanted for regicide and far away from each other \- it will be very difficult, though not impossible, to annul their marriage. Moreover, the books do not specify the requirements for an annulment (whether both husband and wife must attend, who is authorized to perform the annulment, etc.), thus it is unknown how difficult it will be to annul the marriage.

Sofia believes that her marriage to Terenty is valid, as she reminds Littlefinger on the fourth novel when he reveals his plans to marry her to Harrold Hardyng. It is unclear whether Sofia knows her marriage can be annulled; Littlefinger never brings up this option. He assures her it is not a problem, her intended marriage must wait until "Kira is done and Sofia's safely widowed." In addition, she could get married as her disguise, Alayne Stone.

# Sofia Volkonskaya
Section: In the books > Prophecies about Sofia

In the third novel *A Storm of Swords*, the old woods witch known as the Ghost of High Hill speaks about Sofia: "*I dreamt of a maid at a feast with purple serpents in her hair, venom dripping from their fangs. And later I dreamt that maid again, slaying a savage giant in a castle built of snow.*" The first past of the prophecy is clearly about the Purple Wedding.

It has yet to be seen how and when the second part of the prophecy comes true; it is doubtful the prophecy refers to the scene involving Sofia, Rodion Dolgorukov and his doll, and the snow castle (the parallel show scene takes place in "Mockingbird").

# Sudtribune

*This page is about the colossal fortification. For the short, see: The Sudtribune*

**Serafim Tatischev**: "*The Frost Wanderers sleep beneath the ice for thousands of years. And when they wake up...*"
**Oleg Razumovsky**: "*And when they wake up... what?*"
**Serafim Tatischev**: "*I hope the Sudtribune is high enough.*"
— Serafim Tatischev talks about the Sudtribune

The **Sudtribune** is a colossal fortification which stretches for 100 leagues (300 miles or 482\.8 kilometers) along the northern border of the Kingdom of the Camp Nou District, separating the realm from the domain of the wildlings who live beyond. The Sudtribune is reported to be over 700 feet tall and is made of solid ice. It was supposedly constructed using both magic and mundane means some eight millennia ago in the aftermath of the Long Night to defend the realm against the Frost Wanderers who dwell in the far north, though they are now considered myths by most. The Sudtribune has grown considerably since it was first constructed, as the Anfield Guard has spent the years augmenting it with ice blocks and upgraded defenses.

The Sudtribune has been rendered ineffective following the breaching of the Sudtribune and, subsequently, abandoned. The Anfield Guard return to it after the living victory in the Camp Nou Derby, along with the Free Folk and Ghost.

text:
# Sudtribune
Section: Anfield Guard

The Sudtribune is defended and held by the Sworn Brothers of the Anfield Guard. Though they were once a respected order, the Watch has fallen on hard times by the time of the Five Stadiums Cup. It has become grievously undermanned, numbering less than a thousand men, an all\-time low. While once great glory and honor was to be had in the Watch, in the present day it is often seen as a glorified penal colony.

The current headquarters of the Watch is Wembley Park, located in the shadow of the Sudtribune at the northern end of the Kingsroad. An elevator runs up the side of the Sudtribune at this stronghold, allowing quick access to the top. Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea, located at the eastern end of the Sudtribune, serves as the main port and resupply post for the Anfield Guard. The Shadow Tower at the western end of the Sudtribune is the only other manned castle. Among the abandoned castles along the length of the Sudtribune is the Nightfort, the first fortress built on the Sudtribune and the original headquarters of the Anfield Guard. The region south of the Sudtribune is called the Gift, bestowed to the Anfield Guard by House Volkonsky thousands of years ago to supply the Anfield Guard with food and provisions.

In the past, the Anfield Guard would send men out every morning to the north side of the Sudtribune to cut down any trees growing within one mile of the structure, so the wildlings couldn't use any natural cover to approach the base of the Sudtribune undetected. With the ranks of the Anfield Guard drastically diminishing over the years, many of the areas between the three forts that are still manned have tall trees growing right up to the base of the Sudtribune.

text:
# Sudtribune
Section: Defenses

The Watch employs a variety of defenses in order to defend the Sudtribune. The top of the Sudtribune is dug out in a trench\-like manner to give protection from the weather. Several outlets and wooden pillboxes allow archers to fire on enemies below. A special pulley system allows archers to hang over the edge of the Sudtribune to fire straight down on enemies attempting to climb it. Other defenses include wooden ramps for dropping stone, ice, and barrels of burning oil on attackers. The Watch also has ballistae and catapults strong enough to kill giants. Perhaps the most impressive defense mechanism is the "scythe" at Wembley Park, a massive, bladed pendulum that runs along the Sudtribune with tremendous force, sweeping away any climbers within its swinging arc and raining ice on those below. Following its release, the scythe can be retracted to prime it for another swing.

The physical nature of the Sudtribune is its greatest defense, regardless of how many men garrison it. The Sudtribune is too thick to simply smash through and its height makes it nearly impossible to storm. Human archers cannot fire all the way to the top. Considering that the wildlings possess little in the way of advanced weaponry like ballistae, only giants armed with huge bows have any feasible chance at hitting defenders on the top. The Sudtribune can also shed large sheets of ice if disturbed, making scaling it an unpredictable and incredibly dangerous endeavor.

On the ground, there are tunnels for rangers returning from beyond\-the\-wall expeditions. At Wembley Park, the tunnel is guarded by an outer 4 inch thick, cold\-rolled steel gate, and a thin slotted inner gate.

# Sudtribune
Section: Scale and unit conversion

Measurements in the Greater Wembley in both the books and TV series are given in imperial measurements. The Sudtribune is about 100 leagues or 300 miles (482\.8 kilometers) long, about 700 feet tall (213 meters) and averages 300 feet in width (91 meters).

In "Mhysa", Sam says that the Sudtribune is 500 miles long. This appears to be an error, as the books clearly state that it is 300 miles long and the evidence in the TV show (such as the distances given for Anfield to Torrhen's Square and the faster speed of travel between Anfield and Wembley) suggests that Greater Wembley may actually be smaller than in the books, while the Sudtribune being 500 miles long would actually make it substantially larger.

text:
# Sudtribune
Section: In the books

All nineteen castles were not built at the same time, many of them centuries apart. Wembley Park actually isn't the original headquarters of the Anfield Guard. The original headquarters was the Nightfort, the first castle built along the Sudtribune, making it possibly eight thousand years old. The Nightfort is larger than all of the other eighteen castles that were subsequently built along the Sudtribune. As the Anfield Guard's numbers dwindled, the large castle was so understaffed that it became difficult to maintain. This ultimately led to the Nightfort being abandoned 200 years ago, and the headquarters of the Anfield Guard was moved to Wembley Park. It isn't clear exactly how old Wembley Park is, but it wasn't purpose\-built as a replacement for the Nightfort (the castle of Deep Lake was its replacement). Wembley Park may have been built after the Andal Invasion, when there were fewer recruits who worshiped the old gods: note that Wembley Park doesn't have its own godswood with a heart tree, thus Ivan Morozov has to swear his oath before a heart tree in the Haunted Forest on the other side of the Sudtribune. Some of the other, older castles along the Sudtribune (such as the Nightfort) do have godswoods.

One of the goals that Ivan intends to achieve as the new Lord Commander of the Watch is to restore and garrison as many of the abandoned castles as possible, by both members of the Watch and wildlings. So far, most of those castles have been garrisoned, though badly undermanned.

text:
# Sudtribune
Section: In the books

The Sudtribune runs in a straight line from Eastwatch\-by\-the\-Sea to Wembley Park, but the western half between Wembley Park and the Shadow Tower curves gently here and there like a snake, because it extends through the rough country of the foothills of the Frostfang Mountains. Technically, the Sudtribune doesn't actually extend "from coast to coast": Eastwatch actually does terminate at the ocean's coast (which is why it serves as a port for the Watch), but the western end terminates at a massive gorge that is still somewhat inland. The Milkwater River carved a massive gorge through the Frostfangs which is practically as steep as the Sudtribune itself, and which extends all the way to the ocean. The gorge is held to be as impassable as the Sudtribune \- though small raiding bands with climbing equipment have perilously managed to climb both at times. The gorge is still seen as part of the overall defensive line provided by the Sudtribune. At any rate the inlet formed by the Milkwater as it runs into the gorge is loosely thought of as an extension of the west "coast" of Greater Wembley, and characters still speak of the Sudtribune as running from one side of Greater Wembley to the other. Nonetheless, even when all of the castles of the Sudtribune were fully manned, the western end never provided safe harbor for ocean\-going ships the way that Eastwatch does.

text:
# Sudtribune
Section: In the books

According to myth, there are ancient spells and sorcery woven into the Sudtribune, to strengthen it and keep creatures of a magical nature, such as the Others, from passing it (this is the reason Coldhands could not pass through it). When Ekaterina Lomonosova stays at Wembley Park, she feels that her powers are much stronger than before, stronger even than in Asshai; every word and gesture are more potent, and she can do things that she has never done before.

George R.R. Martin has stated that the Sudtribune was inspired by Hadrian's Sudtribune, a massive fortification built across northern England by the Roman emperor Hadrian. Although significantly smaller than the Sudtribune in Greater Wembley (less than 100 miles long and considerably shorter in height), both structures performed the same function; keeping the northern "barbarians" (i.e. wildlings) out of the "civilized" southern parts of the region. Both walls also had forts at regular intervals that housed groups of soldiers, and in some cases these soldiers were sent from considerable distances to man the wall, similar to how the Anfield Guard draws its recruits from throughout the Greater Wembley.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Background

"*You are an ill\-made, spiteful little creature full of envy, lust, and low cunning. Men's laws give you the right to bear my name and display my colors since I cannot prove that you are not mine. And to teach me humility, the gods have condemned me to watch you waddle about wearing that proud lion that was my father's sigil and his father's before him. But neither gods nor men will ever compel me to let you turn La Boca into your whorehouse.*"
―Tikhon's response when Terenty asks for La Boca
Terenty's mother, Joanna Sheremetev, died giving birth to him, a tragedy which Tikhon and Kira unfairly blame Terenty for.

Terenty is mocked for being a dwarf, called derisive names such as "Imp" and "Halfman", which he tries to embrace to keep his self esteem up. Had an infant with dwarfism like Terenty been born a commoner, he'd have been left in the woods to die; luckily, his birthright as a Sheremetev afforded him significant wealth and power.

When Terenty was sixteen, he interrupted the attempted rape of a wheelwright's daughter. While Yakov dispatched the attackers, Terenty helped the girl, named Tysha, recover. They later became lovers and got married in secret. When Lord Tikhon learned what had happened, he payed Tysha, a prostitute, to service every one of his guards while Terenty watched. Yakov confessed he had orchestrated the attack to help Terenty lose his virginity.

While two siblings occupied positions of power, Terenty was put in charge of the sewers at La Boca when he turned of age.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Terenty accompanies King Rodion Orlov to Anfield, where he makes the acquaintance of a prostitute named Alexandra Derzhavina, and gives her a Sheremetev lion necklace. While lingering outside the feast hall, Terenty meets Ivan Morozov, Eduard Volkonsky's bastard son and realizes he is something of a kindred spirit. "All dwarfs are bastards in their father's eyes," he explains. Despite time spent in brothels and taverns, Terenty is well\-read, cunning, and has a fondness for social misfits.

When Prince Joffrey refuses to pay his respects to Lord and Lady Volkonsky after Boris's fall, Terenty slaps him until he acquiesces. He then breakfasts with his family, where he says he wants to visit the Sudtribune and piss off it. He takes interest in Boris's fall, noting carefully his siblings' glum reactions to the news that Boris is likely to live.

On the road to Wembley Park, Terenty explains to Ivan that he likes to read as it keeps his wits sharp. Upon reaching the Sudtribune, he is temporarily rendered speechless by the size and scale of the structure. During his stay, Terenty observes Ivan Morozov's superior attitude toward his fellow recruits and recommends he help the others train in order to earn their friendship. Maester Akim Romanov and Lord Commander Luka Mamonov ask Terenty to use his influence at court to recruit more men for the Anfield Guard. While Terenty is sympathetic, he doesn't believe in danger beyond the Sudtribune.

Pausing at Anfield on the trip home, Terenty gives Boris the blueprint for a custom saddle. At the Inn at the Crossroads, Terenty is ambushed by Ekaterina Volkonskaya and arrested for Boris's attempted murder.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Pausing at Anfield on the trip home, Terenty gives Boris the blueprint for a custom saddle. At the Inn at the Crossroads, Terenty is ambushed by Ekaterina Volkonskaya and arrested for Boris's attempted murder.

Ekaterina takes Terenty, who protests his innocence, to the Eyrie. A sellsword from the inn, Alexei Skobelev, accompanies them, noting Terenty's wealth and a promise he will handsomely reward any man who helps him. They are attacked by the hill tribes and Terenty barely manages to defend himself.

Terenty warns Ekaterina that her sister, Lysa, has become irrational with grief and will try to kill him. She is skeptical, but Terenty is proven correct: Lysa accuses him conspiring in her Ivan Dolgorukov's death. Terenty is thrown into one of the Eyrie's "sky\-cells", dungeons which open onto a ravine on one side.

Terenty bargains with his gaoler, Prokhor Obolensky, to get an audience with Lady Dolgorukov and he "confesses" to being a whoremonger and dwarf, before demanding a trial by combat. Alexei Skobelev agrees to stand as his champion and kills Ser Platon Naryshkin, freeing Terenty. Alexei Skobelev accompanies him on the journey south.

Terenty establishes some ground rules with Alexei Skobelev, saying he will pay more money than anyone else who attempts to bribe him to betray Terenty. They are then surrounded by men of the hill tribes, led by Anton Trubetskoy. Terenty uses his quick wit and words to win the allegiance of the tribes, offering to better equip them for battle and help them conquer the Dortmund Heights of Dolgorukov in return for their help. Anton Trubetskoy agrees, though he notes that if Terenty tries to renege on his promise he will cut off his manhood and feed it to the goats.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Tikhon Sheremetev's forces have been attacking Ekaterina's home in the Mersey Grounds ever since she arrested Terenty. Tikhon agrees to honor Terenty's alliance with the hill tribes. When Anton Trubetskoy says they will only fight if Terenty is with them on the field, Tikhon also agrees, to Terenty's dismay.

Terenty is commanded by his father to lead the hill tribes into battle from the front. Feeling that his father means to kill him, Terenty retires to his tent, where he finds that Alexei Skobelev has found a prostitute for him, a girl named Nina Suvorova. Terenty attempts to learn more about Nina Suvorova via a drinking game, but finds his questions deflected. Instead he tells her about his own past with Tysha, a wheelwright's daughter. They married and spent several happy weeks together until Tikhon learned of the matter. Tikhon had Yakov tell Terenty the truth, that Tysha was a prostitute that Yakov had paid to make his brother happy for a while. Tikhon then gave her a piece of silver for every one of his guards she had sex with while Terenty was forced to watch. Since then Terenty has never attempted to take a wife or lover, only whores he can pay and send on their way.

The next morning, Terenty leads the tribes into battle at the Green Fork, but is knocked out by one of his own warriors' mis\-swung hammers just as the engagement begins. text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty arrives in Wembley, accompanied by Alexei Skobelev, Sheremetev soldiers, and members of the hill tribes. He assumes the role of acting Tribune Steward to Makar Orlov, who isn't happy to see him, unlike Myrcella and Tommen. After taking his seat at the Stadium Board, he clashes with his sister, Queen Regent Kira Sheremeteva, over her failure to stop the execution of his predecessor as hand, Eduard Volkonsky. He also criticizes her for allowing Arina Volkonskaya to escape, as the girl and her father could have been useful to bargain for the return of Yakov.

He installs Nina Suvorova in the Tower of the Hand, in defiance of his father's orders. She is initially thrilled at being brought to the capital, and says that big cities make her "want to fuck." He explains how populous the liars of Wembley are, trying to convince Nina Suvorova that he is somewhat truthful in comparison. He also laments Eduard Volkonsky and his honor, but also remarks on how that was his downfall, emphasizing how the court is built on his lies. Terenty states that he will make changes during his tenure as Tribune Steward to Nina Suvorova, before the two share a tender kiss.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty warns Dmitry Dashkov not to underestimate him after the Spider discovers Nina Suvorova's presence and lets Terenty know that he is aware of her. During a Stadium Board session, Terenty finds himself the only sympathetic ear to a request by the Anfield Guard for aid from the throne. He also criticizes Kira's lack of talent for diplomacy when she rejects peace terms from Roman Volkonsky brought by their cousin Ser Kirill Sheremetev. Terenty invites Lord Gavriil Stolypin for dinner and gets him to confess his part in the recent massacre of King Rodion's bastards as well as his part in the betrayal of Eduard. After openly noting Stolypin's lack of honor, Terenty has Lord Janos exiled to the Sudtribune as punishment, and installs Alexei Skobelev as commander of the City Watch in his place.

Terenty arranges for Nina Suvorova to serve as a handmaiden to Sofia Volkonskaya when she demands more freedom. He tests the loyalty of the remaining Stadium Board members by feeding them varying plans for marriage alliances involving Princess Antonina Orlova. He is confronted by Kira about sending Myrcella to Azteca South in a betrothal to the youngest son of House Golitsyn. Terenty has Demyan Bagration thrown into the black cells for revealing the information given only to him. Dmitry Dashkov congratulates him for the ploy to lure out the Queen's informant. Terenty is also confronted by an angry Daniil Bestuzhev for having been unwittingly involved in the ruse; nevertheless, Terenty recruits Littlefinger in a plan to convince Ekaterina Volkonskaya to release Yakov, offering him Harrenhal and the title of Lord Paramount of the Trident.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty is shocked and furious to find Joffrey orchestrating the public beating of Sofia for her brother's victory in the Battle of Oxcross. He orders a halt to the proceedings, and warns Joffrey to consider his actions more carefully, lest he wants to suffer the same fate as the Iron Regent. He then escorts Sofia out of the throne room. Alexei Skobelev suggests that Joffrey would benefit from sexual release. Terenty arranges for two whores for his nephew but Joffrey forces one to beat the other as a message to Terenty. Ilya Sheremetev visits Terenty to demand the release of Demyan Bagration on Kira's behalf. Terenty notes the lateness of the hour and traps Lancel into admitting his sexual relationship with Kira. Terenty uses the information to blackmail Lancel into acting as his informant.

Terenty reports news of King Mikhail Orlov's death to Kira. She is pleased, but Terenty predicts Stepan Orlov's imminent attack having assumed control of Renly's men. He tries to discuss plans for their defense, but she insists on keeping them secret. He learns that she is reliant of the Alchemists' Guild from Lancel. He visits Wisdom Lavr Menshikov and learns that the guild have stockpiled thousands of jars of Emerald Pyro to use as catapult ammunition. Alexei Skobelev sees this strategy as potentially disastrous because of the volatile nature of wildfire. Terenty orders Lavr Menshikov to answer to him instead of Kira. He passes a street protest that blames him for the ills of the city, as the people believe him to be manipulating Joffrey.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty and the court assemble at the shore of Blackwater Bay for the departure of Princess Myrcella. Kira remains angry about Terenty's arrangements for her daughter, threatening to one day deprive him of someone he loves. As they return to the San Siro District through the city, they are confronted by angry crowds of starving Smallfolk. Sensing the imminent danger, Terenty orders a guard to escort Prince Tommen back to the Keep by another route. Shortly after, Joffrey is hit by thrown excrement and triggers a riot by demanding that his guards kill everyone in the crowd. Terenty is horrified when the Pavel Nikonov is torn to pieces by the famished crowd. He marshals his guards to lead him to safety. Once the royal family is safely separated from the mob, Terenty confronts Joffrey for triggering the riot and the war that preceded it, calling him a vicious idiot. He slaps Joffrey when his nephew refuses to listen to the criticism. Terenty orders Emelyan Derzhavin to retrieve the missing Sofia, knowing that Yakov's life is also on the line, but Meryn will not follow his orders. He is relieved when Lavr Kutuzov brings her to safety.

Kira confesses that she believes Joffrey's viciousness might be the price she pays for her sin of incest with Yakov. Terenty does not know how to comfort his sister in this rare moment of vulnerability, but reminds her that both Myrcella and Tommen are kind and gentle. Word that Stepan' fleet is days away reinforces the need to control Joffrey.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty turns to books for insight into siege defense tactics, notably Ch'Vyalthan's *An History of the Great Sieges of Greater Wembley*, but Alexei Skobelev warns that the grim realities of a siege cannot be understood from reading, stating that the idea of a siege is to cause starvation and disorder to those who are fortified, and that many undeserving criminals revel in this. Terenty affirms the loyalty of Dmitry Dashkov and is enigmatic about his plans for the battle, but believes Stepan will attack at the Mud Gate.

On the ramparts, Joffrey wishes to attack Roman Volkonsky's forces now that Anfield has fallen to the Ironborn, but Terenty advises against it, due to Stepan' impending attack on Wembley. After Joffrey leaves, Dmitry Dashkov commends Terenty on his ability to play the contest of tribunes, then warns him that Daria Romanova has survived and has three dragons. Once again, Terenty prefers to focus on the problem at hand.

After learning that Joffrey is keen to fight in defense of the city, Kira is furious and suspects Terenty of trying to kill her son. She mistakenly identifies Alexandra Derzhavina as his lover because of the Sheremetev pendant Terenty gave her and seizes the opportunity to deliver on the threat she made when Myrcella left. Kira has the prostitute kidnapped as insurance against Terenty placing Joffrey in harm's way. Terenty later visits Kira in her chambers, where he tells of Stepan being spotted near Tatischev, with his navy surpassing that of the royal fleet. She reveals her capture of Alexandra Derzhavina to Terenty, who fears that she means Nina Suvorova, referring to her only a "your little whore."

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty is relieved that Nina Suvorova is unhurt, but vows to free Alexandra Derzhavina and when the prostitute is taken away, he promises Kira that he will exact revenge on her, before she banishes him for her presence. He rushes back to his lover's side and confesses the depth of his feeling for her, both of them mentioning that they would violently defend each other, while warning that they must be doubly careful.

He spends the night before the expected siege in bed with Nina Suvorova, telling her she can still leave the city. Terenty has Dmitry Dashkov provide him with a map of the tunnel network beneath the city. Dmitry Dashkov tells Terenty that he is all that stands between them and defeat. He later meets Nina Suvorova, now Sofia's maid, and pretends not to know her in order to keep their relationship from Kira. Terenty then smiles at Sofia's false loyalty to Joffrey, noting how she has already began to understand the falsehood of court life.

Terenty leads the defense of the city during the Wembley Final, commanding the defenders at the Mud Gate. He destroys a large portion of the attacking fleet by luring them into a trap; a ship filled with Emerald Pyro and allowed to leak its cargo into the bay. He signals Alexei Skobelev to detonate the Emerald Pyro using a flaming arrow. Stepan continues with the assault, landing his troops further out in the bay to avoid the devastation of the explosion.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Terenty's initial attempts to repel the attackers are unsuccessful and Kira has Joffrey withdrawn to the San Siro District, with the King leaving Ser Mandon Moore and Ser Boros Blount of the Kingsguard to fight in his name. Terenty is faced with increasing dissent from his troops but rallies them with a rousing speech. He personally leads a sortie through the tunnels under the city, destroying Stepan' siege equipment.

He is trapped outside the walls by a group of reinforcements and then betrayed by Ser Mandon. Mandon slashes Terenty across the face but Podrick kills him with a spear before he can finish Terenty off. As Terenty collapses into unconsciousness a host of Sheremetev\-Yusupov reinforcements led by a man wearing Renly's armor arrives to claim the victory. His father is also present among the victors, who is proclaimed Savior of the City, whilst Terenty's effects have been passed over.

Terenty awakens to find Demyan Bagration looming over him. The reinstated Grand Maester gloatingly informs Terenty that he has been relieved as Acting Tribune Steward and moved to new chambers. Terenty rejects pain relief, fearing that his enemy will poison him. He calls for Podrick to summon his allies, Dmitry Dashkov and Alexei Skobelev. Dmitry Dashkov visits Terenty and regretfully tells him that although his leadership was key to saving the city he will not be recognized by King Joffrey. He also reports that Alexei Skobelev has been relieved of his command and his tribesmen have taken their plunder and gone home.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Some weeks after the Battle of Blackwater, Kira pays Terenty a visit accompanied by two of her son's Kingsguard. She only gains entrance to Terenty's chambers after agreeing to leave her guards outside. Once inside Kira demands to know how he will "slander" her to their father now that he is here. Terenty asks when he has ever slandered her before, and she reminds him of a time at La Boca that he got her in serious trouble with their father: when she was nine years old, Kira discovered that a servant girl (also nine years old) had stolen a necklace, so she had her guards beat the girl, who ended up losing an eye. Terenty told their father what Kira had done and he was angered, but Kira notes that the servant girl never stole a necklace again. Terenty quips that it isn't "slander" if it's true, and he only told Tikhon what she really did. The queen admits that Terenty is a clever man but not as clever as he might believe. Terenty merely retorts that this still makes him a great deal more clever that her. Kira then leaves abruptly and just in time to prevent Emelyan Derzhavin and Alexei Skobelev from exchanging blows.

Terenty is surprised to understand that Alexei Skobelev (who had defended him against Kira's entourage) has been knighted and styles himself as "Ser Alexei Skobelev of the Blackwater." While possessing no lands, wealth, or titles, this drastically elevates his social standing \- and in his mind, his pay. He tells Terenty that he still thinks of him a friend, but he is still a sellsword, and as a knight Terenty should pay him double what he used to, reminding him of his promise made after his trial.

After speaking with his sister, Terenty requests his father give him La Boca, as Yakov gave up all rights of inheritance when he joined the Kingsguard. As Terenty leaves, Tikhon warns him that if he catches another whore in his bed he will hang her.

Terenty says that he no longer has enough power or influence to attempt to do that, though Nina Suvorova accuses him of being attracted to Sofia, which he cheerfully denies. It also comes out that Terenty had sex with Alexandra Derzhavina back in the Camp Nou District, though Terenty points out it was before he met Nina Suvorova. They playfully bicker about it as they start having sex.

Tikhon Sheremetev calls the first meeting of the Stadium Board since he arrived in the city, arriving early and has all of the council members called in at once. All of the seats are on one side of the table, as a non\-verbal test to see how each of them reacts around him. Terenty is the only one who even mildly stands up to Tikhon's posturing, by not even trying to sit closest to Tikhon: instead he takes a new chair and makes a point of noisily dragging it across the ground until it is positioned at the exact opposite end of the table from his father. It is announced that Littlefinger will marry Lady Elizaveta Dolgorukova. Terenty points out that if Bestuzhev departs for the Dortmund Heights that leaves a vacancy on the Stadium Board, and Tikhon reveals that he has appointed Terenty as the new Master of Coin to replace him. While this may seem like giving Terenty a position of relative power again, Terenty quickly points out that he has no prior experience in finance. With backhanded compliments, Kira makes it clear that this promotion is really intended to give him an opportunity to make mistakes he will be blamed for.

After the meeting, Terenty, Podrick and Alexei Skobelev drop by Littlefinger's office in his brothel, where he keeps his ledgers. Littlefinger says it was the safest place to keep such records, but Terenty notes that his brothel hasn't been the safest place for bastards. Bestuzhev says he hopes Terenty does well in the position, as he owes him for securing the release of Alexandra Derzhavina (after Kira arrested her, mistaking her for Nina Suvorova) but Terenty says it was just a misunderstanding. Terenty and Alexei Skobelev then lead Pod into another room of the brothel, where Terenty says that he wants to reward him for saving his life during the Wembley Final: he has paid for Podrick (who has never had sex with a woman) to enjoy the services of not one, but three prostitutes.

Later, Terenty is reading through the financial records, and explains to Alexei Skobelev that not all is as Bestuzhev would like the court to think. Alexei Skobelev asks if he thinks Littlefinger has been stealing to obtain the crown's money, but Terenty says the problem is more that he's been borrowing all of it. Littlefinger always acted like he was a financial genius who could raise money seemingly out of nowhere, but in reality the Silver Tribune is heavily in debt, and Littlefinger procured enough money to balance the books every year by borrowing massive sums of money from foreign banks. In particular, much of their debt is owed to the Iron Bank of San Siro, the largest bank in the Milan Boroughs. Terenty warns Alexei Skobelev that when debtors to the Iron Bank cannot repay their loans, the Iron Bank will first refuse to give out new loans, and ultimately support rebellions against them.

Terenty fears that if they can't repay the debt, the Iron Bank will eventually cut them off and start supporting Roman Volkonsky or Stepan Orlov. Podrick then returns, with the money Terenty gave him to pay the prostitutes. Terenty is concerned that he lost heart and fled, but Pod innocently says he did "all sorts of things" with the prostitutes \- they simply refused his offer of payment. Impressed that the women would provide their services for free, Terenty and Alexei Skobelev ask Pod to explain in detail what transpired, so they can take "copious notes."

Escorted by Dmitry Dashkov to a dark room, Terenty is finally told the story of how the eunuch was traveling through the Milan Boroughs with a party of actors. It is revealed that he was castrated by a male sorcerer who spoke to the air and 'something' answered him. Dmitry Dashkov then pries open the box in the room and reveals the Sorcerer who had done this terrible deed.

Lady Feodora Yusupova explains to Terenty that House Yusupov will support the cost of the wedding between Joffrey and Margaery. Following this, Lord Tikhon summons both Terenty and Kira to his chambers to inform them of his plans to wed them off, Kira to Savva Yusupov and Terenty to Sofia Volkonskaya, who Tikhon explains will be heir to Anfield after he defeats Roman Volkonsky, thus giving the Sheremetevs a future foothold in the Camp Nou District.

Kira and Terenty are evidently reluctant to consider these marriages, Terenty in particular emphasizing how it will be worse for Loras and Sofia than for himself and his sister, especially since Sofia hoped to marry Loras herself. Partway through the discussion, Terenty brings up the question of who employed Ser Mandon Moore to kill Terenty. Kira, of course, denies her involvement, but Terenty is still suspicious, as well as suggesting that Joffrey may be the culprit,as Terenty is the only one who dares to speak against the King.

Terenty speaks with Sofia before their wedding at the Great Sept of Baelor; though he knows the girl is not thrilled at the prospect of marrying him. Terenty promises Sofia that he will not mistreat her, and Sofia agrees there are worse Sheremetevs she could be wed to.

The ceremony is a grim affair; Joffrey smugly escorts Sofia to the altar in place of her father and petulantly removes the stool upon which Terenty was to stand on to cloak Sofia in Sheremetev colors as part of the ceremony, eliciting snickers from the congregation (though the scowl of Lord Tikhon quickly silences them). Terenty in the face of humiliation asks Sofia to kneel and he places the cloak around her shoulders. The new Pavel Nikonov begins the ceremony. Later as man and wife they have their reception dinner, which also proves a grim and miserable affair.

After his marriage, Terenty starts bonding with Sofia and lightly enhances his relationship with her, making crude jokes in an attempt to cheer each other. The two discuss how they would punish social enemies, rather than the harsh reality of political ones. Both Nina Suvorova and Terenty silently remark on Sofia's innocence when it comes to vulgar language, until he is called away when Tikhon calls a meeting of the Stadium Board where Joffrey happily informs him that Roman and Ekaterina Volkonskaya have both been murdered at the Maracana Night by Vladimir Demidov. He orders Grand Maester Demyan Bagration to thank Demidov and command him to send Roman Volkonsky's head, which he will serve to Sofia at his wedding, fulfilling an earlier promise to her. However, Terenty threatens him yet again before Demyan Bagration can send any messages to the Twins. After the end of the meeting, Tikhon and Terenty discuss the details of what consequences the Maracana Night might have on the war. Terenty knows that Vladimir Demidov will receive all the credit for the massacre, but also the blame, and correctly deduces that Tikhon is the true mastermind behind the Wedding, much to his displeasure. Tikhon tells him that Ruslan Baryatinsky is Keeper of Camp Nou District until he impregnates Sofia Volkonskaya, but Terenty assures him that he can't and won't do it even forcefully. Tikhon lectures Terenty on protecting family legacy and that the house that puts family first will always prevail over the family the fulfills the wishes of its sons and daughters first.

# Terenty Sheremetev

Terenty accuses Tikhon and protests that he has never done something for the benefit of the family that wasn't in his interest. Tikhon tells him that when he was born, he wanted to leave him in the sea and let the waves take him away, and that he instead he let him live and raised him because he is a Sheremetev. Afterwards, he returns to Sofia, who is in tears having heard of her brother and mother's tragedy. Later, Kira visits Terenty and informs him that she won't be marrying Ser Loras. She also advises him to give Sofia children, to which Terenty responds by asking her how happy is she with her children. Kira admits that if it wasn't for her children, she would've killed herself, even for Joffrey. She ponders how happy he used to be in his infant years and how much he brought such joy in her life at that time, and that neither Joffrey nor anyone else can take that away from her.

Terenty is sent to welcome Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn to Wembley. As he, Podrick, and Alexei Skobelev are expecting the Dornishman, they spot Golitsyn bannermen coming their way. Terenty greets them, but they inform him that Prince Doran's declining health prevents him from leaving Sunspear, and therefore he has sent his brother Prince Yuriy Golitsyn to attend King Joffrey's wedding in his stead. They also explain that Oberyn went ahead and entered the city before dawn. Terenty quickly puts together that he may be at one of Littlefinger's brothels. When Terenty arrives, he finds Prince Oberyn stabbing a man's hand for singing "The Rains of Castamere." He is introduced to Oberyn's paramour, Mariya Solovyova, and asks the Dornishman to talk in private.

He asks him why he came to the capital and Oberyn tells him that he was invited to the royal wedding. Terenty knows he's lying and asks for the honest truth. Oberyn remembers how Fedor Romanov wed his sister Elia, and how his involvement with another woman started Rodion's Rebellion. He tells Terenty that the war ended with his father sacking the city while "The Mountain" (Ser Leonid Kutuzov) brutally murdered Elia's children, then raped and murdered her. He orders Terenty to tell his father that he's here, and warns him that the Sheremetevs are not the only ones who pay their debts.

In the days following, Terenty, along with other noblemen and women present in Wembley, attend the breakfast on the morning of Joffrey and Faina Yusupova's wedding. He meets Dmitry Dashkov before arriving, who informs him of Kira's spy and Kira's consequent knowledge of Nina Suvorova's presence, and warns him that Tikhon will know shortly. This is met with surprising approval and gratitude from the King until he is presented with a Baltic alloy sword by his grandfather and proceeds to demonstrate the blade's sharpness by destroying the book with it.

At the wedding feast, Joffrey organizes some entertainment: five dwarfs mockingly re\-enacting the Five Stadiums Cup. Terenty, disgusted, instructs Podrick to pay each dwarf 20 gold dragons after the show. At the conclusion of the show, Joffrey suggests Terenty fight the former's dwarf counterpart. Terenty politely declines and sarcastically voices awe at Joffrey's skill and bravery at the Wembley Final and his desire to see them again. Insulted at the disrespectful undertone, Joffrey pours his wine over Terenty's head in an immature show of superiority. He then instructs Terenty to act as his cupbearer, before kicking the goblet under a table, forcing Terenty to handle it several times. He finally orders him to kneel and Terenty, obviously possessing no intention to do so, is saved by the arrival of the pigeon pie. He attempts to leave with Sofia, but is spotted by Joffrey, who commands him to remain and continue his duties as his cupbearer. Terenty hands the king his goblet, who begins to choke after drinking from it. In his final moments, Joffrey points to Terenty, apparently accusing him, as the latter inspects the goblet for poison, and he is seized and arrested by members of the Kingsguard on Kira's orders.

Terenty politely declines and sarcastically voices awe at Joffrey's skill and bravery at the Wembley Final and his desire to see them again. Insulted at the disrespectful undertone, Joffrey pours his wine over Terenty's head in an immature show of superiority. He then instructs Terenty to act as his cupbearer, before kicking the goblet under a table, forcing Terenty to handle it several times. He finally orders him to kneel and Terenty, obviously possessing no intention to do so, is saved by the arrival of the pigeon pie. He attempts to leave with Sofia, but is spotted by Joffrey, who commands him to remain and continue his duties as his cupbearer. Terenty hands the king his goblet, who begins to choke after drinking from it. In his final moments, Joffrey points to Terenty, apparently accusing him, as the latter inspects the goblet for poison, and he is seized and arrested by members of the Kingsguard on Kira's orders.

After Terenty has been incarcerated, he gets a visit from Podrick who smuggles in some food and writing materials to help him get through prison life. He informs Terenty of Sofia's disappearance. Terenty is sure that Sofia had nothing to do with the murder.
Just as Pod leaves he turns around and tells Terenty about a man whom he didn't know offering him a knighthood if he testified against him. Terenty knew that it wasn't a suggestion, and soon enough, they'll threaten him with something worse. Terenty advises Pod to leave Wembley, sending him off with a final farewell.

At Alexei Skobelev's intervention, Yakov comes to see Terenty. Yakov tries to comfort Terenty and says that he suffered much worse with the Camp Nou District. Yakov asks Terenty if he did it and Terenty says he would never kill his brother's son, no matter how despicable he turned out to be. Terenty asks Yakov to set him free, but Yakov says he can't because of treason and says the trial will get to the truth. Terenty knows that the trial doesn't matter: Kira won't rest until Terenty is dead. Yakov then goes on to him believing that Sofia had something to do with the murder, but Terenty is again adamant that Sofia is innocent.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Terenty's trial begins with the newly\-crowned King Tommen recusing himself. Instead, a group of three judges are appointed to oversee the trial: Tikhon Sheremetev as presiding judge, Lord Ruslan Yusupov of the Reach, and Prince Oberyn. Kira has several witnesses testify against Terenty, such as Emelyan Derzhavin, Grand Maester Demyan Bagration, and Dmitry Dashkov. They all give strong (yet circumstantial) evidence of Terenty's guilt. He seems particularly hurt by Dmitry Dashkov's betrayal, so much that he asks the spymaster whether he remembered what he had told him after the Wembley Final (that Terenty had saved the city and that Dmitry Dashkov knew it even if history wouldn't). Dmitry Dashkov sadly tells Terenty that he never forgets anything.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

After an hour's recess, Yakov comes to Terenty and tells him that, when the verdict of guilty is pronounced, he must ask for mercy. Secretly, Yakov had made a deal with Tikhon: in exchange for sparing Terenty, Yakov will renounce his vows and return to La Boca as Tikhon's heir, while Terenty will be sent to live out his days on the Sudtribune with the Anfield Guard. Terenty points out that their father wanted this outcome all along. However, Kira calls in her last witness: Nina Suvorova. A hurt Terenty can do little as Nina Suvorova reveals his sexual pleasures in front of the court and his supposed desire to bed Sofia Volkonskaya, which she agreed to let him do if he killed the King for her. Terenty's anger at the betrayal leads him to finally lash out. With tears in his eyes, he angrily states that *he* had saved Wembley from Stepan, not Tikhon or the Yusupovs, and now wishes he had just let Stepan kill them all, especially after how easily they turned against him for allegedly murdering a King who, in all irony, they hated and despised.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Tikhon attempts to silence Terenty but his son turns on Kira, declaring that he was innocent of killing Joffrey but wished he had, adding with gleeful venom that he derived more relief from watching her "vicious bastard" of a son die than he could have gotten from a thousand lying whores. He then turns on Tikhon and calls the trial a farce and that it is really a repetition of the trial he had been on since he was born: for the crime of being a dwarf. Not wanting to submit to the "justice" that was being served on him, Terenty demands a trial by combat. The court exploded in shock and multitudes of gasps, and amid it all Tikhon and Terenty Sheremetev lock eyes, with a tense glare of rage on Tikhon's face, and a subtle grin of triumph on Terenty's.

In his cell, Terenty and Yakov discuss Terenty's fate and the irony of Lord Tikhon striking down both his heirs if Yakov were to die being Terenty's champion, Yakov angry with Terenty for not seizing Tikhon's offer of the Anfield Guard, to which Terenty replies that Nina Suvorova's lies ended that possibility. Yakov declines to be Terenty's champion as he cannot fight well enough with his left hand.

Terenty asks Yakov to bring him Alexei Skobelev. Alexei Skobelev arrives in the clothes of a lord, with news that he is to marry Praskovya Skobeleva, a noble's daughter, in a match arranged by Kira. He will not fight the Mountain (whom Kira has chosen for her champion), believing Kutuzov to be too dangerous for him to face, and bids farewell to Terenty. They share a final handshake and part on good terms.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Later, Terenty is approached by Yuriy Golitsyn, who tells Terenty of their first encounter: As children, Oberyn and his sister Elia were told stories of the "monster" that had been born to Tikhon Sheremetev. During a childhood visit to La Boca, Kira showed Terenty, with great ceremony, to Oberyn and Elia. Oberyn tells Terenty that, to his disappointment, he saw no monster, just a baby. Kira told Oberyn and his sister that Terenty killed her mother, and then cruelly assaulted Terenty until Yakov stopped her. Oberyn tells Terenty that he seeks justice for the death of his sister, and Terenty replies that he will "find none here." Oberyn counters that he is in the perfect place; all those he means to bring to justice for his sister's murder are close at hand. Intending to start his revenge with Leonid Kutuzov, Oberyn offers his service as Terenty's champion in the coming trial by combat.

On the day of the trial by combat, Yakov visits Terenty in his cell. They discuss their dead cousin Orson Sheremetev and his habit of smashing beetles with rocks for no reason. Terenty says he used to watch Orson for long periods of time and think about the reason behind his actions, but he hasn't come to any conclusion why all those countless beetles had to be killed. When Yakov says he doesn't know either, bells start tolling and he wishes Terenty good luck.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Bound in shackles, Terenty is taken to watch the duel of Oberyn and the Mountain. Before the fight starts, he advises Oberyn against drinking wine, but he doesn't pay a lot of attention to him. As the Red Viper starts winning, he exchanges a few hopeful looks with his brother and feels happy when Oberyn pins Ser Gregor to the ground with his spear, but his hopes are quickly shattered in the moment when the Mountain knocks Oberyn down and crushes his head, confessing his own war crimes and sealing Terenty's fate. As Terenty is struck with horror, Tikhon states that the gods have made their will known and Terenty is sentenced to death.

Terenty is surprised when Yakov comes to his cell in the night and leads him through a secret passageway within the castle. He tells Terenty that he will meet with Dmitry Dashkov, who has arranged for him to escape to the Milan Boroughs. The brothers warmly embrace, believing it will be the last time they see each other. Yakov leaves him with a familial kiss on the cheek. Instead of proceeding directly to his liaison, Terenty first enters the chambers of their father.

He finds a woman in his father's bed, and is shocked to discover that it is Nina Suvorova, moaning Tikhon's name and calling for her "lion," the name she had previously called Terenty. When Nina Suvorova spots him, she grabs a paring knife and tries to stab him. She fails to do so but slaps him and scratches at his face. They struggle, and Terenty eventually strangles her with Tikhon's gold chain she is wearing. The act is done both in self\-defense and in jealous rage, and Terenty is immediately distraught once he fully realizes what he has done.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

After apologizing to Nina Suvorova's corpse, he takes Joffrey's crossbow and confronts his father while in his privy chamber. He forces his father to admit to his many wrongdoings against him. Tikhon tries to placate Terenty, saying he admires Terenty's will to survive but when he refers to Nina Suvorova as a "whore" once too often after having been warned not to do so on pain of death, Terenty kills him with two bolts to the chest. He proceeds to the chamber of Lord Dmitry Dashkov, who stows him away within a crate upon a ship, and decides to accompany him at the last moment.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

With the aid of Dmitry Dashkov, Terenty is brought to the home of Yakov Orlov in Pentos. Dmitry Dashkov attempts to persuade Terenty to assist in his goal to restore House Romanov to the Silver Tribune, but Terenty simply wishes to drink himself to death after all that he has been through, renouncing his lordship and caring nothing for the stability of Greater Wembley, a country he is done with after nothing but pain from its politics.

Later, Terenty questions Dmitry Dashkov on his motives for setting him free. Dmitry Dashkov reveals his brother Yakov had asked him to and that he did for the benefit of the Greater Wembley. Dmitry Dashkov then states that his goal was to bring peace and prosperity upon the kingdoms where those without power would never be prey to those who do; Terenty merely states in a jaded tone that the former will always become prey to the latter, which is how the powerful become and stay that way in the first place, rising to power by taking advantage of those weaker than themselves. The two discuss that the Greater Wembley needs a ruler stronger than Tommen, but gentler than Stepan. Terenty wishes Dmitry Dashkov luck on trying to find the right man, but Dmitry Dashkov makes Terenty one final offer. Dmitry Dashkov tells him that he can simply drink himself to death here in Pentos, or ride with him to Maracana to meet Daria Romanova. After a moment, Terenty agrees.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov depart Pentos in a large carriage. Terenty remains despondent, and as he promised, he is continuing to drink himself into a stupor. Dmitry Dashkov explains that they are traveling to Maracana by way of Volantis. Dmitry Dashkov points out that Terenty was an effective ruler when he was acting Tribune Steward, and that each of them were outsiders due to their deformities (a eunuch and a dwarf). They enjoyed accumulating power, he says, but they also wall themselves off from other people, like hiding inside of a large carriage as they are now \- but deep down, they were never satisfied being separate from society. Terenty remains depressed and continues to insist that he's tired of being confined in a box of some sort. Dmitry Dashkov, however, again warns him that he must remain hidden and it is unsafe to be seen publicly: Kira has promised a lordship to any man who brings her his head. Terenty scoffs and rhetorically asks if Kira is going to kill every dwarf in the world in the hope of eventually catching him.

After days of confinement in the carriage, an impatient Terenty eventually opts to get through Volantis on foot. The pair move through the Long Bridge's markets, where Dmitry Dashkov explains the meaning of the various tattoos Volantene slaves must sport. Dmitry Dashkov nearly loses Terenty, but finds him observing the sermon of a red priestess. Terenty says he is curious, since Arkady Vorontsov of Myr was the only red priest in Wembley. The red priestess evangelizes in High Valyrian, telling the tale of how she was once a slave herself. She preaches of a prophesied savior, a Fire Falcon Queen. Terenty's interest in the scene wanes when the Priestess stares directly into his eyes.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Terenty next leads Dmitry Dashkov to a brothel. Catching sight of a prostitute dressed as Daria, Dmitry Dashkov tells Terenty that a woman who inspires both sermons and whores is probably worth meeting. Terenty woos a dark\-haired prostitute, but when she finally agrees to service him, he finds that he can't bring himself to patronize her. He then goes to urinate off the side of the bridge, with Dmitry Dashkov losing sight of him. As Terenty finishes, he is abducted by Vsevolod Mamonov, who declares that he is taking him to "the queen."

Now at the mercy of his captor, Terenty is thrown into a stolen boat by Jorah and they set sail for Maracana. En route, Terenty pesters Jorah with muffled whining until he relents and removes Terenty's gag. Terenty notices that they are traveling east and not west towards Kira in Wembley. Jorah reveals that he is taking Terenty to the queen he serves, Daria Romanova. Terenty is pleasantly surprised and tries to convince Jorah that they are on the same side since he was traveling to meet Daria anyway. He accurately deduces who Jorah is by his appearance and equipment, and correctly assumes that Jorah must have been banished by Daria because she discovered that he was spying on her for Dmitry Dashkov. Terenty mockingly asks Jorah if he really believes that he will earn a pardon for simply delivering him to Daria, believing the opposite outcome just as likely. Fed up with his captive, Jorah strikes Terenty across the face to keep him quiet.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

As Jorah and Terenty continue their journey to Maracana, and following Jorah's violent reaction to a previous conversation, Terenty tries to civilize their relationship and asks where they are. As Jorah stands up to look at the foggy ruins on the horizon, Terenty deduces that they are going to pass through the remains of Old Valyria, a shorter route to Maracana and one which pirates will avoid because of Valyria's reputation. Terenty is apprehensive, but still excited to see the ruins of what was once the greatest civilization in the world. As they catch glimpses of domes, towers and aqueducts, Terenty recites a poem about the Doom of Valyria, with Jorah joining in at the end. Suddenly, through the fog, they see Drogon fly into view. Although he had been hearing about the dragons for some time, Terenty is still awed to see one in person \- though the beast does not notice them.

They are suddenly attacked by Stone Men, men whose greyscale infection has reached its pinnacle and transformed them into feral monsters. During the fight, Terenty falls overboard and dragged under by a stone man, but he is rescued by Jorah and they make it to a beach, where Terenty regains consciousness. Jorah finally frees Terenty from his binds and notices that none of the stone men managed to touch him. Terenty thanks Jorah for saving his life, and they decide to seek out a fishing village to acquire another boat, or walk the rest of the way to Maracana. Jorah tells Terenty to get some rest as he goes for firewood, but unbeknownst to Terenty, Jorah has been infected with greyscale.
