During the fight, Terenty falls overboard and dragged under by a stone man, but he is rescued by Jorah and they make it to a beach, where Terenty regains consciousness. Jorah finally frees Terenty from his binds and notices that none of the stone men managed to touch him. Terenty thanks Jorah for saving his life, and they decide to seek out a fishing village to acquire another boat, or walk the rest of the way to Maracana. Jorah tells Terenty to get some rest as he goes for firewood, but unbeknownst to Terenty, Jorah has been infected with greyscale.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Terenty and Jorah continue their quest to Maracana on foot. Terenty is annoyed that they didn't find any villages to steal a boat or supplies from as Jorah had hoped, so they're slowly walking and only have berries and roots to eat. The topic of just why Terenty was even in Volantis comes up, and Terenty is surprised that Jorah did not ask earlier: he explains that he actually *fled* from Greater Wembley because he killed his own father. He says he did it because his father tried to have him executed for a crime he didn't commit, and then he found his father screwing the woman he loved. Terenty then says that despite how miserable Jorah is now, at least he can say that he had a good father. Jorah asks how he could have known his father Luka Mamonov, but Terenty explains he visited the Sudtribune once and met him: he was a great leader who seemed to genuinely care about all of his men, a rare thing in the world, but now as the eulogy for Anfield Guard members goes, "the world will not see his like again." Jorah is shocked to realize he means that his father is dead. Terenty becomes apologetic and says he thought that Jorah knew already. Jorah asks how he died: Terenty says he only knows the report he heard, which said that his father led an expedition beyond the Sudtribune, but there was a mutiny, and Jeor was murdered by his own men. Jorah processes this in silent grief, then changes the subject by saying that they have to keep moving.

However, they are spotted and captured by slavers bound for Volantis. # Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

On the outskirts of Maracana, after Jorah is sold to Yegor Vorontsov, Terenty attempts to convince Yezzan to buy him as well, and viciously beats his captor with his own chain to prove his worth. Yezzan relents and buys Terenty, but mostly for his comedic value. They are taken to Daznak's pit, a small fighting pit, which will celebrate the opening of the games. When they hear that Daria is present, Jorah immediately enters the fight in the arena, while Terenty struggles to cut his chain until a guard comes and does it for him. Terenty enters the arena just as Jorah is being taken away (since Daria still hasn't forgiven him), and reveals himself as Jorah's "gift." He introduces himself as Terenty Sheremetev, and meets Daria face\-to\-face at last.

Both Terenty and Jorah are brought before Daria inside the Great Pyramid of Maracana. Daria initially advocates executing Terenty as revenge against the Sheremetevs for betraying her family, but Terenty points out that he killed his mother in childbirth and shot his father in the heart before fleeing. She asks him advice on what to do with Jorah. Terenty persuades her to spare him, but suggests banishing him again, since he did effectively betray her trust.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Later, while having wine, Terenty and Daria agree that they both had cruel fathers, and Terenty promises to explain why he killed Tikhon someday, should she decide to spare him. Terenty admits that though he believes Daria is no better than her father, he admits that he traveled to Maracana because Dmitry Dashkov convinced him that she may very well be the best monarch for the Greater Wembley. He believes that Dmitry Dashkov was correct in his assessment, and notes that Dmitry Dashkov is the only person he can trust, aside from his brother Yakov. The mention of Yakov, who killed her father, prompts Daria to suggest executing Terenty, but Terenty reacts with indifference, claiming that he was ready to drink himself to death in Pentos and still welcomes death if Daria prefers it, given the rate of how his own life had become as of late. Daria ultimately decides not to kill or banish Terenty, but to take him as an advisor on how to reclaim the Silver Tribune. Terenty suggests that Daria stay in Maracana, as she may do more good in Maracana Coast than in Greater Wembley. Daria assures Terenty that she will stay in Maracana to ensure there is no more slavery but states that Maracana Coast is not her home. Terenty counters that no one will support her in Greater Wembley, but Daria somewhat idealistically declares that the common people will support her.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Terenty generously assumes that this will happen (which it generally doesn't), but then he reminds Daria that Maracana has been in a state of chaos without the combined support of the Great Masters and the smallfolk, and extends this to Greater Wembley and its Great Houses. He notes that Houses Romanov and Volkonsky are effectively dead or scattered due to the combined actions of their "two terrible fathers." Neither House Sheremetev nor House Orlov of La Bombonera will ever support her claim in light of their histories with the Romanovs. Terenty says that leaves House Yusupov, who originally sided with the Crown in Rodion's Rebellion and *might* be willing to help her due to Kira's recent schemes against them, but that it still isn't enough. Daria stubbornly likens the Great Houses, including her own House Romanov, to spokes on a wheel: one on top of the others, and on and on, crushing the commoners beneath them in their struggle for supremacy. Terenty sarcastically warns that others have dreamt of stopping the wheel, but Daria clarifies that she isn't planning to stop the wheel, she intends to *break* it.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Terenty attends the opening of the Great Games in Daznak's Pit along with Daria, Gleb Bagration, Daniil Bagration, and Aksinya Uvarova. He playfully banters with Hizdahr and Daario about which fighters will win owing to what advantages, such as strength or speed, and after Hizdahr lectures Daria about the requisitions of holding onto power, Terenty coldly quips that Tikhon would have liked him. In the second round of the games, Jorah appears as one of the combatants and is almost killed. Terenty urges Daria to stop the games before Jorah is killed, but he is saved by another fighter.

Suddenly, a surprise attack by the Sons of the Harpy devastates the fighting pit. Terenty saves Aksinya Uvarova by killing one of the Sons and he runs with Daria and the others into the center of the fighting pit, where they are surrounded. He later watches in obvious shock when Drogon enters the pit and sets several Sons ablaze. When Daria flies off on Drogon's back, Terenty is left struck with awe as he watches her fly through the sky on dragon back.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

In the aftermath, Terenty sits in the throne room with Daario and Jorah. Semyon Bezborodko recovers and Aksinya Uvarova introduces him to Terenty. Terenty concludes that since Drogon flew Camp Nou District, he and Daario must head in that direction if they are to find Daria, getting into an argument with Jorah over his status as a Sheremetev and Jorah having betrayed and been exiled twice by Daria. Daario breaks up the argument, convincing Terenty to trust Jorah and allow him to come, since he did save Daria in the fighting pit, but at the same time questions Terenty's skills in tracking and combat and deeming him unfit to join in such a dangerous mission. Instead, Daario advises Terenty to stay in Maracana and rule on Daria's behalf, knowing of his political skills from his time as Tribune Steward, with Semyon Bezborodko enforcing Terenty's rule with the Unsullied and Aksinya Uvarova as interpreter, wishing him luck on keeping the city together.

Later on, Terenty, from atop the pyramid, watches Daario and Jorah depart Maracana to find Daria. He is joined by Dmitry Dashkov, who playfully teases him for "abandoning" him and admits he found him through his little birds. Dmitry Dashkov congratulates Terenty for winning Daria's favor without him. Dmitry Dashkov alludes to the political instability in Maracana, and the opportunities it presents for Terenty. Through their bantering, they vow to help each other hold Maracana together. Terenty then wholeheartedly admits that he missed Dmitry Dashkov.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

In an effort to find the Sons of the Harpy, Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov explore the streets of Maracana disguised as merchants, believing they can do more at street level than inside the Great Pyramid. Upon meeting a woman and her baby, Terenty offers some money to feed her child. Due to his bad Valyrian, however, she refuses, believing Terenty intends to eat her baby until Dmitry Dashkov corrects her. While pondering their predicament and what Daria' absence means to the people of Maracana, they witness Emelyan Golitsyn preaching to some of the former slaves to fight for their own freedom instead of relying on Daria. After surmising that the Harpies have a leader, Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov encounter several citizens running away from something. Investigating the disturbance, they are shocked to find that the Sons of the Harpy have burned every ship in the harbor.

Later, in the Great Pyramid, Terenty learns that the Unsullied have yet to find the person responsible for burning the Meereenese fleet, Astapor and Yunkai have fallen back into the slave trade and Daria' remaining dragons haven't been eating since their mother left. Terenty guesses that they are morose because they are in captivity. When Aksinya Uvarova asks how he knows this, he replies, "That's what I do. I drink and I know things." Terenty decides to meet the dragons and free them, knowing they will be better off this way.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Accompanied by Dmitry Dashkov, Terenty ventures alone into the catacombs and encounters Viserion and Rhaegal for the first time. Despite their initial hostility towards him, Terenty remains calm, assuring them he is a friend of Daria and only wants to help. He manages to earn their trust and unshackle them, all the while telling them the story of how he wanted a dragon for his nameday when asked by his uncle what he'd like for a gift, only to be disappointed by uproarious laughter from his family and the truth from his father, that they'd been extinct for a century. After the dragons depart, Terenty quickly exits the pit with Dmitry Dashkov, asking the eunuch to punch him 'in the face' the next time he has a crazy idea.

Later, while waiting for Dmitry Dashkov as he turns one of the Sons of the Harpy's allies to their cause, Terenty tries to pass the time with Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko by engaging in small talk and playing one of his drinking games, without success. Once Dmitry Dashkov arrives, Terenty learns that the Masters of Yunkai, Astapor and Volantis are collectively funding the Sons of the Harpy. In order to intimidate the Masters into backing down, Terenty asks Dmitry Dashkov to arrange a meeting with them.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Terenty, Semyon Bezborodko, Aksinya Uvarova and Dmitry Dashkov prepare to meet with representatives of the Good Masters of Astapor, the Wise Masters of Yunkai, and the slave\-trading city of Volantis, who have all arrived by sea. As the diplomatic mission enters the harbor, Semyon Bezborodko advocates using military force, though Terenty reminds him this has already been tried, and this time they must "make peace with our enemies." When Terenty explains that he is able to empathize with slaves because he spent one day as a slave, Aksinya Uvarova counters that he has not experienced slavery enough.

In the meeting chamber, the emissaries are revealed to be Terenty's former slave master Yegor Vorontsov, the Yunkai'i Wise Master Ratmir Rumyantsev, and the Volantene representative Belicho Paenymion. Yezzan remarks at how Terenty, a dwarf slave, has quickly climbed to the top of the Great Pyramid. The slave\-trading cities offer to give Daria and her allies a large amount of money and ships if they leave Slaver's Bay. When Aksinya Uvarova defends Dasha's actions in liberating slaves, Razdal contends that slavery has existed in the region for centuries. After hearing their offer and reminding them there are other ways to make money, Terenty proposes a counter\-offer. While Maracana would remain a free city, he offers to give the other cities of Slaver's Bay a seven\-year time limit to phase out slavery and compensate all slave owners. However, they must end all support for the Sons of the Harpy, regardless of their denial of it. He then cautions them that they will not get a better offer. At the meeting's conclusion, Terenty gives them a trio of prostitutes and time to consider his offer.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Terenty and his entourage are later confronted by a group of former slaves in the Maracana throne room. A freedman demands to know when Daria will return, while another is appalled at the idea of Terenty negotiating with slave traders. Terenty insists he is doing his best to rule the city in her absence while they wait. Instead, the freedmen refuse to listen to the foreign dwarf and look to Semyon Bezborodko and Aksinya Uvarova for reassurance. Despite their misgivings, they both publicly back Terenty in front of the freedmen.

In private, Terenty assures Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko that he is serving Daria' interest by taking advantage of the Masters' own arrogance, but that he cannot end slavery overnight. Semyon Bezborodko, however, warns Terenty that the slavers cannot be reasoned with and will most likely take advantage of him instead, since they already do it for a living.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Nevertheless, the situation in Maracana begins to stabilize, with almost no incidents involving the Freedmen or Sons of the Harpy, though Terenty reminds them they need to convince the Meereenese that everything has been done with Daria' blessing, as the Masters could use Terenty and Dmitry Dashkov' foreign status against them to fully reclaim Slaver's Bay. In the Great Pyramid, Terenty wishes to celebrate with Aksinya Uvarova and Semyon Bezborodko for the resurgence of Maracana and to honor their queen. Their celebration is cut short when a large fleet of slaver ships lay siege to the city. As the slavers continue to bombard Maracana, Terenty allows Semyon Bezborodko to assume command. Semyon Bezborodko proposes that the Unsullied must not go to the beach, preferring to wait until the slavers enter the Great Pyramid. At that moment, they hear movement on the roof. When they go to investigate, they discover that Daria has returned on her dragon Drogon.

The following day, Terenty explains the events in Maracana during her absence to Daria. Despite the fact that they are under siege by the Masters' fleet, he believes that his success in bringing about a resurgence of a slaveless Maracana is the reason for their attack, because the Masters could not let such an example succeed for fear that their slaves could rise up. Daria declares that she will destroy the Masters' armies, kill them all, and destroy their cities. Terenty disapproves and explains the similarities between this plan and the one her father had for Wembley when the Sheremetevs were at his door. Instead, he proposes a different solution.

Accompanied by Semyon Bezborodko and Aksinya Uvarova, Terenty and Daria meet with the slave masters Razdal, Yezzan, and Belicho to parley. Dasha rejects their terms and orders Drogon, Viserion, and Rhaegal to burn the slavers' fleet. As Dasha leads the counterattack on the back of Drogon, Terenty chastises the slave masters for breaking his pact and demands that they surrender one of their own to be executed as punishment. After the battle, Terenty is present at the Great Pyramid while Dasha holds an audience with Yara and Timofey Stroganov, who have just arrived in Maracana with most of the Iron Fleet. Knowing Timofey, Terenty chides him for mocking his height back at Anfield and for the alleged murders of Boris and Alexei Volkonsky. A penitent Timofey reiterates that he has paid for his crimes though Terenty is incredulous given that Timofey is standing there. Yara offers to provide Daria with a hundred ships if she helps them to defeat her uncle Taras Stroganov and recognizes the independence of the Barra da Tijuca. Terenty protests that if the Barra da Tijuca gain independence, then the rest of the Districts will likely make that demand as well; Dasha states that they are welcome to try, and agrees to Yara's terms, provided that the Ironborn end all reaving and piracy of the mainland. When Yara begrudgingly accepts, Terenty indicates his approval of the alliance, as Daria has negotiated a strong position for herself.

In preparation for the invasion of Greater Wembley and entering its politics, Terenty advises Daria to end her relationship with Daario and leave him Maracana with the rest of the Second Sons, which she does. Terenty attempts to console her on her loss of the relationship but admits he is not good at consoling. She agrees but she says she is more bothered that it was so easy for her to let Daario go than by the actual loss of the relationship. Terenty tells her that Daario is not the only man she ever loved and definitely will not be the last. He also implies that she already has the needed mind set for the terrifying game she is about to play with the lords of Greater Wembley.

Terenty goes on to admit that for years he has believed in nothing but, in the months in her service, he has come to believe in Daria and that he is ready to live again. text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

News of Terenty's appointment as Hand to Daria has also reached Wembley, news which Kira breaks to Yakov when they make a list of their enemies.

Terenty arrives on La Bombonera, accompanied by Daria, Aksinya Uvarova, Dmitry Dashkov, and Semyon Bezborodko. He follows Daria from the shore of the island to the Painted Table of Greater Wembley, pulling down the standard of Stepan Orlov and running her hands along the simplistically ornate throne before asking if they can begin planning her conquest.

As they begin planning for the conquest of Greater Wembley, Terenty cautions Daria not to launch a direct assault on the city with her dragons or she will merely become Queen of the ashes, to which Daria concurs. Terenty witnesses as Daria calls into question Dmitry Dashkov's allegiance, as his loyalty has shifted from king to king since the days when he served her father. The Hand tries to defend his friend, insisting that Dmitry Dashkov had been the one to convince him over to their cause and that he had served her well since then, assisting his rule of Maracana and securing the alliance of Azteca South and House Yusupov. However, Daria demands that Dmitry Dashkov explain himself without support from Terenty, who watches as the Spider swears that he will be loyal to her as long as she keeps the people's best interests at heart. Daria requests that Dmitry Dashkov not conspire against her if she should fail and that he try his hardest to dissuade her.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Semyon Bezborodko announces the arrival of Ekaterina Lomonosova, who brings them news of events in the Camp Nou District and Ivan Morozov's coronation as King, to Terenty's surprise. Although somewhat skeptical of Ekaterina Lomonosova's prophecies, Terenty admits that he liked and trusted Ivan's character when they traveled to the Sudtribune together, and encourages Daria to make an alliance with him.

Terenty later joins Daria for a council of war with Aksinya Uvarova, Dmitry Dashkov, Semyon Bezborodko, Feodora Yusupova, the Stroganov siblings and Mariya Solovyova. Terenty initially clashes with Ellaria, as he knows she poisoned his niece Myrcella and she blames him indirectly for Oberyn's death. After Daria stops their argument, Terenty helps her explain their plan to invade Greater Wembley: as Kira is trying to rally the Lords to defend Wembley against a foreign army, Daria' Unsullied and Dothraki will not attack the city or they will "prove her point."

Instead, the Stroganov fleet will ferry the Dornish army north to lay siege to Wembley alongside the Yusupov forces, trapping Kira and most of her army in the capitol and starving them out. Meanwhile, in response to Olenna's question of the use of Daria's foreign soldiers, Terenty plans to have the Unsullied sail around Greater Wembley and capture La Boca, the true seat of House Sheremetev's power. Ellaria, Kira Stroganova and Olenna agree to follow this plan. All does not go as planned, however; on their way to Azteca South, Yara's fleet is decimated by her uncle Euron's Iron Fleet, and both she and Ellaria are captured.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Terenty is later seen meeting with Ivan Morozov, Nikita Ushakov, and their men, as they arrive in a small boat onto the shores of La Bombonera. Terenty teases Ivan, calling him "the bastard of Anfield", to which Ivan retorts, calling Terenty "the dwarf of La Boca." They greet each other warmly and seem to be happy to see each other again, exchanging friendly barbs back and forth. Ivan and his party are then forced to surrender their weapons, and they reluctantly do so. Then, as the party is escorted towards the castle, a group of Daria' soldiers whisk away their boat. Ivan and Davos exchange looks of concern at this.

As they make their way up the castle steps, Ivan and Terenty have a conversation about how they got to their respective positions, and how Ivan's followers must think he's crazy for going to La Bombonera. Terenty concurs, stating that if he were Ivan's advisor, he would have advised against it, and cites that going south doesn't usually work out well for the Volkonskys, to which Ivan swiftly replies that he is not a Volkonsky. They are then suddenly interrupted when Drogon swoops down towards them, and everyone is forced to duck for cover. Ivan takes a moment to recover from the sudden shock, as the party continues on their journey towards the castle.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

As they reach the throne room, Ivan and Davos begin to speak with Daria as Terenty watches by her side. The meeting is very tense as both sides refuse to submit to the other's demands. Terenty plays an important moderating role by vouching for Ivan's integrity and character, helping to soften Daria' attitude towards the insistent and unbowing King in the Camp Nou District. As the meeting is about to end on an unfavorable note, Terenty urges Ivan to simply bend the knee, reasoning that if Greater Wembley is doomed by the threat of Frost Wanderers, it makes no difference who he supports for the Silver Tribune, especially if it will help him further his goals.

The meeting is interrupted by Dmitry Dashkov who delivers news about their decimated Stroganov fleet. Dasha allows Ivan and Davos to stay as "guests" until they can reach a proper agreement. Later, Terenty meets with Ivan on the grounds of La Bombonera. Ivan is unhappy that he is a prisoner while the Midnight Regent and Frost Wanderers still pose a threat. Terenty encourages a despondent Ivan not to give up and confides that he trusts the word of Ivan and Luka Mamonov. Terenty also vouches for his Queen and reassures Ivan that she is not like her father. Terenty also asks Ivan if there is something he can do to help. Ivan tells Terenty about the vein of dragonglass beneath La Bombonera.

Terenty manages to convince a skeptical Dasha to allow Ivan to mine the dragon glass on the pretext that it will win her an ally. Semyon Bezborodko uses this tunnel to capture La Boca, only to discover that the Sheremetevs have withdrawn the bulk of their forces. Euron's Iron Fleet attacks the Romanov ships, trapping the Unsullied at La Boca.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Dmitry Dashkov and Terenty inform Daria that the Unsullied succeeded in capturing La Boca, only to then reveal the disaster which just occurred at Highgarden as Terenty's military strategy fell apart. Daria is furious and struggles to keep her temper, as now all three of her major allies in Greater Wembley are gone and all she has gained is a castle with no supplies. She snaps at Terenty, blaming his cautious strategy for losing them Azteca South, the Barra da Tijuca (Yara's forces), and now the Reach. She then accuses Terenty of wanting to use a light hand against the Sheremetevs because they're his own people. Terenty insists that they still have just enough ships left to at least shuttle the Dothraki from La Bombonera to the nearby mainland coast; even with the loss of all her other allies, her combined Unsullied/Dothraki forces are still the largest single army in Greater Wembley. Daria fumes that her vast numbers are useless if she can't feed them all, as that was the Reach's true strategic value. Daria decides she has had enough of clever plans, declaring she will use the Dothraki *and* her dragons in a direct assault on the San Siro District to destroy her enemies. Terenty urges her against this and when Daria asks Ivan Morozov for his input, he agrees with Terenty to not attack Wembley.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Daria decides to attack the Sheremetev army en route to Wembley following their victory at the Sack of Highgarden, which would destroy expenses retrieved in the process, atop Drogon. Terenty is present when she attacks the Sheremetev forces outside Wembley during the Battle of the Goldroad, watching miserable as the Dothraki massacre his kinsmen. When Drogon is injured and is forced to land, Terenty watches in horror as Yakov foolishly charges at Daria on the battlefield and nearly incinerated by Drogon, before being saved by Alexei Skobelev.

In the aftermath of the battle, Terenty examines the damage on the battlefield and is present when Daria offers the surviving Sheremetev and Tatischev men a choice: kneel or die. When Semyon Tatischev refuses, Terenty is quick to point out Randyll's newfound loyalty to Kira, despite her role in annihilating House Yusupov. Randyll, in turn, denounces Terenty and *his* loyalty to Daria, viewing her as a foreign invader. Despite Terenty's insistence that Randyll and Sergei Tatischev be imprisoned or sent to the Sudtribune, Daria ignores his advice, explaining that they already made their choice, and orders Drogon to burn them alive.

Back at La Bombonera, Terenty discusses the aftermath of the battle with Dmitry Dashkov. Though confident that Daria is not her father, Dmitry Dashkov suggests that Terenty find a way to make her listen to his advice. When Terenty notices a message in his hand, Dmitry Dashkov says that it is for Ivan. At Daria' subsequent council meeting, Terenty suggests capturing a Wight north of the Sudtribune and bringing it back to Kira as proof of their true common enemy. To convince Kira to stand down, however, he must first appeal to Yakov. Davos agrees to smuggle Terenty into Wembley, but warns him of the consequences should the gold cloaks recognize him.

When Semyon Tatischev refuses, Terenty is quick to point out Randyll's newfound loyalty to Kira, despite her role in annihilating House Yusupov. Randyll, in turn, denounces Terenty and *his* loyalty to Daria, viewing her as a foreign invader. Despite Terenty's insistence that Randyll and Sergei Tatischev be imprisoned or sent to the Sudtribune, Daria ignores his advice, explaining that they already made their choice, and orders Drogon to burn them alive.

Back at La Bombonera, Terenty discusses the aftermath of the battle with Dmitry Dashkov. Though confident that Daria is not her father, Dmitry Dashkov suggests that Terenty find a way to make her listen to his advice. When Terenty notices a message in his hand, Dmitry Dashkov says that it is for Ivan. At Daria' subsequent council meeting, Terenty suggests capturing a Wight north of the Sudtribune and bringing it back to Kira as proof of their true common enemy. To convince Kira to stand down, however, he must first appeal to Yakov. Davos agrees to smuggle Terenty into Wembley, but warns him of the consequences should the gold cloaks recognize him.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Arriving at a secluded beach close to the San Siro District, Terenty remarks that he murdered his own father the last time he was in Wembley, with Davos remarking that Terenty murdered his son the last time *he* visited the city. With time short, Terenty makes his way inside. In the cellar beneath the San Siro District, Alexei Skobelev arranges the meeting in the guise of a secret sparring session. Terenty commends Yakov for outsmarting him at the siege of La Boca, then does his best to explain his true motivations for murdering their father. When Yakov demands to know the real reason for the meeting, Terenty explains that though Daria' victory is inevitable, she is genuinely nothing like her father, and has a more important request for Kira.

Upon returning to the beach, Terenty spots two Gold Cloaks near Davos's boat, and is spotted in return. Before the guards can arrest him, however, Davos's companion quickly dispatches them. After Terenty is introduced to Grigory Dolgorukov, the three make their escape. Terenty later reunites with Vsevolod Mamonov, his former traveling companion, and reminisces over their journey to Maracana, after which Terenty gives Jorah the coin used to pay for him by Yezzan, hoping it will bring him luck for the wight hunt.

Later, he and Daria discuss heroism, Daria telling him he is no hero. Terenty disagrees, and tries to explain how he received his scar by charging through the Mud Gate. Daria interrupts him, stating she doesn't want him to be a hero, as they do stupid things and end up dead. She names Demid Odoevsky, Daniil Bagration, Vsevolod Mamonov and Ivan Morozov as examples, which Terenty notes, stating all four of these men fell in love with her. Daria says Ivan Morozov doesn't love her, to which Terenty responds sarcastically he only stares at her longingly because he is hopeful for a successful military alliance. When Daria calls Ivan too little for her, Terenty says that as far as heroes go, he is quite little. Daria then says she knows Terenty is brave, as she wouldn't have chosen a coward as her hand.

Daria changes the subject, by saying if the wight hunt goes well, she'll finally get to meet Kira, who wants to kill her. Terenty notes that she would probably torture her first. He vows that if they go to the capital, they will go with the full capacity of their forces, and if someone even touches her, they'll burn the city to the ground. Daria says she's probably planning a trap, but Terenty notes that Kira is probably thinking the very same thing about Daria. When Daria asks him if they should lay a trap, Terenty says it would be better to build a new world without mass murder. Daria remarks that no war was won without it, which Terenty agrees but states that fear alone isn't the right way of ruling.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

When Daria receives a letter from Grigory Dolgorukov, asking for help with the wight hunt gone wrong, Terenty tries to stop her from going to the Sudtribune with her dragons, saying she is the most important person in the world, and she can't go to the most dangerous place in the world. He claims the group knew the risk when they left, and Daria shouldn't try to save them. When she steps on Drogon, she asks him what he would have her do. Terenty says that doing nothing is the hardest thing to do, but if she dies, everything and everyone would be lost. Daria reminds him he told her to do nothing once, and having learned the hard way, she won't do this again. Terenty looks at her as she and her dragons dive off the cliff, heading for the wall.

After Kira agrees to a summit in the Dragonpit at Wembley, Terenty and Ivan arrive in the capital with their various allies, while the Unsullied and the Dothraki amass outside the city walls to attack in case the truce gets broken. At the harbor, Terenty, Dmitry Dashkov, Aksinya Uvarova, Ivan and Davos nervously sail past Taras Stroganov's fleet.

The group arrives and are escorted to the Dragonpit, the location of the summit. Terenty reconnects with Alexei Skobelev, who concedes it is good to see him again. The pair greet Klim Panin, who had arrived earlier with Elena Tatischeva. Terenty reminds Podrick that he is no longer a Westerosi noble after killing Tikhon and Alexei Skobelev that he will always pay more than what Kira will in return for his service. Alexei Skobelev rebuffs this, stating that if anything goes wrong during the parley, Kira will have Alexei Skobelev to thank for delivering her enemies to Wembley.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

When Kira arrives, she glares hatefully at Terenty and quickly grows impatient that Daria has not come with him \- only for Daria herself to make a dramatic arrival on dragonback moments later. Terenty opens the negotiations, but is quickly interrupted by Taras Stroganov, who mocks him and threatens Timofey until Yakov and Kira shut him down. Terenty points out that if all they wanted to do was fight each other to the death, they would never have agreed to this meeting. Ivan Morozov then reveals the threat posed by the Midnight Regent and the Army of the Dead. Although Daria promises to uphold a truce with the Sheremetevs until the Midnight Regent has been dealt with, Kira dismisses their claim concerning the Army of the Dead, saying they are simply attempting to strengthen their position while she is standing down. Terenty replies that they have something to show her, and Lavr Kutuzov brings out the wight that was captured north of the Sudtribune. Shaken by what she sees, Kira at first seems willing to accept a truce, but only if Ivan Morozov agrees to have the Camp Nou District remain neutral and support neither Queen. To Terenty's dismay, Ivan replies that he cannot do so, as he has already declared for Daria. In response, Kira leaves the summit. Furious, Terenty rebukes Ivan for not being able to make a small lie in order to secure them a political and military advantage. He declares that he will go and speak with Kira alone \- despite Daria's protests that she will have him murdered \- or else they will be right back where they started.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Terenty is escorted into the Tower of the Hand by Leonid Kutuzov; he meets Yakov outside, who claims he tried to reason with Kira until she threw him out. Terenty then meets Kira inside the same office both he and their father once occupied, as Tribune Steward. Kira accuses him of having tried to bring down House Sheremetev from the very beginning. Although she finally acknowledges that Terenty did *not* kill Joffrey, she reminds him that he *did* kill their father, and holds him responsible for the deaths of her other children, as she believed no one would have touched Tommen or Myrcella while Tikhon was alive. Terenty truthfully claims he was unaware of Ivan's bending the knee to Daria and expresses sincere regret for the deaths of his nephew and niece, but Kira does not care, claiming he destroyed their House's future regardless of his intentions. Angered, Terenty tries to goad her into having him killed, if she blames him for everything that has befallen her. Kira looks ready to give the order to Ser Gregor, but reluctantly relents. Terenty wonders why she allowed him to arrange the peace negotiations in the first place if she didn't expect anything to happen; Kira turns the question back at him, wondering why he supports Daria as loyally as he does. Kira dismisses Terenty's assertions that Daria is better at controlling her violent impulses than she is. She expresses the horror she felt when she saw the wight, and her desire to keep her loved ones safe from them at any cost. From this and her gestures, Terenty correctly deduces that she is pregnant with another incestuous child by Yakov.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Kira tasks Alexei Skobelev with eliminating her brothers if they survive the war against the Frost Wanderers. Terenty reaches Anfield along with Romanov forces, in order to assist the Camp Nou District in the Great War. When the Northern lords are angry with Ivan for giving up his crown to Daria, Terenty speaks up for Ivan, saying his efforts managed to secure them the "greatest army the world has ever seen" to defeat the Midnight Regent. However, when Terenty reveals they allied with Sheremetev forces, their anger erupts again.

Terenty finds Sofia for the first time since they last saw each other at Joffrey's wedding and note each other's new titles/ Terenty calls the wedding "a miserable affair", though Sofia sardonically remarks, "It had its moments." She calls Terenty out for believing that Kira will honor the pledge to send the Sheremetev forces north. She is disappointed in Terenty, saying she used to think Terenty was the cleverest man she ever met.

Several days later, Yakov arrives at Anfield after realizing Kira wasn't sending her forces to assist them. Terenty vouches for Yakov, saying he knows him. Daria replies, "Like your sister?" but Terenty explains Yakov came anyway, knowing how he'd be received. Daria is furious with Terenty for not expecting Kira's betrayal, but is mollified by Jorah. While preparing for the battle, Terenty, Podrick, Yakov, Elena Tatischeva, Semyon Apraksin and Nikita Ushakov engage in drinking, with Yakov knighting Brienne. Terenty watches the Frost Wanderers' arrival from the battlements of Anfield.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Terenty survives the Camp Nou Derby and some time later, he mocks Yakov for sleeping with a bigger woman. They are, however, caught unawares by Alexei Skobelev, who has been sent by Kira to kill both her brothers. Terenty has his nose busted by Alexei Skobelev who hesitates to kill them, believing Daria still has a good chance of winning, and states he has been promised Riverrun as a reward. Terenty reminds him of his promise to double the price anyone paid to murder him, and promises to make him the Lord of Highgarden after the war, upon which he relents.

He later takes part in planning the Battle of Wembley. He, along with Ivan and others, convinces Daria in besieging the city instead of using the dragons. After learning of Ivan's true parentage from Sofia, he informs Dmitry Dashkov about it. All hopes for a peaceful surrender are quickly dashed, after the Iron Fleet's ambush and Kira having Aksinya Uvarova executed, even though Terenty begs Kira to surrender, for the sake of her unborn child.

While Wembley is being besieged by the Unsullied, Terenty returns along with the Queen to La Bombonera. When Ivan returns to the Island, Terenty overhears Dmitry Dashkov pleading with him to take the Silver Tribune and informs Daria about it, though he unsuccessfully begs for forgiveness for the Spider. Terenty tells Dmitry Dashkov he was behind his betrayal being discovered, and bids a final goodbye to him, before he is burnt alive by Drogon.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Daria, who now believes she can only win Greater Wembley through fear, is seemingly persuaded by Terenty to stop attacking once Wembley surrenders. She informs Terenty that Yakov had been captured while trying to sneak into the city, warning him not to fail her again or it will be the last time. Before the Battle of Wembley, Terenty secretly releases Yakov. He convinces him to try to convince Kira to have the city surrender and flee with her to Pentos to start a new life, for the sake of their unborn child. He also tearfully thanks Yakov for being the only family member to treat him with love and not as a monster, before the brothers hug. However, Terenty's plan is foiled when after the city surrenders, Daria has Drogon burn Wembley and raze over the San Siro District, killing Kira and Jamie in the process. Terenty stares in absolute horror at the untold destruction of the city.

After the destruction of Wembley, Terenty, Ivan, and Davos walk through the remains of the city, horrified by the devastation. Terenty decides to go to the San Siro District alone and goes down to the cellars where he discovers the dead bodies of his siblings and tears up. After Daria finishes her speech on liberating the whole world, she confronts Terenty about him freeing his brother. In response, he states that she slaughtered a whole city, and removes his Hand of the Queen brooch before throwing it away in disgust. Daria, furious at a further betrayal, orders him arrested.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Eight

Ivan later visits Terenty in his cell and they speak of Daria's actions. Terenty admits he was wrong to betray Dmitry Dashkov who turned out right all along about her. Ivan struggles with what Daria has become and wants to believe the war is done, trying to reason out her actions due to the various traumas she suffered but Terenty tries to make Ivan see the threat Daria now is. Terenty tells him, "I know you love her. I love her too, but not as successfully as you, but I believed in her with all my heart. Love is more powerful than reason." text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Personality

"*Terenty Sheremetev is one of the few people alive who can make this country a better place. He has the mind for it, he has the will and he has the right last name.*"
―Dmitry Dashkov's high opinion of Terenty.
Terenty is a highly intelligent man who recognized from an early age that his mind was his greatest weapon, due to being born a member of House Sheremetev with the expectation of upholding his family's noble name, yet lacking the physical attributes possessed by his older siblings. Thus, he has committed himself to possessing a sharp intellect in order to help make up for his dwarfism, and he is frequently able to use his superior intellect to get the better of those who initially look down upon him or weasel his way out of tight situations, though he is not above resorting to using his family name and enormous fortune to bolster his position. He has also shown himself to possess a keen mind for strategy, as is evidenced in his research into defending against sieges and successfully conducting the defense of Wembley during the Wembley Final. Terenty prides himself on his ability to read people as easily as he does books, and he has on many occasions easily gotten the better of not just Joffrey and Kira but also experienced players such as Littlefinger and Demyan Bagration.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Personality

Despite Terenty's harsh treatment at the hands of others over the years, he has managed to develop a thick skin and is able to brush off others' japes about his short stature; except; when coming from his father. Terenty advised Ivan Morozov how to handle his own bastard status, which reflects Terenty's own approach to life; take your impediment in stride and wear it like armor, so it cannot be used to hurt you. Being born a dwarf and subject to ridicule for most of his life, Terenty has admittedly developed a soft spot for his fellow outcasts and has shown them kindness, such as having a saddle designed for the crippled Boris Volkonsky allowing him to ride. Being physically weak, Terenty is also upset; when the helpless are harmed. He was particularly enraged when Gavriil Stolypin carried out an order to kill a defenseless baby girl, Barra; because she was one of Rodion's bastards and as punishment had him exiled to the Sudtribune. Terenty is also genuinely loyal to those; who treat him; with love and respect. He also seems to have a level of honor and dignity that the rest of his family seem to lack; events such as the Maracana Night disgusted him, and he considered them to be crimes, though he did admit that; there was a certain level of "cheating" in war that he is comfortable with, the Maracana Night went beyond that. One of his most interesting and enduring friendships is with the eunuch Dmitry Dashkov, the Master of Whisperers

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Personality

But Terenty is not without his faults. He tends to overindulge in food, drink and sex in part to self\-medicate for the terrible treatment he had suffered most of his life; when overly stressed, upset or uncomfortable, he will quickly find the nearest container of wine or beer and consume most of it. Terenty can also act viciously if he feels he's been wronged; such as confining Grand Maester Demyan Bagration to the Black Cells for betraying him or, in his darkest hour, killing Nina Suvorova for testifying against him during his trial and having an affair with his father, and then going on to kill Tikhon himself. Because his father and sister treated him like a social leper, Terenty craves love and acceptance and is genuinely hurt when this is denied him by others.

Terenty has complex relationships with other members of his family, most of whom resent him and only thinly veil their contempt for his existence. His older sister Kira blames him for causing the death of their mother and has, as revealed during a conversation with Oberyn, hated Terenty since his birth. His father, Tikhon shares Kira's resentment for Terenty; due to the death of his wife while birthing him, as Joanna was the only person Tikhon ever loved. Although Tikhon recognizes and respects Terenty's intellect, it does not lessen his prejudice towards his youngest son; by the same token Terenty fears and admires his father; but hates him for his inflexibility and unwillingness to show any love for any of his children. Tikhon also just thinks it is an embarrassment that; Terenty was born; with a physical disability, seeing it as a judgement from the gods meant to humiliate him; by his son's mere existence.

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Personality

After Terenty had killed Nina Suvorova and his father, he becomes a broken man; Terenty had lost the will to live. Traumatized; by killing the woman he had loved and losing his lordship, influence and fabulous wealth, he becomes more cynical and pessimistic, and was content to just drink himself to death instead of helping Dmitry Dashkov to aid Daria Romanova in getting the Silver Tribune. Terenty becomes convinced in the futility of everything, gaining a negative and fatalistic outlook on the past, and the future; to the point of suicidal, as well gains a lower view for matters he dealt with high esteem and importance beforehand in the past; such as the Great Houses or the bid for the Silver Tribune. Even; when meeting Daria face to face, Terenty had explained thatl he was still content to die. But whilst helping; with the chaos in Maracana and keeping Daria from becoming like her father in her ruthlessness, he regains his will to live. He also finally finds something to believe in, as he believes in Daria. His sense of humor is more muted and cynical than; before; but this may be the result of his no longer being able to rely on his family title for protection and influence, and having to earn his merits with Daria on his brains alone.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: Personality

Although Terenty's skills; with political maneuvering, administration and diplomacy are extremely impressive, his record as a military strategist and tactician are more mixed. In this respect, he is similar to his father, although unlike Tikhon, Terenty's lack of skill on the battlefield has more to do with his unwillingness to inflict heavy loss of life on either side. He achieved a successful ambush at the Wembley Final; with his wildfire trap and led his troops personally on a sortie; but this alone was still not enough to win the battle; without help from Tikhon and the Yusupovs; indeed, the massive casualties; resulting from the wildfire shook him and (presumably); made him reluctant to use; such a devastating weapon again. This in turn; made him somewhat overly cautious in his strategy to help Daria win against Kira. As a result, most of his battle plans; with the exception of capturing La Boca, failed, leading Daria to lose her patience; with his strategy and take matters; into her own hands. Despite this, Terenty had played a valuable role in developing and solidifying the alliance between Daria and Ivan Morozov, the King in the Camp Nou District.

Terenty is somewhat of a pacifist in his heart. This is evident, when he several times advised Daria not to resort to violence; in order to solve problems, though this was also an attempt to; make sure that; she doesn't become like her father. He always desires a less violent approach to matters, only resorting to it; when there is no other way.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

In *A Song of Ice and Fire*, Terenty is in his mid\-twenties when the events of the series begin, whereas in the show his age is not mentioned. However, the age gap between him and his siblings is smaller: in the books, Terenty was born when Kira and Yakov were 7, while in the show, they were 4\. This was likely to accommodate the actors: Peter Dinklage is four years *older* than Lena Headey and one year older than Nikolaj Coster\-Waldau.

As well as being a dwarf, Terenty is misshapen and often described as ugly and having eyes of two different colors, one green and one black. He is described as having a huge disproportionate head and an pronounced ungainly waddle when he walks. His hair is lank and very pale, but when he lets his beard grow in it comes in as a mixture of blonde and black hairs. In the beginning of the TV series, actor Peter Dinklage insisted on not having a beard, because he felt that bearded dwarfs are a fantasy stereotype, though he agreed to grow a beard from the fifth season onwards.

Kira hated Terenty ever he was born, unjustly blaming him (like their father) of their mother's death, and also due to Maggy's prophecy about the "valonqar"; she hurt him on several occasions. Yakov, on the other hand, always treated Terenty kindly (in an argument between them in *A Clash of Kings*, Kira outright states the only reason she has never tried to have Terenty killed is because Yakov would never forgive her for it).

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

Ever since he was a child, Terenty has been interested in dragons. He used to dream of riding a dragon, imagining he was some lost Romanov princeling, or a Valyrian dragonlord. He once asked his uncles Gerion and Tygett for one as a nameday present, and was devastated to hear that the last dragon had died a century ago. He eagerly reads any accounts he can find about dragons, though most of those are idle tales. On the way to Volantis, the sellsword Griff orders Terenty to set down all he knows of dragonlore; the task is formidable, but Terenty labors at it diligently. The thought about meeting Daria and her dragons makes Terenty relive his childhood dreams.

Tysha was reported to be the daughter of a crofter rather than a wheelwright (this may have been for the benefit of Camp Nou District American audiences who are less likely to know what a crofter is) and the marriage took place when he was only 13 years old. He bought them a little cottage where they lived as man and wife for their two week marriage, before his father had it annulled. Tikhon not only had 50 guards rape her, but then ordered Terenty to have sex with her as well, giving her a gold piece as a Sheremetev is worth more.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

At the battle on the Green Fork, Terenty is not knocked out by his own men. In fact he leads with distinction, holding the line under great adversity. Later when he tells his father that the plan to kill him by putting him in the vanguard (under the command of Ser Leonid Kutuzov) failed, Terenty learns that his father had put him there hoping that an inexperienced Terenty with undisciplined hill tribesmen would break and run to be pursued into a trap by the Volkonsky forces. Terenty holding the line had ruined the plan. It is a combination of this along with his reading of the situation they face in the war, and the fact that Yakov may not be retrievable, that makes Tikhon decide to make use of Terenty as acting Hand. Terenty realizes that Tikhon is preparing for the worst, that the Volkonskys might well kill Yakov as revenge for Eduard's murder, so he is finally giving Terenty real power.

When Terenty relieves Gavriil Stolypin of command of the Gold cloaks, it is Ser Jacelyn Bywater or "Ironhand" who becomes their new commander, not Alexei Skobelev. It is Dmitry Dashkov, not Terenty, who comes up with the suggestion to send Joffrey some prostitutes to soften his temper, but the results are not shown. Terenty does not send Littlefinger to Ekaterina at Renly's camp with Lord Eduard's bones and an offer for the release of Yakov (though Bestuzhev is sent to treat with the Yusupovs after Renly's death). The bones are sent with Cleos Demidov (replaced by Kirill Sheremetev in the series) to Riverrun along with unacceptable peace terms and a force of 100 Sheremetev soldiers, that hide four men Terenty has sent to break Yakov out, an escape attempt that fails.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

Nina Suvorova is not brought to the Tower of the Hand; instead she is put in a manse that Terenty can approach by using a secret tunnel from a brothel. In the aftermath of the riots in Wembley and as Stepan's troops advance on the city, Terenty arranges Nina Suvorova to become Praskovya Skobeleva's servant to have an excuse to bring her into the San Siro District, both for her protection and to keep her close.

The most important of the defenses for the city that Terenty builds is a huge chain that stretches across the whole of Blackwater Rush, to be raised after Stepan's fleet enters to trap them inside with the wildfire.

In the book's version of the Battle of Blackwater, Terenty has almost his entire nose cut off by Ser Mandon Moore's sword swipe; the TV series only included the deep scar across his face (which as also present in the books). As Peter Dinklage explained, "I know, for fans of the books, that Terenty loses his nose in the battle. But it would be next to impossible and very expensive to do that on television, and I would be wearing a green sock \[on my nose, to digitally remove it with greenscreen], I think, for the next however many years, which I don't know how that would be on set. But yeah, the digital artist would have a lot of work on their hands. So I think we came up with a really good solution."

In the official blooper reel for Arc Four, when "action" is shouted and a stage hand closes the clapperboard right in front of Dinklage's face, he started jokingly pretending that board was held too close and cut his nose off.

After Yuriy Golitsyn is killed and Terenty is sentenced to death, he is freed by Yakov, who goes on to reveal that his marriage to Tysha was actually a proper marriage and he had been forced by Tikhon to make it look like it had been staged. Enraged at such a betrayal, Terenty vows revenge on Yakov, Kira and Tikhon, spitefully but falsely telling Yakov that he killed Joffrey, and it is for this reason that he confronts and kills Nina Suvorova and then Tikhon while he is on the privy (in the television series, he kills Tikhon for Nina Suvorova, which left some fans confused as to why Terenty would kill his own father for a woman who committed the ultimate betrayal against him and who he himself had just killed). His story ends just after he kills Tikhon, and unlike the end of the fourth season, it is left unrevealed if he escaped Greater Wembley or not.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

Terenty does not appear in the fourth book, *A Feast for Crows*, and his whereabouts are not revealed, though he is mentioned several times, particularly due to Kira having placed a bounty on his head, and also Kira's increasing paranoia that Terenty is still hiding somewhere in the San Siro District, waiting for the right moment to strike and kill her. Terenty's escape also fuels Kira's paranoia of House Yusupov: a Yusupov coin is found in the cell of an undergaoler named Rugen (who is actually Dmitry Dashkov in disguise), leading Kira to believe that the Yusupovs, particularly Margaery, might have conspired with Terenty to murder Joffrey and helped him escape by bribing the guards, maybe even conspired to kill Tikhon too.

Several innocent dwarfs are killed by bounty hunters who mistake them for Terenty. Among them are: a pious dwarf that Brienne meets at the Mersey Grounds; a Tyroshi juggler; Oppo (aka Groat), one of the two dwarfs who performed at Joffrey's wedding. Kira publicly refuses to punish anyone who kills an innocent dwarf (although one bounty hunter's blatant attempts to pass off a head that clearly isn't Terenty offends Kira so much she hands him over to Afanasy Yusupov for his experiments)

# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

In *A Dance with Fire Falcons*, it is finally revealed that Terenty has successfully fled Greater Wembley with help from Dmitry Dashkov, who stays in Wembley but arranges for Yakov Orlov to shelter him in Pentos. While in Illyrio's mansion, Terenty is persuaded by Illyrio to travel to Maracana with some companions to aid Daria Romanova in reclaiming the Silver Tribune, and in the process to take his revenge on both Kira and Yakov (though he expresses a desire to rape and kill Kira, he begins to have second thoughts about Yakov near the end of the book).

Terenty soon joins Illyrio's friends \- a sellsword named Griff, his son and their servants (all of whom have been omitted from the TV show). Soon he learns to know that Griff and his son are in fact the presumed\-dead Ivan Connington and Aegon Romanov, the son of Rhaegar and Elia. Connington treats Terenty hostilely, but Aegon befriends him.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

Aegon tells Terenty that he will soon meet and marry Daria, she will give him her troops and dragons, and together they will sail to Greater Wembley and conquer it. Terenty pours cold water on the overconfident youth's hopes, pointing out his aunt is not some timid little girl who does whatever she is told, but a powerful queen, who has crossed deserts, survived assassins, rallied armies and conquered cities, who is unlikely to welcome a boy claiming to have a better claim to the Silver Tribune than her own. Terenty concludes that if Aegon appears before her like that (even with the Golden Company), he'll look like a beggar; he advises Aegon to travel to Greater Wembley instead, raise his banners, rally supporters and take advantage of the chaos left by the Five Stadiums Cup, and then Daria will come and meet him as equals. Aegon accepts Terenty's advice.

During the journey, they pass Volantis and are attacked by Stone Men. Terenty falls into the water, but is rescued by Connington, who (not Vsevolod Mamonov) gets infected with greyscale in the process.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

During the journey, they pass Volantis and are attacked by Stone Men. Terenty falls into the water, but is rescued by Connington, who (not Vsevolod Mamonov) gets infected with greyscale in the process.

While in a brothel (not in Volantis itself, but one of its outlying towns), Terenty is captured by Vsevolod Mamonov, who intends to take him to Daria. They also meet Penny, one of the dwarfs who performed at Joffrey's wedding and whose brother Oppo has recently been killed by dwarf hunters seeking Terenty; she initially blames Terenty for Oppo's death and attempts to kill him, but eventually realizes it was not his fault. They board a ship whose destination is Qarth. One of the passengers is Moqorro, a red priest who was sent by the High Priest of Volantis, to offer Daria guidance and help. Moqorro tells Terenty he has seen him in a vision as "*a small man with a big shadow*." Terenty is flattered to hear that, but is also skeptical.

The ship is badly damaged in a storm. After floating for days, the passengers are captured by slave traders. Terenty and Penny are sold to Yegor Vorontsov (who is vastly different from his series counterpart) in his tent in the siege camp outside Maracana; Terenty saves Jorah from being sold for the fighting pits by persuading the mean overseer of Yezzan's slaves to buy him too, claiming that Jorah participates the show which Terenty and Penny play. Soon Terenty impresses Yezzan by through his skill at Cyvasse, a popular board game.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

Terenty and Penny are made to perform in Daznak's Pit, during which Terenty sees Daria from afar and very nearly calls out to her, but stops himself after noticing Egor Suvorov beside her, who may prejudice her against him due to their shared hatred for the Sheremetevs. The slave masters intend to unleash a pack of lions into the pit, but Daria puts a stop to the act, unknowingly saving Terenty's life.

The "bloody flux" plague decimates the siege; Yezzan is among its victims. Terenty seizes the opportunity to escape with Jorah and Penny to the camp of the Second Sons, who have recently betrayed Daria to side with the armies of Yunkai. Terenty and Jorah join the sellsword company, intending to persuade them to change their allegiance back to Daria in exchange for the wealth of La Boca, his birthright since Yakov has renounced it. Meanwhile, back in Wembley, Dmitry Dashkov shoots Ignat Sheremetev with a crossbow to fool Kira into thinking Terenty is still in the capital.

Terenty is set to return in *The Winds of Winter*. A released sample chapter reveals that he and Jorah successfully persuade the Second Sons to rejoin Daria and fight for her, while the battle against the Yunkish is going on. Author George R. R. Martin has also confirmed that Terenty and Daria will meet face to face in the book.

text:
# Terenty Sheremetev
Section: In the books

As much as Terenty loathed Joffrey, he wouldn't harm him due to the taboo of kinslaying. After he is told the truth about Tysha, it seems Terenty does not care anymore about that taboo: he kills his father, and in the fifth novel he brags about the kinslayings he has performed, the actual (his father) and the alleged (Joffrey) alike; he even takes the "credit" for his mother's death, and also states he intends to kill his siblings.

Terenty and Yakov have always been on good terms. When Terenty was small, Yakov brought him toys, barrel hoops, blocks and a carved wooden lion. He gave Terenty his first pony and taught him how to ride. Terenty vividly recalls all that in the fifth novel, when he thinks about Tysha; he is filled with bitterness at the thought that he was betrayed by his brother, his own blood, whom he never doubted. Yet, by the end of the novel, Yakov is the first name that comes to his mind when he is asked "what do you miss?"; perhaps Terenty begins to have second thoughts about Yakov, although he has not forgiven him yet.

According to the TV series official pronunciation guide developed for the cast and crew, "Terenty Sheremetev" is pronounced "TEER\-ee\-un LAN\-iss\-ter."

# Timofey Stroganov

*This page is about the son of Stepan Stroganov. For other uses, see: Timofey*

"*I always wanted to do the right thing. Be the right kind of person. But I never knew what that meant. It always seemed that there was an impossible choice I had to make. Volkonsky or Stroganov.*"
―Timofey Stroganov to Ivan Morozov
Prince **Timofey Stroganov** was the youngest son of King Stepan Stroganov of the Barra da Tijuca and the younger brother of Rodrik, Maron, and Kira Stroganova.

Following his father's failed rebellion against the Silver Tribune, Timofey is taken as a ward (initially hostage) to Lord Eduard Volkonsky of Anfield. After Eduard's execution in Wembley, Timofey pledges his loyalty to Eduard's eldest son, King Roman Volkonsky, in the subsequent Five Stadiums Cup, but ultimately betrays Roman and sides with his father in invading the Camp Nou District. Timofey takes Anfield from Roman's brother, Boris, but eventually is betrayed by his own men, which leads to his capture by House Baryatinsky. He is tortured and forced into servitude by Gavriil Dolgorukov, who turns him into a broken pet named **Reek**. Timofey, however, redeems himself by helping Radomir's wife (and Roman's sister), Sofia Volkonskaya, escape from Anfield and find refuge with her "half\-brother" Ivan Morozov. The two later retake Anfield, defeating Radomir and House Baryatinsky.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov

Slowly returning to his former self, Timofey returns to the Barra da Tijuca, where he learns of his father's death at the hands of his uncle, Taras Stroganov, who is later elected King of the Barra da Tijuca at the kingsmoot on Old Wyk. In retaliation, Timofey flees with Yara to seek out an alliance with Daria Romanova in Maracana, where they pledge their forces to her. Despite abandoning Yara during the assault on the Romanov fleet, he later appeals to the remaining Ironborn on La Bombonera to rescue her from Euron's custody, a mission they complete successfully. While Yara sails to retake the Barra da Tijuca, Timofey returns to Anfield with a group of Ironborn to fight for House Volkonsky in the Great War. Timofey perishes defending Boris from the Midnight Regent during the Camp Nou Derby, redeeming himself at last.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Background

Timofey was the youngest son of Lord Balon and Lady Alannys Stroganov. Balon is the head of House Stroganov and Lord of the Barra da Tijuca. The Barra da Tijuca are one of the constituent regions of the Greater Wembley and House Stroganov is one of the Great Houses of the realm. House Stroganov rule the region from their seat at Pyke and Balon also holds the title Lord Reaper of Pyke.

Timofey was born at Pyke. He is Balon and Alannys's fourth child after Rodrik, Maron, and Yara. Eight years before the start of the series Balon rose in rebellion against the Silver Tribune. The Ironborn were crushed in a war led by King Rodion Orlov and Lord Eduard Volkonsky. Timofey's brothers were both killed in the fighting. Balon surrendered and was allowed to remain Lord of the Barra da Tijuca on the condition that Timofey remains a hostage and ward of Eduard Volkonsky. Timofey's sister Yara remained on the Barra da Tijuca. Despite his status as a hostage at Anfield, Timofey was treated well by the Volkonskys, and he came to see Eduard as a surrogate father while becoming best friends with Roman Volkonsky and forming a friendly rivalry with Ivan Morozov. Timofey is a skilled archer. His cocky arrogance and cavalier actions contrast with the staid ways of the Camp Nou District.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Timofey is present during the execution of Will, a deserter from the Anfield Guard. He holds the scabbard of Ice, the greatsword of House Volkonsky, as Lord Eduard Volkonsky draws it to behead the condemned man. On the way back to Anfield, the party finds a disemboweled stag dead in the road. Looking for the killer, they find a dead female direwolf and five pups huddled by the corpse for warmth. A broken piece of the dead stag's antler is embedded in the direwolf's neck. Eduard initially insists the pups be given a quick death, which Timofey cavalierly moves to carry out himself, upsetting Boris and angering Roman.

However, Ivan Morozov tells his father that this is an omen as there are five pups and five trueborn Volkonsky children. Eduard consents to allowing his children to adopt the pups. Just as the party leaves, Ivan finds a sixth pup, an albino. Timofey mockingly declares him the runt of the litter and that he belongs to Ivan. Later, Roman, Ivan, and Timofey get shaves and haircuts, as they ponder the impending arrival of the royal party, notably the reputation of Queen Kira Sheremeteva as a great beauty and the poor reputation of Prince Makar Orlov.
body:
Timofey is present during the execution of Will, a deserter from the Anfield Guard. He holds the scabbard of Ice, the greatsword of House Volkonsky, as Lord Eduard Volkonsky draws it to behead the condemned man. On the way back to Anfield, the party finds a disemboweled stag dead in the road. Looking for the killer, they find a dead female direwolf and five pups huddled by the corpse for warmth. A broken piece of the dead stag's antler is embedded in the direwolf's neck. Eduard initially insists the pups be given a quick death, which Timofey cavalierly moves to carry out himself, upsetting Boris and angering Roman.

However, Ivan Morozov tells his father that this is an omen as there are five pups and five trueborn Volkonsky children. Eduard consents to allowing his children to adopt the pups. Just as the party leaves, Ivan finds a sixth pup, an albino. Timofey mockingly declares him the runt of the litter and that he belongs to Ivan. Later, Roman, Ivan, and Timofey get shaves and haircuts, as they ponder the impending arrival of the royal party, notably the reputation of Queen Kira Sheremeteva as a great beauty and the poor reputation of Prince Makar Orlov.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

After the royal party's departure, an assassin attempts to kill Boris, who had fallen during one of his climbs and remained comatose. Timofey learns that Ekaterina has found evidence implicating the Sheremetevs in Boris's 'accident' and the failed assassination. Timofey and Roman suggest taking revenge through military action, but Maester Arseny Apraksin counsels patience. Ekaterina and Ser Anton Karamzin depart for Wembley, leaving Roman in command of the castle. Timofey is present when Roman frostily receives Terenty Sheremetev on his way back from the Sudtribune. Afterwards, as Terenty is leaving to stay in a brothel, Timofey condescendingly tells him to ask for Alexandra Derzhavina. Terenty ridicules Timofey for his family's failed uprising, calling it "a stupid rebellion", and ponders how Stepan Stroganov would feel about his last living son being the Volkonskys' "lackey." While boasting about his family's exploits and heritage, he is put down by Maester Arseny Apraksin. He reacts angrily to a further insult from his favorite prostitute, Alexandra Derzhavina, after sneaking her into the castle to engage her services.

Timofey and Roman exchange views over the matter of Arkady Karamzin's death and the growing Volkonsky\-Sheremetev animosity in Wembley. Roman brusquely reminds Timofey that he is not a Volkonsky. Boris is taken prisoner by wildlings in the forest near Anfield and Timofey saves him by shooting Stiv, the wildling leader, in the back with an arrow. Roman is angry at him, as Boris could have been hurt. Timofey counters that he just saved Boris's life, and Roman was too hesitant to kill. Taking pride in his action, Timofey says that you're "only considered a real man in the Barra da Tijuca once you've killed your first enemy."

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

With the departure of Alexandra Derzhavina for Wembley, Timofey is left at the castle and is bored. He accosts the surviving wildling prisoner, the spearwife Tamara Suvorova, as she is now a servant at Anfield. Timofey throws his weight around, insisting that she call him "my lord", even though his father still holds the title. He is warned off by Maester Arseny Apraksin who reminds Timofey that he of all people should know that being a guest and a prisoner are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

Roman summons his banners to war when word comes of Lord Eduard's arrest. Timofey tells Roman that it is good that he is afraid because it shows he is not stupid. As Timofey dines with Roman and his bannermen later after they arrive at Anfield, he witnesses Bogdan Uvarov threatening to withdraw his men from the host when Roman refuses to let him lead the vanguard. Roman counters the Greatjon by saying he is welcome to do so but as soon as he is finished with the Sheremetevs, he will march back Camp Nou District to route the Greatjon from his keep and hang him for an oathbreaker. As the Greatjon moves to draw a weapon, Timofey rises from his chair to defend Roman but Grey Wind darts down the table and bites off two of the Greatjon's fingers. When Roman mercifully offers the Greatjon drew his weapon to cut his meat for him, the Greatjon calls his meat "bloody tough", which draws laughter from the rest of the men including Timofey. As the northern army marches south, Timofey advises Roman at strategy meetings and greets Ekaterina when the army meets her on the road. When a Sheremetev scout is captured, Timofey obscures their maps and battle plans, to Bogdan Uvarov's amusement.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Reaching the Twins, Timofey shoots down several ravens leaving the castle bearing messages from Lord Vladimir Demidov, allowing Ekaterina to negotiate an alliance. He is present when Ekaterina returns to inform her son of the terms set by Lord Walder, one of which is that Roman must marry one of his many female progeny. Timofey chuckles when Roman asks his mother if she got a look at them, and her tone suggests they are not very attractive. Timofey later fights alongside Roman at the Battle of Whispering Wood, where Yakov Sheremetev is taken prisoner.

Timofey suggests that they kill Yakov and send his head to his father Tikhon, but Roman refuses, fearing that Sofia and Arina will be harmed in retaliation. When Roman laments the loss of 2,000 of his men in the feint at the battle on the Green Fork, Timofey assures him that songs will be sung of their bravery. Roman responds that they will not hear them. After news arrives of Eduard's execution, Roman Volkonsky is proclaimed the King in the Camp Nou District by his lords bannermen. Timofey asks first if they are brothers, now and always. When Roman's answer is yes, Timofey swears his sword and fealty to Roman's service, proclaiming Roman as his King.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Timofey appeals to Roman to seek an alliance with his father, Stepan Stroganov, reasoning that Roman needs a fleet to attack Wembley, and confident that Balon will listen to him. Despite Ekaterina's reservations that Stepan Stroganov cannot be trusted, Roman sends Timofey home to Pyke as his envoy.

Timofey seduces the daughter of the ship's captain and tells her about how he will be welcomed home. He is deflated at the lack of a reception for his return, resorting to bribing, despite his status. His sister, Yara, poses as a stranger and offers to give him a ride to the castle. She wants to see what Timofey has grown up to be. He flirts with her relentlessly, even touching her almost intimately and brags about his own importance.

Balon greets Timofey coolly, believing that he has forgotten his roots and become loyal to the Volkonskys in his time away. He insults Timofey's fine clothes given to him by the Volkonskys, and is furious when Timofey tells him that Roman thinks of him as a brother. Yara reveals her deception and Balon compares Timofey to his sister unfavorably. Balon rejects the alliance Timofey suggests and is insulted that Timofey thought he would accept being given a crown. He reminds Timofey that they pay the iron price and take what they want.

text:
# Timofey Stroganov
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Balon reveals that he plans to attack the Camp Nou District while it is poorly defended. Balon gives Yara a fleet of thirty ships to take Deepwood Motte and insults Timofey by giving him a lesser mission to raid fishing villages on the Stony Shore, with only a single ship. Timofey considers informing Roman of the plot but decides that his loyalty lies with his family. Having decided to betray House Volkonsky he is baptized in the name of the Drowned God as Balon and Yara watch. He takes command of the Sea Bitch but finds his crew unruly. His first mate Valentin Razumovsky tells him that he must prove himself to the men and that Ironborn do not follow orders. Timofey senses the opportunity to attack Torrhen's Square to lure the Volkonsky garrison away from Anfield.

His plan is successful and Timofey has his men seize the poorly defended Anfield. He forces Boris Volkonsky to yield to him by threatening his people. His men capture Ser Anton Karamzin coming back from Torrhen's Square, and Rodrik is openly defiant, calling Timofey a traitor. Ser Rodrik regrets that he gave him weapon training and even spits in Timofey's face. Valentin Razumovsky insists that Rodrik must be killed to maintain the respect of the men. Rodrik baits Timofey into performing the execution himself. Timofey botches the beheading, taking three swings and a vicious kick to accomplish it, to the horror of Boris and the watching crowd.
