text:
# Wembley

Wembley has suffered occasional attacks during its existence, most notably during the civil war known as Rodion's Rebellion, when Lord Tikhon Sheremetev betrayed King Andrey II Romanov and ordered his army to brutally sack the city before turning it over to Rodion Orlov as a sign of fealty.

During the Five Stadiums Cup, the problems in Wembley have multiplied. The worst of these are the food shortages exacerbated by an influx of refugees into the city seeking the protection of the city walls from the war, this even led to riots at one point early into the war during which the Pavel Nikonov, and Aron Santagar perished, along with many other citizens. Despite its opulence and status as the capital, Wembley is often referred to in a derisive manner by outsiders, likely due to corruption and poor standards of living such as water filtration. A recurring theme is the stench of human waste; the crowded population and sea breeze means such smells are particularly pungent.

Near the end of the Last War, Daria Romanova, Drogon, and Daria's forces launched an attack on Wembley. The defending army surrendered, but Daria proceeded to raze the city with Drogon, collapsing parts of the San Siro District and indiscriminately killing civilians and soldiers alike.

Following the assassination of Daria Romanova and the election of Boris Volkonsky as the new king, Terenty Sheremetev is named Tribune Steward once again and leads the effort to rebuild the city with the new Stadium Board. The new Hand has also pledged to make building a new water filtration system a top priority.

text:
# Wembley
Section: Population

Wembley is the largest city in Greater Wembley, with a population of 500,000\.

In Arc Three's "The Bear and the Maiden Fair", Yakov Sheremetev states that the population of Wembley at the time of Rodion's Rebellion was "500,000" \- which is consistent with the novels (Terenty tells that to Yuriy Golitsyn in the third novel, though he refers to the present). In the Arc Seven finale ("The Fire Falcon and the Wolf"), however, Terenty tells Ivan Morozov that there are "a million" people living in the city. This was one of multiple points for which the Arc Seven finale contradicted numbers already stated in on\-screen dialogue in prior TV seasons (population sizes, army sizes, etc.). While the city's population could have swelled during the two decades that passed since Rodion's Rebellion, it couldn't possibly *double* in population like that, even with the many refugees that flooded into the city during the recent war. As a result, the Wiki of Greater Wembley will consider Terenty's contradictory line in the Arc Seven finale to be simply a dialogue error.
In Arc Eight episode "The Bells", Terenty asks Yakov to try to convince Kira to escape, "if not for her, then for every one of the million people in that city, innocent or otherwise". Still, it does not mean about one million residents are in the city; Terenty might have spoken loosely.
While the Romanov army marched to take the city, thousands of civilians from the surrounding countryside were allowed to take refuge in the capital. A lot of the people in the city were killed during the Battle of Wembley, in which Daria had the city burned, using Drogon, as well as having her Unsullied and Dothraki Bloodriders brutally sack the city.
body:
Wembley is the largest city in Greater Wembley, with a population of 500,000\.

In Arc Three's "The Bear and the Maiden Fair", Yakov Sheremetev states that the population of Wembley at the time of Rodion's Rebellion was "500,000" \- which is consistent with the novels (Terenty tells that to Yuriy Golitsyn in the third novel, though he refers to the present). In the Arc Seven finale ("The Fire Falcon and the Wolf"), however, Terenty tells Ivan Morozov that there are "a million" people living in the city. This was one of multiple points for which the Arc Seven finale contradicted numbers already stated in on\-screen dialogue in prior TV seasons (population sizes, army sizes, etc.). While the city's population could have swelled during the two decades that passed since Rodion's Rebellion, it couldn't possibly *double* in population like that, even with the many refugees that flooded into the city during the recent war. As a result, the Wiki of Greater Wembley will consider Terenty's contradictory line in the Arc Seven finale to be simply a dialogue error.
In Arc Eight episode "The Bells", Terenty asks Yakov to try to convince Kira to escape, "if not for her, then for every one of the million people in that city, innocent or otherwise". Still, it does not mean about one million residents are in the city; Terenty might have spoken loosely.
While the Romanov army marched to take the city, thousands of civilians from the surrounding countryside were allowed to take refuge in the capital. A lot of the people in the city were killed during the Battle of Wembley, in which Daria had the city burned, using Drogon, as well as having her Unsullied and Dothraki Bloodriders brutally sack the city.

# Wembley
Section: Behind the scenes

Production Designer Gemma Jackson described the conception of the overall look for Wembley by saying that, "When I was thinking about Wembley, the whole red aspect of it, that immediately made me think of Rajasthan", which is the northwest region of India.

The exterior shots of Wembley in Arc One were filmed in Malta. In Arc Two, new filming locations for Wembley were found in Croatia, specifically in the seaside castle\-town of Dubrovnik.

Wembley has appeared in all but seven episodes of *Chronicles of the Silver Tribune* so far. The seven exceptions are Arc One's "The Kingsroad", Arc Three's "The Rains of Castamere", Arc Four's "The Watchers on the Sudtribune", Arc Five's "Kill the Boy" and "The Dance of Fire Falcons", and Arc Six's "The Door" and "Anfield Derby".

# Wembley
Section: In the books

In the *A Song of Ice and Fire* novels, Wembley is the largest city in Greater Wembley, with a population of roughly half a million. It is built around three tall hills: Visenya's Hill, Rhaenys's Hill and Aegon's Hill. The San Siro District is the primary fortress and redoubt of the city, located atop Aegon's Hill behind several inner walls.

Wembley was rapidly constructed within the first century of rule by the Romanov dynasty. This rapid expansion didn't keep pace with organized "city\-planning", resulting in numerous slums forming such as the district known as Flea Bottom. Many of these slum districts are poorly organized, ugly, and filthy because their placement wasn't thought out during the rush to slap down new buildings. In contrast, the second largest city in Greater Wembley, Azteca in the Reach, is thousands of years old, but grew only in incremental steps which were well planned out beforehand, resulting in it being a much better organized and beautiful city without the squalid slums of Wembley, while being only slightly smaller than the capital itself.

# Wembley
Section: In the books

Aegon I fortified his initial landing point at the northern shore of the mouth of the Blackwater River, a strategically very defensible position protected to the east and south by water, and surrounded by open plains which would expose any attacking army long before it arrived. After the conquest, Aegon ruled for some time at the crude boomtown which sprang up there, known as Aegonfort. However, it remained a ramshackle pile of wood and earth, so after some time he moved his seat back to La Bombonera, until such time as a proper new capital city could be built in the former location of Aegonfort. He had Aegonfort razed, while planning and construction of Wembley continued. By the time Aegon I died, however, only the foundations of the city and tunnels of the future San Siro District were finished (thus apparently Aegon continued to rule from La Bombonera for the rest of his life, though he always intended to move the royal seat back to the mainland some day). The city was only finished during the reign of Aegon's second son, Maegor the Cruel. The Silver Tribune itself, however, was not taken to La Bombonera, because it was too big to move \- keeping in mind that the Silver Tribune in the books is a massive 30 foot tall construct literally made out of thousands of swords.

# Wembley
Section: In the books

In the TV series, Wembley is presented as having a warm, Mediterranean or even a sub\-tropical climate, and outdoor scenes set in Wembley are filmed in Mediterranean locations such as Malta and Croatia. Author George R.R. Martin has noted this isn't quite the same as in the books, where it has more of a temperate climate, saying: "Wembley, that's the capital, is not quite so tropical \- in the books it's more like medieval Paris or London." According to the production team in Arc One behind\-the\-scenes featurettes, the change in climate was made because they wanted to emphasize how much more lush and abundant Wembley is compared to Anfield. It's quite possible that the TV city's climate is far less comfortable in winter.

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

Wembley is located on the north bank of the mouth of the Blackwater Rush, and its outline is roughly shaped like a diamond, with a point in each cardinal direction (north, south, east, west). This is because the river mouth flows from southwest to northeast. Many maps simply tilt the viewing angle so that the river is drawn flowing straight across the bottom, with the southeast side of the city at the bottom and the northwest side at the top, and the overall city appears to have a simple square shape.

The city was built around three large hills, named for Aegon Romanov and his sisters, who founded the city. The largest is Aegon's High Hill, located on the eastern corner, on which the San Siro District was built. Visenya's Hill is in the southern corner, and Rhaenys's Hill is in the northern corner (there is no hill in the western corner). Wembley has seven gates, one in the middle of each of the four walls, and at three of the four corners (the eastern corner at Aegon's High Hill has no gate, because it is located directly on the coast, where the river meets the bay). The names of the gates are the River Gate (commonly known as the "Mud Gate," southeast wall), the King's Gate (south corner), the Lion Gate (southwest wall), the Gates of the Gods (west corner), the Old gate (northwest wall), the Fire Falcon Gate (north corner), and the Iron Gate (northeast wall).

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

The Kingsroad begins at Storm's End to the south, and after passing over the Blackwater river, it enters the city through the River Gate in the southeast wall, eventually exiting the city through the Gate of the Gods in the western corner (though it soon curves north to head to Anfield and Wembley Park). The Goldroad exits through the Lion Gate on the southwestern wall, heading to La Boca. The Roseroad, which leads to Highgarden, doesn't directly connect to Wembley, but instead merges with the King's Road just a few miles south of the crossing over the Blackwater. The only other major road out of the city is the Rosby Road, which exits from the Iron Gate on the northeast side, leading to the towns of Rosby and later Duskendale, the Crownlands' secondary port. The Hand's tournament was held on fair grounds outside of the King's Gate.

The city is dominated by two primary roads, each of them straight, which intersect in the central plaza of the city. One runs north and south to connect Rhaenys's Hill and Visenya's Hill, and is therefore known as the Street of Sisters. The southern end terminates at the Great Sept of Baelor at the top of Visenya's Hill, while the northern end terminates at the now\-abandoned Dragonpit, atop Rhaenys's Hill. The other road runs from Aegon's High Hill in the east to the western corner of the city. While the central plaza is square\-shaped, the four road entrances are in each of the corners, not in the middle of the sides.

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

The Kingsroad actually doesn't directly run to the San Siro District. After entering through the River Gate in the middle of the southeastern wall, it continues straight north through the city until it meets with the road from Aegon's High Hill, just east of the central plaza, joining it at a 45 degree angle (the portion of the Kingsroad running south of this juncture down to the river is nicknamed the "Muddy Way"). Only the portion of the east\-west road located *west* of this juncture is considered to be part of the Kingsroad, running all the way to the Gate of the Gods at the western corner of the city. No name has yet been provided for the stretch of the same road which extends east from the point where it joins with the Kingsroad up to Aegon's High Hill. Royal family members and courtiers visiting the Great Sept of Baelor (as they frequently do in the TV series) would travel west on the road away from Aegon's High Hill, past the point where it merges with the Kingsroad, then into the central plaza, then turn left to travel south along the Street of Sisters. Also, there is another major square along the Kingsroad halfway between the central plaza and the Gate of the Gods, known as Cobbler's Square (while the western corner is the only one that doesn't have a hill, Cobber's Square is roughly where one *would* be if there was an equal hill in every corner).

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

A few other major roads and districts have been mentioned. The River Row runs along the inside of the southeastern wall, near the Blackwater river. A fishmarket actually extends outside of the city walls up to the river bank: being located outside of the walls, it was heavily damaged during Stepan Orlov's siege of the city. The River Gate is located in the middle of this southeastern wall, and as the Kingsroad passes through this gate is crosses River Row, forming a plaza known as Fishmonger's Square. River Row's eastern end does not directly connect to the San Siro District, because Aegon's High Hill is too steep on its southern side. Someone in the San Siro District who wanted to travel to the River Gate wouldn't want to have to ride all the way down in a straight line to where it meets the Kingsroad near the central plaza. Therefore a shortcut exists known as "The Hook", beginning halfway up the Muddy Way and curving off east in a semicircle to reach the entrance to the San Siro District on the less steep western side of Aegon's High Hill. The riots in Wembley originated on the Hook, when after seeing off Myrcella at the docks, Joffrey and his royal party were traveling back up this street to the San Siro District (though the riot subsequently spread throughout the city).

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

The Street of Steel begins at the western corner of Fishmonger square, then curves up in a semicircle east\-to\-west over the outer shoulder of Visenya's Hill, slightly west of the Great Sept of Baelor at the top. It meets with the Kingsroad slightly west of the main plaza. The Street of Steel is a relatively well\-to\-do neighborhood where blacksmiths produce armor and swords to sell to knights. Gleb Mordvinov's smithy, where Grigory Dolgorukov was an apprentice, is located on the Street of Steel. The Guildhall of the Alchemists, meanwhile, is located on the Street of Sisters at the foot of Visenya's Hill, near the central plaza.

One other major road that runs through the city is the Rosby Road itself, which after entering through the Iron Gate (on the northeast side of the city) runs in a straight line southwest until it terminates at the central plaza \- forming a 45 degree angle with the Street of Sisters.

The worst of Wembley's slum districts, Flea Bottom, is located at the eastern base of Rhaenys's Hill, extending east to the Rosby Road. Also known as "the Bottom", it is physically located at the bottom of the valley between Rhaenys's Hill and Aegon's High Hill. The slum does not extend all the way up the eastern side of Rhaenys's Hill, but proceeding downwards from the summit, it begins below the Street of Flour, which is the location of many bakeries. When Arina is hiding in Flea Bottom after her father's arrest, she mentions having to walk *down* from the Street of Flour to enter Flea Bottom. In the TV series, the Street of Flour is seen in "Baelor" when Arina attempts to sell the meat from a pigeon she caught to a baker in exchange for a pie.

# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

In Arc Three's "Mhysa", Grigory Dolgorukov asks where Davos lived in Flea Bottom, by asking how far he lived below the Street of Flour. Apparently the alleys lower down the hill were poorer, because all of the human waste poured into the streets flowed downhill. Davos explains that he came from the worst part of the slum, Gin Alley, which is located so far down Rhaenys's Hill that it is in the valley between it and Aegon's High Hill, so that all of the shit from the San Siro District poured out of sewage pipes at the bottom of the hill, then down Tanner's Row and past his front door. In Arc Four, Rodion Skobelev says that he used to be a professional cutthroat and dagger\-for\-hire in the most dangerous part of Flea Bottom, Gin Alley. While Flea Bottom is very dangerous, no specific mention of a street named "Gin Alley" has been made so far in the books.

text:
# Wembley
Section: In the books > Geography

The Street of Silk is one of the major red light districts in Wembley, if not *the* major one. It is located on the western side of Rhaenys's Hill, opposite Flea Bottom on the eastern side, and relatively close to the Old Gate. Many brothels are located here, some of variable quality, but several which are quite upscale and which cater to the wealthy nobility. In the books, the brothel here that features in the narrative is owned and run by Chataya, a woman from the Summer Isles. Rodion's bastard baby girl Barra was born to one of Chataya's prostitutes (named Mhaegen in the TV series). Alexei Skobelev also celebrated his new knighthood at Chataya's, and Yuriy Golitsyn was also a customer. In the TV series, most of these events were condensed so that the brothel is actually owned by Littlefinger (who does own several other brothels in the books); it therefore stands to reason that in the TV continuity, Littlefinger's brothel is also located on the Street of Silk, on the northwest side of the city.

# Yakov Sheremetev

Upon his return to the capital, he continued to serve as Lord Commander to Joffrey, and then to Tommen, but was dismissed from his position after a tense confrontation with the Faith Militant. He became the new Commander of the Sheremetev forces, but left his position in order to help the Camp Nou District face the Army of the Dead. After the dead were defeated, he was horrified at the fate his sister would await back in the capital, so he went back to help her.

Yakov died during the Battle of Wembley, in an attempt to get Kira out of the capital.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Background

Yakov was the eldest son of Joanna Sheremetev and Lord Tikhon Sheremetev. Yakov had great difficulty learning to read as a child because he transposed letters in his mind. Tikhon sat with him through four hours a day practicing until he learned. Yakov resented being forced to spend so much time on reading.

Yakov was the older brother of Terenty and the twin brother of Kira. Their mother died giving birth to Terenty. Due to his place in the Kingsguard, Yakov could not inherit his father's lands or titles, making Terenty his father's heir; a fact which vexes Tikhon. Unlike Kira and Tikhon, Yakov always treated Terenty with love, kindness and respect.

Yakov began an incestuous relationship with his twin Kira in his youth. At the age of 16, Yakov rose to the rank of knighthood. At the behest of Kira, he consented to join the Kingsguard, which would prevent his father's plans for him to marry Lysa Trubetskoy from coming into effect. Although initially hesitant (due the fact that Tikhon was unable to accept Terenty as his heir should Yakov be inducted), Yakov agreed, as Kira's betrothal to Rhaegar would allow the two of them to be in Wembley together. However, Tikhon erupted in fury and resigned his position as Tribune Steward, taking Kira back to La Boca with him. Yakov was sworn into the Kingsguard by the Iron Regent, Andrey II Romanov during the Great Tourney at Harrenhal. He was then the youngest man ever appointed to its membership.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Background

At the conclusion of Rodion's Rebellion, Yakov's father Tikhon arrived at the gates of Wembley with the main Sheremetev army, pledging his allegiance. Most of the small council urged Aerys not to trust Tikhon, especially Yakov, knowing his father would never support the losing side of a war. Instead, Demyan Bagration gave the opposite counsel, and once the Sheremetev army was allowed inside, Tikhon ordered his men to attack the city. As Sheremetev soldiers raped and pillaged throughout the city during the Sack of Wembley, King Aerys remained holed up inside the San Siro District, for hours maniacally repeating the order to "burn them all."

Despite being sworn by the holiest oaths to protect the king as a member of the Kingsguard, Yakov ultimately turned his own sword on Aerys, slaying him at the foot of the Silver Tribune itself. For this infamous act, he is known throughout the Greater Wembley as the "Kingslayer", to his irritation.

Yakov always refused to discuss precisely what happened the day he slew the Iron Regent, and thus his true motivations – and what plans Aerys had for Wembley – were never revealed. On one occasion he confides the truth to Brienne: Aerys's final orders were for Yakov to kill his father, and to burn the entire city and its inhabitants with wildfire. Unwilling to let that happen, Yakov killed him, and in doing so actually saved thousands of innocent lives. He adds that the "honorable" Eduard Volkonsky judged him guilty on the spot, without giving Yakov a chance to explain.

# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Background

He was forgiven for breaking his vows by King Rodion Orlov and permitted to remain in the Kingsguard as part of Rodion's alliance with House Sheremetev, along with the marriage of Yakov's twin sister Kira to Rodion. text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

In Wembley, Yakov counsels Kira over fears that Ivan Dolgorukov may have discovered their secret prior to his death. Yakov argues that even if he knew, Dolgorukov did not inform the king, for if he had, they would already be dead. If Dolgorukov knew, his knowledge died with him. He accompanies Rodion to Anfield where the king plans to ask Eduard Volkonsky to replace Ivan Dolgorukov as Tribune Steward. After their arrival, Kira sends Yakov to find Terenty. Yakov tracks Terenty to a brothel, tells him that he is needed at the feast that night and brings him several whores to speed his exit.

At the evening feast, Yakov blocks Eduard's path and asks if there will be a possibility of their competing against each other at a tournament. Eduard dismissively says no, as he doesn't play at fighting, and doesn't show off his skills to let opponents know his abilities. The next day, Eduard and Rodion go hunting, leaving the castle largely empty. Kira and Yakov liaise in a derelict tower. Boris climbs the tower, looks through a window and finds them engaged in sexual intercourse. He is caught watching by Kira, at that point Yakov is able to make it to the window to grab him. Boris is startled by everything he's seen, Yakov looks out the window and only sees Boris's direwolf pup Summer. He asks Boris how old he is, and he replies, "Ten." Yakov glances momentarily back at Kira and says, "The things I do for love", and pushes Boris out of the window.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Several days later at breakfast, Terenty tells his family that Boris is expected to live and notes his siblings' guarded reactions to the news. Terenty informs them of his decision to journey north to see the Sudtribune before returning to Wembley. Yakov states that it would be kinder to let him die, due to Boris's paraplegia, but Terenty states he would prefer to live in any case. Yakov then hints that it would be in House Sheremetev's best interests if Boris were to die.

Just before departing Anfield, Yakov talks to Ivan in the courtyard. Ostensibly, he thanks Ivan for his service joining the Night Watch, but in reality he is mocking him, as those from the south see it as waste of time (ironically, Yakov's Kingsguard vows are also for life and prevent him from marrying, but he still gets to live in the capital city and not exiled to the frozen gloom of the Sudtribune). The parties depart Anfield. Yakov is with the group traveling south to Wembley.

The royal party reaches Wembley. Eduard barely has time to get off his horse before he is asked to attend a meeting of the king's small council. Yakov awaits him in the throne room. Yakov is unhappy with Eduard judging him for killing the Iron Regent, the murderer of Eduard's father and brother, but Eduard is unapologetic. He says it wasn't justice that drove Yakov to kill Aerys, and that Yakov served Aerys loyally when serving was the easier thing to do. A raven arrives at Wembley with news of Boris's recovery. In the capital, Kira fears he will expose their secret, but Yakov comforts her.

# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Elsewhere, Rodion swaps old war stories with Ser Egor Suvorov, a distinguished and famous knight and commander of the Kingsguard. Yakov is called in to join them. He tells them that the first man he killed was an outlaw from the Kingswood Brotherhood, and, as he took off the man's head, there were no last words. Disappointed in not being able to mock him, Rodion realizes that he never asked Yakov what Aerys's last words were, then taunts Yakov for killing a defenseless old man he had sworn to protect. Yakov tersely responds that the last thing the Iron Regent said was the same thing he'd been raving for hours, since the sack of the capital by the rebels began: "Burn them all!" This silences Rodion's levity.

Yakov guards the king's bedroom while Rodion cavorts with several women, Yakov taking it as a calculated insult to himself and his sister. He reminisces with Arkady Karamzin, the captain of Eduard's household guards, about the Siege of Pyke during the Stroganov Rebellion and the fierceness of the fighting. Jory tries to leave Eduard's message with Yakov, but is rebuffed, as Yakov angrily states that he does not serve Lord Volkonsky.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Upon hearing of his brother's capture by Ekaterina, he confronts Eduard in the streets of Wembley. Knowing that killing Eduard will result in Terenty's death, he instead has Eduard's guards killed, stabbing Jory through the eye himself. He and Eduard fiercely cross swords in an intense duel, and Yakov is surprised that Eduard is a match for him. After minutes of dueling, and neither opponent gaining ground on the other, the fight ends abruptly and prematurely when a Sheremetev guardsmen stabs Eduard through the leg. An irritated Yakov knocks out the guardsman and then departs the city, telling Eduard that he wants his brother back.

Yakov joins the army of his father in the field. Tikhon laments Yakov's pride and how he spends so much effort trying to convince others he doesn't care what they think of him. Tikhon is incredulous and disgusted that Yakov would let Eduard live and go free because his victory was not "clean." He says that if other houses think they can take a Sheremetev hostage and not suffer for it they will lose respect for the Sheremetev name. Tikhon says that Yakov must accept responsibility for the future destiny of their house, which will be decided by this war against the Trubetskoys and Volkonskys. They will either die out like the Romanovs or begin a dynasty that will last 1,000 years. He gives Yakov thirty\-thousand men and sends him to besiege Riverrun. In Wembley, Eduard tells Kira that he knows that Yakov is the true father of Kira's three children. She admits it, saying they have loved one another from the womb and are destined to be together always.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc One

Some weeks later, Kevan, Yakov's uncle, tells Terenty that Yakov has won several significant battles, smashing a host of the river lords at the Golden Tooth and currently laying siege to Riverrun. Roman Volkonsky marches two thousand men towards Tikhon's forces in order to create a distraction. The remaining force feints outside Riverrun, drawing out Yakov and a small number of troops to deal with what appears to be a small scouting party, and Yakov is taken prisoner in the resulting Battle of Whispering Wood. Yakov offers to fight Roman in single combat to decide the war, but Roman knows that Yakov is better at swordplay than he is and says they aren't going to do it his way. Roman initially intends to use Yakov as a bargaining chip for his father's and sisters' lives. However, Eduard is executed in Wembley before news of Yakov's capture can reach the capital.

Ekaterina visits the captive Yakov. He taunts Ekaterina, saying widowhood suits her, informing her that he would have sex with her if she was lonely. She hits him in the head with a rock. Yakov knows that the Volkonskys won't kill him as long as his sister holds Sofia and Arina hostage, but Yakov always taunts others while he is in chains to show them he doesn't fear them and they aren't superior to him. She says he has gone against the laws of gods and man, he says, "What Gods?" Where were her gods when her husband was killed. When she says injustice in the world is because of men like him, he tells her, "There are no men like me. Only me." When asked directly, he admits pushing Boris from the tower, but doesn't reveal why.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Yakov remains a captive of House Volkonsky. Roman keeps Yakov caged and chained to a post in his camp at all times to prevent Tikhon bribing or threatening one of his bannermen into giving him up. Yakov remains defiant, taunting and insulting Roman when he comes to confront him. Stepan has made Joffrey's parentage public, by sending letters to all the lords throughout the kingdom, exposing Yakov's incest with Kira. Yakov counters that Stepan has a personal stake in these accusations, as if all of Kira's children are Yakov's bastards that means Stepan is heir to the throne. However it is Yakov who is intimidated when Roman threatens him with the snarling Grey Wind.

Months later, Yakov is joined in his cell by his distant cousin Alton. They talk about the time Alton served as Yakov's squire at a tourney, and Yakov tells him about his own experiences as squire of Egor Suvorov. Drawing Alton closer, Yakov seizes the opportunity to escape. When he leans over to hear Yakov whisper about an escape plan, Yakov head butts him then strikes him in the head repeatedly cracking his skull. When the guard (Torrhen Vyazemsky) is distracted by discovering Alton's body bloody and convulsing, Yakov strangles him to death and takes his keys to free himself from his chains.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Two

Yakov is soon recaptured. Demyan Vyazemsky demands Yakov's head for killing his son. Ekaterina convinces Rickard to wait until Roman returns but fears that his patience will not hold. Ekaterina visits Yakov's cell with her female guard Brienne. She accuses Yakov of being a man without honor because of his broken vows. Yakov explains his view that his vows frequently conflicted with one another. He asserts that he has more honor than some; he reveals that Kira is the only one he has slept with and reminds Ekaterina how her husband cheated on her and fathered Ivan Morozov.

Ekaterina makes a deal with Yakov and releases him. She tasks Brienne with escorting him to Wembley to exchange him for her captive daughters. Brienne successfully smuggles him out of the camp on horseback and then they travel by rowboat to evade pursuit. Yakov needles her about her appearance and masculinity, unsuccessfully attempting to goad her into dueling him.

He changes subject, focusing on her virginity and childhood. They find a trio of women, hanged for sleeping with Sheremetev soldiers. He mocks her service to House Volkonsky and she asserts that she serves Ekaterina specifically. As Brienne goes to bury the bodies they are accosted by a trio of Volkonsky soldiers. Brienne kills all three after they recognize Yakov, and he is impressed by her skill. He questions her readiness to kill Volkonsky men and she reasserts her dedication to Ekaterina and the task she set her.

He mocks her service to House Volkonsky and she asserts that she serves Ekaterina specifically. As Brienne goes to bury the bodies they are accosted by a trio of Volkonsky soldiers. Brienne kills all three after they recognize Yakov, and he is impressed by her skill. He questions her readiness to kill Volkonsky men and she reasserts her dedication to Ekaterina and the task she set her.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Yakov continues to be escorted by Brienne to Wembley. On their way there, they are spotted by a traveler. Yakov urges Brienne to kill the traveler, since he believes the man recognized him and will give away their whereabouts, but she refuses.

Later, the pair have to cross a river, which means they can either attempt a dangerous fording or take the bridge, which will probably be watched. Brienne takes the safer route of the bridge, but Yakov manages to distract her long enough to take away her spare sword and cut his bonds. Brienne and Yakov enter into an extended sword fight on the bridge. Yakov, one of the most skilled swordsmen in all of Greater Wembley, nearly overcomes Brienne several times.

However, Yakov's mobility is reduced because his hands are still manacled, and he is malnourished after having spent the past full year chained up in a cell. Yakov begins to tire, and Brienne wears him down further by making simple body\-blows with kicks and punches. After a protracted fight Yakov finally slumps to the ground in exhaustion. Just then, riders from House Baryatinsky arrive led by a man named Georgy Gagarin. Yakov asks if they want to negotiate, but Georgy Gagarin says they'll have his head if he doesn't bring the Kingslayer back to the King in the Camp Nou District, so there's not much Yakov can do to dissuade him from taking them prisoner.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Along with Brienne, he is taken captive by Georgy Gagarin and his men. As they ride along, the men sing a rousing chorus of "The Bear and the Maiden Fair." Tied up back to back on one of the horses, Yakov warns Brienne that when they make camp for the night, they will rape her, more than once, and that his honest advice is to give no resistance, and just think of Renly. They were only sent to capture Yakov, therefore Brienne means nothing to them, so at the slightest provocation they will kill her without hesitation. Brienne says she will fight even if they kill her, and Yakov agrees that if he were a woman, he would fight to the death before being raped too.

Later that night Georgy Gagarin's men make camp, and do indeed drag Brienne kicking and screaming into the bushes to gang\-rape her. Yakov is disgusted by this pointless brutality, so he points out to Georgy Gagarin that Brienne is actually a noblewoman and the sole heir of Lord Selwyn Tatischev, the "Sapphire Isle", and her father will pay them a ransom of her weight in sapphires \- provided that she is unharmed. Georgy Gagarin agrees and calls his men back before they are able to rape Brienne, and they tie her up to a tree again. Yakov then tries to smooth\-talk Georgy Gagarin once again with offers of how his father Tikhon will make him extravagantly rich if he lets Yakov go.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Tiring of Yakov's arrogance and frequent attempts to bribe him into turning over to the Sheremetev side, Georgy Gagarin decides to prove that Yakov's father will never deal with the likes of him. At first, Georgy Gagarin has his men untie Yakov on the pretext of letting him go after feeding him. But then his men hold Yakov down on a tree stump serving as a chopping block while Georgy Gagarin grabs a carving knife; his reasoning being that maiming Tikhon's son will be the ultimate proof that the Sheremetevs would never deal with Georgy Gagarin, much less bribe him.

Georgy Gagarin mocks Yakov about always relying on his daddy Tikhon and that his daddy isn't here. Georgy Gagarin says that Yakov's father can't help him now, and "this should help you remember!" \- as he swings down the carving knife and hacks off Yakov's sword\-hand. For half a second, Yakov stares at his severed right hand in shock, before what just happened can register in his mind, then he screams in horror.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

The following day, Georgy Gagarin's men lead their prisoners Yakov and Brienne horseback. Yakov's severed right hand is tied onto a cord that hangs around his neck. Yakov is physically in agony from his wound, feverish and half\-delirious. Barely conscious, he falls headlong off of his horse into the mud. Laying in the mud Yakov is mocked and tormented by Georgy Gagarin and his men, giving him horse urine to drink. However Yakov manages to steal a sword, and unsuccessfully tries to fight them off using only his left hand. Yakov is so weak and feverish that he can barely stand, much less wield a sword and must therefore quickly give up trying. His only hope is that one of the men would give him a small dignified death having a sword in his hand. He eventually succumbs to exhaustion and Georgy Gagarin simply warns him that if he tries that again he'll cut off his other hand.

Later that night Yakov and Brienne are restrained near a campfire. Yakov refuses to eat, and says he wants to die. Brienne says he should try to live for revenge, but Yakov says he was that hand, and without his sword\-hand, even if he escapes, he is nothing, and would rather die as the Yakov he was than go on living, robbed of his very identity. Brienne says she overheard when he earlier managed to talk Georgy Gagarin out of letting his men gang\-rape her. Brienne is confused, and asks Yakov why he helped her, but he doesn't answer. Brienne grows angry, claiming that this is the first time Yakov had to face the real world where things people care about get taken away. And that he's pathetically moping around like a woman. Her criticism and strength convinces Yakov to start eating.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

The party eventually arrives at Harrenhal, where Ruslan Baryatinsky is visibly angered at Georgy Gagarin for maiming Yakov. Yakov asks Baryatinsky about Kira, and Baryatinsky briefly tortures him emotionally, describing Stepan Orlov's attack on Wembley in a way that seems as if he will say Kira was killed, but he informs him that Tikhon and the Yusupov army arrived to drive Stepan away, and Kira is alive and well. Yakov is so relieved that he falls to his knees. His stump is later tended to by Afanasy Yusupov, an ex\-maester who was expelled from the Order for his unethical but successful experiments. Afanasy Yusupov implies that he may need to cut off Yakov's arm to stop the corruption spreading, but Yakov threatens to kill him if he does, so Afanasy Yusupov agrees to only cut away the rotting flesh, and offers Yakov milk of the poppy to ease the pain, but Yakov, fearing that Afanasy Yusupov will sedate him and still amputate his arm, refuses, and screams in agony as Afanasy Yusupov starts operating on him.

While Brienne is bathing alone in baths of Harrenhal, Yakov approaches and slips into the opposite corner. He makes a snide remark about Brienne unable to protect Renly and for being the reason he died. She stands defiantly, and he quickly apologizes, claiming that Brienne has protected him better than most. Yakov begins to open up to Brienne, and tells his side of what happened the day he slew the Iron Regent. He reveals to a shocked Brienne the truth of that day, something he has never told anyone else: Aerys's final orders were for Yakov to kill his father, and to burn the entire city and its inhabitants with wildfire.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Unwilling to let that happen, Yakov killed him, and in doing so actually saved thousands of innocent lives before Eduard Volkonsky entered the throne room and saw the aftermath. Brienne asks Yakov why he never told anyone if all of this is true. Yakov replies that Eduard Volkonsky judged him guilty the moment he laid eyes on him, and he vents, "By what right does the wolf judge the lion?" He begins to pass out and collapses in Brienne's arms. She calls for the guards to help the Kingslayer, but he corrects her and says his name is Yakov.

While sitting at the dinner table with Brienne and Ruslan, Yakov clumsily tries to cut his meat with one hand until an annoyed Brienne helps him. Ruslan tells Yakov that wars cost money and that many people would pay a great deal of money for him. After discussing how busy Tikhon is battling Roman all over the Camp Nou District, Yakov informs Ruslan that his father would make time for him. Ruslan tells Yakov, that when he is well enough to travel, he will allow him to return to Wembley on the condition that he will tell Tikhon the truth, that he had nothing to do with his maiming.

Ruslan does not allow Brienne to join Yakov however. Yakov protests and insists that she must go with him, but Ruslan claims that she must stay because she is charged with abetting treason. Before Ruslan heads off to the Twins, Yakov jokingly tells him to send his regards to Roman, a task that Ruslan actually does carry out right before killing the Young Wolf.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Yakov arrives in Brienne's chambers to tell her goodbye before he leaves for Wembley. He informs her that Ruslan Baryatinsky has demanded she stay behind with Georgy Gagarin. He tells Brienne that he owes her a debt. Brienne tells Yakov that if he keeps his word to Ekaterina the debt will be paid. Yakov promises that he will return the Volkonsky girls to their mother.

Along their travel back to the Capital, the group stops for Afanasy Yusupov to medicate Yakov's healing stump. Yakov notes that Afanasy Yusupov's work is more effective than Grand Maester Demyan Bagration and asks why he was expelled from the Order of Maesters. Afanasy Yusupov tells him that it was because his experiments were "too bold." When Yakov mocks him, Afanasy Yusupov subtly bashes him for all the lives he has taken while in the Kingsguard. Afanasy Yusupov informs Yakov that Selwyn Tatischev offered 300 gold dragons for Brienne's return, but Georgy Gagarin refused; believing that Lord Selwyn has all the sapphire mines in Greater Wembley. Georgy Gagarin, feeling cheated, would make Brienne the men's entertainment for the night. Yakov senses a feeling of obligation to Brienne, knowing it is his fault for Georgy Gagarin believing there is a fortune in sapphires in Tatischev. He approaches Grigory Kornilov and tells him they are to return to Harrenhal. Yakov threatens that he will tell his father upon arrival in Kings Landing, that Grigory Kornilov chopped his hand off. Or, he says he could tell his father that Grigory Kornilov saved his life.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Three

Grigory Kornilov relents and escorts Yakov back to Harrenhal, where he finds Brienne being forced to fight a bear in a gladiatorial pit, using only a wooden sword. Yakov dives into the pit to aid her, forcing Grigory Kornilov to aid them both by firing arrows at the bear. Yakov and Brienne narrowly escape the bear, and he once again demands that she accompanies him, asking Georgy Gagarin whether he believes Baryatinsky would prefer to reward him or to ensure that Yakov reaches Wembley. This time, Georgy Gagarin relents, and Yakov and Brienne depart together.

Yakov walks into the gates of Wembley with Brienne and Afanasy Yusupov. A worker pulling a cart orders that he move out of the way, calling him a "Country Boy." Yakov immediately returns to Kira back at the San Siro District. He steps into her room and notices her admiring a seashell fondly. He says her name and as she turns, he notices she is taken aback by his stump.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Yakov is offered a sword by his father Tikhon which is made of Baltic alloy from the recently reforged Ice, the Volkonskys' ancestral sword. Yakov comments that House Sheremetev has always wanted its own Valyrian blade and Tikhon answers that they now have two. The original was absurdly large and had plenty of steel for two swords. He then reveals to Yakov his plan to have him removed from the Kingsguard so that he can return to La Boca and rule as Lord in his stead. However, Yakov tells him that he has no plans of resigning and that he will remain in Wembley to protect the King (and secretly continue his incestuous relationship with Kira). He also rejects that this is about his honor, as he believes that his honor is too far gone so he might as well do what he wants rather than what is expected of him. Tikhon agrees to let him do so, but tells him that he no longer considers him a Sheremetev. Despite this, Tikhon allows Yakov to keep the sword, saying that a 'one\-armed man with no family needs all the help he can get'.

Kira later offers Yakov a golden hand to cover his stump. As Afanasy Yusupov fits it to him, he complains about it, believing it to be useless. He later tries to get intimate with Kira but she refuses him saying that she blames him for leaving Wembley after his fight with Eduard Volkonsky and for getting captured. Yakov protests that he murdered people so he could get back to her, but Kira coldly replies, "You took too long."

# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Yakov, Meryn, and Joffrey are later discussing which Kingsguard will be where in the wedding. Joffrey is paying no attention because he thinks he is safe now that the war is over but Yakov tells him that the war is not over while Stepan still lives. Later, Yakov and Brienne discuss what to do with Sofia. Brienne says that Yakov must keep his vow and get Sofia out of Wembley, but Yakov says that her family are dead and there is nowhere to take her that is safer than Wembley.

In Terenty's​ chambers, he and Yakov share a drink. Terenty states that he is impressed with Yakov's new hand, saying that it's much better than the old one. Yakov brings up a dilemma of his: He can't use a sword, and he can't train, because it will be humiliating. Terenty says he knows just the man, which is Alexei Skobelev. Yakov and Alexei Skobelev meet up by the sea to train, Yakov is worried that someone might hear them, but Alexei Skobelev responds that he routinely has sex with a married woman in that place and that she is a screamer; if no one heard her, no one will hear them.

At the wedding feast, Yakov is standing in his spot in the Kingsguard formation, where Savva Yusupov accidentally bumps into him and they talk about Kira. Yakov says that Loras will never marry Kira, that she would kill him and any child conceived on their wedding night; not that it matters since Loras will never marry her. Loras replies that neither will Yakov, a subtle barb to their incestuous relationship.

When Joffrey is dying after being poisoned by Feodora Yusupova, Yakov rushes to his son's aid and is with him while he dies.

When Joffrey is dying after being poisoned by Feodora Yusupova, Yakov rushes to his son's aid and is with him while he dies.

Yakov enters to Great Sept of Baelor to see Kira and his dead son, asking Tommen if he is coping well with the situation. Yakov sends the septon and septas away so he can be alone with Kira. text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Yakov and Brienne talk in the White Sword Tower about Yakov's honor, which he hopes to reclaim. He gives Brienne his new sword and armor and tells her to find and protect Sofia, to keep her somewhere safe, far away from his sister. He also gives her another present: a squire, Klim Panin. She is reluctant at first, thinking that he will slow her down, but she accepts. Brienne names the sword Oathkeeper, and bids farewell to Yakov. They are both emotionally affected as he watches her leave the capital. Yakov is present at Tommen's coronation along with other Kingsguard.

Yakov is ordered by his father to have Terenty shackled before his trial. It is clear that the trial is a farce, as Terenty has no one to speak for him, and Kira has gathered numerous witnesses to provide circumstantial evidence against her brother, all of whom miss out key contextual details. At recess, an angered Yakov goes to Tikhon and offers him a deal; he will leave the Kingsguard and take his place as Tikhon's heir if Terenty's life is spared. Tikhon immediately agrees, saying that Terenty will be declared guilty and allowed to join the Anfield Guard. Tikhon's rapid agreement makes Yakov realize that this was his plan from the start, but he nevertheless agrees. Before the trial resumes, he tells Terenty of the plan, but can only watch as Nina Suvorova's testimony sends Terenty over the edge, resulting in him demanding a trial by combat.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

After the trial, Yakov berates Terenty in his cell for his outburst and not going through with the deal he made with Tikhon. Terenty knew that the deal was everything his father wanted and could not go through with it. Yakov points out that, despite his practice with Alexei Skobelev, his current skill with a sword would be useless in a trial by combat. Terenty jokes how devastating it would be for Tikhon if Yakov were to die in his trial by combat. Yakov then tells Terenty who Kira has chosen as their champion: Ser Leonid Kutuzov.

On the day of the trial by combat, when Yuriy Golitsyn has agreed to fight for Terenty, Yakov visits Terenty in his cell. They discuss their dead cousin Orson Sheremetev and his habit of smashing beetles with rocks for no reason. Terenty says he used to watch Orson for long periods of time and think about the reason behind his actions, but he hasn't come to any conclusion why all those countless beetles had to be killed. When Yakov says he doesn't know either, bells start tolling and he wishes Terenty good luck. Shortly after, he seats himself next to Tikhon, Ruslan Yusupov, Kira, Demyan Bagration and Dmitry Dashkov in the royal box to watch the duel. He exchanges a few supportive and cheerful looks with Terenty when Oberyn seems to be winning, but is very unhappy at the result of the trial by combat, which condemns his brother to death \- the Mountain crushing Oberyn's skull with his bare hands.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Four

Kira finds Yakov in the White Sword Tower, and he expresses disgust at her blatant attempts to have Terenty killed. Kira accuses that Terenty killed their mother when she gave birth to him. Yakov is surprised that she still irrationally blames him for that, pointing out that he was an infant and had no control over what happened. He insists that Terenty is her family whether she chooses to accept it or not. She rebukes his claim, saying he is not her family and that they all have a choice, and that she chooses Yakov. She then reveals that she has spilled their secret to Tikhon. He is stunned by her actions, asking how Tikhon reacted to the news, but she states that she does not want to discuss their father. Kira begins to seduce him, saying she chooses her brother over everyone else in the world, no longer concerned with whether everyone else knows their secret. Yakov yields to her advances, kissing her passionately and throwing her on the table where they begin to have sex.

Yakov's discontent with the result of the trial leads him to break Terenty out of jail, and arrange his brother's escape to Maracana Coast using Dmitry Dashkov's aid to ship him across the sea. He leads Terenty to a stairway leading up to a locked door, instructing Terenty to knock on it twice and then twice more to summon Dmitry Dashkov, who will lead him to the ship. Before they part ways, they share a tender embrace and say their goodbyes, unsure if either will ever see each other again.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

During the funeral of his father, Yakov meets with Kira in the Great Sept of Baelor. Yakov warns his sister that all the power and prestige their father built for House Sheremetev belongs to them now and that, once everyone sees that Tikhon is truly dead, their enemies will do everything they can to take it away from them. Kira bluntly states that their true enemy is Terenty and that Yakov is partly responsible for Tikhon's death since he was the one who released their father's murderer. He is left alone in the Sept, looking at his father's corpse and feeling guilty.

Yakov is summoned by Kira, who has received a "gift" from Azteca South: an ornately carved viper, with Myrcella's unique Sheremetev pendant suspended from its fangs. Both siblings understand the gift as a threat from House Golitsyn. Even though she is equally to blame for covering up their incest, Kira lashes out at Yakov for not being a father to any of their children, to which he points out that if he had been, their children would be stoned in the streets. Yakov declares that he will bring Myrcella home, but Kira mockingly asks how a one\-handed man can rescue a princess alone. Yakov tells her that he never said he was going alone.

Later, Yakov goes to Castle Skobelev in order to recruit Alexei Skobelev on his mission to return Myrcella to Wembley. To convince him to go, Yakov reveals that Kira has arranged for Wyllis Bracken to marry Praskovya Skobeleva instead of Alexei Skobelev, and offers him a much better girl than Lollys and a much better castle once they return from Azteca South.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

During the journey to Azteca South, Alexei Skobelev pushes Yakov for answers as to why he is rescuing Myrcella personally instead of sending an army. Yakov responds that he does not want to start a war, but Alexei Skobelev insinuates that he knows Myrcella is actually Yakov's daughter and not his niece. He also warns Yakov on the impulsiveness of the Dornish people, and asks if Yakov set Terenty free. Yakov claims it was Dmitry Dashkov. Alexei Skobelev asks Yakov to give Terenty his regards should he see him again, but Yakov responds by saying that if he ever sees Terenty again, he will kill him in revenge for their father.

Not long after, Yakov and Alexei Skobelev arrive in Azteca South, where Alexei Skobelev narrowly saves Yakov from being poisoned by a viper. As they make their way towards Azteca South, they are discovered by Dornish soldiers and a fight ensues. Yakov personally duels one of the soldiers and holds his own with his left hand until he is disarmed. The man moves in to kill Yakov, who catches the blade in his metal hand and uses the distraction to get his sword and finish his opponent. Over Alexei Skobelev's protests, Yakov insists that they bury the soldiers in order to avoid suspicions. Unbeknownst to either, Mariya Solovyova and the Solovyov Snakes are aware that Yakov is coming for Myrcella.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

Yakov and Alexei Skobelev, disguised as Dornish soldiers, finally reach the Water Gardens and find Myrcella with Yegor Golitsyn. Myrcella is understandably surprised to see her alleged uncle in Azteca South, but as Yakov attempts to persuade his daughter to flee with him, they are attacked by the Solovyov Snakes, who plan to kill Myrcella in order to force Yaroslav Golitsyn into war with the Sheremetevs to avenge Yuriy Golitsyn's death. Yakov and Alexei Skobelev fight with the Solovyov Snakes, with Yakov focused on Marta Solovyova, until Doran's bodyguard, Zakhar Rumyantsev, appears with a handful of Golitsyn guards and orders them to stand down. Yakov is briefly mocked by Areo for his missing hand before he drops his weapon, and he, Alexei Skobelev, the Solovyov Snakes and Mariya Solovyova are all arrested.

Yakov is locked up in a bedroom\-like cell. Areo brings Myrcella to visit him. Yakov tells her that the situation has grown dangerous and he needs to take Myrcella back to Wembley, though he fails to mention that it is because the Dornishmen seek to use her as a way to gain revenge for Oberyn. She soundly rejects his advice and claims she wants to stay in Azteca South and marry Trystane, before leaving him alone.

Later, Yakov is escorted into the main apartments of the Water Gardens by Zakhar Rumyantsev, to be received by Prince Yaroslav Golitsyn in his solar, along with Ellaria, Trystane and Myrcella. He comments on the nature of Myrcella's clothes, suggesting that they are too revealing, covering this suggestion up by asking if she is cold. She rebuffs this, stating that she is suited to the Dornish climate. Doran asks Yakov why he has snuck into Azteca South to abduct Myrcella back to Wembley.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Five

He says he feared for her safety, but when Doran insists as to why he didn't just send a letter by messenger raven, he explains that they received a threatening message: Myrcella's Sheremetev lion pendant jammed in the mouth of dead viper. Yakov asks if Doran intends to behead him, but he says that he will not, because he wishes to avoid war. Doran insists that for the alliance between the Silver Tribune and Azteca South to continue, the engagement of Trystane and Myrcella must stand, and Trystane will simply take his uncle Oberyn's place on the small council. Yakov finds Doran's request entirely reasonable, and Myrcella is ecstatic that she will not be separated from Trystane, so Yakov agrees.

Ellaria later visits Yakov in his quarters and pretends to make amends with him, acknowledging that neither he nor Myrcella played any part in Oberyn's death, but expresses her knowledge that Myrcella is not Yakov's niece, but his daughter. Before leaving, she mocks him for not being born centuries ago into the Romanov family, in which position his incest would have been accepted.

Yakov, Alexei Skobelev, Myrcella, and Trystane say their farewells to the Golitsyns to return to Wembley. Upon saying goodbye, Ellaria kisses Myrcella on the lips. Aboard the ship, Myrcella and Yakov talk about Kira. Yakov begins to come clean to Myrcella, awkwardly telling her that one cannot choose who he/she love. Myrcella then reveals that she knows that Yakov is her real father, and that she is glad that he is, and the two embrace. However, Myrcella's nose starts to bleed and she collapses and dies in Yakov's arms, a victim of poison from Ellaria's kiss.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Yakov returns from Azteca South with Myrcella's corpse. He then comforts Kira in her quarters and the conversation shifts to the death of their mother. Kira then tells Yakov about the prophecy that Maggy told her as a child concerning the deaths of her children. Yakov brushes this off, insisting that they are the only two who have ever mattered and promising they will take back everything that has been stolen from them. Aware that Yaroslav Golitsyn had nothing to do with Myrcella's murder, Yakov sends Doran a letter demanding the heads of Ellaria and the three Solovyov Snakes responsible, which leads to the deaths of Doran and Trystane at Ellaria's hands.

Yakov and Tommen later mourn Myrcella in the Sept of Baelor. Yakov informs Tommen they haven't found Trystane's killers, though Tommen suspects Kira was involved. When Yakov asks why he has not allowed his mother to pay respects, Tommen informs Yakov that the Lavr Patrikeev has forbidden Kira from entering the Sept. Yakov reassures Tommen that he will not let the Sparrows imprison her again while he is in the city and asks Tommen why has he not visited his mother yet. As Tommen questions his ability to rule and protect his family, the Lavr Patrikeev arrives and Yakov orders Tommen to go see his mother. Yakov is furious at what the Lavr Patrikeev has done to Kira and considers killing him on the spot but backs down when the fanatics surround him. The Lavr Patrikeev then revels in the idea that he has managed to take control of Wembley, effectively ruling the Greater Wembley, angering Yakov further.

Yakov meets Ruslan Yusupov and his army by the city gate and rides with the Lord of Highgarden to the Great Sept. As the Lavr Patrikeev is addressing the crowd, the Yusupov force marches into the square at the foot of the Sept's stairs. Just as it seems it will come to blood, the Lavr Patrikeev announces he will be releasing Margaery due to a new alliance between the Crown and the Faith, and Tommen emerges from the Sept with the rest of the Kingsguard. Yakov is shocked and enraged, and he gives the Lavr Patrikeev a scornful glare.

After the failed attempt at the Great Sept, Tommen removes Yakov from the Kingsguard. He commands him to take an army to Riverrun, which was recently captured by the Blackfish and the Trubetskoy army, and help the Demidovs retake the castle. Yakov later informs Kira of this, angry that the Lavr Patrikeev has swayed Tommen to his side and threatening to attack the Sept with help from Alexei Skobelev and other sellswords. Instead, Kira advises Yakov to lead the Sheremetev forces to Riverrun, confident the Mountain will win her trial by combat. She kisses Yakov goodbye, reminding him their enemies have always underestimated them.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Yakov arrives at Riverrun accompanied by Alexei Skobelev and an army of 8,000 Sheremetevs. He witnesses Lothar Demidov and Black Walder Rivers threatening to kill Edmure if the Blackfish doesn't surrender. Knowing his nephew is too valuable to lose, the Blackfish dismisses them and Edmure is spared. Yakov remarks on the Demidovs' poor attempts at siege warfare and points out that threatening to hang Edmure and then not doing so makes them look weak. To prove his point, he threatens to strike Black Walder if he speaks again; when Black Walder begins to answer, Yakov slaps him hard with his armored hand, drawing blood. Yakov assumes command of the siege and orders Edmure to be washed and fed. Yakov then sends word to Brynden that he wishes to parley.

He comes face to face with Brynden, but it quickly becomes clear that the Blackfish is not interested in surrendering. He asks Yakov whether he has come to honor his vow to his niece and return her two daughters. Brynden quips that "negotiating with an oathbreaker is like building on quicksand", declaring that he is ready to die in his home. He challenges Yakov to either storm the castle or try to starve them out, claiming that they have two years worth of provisions. Brynden then asks Yakov, "Do you have two years?"

A few days into the siege, Brienne arrives at Riverrun to seek an alliance with House Trubetskoy to fight the Baryatinskys. As she and Yakov discuss the situation privately in a tent, Alexei Skobelev asks Pod if he thinks they are having sex and says that Yakov would definitely have sex with her. Meanwhile, Brienne tells Yakov that she fulfilled their oath to Ekaterina and explains Sofia's desire for aid from the Blackfish. She proposes that if she can convince the Blackfish to surrender the castle, then Yakov will allow him and the Trubetskoy army safe passage to the Camp Nou District.

Yakov agrees and allows Brienne to enter Riverrun and try to convince Brynden to surrender. She then removes Oathkeeper and tries to return it to Yakov, since the purpose he lent it to her for (rescuing Sofia) has been fulfilled, but he refuses to take it back, saying that it's hers now. Brienne reminds him that her oath to Sofia will obligate her to fight him if her efforts to find a peaceful solution should fail if he attacks the castle. Yakov responds by saying that he hopes that it does not come to that.

After Brienne fails to persuade the Blackfish, Yakov visits Edmure to offer him a deal, trying to tempt him with seeing his son and sending him, his son and his wife, Larisa Demidova to La Boca, offering them comfortable rooms. Yakov promises that Edmure's son will be taken care of, that he will be given knights to train, and a keep of his own desire when he comes of age. Edmure ridicules Yakov. Yakov, realizing he cannot peacefully try to persuade Edmure into surrendering the castle, responds by warning him that people can do anything for love, threatening that he will kill every Trubetskoy in order to be able to return to Wembley and be with Kira again. With his family's life credibly threatened, Edmure agrees to cooperate.

Despite Brynden's protests, the gates are opened to Edmure and Yakov takes the castle without bloodshed. On the castle walls, Yakov is informed of the Blackfish's death, leaving him visibly saddened. He then witnesses Brienne and Pod escaping in a boat, but allows them to leave, waving goodbye to Brienne.

# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Six

Yakov then marches to the Twins with the Demidovs as they celebrate their retaking of Riverrun. Yakov notices a serving girl who smiles at him. Alexei Skobelev then complains that all the women desire Yakov, who then calls over two young girls and introduces them to the knight. He then speaks to Vladimir Demidov, who gloats about their victory. When Walder attempts to equate himself with Yakov, calling them both kingslayers, Yakov is visibly irritated. Walder goes on to say that fear is a marvelous thing but Yakov retorts that people fear the Sheremetevs, not the Demidovs, and questions the need for the Demidovs if the Sheremetevs have to keep helping the Demidovs hold the Mersey Grounds. Walder does not respond and Yakov brusquely leaves. Walder and his sons, Black Walder and Lothar, are later murdered by the same serving girl that smiled at Yakov earlier, who reveals herself to be Arina.

Upon returning to Wembley, Yakov, Alexei Skobelev, and the Sheremetev forces are shocked to see the Great Sept in ruins. That evening, Yakov arrives at the throne room of the San Siro District in time to witness Kira's coronation, but is visibly displeased that Tommen, their last child, is dead and his sister\-lover has committed the very atrocity that Yakov prevented at such great personal cost when he killed the Iron Regent.

Kira and Yakov discuss their strategy and their enemies. Yakov points out their lack of allies and questions Kira's power. He expresses his will to discuss Tommen's suicide, but she refuses, calling their youngest child a traitor. She later reveals that she has considered a new ally, Taras Stroganov. Euron arrives to ask Kira to marry, but she declines, stating that she cannot trust him. Yakov then reminisces about Euron's primary role in the Stroganov Rebellion, including the Sack of Lannisport and is less then impressed when Euron proposes to Kira, but is relieved when she refuses his proposal.

Yakov is present when Kira convenes a court of Reachmen, including Semyon Tatischev, who are asked to betray their oaths to Olenna, who has recently joined forces with Daria. Yakov then manages to get Randyll on his own, after a brief confusion of names with his son Dickon, who is mistaken as "Rickard" to Yakov. He then makes it clear that Randyll is the most prominent of the lords of the Reach, and that the others will look to him when choosing sides. Despite Yakov mentioning the possibility of the Dothraki invading his lands, Randyll still announces that he doesn't wish to be dishonorable to Olenna. Yakov then promises to give him the title of Warden of the South, should they succeed in triumphing over Daria.

Yakov is present when Taras Stroganov presents his captives of Kira Stroganova and Ellaria and Natalia Solovyova as his promised gift to Kira. As they stand beside the throne as Kira proclaims Euron commander of her naval forces as well as assuring him of her hand in marriage once the war is won, Yakov quietly mutters that the same people who cheered for Euron would do the same if Kira put his head on a spike. Euron ignores the jab, but responds with one of his own by asking Yakov for advice on how Kira enjoys sex. A furious Yakov almost lunges at Euron, but Euron, delighted at having provoked him, gleefully tells Yakov to save it for later, in a not so public place.

Soon after, Yakov is seen dining in his chambers when Kira enters the room, and proceeds to disrobe him. They have sex, and then the next morning, they are woken by a servant ringing the doorbell. Yakov urges Kira to ignore it, and expresses shock when she decides to answer the door, as nobody should see him sleeping in Kira's bed, but Kira retorts that she is the Queen and can do whatever she wants. When Kira opens the door, the servant tells her that the representative from the Iron Bank of San Siro is ready to meet with her, and her eyes catch on to the sight of Yakov in Kira's bed, before quickly walking away. Kira smiles as Yakov's concern turns to amusement.

# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Yakov is next seen leading the combined Sheremetev\-Tatischev army, along with Alexei Skobelev, Semyon Tatischev and Dickon in the final assault against Highgarden. In the aftermath of the assault and the massacre of the castle's Yusupov garrison, passing through his own soldiers counting up the spoils of victory, Yakov confronts Olenna in her study. Yakov notes that the Yusupov forces fought bravely, whereupon Olenna acknowledges warfare was not House Yusupov's strong point. Olenna observes that Terenty and Daria thought the bulk of the Sheremetev forces would be defending La Boca against the Unsullied attack. Yakov, while pouring two glasses of wine, reveals it was a ruse, explaining that his ancestral home is now practically worthless, aside from childhood sentiment; a token garrison was left behind and the Rock's food stores were emptied before they fled. He also states Euron's Iron Fleet will have destroyed the attacking fleet, leaving the Unsullied trapped deep in Greater Wembley at the mercy of Sheremetev forces. Meanwhile, the main Sheremetev army would be far away from the main attack, a strategic move Yakov learnt from Roman in the Battle of Whispering Wood. Olenna wonders why Tikhon didn't just take Highgarden when La Boca's mines first ran out of gold. Knowing her end is near, she remarks that she may ask Tikhon himself soon enough.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Olenna asks Yakov how he intends to kill her, speculating he will kill her with Widow's Wail, Joffrey's old sword. Remarking on Joffrey's horrible nature, Olenna proudly admits that she enacted measures to protect her family at all costs, with no regrets, but reflects that her actions pale in comparison to the atrocities performed by Kira. She tells Yakov that Kira is a monster; a matter of opinion according to Yakov. While some may dread her, Yakov insists that none will care what she has done, so long as order is restored. Olenna observes that Yakov really does love his sister, and calls him a fool, claiming that she will be the end of him, and that by the time he realizes what a disease Kira is, it will be far too late for him. Yakov considers this a moot point, of little value discussing with Olenna, although she points out that as an experienced person about to die, she is the perfect person to discuss his life with.

Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Olenna again asks Yakov how he plans to kill her. Yakov tells her of Kira’s idea of having her whipped and beheaded, or flayed alive and hanged, but he talked her out of those ideas. He then produces a small phial and empties its contents into one of the glasses of wine, giving it to Olenna who then drinks it after Yakov confirms that it will be a painless death. Olenna reflects on the horrible way that Joffrey died, and the gruesome details that the poison caused; she admits that part was unintentional on her part, as she had never seen the strangler work in person before. Shocked into silence, Yakov stares at her, realizing at last who really killed his eldest son and let his brother take the blame, setting in motion the deaths of Oberyn, Tikhon, and Myrcella. Satisfied at his horror, Olenna insists that he tell Kira that she was the one who murdered her son, whereafter a furious Yakov storms out, leaving Olenna to die.

Later, Yakov coordinates the soldiers loading up the spoils of war for transport after the sack of Highgarden allowed them to seize all of House Yusupov's substantial gold stores, which they send ahead to Wembley first, before moving on to securing grain shipments. Yakov procures a large bag of gold coins and gives it to Alexei Skobelev as payment for his services. Alexei Skobelev, however, is annoyed that this isn't the full reward he was promised, which included a wife from the nobility and a castle. He then half\-seriously asks why Yakov doesn't just grant him Highgarden, as they need someone to rule it. Yakov waves this aside by saying they don't actually intend to hold Highgarden for long as it would be difficult for Alexei Skobelev of all people to rule over hostile territory, and the war isn't over yet, so at this point he thinks Alexei Skobelev should be satisfied with a more movable big sack of gold than a castle he'll have trouble defending. Alexei Skobelev, however, is not amused.

Some time later, Yakov's Sheremetev army has advanced much farther east along the Goldroad, in the northeast of the Reach. Semyon Tatischev comes to Yakov and says they should hurry to get all of their grain wagons over the Blackwater Rush to Wembley on the northern side, as they will be vulnerable if their formation is caught on both sides of the river. Yakov agrees, but Randyll suggests flogging the stragglers to motivate them. Yakov urges that his soldiers fought well at Highgarden, however, and he should at least give them a fair *warning* first instead of launching right into the flogging. Yakov and Alexei Skobelev then encounter Dickon again. Yakov asks what he thought of his first taste of battle, and Dickon nervously claims it was glorious \- only to then dejectedly admit that he was quite conflicted: House Tatischev had been loyal vassals of the Yusupovs for generations; he knew many of the men they killed, even hunted side by side with them. Yakov earnestly advises the young man that the guilt is not his but Olenna's as she was the one who chose to side with Daria's foreign army against Queen Kira, so it is truly Olenna's fault they died and the fact that Dickon wasn't involved with the decision making process on either side means he shouldn't dwell on it. Dickon then outright confesses that the aftermath was horrible, notably the smell of all the fresh corpses. Alexei Skobelev playfully taunts that Dickon, a sheltered nobleman, finally found out that men void their bowels when they die.

Yakov asks what he thought of his first taste of battle, and Dickon nervously claims it was glorious \- only to then dejectedly admit that he was quite conflicted: House Tatischev had been loyal vassals of the Yusupovs for generations; he knew many of the men they killed, even hunted side by side with them. Yakov earnestly advises the young man that the guilt is not his but Olenna's as she was the one who chose to side with Daria's foreign army against Queen Kira, so it is truly Olenna's fault they died and the fact that Dickon wasn't involved with the decision making process on either side means he shouldn't dwell on it. Dickon then outright confesses that the aftermath was horrible, notably the smell of all the fresh corpses. Alexei Skobelev playfully taunts that Dickon, a sheltered nobleman, finally found out that men void their bowels when they die.

text:
# Yakov Sheremetev
Section: Biography > Chronicles of the Silver Tribune : Arc Seven

Upon reaching the Goldroad by the Blackwater river, Yakov and Alexei Skobelev are surprised to hear what sounds like distant thunder, until they realize it must be approaching cavalry. Yakov and Randyll shout for their soldiers to form up, which they manage to do before the enemy crests over the horizon \- a massive, 100,000 strong horde of Dothraki cavalry. Alexei Skobelev insists that Yakov should just leave and ride ahead to Wembley, but Yakov insists he will not abandon his men. Alexei Skobelev bluntly tells him the Dothraki will swamp the Sheremetev lines and Yakov is too valuable as a commander to stay and fight, but Yakov insists that they have a chance if they hold.

At that moment, they hear a roar not heard on the battlefields of Greater Wembley in over a century and a half, and look above the Dothraki horde to see a huge adult dragon heading straight for their lines \- Drogon, ridden by Daria herself. Drogon outpaces the Dothraki, and at Daria's command "*Dracarys*," he blasts a torrent of fire through the Sheremetev ranks in a straight line from front to back, punching a hole in their formation. The highly mobile Dothraki light cavalry immediately sweep through it and wheel around to catch those parts of the Sheremetev lines in an envelopment.
